Existing guarantees often rely on structural or mixing assumptions, while stationarity and ergodicity alone do not permit consistent testing. In this work, we identify a class-level boundary governed by shared nontrivial Koopman eigenvalues, which represent common persistent oscillatory frequencies of the two processes. When no such eigenvalues are shared, we extend shift-based rank calibration with finite-window dependence witnesses and a data-adaptive threshold to construct a deterministic, weakly consistent test with finite-sample false-positive control, without quantitative mixing assumptions. Conversely, we show that no possibly randomized test can achieve vanishing false-positive probabilities under every independent jointly totally ergodic law while consistently detecting every dependent jointly totally ergodic law with a shared nontrivial eigenvalue. This impossibility already holds for binary observations and persists within any prescribed nonempty open eigenvalue window, identifying a spectral obstruction to universal learning of full-process independence.

title: Graftings and cograftings for species
abstract: We introduce graftings and cograftings for vector species, modelled on the elementary operations of adjoining and deleting a root in a rooted forest. We relate these maps to operads, up and down operators, and obtain nontrivial balanced pairs, admitting pair of creation/annihilation operators with commuting relations. We establish universal properties for the species of rooted forests. Using Fock functors, we recover the classical Connes--Kreimer Hopf algebra, its noncommutative planar analogue, and Foissy's $q$-infinitesimal Hopf algebra.

title: Networks with Memory and Isospectral Reduction
abstract: Restricting the linear dynamics of a graph to selected vertices generally introduces memory, because interactions can pass through hidden vertices before returning. The resulting rational memory kernels give isospectral reduction a dynamical interpretation and identify latent graph symmetries with symmetries of the observed evolution.

title: Grothendieck Pairs, Functors and Profinite Invariants
abstract: As another variation of profinite properties, we define the notion of natural profinite invariants: functorial invariants, inducing isomorphisms for every Grothendieck pair. We give a characterisation of when adjoint functors are natural profinite invariants and describe a strategy on how to disprove natural profinite invariance. By means of examples we show that the notions of profinite invariance and natural profinite invariances are logically independent.

title: Noise Calibration and Exact Recovery for Multiview Ordinal Rearrangement Data
abstract: We studied simultaneous recovery of a latent group count, subject partition, and signature means from multiview ordinal ranks. A normalized reference rearrangement score is an affine Spearman correlation; the problem concerns the information retained by several such scores and their noise geometry. We develop an ordered-gap estimator with direction-specific concentration radii. Its finite-sample guarantee separates signature noise, missing groups, and candidate coverage, and allows the group count to grow under an attainable-margin condition. A coordinatewise partition followed by label-tuple refinement recovers groups even when every individual coordinate has population collisions. A binary-code construction explains why the one-dimensional inverse-group margin restriction need not govern a retained coordinate bank. We derive actual-law concentration from bounded ranking modules and a fixed-dimensional combinatorial central limit theorem under an observed permutation representation. A binary ordinal submodel gives logarithmic exact-recovery information scales. A subject-effect construction distinguishes persistent overlap from reducible measurement noise, and an additional ordinal anchor quantifies how new information lowers that error floor. Five focused simulation scenarios illustrate direction-specific calibration, growing-group recovery, coordinate collision resolution, variance reduction, and the effect of an additional ordinal anchor.

title: Hydrodynamic and Dynamical Phi^4 Limits of Ising-Kac Models with Diffusion-Based Interactions on the Sierpiński Gasket
abstract: We introduce a general form of Ising--Kac interactions through heat-kernel averaging, with the heat-time parameter replacing the role of the interaction range. From the viewpoint of Dirichlet forms theory, this construction provides an intrinsic analogue of the mesoscopic averaging in classical Kac models when translation invariance is unavailable. We then investigate limits of this model on graph approximations of the Sierpiński gasket. For the associated Glauber dynamics, we establish a hierarchy of scaling limits for the magnetization field. First, at fixed interaction heat time and inverse temperature, we derive a nonlocal hydrodynamic equation on the continuum gasket. Second, as the heat time vanishes and the inverse temperature approaches its mean-field critical value, suitably rescaled hydrodynamic solutions converge to the solution of the deterministic Allen--Cahn equation. Finally, under a joint scaling of graph refinement, interaction heat time, and inverse temperature near criticality, we prove convergence of critical magnetization fluctuations to the solution of the dynamical $Φ^4$ equation. These results provide a concrete realization of the Ising-$Φ^4$ correspondence in a geometric setting with non-integer spectral dimension.

title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
abstract: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $Σ_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $Σ_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigulé and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouché's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.
comment: 25 pages, 3 figures. Figure-generation code, numerical data and exact-arithmetic checks included as ancillary files

title: Orthogonal Inference for Conditional Z-Estimation without Cross-Fitting: A Distributional Nearest-Neighbor Approach
abstract: Estimating conditional parameters, such as heterogeneous treatment effects, often requires rich covariate adjustment, even when the parameters are reported along only a few dimensions. Fitting nuisance functions on the full sample makes all observations available for adjustment, but creates dependence between fitted scores and the observations at which they are evaluated, which is typically avoided by cross-fitting. We develop pointwise inference with full-sample nuisance predictions for exactly identified conditional moment equations, recovering conditional average treatment effects as a special case. We localize the estimating equations around the reporting point using distributional nearest neighbors (DNN), a U-statistic-based averaging procedure. Under sufficient conditions on the local design, orthogonality, prediction accuracy and quantitative deletion stability, the estimator is asymptotically normal, and a frozen-score jackknife consistently estimates its limiting covariance with nuisance predictions held fixed. In simulations, full-sample and cross-fitted inference perform similarly, with coverage shortfalls from nuisance approximation error, spatial bias and heavy studentized tails. An application to 401(k) eligibility using Survey of Income and Program Participation data finds similar estimates across nuisance prediction methods, with wide normal-reference intervals.
comment: 36 pages (including appendices and references), 4 figures, 5 tables; supplementary material: 12 pages, 2 figures, 17 tables

title: Dice enterprises and polynomial approximation: uniform query tails
abstract: A binary-output dice enterprise uses independent rolls of a die with unknown face probabilities $\mathbf p$ (along with fair coin flips) to simulate a coin with bias $f(\mathbf p)$. We determine which power-law tails, uniform over the closed probability simplex, are attainable for the number $N$ of rolls. For continuous $f$ with values in $(0,1)$ and $q>0$, some enterprise for $f$ satisfies $\sup_{\mathbf p}\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf p}(N>n)=O(n^{-q})$ if and only if $f$ can be approximated uniformly by polynomials of degree $k$ with error $O(k^{-2q})$. When this holds, the same tail bound is attained by an oblivious enterprise, which chooses its number of rolls before rolling. The characterization extends to multiple dice, with total degree on a product of simplices; it then suffices to roll the dice in a fixed cyclic order. For $q>1$, these enterprises have a uniformly bounded expected number of rolls.

title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
abstract: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.

title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

title: Compactification of parabolic Hermitian--Einstein moduli spaces on complex surfaces
abstract: Let $\overline{X}$ be a compact complex surface with a Gauduchon metric, and let $D\subset\overline{X}$ be a smooth connected divisor. We construct an Uhlenbeck compactification of the moduli space of rank-two parabolic Hermitian--Einstein connections with prescribed holomorphic determinant.

title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $φ$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $ρ$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_ρ$, $\overlineΔ_ρ$, $IC_ρ$, and $δ_ρ$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}π$, $i_{b\sharp}π$, $i_{b\sharp!}π$, and $i_{b!*}π$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $π$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $φ$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
abstract: We prove a Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
abstract: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrowΩΣX$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

title: Stationary Limits of the Point Spectrum
abstract: We give an example of a directed set whose Tukey spectrum is not closed under stationary limits. This is a counterexample to a theorem due to Isbell from the 60's. We isolate a combinatorial principle arising from our example, between stationary reflection and weak compactness.

title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.

title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
abstract: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth. Our proof combines the thinning-and-sprinkling technique with a novel counting algorithm.

title: Regularity theory for non-local almost minimal surfaces via Euler-Lagrange inequalities at small scales
abstract: We extend the notion of non-local almost minimal sets introduced in [Dipierro, Valdinoci, and Villa, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)] by admitting lower-order powers for the remainder term. We combine classical techniques and a new, weaker version of the Euler-Lagrange inequalities (at a microscopic scale) to obtain $\mathcal{C}^{1,α}$-regularity for non-local almost minimal sets, up to Hausdorff dimension $n-3$. In turn, this formulation is well-suited for the non-local counterpart of the so-called Massari's problem for sets with prescribed mean curvature. In particular, such a generalization allows us to consider sets with $L^p$ non-local mean curvature (with $p\geq n/s$), which do not satisfy any curvature equation (neither in the classical nor in the viscosity sense). The results presented here lie beyond the reach of previously established methodologies. Indeed, the approach developed herein is based on a conceptual shift relative to the existing literature, which relied on a strong form of the Euler-Lagrange equation that is not available for general non-local almost minimal sets.

title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
abstract: Lane-changing (LC) maneuvers are highly challenging vehicle interactions, with substantial implications for traffic safety and efficiency. Developing effective LC strategies for connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic is complicated by the uncertainty associated with surrounding-vehicle behavior and the computational burden of embedding realistic prediction models within optimization schemes. To capture these complex interactions while retaining tractability, this study proposes a data-driven optimization framework that embeds neural network (NN) surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a Bézier-curve-based trajectory planner. Specifically, the safety cost during the LC process is quantified via a surrogate composed of an input convex recurrent neural network (ICRNN) encoding the planned trajectory, a fully input convex neural network (FICNN) embedding the LC duration, and a partially input convex neural network (PICNN) decoder fusing them with historical traffic states; separately, another FICNN surrogate approximates the optimal lateral comfort cost as a function of the LC duration. Both surrogates are embedded via linear programming (LP) formulations, avoiding the binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer programming (MIP) approaches for NN-embedded optimization. We further theoretically establish their exactness at optimality and extend the framework to problems with additional analytical objective terms and multiple surrogates. Experiments on a hybrid dataset combining real-world and simulated trajectories demonstrate that the proposed method achieves surrogate accuracy competitive with unconstrained baselines while substantially improving optimization efficiency over conventional MIPs. Closed-loop simulations further show that the proposed planners markedly reduce the weighted planning cost and consistently outperform baseline methods.

title: Memorization Capacity of Invariant Convolutional Neural Nets
abstract: Neural networks are powerful memorizers which are often able to interpolate their training data even when the labels have been randomized. While there exists an extensive literature on the memorization capacity of fully connected networks, in practice more specific architectures with problem-dependent properties are preferred, such as convolutional networks for image classification. In this paper we consider convolutional networks which are invariant with respect to a given arbitrary finite group of orthogonal transformations, which may include translations, reflections, and/or rotations of images and invariances of higher order tensors. We prove upper bounds on the size of an invariant convolutional neural network with threshold activations that is required to interpolate a given dataset with two classes. Our bounds are formulated in terms of a complexity measure that takes the invariant structure into account and is instance-specific, i.e., it is related to the mutual arrangement of the classes in the given dataset and their geometric properties rather than the number of samples. Our proof is constructive: for given input data, instances of an interpolating network can be computed via a randomized algorithm with high probability. In numerical experiments we investigate the practical effectiveness of this algorithm.

title: Variable Metric Three Operator Splitting
abstract: To minimize the sum $f + g + h$ of three convex functions when $f$ is differentiable with a Lipschitz-continuous gradient, we present a proximal algorithm, variable-metric three operator splitting (VMTOS), a generalization of the three operator splitting (TOS) scheme of Davis and Yin. We establish convergence guarantees by controlling changes in the metric. The smallest saddle-point residual among the first $k$ primal-dual iterates is $\tilde{O}(k^{-1/2})$. When $f$ and the convex conjugate $h^*$ are strongly convex and the accepted metrics and their inverses are uniformly bounded, the rate improves to $\tilde{O}(β^k)$ for some $β\in (0,1)$. We develop a practical Barzilai--Borwein update for diagonal metrics that satisfies our bound on metric changes. Under the same strong convexity assumptions, this update guarantees the required uniform metric bounds, yielding R-linear convergence. Numerical experiments on benchmark optimization problems show that VMTOS is competitive with other proximal algorithms.

title: Controllability of Nonlocal Partial Differential Equations
abstract: This chapter provides a short survey of recent developments in the controllability of nonlocal partial differential equations. We first review controllability results for evolution equations involving nonlocal spatial operators. Particular attention is devoted to unique continuation properties, observability inequalities, and Carleman estimates in establishing controllability properties. We then discuss controllability issues for partial differential equations with memory terms, highlighting how memory effects influence reachable states, null controllability, and exact controllability. We review and compare various analytical techniques developed to overcome the difficulties arising from the nonlocal structure. We also provide a critical assessment of some of these methods. Throughout the chapter, we emphasize the interplay between controllability and observability, the adaptation of classical control methods to nonlocal settings, and the distinctive phenomena that arise in comparison with local equations. We then discuss geometric inequalities and their role in the controllability of diffusion models. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current challenges and several open problems, aiming to provide directions for future research.

title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

title: A Gaschütz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
abstract: The classical Gaschütz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=Φ(\frac{a-nα_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $α_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $λ=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.

title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
abstract: In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance. We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.

title: A Note on the Smoluchowski Coagulation-Fragmentation Equation with Fractional Laplacian
abstract: In this work, we assess the well-posedness of the Smoluchowski coagulation-fragmentation equation with fractional Laplacian. In particular, we consider a truncated set of discrete Smoluchowski-type equations modeling the formation of clusters, with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, where the diffusive term describes a non-standard behavior in the movement of particles ('anomalous' diffusion).

title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_μ$ and the mass element $q_σ$. We show that $p_μ-q_σ=wp_μ$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
abstract: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, Łochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

title: Universality in randomly connected neural networks: old and new on a conjecture of Geman and Hwang
abstract: Randomly connected networks are ubiquitous in computer science, physics or biology. A central question is whether, and how, their collective dynamics depend on the choice of the distribution of the random couplings. Forty years ago, Geman and Hwang formulated a precise version of this \emph{universality} question for randomly connected neural networks. We come back to these conjectures, review what was proven since, provide a few new extensions and propose new conjectures in this paper. For $n$ neuron networks with couplings with a mean scaling as $1/n$ and light enough tails, two classes of limits are expected. For \emph{weakly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance $o(1/n)$, the network is predicted to converge to a McKean--Vlasov equation, and a broad literature has established this under general assumptions. For \emph{strongly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance of order $1/n$, the limit is a non-Markovian equation driven by a self-consistent Gaussian process. After landmark results for Gaussian couplings, universality was only recently established for linear interactions, while the continuous-time nonlinear case relevant to neuroscience remained open. Here, in the weakly heterogeneous regime, we prove quenched convergence on every time interval under a fourth-moment assumption only, and convergence in probability under an assumption slightly stronger than a second moment. In the strongly heterogeneous regime, we prove convergence for nonlinear interactions in continuous time, averaged over sub-Gaussian couplings and on every time interval, by a relative-entropy comparison with Gaussian couplings. We then extend the conjecture to heavy-tailed couplings, and propose a limit driven by a self-consistent $α$-stable process, for which we prove existence for every $α\in(0,2)$ and uniqueness for $α\in[1,2)$, and provide extensive numerical evidence in all three cases.

title: Anisotropic error estimates for the $L^{2}$-projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces
abstract: Anisotropic error estimates are determined for the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces in two and three dimensions. These estimates are determined in $W^{m,p}$-seminorms, in which $p \in [1,\infty]$ and $0 \le m \le k+1$, where $k \ge 0$ is the polynomial degree. The analysis relies on a geometric condition that is equivalent to the maximum angle condition. As an application, an apriori error analysis is presented for a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin discretization of the Poisson problem on two and three dimensional anisotropic meshes.

title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_σ$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(φ)$, where $φ$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(φ)$, where $φ$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $Λ$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.

title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
abstract: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.

title: The vanishing viscosity limit for the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations around a small obstacle
abstract: We investigate the interaction between a vanishing obstacle and the vanishing viscosity limit in the setting of the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. We work in the space exterior to a small obstacle in three dimensions. We prove quantitative convergence rates, assuming that the obstacle is sufficiently small, namely smaller than a constant times the viscosity. The convergence holds as long as the solution to the limit problem is known to exist and stays sufficiently smooth. This extends the results of Iftimie, Lopes Filho and Nussenzveig Lopes to the inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations. Moreover, we can show improved convergence rates and convergence of the gradient in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

title: Continuous Envy-Free Allocation via Reciprocal Preference Matrices: An Alternative to Sperner-Based Discretization
abstract: Fair allocation problems on a continuous simplex are often approached through Sperner-type discretizations: agents label mesh vertices according to their preferences and a fully labelled elementary triangle gives a discrete localization of a fair outcome. We develop a continuous alternative for three agents and three alternatives by representing preferences with multiplicatively consistent reciprocal pairwise-comparison matrices. Two independent ratios per agent induce exact linear indifference boundaries and turn envy-free allocation into a finite-dimensional feasibility problem. For the six possible assignments, we introduce an assignment score $Φ$ built from the agents' consistent priority vectors and prove that an incentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique minimizer of $Φ$, whereas a disincentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique maximizer. Consequently, the strict solution region is either empty or a unique convex preference region whose closure lies in the interior of the simplex. The weak solution set is never empty and degenerates exactly when $Φ$ has ties. We also compare the exact continuous formulation with Sperner-based discretization, including the boundary convention required in the disincentive model. Under exact consistency, the model uses six independent pairwise thresholds, whereas a regular triangular mesh with resolution $m$ contains $(m+1)(m+2)/2$ vertices. The method therefore exchanges a stronger parametric preference assumption for an exact continuous solution set and a resolution-independent elicitation stage.

title: Proximal R2 Priors for Structured Variance Allocation
abstract: Scientific domain knowledge in regression often concerns structural relationships among model terms, which are typically encoded as parameter constraints. Since such relationships rarely hold exactly in practice, prior distributions should encourage them while at the same time retaining support for scientifically plausible departures. Accounting for these relationships becomes more pressing in modern regression, where high-dimensionality is usually present and regularisation is essential. $R^2$ decomposition priors provide an interpretable foundation for regularisation by placing a prior on total explained variance and distributing the implied signal across model terms. We introduce the Proximal R2 prior, which uses proximal relaxations to encode these relationships as soft constraints on the variance allocation. Our formulation yields differentiable posteriors compatible with standard gradient based samplers. Theoretically, we prove that our prior preserves the characteristic marginal properties of global-local shrinkage priors. Moreover, we establish posterior consistency and contraction rates in growing dimensions, showing that the inclusion of structural relationships and proximal methods do not alter the shrinkage properties. Notably, these results demonstrate that the structural constraints in the model do not hinder posterior recovery. Simulation studies and real-data applications to interaction and generalised additive models demonstrate that our prior improves parameter recovery, out-of-sample prediction, and sampling efficiency over existing constrained and unconstrained shrinkage priors, even under structural misspecification.

title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kroó's conjecture
abstract: We resolve Kroó's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kroó's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
abstract: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[θ_1,\ldots,θ_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$. We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

title: Principal-agent hypothesis testing under adaptive experimentation
abstract: Principal-agent hypothesis testing studies statistical contracts in which a principal rewards an agent according to data the agent generates. Existing work focuses on the single-shot setting, where the agent produces a single dataset. We extend the framework to sequential settings, where evidence accumulates over time, rewards may be deferred to the end or disbursed incrementally, and the agent may stop the contract at a strategically chosen stopping time. We call a contract null-deterring if no ''null agent'' (those whose data-generating distribution lies in the null hypothesis) can profit in expectation under any stopping rule, and our main conceptual result shows that such contracts are characterized by e-processes. We then turn to the agent's best response and identify the optimal stopping rule through the Snell envelope of the reward process. We develop simpler, more interpretable approximations that often require the agent to have only partial knowledge of its distribution.

title: Connecting Base-Extension Semantics, Beth Semantics, and Ecumenical Logic
abstract: We investigate the relationship between base-extension semantics, Beth semantics, and Prawitz's ecumenical logic. We first present a base-extension semantics for the propositional fragment of Prawitz's system and prove that it is sound and complete. The semantics interprets intuitionistic and classical operators directly within a common proof-theoretic framework, without reducing the classical operators to their intuitionistic counterparts by means of a translation. We then analyse the effect of incorporating Beth-style clauses into base-extension semantics. When arbitrary bases are admitted and $\bot$ is governed by atomic explosion, these clauses trivialise. By contrast, when $\bot$ is treated as a basic sentence and attention is restricted to consistent bases, the Beth-style clauses for atoms and disjunction characterise, respectively, classical atoms and classical disjunction in Prawitz's system. We also obtain equivalent, path-independent formulations of the classical clauses for atoms, disjunction, and implication. These results reveal that the consistency constraint is not merely a technical restriction: within base-extension semantics, it transforms clauses originally associated with intuitionistic semantics into semantic characterisations of classical operators.

title: An asymptotic Jensen-Polya criterion for GRH
abstract: The Jensen--Pólya criterion expresses the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta-functions as a real-rootedness condition on their Jensen polynomials. Previous asymptotic results require large shifts, while computations establish real-rootedness in the Riemann case through a finite range of degrees. Here we study the unshifted family as the degree tends to infinity. For every number field $K$, we prove unconditionally that $J_{K,d}(X)$ is nonzero and has at least $d-C_K\sqrt{d\log d}$ distinct negative real zeros for all sufficiently large $d$, where $C_K>0$ depends only on $K$. Therefore, the proportion of real zeros tends to one with error $O_K(\sqrt{\log d/d})$. The main theorems have been autoformalized in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.
comment: 16 pages (extends and generalize old work by the author and others to the unshifted setting). Comments welcome

title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.
comment: 43 pages, 39 figures, 2 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Paul-A-Sanders/Criticality_classification

title: All-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: Call a finite nonempty point set $S\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the number of hyperplanes perpendicular to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. In 2026, Francisco Santos presented a question of Juan Benigno Seoane-Sepúlveda on the existence of all-even sets in dimensions $3$ and higher, together with examples of such sets in dimension $2$. Call a set $S\in\mathbb{R}^d$ line-all-even if for every direction $\ell \in \mathbb{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ the number of lines parallel to $\ell$ that intersect $S$ is even. As Santos pointed out, every all-even set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is line-all-even. We conjecture that there exist no line-all-even sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that affinely span $\mathbb{R}^3$ We show that our conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every planar all-even set satisfies a certain property, which we call height-rigidity. This property has a natural interpretation in linear algebra terms. Furthermore, we present a hierarchy of properties of planar point sets that imply height-rigidity. We construct several all-even sets in the plane, including some infinite families, and show that all the sets we constructed are height-rigid. In addition, we prove that every all-even set in the plane that can be covered by six or fewer parallel lines is height-rigid.

title: Dual Area-Volume-of-Fluid (DAVOF): co-advecting volume and face-area fractions for a closed-form, cell-local interface normal and position on unstructured meshes
abstract: Geometric Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) on unstructured polyhedral meshes reconstructs the interface orientation from the volume fractions of a stencil of neighbours; on irregular cells and in the presence of wisps it degrades, and the curvature built on it drives the parasitic currents of capillary flows. We transport, consistently to the volume fraction of every cell, the wetted fraction of every face area. From the area and volume fractions, closed-form equations recover the interface normal and position of a cell, for the first time in VOF: the normal from one sum over the cell's own faces, the divergence theorem on the liquid sub-volume, and the plane's position from a second, without neighbours or iteration. Both identities are exact for a plane on hexahedral, perturbed and polyhedral cells. On a sphere and an ellipsoid the normal has the order of the face fractions, the position is second order for every state and mesh, and a quadric through one ring of recovered normals gives a converging curvature where the reference models show none. Transported with the plane clipping, the ring normal, the same identity on the union of the cell's ring, stabilises the state and carries a sphere over 3.3 diameters bounded and conservative, first order in the face fractions as the clipping law predicts, at plicRDF's position and shape errors. A preliminary transport implementation with one paraboloid per cell, its frame from the normal, its curvature tensor from the ring and its position from the volume fraction, carries the sphere bounded and conservative over the resolution ladder with face fractions of order 2.8 per period with the exact normal and 2.1 with the ring quadric's normal over N = 32 to 128. The loop has the order of the normal it is fed; a transported normal of second order is the research goal. This document is the basis on which the further development of the method is documented.
comment: 45 pages, 9 figures, 18 tables. Code: https://github.com/tmaric/TwoPhaseFlow (branch davof) and https://github.com/leia-openfoam/leia (branch development)

title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.

title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_δ$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.

title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
abstract: For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $0<p<\infty$, let $$ G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}, $$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the spectra obtained by passing to subsequences and, for Schauder basic sequences, to normalized successive blocks. Their possible values are exactly $$ \varnothing,\quad (0,\infty),\quad (1,\infty),\quad [r,\infty),\quad (r,\infty)\qquad (r>1), $$ and the possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every admissible pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization, even in the fixed dual $\ell_\infty(\mathfrak c)=\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, and may be realized with empty spectrum for the original sequence. We also determine sharp universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for $p$-strong normality at a fixed exponent, $c_0$ for the whole subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. More generally, for every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal $A\subsetneq c_0$, membership of the error sequence in $A$ is exactly the universal condition preserving density of the $A$-summability domain. Finally, we extend the author's 2012 selection example from exponent one to every $p>0$ and to every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal. The good subsequences are exactly those whose index sets have uniformly bounded runs of consecutive integers; in the good case the detected quotient is isomorphic to $c_0$ and the whole selected sequence is weak-star Schauder basic.

title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

title: Gradient Estimates for Hessian Equations with Measure Data
abstract: In this article, we establish the interior gradient estimates for $k$-Hessian equations with measure data. We use the ideas from the potential theories for the $p$-Laplacian type equations and pointwise estimates of $k$-subharmonic functions by Labutin. The interior gradient regularity is optimal for $k\geqslant3$, while for $k=2$, we prove the interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ and $C^{1,α}$ estimates for $2$-subharmonic solutions.

title: The geometry of Floquet states
abstract: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians. The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

title: A Feasible-Direction-Type Method for Nonconvex Optimization with Infeasible Starts
abstract: We develop an infeasible-start extension of the Topkis--Veinott feasible-direction method for nonconvex composite optimization. At each main iteration, a strongly convex local model is used to obtain objective descent while limiting increases in constraint violation. A separate feasibility-reduction step is invoked when feasibility improvement is needed. Under a feasibility-reduction condition, we establish the standard first-order rate for reducing the Fritz John residual and constraint violation. We then verify that both proximal-gradient and regularized Gauss--Newton methods applied to minimizing the squared constraint-violation function satisfy the required feasibility-reduction property under a Polyak--Łojasiewicz condition. Numerical experiments compare the reduction methods, including an experimental prox-linear variant, and compare the scalar-regularized and curvature-enhanced subproblem formulations.

title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.

title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
abstract: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $Θ= [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $Θ$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.

title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

title: Representations and $n$-universality of hermitian lattices over local and number fields
abstract: Let $E/F$ be a quadratic field extension. For any positive integer $n$ an integral hermitian form over $E/F$ is called $n$-universal if it represents all integral hermitian forms of rank $n$ over $E/F$. We study $n$-universal hermitian forms when $F$ is a local field of characteristic $\neq 2$ or a number field. In the local case, we characterize $n$-universal integral hermitian forms and provide finite criterion sets for $n$-universality. In the number field case, we show that an indefinite integral hermitian form is $n$-universal if and only if it is $n$-universal everywhere locally.

title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.

title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
abstract: Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$. In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

title: Order invariance of the generalized Rosenblatt transform on standard Borel spaces
abstract: The Rosenblatt transform maps a random vector to independent uniform variables through successive conditional distribution functions; for laws on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with atomless conditional distributions and a fixed order of the coordinates, it is the almost surely unique monotone triangular map with this property. For a fixed reference law, transform-based tests remain valid under every fixed admissible order, but that choice can still affect their statistical power. We extend the generalized Rosenblatt transform to laws on countable products of standard Borel spaces, which requires, in addition to an order on the index set, a total order on each component space. For fixed orders, we establish identification and uniqueness results for this extended generalized Rosenblatt transform (EGRT) that parallel those for the classical transform. We then characterize order dependence in two senses: first demonstrating conditions under which the EGRT is invariant under linear extensions of prescribed partial orders, and second showing that under every admissible order the output of the EGRT retains all the statistical information from the input observations over reference-dominated families. We close with a brief discussion of what these results mean for the relationship between order choice and goodness-of-fit testing.

title: Composition factors and finite representation type
abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky recently introduced the theory of non-commutative error-correcting codes, generalizing classical coding theory to arbitrary groups via $δ$-robust subsets used to detect proper subgroups. Building on this foundation, this paper systematically studies an analogue of random codes for arbitrary groups, exploring the extent to which the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound holds in this non-commutative setting. While random universal codes of linear size in free groups are shown to be asymptotically bad, we establish a complete characterization for general families of finite groups. Specifically, a family of finite groups admits good random codes (forming a GV family) if and only if it exhibits uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. Furthermore, we provide explicit quantitative bounds on the rate and optimal distance range based on intrinsic parameters, proving that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families and determining the exact probabilistic rate for direct powers of a fixed finite simple group.

title: The General-Relativistic Limit of f(R) Gravity
abstract: We establish the general-relativistic limit of f(R) gravity coupled to a massless scalar field for small, asymptotically Euclidean, well-prepared Cauchy data near Minkowski spacetime. We prove global existence and future causal geodesic completeness, with uniform estimates for the metric, matter, and rescaled effective field as an admissible family of modified Lagrangians f(R) approaches the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian R. The physical and conformal metrics and the matter field converge to the limiting Einstein-massless-scalar development, uniformly on the entire future spacetime, together with finitely many space and time derivatives. The effective field, defined by a nonlinear reparametrization of the physical scalar curvature, converges to the scalar curvature of the limiting Einstein development. The main analytical difficulty is that the effective-field mass tends to infinity, while its evolution equation becomes an algebraic trace relation. Small field amplitudes may coexist with high-frequency oscillations and comparatively large derivatives, whose quadratic contributions must be controlled uniformly. Using the Euclidean-hyperboloidal foliation method and adapted wave coordinates, we analyze a quasilinear wave-Klein-Gordon system whose nonlinearities do not satisfy the classical null condition. We combine oscillatory estimates, weighted interior and exterior energies, and propagation estimates for the discrepancy from the Einstein trace relation. Quantitative convergence on compact regions and uniform spacetime decay yield global convergence.

title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper étale correspondence $Ω:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(Ω)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
abstract: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.

title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $Φ^4_3$
abstract: We determine the leading small-time Wasserstein action of the full spatial laws of centered KPZ and dynamical $Φ^4_3$, both started from zero. The leading term is Gaussian, with an explicit heat-trace constant. A common comparison also determines the ratio of length to displacement. For KPZ, a first-chaos cancellation yields a quadratic coupling error. For $Φ^4_3$, two weighted entropies and an adjoint estimate give comparison bounds uniform in the spectral cutoff. Integrating a Gaussian rotation gives a differentiable realization of the full law; the comparison holds at every positive time.

title: Rennala NSGD: Asynchronous Stochastic Optimization Beyond Euclidean Geometry
abstract: The empirical success of matrix-aware optimizers, such as Muon (Jordan et al., 2024) and Shampoo (arXiv:1802.09568), highlights the potential of non-Euclidean geometry for deep learning, including large language model (LLM) training. Despite this progress, the theoretical understanding of stochastic optimization in general normed spaces remains limited, particularly in distributed settings. We analyze minibatch stochastic gradient descent (SGD) for smooth nonconvex optimization with respect to an arbitrary norm on a finite-dimensional space. Using the framework of $κ$-regular normed spaces (arXiv:0809.0813), we derive high-probability oracle complexity bounds under a light-tail condition stated directly in the dual norm induced by the update norm. The bounds make the dependence on geometry explicit through the regularity constant $κ$ of the dual space. In the Euclidean case, our bound recovers the standard minibatch SGD rate up to logarithmic factors. For some non-Euclidean geometries and noise models, it is sharper than bounds obtained by converting a Euclidean noise assumption, reducing a linear dimension dependence to a logarithmic one. Building on this framework, we introduce Rennala NSGD, a semi-asynchronous distributed algorithm, and establish wall-clock time complexity guarantees under fixed, heterogeneous worker computation times. In the Euclidean case ($κ=1$), our bound matches the parameter dependence of classical Rennala SGD up to logarithmic factors.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 111 pages, 2 algorithms, 3 tables

title: Structured Pruning of Feedback Delay Networks
abstract: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) are recursive filter structures used to synthesise artificial reverberation. Their feedback matrix governs both energy exchange between delay lines and the computation required at every sample, making its design central to balancing an FDN's acoustic performance and implementation efficiency. In this work, we develop an FDN-specific structured pruning method that connects these acoustic and computational concerns, allowing high-order dense orthogonal designs to be fitted to efficient implementations. The feedback matrix is replaced by stages of fixed permutations and small orthogonal blocks. We characterise connectivity growth with the network depth and derive exact conditional block updates for matrix fitting, followed by refinement against the reference FDN magnitude response. The resulting factors admit direct vectorised evaluation, with arithmetic cost and coefficient storage scaling linearly with network size for fixed block size and depth. On an Apple M2, the selected staged kernels achieve feedback-multiplication speedups over dense BLAS ranging from approximately threefold to over twentyfold across the tested network sizes, while substantially reducing coefficient storage. Objective metrics and listening tests indicate that the proposed staged approximations closely preserve the spectral and temporal character of their dense references. An analysis of processor utilisation and register reuse explains why execution time depends on more than the operation count. Finally, block size and depth provide practical control over response fidelity, storage, and real-time cost, allowing acoustic design to precede the choice of an efficient implementation.
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to the IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing

title: Central limit theorems for high-dimensional ridge regression under uniform subsampling
abstract: We study ridge regression based on uniformly subsampled observations in high-dimensional linear models, where the number of predictors and the sample size grow proportionally. Subsampling is implemented through independent Bernoulli indicators with a common selection probability. We establish central limit theorems for linear contrasts of the ridge estimator, allowing for non-Gaussian predictors and general population covariance matrices. Under a vanishing-signal assumption, we obtain an explicit bias correction in the isotropic case and develop consistent estimators of the asymptotic variances. These results enable asymptotically valid tests for linear contrasts of the regression parameter in the isotropic setting. Our proofs exploit the resolvent representation of the ridge estimator and combine leave-one-out arguments with deterministic equivalents from random matrix theory.

title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.

title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

title: Sharp global stability for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near equilibrium
abstract: We study the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near a global Maxwellian and have found the bifurcation between the stability and instability in $H_{x}^{s}$ Sobolev space. We prove a strong-weak type instability result in the $s<1$ regularity regime, and establish the global stability under the regularity $s>1$ via the interplay between the dissipation and dispersive effects. In this intricate competition of dispersion, dissipation, large-velocity growth, and the asymmetric nature of the gain and loss terms, we prove that the instability is jointly generated by the dispersive effect and the loss term structure. To reach the sharp regularity for the global stability, we incorporate the dispersive effect into the dissipative energy framework for the analysis near equilibrium. This hence concludes sharp threshold and provides a complete characterization of global well-posedness near equilibrium.

title: Eternal Total Positivity and Matrix-Dependent Hadamard Thresholds
abstract: We study entrywise powers of totally positive matrices. Our first question is which matrices remain totally positive under every positive Hadamard power. We call them eternally totally positive. Our second question concerns a fixed totally positive matrix: what is the smallest exponent after which all of its entrywise powers are totally positive?
