We develop a powerful Random Duality Theory (RDT) based framework to analyze correlated data and already on the first level of RDT lifting obtain capacity characterizations that remarkably well match behavior exhibited through simulated dynamics. Moreover, characterizations explicitly feature correlation parameters $M$ and $r$, which allows to precisely determine their effects on phase-transitioning behavior of the underlying dynamics. Our results are also a well-fitting complement to the existing literature. Namely, to circumvent challenging statistical mechanics analyses, an alternative combination of spectral and replica methods is considered in [4]. We confirm that [4]'s elegant spectral characterizations are excellent approximations in the low correlated regime. At the same time, we also close the gap in the regimes with higher correlation levels where spectral methods deviate from the practical dynamics performance.

title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.

title: Optimal approximation error approach in Bayesian inverse problems
abstract: In many inverse problems, evaluating the forward operator is computationally expensive, making it common practice to accelerate inference with a less costly approximate model. However, such approximations introduce unwanted bias and must be carefully accounted for to ensure the reliability of the solution. This phenomenon is particularly pronounced in Bayesian inference, where accurate posterior characterisation typically requires a large number of forward model evaluations. In this paper, we focus on the approximation error model (AEM), which compensates for the modelling error by adjusting the likelihood density. More precisely, AEM incorporates the model error into the additive Gaussian noise distribution. A central challenge in this approach is how to choose the modified noise mean and covariance in a principled way. To address this, we propose a new framework, optimal approximation error (OAE) which determines the noise model by minimising the expected information loss, measured via the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the true and approximate posterior distributions. We show that the standard enhanced error approach (EEA) is recovered as the minimiser of the expected divergence between likelihoods rather than posteriors and develop OAE as a direct alternative targeting posterior accuracy. We establish bi-convexity of the OAE objective, introduce a regularised, provably convergent proximal alternating minimisation scheme, and derive closed-form expressions in the Gaussian linear setting. We further show that OAE estimates computed from empirical training data are statistically consistent. Numerical experiments on a linear CT problem and a nonlinear Darcy-flow problem show that OAE improves posterior accuracy relative to both the uncorrected and EEA-corrected likelihoods.

title: Turán number of three disjoint cliques of arbitrary sizes
abstract: The Turán number $\rm ex(n,H)$ of a given graph $H$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. In this paper, for all $p\ge q\ge r\ge 2$ and $n\geq p+q+r$, we determine the exact value of $\rm ex(n,K_p\cup K_q\cup K_r)$ and describe all extremal graphs.

title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
abstract: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.

title: Inverse Scattering of Periodic Surfaces with Multilayer Superlenses: Perturbation Analysis and Resolution Enhancement
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of inverse scattering for periodic surfaces through a multilayer superlens. Using the transformed field expansion, we derive a highly explicit reconstruction formula. We theoretically prove that under perfect matching, the reconstruction factor is independent of the number of layers and depends solely on the total material thicknesses, achieving uniform boundedness when the slab thickness dominates. By establishing first-order perturbation formulas and high-frequency asymptotics, we quantify how small material losses induce exponential amplification of high-frequency errors. Crucially, we show that increasing the number of layers substantially reduces this amplification coefficient. Consequently, for fixed total thicknesses, multilayer structures offer significantly improved stability and extended resolution limits for subwavelength reconstruction.

title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
abstract: We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

title: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
abstract: In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.

title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
abstract: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin, with the convergence time arbitrarily assigned a priori and independently of the initial condition. Two static output-feedback methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is not provided for general MIMO systems; for SISO systems, the constant current-output gain can be readily selected. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For unknown constant measurement delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation is also presented. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

title: Controllability-Based Input Allocation in Quantum System
abstract: Understanding how local perturbations influence global quantum dynamics is important for analyzing and designing large-scale quantum systems. Existing quantum centrality measures often rely on static correlations or entanglement and do not directly capture perturbation propagation under unitary evolution. We formulate controllability allocation scoring for quantum input-output dynamics governed by the Schrodinger equation. Using the multiobservable quantum-control Gramian, we introduce virtual local Hamiltonian perturbations along a nominal trajectory and decompose the terminal-output response into channel-wise Gramian contributions. A simplex-constrained log-determinant optimization combines these contributions to define a volumetric controllability allocation score (V-CAS), specifying an optimal allocation of virtual input intensities among local Hamiltonian perturbation directions. The score measures their cooperative dynamical influence and depends on the output and trajectory. We characterize the output Gramian's range and minimum-energy properties and derive a drift-independent sufficient condition ensuring score uniqueness for almost every terminal time at which the problem is feasible. For quantum many-body systems, we develop a matrix-product-state and time-evolving-block-decimation implementation that avoids explicitly constructing exponentially large state-transition matrices. We also derive an error bound propagating Trotter and MPS-truncation errors to the discrete output Gramian. Numerical experiments show that the score captures finite-time influence patterns distinct from those identified by static correlation- and entanglement-based measures and can inform target-independent control-channel preselection.

title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
abstract: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.

title: Stability of a Fréchet-type functional equation
abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fréchet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of Găvruţa.

title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $μ$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincaré inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

title: The residue field as an infinite syzygy
abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m},k)$ be a commutative Noetherian ring which is either local or positively graded over the field $k$. We provide a method based on liftings for constructing free coresolutions of $k$ over $R$. We apply this method to twisted trivial extensions of the node $k[u,v]/(uv)$ to build a family of positively graded $k$-algebras of dimension $1$ over which $k$ is an infinite graded syzygy, resolving an open question of Iyengar in the negative. We also prove a formula for alternating sums of lengths of Ext modules when $R$ is positively graded, and use it to show that a graded free coresolution of $k$ cannot dualize to a resolution unless $R$ is Artinian Gorenstein.

title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $γ_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_jγ_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables; ancillary verification scripts and certificates in anc/

title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent. For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure. Ancillary file: exact-arithmetic verification script (Julia)

title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ol}(G)\le\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|)$. The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. No restriction is imposed on the order of the group or on the stabilizer of the set of subset sums.

title: An analogue of $Γ$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $Γ$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.
comment: 37 pages, 14 figures; catalogue of the 338 orbits and the output of the exact checks in the appendices

title: Crescent configurations in three dimensions
abstract: A crescent configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities $1,\ldots,n-1$. We construct such a configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $n\geq3$, giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle's theorem. We also give explicit integer-coordinate configurations with $O(n\log n)$ bits per coordinate, and prove that every finite initial segment of the sequence $(\cos j,\sin j,2j)_{j\geq0}$ of length at least three is a crescent configuration.

title: The Minimax Complexity of Federated Optimization under Interpolation: The Role of Oracle Models
abstract: We study the minimax complexity of smooth convex stochastic optimization with intermittent communication: $m$ workers run for $N$ rounds, and between consecutive communication rounds each worker makes $K$ sequential stochastic gradient queries. We focus on the interpolation regime, in which all sample losses share a common minimizer, so that the gradient noise vanishes at the solution. Let $L$ be the smoothness of the objective, $H_s\ge L$ the smoothness of the sample losses, and $R$ the distance from the initial point to a minimizer. We consider three oracle models that provide increasing information: an unbiased stochastic gradient oracle $g(x,ξ)$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}_ξ\|g(x,ξ)\|^2 \leq 2H_s\bigl(F(x)-F(x^*)\bigr)$, gradients of the sample losses at fresh samples, and repeated gradient queries to stored samples. Up to logarithmic factors, all our results are described by two rates: \[ R^2\min\left\{L,\;\frac{H_s}{KN},\; \frac{L}{N^2}+\frac{H_s}{mKN}\right\} \qquad\text{and}\qquad R^2\min\left\{L,\; \frac{\min\{L,H_s/K\}}{N^2}+\frac{H_s}{mKN}\right\}, \] Under the weak growth condition, the first rate is the minimax rate, attained by the best of three simple baselines, as in the classical bounded-variance setting. With repeated access to samples, the second rate becomes the minimax rate for general convex objectives. For general convex objectives with fresh sample gradients, the minimax rate lies between the two rates. Our lower bounds apply to arbitrary randomized intermittent-communication algorithms.

title: Asymptotic Formula of the Lifespan of Classical Solutions to 1D Quasilinear Wave Equations
abstract: We study the lifespan \(T^*(\varepsilon)\) of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional quasilinear wave equation $u_{tt}-(c(u)^2u_x)_x=0$, with initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$. We assume that $c'(θ)\sim a|θ|^{p-2}$ as $θ\to 0$, where \(a>0\) and \(p>3\) or $p=2$. We obtain explicit asymptotic formulas for $T^*(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. We treat both the case $ψ\in L^1(\mathbb R)$ and the case $ψ=ψ_1+\Braket{x}^{-α}$, where \(ψ_1\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) and \(0<α\le1\). Our results identify the dependence of the lifespan scale on the decay exponent, including the borderline case $α=1$. The proof combines Riccati equations along characteristics with a scaling argument inspired by Lindblad.

title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
abstract: We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -Δu+u+λ|u|^{q-1}u =μ|u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$ where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $λ,μ>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.

title: Einstein Metrics and Quantum Control on Symmetric Tensor Product Quotients
abstract: Let $M_n=(\mathrm{PU}(2)^n\rtimes S_n)\backslash\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$ be the space of projective $n$-qubit unitaries modulo local unitaries and permutations of the qubits. We prove that for all sufficiently large $n$ the manifold $M_n$ carries exactly two $\mathrm{PU}(2^n)$-invariant Einstein metrics up to scaling. Both Einstein metrics have uniformly bounded diameter after normalizing two-qubit costs, although approximating a Haar-random unitary requires exponentially many two-qubit gates. In contrast, we construct non-Einstein metrics with nonnegative Ricci curvature and exponentially growing typical control distances, and determine the sharp curvature threshold for this family.

title: The Characteristics of Finite Projections of Certain Stochastic Processes and Queues
abstract: This thesis studies finite projections of transient regenerative processes, constructed by conditioning regeneration cycles to be finite. It develops comparisons between the original and projected laws, including finite-time bounds and best-approximation properties for specified metrics and comparison classes. Applications concern birth-and-death processes, Markov chains and semi-Markov processes, with explicit queueing examples. Structural results describe projections associated with different regeneration states, invariant measures and connections with Martin boundary kernels. The thesis also studies reconstruction of birth-and-death rates from passage-time laws and continued-fraction representations of Laplace-Stieltjes transforms for skip-free semi-Markov processes, together with truncation-error bounds. This is a corrected English edition of a Romanian doctoral thesis completed in 1998 and defended in 1999. The preface distinguishes the historical work from corrections and later additions made for this edition.
comment: 89 pages; corrected English edition (2026) of the author's Romanian doctoral thesis, State University of Moldova, 1998; defended 15 January 1999

title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(δ\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.

title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
abstract: The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them. We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product. Our main tool is a strengthened form of the generating family method of Ahlswede--Khachatrian, based on standard generating families and on local modifications of cross-intersecting families, which we call mutations. It treats two completely different types of extremal structures in a unified way and, unlike the original method, needs shifting in only one step.

title: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
abstract: We construct three binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ with weight enumerators for which no binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ were previously known to exist. This completes the determination of the weight enumerators that occur for binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$.

title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics
abstract: Bisimulation metrics offer a principled notion of task-relevant state similarity in reinforcement learning, but existing constructions and methods are largely confined to discounted MDPs, where contraction arguments ensure well-defined fixed points and downstream guarantees. We develop a unified foundation for bisimulation metrics in undiscounted settings, that is total- and average-reward problems, by replacing the standard operator-centric view with a game-centric one: we interpret prior metric operators as Bellman-Shapley operators of zero-sum turn-based games and define metrics as the corresponding game value functions, yielding unique definitions even when $γ=1$. This game-theoretic foundation facilitates transfer of dynamic-programming theory and algorithms. We also use this game-centric perspective to characterize how metric finiteness depends on structural properties of the underlying MDP and motivate certain directed metrics that remain finite in weakly communicating MDPs. We further introduce an abstract framework for modifying the games' action spaces, allowing general transition coupling sets, that recovers many existing metrics and guides new constructions. Finally, we prove that these metrics bound total-reward and, when the optimal gain is state-independent, optimal relative value differences. We also provide error and suboptimality guarantees for aggregation-based planning in total- and average-reward settings.

title: Tight Stationarity Transfer and Repeatability for Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods
abstract: Proximal-gradient methods are widely used for composite optimization, but inexact proximal updates introduce a residual in the proximal optimality condition, complicating the analysis of how stationarity changes across a step. We study this question for composite objectives consisting of a smooth convex term and a possibly nonsmooth weakly convex term, focusing on the relationship between the directional-stationarity measures at the input and output points of an inexact proximal-gradient step. We first establish separate input and output bounds, but their combination can yield a conservative estimate because their worst-case residual directions may differ. By exploiting the magnitude and orientation of this shared residual, we establish tight joint bounds and derive an exact one-step stationarity-transfer factor that strictly improves the estimate from separate bounds in the short-step regime. We also identify the precise residual-tolerance threshold for finite uniform stationarity transfer. A further distinction emerges over multiple steps: endpoint worst cases can repeat over arbitrarily many iterations, whereas interior worst cases cannot persist across two consecutive steps, yielding strict two-step submultiplicativity. These results also provide principled tolerance-selection rules, descent estimates, and stationarity-complexity guarantees for inexact proximal-gradient methods.

title: A lattice order on the complex field
abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers admits a lattice order compatible with addition and multiplication. We answer the question affirmatively. Using a valuation with value group $\mathbb{Q}$, we construct a positive cone $P$ by a transfinite recursion of countable ordinal length. At each stage we extend a lattice order on a subspace while preserving its lattice operations in the whole field and maintaining multiplicative closure of the ambient positive cone. These subspaces eventually exhaust $\mathbb{C}$. The construction depends on choices of a valuation extension, compatible rational powers and vector-space bases. The cone $P$ contains $1$ and satisfies $\{x\in P\setminus\{0\}:x^{-1}\in P\}=\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. The induced order is not total: $i$ is incomparable with $0$. For a chosen transcendental element $t$ and $i^2=-1$, one may prescribe $0\vee i=(t+i)/2$ and $0\vee(-i)=(t-i)/2$. Varying the first extension yields exactly $2^{\mathbf c}$ distinct lattice positive cones on $\mathbb{C}$, where $\mathbf c=|\mathbb{C}|$. The count concerns cones as subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.

title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
abstract: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is (semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable on the K3 surface.

title: A note on a problem of Ma and Chen
abstract: Let $S=(s_1,s_2,\cdots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. For any real number $α>0$, let $S_α=(\lfloorαs_1\rfloor,\lfloorαs_2\rfloor,\cdots)$. We prove that if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists $0<α<1$ such that $S_α$ is strongly complete. In addition, this gives a negative answer to a problem of Ma and Chen in [Acta Arith. 203 (2022), 307--318]. We also prove that the same result is true if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
abstract: L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open. In this paper, we study the L-extendability of functions on the integer lattice. We first obtain a necessary condition: L-extendable functions are integrally convex. We then consider a special subclass of L-extendable functions, namely, those whose local convex extensions give L-convex relaxations. This subclass has a useful optimization property: the optimal value of the original function coincides with that of the $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation given by its local convex extension, a property not guaranteed for general $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxations. We characterize this subclass by showing that a function is L-extendable through its local convex extension if and only if it is integrally convex and its restriction to every unit hypercube is D-convex, where D-convexity is a discrete convexity associated with reflected Freudenthal simplicial divisions. This subclass strictly contains the class of D-convex functions. We also give a combinatorial characterization of D-convex subsets of the vertices of a unit hypercube: a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is D-convex if and only if it is majority-closed and contains a relative opposite pair.

title: On $q$-middle convolution and generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation
abstract: We investigate higher-order $q$-difference equations obtained by successive applications of a $q$-analogue of addition and the $q$-middle convolution. We construct an $n$-dimensional system of linear $q$-difference equations and derive a single $q$-difference equation whose coefficients are polynomials of degree at most $1$ in the independent variable. Under certain conditions on the parameters, the resulting equation is a generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation of order $n$. We also obtain a multiple Jackson integral representation of solutions and give sufficient conditions for its convergence. By suitably choosing the functions appearing in the integrand and specializing the parameters, we obtain $q$-hypergeometric series solutions of type ${}_n φ_{n-1}$.

title: Classification of threshold dynamics for the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous NLS
abstract: We study the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation $i\partial_{t}u+Δu+|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{4-2b}{d}}u=0$ in dimensions $d\ge3$. For $\frac12<b<\min\{2,d/2\}$, we prove that every forward-global $H^1$ solution with mass equal to that of the ground state $Q$ either scatters forward or coincides with $e^{it}Q$, up to phase rotation and scaling. As a consequence, every solution with nonradial $H^1$ initial data at the ground-state mass must be global and scatter in both time directions. For $0<b\le\frac12$, analogous rigidity and scattering results hold under an additional finite-variance assumption. The key new ingredients in our proof are a nonradial incoming/outgoing decomposition and exterior frequency-decay estimates, which yield the kinetic-energy localization needed for a localized virial argument.

title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

title: Moments propagation in the Vlasov equation and application to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
abstract: In this paper, we study how the propagation of particle moments depends on the fluid velocity in the Vlasov equation. We present some new moment estimates involving the velocity in this equation. As an application, we establish Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin-type regularity criteria involving only the velocity field for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov system.

title: A time-map description of the one-dimensional (p,q)-Laplacian Fučik spectrum
abstract: We study a one-dimensional Fučik-type boundary value problem (BVP) driven by the nonhomogeneous, one-dimensional $(p,q)$-Laplacian, \[ -\left(|u'|^{p-2}u' + |u'|^{q-2}u'\right)' = λ(u^+)^{p-1} - μ(u^-)^{q-1}, \qquad u(0)=u(L)=0, \qquad L>0, \] where $1<q<p$ and $λ,μ\in\mathbb{R}$. The problem is asymmetric: the positive component is paired with the $p$-power and the negative component with the $q$-power. This asymmetry prevents the standard homogeneous $p$-Laplacian scaling argument from producing explicit Fučik curves. We first prove a quadrant reduction theorem. Any positive nodal interval for a solution forces $λ>0$, and any negative nodal interval forces $μ>0$. Hence, all sign-changing solutions occur for values of $(λ,μ)$ in the positive quadrant. Outside the positive quadrant, only one-sign solutions can occur. We also formulate the equation as an autonomous planar system and establish existence and uniqueness for its initial value problem in the positive quadrant. We then impose the second Dirichlet condition through a shooting formulation and show that every zero of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is simple and isolated. This provides the dynamical foundation for the subsequent construction and gluing of nodal humps of solutions. Inside the positive quadrant, we use a classical one-dimensional time-map method to obtain a projected-geometry description of the spectrum, or the set of values of $(λ, μ)$ for which there exist nontrivial solutions. Every nodal solution has a common energy $E>0$ shared by all positive and negative humps.

title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.

title: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method
abstract: Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks (PIHNNs) exploit complex-analytic representations to satisfy homogeneous PDEs by construction, but their extension to nonhomogeneous problems is nontrivial. We propose a hybrid physics-informed holomorphic neural network (HPIHNN) framework based on a decomposition of the solution into particular and homogeneous components. The particular component is computed by a spectral method on a simple extended domain, while the homogeneous component is approximated by a PIHNN trained only on the boundary with modified boundary data. The resulting formulation avoids meshing complex geometries and retains the dimensionality-reduction advantage of holomorphic representations. The method is applied to nonhomogeneous Poisson, Stokes, biharmonic, linear elasticity, and Helmholtz equations. Numerical experiments covering complex geometries, corner singularities, and nearly incompressible regimes demonstrate that the proposed method accurately resolves the corresponding solutions and, in the considered tests, generally achieves lower errors and shorter training times than standard PINNs. The results indicate that coupling spectral particular solutions with holomorphic neural approximations provides an efficient approach to nonhomogeneous PDEs on complex domains.

title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
abstract: Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

title: Damped stochastic mirror descent for non-smooth ill-posed problems in Banach space
abstract: We introduce a damped variant of the stochastic mirror descent method for systems of non-smooth nonlinear ill-posed operator equations in Banach spaces. At each iteration, the method samples a random subset of the equations, performs a mirror-descent step in the dual space with an adaptive step size derived from the discrepancy principle, and applies a damping term that prevents the iterates from drifting away from the initial guess. The scheme accommodates non-smooth forward operators through a family of bounded linear surrogates, admits general $p$-convex penalty functionals which also includes trained convex penalty, allows the noise level to differ from equation to equation, and dispenses with two classical requirements, namely reflexivity of the image space and Gâteaux differentiability of the forward operator. We study its regularization properties under an \textit{a posteriori} stopping rule by proving first that the iteration terminates after finitely many steps almost surely, and then that the mean-square error of the iterates tends to zero as the noise level vanishes. Numerical experiments on a system of non-smooth semilinear inverse source problems and the identification of a diffusion coefficient confirm the theoretical analysis and shows improved convergence results.

title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
abstract: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

title: Meromorphic solutions of a nonlinear differential-difference equation with two exponential terms
abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. We study finite order meromorphic solutions of the nonlinear differential-difference equation \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+P_{d}(z,f)=p_{1}(z){\rm e}^{α_{1}z^{k}}+p_{2}(z){\rm e}^{α_{2}z^{k}}, \end{equation*} where $P_{d}(z,f)\not\equiv 0$ is a difference polynomial in $f$ of degree $d\leq n-1$ whose coefficients are small meromorphic functions with respect to $f$, $p_{1},~p_{2}$ are nonzero meromorphic functions with $T(r,p_{j})=o(r^{k})$, $j=1,2$, and $α_{1}\neqα_{2}$ are nonzero constants. We prove that every such solution has order exactly $k$, and obtain sufficient conditions on $n,~d,~k$ for the equation to admit no finite order meromorphic solution with $N(r,\frac{1}{f})=S(r,f)$. Our results extend the known ones from linear exponents $z$ to polynomial exponents $z^{k}$, and replace the linear difference polynomials with the degree restriction $d\leq n-2$ assumed in the literature by general ones of degree $d\leq n-1$. Examples show that the restrictions on $n$ and $d$ are sharp.

title: Inflection sets of permutations
abstract: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $σ'(i)=σ(i+1)-σ(i)$ of a permutation $σ\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $σ''(i)=σ(i+1)+σ(i-1)-2σ(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them. We then study which sets of pairs of integers $(i,j)$ are the inflection set of some permutation and whether a given set is witnessed in $\Sym_n$ for infinitely many $n$. We show that exactly $14$ permutations of $[n]$ have no inflections when $n\ge5$. For a single inflection $\{(k,m)\}$, we determine all $n$ for which it is witnessed in $\Sym_n$: we prove it is always witnessed, and it is witnessed for only finitely many $n$ if and only if $m\ge 2k+1$. In that case, all such $n$ satisfy $2m-2k+1\le n\le 2m-k+2$ (apart from $k=2$, $n=m+1$), and, perhaps surprisingly, this range has gaps once $k\ge 10$, the smallest occurring at $(k,m,n)=(10,21,30)$. Finally, we characterize maximally inflected permutations, whose second derivative alternates in sign, and show that their number $|\mathcal M_n|$ satisfies $2E_n\le|\mathcal M_n|\le(2/3)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1}\,n!$, where $E_n$ is the Euler zigzag number.

title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
abstract: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions. These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.

title: Introduction to Separable Simplicial Algebras
abstract: We study separable simplicial algebras and Azumaya simplicial algebras.

title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
abstract: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.

title: Bound-preserving and mass-conserving projection BCFD methods for incompressible miscible displacement in porous media
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze two novel structure-preserving projection schemes for the incompressible miscible displacement problem in porous media. These schemes are specifically designed to preserve two essential physical properties--concentration bounds and the mass balance identity, and are accompanied by a rigorous error analysis for the projection approach. Both schemes are second-order accurate in space but differ in temporal accuracy: one is first-order and the other is second-order. Methodologically, both schemes comprise a prediction step for the concentration variable, based on a second-order modified upwind discretization together with an implicit-explicit finite difference approximation, followed by a projection (or correction) step that enforces the desired physical constraints, namely bounds and mass conservation. For the first-order temporal scheme, the velocity and pressure are solved at the first step on staggered spatial grids with explicit treatment of concentration. In contrast, for the second-order scheme, to ensure well-posedness and to suppress non-physical oscillations in the simulation, the velocity and pressure are solved at the final step with the concentration treated implicitly. A rigorous numerical theoretical framework is established for the first-order scheme, encompassing optimal-order error estimates, stability, and proofs of the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solutions. The numerical analysis framework is further extended to the more involved second-order scheme, and the corresponding theoretical results are briefly outlined. Finally, numerical examples, including some 'real' simulations, are presented to verify the theoretical findings and demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed schemes. In particular, the occurrence of viscous fingering is successfully captured and confirmed by the numerical results.

title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Matérn/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part II: Langevin Dynamics
abstract: We consider the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem on the sphere, in which we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\mathcal{S}_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N:\lVert x\rVert^2=N\}$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. Continuing the program initiated in Part I [arXiv:2610.16705], we show that spherical Langevin dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization. Together with Part I, our results demonstrate that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.
comment: Companion paper to arXiv:2610.16705 (Part I). 71 pages, 1 figure

title: Strong approximations for dependent random fields
abstract: We establish strong Gaussian approximations for centered stationary random fields on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, represented as measurable functions of i.i.d.\ innovations. Under finite $p$th moments, $p>2$, and sufficiently fast decay of spatial dependence, we construct a single coupling of the field with an i.i.d.\ Gaussian field. Its partial sums, scaled by the long-run standard deviation, approximate those of the original field almost surely, uniformly over all rectangular prefixes and all observation scales. Over a cube of side length $n$, the approximation error is $O_{\mathrm{a.s.}}(n^{\max\{d/p,(d-1)/2\}})$ up to logarithmic factors. While $d/p$ is the familiar moment term, the surface term $(d-1)/2$, absent for independent planar arrays, emerges as a cost of dependence, and cannot be removed even for finite-range Gaussian fields. The assumptions accommodate nonlinear and noncausal fields without imposing mixing. The proof combines a permanent dyadic blocking, a local Gaussian coupling in tensor Haar coordinates driven by a Doob martingale with vanishing conditional third moments, and a comparison of the resulting dependent Gaussian blocks with white noise.

title: Two-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions
abstract: It is trivial that $1$-dimensional $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates. Coupier, Henry, Jahnel and Köppl proved the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in dimension 2; and then for sufficiently large dimensions, Bäumler, Jahnel, Köppl, Lodewijks, Reeves and Tóbiás showed this is still true. In this paper, we verify that the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions $d\ge 3.$

title: Soliton resolution conjecture and soliton gases for the Benjamin-Ono equation with infinite-order multisolitons in the sharp well-posedness space
abstract: We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for infinite-order multisoliton solutions in the sharp well-posedness space $H^s(\mathbb R)$, $s>-\frac12$, and construct soliton gases in $H^{s}(\mathbb R)$ with arbitrary $s\in\mathbb R$, for the Benjamin--Ono equation. In particular, our work addresses two important open problems about inverse spectral for Lax operator, including the problem of spectral characterization of infinite-order multisolitons and that of determining the range of their asymptotic parameters. A central ingredient of our work is a spectral decomposition adapted to rough initial data. This extends the global soliton--radiation description to weakly weighted $H^s$ data while allowing infinite negative eigenvalues. Another important ingredient is a continuous norming action that extends finite inverse spectral shifts to gas limits while retaining a full continuous norming weight. Our framework provides a basis for studying infinite-order soliton resolution and the construction and asymptotics of soliton gases for nonlocal equations.

title: Convex-SKM-Net: Low-Latency Block Halfspace Corrections for Neural Convex Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: Fast inference and strict constraint satisfaction are essential for learning-based decision-making. Existing methods often rely on constraint-specific projections or feasible-set parameterizations, while iterative repair can be costly. We introduce Convex-SKM-Net, a convex constraint-satisfaction layer that forms linearization halfspaces from residual and (sub)gradient oracles without constraint-specific inequality projectors. It applies fixed-depth dual projected-gradient descent (dual PGD) to minimum-displacement block problems using GPU-friendly matrix operations. We jointly learn the predictor and a positive-definite mobility, adapting the correction geometry to improve objective quality. We prove convergence of the outer iterates at fixed dual depth and linear convergence in distance under Slater's condition and bounded subgradients. All our test outputs on three second-order-cone model-predictive control (SOC-MPC) horizons and six power-system convex relaxations satisfy a $10^{-3}$ feasibility tolerance. Comparisons with the latest constraint-satisfaction methods show inference speedups of up to $144.3\times$ on SOC-MPC and $7.7\times$ on a convex quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) benchmark with joint training. On QCQP, the mean objective gap is $0.012\%$, with full test feasibility at $10^{-4}$. Learning mobility reduces the five-seed affine-task mean gap by $22.4\%$ and improves gaps in matched power-system comparisons.

title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.

title: In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
abstract: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.

title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
abstract: Benders decomposition and column generation solve large optimization problems by passing cuts, columns, and dual values between a master problem and subproblems, and are hard to implement correctly. Large language models now automate parts of algorithm design, which points toward agents that build decomposition solvers for new problems. As a first step toward such agents, we study how well current coding agents design and implement these two algorithms, and how they fail. We introduce DecompGym, 81 instances from nine problem families (five Benders, four column generation), in which an agent writes a solver for a prescribed method. Each solver must meet three criteria: execution within a 60-second time limit; numerical feasibility together with a method audit, in which an LLM judge reads the solver's code; and an objective within 1% of the stored optimal objective. We evaluate 12 GPT, Claude, and Gemini models running in coding-agent tools. Over up to ten attempts, we compare independent regeneration with reflection, which first diagnoses the failure. On the first attempt, two models solve every instance and seven solve more than 90%. Most Benders failures (48 of 62) are missing or suboptimal solutions. The most common column-generation failure is a method-audit rejection. Output checks alone would accept 93 of the 108 attempts that fail the method audit. The most common rejection, an optimalif, occurs 96 times, 92 of them in one model.Reflection turns 66% of retries into successes, compared with 39% for regeneration, and it repairs method-audit failures, for which the judge names the defecective gaps. Agents for decomposition therefore need checks on how a solver reaches its answer and feedback that locates the error. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/SIKAI-C/DecompGym.

title: Endpoint estimates for spherical maximal operators acting on radial functions in hyperbolic spaces
abstract: In this article we investigate spherical maximal operators $\mathfrak m^α$ of real order $α$ acting on radial functions in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$. We show that for every $n\geq 2$, $1<p\leq\infty$ and $α>(1-n)/2$, $\mathfrak m^α$ is bounded on $L^p_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$ if and only if \begin{align*} \begin{cases} α>1-n+\frac np, & 1<p\leq 2, α>\frac1p-\frac{n-1}2, & 2<p\leq\frac{2n}{n-1}, α\geq\frac{1-n}p, & p>\frac{2n}{n-1}. \end{cases} \end{align*} Moreover, we show that for $1<p\leq 2n/(n-1)$ and \begin{align*} α= \begin{cases} 1-n+\frac np, & 1<p\leq 2, \frac1p-\frac{n-1}2, & 2<p\leq\frac{2n}{n-1}, \end{cases} \end{align*} $\mathfrak m^α$ is bounded from $L^{p,1}_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$ to $L^{p,\infty}_{\mathrm{rad}}(\mathbb H^n)$.

title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.

title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
authors: with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley
abstract: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $Δ$, with $K_R+Δ$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $ψ$ in the algebra and even the image of $ψ$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $Δ$ for which $(X,Δ)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+Δ$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.

title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincaré duality.

title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.
comment: 186 pages; to appear in Acta Numerica

title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
