abstract: All traditional encryption schemes share a fundamental operational vulnerability: encrypted data must be decrypted before it can be used. Fully homomorphic encryption eliminates this vulnerability by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, but existing FHE schemes impose substantial practical constraints that limit deployment. This paper presents a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key FHE scheme. GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
abstract: This work proposes a hyper-reduced order model for coupled hydro-mechanical simulations of elastoplastic deformation and water flow in partially saturated soils. These simulations are used to monitor and assess the safety of geotechnical structures such as earthfill dams, where calibration, uncertainty quantification and scenario analysis require solving the same transient model many times for different parameter values. The displacement and the pore pressure are approximated in a field-split reduced basis obtained by proper orthogonal decomposition, and the Galerkin-projected equations are integrated with decomposed cubature rules, one per balance equation, built with the energy-conserving sampling and weighting (ECSW) method. Each residual is split into an affine part and a nonlinear correction: the affine part is computed exactly, at negligible online cost, so that the cubature rule only needs to approximate the correction, which is localized in space. The construction is independent of the constitutive model choices and is implemented in FEniCSx by assembling the original variational forms on the small set of elements selected by ECSW. The method is tested on two- and three-dimensional dams retaining tailings and water, simulating a raise of the dam and the subsequent consolidation phase, with the friction angle, stiffness and hydraulic conductivity of the dam material and the height of the raise as varying parameters. The hyper-reduced model reproduces the displacement and pressure fields with errors below $0.5\%$ with respect to the finite element solution, achieving speed-ups of up to $43\times$ in two dimensions and $77\times$ in three. These performance gains grow with the extent of the plastic yielding, and the selected elements concentrate in the plastified and unsaturated zones, whose size is set by the physics rather than by the mesh resolution.

title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
abstract: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
abstract: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
abstract: Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erdős and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$. In this paper, we prove a sparse canonical Rado theorem. For every irredundant partition-regular matrix $A$ of positive rank with $k\ge3$ columns, and every prescribed partition witnessing the columns condition, if $p\ge Cn^{-1/m(A)}$, then with probability at least $1-e^{-cnp}$ every colouring of $[n]_p$ contains $$Ω\big(p^k n^{k-\rank(A)}\big)$$ canonical solutions of $A\mathbf x=0$ with distinct coordinates. A matching 0-statement holds when the prescribed partition has one or at least three blocks; the Schur equation shows that it can fail for two-block patterns. For every prescribed partition, we also establish a robust threshold at the same scale under deletion of a fixed positive proportion of the random set.

title: Relative derived delooping levels and torsion intervals
abstract: Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq \text{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The heart $\mathcal H=\text{Fac} U\cap \mathcal{V}^\perp$ inherits the exact structure from mod$A$ and admits an Ext-progenerator $P$. Let $B=\text{End}_A(P)$. We define the relative derived delooping level on the exact heart $\mathcal H$ and compare it with the relative delooping level on $\mathcal {H}$ and the derived delooping level of $B$. We show that $\text{Findim} B^{op}$ is bounded by the relative derived delooping level on the $\mathcal H$. For a wide heart, the relative derived delooping level on the heart equals the derived delooping level of $B$. We obtain explicit bounds from representation-finite relative syzygy strata and characterize global first-order finiteness using an Ext-injective cogenerator.

title: On $π$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces
abstract: Let $π$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $π$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $π$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $π$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $π$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $π$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $π$-ideals and central $π$-nilpotency.

title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_α$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_α^k$ on $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<α\leq1$. We also show that, for every $α>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
abstract: We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership. We also identify a perverse coherent limiting heart in the opposite angular sector. The key ingredients are uniform HN-phase estimates for bounded families of pure sheaves, coefficient bounds for the coherent images of potential destabilizers, and a criterion forcing narrow exact sequences in the varying hearts to be bounded saturated coherent sequences.

title: On δ-derivations of \mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}
abstract: We study $δ$-derivations of the finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebra $\mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}=\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})\ltimes\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$, where $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ is the natural $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$-module. For $n>1$ and $δ\ne1$, we prove that every nonzero $δ$-derivation occurs at $δ=\frac12$ and is a scalar multiple of the identity. For $n=1$, we explicitly describe the four-dimensional space of $(-2)$-derivations.

title: Separation Theorems for Increasing Convex and Weak 3-Convex Orders on Real-Valued Random Variables
abstract: We examine separation theorems for the increasing convex (stop-loss) order and weak 3-convex order. We improve prior proofs for the increasing convex order by using integrated survival functions. We extend the separation theorem for weak 3-convex order from non-negative random variables to general real-valued random variables with finite second moments via a constructive approach based on higher-order integrated survival functions. A counterexample verifies that the $3$-convex order and $2$-convex order chain does not hold for the weak $3$-convex order. Our results enrich stochastic order theories for actuarial science and risk management.

title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes
abstract: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
abstract: We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter. Secondly, we study finite multitensor 2-categories, that is, finite linear 2-categories equipped with a monoidal structure for which every objects has duals. We extend several results about fusion 2-categories to our present setting. In particular, we investigate the properties of the 2-category of bimodules over a rigid algebra $\mathcal{A}$ in a finite tensor 2-category $\mathfrak{C}$. We show that, if $\mathfrak{C}$ has adjunctible projectives, then the 2-category of $\mathcal{A}$-$\mathcal{A}$-bimodules in $\mathfrak{C}$ is a finite multitensor 2-category. This construction provides many examples of finite tensor 2-categories. For instance, the Drinfeld center of a finite tensor 2-category with adjunctible projectives is a finite tensor 2-category.

title: RePAIR: Inverting Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Despite significant advances in computer vision, semantic segmentation models remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing a security risk. These attacks redirect pixels of a chosen victim class to an attacker-specified target class when a trigger is present, while preserving clean predictions. Existing defenses are largely derived from image classification, while dedicated segmentation defenses remain scarce and typically require retraining or model modification. We introduce RePAIR, a post-hoc, label-free, attack-unaware defense based on the observation that backdoor-induced shifts can be stronger in the classifier head than in internal representations, leaving recoverable victim-class semantics. RePAIR infers the victim-target relation from an unlabeled, potentially contaminated image pool, constructs a safety-approved semantic reference, and localizes suspicious pixels by comparing head predictions with internal semantic evidence. It then applies feature-space and output corrections toward the inferred victim semantics, while conservative localization and output constraints limit changes to benign predictions. We model the attack as adversarial probability transport and repair as its approximate reversal, deriving bounds and sufficient conditions for localization, residual attack success, clean-side changes, defense-induced target predictions, and attack-unaware pair identification. Experiments across segmentation architectures and attack settings show that RePAIR substantially reduces attack success while largely preserving clean performance.
comment: 26 pages total, 9 pages main paper, 2 figures

title: Extended stability timescales for the 2D3C rotating stratified Boussinesq equations
abstract: We study the time evolution of a vertical-slice model for incompressible inhomogeneous rotating fluids perturbed around a stably stratified rest state with linear buoyancy profile. For $\varepsilon$-small localized initial data with vanishing potential vorticity, we prove that solutions remain of size $O(\varepsilon)$ up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-\frac43}$, and up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ in a regime where the Brunt--Väisälä frequency and the Coriolis parameter are comparable. The first result relies on linear dispersion with amplitude decay rate $\langle t\rangle^{-\frac12}$, while the second exploits the absence of three-wave resonances via a normal form transformation. Our results remain valid for small nonzero initial potential vorticity, whose size is propagated by means of an intrinsic change of coordinates.

title: Resolving a Problem of Lv and Koolen on the Smallest Eigenvalue of Distance-Regular Graphs
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D\ge3$, and eigenvalues $k=θ_0>θ_1>\cdots>θ_D$. Put $b\coloneqq b_1/(θ_1+1)$, and let $1=u_0>u_1>\cdots>u_D$ be the standard sequence associated with $θ_1$. Lv and Koolen asked whether the negative of the smallest eigenvalue of a distance-regular graph can be bounded above in terms of its diameter $D$ and the parameter $b$ alone. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proving that $-θ_D\le\prod_{i=2}^D(1-u_i)/(u_1-u_i) <(b+1)^{D-1}$. Equality in the product bound holds if and only if $Γ$ is $Q$-polynomial with respect to the primitive idempotent corresponding to $θ_1$. For every integer $D\ge4$, we further establish the explicit bound $-θ_D\le b^{D-1}+b^{D-2} +\frac{27}{2}(D-2)b^{D-3}$ whenever $b\ge\max\{8,\sqrt{12(D-2)}\}$. Both leading coefficients are best possible for each fixed $D\ge4$. The proof uses a spectral product theorem of Micchelli and Willoughby applied to Schur multiplication in the Bose--Mesner algebra.

title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
abstract: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $ω$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.

title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
abstract: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.

title: Factorizations by column blocks and Schubert polynomials as products of key polynomials
abstract: We classify the Schubert polynomials that are products of key polynomials and explicitly determine their finest key factorization. Their indexing permutations are precisely those avoiding ten classical patterns of length six, which form the minimal pattern basis. More generally, the connected components of the column interaction graph give the unique finest factorization of a dual flagged Weyl character into nonconstant diagram characters. Every other such factorization is obtained by grouping these components. We also prove Makhija's conjecture on products of elementary symmetric polynomials in initial alphabets, allowing repeated alphabets. In this case, the elementary factors are uniquely determined, up to order, by the nonempty Rothe columns.

title: Dependent choice and iterated beta_n-model reflection
abstract: In this paper, we consider conservation results for iterated $β_n$-model reflection principles. Using these principles, we characterize the $Π^1_{m+2}$-, $Σ^1_{m+2}$- and $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$-consequences of $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{DC}_0$ and $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{TDC}_0$ for $m \leq n$. Here, $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$ denotes the set of Boolean combinations of $Π^1_{m+2}$-formulas, and $\mathsf{TDC}$ stands for transfinite $\mathsf{DC}$. We also show that, in each case, the stronger theory has a super-exponential speed-up over the corresponding conservative subtheory.

title: Robust global supply chain reconfiguration under tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
abstract: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to trade policy shocks and physical disruptions arising from common geopolitical events. We develop a robust optimization framework with two decision stages for strategic supply chain reconfiguration. Supplier qualification and transportation arc activation decisions are made before uncertainty is realized, while operational flows adapt afterward. Geopolitical uncertainty is represented through country level shocks that can jointly trigger tariff escalation, policy induced restrictions on cross border capacity, facility disruptions, and physical transportation failures. The resulting min max min problem is reformulated by dualizing the operational recourse problem, yielding a nonconvex mixed integer bilinear adversarial problem solved within a column and constraint generation procedure. Comparison with complete enumeration verifies the implementation on small instances, while experiments on 60 synthetic supply chain networks of varying sizes assess computational performance. The results show that omitting geopolitical transmission channels during strategic design can lead to substantial deterioration in cost and service under full geopolitical stress. Broader protection is achieved primarily through changes in transportation network configuration rather than increased supplier qualification. Robust performance also depends on the severity and composition of geopolitical consequences, with restrictions on cross border capacity exerting a stronger effect than comparable proportional changes in tariff severity over the tested ranges. A geographically grounded case analysis further shows that the value of individual uncertainty channels depends on network structure and geographic exposure.

title: Bethe Cycles, Frobenius Identities, and Quantum/Classical Duality
abstract: We study Frobenius action on the trigonometric Ruijsenaars--Schneider system associated with cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties. The construction continues the program initiated by Etingof and Varchenko and developed in quantum $K$-theory by the author and Smirnov. We explain how the monodromy eigenvectors recently constructed by Tarasov and Varchenko fit the quantum/classical duality between Bethe equations and tRS level sets. At a root of unity, all partial shifts cancel in the Newton--Adams combinations of the tRS Hamiltonians, leaving precisely the operators obtained by Frobenius action. This proves compatibility of the joint eigenvalue problem with Frobenius action in every rank and at every root order.

title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
abstract: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $Δ$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408Δ$.

title: Sharp global \(L^2\) estimates for oscillatory integral operators with quasi-homogeneous phases
abstract: For one-dimensional oscillatory integral operators with real-analytic phases, the seminal work of Phong and Stein established that the Newton polygon of the mixed Hessian of the phase determines the sharp local \(L^2\)-decay. The local theory relies on spatial localization near the origin and therefore does not capture the global geometry of the real zero set of the Hessian. For globally defined operators, unbounded real zero curves of the Hessian can make the global decay strictly slower than the local decay or destroy \(L^2\)-boundedness altogether. We establish a global analogue of the Phong--Stein theory for quasi-homogeneous polynomial phases. We introduce a family of Newton polygons adapted to the regions near and away from the real zero curves of the Hessian, together with the corresponding box-area scales. The relative geometry of these Newton polygons and area scales characterizes global \(L^2\)-boundedness and determines the sharp \(L^2\)-estimates in the high- and low-frequency regimes. As an application, we determine the exact range of anisotropic homogeneous \(L^2\)-Sobolev estimates for the associated global Radon transform.

title: Compact generation and perfect objects in homotopy categories of exact model structures
abstract: Compact generation allows large triangulated categories to be studied through suitably small objects. For homotopy categories arising from exact model structures, a natural question is how this intrinsic notion of smallness relates to finite presentation in the underlying exact category. In this paper, we investigate this relation for hereditary projective model structures generated by finitely presented Gorenstein projective objects. We establish compact generation and study the stronger requirement that every compact object admits a finitely presented cofibrant representative. We call objects with such representatives perfect. Under local coherence and the existence of enough projectives among the finitely presented objects, the finitely presented cofibrant objects form a Frobenius category whose stable category describes the perfect objects and whose idempotent completion recovers all compact objects. The relative $Q$-shaped setting, for suitable small categories $Q$, makes explicit how these finiteness properties depend on the choice of exact structure. The pure exact structure yields a compactly generated homotopy category, called the $Q$-shaped pure derived category. On the other hand, the split exact structure yields the $Q$-shaped homotopy category, which is compactly generated only in the pure semisimple case, analogously to the classical homotopy category of complexes. Finally, for acyclic $Q$ and for left artinian rings, we show that every compact object admits a strictly perfect representative. In particular, we establish that compact and perfect objects coincide, proving the conjecture of Holm and Jorgensen under these hypotheses.

title: Counting the Fixed Points of Binary Belief Propagation: Generic Degree, Syzygies, and Real Solutions
abstract: How many fixed points does belief propagation have on a binary pairwise model? Over complex parameters, the admissible equations of a finite loopless multigraph form an algebraic family whose generic degree we determine: it is a graph state sum over edge sets without vertices of degree one, each vertex of positive degree contributing one less than its degree. We give two geometric realizations of this state sum. The first is the total Betti number of a universal edge-incidence ring constructed without parameters. Its full graded Betti table is the state sum, its Tor algebra is natural for noncontracting graph maps, the alternating numerator recovers the graph polynomial of Watanabe and Fukumizu, and an Artin reduction by a regular sequence realizes the one-variable specialization, corrected for tree components. The second lies in the actual family: at the strong-field boundary each state factor is a ramification index, and at sufficiently strong field the state charts exhaust the admissible complex fiber. For fixed nonzero real couplings, every Eulerian message-sign sector contains a real fixed point at every external field, and strong fields attain this lower bound: one admissible real fixed point per element of the binary cycle space and one positive fixed point. For graphs of maximum degree at most three, this minimum equals the number of minimal module generators of the edge-incidence ring. One state decomposition connects the complex degree, graded syzygies, and an attained minimum real count. The degree, selected ring and resolution statements, and the real counts are formalized in Lean 4.
comment: 33 pages (main text and supplementary material SM1-SM6 in one PDF), 1 figure. Lean 4 formalization of the main results: https://github.com/ywatanabex/bp-degree-syzygies-lean

title: Characterization of Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
abstract: The aim of this paper is to obtain the characterization of Fourier transform for functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $H$, defined on the groups $G=\R^n,\,G=\Z/n\Z$. In the first part of the paper, we consider the Fourier transform as a bijective mapping on $S_H$, the space of all $H$-valued smooth rapidly decaying functions on $\R^n$, which naturally extends bijectively to the dual space $S_H'$. Within this framework, we characterize the Fourier transform in terms of the convolution theorem, supplemented by additional structural properties of the Fourier transform. In the second part of the paper, we consider the discrete setting, where the Fourier transform is an operator on $L^1(\Z/n\Z, H)$, and we provide corresponding characterization based on its essential properties. In contrast to the classical setting, a key assumption in our framework involves the interplay between two distinct convolution operations. As a consequence, the structure of our proof diverges notably from the classical case and introduces additional complexities.

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo methods for random nonlinear eigenvalue problems
abstract: We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) estimator to compute statistical quantities of interest of solutions to parameter-dependent nonlinear eigenvalue problems. The main difficulty for this problem is that parametrized eigenpairs often lack a globally well-defined parameter-to-solution map due to crossings and bifurcations. These phenomena render eigenvalue-tracking infeasible in multi-dimensional parameter domains. To overcome this issue, we propose both an Eulerian and a Lagrangian perspective on parameter-to-solution maps for nonlinear eigenvalue problems, which remain well-defined even in the presence of local crossings and bifurcations. Their implementation is based on a straightforward modification of Beyn's contour integral approach. Building on these maps, we propose an MLMC estimator that does not rely on matching eigenvalues or eigenvectors across samples or discretization levels. Nested approximation spaces and inter-level prolongation are only required when statistical quantities of interest related to the eigenspaces are of interest, but not for quantities of interest related to the eigenvalues. We demonstrate the feasibility and validity of our approach by numerical examples using a quasi-Monte Carlo method, including a nonlinear formulation of the Laplace Dirichlet eigenvalue problem on random domains in three dimensions motivated by the work of Steinbach and Unger. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work considering the approximation of statistical quantities of interest for random nonlinear eigenvalue problems.

title: A characterization of equality between de Branges--Rovnyak and Dirichlet spaces
abstract: We characterize when a de Branges--Rovnyak space coincides with a harmonically weighted Dirichlet space. We obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for this identification, which settles a long-standing open problem. We illustrate the result with several examples, that include measures supported on uncountable sets.

title: Homotopy operations on higher Lie algebras
abstract: We determine the multiplicative structures of the homotopy operations on derived Lie algebras, derived restricted Lie algebras and partition Lie algebras, as well as the relation between these. Under Koszul duality, this follows from a calculation of the homotopy operations on derived rings, p-truncated algebras and divided power algebras over $\mathbb{F}_p$.

title: Highest weight vectors in queer Howe duality
abstract: We use Gauss decomposition to study the singular vectors in the regular representation on the coordinate superalgebra of the big cell of the queer supergroup. This gives explicit bases for the highest weight spaces in queer Howe duality. As an application, the same method recovers the explicit highest weight vectors in the general linear case obtained by Cheng and Wang.

title: Acceleration of the Method of Alternating Projections on subspaces by GMRES
abstract: In this paper we propose a GMRES-accelerated version of the Method of Alternating Projections (MAP) for subspaces. It is proved that the accelerated version not only converges to a feasible solution, but also solves a best approximation problem. Comparisons are made with other accelerations proposed in the literature, for solving saddle point problems.

title: Emergence of large densities in a chemotaxis system with signal-dependent motility
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the emergence of large densities of a cell population in finite time in the following parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system with signal-dependent motility and a source term of logistic type \begin{equation} \begin{cases} u_{\varepsilon t} = Δ(e^{-v_\varepsilon}u_\varepsilon) + \varepsilon(κu_\varepsilon - μu_\varepsilon^2) ,\\ 0 =Δv_{\varepsilon}-v_\varepsilon+ u_{\varepsilon}. \end{cases} \end{equation} in a smooth bounded domain $Ω\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ with homogenuous Neumann boundary conditions and parameters $κ,μ>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. We will show that the solution $u_\varepsilon$ can exceed any certain value $M>0$ before a time $T(M)>0$ under the condition that $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small. To prove the result, we show convergence of classical solutions of the first system to classical solutions of the corresponding limit system as $\varepsilon\searrow 0$ \begin{equation} \begin{cases} u_t=Δ(e^{-v}u),\\ -Δv+v=u. \end{cases} \end{equation} The main challenge is to find suitable bounds for $u_\varepsilon$ and $v_\varepsilon$, that are $\varepsilon$-independent, in Lebesgue and Hölder spaces, whereas for fixed $\varepsilon>0$ global existence and boundedness is known.

title: From Walks to Skeletons: A Reusable Transport Architecture for Interactive Monte Carlo PDE Solvers
abstract: Walk-on-Spheres (WoS) enables mesh-free solutions of elliptic PDEs, but conventional methods repeatedly discard sampled trajectories, limiting their efficiency in interactive applications. We introduce reusable transport skeletons, a persistent representation that organizes stochastic walks into a shared computational graph. Our framework enables efficient reuse across spatial queries and boundary conditions, while supporting progressive refinement, structure-preserving compression, and local adaptation to dynamic geometry. It further enables interactive editing of transport between selected regions. Experiments demonstrate substantial computational savings while preserving solution accuracy. By transforming transient stochastic trajectories into reusable transport structures, our method provides a flexible foundation for interactive Monte Carlo PDE solving.

title: Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.

The manuscript did not disclose AI assistance with language editing, translation, typesetting, some mathematical derivations, or reference searches. The core ideas and original formulas are the human authors' work. Some derivations need independent verification; we therefore request withdrawal

title: A class of degenerate elliptic problems involving the Grushin operator: critical mass and ground states
abstract: We study the following degenerate elliptic equation with combined nonlinearities and prescribed mass \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \begin{cases} -Δ_γu+ωu+|u|^{p-2}u=|u|^{q-2}u \ \ \mbox{in }\mathbb{R}^{N}, \\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^{N}} |u|^{2} \mathrm{d}z=c, \end{cases} \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $Δ_γ$ is the Grushin operator and $ω\in\mathbb{R}$ appears as an unknown Lagrange multiplier. We characterize the critical mass threshold and the energy ground state solutions. Firstly, we prove the existence of optimizers for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality involving the Grushin operator together with estimates for the related best constant. Secondly, we characterize the critical mass by the best constant of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality and prove the existence of $x$-radial energy ground state solutions. Finally, we describe the relation between the $x$-radial action and energy ground state solutions, and the optimizers of Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. The strategy developed here is based on the interplay between the mass-preserving scaling and a sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. It therefore suggests possible extensions to other prescribed-mass problems with competing homogeneous terms and threshold-mass phenomena.

title: Dynamic Properties of Numerical Solution for Stochastic Epidemic Models with a Fully Implicit Form
abstract: This paper establishes a fully implicit model to investigate the spread of epidemics and studies its dynamic properties, extending the semi-implicit model in Yang et al.(Commun. Nonlinear Sci. Numer. Simul., 152 (2026) 109140 ). We first employ the split-step backward Euler method to address the non-adaptability arising from backward Euler discretization and ensure the global convergence of the numerical solution. By linearizing the model, the computational cost is reduced at the expense of a slight increase in error, effectively avoiding complex iterative solution processes. Then, we derive the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness of the numerical solution, and obtain its global convergence order. On this basis, the extinction and persistence of the disease are investigated under three different scenarios. The results indicate that environmental noise is a key factor leading to disease extinction. Finally, numerical simulations visually verify the obtained theoretical conclusions.

title: Exploring Neural Dynamics with Time Delays: A Numerical and Bifurcation Analysis Approach
abstract: The Wilson-Cowan model is a classic example of a ``neural mass model'' - a simplified yet powerful way to describe the activity of large networks of neurons. It is particularly interesting because, even in its relatively simple form, it can produce a surprising variety of behaviours, from steady rhythms to complex oscillations. A key factor influencing these dynamics is the presence of time delays, reflecting the time it takes for signals to travel between neurons. This article offers an accessible introduction to the Wilson-Cowan model, focusing on how these time delays affect its behaviour. We explore the core concepts behind the model, survey the existing literature, and introduce some numerical techniques specifically designed for analysing such delay differential equations. We also provide a practical, hands-on tutorial on using the DDE-BIFTOOL software package, demonstrating its application to the Wilson-Cowan model. Downloadable code allows the reader to reproduce our results and to explore the model's dynamics further, including MATLAB code for all computations, using DDE-BIFTOOL for the continuation, and Python versions of simulation codes.

title: On the Minimum Speed for a Fire Blocking Problem
abstract: We consider a dynamic blocking problem: a fire, starting on a bounded open set $R_0\subset\mathbb R^2$, propagates in the plane with unit speed in all directions. To block it, a barrier can be constructed in real time, at speed $λ>0$. A long standing conjecture by the first author states that the fire can be entirely surrounded by the barrier, in finite time, if and only if $λ>2$. The present paper improves on earlier lower bounds. Namely, if $λ\leq Λ=1.62621170228\ldots $ we show that the fire cannot be blocked. We also prove that, if $λ\leq 2$, the fire cannot be blocked by constructing a barrier which is a simple closed curve. More precisely, if the barrier does not contain purely delaying arcs, i.e.~arcs which are eventually surrounded by the fire on both sides, then for $λ<2$ the region burned by the fire at time $t>0$ has area $A(t)>(2-λ)t^2/4$.

title: The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube
abstract: Let $R_\infty(n)$ be the maximal Banach--Mazur distance from an $n$-dimensional real normed space to $\ell_\infty^n$. We prove that $R_\infty(n)\ge cn^{2/3}(\log(2n))^{-10}$. Together with the upper bound of Friedland, Naor, and Youssef, this gives $R_\infty(n) = n^{2/3+o(1)}$. The examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with $2n$ generators, and the lower bound holds with exponentially high probability. A joint minimization over coefficient representations and positive weights yields an exact second-variation identity and sparse coefficients. A Gaussian projection argument controls all low-rank completions of the recorded matrix. An adaptive choice of exceptional generators then reduces the remaining case to a fixed-shift Gaussian small-ball estimate over two finite nets.

title: Topology of rational equivalence closures and Lawson homology
abstract: Rational equivalence need not be closed in the Chow topology, and its closure can have infinitely generated homotopy groups. For a connected reduced complex projective variety, we prove that this closure is locally contractible and that its quotient in the algebraically trivial cycles is a finite or countable weak product of circles. The quotient map admits a global continuous section. Consequently, the higher homotopy of the cycle space is carried by the closure and is canonically identified with Lawson homology. We describe the remaining fundamental group quotient and its integral Walker comparison. Applications include smooth projective examples with infinite rank closure homotopy throughout prescribed finite intervals and a family of abelian threefolds with four simultaneously dense, nonconstructible quotient rank strata.

title: A characterization of equality in the edge-localized Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality
abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n\ge2$. Let $e(G)$ and $ω(G)$ denote its number of edges and clique number, respectively. Let $λ_1(G)\ge\cdots\geλ_n(G)$ be its adjacency eigenvalues. In 2007, Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G\neq K_n$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\left(1-\frac1{ω(G)}\right)e(G).$ This conjecture was recently completely resolved by Coutinho, Liu, Spier, Tang and Zhang. For every edge $e\in E(G)$, let $c_G(e)$ denote the maximum order of a clique containing $e$. Kannan, Kumar and Pragada proposed the edge-localized conjecture $λ_1^2(G)+λ_2^2(G)\le2\sum_{e\in E(G)}\left(1-\frac1{c_G(e)}\right)$ for every graph $G\neq K_n$. This conjecture was subsequently proved by Shaik. In this paper, we provide complete structural characterizations of the equality cases in both the Bollobás-Nikiforov inequality and its edge-localized version.

title: On finite covers of projective spaces, generic outside of codimension three
abstract: In the article, we generalize to an arbitrary dimension results obtained by the author and S.Yu. Nemirovski that related to Chisini's conjecture claimed that if $B$ is the discriminant of two generic covers $f_i:X_i\to \mathbb P^2$, $i=1,2$, and $\max (°f_1,°f_2) \geq 5$, then $f_1$ and $f_2$ are equivalent covers.

title: The Kothe Radical in Novikov Algebras
abstract: We study the Kothe radical (the upper nil radical) in the variety of Novikov algebras. We prove that the class of weakly right nilpotent Novikov algebras coincides with the class of r-nil algebras and forms a radical class. We establish that the Kothe radical is a hereditary radical in the variety of Novikov algebras. Furthermore, we obtain a structural description of the Kothe radical as the intersection of ideals whose corresponding quotient algebras are prime K-semisimple algebras. Finally, we construct an example of a prime r-nil Novikov algebra over a field of characteristic p>0, which implies that the Baer radical is strictly contained in the Kothe radical in this case.

title: The unilateral 2-linkage problem
abstract: We study a new variant of the classical linkage problem for digraphs, which we call {\bf unilateral linkages.} A digraph $D$ is {\bf unilaterally $\bm{k}$-linked} if it satisfies that for every choice of $2k$ distinct vertices $s_1,s_2,\ldots{},s_k,t_1,t_2,\ldots{},t_k$ there are vertex disjoint directed paths $P_1,\ldots{},P_k$ in $D$ such that $P_i$ is either an $(s_i,t_i)$-path or a $(t_i,s_i)$-path for each $i\in [k]$. This is a relaxation of the property of $D$ being $k$-linked, where we insist that each $P_i$ must go from $s_i$ to $t_i$. Clearly every $k$-linked digraph is also unilaterally $k$-linked. It is easy to see that the unilateral linkage problem is NP-complete for general digraphs and that it is trivial for semicomplete digraphs (digraphs with no pair of non-adjacent vertices). We show how Thomassen's construction of highly connected digraphs which are not 2-linked can be modified to show that there is no connectivity which guarantees that a digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. We show that every 4-strong split digraph and every 5-strong semicomplete multipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Both bounds are best possible. A digraph is {\bf co-bipartite} if its vertex set can be covered by two induced semicomplete digraphs. We prove that every 6-strong co-bipartite digraph is unilaterally 2-linked. Here we do not know whether the correct answer is 5. We also prove that every 16-strong digraph with independence number at most 2 is unilaterally 2-linked.

title: Geometric structures, orbit closures and invariant measures in moduli spaces
abstract: Building on the seminal work of Eskin, Mirzakhani and Mohammadi in the context of dynamics on moduli spaces, we introduce linear loci and linear measures to provide a relatively basic description of orbit closures and invariant measures in strata of translation surfaces. We use this to discuss geometrical properties of orbit closures and invariant measures from the perspective of geometric structures.

title: Rigidity of Exact Contractivity in the Complex Polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille Inequality
abstract: The complex polynomial Bohnenblust--Hille inequality bounds the coefficient $\ell_{2m/(m+1)}$ norm of a complex $m$-homogeneous polynomial by its supremum norm, with a constant independent of the number of variables. For each fixed integer $N\ge3$, we characterize the choices of $N$ degree-$m$ monomials for which the inequality holds with optimal constant $1$ for every polynomial supported on them, provided $m$ exceeds an explicit threshold depending only on $N$. This holds precisely when their exponent vectors contain no nontrivial three-term arithmetic progression; equality for a nonzero polynomial then holds only for monomials. We also prove that, in the same degree range, every polynomial with at most $N$ nonzero coefficients that violates the constant-one inequality has a unique coefficient of maximal modulus, whose exponent is the center of such a progression in its support. Exact contractivity also follows from a comparability condition on the two largest coefficients, with a degree threshold that necessarily depends on the number of nonzero monomials.

title: Large values of Hardy's Function from the Selberg class
abstract: Let $Z_F(t):=F(1/2+it) H(1/2+it)^{-1/2}$ denote Hardy's function, where the function $F(s)$ belongs to the Selberg class with polynomial Euler product and satisfies the functional equation $F(s)=H(s)\overline{F}(1-\bar{s})$. We prove that for every function of degree $1$ and for certain functions of degree $2$ belonging to the Selberg class, one has \begin{align*} \max_{T\leq t\leq 2T} \pm Z_F(t) &\gg \exp\left(C_F \sqrt{ \frac{\log T}{\log \log T} } \right), \end{align*} where the constant $C_F$ depends on $F(s)$ and are explicitly determined.

title: Maximum Energy of Integral Circulant Graphs with Same-Parity Exponents
abstract: The energy of a finite graph is the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. Let n be p to the power a times q to the power b, where p and q are distinct primes at least five and a and b, both positive integers, have the same parity. Among all nonempty sets D of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is maximised by exactly two divisor sets: the divisors p to the power i times q to the power j with i plus j odd, and the divisors with i plus j even after removing p to the power a times q to the power b. We also determine the exact maximum energy. For the proof, weighted prime-power Ramanujan transforms yield an exact tensor-product representation of the graph energy, reducing the extremal problem to a weighted cut separating two prescribed vertices. After a sign conjugation, the relevant transforms decompose into embedded path blocks; the nontrivial blocks correspond to a weighted path together with chords of length three of weight negative one. We prove a sharp lower bound for cuts separating the two prescribed vertices in Kronecker products of these path blocks. For products of two such nontrivial blocks, equality holds only for cuts that isolate one of the two prescribed vertices. Combined with the energy-to-cut correspondence, these equality cases yield exactly the two maximising divisor sets.

title: RoRo stowage planning: a systematic study of mathematical formulations
abstract: Stowage planning for Roll-On/Roll-Off (RoRo) vessels can be represented with different mathematical formulations for efficient stowage plans: hybrid-slot, grid-based, and lane-based representations. In this work, we implement and compare three formulations equally across a diverse set of instances. We extend these three representations to handle heterogeneous cargo in terms of size and weight, and to address advanced stability requirements, such as centre of gravity limits, stress force limits, and ballast-water adjustments. We evaluate the models in three configurations: cargo placement, simple stability with centres of gravity limits and ballast adjustments, and full stability, which adds shear-force and bending-moment limits. The tests are conducted on three different vessel sizes and solved with a mixed-integer programming solver. The hybrid-slot and grid-based models both perform well finding solutions for 447 out of 486 instances across all configurations; however, the hybrid-slot model placed 8% more cargo than the grid model. By contrast, the lane model only finds solutions for 142 instances and placed 15% less cargo than the grid-based model. The solutions generated by the hybrid-slot model are validated using a commercial vessel-stability software to verify our stability estimations, showing issues in only 24 of 162 instances, which are easily avoided by tightening the stability constraints. Finally, we address the placement of hazardous and refrigerated cargo in an efficient manner for the hybrid-slot model by employing lazy constraints which is shown to solve realistic sized instances.

title: Boundary Geometry Determines Optimal Shallow ReLU Approximation under Weighted Coefficient Constraints
abstract: We study how boundary geometry affects $L^q$ approximation by shallow ReLU neural networks on convex bodies $K\subset\mathbb R^d$. The target classes are unit balls of weighted variation spaces that can enlarge classical spaces by incorporating domain geometry into constraints on output coefficients. We establish upper and lower bounds for arbitrary convex bodies and determine the optimal polynomial approximation exponents for all planar convex bodies and their products with polytopes, including cubes and circular cylinders. For $C^2$ convex bodies, we determine the optimal exponents in a dimension-dependent range of $q$ extending beyond $2$. When all principal curvatures are positive, the result extends to every finite $q\ge2$. For these classes, the dependence of the optimal exponent on the domain is captured by a single geometric growth exponent associated with small boundary caps. We also identify sharp weight thresholds for retaining the classical approximation exponent and improve previous weights on Euclidean balls while preserving the classical $L^2$ approximation rate. When the target is given as a finite ReLU network, the upper bounds can be realized by a compressed network using only the original neurons, without increasing the weighted coefficient sum. These results show that boundary geometry can change the optimal exponent even when dimension, error norm, and weighting rule are fixed.

title: Principal profiles, characteristic communication and critical asymptotics for cooperative nonlocal systems on the circle
abstract: We study cooperative nonlocal transport on a circle with species-dependent constant velocities and arbitrary $L^1$ probability kernels. For periodic coefficients, the period map is a compact perturbation of the no-jump map. We construct separate receiving and sending characteristic scans: under a two-tree condition based at one active component, a positive Floquet profile exists exactly when the full period map has strictly larger spectral radius than its no-jump part. The other jump rates may vanish. The scans provide an integral minorant and positive jump return; a separate coefficient inequality verifies the spectral gap. Smooth locking examples distinguish communication from frozen-time mixing, while a resonant example separates positive return from spectral separation. Autonomous nonzero velocities and union-graph connectivity yield a simple principal pair; one active component suffices for exponential mixing. We also prove local perturbation results. For quadratic self-regulation, the same principal projection gives a transverse response whose averaged cubic coefficient is a nonnegative asymptotic variance. It determines both the critical $t^{-2}\log t$ correction and the second-order period-averaged amplitude of the positive branch.

title: A minimising principle for interval covers of zigzag persistence modules
abstract: Zigzag persistence modules serve as an essential tool in topological data analysis. The fundamental theorem of persistent homology states that any zigzag persistence module decomposes into a direct sum of simple building blocks called interval modules. We consider an interval cover, a possibly redundant family of interval submodules spanning every vertex space of a finite zigzag persistence module. We give an elementary descent argument that replaces a redundant cover with a minimal one that is an interval decomposition. This provides an optimisation perspective on persistence modules and their interval decomposition. As an application, we give an estimate of the generalised rank invariant in terms of a cover.

title: The numerical range of limits of real rational functions
abstract: Given two nonzero polynomials $f, g \in \mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ vanishing at the origin $0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$, we study the numerical range of the limit $$ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{f(x)}{g(x)}, $$ denoted by $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$, which is defined as the set of all possible limits of the rational function $\displaystyle\frac{f}{g}$ as $x$ tends to $0$. When $n = 2$ and $g$ has a non-isolated zero at $0$, we describe all possible forms of $\mathcal{R}_{f,g}$ and provide an effective algorithm to compute this set based on Puiseux expansions. This is a follow-up to our recent results~\cite{Dinh2025}, in which we only considered the case when $0$ is an isolated zero of $g$.

title: Pontrjagin Classes of Locally Spherically Symmetric Projectively Affine Sprays
abstract: By Chern--Weil theory, rational Pontrjagin classes are represented by curvature forms. Sprays, which require no metric and include all Finsler and Riemannian geodesic sprays, provide a natural setting for the vanishing problem. Shen and Zhao proved that if a manifold admits a locally projectively flat spray, then all of its rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. We ask whether this rigidity persists for the wider class of projectively affine sprays. We prove that if a smooth manifold admits a locally spherically symmetric projectively affine spray, then all rational Pontrjagin classes vanish. Stronger, the Pontrjagin forms of the associated Berwald spray vanish identically as differential forms, a genuine geometric rigidity. Hence a manifold with nonzero rational Pontrjagin class cannot carry such a spray; in particular, it admits no Riemannian metric whose geodesic spray is locally spherically symmetric. We also construct non-Berwald, non-projectively-flat examples with identically vanishing Pontrjagin forms, showing the phenomenon is not a byproduct of projective flatness.

title: An inverse moving point source problem in inhomogeneous acoustic media: uniqueness, stability and reconstruction
abstract: This paper is concerned with the simultaneous recovery of the trajectory and intensity of an unknown moving point source in an inhomogeneous acoustic medium. We prove that the whole-boundary measurements over a finite time interval uniquely determine the moving source. Furthermore, under suitable propagation and rank assumptions, Lipschitz stability of determining both the trajectory and intensity is derived using waveforms measured at four fixed receivers outside the source region. A novel Volterra--Euler reconstruction scheme is developed for solving the inverse problem, and the error estimate is derived for the proposed scheme. Numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed numerical method.

title: Spherical Averages on nilpotent Groups
abstract: In this paper, we study the spherical maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_{S^{d-1}(A)}$, which is associated with the sphere $S^{d-1}$ embedded in the horizontal plane of some nilpotent group $\mathbb{G}_A$. Here, $\mathbb{G}_A$ is the group identified with $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, and its group law is determined by the $d\times d$ real matrix $A$. Specifically, when $A$ is a skew-symmetric matrix $J$, which is the case of the Heisenberg group, it was known that the spherical maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_{S^{d-1}(J)}$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{G}_J)$ for $p$ in the range $(\frac{d}{d-1},\infty]$. In this paper, we extend the results from the skew-symmetric matrix $J$ to a more general class of invertible matrices $A$. We aim to classify the range of $p$ for which the operator $\mathcal{M}_{S^{d-1}(A)}$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{G}_A)$ based on the eigenvalues of $A$.
journal_ref: Studia Math (2025) 282(1) 25-26 Published at Studia Math 282(1) 25-67 2025

title: The Edge Geodesic Transversal Problem
abstract: For a given connected graph $G(V,E)$, the geodesic transversal problem finds a set $S$ of vertices of $G$ with minimum cardinality such that every maximal geodesic of $G$ contains at least one vertex of $S$. The cardinality of such a smallest set $S$ is called the gt-number of $G$ and is denoted as $gt(G)$. In this paper, we introduce the \textit{Edge geodesic transversal problem} as the edge-based extension of the geodesic transversal problem. The problem of determining a set $S\subseteq E(G)$ with minimum number of elements such that every maximal geodesic $P$ in $G$ traverses at least one edge of $S$ is called the edge geodesic transversal problem, and the cardinality of such a set is called the edge geodesic transversal number or the $gt_e$-number of $G$, denoted as $gt_e(G)$. Further, we investigate the effect of an edge cut of a graph on the edge geodesic transversal problem and prove a novel result called the edge cut transversal theorem which is used in the computation of edge geodesic transversal number of hypercube, stacked prism and ladder graph.

title: Dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations
abstract: This paper is concerned with the dissipative weak solutions to the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations. For any $γ\in \left[ {0,\frac{1}{5}} \right)$, we establish the existence of $γ$-Hölder continuous weak solutions that exhibit a strict energy dissipation in expectation. For any $γ> \frac{1}{3}$, we prove that the three-dimensional stochastic Euler equations do not possess dissipative solutions satisfying the corresponding spatial $γ$-Hölder regularity. It is well known that the stochastic forcing inevitably gives rise to additional stochastic effects to the Reynolds stresses, which cannot be treated by the differential estimates in the classical convex integration scheme introduced by Buckmaster, De Lellis, Isett and Székelyhidi (Ann. Math., 182(1):127--172, 2015). To address this difficulty, we develop a novel material integration technique into the stochastic convex integration scheme, so that those stochastic Reynolds stresses are quantified.

title: Large deviations from a stable steady state for damped dispersive PDEs with vanishing random kicks
abstract: We study the behaviour of stationary measures for a class of dispersive PDEs damped by a linear zero-order term and perturbed by a small kick noise. Under some natural assumptions on the law of the noise, we prove that any family of stationary measures satisfies the large deviation principle in the vanishing noise limit. The result highlights the role of nonlinear smoothing and applies to the nonlinear Schrödinger and Korteweg-de Vries equations, and to a variety of random perturbations including Gaussian and exponential variables.

title: Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks theorems and dual geodesic symmetries on statistical manifolds
abstract: We establish Cartan-Ambrose-Hicks (CAH) theorems for statistical manifolds and characterize statistical symmetric spaces by dual geodesic symmetries. These theorems determine statistical structures up to local statisticmorphism by comparing the curvature of an alpha-connection and the skewness tensor using radial geodesics and parallel displacement of that connection. The Levi-Civita formulation characterizes local statisticmorphisms by comparing the radial Jacobi operators of Riemannian curvature and the skewness tensor using Levi-Civita parallel displacement. The same characterization holds with statistical curvature in place of Riemannian curvature. For Hessian manifolds, comparison of the skewness tensor alone is necessary and sufficient. For connected statistical manifolds, we prove the equivalence between the homogeneous definition of statistical symmetric spaces and the existence of global dual geodesic symmetries at every point. The CAH theorems give the necessary and sufficient conditions for maps constructed from exponential maps of dual connections to be local dual geodesic symmetries, preserving the metric and interchanging the dual connections. Such local symmetries exist at every point if and only if the Riemannian curvature and skewness tensors are Levi-Civita parallel. For Hessian manifolds, this condition is equivalent to the equality of the Hessian and dual Hessian curvature tensors.

title: Decompositions of birational toric morphism between threefolds
abstract: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a birational morphism between smooth projective threefolds, Kollár asked that if $f$ could be decomposed into smooth blow-downs and smooth flops. In this paper we show that the toric version is true.

title: Density and Defect Distribution of Reduced Ideals Missed by the Reduction Algorithm in Real Quadratic Fields
abstract: Schoof asked how many reduced Arakelov divisors cannot arise from the reduction algorithm. Tian and Tran subsequently characterized the image of this algorithm in real quadratic fields as precisely the $1$-reduced ideals. We give a quantitative answer to Schoof's question in the real-quadratic setting by determining the asymptotic proportion of reduced ideals missed by the algorithm. A key arithmetic input is the criterion that a reduced ideal with associated reduced form $(A,b,-r)$ fails to be $1$-reduced if and only if $A-r<b<2(A-r)$. Hence the missed ideals occupy an explicit region of the natural extension of the Gauss map whose relative measure is $λ_{\mathrm{ex}}=\frac{\log(4/3)}{\log4}$. In particular, the missed region occupies exactly half of the digit-one cylinder with respect to the invariant measure. We establish this limiting proportion in two settings. A lattice-point count gives the average asymptotic over fundamental discriminants $Δ\le X$, with error $O(X^{-1/4+\varepsilon})$. For individual real quadratic fields, Duke's equidistribution theorem yields $\operatorname{ECal}(Δ)/κ(Δ) \toλ_{\mathrm{ex}}$ as $Δ\to\infty$. We also determine the limiting distribution of the canonical defect $k/\sqrtΔ$ of the missed ideals. This distribution is supported on $[0,1/\sqrt3-1/2]$, and its lower tail is asymptotic to $\frac{2}{\log(4/3)}t\log(1/t)$ as $t\to0^+$. An exact relation between the integer defect and an endpoint coordinate of the natural extension allows us to transfer equidistribution to the defect law.

title: Laws of the iterated logarithm for the range of once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$
abstract: In this paper, we study once-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$, and prove sharp Chung-type and Hartman-Wintner laws of the iterated logarithm for the range. Let $R_n$ denote the range at time $n$ and let $c>0$ be the reinforcement parameter. Then, almost surely, \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n}{\sqrt{n/\log\log n}}=\fracπ{\sqrt{2}}, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{cR_n}{\sqrt{2n\log\log n}}=1. \end{equation*} The proofs are based on the independent increment decomposition of the inverse range and sharp generating function estimates.

title: Existence of a third self-similar solution of the Yang--Mills equation in high odd dimensions
abstract: In a recent paper~\cite{BGW}, Bizoń, Glogić, and Wasserman (BGW) reduced the classification of smooth self-similar Yang--Mills profiles in odd spatial dimensions $d\ge11$ to an algebraic problem of counting roots of an explicit polynomial in a prescribed interval. Two roots correspond to explicit profiles. BGW conjectured that there is exactly one additional root and verified this in a range of odd dimensions. Here, we prove the existence of an additional root, and hence of a third smooth self-similar profile, in every odd dimension $d\geq11$. The proof combines an endpoint sign calculation for the resonance polynomial with an algebraic argument showing that the third root is distinct from the two explicit ones. Uniqueness remains open in general.

title: Verifying Control Invariance of H-Polytopes is coNP-Complete
abstract: We prove that verifying whether an H-polytope is control invariant for a discrete-time linear system with polytopic input constraints is \textsc{coNP}-complete. This establishes a fundamental computational complexity barrier for set-theoretic control. As an immediate consequence, the exact computation of maximal control invariant subsets of H-polytopes is \textsc{coNP}-hard. These hardness results hold regardless of whether the input constraint set is given in H- or V-representation.

title: A Bounded Closed Convex Set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ without Modulus Support Functionals
abstract: We construct a bounded closed convex set in $c_0(\mathbb{C})$ on which no nonzero continuous complex-linear functional attains its maximum modulus. Consequently, this answers in the negative the two longstanding questions raised by Deville, Godefroy and Zizler in \cite[p. 35]{DGZ}. The construction uses a small perturbation of the identity on $c_0(\mathbb{R})$.

title: On surfaces, that fill the space
abstract: The article is devoted to the construction of dimension-raising maps of cubes with the highest possible Holder exponent. In particular, a square-to-cube mapping with a Holder exponent of $2/3$ is constructed, which is a solution to the V.I.Arnold problem.

title: Brownian covariances on an interval: a complete endpoint classification
abstract: Brownian motion and the Brownian bridge have covariance kernels that are Green's functions of the negative second derivative on the unit interval, with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. We characterize the Green's functions of all strictly positive real self-adjoint realizations of this operator. The kernels are in one-to-one correspondence with positive-semidefinite $2\times2$ endpoint covariance matrices. We call the associated centered Gaussian processes Brownian processes. Each is a standard Brownian bridge plus the affine interpolation of an independent Gaussian endpoint vector. Singular endpoint covariance matrices give hard endpoint constraints, such as the pinned start $X(0)=0$ of Brownian motion. This parametrization gives explicit operator domains and energy spaces. On every mesh it gives an exact sparse precision matrix, so the likelihood of $n$ observations can be evaluated in $O(n)$ operations. Nonnegative realizations with a null space are treated separately through orthogonally normalized pseudoinverses, which are proper Gaussian covariances.

title: Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
abstract: High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.

title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
abstract: We propose a minimizing-movement framework for constructing parametric finite element methods (PFEMs) for anisotropic curve shortening flows. The cornerstone is an admissible modified energy: a smooth, convex, and iteration-dependent surrogate that majorizes the original anisotropic energy and agrees with it at the current iterate. For any fixed finite element degree $n\geq1$ and any positive surface energy density $γ\in C^2(\mathbb{S}^1)$, the unconstrained one-step problem has a unique solution for any time-step size whenever the parametric derivative of the current discrete curve does not vanish on any mesh element. It also satisfies a one-step discrete energy dissipation inequality. It therefore preserves the variational structure of the underlying $L^2$-gradient flow. The framework recovers a variational interpretation of Dziuk's isotropic scheme and applies directly to the weak anisotropies. For strong anisotropies, a convex splitting removes the weak-anisotropy restriction on the original density. A scalar constraint further extends the framework to area-preserving flows. Numerical experiments exhibit approximately the expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic examples. They also confirm energy dissipation and area preservation. In the strongly anisotropic regime, the computations produce sharp facet-like profiles but reveal mesh-scale oscillations under the grid refinement.

title: Negative edge correlation in complete bipartite graphs
abstract: We prove strict pairwise negative correlation under both the uniform forest measure and the uniform connected-subgraph measure on the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$ for all $m,n\geq2$. Under the connected-subgraph measure, any two distinct edges of a fixed copy of $K_{2,2}$ remain strictly negatively correlated after conditioning on the subgraph induced by the remaining vertices.

title: ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
abstract: Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.

title: When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure
abstract: Token systems support repeated service exchange without monetary transfers, but their viability depends on the stability of token balances. We study token systems with compatibility constraints among agents. A requester is randomly sampled in each period, and only a few randomly sampled agents are available to provide service. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and show that the minimum-token rule, which selects the available provider with the lowest token balance, achieves the optimal stability region. We then apply this stability criterion to a random token system generated from stochastic block models with uniformly sampled requesters. We tightly characterize the stability regime by identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.

title: The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends
abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
comment: 26 pages, 7 figures. Interactive 3D models: https://surfaces.igorkozyrev.com/#costa . The scripts for the numerical experiments are attached as ancillary files (anc/scripts)

title: Different approach to certain problems in univalent function theory
abstract: Using different approach we consider some problems for the class $\mathcal{S}_{ex}^{\star}$ defined by the condition $\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\prec e^{αz}$, $0<α\leq1.$ Our method is more simple than that used by Das and Sarkar in their work: \textit{Sharp coefficient estimates for the exponential starlike class $S^\star_{ex}$} (\cite{DS26}).

title: The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture
abstract: Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $δ_i(g)=X_i$ and $δ^α(g)=(\partial^αh^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $δ^α(g)=0$ for $|α|=(°h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $δ^α(g)(x_0)/α!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.

title: Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure
abstract: This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials.
