Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We describe a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

title: Learning on-the-fly quasi-stationarity diagnostics from low-dimensional surrogates
abstract: Accelerated dynamics methods, such as parallel replica dynamics, require estimates of the decorrelation time, after which a process trapped in one of its metastable states is distributed according to the quasi-stationary distribution (QSD). In a method proposed by Binder, Lelièvre and Simpson, decorrelation times are defined by coupling a particle approximation of the non-linear conditioned probability flow of the process with MCMC-inspired diagnostics. We explore an alternative to MCMC diagnostics, based on coarse-graining of non-linear probability flows and simulation-based inference. We first develop a coarse-graining framework for killed Markov jump processes conditioned on survival, proving uniform-in-time, non-asymptotic estimates approximating the non-linear probability flow of the true process by the non-linear flow of a surrogate process, defined with a collective variable. The framework does not assume reversibility of the true process, and also gives bounds which scale explicitly in an adiabatic regime. Motivated by these results, we then construct a quasi-stationarity diagnostic using simulation-based inference: a recurrent neural network (RNN), trained on particle approximations of non-linear effective flows, estimates posterior probabilities of decorrelation. The learned diagnostic is then transferred to collective-variable traces of high-dimensional particle approximations. We investigate the behavior and robustness of this diagnostic on a set of numerical experiments, comparing it to the MCMC diagnostic of Binder et al.\ on both synthetic examples and a molecular system, in and out of its training prior distribution. When its prior assumptions hold, the RNN diagnostic outperforms the MCMC diagnostic in ROC analysis, is less conservative, fails less often, and has an interpretable decision threshold.

title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

title: AlgebrasTQD: Computing Algebras and Interfaces in Twisted Quantum Doubles
abstract: We present AlgebrasTQD, an open-source code written in GAP (Groups, Algorithms, and Programming), for computing condensable algebras and the corresponding topological boundaries and interfaces of twisted quantum doubles $D^ω(G)$. These algebras can be used to classify 1+1d gapped and gapless phases whose symmetry is related by gauging to a finite group $G$ with anomaly $ω\in H^3(G,U(1))$, to study 2+1d anyon proliferation and to construct logical gates in non-Abelian topological quantum codes. The functions in AlgebrasTQD compute all condensable algebras $A(H,F,γ,ε)$ with their algebra structure and anyons, sort them into isomorphism classes and identify the twin algebras that are inequivalent but share the same anyon decomposition. AlgebrasTQD also determines all the subalgebra relations, the corresponding Hasse diagram and the types of 1+1d phases for any chosen, possibly non-invertible, group-theoretical symmetry. For non-maximal algebras, the code computes the reduced topological order with its $3$-cocycle and the map of anyons across the topological interface. Finally, AlgebrasTQD includes functions that construct certain non-Clifford logical gates via non-Abelian surface codes. We summarize the formulas that are implemented in the AlgebrasTQD code, and we illustrate its use with Abelian and non-Abelian groups including $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ with $ω_\text{III}$, $D_8$, $A_4$ with and without anomaly, twin algebras and twin phases, and the Clifford-hierarchy gates in quantum doubles of dihedral groups. All arithmetic is exact and AlgebrasTQD can be used with any finite group $G$ and 3-cocycle $ω$, limited only by the time and size of the calculation. The code is available at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD
comment: 38 pages, companion paper to the code at https://github.com/AlisonWarman/AlgebrasTQD

title: Quantum dynamics on the sparse Erdős-Rényi graph
abstract: We analyse the large-time asymptotics of the Schrödinger time evolution of a free quantum particle on the Erdős-Rényi graph $\mathbb{G}(N,d/N)$, where the quantum Hamiltonian is given by the adjacency matrix of $\mathbb{G}$. Starting from a state localized at a vertex, the wave function is approximately radial, and we characterize precisely its asymptotic form. Our results in particular cover vertices whose degree is close to $2d$, hence probing the emergence of bound states from a dynamical perspective. This provides a dynamical counterpart of the coexistence of localized and delocalized states established in [arXiv:1905.03243,arXiv:2005.14180,arXiv:2106.12519,arXiv:2109.03227,arXiv:2305.16294], with the former giving rise to a localized mode and the latter to a dispersive wave. Our results hold in the regime $\sqrt{\log N} \ll d \ll N^{o(1)}$, which is the full region in which such dynamical phenomena may exist, and for times $1 \ll t \ll T_N$ for some explicit $T_N \gg 1$.

title: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
abstract: For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant \[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\] where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories with adjoints
abstract: We demonstrate that higher categories with adjoints behave like homotopy types. By the homotopy hypothesis, homotopy types can be regarded as higher categories in which all cells are invertible. We show that replacing invertibility by the existence of higher adjoints still supports a homotopy theory that is at least as rich as classical homotopy theory. The basic invariants of this theory are the homotopy monoidal categories \[ Π_n(X,x)=\operatorname{Ho}\bigl(Ω^n(X,x)\bigr) \] associated to a based $(\infty,\infty)$-category with adjoints $(X,x)$. These invariants are monoidal categories with duals and replace iterated loops with iterated endomorphisms. The classical homotopy groups of the classifying space are recovered as the isomorphism classes of objects in the groupoid completion. We prove a Whitehead theorem for homotopy monoidal categories and show that fibrations of higher categories give rise to long oriented exact sequences of homotopy monoidal categories. To develop homological algebra of higher categories with adjoints, we prove an equivalence between skeletal sequences of categorical spectra with adjoints and categorical chain complexes, extending a result outlined by Lurie in the proof of the cobordism hypothesis.

title: Optimal tradeoffs between variance and sensitivity, via Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry
abstract: While the goal of classical statistical theory is to minimize the variance of unbiased estimators, an additional goal of some recent research is to minimize or constrain other notions of the instability of estimators. In particular, a subset of the authors recently introduced a notion of instability termed "sensitivity", which represents the expected amount that an estimator would change if its inputs were infinitesimally perturbed. In this work, we study the multiobjective problem of minimizing both the variance and sensitivity over unbiased estimators in a given statistical model, and we aim to determine Pareto optimal tradeoffs between these two objectives. Our main results show that the Pareto front for these tradeoffs is precisely determined by endowing the statistical model with the Hellinger-Kantorovich geometry, which interpolates between the Hellinger and Wasserstein geometries that are known to be associated, respectively, with the separate minimization of variance and sensitivity. We also develop a $Z$-estimation technique which constructs estimators that asymptotically achieve Pareto optimal pairs of variance and sensitivity. While computing the Pareto front and constructing the resulting estimators in practice requires solving a continuum of partial differential equations, we fully execute this program in some parametric examples of interest where the analysis is already non-trivial. Our results also shed light on some classical statistical problems, for example by showing that the maximum likelihood estimator achieves the smallest asymptotic sensitivity among all estimators achieving the optimal asymptotic variance.

title: Infranormal Kazhdan subgroups and instability in finite actions
abstract: We prove that the group $G=\mathbb{Z}[1/2]^3\rtimes(\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})\times\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely presented and residually finite, but is not stable in finite actions, answering a question of Gohla and Thom. The proof uses the infranormal Kazhdan subgroup $H=\mathbb{Z}^3\rtimes\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and its normal closure $N$ in $G$. A Kazhdan projection estimate shows that, in any $G$-action weakly contained in finite actions, every $H$-invariant measurable subset is also $N$-invariant. We construct an explicit sofic approximation of $G$ whose limit action contains a measurable subset that is $H$-invariant but not $N$-invariant.

title: $C^{1,α}$ and $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ regularity for the $2$-Hessian equation
abstract: In this paper, for every $\varepsilon>0$, we establish interior and global a priori $C^{1,α}$ estimates for some $α\in(0,1)$ from $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ bounds for bounded smooth $2$-admissible solutions of the $2$-Hessian equation, with the interior estimate requiring only an upper bound on the density. Under positive upper and lower density bounds, we prove global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimates for some $\varepsilon>0$ on bounded strictly mean convex $C^{2,β}$ domains with $C^{2,β}$ boundary values. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, the interior $C^{1,α}$ estimate follows by combining the first result with an interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate obtained by a slight modification of an existing argument. Combining the first result with the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate yields the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate. Known examples show that the $C^{2,β}$ regularity assumptions on the boundary and boundary values are optimal in the Hölder scale for both the global $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ estimate and the global $C^{1,α}$ estimate.

title: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
abstract: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.

title: Attainable forms of intermediate dimensions of complementary sets
abstract: Given a positive, non-increasing sequence $a$ with sum $1$, we consider the family $\mathcal{C}_a$ of closed subsets of $[0,1]$ whose complementary open intervals have lengths given by the terms of $a$. We study which functions $θ\mapsto\overline{\dim}_{\,θ}E$ arise as the upper intermediate dimensions of sets $E\in\mathcal{C}_a$. Under a natural condition on the decay of $a$, we show that these are exactly the functions in the class introduced by Banaji and Rutar that take the value $\overline{\dim}_{\rm B}C_a$ at $θ=1$ and are bounded above by the upper intermediate dimensions of the decreasing Cantor set $C_a$. We also show that the lower bound given by the countable set $D_a$ is rigid: if it is attained at one value of $θ$, then it is attained at all larger values.

title: Improved lattice-packing bounds in small dimensions
abstract: We strengthen the upper bound on the density of a lattice packing in small dimensions. A lattice cannot have too many short vectors; we modify the Cohn--Elkies linear program accordingly by allowing the auxiliary function to be positive on a short interval beyond the minimum distance. For $11 \leq n \leq 16$, our bound is tighter than the three-point bound of Cohn, de Laat and Salmon. For $n \in [17, 23] \cup [25, 40] \cup [43, 57] \cup [62, 75]\cup [83, 91]$, our bound lies below the published numerical values of the Cohn--Elkies bound.
comment: links to a GitHub repository with relevant numerical data

title: Hidden Singularity and Fractal Dimensions for Extended Harper Operators
abstract: We prove that, for every irrational frequency, the spectra of the extended Harper family throughout the zero-measure regime have finite $1/2$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and lower box dimension at most $1/2$. Both numbers improve to $1/3$ on the isotropic critical boundary. The proof is based on a family of unitary transformations, that specializes to the chiral transform of [BJK] for the case of the critical almost Mathieu. This family allows to make every operator in this regime spectrally equivalent to a singular Jacobi operator. Using these singular representatives, we apply the method of [BJK] to construct covers by $O(q_n)$ intervals of total length $O(q_n^{-1})$, improving to $O(q_n^{-2})$ on the isotropic boundary, where $q_n$ is the denominator of a canonical approximant to $α$. The covers give upper box bounds and, with packing estimates, examples where the box-counting dimension fails to exist.

title: Recertifying decisions via e-closure: uniform improvements of conformal risk control and randomized e-BH
abstract: Statistical procedures often control expected loss at a prescribed level while leaving part of their risk budget unused. Building on the e-value representation of risk-controlled decisions and the e-closure principle for multiple testing, we formulate recertification, a general paradigm for improving procedures by exploiting computable slack in their validity certificates. A valid procedure's losses normalized by their risk budgets form a state-indexed e-value collection; conversely, decisions whose normalized losses are bounded by this collection inherit its risk guarantees. Recertification uses distributional structure to quantify slack, enlarge the certifying e-values while preserving validity, and construct less conservative decisions. We develop two applications. For conformal risk control (CRC) with a known loss family, recertification redistributes unused risk budget among the held-out points of each hypothetical augmented sample. The resulting controller is valid under every finite exchangeable law and no more conservative than CRC on any calibration sample. For convex losses on an interval of actions, repeated recertification converges geometrically to an admissible controller. For false discovery rate control with arbitrarily dependent e-values, recertification exploits unused conditional budgets in randomized e-BH. It yields a closed-form randomized procedure whose rejection set contains that of randomized e-BH for every realization of the shared randomization and whose expected number of rejections is maximal subject to the same conditional budget constraints. Recertifying with the larger e-collection of closed e-BH gives a second closed-form procedure whose rejection set contains that of the first. Experiments on CIFAR-100 hierarchical classification and multiple testing simulations demonstrate improved budget utilization, informativeness and power over the baselines.

title: Morse index characterization of the Veronese projective plane
abstract: Following Simons' seminal work in 1968, every closed, connected, embedded minimal surface in the four-sphere that is not totally geodesic has Morse index at least five. In this paper, we prove that equality holds if and only if the surface is congruent to the Veronese projective plane. Relying on recent advances by Bernstein and Ketover, this characterization settles Kusner's 1996 conjecture on the minimizers of the Willmore functional in dimension four for surfaces whose normal bundle has nonzero Euler number. This is always the case, in particular, for embeddings of nonorientable surfaces whose orientation double cover has even genus.

title: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ for even $n$: rigid sequences, products, and growth beyond Harborth's bound
abstract: Let $s(C_n^r)$ be the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant of $C_n^r$ and $η(C_n^r)$ the short zero-sum constant. For even $n$, Harborth's construction gives $s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+1$, with equality when $n$ is a power of two. Wang and Zeng recently showed that this bound is strict for every $r\ge4$ and every even $n$ that is not a power of two, with an excess of $2^{r-3}(m-1)$, where $m$ is the odd part of $n$; this disproves Properties C and D. We show that the excess grows faster than $2^r$. For every even $n=2^am$ with odd $m\ge3$ and every $r\ge4$, \[ s(C_n^r)\ge2^r(n-1)+(m-1)\,2^{r-3}\lfloor r/4\rfloor+1 , \] so that $s(C_n^r)-2^r(n-1)\ge c_n\,r\,2^r$.

title: Properly embedded Legendrian surfaces in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic space
abstract: We show that every open Riemann surface may be conformally properly embedded in the tangent sphere bundle of hyperbolic $3$-space as a Legendrian surface. We achieve this by constructing proper holomorphic Legendrian embeddings in $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$ whose projections to the quotient $\mathrm{SL}_2 (\mathbb{C})/ \mathrm{U}_1$ remain embeddings. As another consequence, every open Riemann surface admits a proper holomorphic Legendrian embedding in the projectivised special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_2 (\mathbb{C})$.

title: Data-Driven Stochastic Control of Delayed Air-Conditioning Systems
abstract: We consider a stochastic optimal control problem arising in the operation of industrial air-conditioning systems with delayed activation effects. The delayed transition between inactive and operational regimes induces a non-Markovian structure in the controlled dynamics. We derive a regression-based discrete dynamic programming algorithm on nested state-control grids. We give a probabilistic proof of convergence of the idealized time-discrete dynamic programming problem to the continuous-time value function. Numerical experiments based on calibrated multidimensional forecast-tracking Ornstein--Uhlenbeck models illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Parabolic Rectifiable Reifenberg for Measures
abstract: We announce a structure theory for measures on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic distance. Our results include a parabolic rectifiable Reifenberg theorem for arbitrary Radon measures, qualitative and quantitative characterizations of regular parabolic rectifiability by Jones square functions, and sharp results for $L^p$ beta numbers. The results hold in every parabolic dimension and extend the theories of Edelen--Naber--Valtorta, Azzam--Tolsa and David--Semmes to space-time. The stated theorems and corollaries, together with their proofs, are formalized in Lean~4 with Mathlib.
comment: Comments are welcome. 15 pages, 7 figures, link to a github repository for formalization

title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $β$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $β> 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $β= 2$.

title: Characterising canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties
abstract: We study Brantner-Taelman's canonical lifts of ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties and characterise their (quasi)canonical lifts in terms of rational $p$-adic Hodge theoretic data. We also show that these canonical lifts need not be of CM type and that the associated local Galois representations need not split as sums of twists of unramified representations, in contrast to classical results for abelian varieties and K3 surfaces.

title: How to get an attractive model
abstract: We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.
comment: 10 pages. v2: Added reference to Master's thesis of Paul Blesse

title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
comment: 36 pages, preliminary version, one comments and references are welcome

title: On the Anderson Dual of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$
abstract: In this paper, we give complete classifications of the finite groups $G$ for which the constant Eilenberg--Mac Lane spectra $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ and $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ are Anderson self-dual up to a virtual representation shift, and we determine all such shifts. For both of these spectra, we determine the representation periodicity lattice for every finite group. As applications, we obtain $RO(G)$-graded universal coefficient theorems relating equivariant homology and cohomology, together with formulas for the Anderson duals of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$-modules. In the $H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ self-dual cases, we identify the graded $\mathbb F_2$-linear dual of the coefficient ring $π_\star^G H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ with a representation shift of the ring as a module over itself. This gives perfect multiplication pairings and graded self-injectivity.

title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
abstract: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

title: Computational complexity of the $H$-coloring problem in cubic graphs
abstract: If $G$ and $H$ are two cubic graphs, then an $H$-coloring of $G$ is a mapping $f: E(G)\rightarrow E(H)$, such that for every $v\in V(G)$ there is a vertex $x\in V(H)$, such that $f(\partial_G(v))=\partial_H(x)$. If $G$ admits an $H$-coloring then it is common to write $H\prec G$. In this paper, for a fixed connected cubic graph $H$, we consider a decision problem, which we call $H$-coloring. In this problem, on the input one is given a connected cubic graph $G$. The goal is to decide whether $H\prec G$. A conjecture by Hakobyan and the author states that $H$-coloring is polynomial time solvable, if $H$ does not admit a $P_{12}$-coloring. Here $P_{12}$ is the unique cubic graph obtained from the Petersen graph by expanding one of its vertices into a triangle. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture under $P\neq NP$, by showing that $S_6$-coloring is NP-complete. Here $S_6$ is the unique cubic graph on six vertices having exactly one bridge. Our second result is an algorithm that solves $H$-coloring problem in time $O^*(c^n)$, where $H$ is a simple connected cubic graph, $n$ is the number of vertices of the input cubic graph $G$ and $c=\sqrt{8}\approx 2.8284$.

title: Maximal curves with trivial automorphism group
abstract: We construct algebraic curves with trivial geometric automorphism group by taking cyclic scalar quotients of curves of the form \[ y^r-y=xR(x),\qquad r=p^e. \] We give a condition on the genus under which the quotient has no nontrivial automorphism. The proof uses the ramification of a degree-$r$ morphism to the projective line, Castelnuovo--Severi, and explicit automorphisms of the covering curve. The quotient also has gonality $r$, with a unique morphism of degree $r$ to the projective line up to an automorphism of the latter. Applying the construction to maximal additive curves gives explicit maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group in every positive characteristic, including families defined over the prime field and of unbounded genus. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first examples of maximal curves with trivial geometric automorphism group. Every maximal curve in these families is covered by the Hermitian curve. For every odd prime $p$ and every $n\ge2$, we prove that the curve $\X_{p,n}$, maximal over $\F_{p^{4n+2}}$, is not a Galois subcover of the corresponding Hermitian curve, even over the algebraic closure. Thus every odd characteristic yields an infinite family of curves covered but not Galois covered by the Hermitian curve. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first such infinite families.

title: Weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for Stirling--Whitney--Riordan and Laguerre polynomials
abstract: In this paper, we establish a sufficient condition for weak Hurwitz stability of extended Turán expressions for the Stirling--Whitney--Riordan polynomials. The proof uses polynomial transformations that preserve zeros in a real interval and in the unit disk. As an application, we prove that the extended Turán expressions for the Bell polynomials are weakly Hurwitz stable. We also prove the corresponding result for the reflected Laguerre polynomials using polynomial approximations. These results settle two conjectures of Chasse, Grabarek, and Visontai.

title: Persistence Pays: Square-root condition-number dependence for Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin Monte Carlo with a non-reversibly updated accept/reject uniform
abstract: We prove accelerated mixing for a Metropolis-adjusted kinetic Langevin sampler: the OBABO splitting with friction $2\sqrt m$, adjusted with Neal's non-reversibly updated uniform, which is redrawn after every epoch of $E$ steps. For targets $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $mI\preceq\nabla^2U\preceq LI$ and an $L_H$-Lipschitz Hessian, started from a Gaussian at an approximate minimizer, the chain reaches total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ after $\tilde O\big(\sqrt{κd}+\sqrt{L_H}(d/m)^{3/4}\big)$ gradient evaluations, where $κ=L/m$ and $\tilde O$ hides logarithmic factors. The $\sqrtκ$ term is necessary, already on Gaussian targets. The proof discretizes Lu's entropic hypocoercivity by means of an entropy inequality for free transport, so that the relative entropy of the unadjusted chain decays at a rate of order $\sqrt m$ up to a discretization bias. With the non-reversibly updated uniform, the leading energy errors of velocity Verlet telescope along a path. A coupling argument combines the two. On Bayesian logistic regression posteriors for two standard data sets, which satisfy these assumptions, the gradient cost of the chain with the non-reversibly updated uniform grows roughly like the square root of the condition number at the posterior mode, and that of standard adjusted OBABO roughly like its $3/4$ power.
comment: 37 pages, 4 figures. Code and data in the ancillary files. Lean 4 formalization of the main results at https://github.com/nawafbourabee/persistence-pays-lean (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23671351)

title: Using the Blackwell-Cover Guessing Strategy to Separate Unobserved Bernoulli Trials - II
abstract: In a prior paper, we investigated what could be said about the number in the pair that was not observed when we employed the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy. In this paper, we generalize prior results to arbitrary distributions. We use a variant of the BlackwellCover strategy ro take pairs of coins chosen from a mixture of two different distributions G and H such that one of the coins is flipped, and as a result of that flip the unobserved (unflipped) coin is placed in one of two sets A and B. We show that, regardless of which distributions are used for G and H, there are situations in which this can be done so that the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in A is less than the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in B. What makes this result surprising, in addition to its generality, is a comparison with a corresponding result for marbles. If one knows that one will always be weighing one of two marbles with different specific weights, such as 10g and 20g, knowing the weight of the marble being weighed automatically determines the weight of the other. However, even if one knows that one will be flipping one of two coins with specific heads probabilities such as 1/3 and 2/3, the outcome of the flip of one of the coins will not immediately enable one to conclude anything about the heads probability of the unflipped coin, which is where the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy comes into play.

title: The generic structure of the singular set in the Stefan problem
abstract: We show that, in every space dimension $n\ge2$, the singular set $Σ$ of a generic (in the Baire-category sense) solution of the Stefan problem is countably parabolically $(n-2)$-rectifiable. In particular, $\dim_{\mathrm{par}}(Σ)\le n-2$. This is achieved by proving the following sharp result: in every space dimension, points of the maximal stratum of a generic solution are discrete in space-time.

title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
abstract: A permutation $σ\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $σ(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k σ(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $Φ_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $Φ_p = Φ_p^{+} \sqcup Φ_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| Φ_p^{+} | - | Φ_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $σ\inΦ_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $Φ_p^{+}$ versus $Φ_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $σ^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
comment: Proof of the claim from arXiv:2605.11137 [math.CO]; sequel to arXiv:2610.08636 [math.NT]; 21 pages, 4 appendices, 6 tables, 6 figures

title: P-stable degree sequence regions for bipartite and directed graphs
abstract: The switch Markov chain is a natural method for sampling graph realizations with a prescribed degree sequence, and $P$-stability is a general sufficient condition for its rapid mixing. Since $P$-stability is often difficult to verify directly, we develop an approach based on the simpler and more readily verifiable property of \emph{full graphicality}. We consider bidegree sequence regions obtained by fixing the two class sizes, the common degree sum, and lower and upper bounds for the degrees in each class. Such a region is fully graphic if every bidegree sequence satisfying these constraints has a bipartite realization. Our main result shows that every fully graphic region of this form is $P$-stable. More precisely, for class sizes $n$ and $m$, the perturbation ratio is at most $(nm)^5$. It follows from a known theory that the switch Markov chain is rapidly mixing on every such region. We also show that full graphicality can be tested on a canonical extremal bidegree sequence and use this characterization to derive several new explicit sufficient conditions. By encoding loopless directed graphs as bipartite graphs, we develop a parallel theory for directed degree sequences. This gives analogous extremal characterizations, sufficient conditions for full graphicality, and $P$-stability and rapid-mixing results for directed degree-sequence regions. The encoding process allows most corresponding statements for the two cases to be formulated and proved in one run.

title: A solution to Haagerup's problem: Normality of weights is commutatively determined
abstract: We prove that a weight on a C$^*$-algebra is lower semi-continuous if it is lower semi-continuous on commutative C$^*$-subalgebras. This can be used to prove a von Neumann algebraic counterpart that a weight on a von Neumann algebra is normal if it is normal on commutative von Neumann subalgebras. This provides an affirmative solution to Haagerup's second problem (Problem 1.11) on normal weights posed in 1975.

title: On the Nash equilibrium for a model of traffic flow
abstract: The paper consider a conservation law model of traffic flow on a highway, where each driver chooses an optimal departure time $τ^d$, based on a departure cost $\varphi(τ^d)$ and an arrival cost $ψ(τ^a)$. Nash equilibria are studied, where no driver can reduce his own cost by changing his departure time. The first results provide continuity estimates on the arrival time, depending on the distribution of departures. In terms of the ${\bf L}^1$ distance, we show that the corresponding map is Hölder continuous with exponent $1/2$ in Lagrangian variables (labelling individual drivers), and Lipschitz continuous in Eulerian space variables. Concerning the regularity of the a Nash equilibrium, our results show that, when the total number of drivers is sufficiently large, a queue alway forms at the entrance of the highway and the corresponding traffic density contains a shock. Moreover, for any number of drivers (possibly small), we prove that for generic $\mathcal C^2$ cost functions $\varphi, ψ$ the Nash equilibrium solution still contains a shock. In the last section of the paper, assuming that the initial departure rate is not a Nash equilibrium, we consider an evolution equation for the departure rate, where each driver keeps changing his daily departure time in order to reduce his own cost. It is proved that this nonlocal integro-differential evolution equation admits a unique solution, globally in time. This provides some theoretical support to earlier numerical simulations, which indicated the dynamic instability of the Nash equilibrium and the possible existence of a chaotic attractor.
comment: Keywords: Conservation laws, shocks, Nash equilibrium, integro-differential evolution equation

title: Traveling Waves for Mixed Nonlocal-Local Systems of Conservation Laws on $\mathbb{S}^1$
abstract: Non trivial traveling waves in genuinely nonlinear conservation laws hardly appear and, in some cases, scalar nonlocal conservation laws inherit this feature. Here, we show that mixed nonlocal-local systems of conservation laws display a far richer scenario. A variety of traveling waves may exist, different components may travel with different speeds and traveling waves can appear as time-asymptotic limits. Technically, these results need a significant extension of Dafermos' "trend to steady state" theory, exploiting properties of Hamiltonian systems solved by generalized characteristics.

title: The Undecidability of FO3 and the Calculus of Relations with Just One Binary Relation
abstract: The validity problem for first-order logic is a well-known undecidable problem. The undecidability also holds even for $\mathsf{FO}3$ and (equational formulas of) the calculus of relations. In this paper we tighten these undecidability results to the following: (1) $\mathsf{FO}3$ with just one binary relation is undecidable even without equality; and (2) the calculus of relations with just one character and with only composition, union, and complement is undecidable. Additionally we prove that the finite validity problem is also undecidable for the above two classes.
comment: Long version of the paper at ICLA'19, with (Ax.1) and (Ax.2) in Section 3 corrected

title: Self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges with large end-to-end distance
abstract: Self-intersection local times serve as the Hamiltonian in the Gibbs measure of continuous polymer models, for which the end-to-end distance is a key quantity. We study multiple self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges, \emph{i.e.}, Volterra Gaussian processes conditioned on their final location $a$, as $\|a\|\to\infty$. For $d$-dimensional $(2,ζ)$-locally nondeterministic processes with $ζ\in(0,2/d)$, we prove that these local times exist in every $L^p$. Under two further conditions on the kernel, the $p$-th moment of the $m$-multiple self-intersection local time of the bridge is of exact order $\|a\|^{-γ}$ for every integer $p\geqslant1$, with $γ=p(m-1)(2-ζd)/(2-ζ)$. In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-α}\}$, $α>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-α})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $α<2$, $α=2$ and $α>2$ respectively.

title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions for a random PDE-ODE model describing glioma invasion and radiotherapy
abstract: We study a stochastic model for the growth and invasion of glioma cells in the anisotropic brain tissue, also incorporating effects of radiotherapeutic interventions and associated uncertainties. The PDE-ODE model couples glioma and healthy tissue dynamics in a nonlinear manner and explicitly includes treatment-related stochasticity through random depletion terms. The macroscopic system has been obtained by an upscaling procedure from a microscopic description in [1]. We prove the existence and uniqueness of local strong solutions to the corresponding stochastic system. The analysis addresses challenges arising from the nonlinear coupling, anisotropic diffusion, taxis mechanisms, and stochastic treatment effects, providing a first rigorous step toward the mathematical understanding of stochastic continuum models for glioma invasion and therapy response.

title: Endpoint gradient bounds for centered convex maximal operators and probability kernels
abstract: We establish the endpoint gradient estimate for centered homothetic maximal averages in every dimension $d\ge2$ over each fixed convex body with $C^{1,θ}$ boundary, $0<θ\le1$. In particular, the centered ball maximal operator satisfies the $W^{1,1}$ gradient bound in every dimension. Neither strict convexity nor a lower bound on the support gap is required. The geometric argument combines concentration in gradient values with nonhomogeneous calibrated rows and a summable radial correction. It extends the scalar refinement, direction-history construction and global assembly of the planar centered-disk proof of OpenAI. A separate transfer theorem gives sharp singular-derivative identities for bounded compact probability kernels once local BV output is known, and gradient continuity under an additional spatial-tail condition. Quantitative contact and translation estimates yield further profile and kernel examples. The estimates retain the fixed body's regularity data; the endpoint for arbitrary $C^1$ and nonsmooth convex bodies remains open here.

title: Entropic hypocoercivity via the Polchinski flow: an application to the lattice sine-Gordon model
abstract: We develop a multiscale criterion for exponential decay of relative entropy in the canonical stochastic quantization of lattice field theories, the underdamped Langevin dynamics of the field and its momentum. For smooth bounded perturbations of Gaussian fields, the criterion requires the uniform operator-norm bound on the smoothed interaction Hessian along the Polchinski flow of Bauerschmidt and Bodineau to have a small $L^2$ norm in the scale variable. The decay constants depend only on this $L^2$ norm and the friction. The proof measures the transfer of momentum dissipation to position on the same scales that decompose entropy. A phase-space extension of the Polchinski flow gives Gaussian coarse-graining that commutes with free kinetic evolution. Integrating position--momentum cross terms over these scales yields a corrector bounded by entropy. A force defect accounts for changes in the averaged interaction force away from equilibrium; its evolution in scale controls the errors in the kinetic estimate. For the massive two-dimensional lattice sine--Gordon model with $0<β<4π$ and small dimensionless local coupling, the criterion gives entropy decay for all finite-entropy initial laws, uniformly in the lattice spacing and the volume. For friction proportional to the mass $m$, the rate has optimal order $m$.

title: The size of an overtwisted disk
abstract: We introduce a notion of size for an overtwisted disk, defined in terms of the Shelukhin-Hofer energy required to stabilise Legendrians in its vicinity. We compute this size for the standard $3$-dimensional overtwisted disk, which we use to prove that certain explicit product hyperdisks in higher-dimensional contact manifolds are overtwisted (and their overtwisted size can be computed explicitly as well). We then use the overtwisted size to establish a number of quantitative results on contact flexibility. Concretely, we (1) obtain quantitative $h$--principles for Legendrians in the complement of an overtwisted disk, (2) construct overtwisted-at-infinity contact manifolds whose Legendrian Shelukhin-Hofer metric vanishes, (3) estimate overtwisted size under contact products and under products with Liouville manifolds, and (4) derive action bounds for contractible Reeb orbits in closed overtwisted contact manifolds.

title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.

title: A Stochastic Proximal-Gradient Method for Regularized Generally Constrained Continuous Optimization
abstract: A stochastic proximal-gradient method is proposed and analyzed for solving regularized optimization problems subject to nonlinear equality constraints and nonnegativity bounds. The objective function's values and gradients are available only through inexact stochastic oracles. The method decomposes each trial step into one component that reduces linearized infeasibility and a second component that seeks optimality while preserving that reduction. Trial steps are accepted or rejected through a relaxed sufficient decrease condition subject to stochastic merit function evaluations. Without assuming unbiasedness of stochastic gradient estimates, it is proved under reasonable assumptions that the method reaches an $ε$-KKT point within $O(ε^{-2})$ iterations with high probability. This guarantee further implies almost-sure termination in finitely many iterations and an $O(ε^{-2})$ bound on the expected iteration complexity.

title: Large Excursions of Reflected Lévy Processes: Local Asymptotics
abstract: This paper establishes uniform local large-deviation asymptotics for excursions of a Lévy process $X$ with negative drift $-β$ and $α$-locally regularly varying Lévy measure $ν$, reflected at its running infimum. Under the excursion measure $\underline n$, we first prove that the lifetime $ζ$ and height $\overlineε$ satisfy \begin{equation*} \underline{n}\big(ζ\in(t,t+δ] \big) \sim \underline{n}(\overlineε\in\big (βt,βt+βδ]\big) \sim\underline{n}(ζ)\cdotν\big((βt,βt+βδ]\big), \quad \mbox{as } t\to\infty, \end{equation*} uniformly in $δ\in[δ_0,\infty]$ for every $δ_0>0$. In contrast to the asymptotic equivalence of the corresponding tail events, fixed-width lifetime and height windows have asymptotically negligible relative overlap. Nevertheless, for any positive function $θ$ satisfying $|X_t+βt|/θ_t\to0$ in probability, \begin{equation*} \underline n\big( |\overlineε-βt| \leq θ_t \,\big|\, ζ\in (t,t+δ] \big) \sim \underline n\big( |ζ-t| \leq θ_t \,\big|\, \overlineε\in (βt,βt+βδ] \big) \to 1 . \end{equation*} For conditioning windows of sublinear width bounded away from zero, both conditional excursion laws converge under spatial rescaling to a single-jump process with deterministic jump size and random arrival time determined by the integrated excursion survival function. An additional time rescaling yields the same deterministic linear descent killed at zero. Finally, we identify the joint limiting distribution of the unscaled pre-terminal position and terminal overshoot, including continuous and discontinuous termination.
comment: 61 pages, 2 figures. We did not use AI to generate any mathematical proofs or to originate any research ideas. All comments are welcomed!!

title: Heavy Heisenberg Algebras, Zero Modes and Modularity
abstract: It is known due to a result of Miyamoto that zero mode correlators of weight $1$ vectors of vertex operator algebras are quasi-modular forms, and that their generating series are Jacobi forms. In this article we generalize this to higher weight vectors. We consider weight 2 vectors that generate what we call heavy Heisenberg algebras. We prove that their zero mode correlators are a specific type of quasi-modular forms. As a consequence, they too can be summed up into a generating series with Jacobi-like modular transformation properties. As an application of our results, we sketch an argument that gives the asymptotic behavior of the dimensions of states of our VOAs.

title: Minimum Contagious Sets in Trees with Degree-Proportional Thresholds
abstract: We investigate how large the minimum size of a contagious set can be among trees of a fixed order. Given a graph $G$ and $ρ\in[0,1]$, an inactive vertex $u$ becomes active when at least $\lceil{ρd_G(u)\rceil}$ of its neighbors are active. An initial set of active vertices is contagious if the process eventually activates every vertex. We obtain exact values for the minimum size of a contagious set in perfect $d$-ary trees. We then determine the exact maximum of this minimum size over all trees of order $n$. We establish this result by bounding the number of pairwise disjoint resistant sets, each of which must intersect every contagious set, and constructing trees that attain the resulting bounds. Finally, by bounding the change in the minimum size of a contagious set under a leaf exchange, we show that, for $0<ρ\leq1$ and $n\geq2$, every integer between $1$ and this maximum occurs as the minimum size of a contagious set in a tree of order $n$.

title: The Weyl Problem for Planar CBB$(-1)$ Surfaces in Hyperbolic $3$-Space
abstract: In this paper, we study the Weyl problem for noncompact convex surfaces in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. We prove that any planar CBB$(-1)$ surface with countably many ends can be isometrically embedded as the boundary of a closed convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{H}^3$ such that each connected component of the ideal boundary of $X$ is either a round disk or a single point. By known rigidity results, such an embedding is unique up to isometries of $\mathbb{H}^3$. Moreover, we show that the assumption of countably many ends can be dropped if Koebe's circle domain conjecture holds.

title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

title: From skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to sharp Ax-Katz congruences and zero counts
abstract: We give a unified account of zero counting in finite-field polynomial rings with commuting variables twisted by a common automorphism. A decomposition into fixed-field slices connects skew evaluation with ordinary polynomial evaluation. First, we derive a slice coefficient formula from the skew Combinatorial Nullstellensatz and use it to deduce skew Chevalley-Warning, including the sufficient condition $n>h\sum_i d_i$. Next, classical Ax-Katz gives the corrected integer congruence $Q^{\max\{0,\lceil(n-h\sum_i d_i)/D\rceil\}}\mid N+(M-1)δ$. We construct homogeneous examples proving optimality for every positive degree table and every number of variables. We also establish a sharp lower bound with a prescribed zero, an input-sensitive coefficient-filtration refinement, and transfers of known bounds for nonlinear zero sets. Detailed calculations explain the origin correction, incomplete norm blocks, and the distinction between characteristic-$p$ summation and higher integer divisibility. Existing geometric, interpolation, and counting theorems are explicitly attributed.

title: Whittle--Matérn metrics and isotropic Gaussian processes on compact metric graphs
abstract: Isotropic Gaussian processes on networks have a covariance that is a function of a distance between locations, but valid constructions have so far required graphs with Euclidean edges and the resistance metric. We introduce a one-parameter family of metrics $d_κ$, $κ\ge0$, on arbitrary compact metric graphs, including those with loops and parallel edges, defined as the variograms of first-order Whittle--Matérn fields, where $κ=0$ corresponds to an intrinsic limiting field. We show that these Whittle--Matérn metrics are invariant under insertion and removal of vertices of degree two, that they decrease monotonically in $κ$, and that they can be evaluated by sparse linear solves. The metric $d_0$ coincides with the resistance metric on graphs with Euclidean edges, and thus extends it to general compact metric graphs without any modification of the graph. For every completely monotone function $r$ and every $κ\ge0$, we show that $r(d_κ)$ is a positive semidefinite function. This yields isotropic Gaussian processes on general compact metric graphs. For $κ>0$ the metric levels off beyond the screening length $κ^{-1}$, which can be used to induce long-range dependence in short-range covariance models, and $κ$ can be estimated from data together with the parameters of $r$. The models are compared on daily traffic maps from the street network of Paris and the motorway network around London. For both, $κ$ is estimated to be positive, $d_κ$ increases the maximised log-likelihood relative to $d_0$ for every covariance function, and it gives the best predictions at randomly held-out locations.

title: Characterizations of the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$ among minimal systems
abstract: Given a minimal system E for a Banach space X, Casazza, Dilworth, Kutzarova and Motakis introduced a multiplication $\otimes$ on span(E) and studied the Schauder bases for which $\|x \otimes y\|\approx \|x\|\|y\|$ asking whether every such basis is equivalent to the canonical unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$. We continue this study in the more general setting of minimal systems that are not assumed to be Schauder bases, and we obtain positive answers under hypotheses that are formally weaker than the ones considered so far: partial democracy instead of democracy or bidemocracy, and truncation quasi-greediness instead of quasi-greediness. Along the way we show that the above multiplicative estimate forces invariance under translations, we characterize when such a minimal system is a Schauder basis, and we give examples showing that the one-sided variants of the estimate behave very differently.

title: Learning Behavioral Parameters of Network Equilibrium Models from Aggregate Mobility Data
abstract: Estimating travel behavior parameters is essential for understanding current travel patterns and for forecasting how travelers may respond to future changes in transportation systems. However, reliable estimation remains difficult when behavior must be inferred from sparse and aggregate observations, especially when jointly recovering several behavioral components. In this paper, we develop a bi-level estimation program for a combined destination, mode and route choice model with congestion. The inner level is a convex program at given scale parameters, and returns the taste coefficients as its dual variables together with the equilibrium travel pattern. The outer level selects the scale parameters by out-of-sample prediction, measured by how well the modeled travel pattern predicts observations withheld from estimation. To solve the bi-level problem at scale, we propose a matrix-free Hierarchical Lagrangian Dual algorithm as the inner solver and an outer search by implicit differentiation, which uses the sensitivities of the inner solution to enable efficient search over the scale parameters and reaches the calibrated scales in a handful of iterations. We validate the approach on Los Angeles County using public origin-destination, mode-share and traffic-count data. Our approach scales to a county-level problem with 2.7 million variables and substantially improves computational efficiency over a general-purpose conic solver. Compared with the fixed-scale benchmark, the calibrated model improves predictive performance at the destination and mode levels, with consistent gains across complementary goodness-of-fit measures.

title: The topological vertex is finitely generated
abstract: The topological vertex computes all genus amplitudes for the open topological A-model in $\mathbb{C}^3$ with branes on three toric Lagrangians and, via gluing, both open and closed string amplitudes on any toric Calabi-Yau threefold. In this note we show that the topological vertex is generated by boundary interactions of three disks and three annuli. A generalization of this result is shown to hold for the refined topological vertex.

title: Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filters based on Log Homotopy
abstract: This work proposes a new Multi-Fidelity Particle Flow Filter (MFPFF) based on a linear control variate framework and multilevel Monte Carlo methods. Conventional particle filters often suffer from weight collapse and particle degeneracy in high-dimensional spaces. Particle flow filters address this by smoothly transporting prior particles toward the posterior distribution, thereby avoiding the need for resampling. This work constructs multi-fidelity particle flow filters by augmenting a small number of expensive high-fidelity particles (full-order model runs) with a large number of inexpensive low-resolution particles (reduced-order surrogates constructed via intrusive Galerkin projection). These surrogates act as control variates to enhance the statistical estimate of the full-order posterior, yielding enhanced analysis accuracy at comparable computational cost. The work focuses on two particle flows based on log homotopy, the stochastic Gromov flow and deterministic Exact flow. Numerical experiments with the Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) and Quasi-Geostrophic (QG) test problems demonstrate that the proposed MFPFF achieves accuracy comparable to high-fidelity simulations while significantly reducing computational expense.

title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
abstract: In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a Demazure atom $A_γ$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_α$, or of a Schur function $s_λ$ and a Demazure character $κ_γ$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule. We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_λ(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_γ(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.

title: Curvature quotient flows and Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in hyperbolic space
abstract: We study quermassintegral-preserving curvature flows in $\mathbb H^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, driven by the curvature quotient $(E_k/E_\ell)^{1/(k-\ell)}$. For $1\leq\ell<k$ with $k+\ell\leq n$, we prove that positive sectional curvature is preserved. Starting from a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive sectional curvature, the flow exists for all time and converges smoothly and exponentially to a geodesic sphere. As an application, we establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities between $W_k$ and $W_\ell$ for smooth bounded convex domains whose boundaries have nonnegative sectional curvature, whenever $0\leq\ell<k\leq n$ and $k+\ell\leq n$. Equality holds if and only if the domain is a geodesic ball. Together with previously known cases, these inequalities give the full family of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for this class of domains in $\mathbb H^6$. We also construct counterexamples showing that $k+\ell\leq n$ is the optimal range for preservation of positive sectional curvature by these flows.

title: Degree-list Kempe equivalence for 3-connected graphs
abstract: In a proper coloring, a Kempe change interchanges two colors on a connected component of the subgraph they induce. For a fixed list assignment $L$, a Kempe change is $L$-valid if it transforms an $L$-coloring into another $L$-coloring. We prove that if $G$ is a $3$-connected graph other than a complete graph or the triangular prism, and $L$ is a list assignment with $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)$ for every vertex $v$, then $G$ has a proper $L$-coloring and any two such colorings can be transformed into one another by a finite sequence of $L$-valid Kempe changes. This proves a conjecture of Chakraborty, Feghali and Mahmoud.

title: Unconditional scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation
abstract: Unconditional global existence and scattering are established for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation with $0<α<3$, below the ground-state energy and kinetic thresholds. The initial data lie in $\dot H^1$, with no radial symmetry, finite-mass, or finite-variance assumption. Annular frequency estimates and Gaussian interaction estimates rule out a compact critical trajectory by first controlling its nonlinear forcing and then recovering its conserved mass.

title: Computing Data-Aware Diagonal Frame Decompositions
abstract: We present a method for computing a specific type of matrix decomposition that combines a structured framework with data-driven adaptation. This framework allows for an efficient and stable representation of signals or images using frames by identifying sets of vectors that naturally capture the essential features of the given data. The resulting decomposition enables the development of regularization techniques that enhance the quality of reconstruction by preserving important signal characteristics while suppressing noise. We develop an optimization-based algorithm to compute the decomposition and establish convergence properties of the resulting iterates. Numerical experiments on synthetic data and tomographic image reconstruction illustrate the behavior of the proposed method and its performance compared to conventional spectral regularization methods.

title: Facet normals of Minkowski sums of staircase simplices
abstract: Staircase simplices are the simplices of the standard (Freudenthal--Kuhn) triangulation of $[0,1]^d$ and of Stanley's triangulations of order polytopes. We study the facet normals of their Minkowski sums and how the number of summands constrains the size of primitive integer normals. We characterize the normals attainable with a prescribed number of summands in terms of $d-1$ linearly independent zero-one vectors orthogonal to the normal, whose supports have an intersection graph that can be colored with one color per summand. This gives a combinatorial characterization of the least number of summands needed to realize a normal. For two summands, all primitive normals have entries in $\{-1,0,1\}$, and we determine which of them occur. For three summands we bound every entry in absolute value by $3^{(d-2)/3}$ and construct normals with entries of order $θ^d$, $θ$ the plastic number; for four summands a second construction gives entries of order $ψ^d$, $ψ$ the supergolden ratio. Since $ψ>3^{1/3}$, the largest coefficients for three and four summands are exponentially separated. For vectors with at most two distinct nonzero entry values, we determine the least number of summands exactly, using a matching-rank formula proved by exterior algebra and representations of symmetric groups. With no restriction on the number of summands, the maximum coefficient equals the classical maximum for facets of $0/1$-polytopes in the same dimension.

title: Sharp volume tests and entropy thresholds for quasilinear elliptic inequalities with gradient reactions
abstract: We investigate positive weak solutions of $-Δ_m u\ge u^p|\nabla u|^q$ on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds without curvature, volume doubling, or Poincaré assumptions. For the superhomogeneous mixed reaction we derive a curvature-free integral volume test by combining two first-order estimates with a recurrence for the mass of a \emph{fixed} density. The same approach organizes the pure-gradient and capacity criteria and yields sharp finite hierarchies of iterated-logarithmic growth bounds, with counterexamples on smooth model manifolds. In the subhomogeneous region, vanishing lower growth of $\log V(R)/R^{m-q}$ forces the Liouville property. On the homogeneous line $p+q=m-1$, we obtain the optimal strict lower-volume-entropy threshold $(p+1)((m-1)/p)^{p/(p+1)}$ for $p>0$ (and $1$ for $p=0$), together with examples at equality. The existing six-region classification is not claimed as new; the advances concern refined volume hypotheses and their model sharpness. The tests remain valid for smooth weighted measures and for locally bounded positive Sobolev solutions. Sharpness is understood within the stated model families; no characterization from volume alone on an individual manifold is asserted.

title: Supply Chain Information Sharing among Competitors: Profit-Based Participation under Market Shocks
abstract: Sharing information can help coordinate supply chain decisions in response to market shocks. Yet, firms must weigh these benefits against the risk of strengthening competitors. We study when competing firms voluntarily join an information-sharing platform to exchange information about market shocks while retaining operational autonomy. Firms differ in information capabilities and decide whether to participate before private signals are realized, creating stochastic information asymmetry. We model participation and quantity decisions as a two-stage dynamic game with incomplete information. For two horizontal competitors, we derive closed-form equilibrium participation strategies that reveal how information power and production efficiency shape participation. Numerical analysis examines more complex supply chain networks. We find that supply chain characteristics impact participation and the level of information asymmetry is a key factor in the equilibrium platform profiles. Firms with similar information power may benefit from joining forces to reduce their competitive disadvantage against higher information power competitors. Cost-inefficient firms may be less willing to participate because their competitors can exploit shared information, and uncertainty can serve as a competitive shield by restricting the actions of more efficient competitors. However, when several competitors join the platform, a cost-inefficient firm may also choose to participate to avoid an informational disadvantage.

title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.

title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
abstract: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

title: On the facets of the Cayley polytope of Stanley's triangulation
abstract: Disjunctions over the cells of a triangulation arise in formulations of piecewise-linear functions. For a poset $P$ on $[d]$, we study the convex hull $D$ of the simplices of Stanley's triangulation of the order polytope of $P$, each lifted by its own indicator vector. Via the Cayley trick, for any disjunction of full-dimensional polytopes, the facets of the convex hull other than those described by the bounds on the indicator variables correspond to the facet normals of the Minkowski sum of the polytopes, and each is described by the full optimal big-M lifting of the supporting inequality with that normal of any one polytope. For Stanley's triangulation, with $M(P)$ the Minkowski sum of its simplices, lifting only the facet-describing inequalities of the simplices need not suffice, unlike some other cases; we show that it suffices if and only if $M(P)$ is alcoved, if and only if deleting one element of $P$ leaves a chain. Otherwise, the coefficients of the additional facet-describing inequalities are governed by the least number $\ell(P)$ of elements whose deletion leaves a chain: for fixed $\ell(P)$, the largest entry of a primitive facet normal grows like $d^{\ell(P)-1}$, and it can be exponential in $d$ if $\ell(P)$ grows with $d$. For $d \geq 3$ and $\ell(P)\leq2$ the sharp bound is $d-2$.

title: Singularity Analysis of Laplace Boundary Integral Equations on Three-Dimensional Domains with Corners
abstract: Solutions to elliptic boundary value problems on three-dimensional nonsmooth domains exhibit singular behavior near edges and vertices. Using layer potential theory, we investigate boundary integral equations for the Laplace equation and characterize the leading singular exponents of the surface density on conical domains. For two canonical geometries, we derive explicit formulas for the two families of edge singular exponents on a dihedral wedge, and characterize the modewise vertex singular exponents on an axisymmetric circular cone through the zeros of associated Legendre functions and their derivatives. Building on these two prototypes and the dilation-invariance property, we formulate the associated operator pencil for general conical domains and develop a nonlinear eigenvalue solver. This solver employs the Nyström method with graded meshes, logarithmically corrected trapezoidal rules, and Brent's method to compute these singular exponents accurately and efficiently. Numerical examples for trihedral cones, regular m-hedral cones, and droplet-type cones verify the effectiveness of our approach and illustrate the interactions between edge and vertex singularities.

title: SCAFFOLD under Hessian Similarity: Sharp Convergence Rates
abstract: One of the main challenges of federated learning is heterogeneous data split among the clients, leading to biased local updates called client drift. The SCAFFOLD algorithm (Karimireddy et al., 2020) corrects client drift with control variates, but its relation to the similarity of client data is not yet fully understood: the original similarity-based guarantees cover only quadratics with a stronger second-order similarity assumption, and a follow-up weakly convex analysis (Luo et al., 2025) obtains a $\sqrt{Lδ}$ dependence for $L$-smooth losses with averaged Hessian similarity $δ$. We analyze SCAFFOLD with minibatch-based control variates and establish linear dependence on Hessian similarity beyond quadratics, for both convex and nonconvex objectives. In particular, for convex objectives with exact gradients, $R$ SCAFFOLD rounds with $K$ local steps lead to an objective gap of order $(L/K+δ)D_0^2/R$, where $D_0$ is the initial distance to a minimizer. When $K=Θ(L/δ)$, it improves the minibatch SGD rate by a factor $Θ(L/δ)$. For nonconvex objectives, we prove an analogous stationarity guarantee under uniform Hessian similarity for a client-selection variant. In both settings, we extend these guarantees to stochastic gradients and prove matching lower bounds for the analyzed methods with constant local stepsizes. We also show that, under partial participation, even identical clients need not obtain the full communication benefit of additional local steps.

title: The Riesz representation in submetric spaces and its probabilistic aspects
abstract: A submetric space is a topological space equipped with a continuous metric that generates a metric topology (usually) weaker than the original one (e.g., a~separable Hilbert space with the weak topology). We show that a positive linear functional on the space of bounded continuous functions on a submetric space is given as an integral with respect to a tight measure if, and only if, it is continuous in the strict topology. Neither local compactness nor complete regularity is required. We link the equicontinuity of a family of functionals in the strict topology to the uniform tightness of the underlying measures, and we provide a probabilistic representation (Skorokhod's parametrization) for such families. Finally, we identify the finest topology on the space of probability measures on a submetric space in which uniform tightness implies relative compactness. In non-metric spaces this topology is strictly stronger than the topology of weak convergence of probability measures.

title: Provably Efficient Q-learning for Robust Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Standard reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms based on Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) are vulnerable to sim-to-real gaps. To address this issue, distributionally robust RL algorithms based on robust MDPs (RMDPs) have been proposed, for ensuring that agents can perform reliably to unpredictable conditions in real-world environments. Despite of the rich literature, \revision{an efficient model-free method is still lacking} for robust RL, particularly for Markovian data, which is more relevant in practical applications. In this work, we take a step towards settling this problem by proposing a sample efficient (asynchronous Q-learning) algorithm for robust RL.
