In particular, consider a $γ$-discounted infinite-horizon RMDP with state space $\mathcal{S}$ and action space $\mathcal{A}$, where the uncertainty set is specified by the total variation (TV) distance with uncertainty level $σ$. Assuming access to a single trajectory of Markovian samples induced by a behavior policy and the nominal transition kernel, the sample complexity of the proposed Q-learning algorithm --- to achieve an entrywise $\varepsilon$-approximation of the optimal Q-function --- is bounded by $$ \frac{1}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}\varepsilon^2(1-γ)^3\max\{1-γ,σ\}} + \frac{t_{\mathsf{mix}}}{μ_{\mathsf{min}}(1-γ)} $$ up to logarithmic factors. Here, $t_{\mathsf{mix}}$ and $μ_{\mathsf{min}}$ denote the mixing time and the minimum state-action occupancy probability of the sample trajectory, respectively. This result is nearly minimax optimal, with an additional factor of $\frac{1}{1-γ}$. Moreover, it achieves a significant improvement over existing bounds.

title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

title: Simple Torsion-Free Linear Groups from Global Division Algebras
abstract: We investigate the reduced norm-one group $\mathrm{SL}_1(D)$ of a central division algebra $D$ of odd degree over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using the Brauer-Hasse-Noether theorem and the Margulis-Platonov theorem, we derive a criterion for abstract simplicity in terms of local division completions. For a division algebra of degree $15$ with local invariants $1/3$, $-1/3$, $1/5$, and $-1/5$, the construction yields a candidate example of an infinite, torsion-free, nonabelian simple linear group. This would provide an affirmative answer to Problem 16.78 of the Kourovka Notebook. The argument was generated using an AI system and has not yet been independently verified by human mathematicians.

title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
abstract: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.

title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
abstract: Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $σ$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $σ$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,σ)$. We prove that if an almost periodic $σ$-preserving action $α$ satisfies that $\overline{α(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,σ)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $α$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $α:G\curvearrowright (D,σ)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $σ$-preserving action with $\overline{α(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere. In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

title: Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p
abstract: Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.

title: On the Hasse principle for a block-diagonal form and a form of lower degree
abstract: We investigate the Hasse principle for systems consisting of one form of degree $k$ which decomposes as a sum of $n$-ary forms, and one general form of degree $d < k$. By exploiting the block structure of the first form before applying Weyl differencing, we refine the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this setting; in particular, for a sum of binary quartic forms and a quadratic form, the requirement $s > 516$ is relaxed to $s > 96$, which also improves on the bound $s > 100$ available for general forms.

title: Phase response approach to networked neural activity models with delays
abstract: Networks of delay-coupled neural mass models alternate between synchrony and anti-phase locking as the delay between brain regions increases. The origin of these delay-dependent bands has remained unclear. Here, we show that a single function, the phase interaction function $H$ of an isolated node, predicts where the bands occur and explains why they repeat. For a Wilson--Cowan model with intra-nodal delay $τ$ and inter-nodal delay $ρ$, we compute the limit cycle and phase response, and hence $H$, by harmonic balance. Each band boundary is a zero of $H'$ shifted by the phase lag $Ωρ$, so the bands repeat in $ρ$ with the oscillation period. Simulations of the full delay-differential networks confirm these predictions, from two nodes, where predicted frequencies agree to second order in the coupling strength, to rings, where the theory also identifies coexisting stable twisted states that random initial conditions rarely reach. At weak coupling, the delays at which synchrony gains or loses stability are set by the node dynamics alone, whereas stable anti-phase states require a bipartite network. For a macaque connectome, metastability peaks at the edges of the synchrony bands, where the stability margin of phase-locking vanishes. The reduction is accurate for coupling strengths well below the slowest Floquet exponent of the node, beyond which a phase--amplitude description is needed. More broadly, vanishing phase-locking stability provides a simple route to metastability in delay-coupled oscillator networks and a candidate mechanism for the flexible coordination of brain dynamics.

title: Efficient ADMM for Soft-Constrained Quadratic Programs via Generalized Slack Projections
abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. In this paper, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) scheme for a broad class of convex slack penalty functions, including all $\ell_k$-norms, without increasing the problem size. The only change to the ADMM scheme is a modified slack projection function, while the remaining algorithm stays the same. We demonstrate our approach on numerical examples, showing significant speedups, and show its flexibility on an energy optimization problem.

title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

title: Generalizing Praeger--Xu graphs
abstract: We uniformly study directed Praeger--Xu graphs and Praeger's generalized family $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$, without requiring that $s\mid r$ and $Γ$ is an undirected graph. Assuming that $Γ\times\overrightarrow{K}_2$ is connected, we determine the full automorphism group of $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ for every $r$ and $s$, prove connectivity, characterize vertex-transitivity, and give an equivalent criterion for $t$-arc-transitivity. We also study when $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(Γ,r,s)$ is a Cayley graph. We also give two applications. First, we give a new family of twin-free connected arc-transitive digraphs of valency $4$ whose vertex stabilizers have exponential growth. We also give a connected regular digraph that is not vertex-transitive but whose direct product with a directed cycle is Cayley.

title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
abstract: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.

title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
abstract: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_θ$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_θ$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

title: Counting transversals in Latin squares over groups of even order
abstract: The number of transversals in a Latin square $L(G)$ whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite group $G$ has been determined computationally for all $G$ of order at most $23$ and for $C_{25}$. However, computation of the number of transversals of $L(G)$ has until now been considered intractable for all non-cyclic groups $G$ of order $32$. We show, for a group $G$ containing an order $2$ normal subgroup $N$, that the image of a transversal in $L(G)$ under the quotient mapping from $G$ to $G/N$ is a $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. We then derive linear algebraic conditions that determine the number of transversals in $L(G)$ whose image under the quotient mapping is a given $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. This allows us to count transversals in $L(G)$ by examining all $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$. Although we can simplify the counting of $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$ by taking advantage of their symmetry group, the linear algebraic conditions can vary over a symmetry class of $2$-plexes. However, in the case that $G$ takes the splitting form $C_2 \times H$, the linear algebraic conditions become invariant over each symmetry class and so the counting of transversals in $L(C_2 \times H)$ reduces to counting the $2$-plexes in $L(H)$ under the action of their symmetry group. We illustrate the power of these techniques by computing the exact number of transversals in $L(C_2^5)$.

title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves II: Smooth bounded domains
abstract: Continuing \cite{NWX} and Part I \cite{AOSI}, we further investigate symmetry for spacetime observability of wave equations. Building on asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) introduced in \cite{AOSI}, we study symmetry under glancing propagation and caustics. We prove that, on every smooth bounded domain in $\R^2$ and for every positive observation time, there is a fixed measurable set satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition. However, the observability inequality fails on this set.

title: Distribution-free predictive inference with instrumental variables
abstract: We study the problem of predictive inference with outcomes missing not at random, when instrumental variables are available. While conformal prediction and weighted conformal prediction provide valid distribution-free inference when outcomes are missing completely at random and missing at random, respectively, inference is generally not possible without additional assumptions when outcomes are missing not at random. In this work, we consider a setting where we remain within the distribution-free framework but instead have access to an instrumental variable (IV). We explore the theoretical possibility of IV predictive inference and establish that it is characterized by a parameter that we refer to as the identification index. We derive an impossibility result for the case where the identification index is not sufficiently large, showing that any distribution-free approach fails to provide informative inference in this case. For the case where the identification index is sufficiently large, we introduce a practical method that achieves informative predictive inference. Our method leverages modern semiparametric efficiency theory which involves deriving the efficient influence function of the identifying functional for sharp IV bounds of the quantiles of the missing outcome, delivering a double robustness property in the coverage guarantee of the proposed framework for IV-based predictive inference. We illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed procedure through simulations and two real-data applications---FES wages and NHANES III self-reported heights.

title: Modular representations of metabelian groups
abstract: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $φ:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+φ(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(φ)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(φ)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.

title: Extending the V-sequence reduction to arbitrary independent distributions
abstract: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent random variables with arbitrary known distributions, where $n\ge2$. The optimal probability $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ of choosing an overall maximum satisfies $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\ge(1-1/n)^{n-1}$, and this bound is attained. We obtain this known sharp bound by extending the reduction lemma of Allaart and Islas (2016) from continuous to arbitrary distributions. We construct a $V$-sequence whose optimal win probability does not exceed that of the original sequence, and then apply the bound for $V$-sequences. The construction first replaces atoms by uniform observations on strictly ordered intervals and applies the original continuous reduction lemma. The reduced distributions are determined by a common critical level and a common probability for splitting a possible atom at that level.

title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*ω_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.

title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
abstract:
For a function $ψ: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} ψ= |ψ|^{-1} \overlineψ\,
ablaψ$ and study the regularity of the map $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ] = 
abla |ψ|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $Λ= \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} ψ]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $ψ\mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} ψ$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $ψ\mapsto |ψ|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|ψ|^{-1} ψ) 
abla ψ$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.

title: Finite-step projective dynamics of Schrödinger cocycles: non-degeneracy, regularity, and rigidity
abstract: We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schrödinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step $L^2$ norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove Hölder bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and Hölder conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions. For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and Hölder bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps $k\ge2$ and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.

title: Computing ${}_{q+1}{F}_q$ via rational conformal maps
abstract: It is well-known that certain Möbius (linear fractional) transformations provide analytic continuation of the Gauss hypergeometric function. These transformations work by exchanging the roles of the three regular singular points and $0$, $1$, and $\infty$ of the Gauss hypergeometric differential equation. Not one of these transformations, however, brings the points $e^{\pm{\rm i}π/3}$ closer to the origin, and convergence in a neighbourhood of these is also troublesome. In this work, we produce a Maclaurin series in optimal complexity after rational conformal mapping that induces pointwise convergence to any ${}_{q+1}F_q$ throughout the cut complex plane $\mathbb{C}\setminus[1,\infty)$. We show that for the optimal parameter values this series converges faster than an approximate mapped Chebyshev series obtained by the ultraspherical spectral method.

title: Sharp Norm Approximation of Covering Markov Operators
abstract: We study the operator-norm approximation of Markov operators associated with finite graph coverings. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a connected covering of degree $d\geq 2$ between finite connected graphs, and let $A_q:C(Y)\to C(X)$ be its fiber-averaging operator. We show that $A_q$ is not a finite convex combination of extreme Markov operators, although such combinations approximate $A_q$ arbitrarily well in operator norm. We determine the exact distances from $A_q$ to convex combinations of at most $m$ extreme Markov operators, with arbitrary or equal convex weights. If $m=kd+r$, where $k\geq 0$ and $1\leq r\leq d$, these distances are $2(d-r+1)/[d(k(d-r+1)+1)]$ and $2r(d-r+1)/(dm)$, respectively. Both distances are attained and depend only on the covering degree $d$ and the number of terms $m$. We also determine when equal weights are optimal and quantify the additional approximation error when they are not. Our proofs use total-variation estimates and continuous rearrangements of labelled weighted atoms. In particular, the unrestricted errors have a common scaled limit, while the equal-weight errors exhibit residue-dependent asymptotic behavior.

title: Grothendieck rings of near-Tambara--Yamagami fusion categories
abstract: We determine the Grothendieck rings of fusion categories over $\mathcal{C}$ containing a nonpointed Tambara--Yamagami fusion subcategory and exactly one further simple object. The subcategory necessarily has rank five, its invertible objects form the Klein four-group, and the coefficient $κ$ of the additional simple object in its tensor square belongs to $\{0,2,7\}$. Each of these three based rings is categorifiable. For $κ=0$, every category belongs, up to tensor equivalence, to the rank-one odd-component extension list of Choi--Lu--Sun. For $κ=2$ we construct an explicit unitary group-theoretical realization, and for $κ=7$ a realization is $\rm{Rep}(\rm{PSU}(3,2))$.

title: Gradient estimates and Liouville theorems for exponentially harmonic functions
abstract: We study exponentially harmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds. Under a lower Ricci curvature bound \(\Ric_g\geq-Kg\), we first establish a local gradient estimate in terms of the oscillation. We then prove a pointwise gradient estimate for solutions bounded from one side. As an application, when \(\Ric_g\geq0\), we obtain a Liouville theorem under a one-sided sublinear growth condition. In particular, every exponentially harmonic function bounded above or below is constant.

title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
abstract: By virtue of the sheer compute demands of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC), modern multi-core microprocessors suffer from severe power density limits and thermal throttling, entailing an urgent need for principled methods for predictive, physics-informed dynamical thermal management (DTM). Here, we introduce a hardware/software co-design physics-informed PDE-constrained DTM throttling optimal control algorithm, ADACT (Adjoint-Driven Adaptive Co-Design Thermal Control), that minimizes thermal risk and cooling energy overhead while maximizing core execution throughput. The underlying physical temperature field is governed by a two-dimensional nonhomogeneous parabolic reaction-diffusion equation with spatially localized, time-varying power source terms and variable convective cooling subject to nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We employ a discretization of the continuous state PDE via a Crank-Nicolson finite difference scheme with a 5-point discrete Laplacian operator on a uniform spatial mesh, which preserves unconditional numerical stability and $O(Δx^2 + Δy^2 + Δt^2)$ second-order temporal and spatial accuracy. To efficiently compute exact gradients, we construct and implement a continuous backward-in-time adjoint state method with L-BFGS as our optimization algorithm of choice. The accuracy and second-order convergence rates of both forward state and backward adjoint solvers are quantitatively verified via the Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS), and gradient accuracy is validated using directional derivative Taylor tests. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ADACT dynamically throttles software power workloads and modulates hardware cooling efforts to strictly uphold physical thermal thresholds while maintaining operational throughput.

title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules
abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.

title: A Liouville Theorem for the Real k-Hessian Equation with a One-Sided Growth Condition
abstract: We establish a scale-invariant interior $C^2$ estimate for smooth solutions of the real $k$-Hessian equation. As an application, we prove that every smooth entire solution of $σ_k(D^2u)=1$ satisfying $u(x)\ge b|x|^2-B$ for some constants $b,B$ with $b>0$ is a quadratic polynomial. For smooth solutions, admissibility is forced by the growth condition. The results also hold for viscosity solutions and for weak solutions in Trudinger's sense. Admissibility is required in the latter case.

title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
abstract: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.

title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
abstract: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
abstract: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. The three Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and the local data are Gauduchon--Tod coframes. We determine local equivalence under diffeomorphisms, common closed real $B$-fields and constant rotations of the triple. On a closed manifold the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: a nonzero period obstructs the exact twist required by the non-Riemannian models. The compact structures form four families, distinguished by $b_1=1,2,3,4$: Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. We determine their parameters, equivalences and finite ordered quotients, including nonorientable canonical lines. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable, satisfy $b_2=2b_1-2$, and are symplectic exactly when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. A twisted Hopf example shows why the untwisted hypothesis is essential. The classification is intrinsic and assumes no initial circle action. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type question of Fino and Grantcharov.

title: On the number of pioneers in high-dimensional critical percolation
abstract: We prove that for critical percolation in high dimension the expected number of pioneers on any set containing the origin is of the same order as the probability that a simple random walk starting from the origin exits the set. Our proof works in all dimensions $d>6$, under the usual assumption that the two-point function is of the same order as the Green's function. As an application we obtain a sharp uniform quantitative bound on the probability that the cluster of the origin intersects any given ball.
comment: No use of AI or LLM tools

title: Berry--Esseen bounds for stochastic approximation with Markovian noise
abstract: This paper studies the convergence rate of the Polyak-Ruppert average estimator in one-dimensional linear stochastic approximation recursion driven by Markov chains, allowing the Markov chain to start from any initial distribution. Under the conditions of positive Harris recurrence, non-periodicity, and one-step domination, combined with the fourth-moment condition of the coefficient function with respect to the stationary distribution, this paper uses the exchangeable pair technique to prove that after deterministic bias correction for the average estimator, a Berry--Esseen bound of order $n^{-α/2}$ can be obtained, where the step size exponent is $α\in (1/2, 1)$. Moreover, for the statistics without bias correction and after variance normalization, the asymptotic normal approximation error is asymptotically equivalent to a normal constant multiplied by $n^{1/2 - α}$.

title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

title: Classifying Leibniz racks
abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
abstract: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincaré inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.

title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
abstract: We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing and writes every other correction as a finite combination of product residues with fewer $Y_L$ factors, coming from the word obtained by replacing one negative mode by a nonnegative one. These results hold at all levels $n\ge0$, without an auxiliary-degree hypothesis. For $n\ge1$ and a homogeneous ordered pair $(u,v)$, two explicit triangular families span the quadratic residue operators modulo the length-one and singular-iterate relations, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,v))\le n(n+1)$. The universal product-coefficient arrays have dimension exactly $n(n+1)$ and three natural bases; restriction to the regular mode square is an isomorphism. This proves operator spanning and gives invertible matrices for two complementary diagonal eliminations. For equal inputs, mode interchange reduces the families to their odd-indexed members, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,u))\le 2\lfloor (n+1)^2/4\rfloor$. The pairwise estimates give an explicit global quadratic bound for any finite homogeneous strong generating set. Heisenberg, Virasoro, and affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ examples illustrate equality and strict inequality in the operator bounds.
comment: 43 pages. Companion paper to arXiv:2610.19501 (Part I). Ancillary files: exact-arithmetic Python checks and a note with explicit quadratic recurrences

title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $α$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
abstract: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

title: Geometric aspects of fault tolerance
abstract: We highlight three geometric aspects of fault tolerance. First, we construct an operator-algebraic formulation of the fiber bundle framework for fault tolerance, and show that a generalization of the Knill-Laflamme conditions implies a flat connection for this framework. Next, we develop this framework for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We show that, for each polarization type, their moduli space embeds smoothly into a Grassmannian of finite-dimensional subspaces of a regularized distribution space. Finally, we explain how GKP codes associated with Jacobians give rise to magic states that can be obtained by code space projections of Gaussian states and identify a $\rm CCZ$-type magic state arising this way.

title: Symplectic singularity as hyperKähler cone
abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperKähler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.
comment: 42 pages. cf., Acknowledgements and use of AI

title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
abstract: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

title: Model reduction in time: Learning flow maps for reducing stochastic dynamical systems in time
abstract: Predictions with dynamical systems can be computationally expensive---even with reduced models---because reaching future prediction times can require many sequential time integration steps. We propose Flow-Map First-Order Trajectory Matching (FM-FTM), a nonintrusive model reduction approach that accelerates ensemble predictions of stochastic dynamical systems by learning flow maps that replace multiple time-integration steps. Our method uses first-order trajectory matching (FTM) to learn a deterministic representation of the stochastic probability-current dynamics and then reduces its evolution over time into a flow map whose evaluation directly yields predictions over long time horizons. Numerical experiments on evolution problems with stochastic forcing demonstrate that FM-FTM accelerates ensemble predictions by up to two orders of magnitude while accurately predicting time marginals and ensemble statistics.

title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability
abstract: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.

title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ denote the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of genus-$g$ hyperbolic surfaces with $n$ cusps. Mirzakhani and Zograf obtained a complete asymptotic expansion as $g\to\infty$ for fixed $n$; its terms are effectively powers of $n^2/g$, so it degenerates once $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in inverse powers of the genus that is uniform in all $n\ge0$. The leading term is an explicit saddle-point expression whose saddle moves with the cusp density $n/g$. It has relative error $O(g^{-1})$, and truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$, the leading term confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrtπ$. We also determine the asymptotic profiles of volume ratios, uniformly in the number of cusps, and of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial, uniformly in the degree; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof uses a positive recursion for mixed $κ_1$--$ψ$ intersection numbers, normalized at the pure-$ψ$ endpoint, and a local limit theorem in the number of cusps.
comment: 84 pages, no figures. v2: added uniform boundary and tight-spectrum results; expanded proofs and updated references, including removal of a withdrawn dependency. An earlier version was first made public on Zenodo on 16 October 2026: https://zenodo.org/records/23414478

title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
abstract: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with Hölder continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions. For expected Wasserstein loss, the minimax rate agrees with the rate under uniform covariates and follows from balancing localization bias against unconditional distribution estimation error. Higher moments of the loss can instead be dominated by unobserved covariate regions, which force an additional risk contribution of order $n^{-1}$, where $n$ is the sample size. An adaptive localization argument gives matching upper bounds. The results cover unrestricted response laws and possibly vanishing Besov densities for $W_1$, and extend to higher Wasserstein orders under uniform response density bounds and integrability conditions. A multiscale lower bound closes the logarithmic gap in unconditional $W_1$ minimax rates in dimension two for both unrestricted distributions and Besov density classes. We also establish minimax rates for conditional Brenier maps under density, integrability, and uniform curvature conditions.

title: A Mathematical Murmuration
abstract: We give a summary of a large group activity presented to primary school children as part of a STEAM (STEM plus The Arts) event. We describe the routine we demonstrated, this was based upon the tutting dance form, and the murmuration of starlings. Indeed, this demonstrates movement/dance as both a viable and engaging form of teaching mathematics.

title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
abstract: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

title: Benchmarking quantum-annealing-based approaches for factory layout planning
abstract: The earlystage of factory layout planning has a direct effect on the operating costs, efficiency, and productivity of manufacturing systems. Conventional automated planning approaches often face a trade-off between solution quality and computational effort. Recent studies have investigated the potential of quantum annealing (QA) for solving factory layout planning problems. However, existing studies have mainly focused on individual QA-based formulations, whereas current hybrid QA solvers support multiple model types that combine QA and classical methods. To explore the potential of QA for factory layout planning, this paper benchmarks four QA based approaches implemented with the corresponding solvers, including an iterative binary quadratic model (IBQM), a hybrid discrete quadratic model (HDQM), a hybrid constrained quadratic model (HCQM), and a hybrid nonlinear model (HNLM). To improve scalability, an iterative decomposition strategy is developed for IBQM, while a candidate selection procedure is introduced for HDQM. The approaches are benchmarked against genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, and a hybrid tabu search and simulated annealing approach on 14 layout instances with different layout sizes, geometric complexity, spatial restrictions, and transport route configurations. The comparative analysis considers solution quality, computation time, and scalability. The results show that QA-based approaches achieve competitive solution quality and substantial computational advantages, reducing computation time by up to 94.51% relative to the classical reference methods. Among them, IBQM obtains the best solution quality in 78.6% of the instances, with a maximum improvement of 17.41% associated with an 81.34% reduction in computation time. These findings provide a basis for their further application in industrial layout planning.

title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic Hölder estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.

title: Acceleration of the BSS Algorithm
abstract: Bartel, Schäfer and Ullrich investigated the BSS subsampling algorithm, which is based on the work by Batson, Spielman and Srivastava. While this algorithm works well, the bottleneck is its complexity of $\mathcal{O}(σ^2nm^3)$ for a frame of $n$ vectors of dimension $m$ and oversampling $σ^2$. We continue their work by showing that the algorithm can be implemented in $\mathcal{O}(σ^2nm^{2.5})$. Moreover, for some special cases, an even faster implementation is possible. In particular, BSS subsampling of Fourier-type frames on a full frequency cube can be implemented in essentially $\mathcal{O}(σ^2m^2(n+m^{1.5}))$.}

title: Extremal Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities
abstract: We study the boundedness of extremal 2D Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities. Sufficient conditions for continuously-distributed measures are given in one-sided and two-sided cases.

title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials
abstract: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.

title: The Schur positivity of Lucas binomial differences
abstract: For positive integers $a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, we prove that the Lucas binomial coefficients satisfy $(-1)^{a+1}(L_{b,c}[X]-L_{a,d}[X])\in\mathbb{N}[e_1[X],e_2[X],h_2[X]]$, resolving Bergeron's conjecture on Schur positivity in two variables. We also prove the same positivity for $L_{u,v}[X]-e_1[X]^{uv-rs}L_{r,s}[X]$ when $rs<uv$. Using Lucas atoms, we establish $e$-positivity for degree-adjusted Lucas multinomial differences under dominance order.

title: Poisson closures and Poisson $A$-algebras
abstract: We study the interaction between the Lie and Poisson subalgebras of a Poisson algebra. Given a Lie subalgebra $U$ of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathcal P_L$, we consider the Poisson subalgebra generated by $U$, called its {Poisson closure}, and investigate when Lie-theoretic properties such as nilpotency and solvability are preserved under this construction. We also study the stability under Poisson closure of several distinguished Lie subalgebras, including maximal nilpotent and solvable subalgebras, Engel and Cartan subalgebras and the derived algebra. As an application, we investigate Poisson $A$-algebras, defined by the condition that every nilpotent subalgebra is a zero algebra. In the finite-dimensional case, we obtain structural results relating Poisson $A$-algebras to Lie $A$-algebras and to the associative structure of the algebra.

title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
abstract: We consider Hölder continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.

title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
abstract: In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $λ_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$, with a formal pole at $λ_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series. Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-Δ)^{-1}δ_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(λ)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $λ_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(λ,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
abstract: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.

title: Geometry of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra
abstract: We give a geometric description of the formal local data of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra, the algebra of differential operators in one variable. The exponential part of the associated formal meromorphic connection is encoded by a truncated jet of an affine plane curve at infinity, and the regular part by a regular formal meromorphic connection. We prove that these geometric data uniquely determine the `elementary' blocks in the formal decomposition of holonomic modules. The resulting correspondence is equivariant under automorphisms of the first Weyl algebra, including the Fourier transform.

title: Pentagon Equation in Deformation Quantization of Character Varieties
abstract: Deformation quantizations of the moduli space of framed flat bundles live naturally in the Drinfeld category. Such quantizations were constructed using the so-called quantum fusion by Li-Bland and Ševera. We give a complete characterization of the dependence of this quantization on combinatorial choices, and prove that these quantizations are all isomorphic, forming vertices of an explicitly constructed complete commuting graph of algebra isomorphism. To this end, we extend the Kontsevich integral methods of Le and Murakami from even associators to all associators. Finally, we also prove that bi-invariant Haar measures provide traces on these quantizations.
comment: 42 pages, many figures. First version, comments are welcome

title: Boundary Layer Criterion for the Low Mach Number and Inviscid Limits in Compressible Fluid-Rigid Body Interaction
abstract: We investigate the simultaneous low Mach number and vanishing viscosity limit for a three-dimensional compressible viscous fluid interacting with a freely moving rigid body. The fluid satisfies the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the no-slip condition on the body surface, while the body evolves according to Newton's laws driven by the fluid stresses. We establish convergence of finite-energy weak solutions to a strong solution of the corresponding incompressible Euler-rigid body system on its interval of existence. Assuming that the initial relative energy tends to zero, convergence holds under a Kato-type condition in a boundary layer whose thickness is proportional to the viscosity. This condition combines vanishing viscous dissipation with a weighted estimate on the fluid momentum relative to the rigid body motion. The proof uses the relative entropy method and a boundary layer corrector adapted to the fluid-rigid body coupling, providing a sufficient condition for convergence in relative energy as the Mach number and viscosity tend to zero simultaneously.

title: The role of density in phase transitions and new perspectives on theta functions
abstract: Let $z\in \mathbb{H}:=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Im(z)>0\}$ and $Λ:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Im(z)}}\big({\mathbb Z}\oplus z{\mathbb Z}\big)$, and set $ θ(α;z):=θ(α;Λ)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{-πα\frac{|m+nz|^2}{\Im(z)}}. $ We study the minimization of the functional $θ(α;z)-bθ(2α;z)$ and establish a complete phase diagram for all $α>0$ and $b\in(0,\sqrt{2})$. For $0<b<\sqrt{2}$, an explicit threshold $b_1=0.0767767081\cdots\in(0,1/10)$ separates two distinct types of phase transitions. Type I: $0<b<b_1$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--rhombic--square--rectangular'' phase transition. Type II: $b_1\le b<\sqrt{2}$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--square--rectangular'' phase transition, without passing through the rhombic lattices. These phase transitions contrast with Montgomery's theorem \cite{Mon1988}, where the hexagonal lattice minimizes the single theta function at all scales, and the recent Bétermin-Faulhuber-Steinerberger theorem \cite{BFS2026} for translated Gaussian lattice sums, where the hexagonal lattice prevails in a min-max structure. In our setting, the density parameter $α$ governs the sequence of optimal lattice shapes, while the competition parameter $b$ controls the emergence of the rhombic phase, which exists for $b<b_1$ and vanishes for $b\ge b_1$. As an application, we resolve Bétermin's conjecture \cite{Betermin2021AHP}. Bétermin predicted a Type I phase transition for the functional $θ(α;z)-(1/10)θ(2α;z)$ with $b=1/10$. We instead rigorously establish that no rhombic lattice is a global minimizer at any density and prove that the system undergoes a Type II phase transition, thereby settling the conjecture in corrected form.

title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.

title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
abstract: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schrödinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\logφ_1)>g$ and $λ_2-λ_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.

title: Gevrey Regularity for a Sum of Two Squares in Two Variables
abstract: We study the Gevrey hypoellipticity of a sum of two squares in two variables, satisfying the Hörmander hypothesis, assuming that the function, $ q $, describing (the space projection of) its characteristic variety vanishes only at a single point, which can be assumed to be the origin. A hypoellipticity result is given in a Gevrey class, depending on $ q $. In some examples the found regularity is known to be optimal.

title: The sparse regularity method for graphs with few even-cycle homomorphisms
abstract: Let $C_k$ denote a cycle on $k$ vertices. Pascadi (2026) established a removal lemma for $C_{2k+1}$ in graphs with few $C_{2k}$-homomorphisms under a dense-pairs condition, using Schatten--von Neumann norms and entropy methods. We give a short proof of a version with more restrictive partition and diagonal requirements, extending the combinatorial approach of Conlon, Fox, Sudakov and Zhao (2021) without using Pascadi's Schatten-norm regularity framework. We illustrate the method with a known sparse removal statement for odd product equations in finite groups.

title: A framework for trackable and modular rounding error analysis
abstract: Robust and meaningful rounding error analysis is becoming increasingly challenging as modern numerical computations involve a rapidly evolving variety of arithmetic formats, precisions, and computational kernels. We propose a trackable and modular framework for rounding error analysis, together with a new notation for bounding accumulated rounding errors. The analysis is trackable in the sense that the origin and propagation of individual error terms remain explicit in the final result, and modular in the sense that local error bounds can be replaced according to the arithmetic, precision, or computational kernel without repeating the structural analysis. We also introduce the notation $γ_n=(1-{\bm u})^{-n}-1$, which provides an alternative to the classical $γ_n^{\mathrm h}=n{\bm u}/(1-n{\bm u})$ notation. A key feature is that our notation does not require the restriction $n{\bm u}<1$ and conveniently handles errors arising from division. Using block LU factorization as a representative example, we show that the framework distinguishes the error sources of different algorithmic variants and permits improved kernels, such as compensated summation and accurate matrix multiplication, to be incorporated directly into the resulting error bounds.

title: Antimagic Labeling of Central Digraphs Constructed from Loops
abstract: Let $(T, \circ)$ be a loop of order $k \geq 3$ and $D_S^*$ the loopless central digraph obtained from the associated central digraph $D_S$ by removing the $k$ self-loops at the diagonal vertices. We construct an explicit arc-labeling $f$ of $D_S^*$ ordering all arcs lexicographically by $(\text{tail}, \text{head})$ and assigning labels $1, \ldots, m$ in that order and prove that $f$ is an antimagic labeling. Consequently, $D_S$ is antimagic for every loop of order $k \geq 3$, a property that depends only on $k$ and is invariant across all non-isomorphic loops of the same order.

title: Solvability and nilpotence of ind-groups via tangent curves
abstract: Answering a question of Kraft and the second-named author, we prove that a connected ind-group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is solvable, respectively nilpotent, if and only if its Lie algebra is. Their derived lengths, respectively nilpotency classes, coincide. We also obtain bounds on the derived length and nilpotency class for regular linear representations of connected ind-groups and for subgroups generated by connected algebraic subgroups. As an application, we give a new proof of the geometric case of a theorem of Belabbas: a solvable Lie algebra of vector fields on an affine variety generated by finitely many locally finite Lie subalgebras is locally finite and finite dimensional.

title: Compact linear combination of composition operators on weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights
abstract: Let $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ be the weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights $ω$ on the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Suppose Orlicz function $Ψ$ satisfies the $Δ_{2}$-condition. In this paper, the compactness of finite linear combination of composition operators on $A^Ψ_ω(\mathbb{D})$ are completely characterized in terms of Julia-Carathéodory type conditions and vanishing Carleson measure, respectively.

title: Modular Existential Closedness
abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(τ_1, \ldots, τ_n, j(τ_1), \ldots, j(τ_n)) \in V$ with $τ_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouché's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

title: A characterization of graphs attaining a lower bound on the dissociation number
abstract: The dissociation number ${\rm diss}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is defined as the maximum cardinality of a vertex subset $D\subseteq V(G)$ such that the induced subgraph $G[D]$ has maximum degree at most $1$. In 2023, Bock, Pardey, Penso and Rautenbach [J. Graph Theory 103 (2023), 661--673] showed that ${\rm diss}(G)\ge n-\frac{1}{3}(m+k+c_1)$ where $n, m, k, c_1$ denote the numbers of vertices, edges, components and induced cycles of length $1$ modulo $3$ in $G$ and they also established a complete characterization of extremal graphs under the vertex-disjoint cycle constraint. Although this partial characterization offers very valuable structural insights, it excludes many simple extremal graphs. So they posed a natural question: How can all extremal graphs be comprehensively characterized without restrictions? In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of all graphs attaining equality in this bound.
comment: Dissociation sets; dissociation number; maximum; extremal graphs

title: Distribution of the First Hitting Point on a Boundary Set for a Random Walk in a Lattice Strip
abstract: We consider a time-homogeneous random walk in a strip of a two-dimensional lattice whose transition probabilities are invariant under shifts along one of the coordinates. We study the limiting distribution of the first hitting point into a boundary set as the initial condition tends to infinity. Explicit expressions are obtained for this limiting distribution for negative and zero mean drift.

title: Quantitative approximation theorem of neural operators for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
abstract: In this paper, we study neural operators for the Dirichet-to-Neumann map (DN map), which is encountered in the famous Calderón's problem. In many numerical methods used for reconstructing the unknown conductivity from the knowledge of the DN map need to evaluate the corresponding DN map at a given conductivity function, which involves solving the boundary value problem for the conductivity equation and taking the Neumann data. Such procedure is time consuming and not effective. Hence, it is a favorable strategy to construct a surrogate to replace the forward map mapping conductivity functions to corresponding DN maps. The main theme of this paper is to derive quantitative bounds on the parametric complexity of these neural operators. In particular, under suitable assumptions, their depth grows at most logarithmically with $\varepsilon^{-1}$, while the relevant spectral and projection ranks grow algebraically. It should be noted that general neural operators suffer from "the curse of parametric dimensionality". This work demonstrates the construction of neural operators for the DN map that does not suffer from such curse.

title: Periodic dynamics of transonic shocks in Euler-Poisson flows
abstract: This paper studies the existence and dynamical stability of time-periodic transonic shock solutions to the one-dimensional Euler--Poisson equations under periodic boundary perturbations. The analysis relies on two key mechanisms: the structural dissipation induced by the transonic shock and the stabilization effect of the positive electric field on the shock position. Using a reformulation of the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions and uniform estimates on the flow and shock perturbations, we establish the existence of a time-periodic transonic shock solution. We further prove its dynamical stability under small perturbations of the initial data.

title: The quermassintegral inequalities for k-convex spiral-star-shaped domains
abstract: We extend the quermassintegral inequalities of our earlier work \cite{GuanLi2009} from star-shaped domains to a substantially broader class of domains in Euclidean space, which we call spiral-star-shaped. A smooth domain is spiral-star-shaped if its boundary satisfies \[ \langle X+A X,ν\rangle>0 \] for some fixed skew-symmetric linear map $ A$, where $X$ is the position vector and $ν$ is the outward unit normal. The vector field $X+A X$ is conformal Killing, with dilation component $X$ and rotational component $A X$; its trajectories combine expansion and rotation, giving rise to the spiral terminology. When $A=0$, it reduces to ordinary star-shapedness, while nonzero $A$ allows domains that are not star-shaped in the usual radial sense. For smooth $k$-convex spiral-star-shaped domains, we prove long-time existence and exponential convergence to a round sphere for a locally constrained inverse curvature flow. The positive spiral support function provides the geometric control needed to treat initial hypersurfaces that need not be star-shaped in the usual sense. Monotonicity of the quermassintegrals along the flow yields sharp quermassintegral inequalities in this enlarged class, with equality if and only if the domain is a ball.

title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
abstract: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. When statistical degeneracy occurs an Active Design of Experiments (DoE) controller dynamically triggers targeted perturbations to decorrelate competing model hypotheses. Evaluated on a continuous stirred-tank reactor exhibiting unmodeled Haldane inhibition, Luong product toxicity, and secondary metabolite autocatalysis, the framework autonomously expanded the state space and recovered ground-truth parameters with under 6% error without a priori kinetic knowledge.

title: Square-Root Clustered Lasso for High-Dimensional Linear Regression with Finite-Sample Theory and Efficient Algorithm Implementation
abstract: This paper proposes a square-root clustered Lasso penalized method for high-dimensional linear regression. By integrating square-root loss with the clustered Lasso penalty, the resulting method enables flexible regression modeling and allows tuning parameter selection independent of the unknown noise level. We establish weak decomposability of the clustered Lasso penalty and a noise-level-free tuning strategy under Gaussian noise. Furthermore, we establish the finite-sample prediction accuracy guarantees for the proposed method. The inherent nonsmoothness of the square-root loss and clustered Lasso penalty poses considerable computational difficulties. To resolve this issue, we develop an efficient semismooth Newton-based proximal augmented Lagrangian algorithm (N-ALM) to solve the corresponding dual optimization problem. The subproblems arising in the iteration are efficiently tackled by the semismooth Newton method, which fully utilizes the sparsity structure of the generalized Jacobian.
