title: The Symmetry of Differential Neural Tangent Kernel under the Orthogonal Group
abstract: The differential neural tangent kernel (DNTK) is a tool for analyzing the training dynamics of overparameterized physics informed neural networks. In this work, we investigate the symmetry of the infinite DNTK under an orthogonal group, for two layer and deep neural networks separately, based on the explicit expression of the DNTK and recursive formula, respectively. The results are for all activations with or without a bias term, and shed insight into the structure of the infinite width DNTK. Then we prove that the integral operators over the unit sphere induced by operators from the same group orbit share the spectrum, and their reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces differ only by an orthogonal transformation, and that the operator fixed DNTK exhibits zonal symmetry on the unit sphere for symmetric operators. Thus the eigenvalue decay rate of the associated integral operator can be derived for shallow networks with RePU activation and zero bias initialization.

title: Derived products and completion defects of inverse limits
abstract: We compute derived products and inverse limits in Grothendieck categories by exact coresolutions. For the product of $r$ doubled affine lines over $B[s]$, where $B$ is any nonzero commutative ring,the exact dimensions of products, epimorphic countable limits, and arbitrary countable limits are $r$, $r$, and $r+1$. We identify the top derived functors for every $B$-module of coefficients. Both obstruction modules contain the countable reduced product as a natural $B$-module direct summand, and a formal-series map relates them by an explicit cokernel sequence. A relative cofree coresolution gives degree shifts over an arbitrary Grothendieck category and computes the localization defect for arbitrary locally nilpotent diagrams. We also construct transfinite scalar extensions preserving a prescribed kernel and its derived limit;these give nonzero completion defects beyond any fixed ordinal.The general epimorphic top-degree vanishing question is not settled by these constructions.

title: Hyponormal and subnormal dual Toeplitz operators
abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize hyponormal dual Toeplitz operators with general bounded measurable symbols by using the Douglas theorem in [R. G. Douglas, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (1966), 413-415]. As an application, the hyponormality of dual Toeplitz operators with radial symbols and polynomial symbols in $z$ and $\bar{z}$ is characterized concretely. Moreover, we obtain complete characterizations for both subnormal dual Toeplitz operators with harmonic polynomial symbols and $\varTheta$-class dual Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols.

title: MDS codes containing a fixed subcode over finite field extensions
abstract: Let $2\le k\le n$ and let $U\le\mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a fixed $(k-1)$-dimensional linear code. We study the $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) codes over finite extensions of $\mathbb{F}_q$ that contain the scalar extension of $U$. Our approach constructs an auxiliary linear code from \(U\). Its full-weight words characterize the desired MDS completions. We prove that \(U\) admits an \([n,k]\) MDS completion over some finite extension of \(\mathbb{F}_q\) if and only if \(d(U)\ge n-k+1\). When this condition holds, the number of these MDS codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ is \[\#\left\{W\le\mathbb{F}_{q^m}^n:U\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^m}\subseteq W,\ \dim_{\mathbb{F}_{q^m}} W=k,\ W\text{ is MDS}\right\}=\frac{χ_{δ_GM(G)}(q^m)}{q^m-1},\] where $G$ is a generator matrix of $U$, $δ_GM(G)$ is its represented derived matroid, and $χ_{δ_GM(G)}$ is its characteristic polynomial. In particular, the formula determines existence over each extension field and the least extension degree for which such an MDS code exists. Examples show that these counts may distinguish different representations of the same column matroid, while monomially inequivalent codes may have identical counts over every finite extension.

title: Integrable distortion II: the p-Weil-Petersson variational problem
abstract: We study the hyperbolically weighted distortion energies \[ \mathcal{I}_p(f)=\int_\mathbb{D} \frac{|μ_f|^p}{(1-|μ_f|^2)^{\max\{2,p\}/2}}\,dA_η\] for finite-distortion disk homeomorphisms with prescribed boundary values, together with the associated inverse problem in the monotone Sobolev class. For $1<p\leq2$, the inverse density is polyconvex precisely when $p\geq p_{\mathrm c}=1+1/\sqrt2$. In this range, quasisymmetric data with finite-energy monotone barriers yield minimisers with holomorphic Ahlfors--Hopf differentials and strong local Sobolev convergence of minimising subsequences. For $p_{\mathrm c}<p<2$, a finite-energy finite-distortion barrier yields a unique absolute monotone minimiser, which is a quasiconformal diffeomorphism and is asymptotically conformal. Together with the boundary-class theorem of Part~I, this characterises the admissible boundary data as $T^p$. The proof combines a selected barrier approximation, uniform scalar gradient estimates and a weighted Reich--Strebel comparison. For $1<p<p_{\mathrm c}$, finite rank-one comparisons bound distortion on the positive-Jacobian set by a cutoff strictly below the ellipticity cutoff. An attained monotone minimum is either a quasiconformal diffeomorphism or has nonzero rank-one derivatives on a set of positive area. For $0<p\leq1$, minimisers with finite distortion, or homeomorphic minimisers with a locally Sobolev inverse, are Möbius maps. We also obtain energy-dependent quasiconformal bounds for regular minimisers when $p>2$. \

title: Extreme proxies for causal identification: deconfounding with outliers
abstract: Causal identification under unobserved confounding typically relies on additional structure, such as a valid instrument or proxy variables. We show that heavy tailed variables offer an alternative route to identification by revealing treatment variation for which confounding becomes asymptotically negligible. Our key assumption is extreme propagation: when an unobserved confounder takes an extreme value, some observed variable in the system (called a safeguard) will become extreme with large probability. This way, selecting extreme treatment observations while safeguards remain non-extreme makes confounding asymptotically negligible relative to the treatment. We call this certification. We derive graphical conditions specifying which latent confounders must be monitored by safeguards and distributional conditions ensuring effective certification. The framework includes valid-instrument and double-proxy structures as special cases, as well as confounded instruments that are invalid in most approaches that do not exploit heavy tails. Geometrically, certification isolates the extremal ray whose slope equals the causal effect. This connects causal identification with multivariate extreme-value geometry and motivates a family of novel simple estimators. Simulations demonstrate performance gains under nonlinear confounding and heavy tails, while revealing limitations in light-tailed regimes (where cancellation can conceal extreme confounding from the safeguards). We validate our methodology in simulation studies and by recovering the ground-truth flow in a river discharge application.

title: Regularity and selfless cp maps
abstract: We investigate the regularity properties of C*-algebras admitting a weakly selfless unital completely positive map.

title: Maximal Spaceability of the set of non-absolutely summing operators in quasi-Banach spaces
abstract: For every $0<p<1$, we establish maximal spaceability of the bounded operators on $\ell_p$ which fail to be $(r,s)$-absolutely summing for all $1\le s\le r<\infty$, using the coordinate-disjointization construction and Maddox's theorem. We give detailed isometric estimates and prove a corresponding maximal spaceability theorem inside the compact operators. The compact result is based on an explicit diagonal multiplier and a single weakly $1$-summable sequence witnessing the simultaneous failure of all admissible absolute summability conditions. A diagonal characterization, a logarithmic compact example, and extensions to operators with values in quasi-Banach spaces containing a copy of $\ell_p$ are also obtained. The constructed subspaces are isomorphic to $\ell_p$ and have maximal algebraic dimension whenever the ambient operator spaces have dimension $\mathfrak c$.
comment: Accepted for publication in the Journal of the Iranian Mathematical Society (JIMS)

title: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
abstract: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_θ\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_θ^\sharp\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{θ,λ\in(0,\infty)}λ^p \underset{\mathcal M_θ(f)(x,t)>λt^γ} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{γp-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{α_{p,γ}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-n,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $γ$. For $\mathcal M_θ^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-1,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $α_{p,γ}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $γ\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

title: A variational model with finite carrying capacity for segregated multi-species populations in the whole Euclidean space
abstract: We study a variational problem motivated by models of multiple segregated species in a nonhomogeneous environment. The analysis combines tools from potential theory, in particular free boundary methods. The main novelty is that we formulate the variational problem in the whole Euclidean space while imposing a finite carrying capacity constraint, which allows us to investigate saturated regions where the species attain their maximal density. In addition, we provide a modeling interpretation of the constrained energy. We show that it arises as the variational limit of energies with increasingly strong crowding and interspecific competition penalties, in the sense that, regardless of their relative rates, every sequence of minimizers of the penalized energies admits a subsequence that converges strongly to a minimizer of the constrained energy.

title: Transport by rough vector fields
abstract: The Cauchy-Lipschitz theorem guarantees that the ODE $\dotγ= b(t,γ)$ is well-posed if $b$ is Lipschitz in space, an assumption too restrictive for applications such as fluid mechanics. In 1989, DiPerna and Lions extended the theory to Sobolev vector fields with bounded divergence. Well-posedness then holds not for individual trajectories but for regular Lagrangian flows: flows that solve the ODE for almost every initial point and compress volume by at most a bounded factor. Their method rests on renormalized solutions of the associated transport equation. This thesis is primarily expository: it presents the DiPerna-Lions theory with detailed proofs. We treat existence, uniqueness and stability of weak and renormalized solutions of the transport equation, deduce existence (for autonomous fields) and uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows, and discuss applications to the two-dimensional Euler equations. Three counterexamples with divergence-free fields show that uniqueness can fail without a growth condition at infinity, if $b$ has only fractional Sobolev regularity (due to DiPerna and Lions), or for $L^1$ solutions when $\nabla b \in L^r$, $r<d$ (the simplest case of a recent construction by Bruè, Colombo and Kumar). Contributions are (1) smooth approximations of $b$ with uniformly bounded divergence for the existence proof; (2) a direct proof of the known uniqueness of regular Lagrangian flows from uniqueness for the continuity equation; (3) a construction of the auxiliary cube-translating field in the example of Bruè, Colombo and Kumar that works for all $d \ge 2$, replacing an extension from two dimensions that is not a vector field on $\mathbb R^d$ for $d \ge 3$.

title: On the elliptic Hall category
abstract: In this paper we study (the positive half of) the elliptic Hall category, a categorical version of the elliptic Hall algebra. Our main result is a computation of categorical versions of the generators in the coherent realization of the elliptic Hall category, i.e., via coherent sheaves on commuting stacks for $\operatorname{GL}_n\times \mathfrak{gl}_n$: we realize them as Hodge associated graded sheaves of certain twisted equivariant $D$-modules on the groups $\operatorname{GL}_n$.

title: Fine points of the moduli space of cubic rational maps
abstract: A rational point of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}_3$ of cubic rational maps is fine if its conjugacy class contains a map defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and coarse otherwise. In the invariants $ξ_0,\dots,ξ_5$ that embed $\mathcal{M}_3$ in $\mathbb{P}(2,2,3,3,4,6)$, we prove that a point with trivial automorphism group is fine if and only if the quaternion algebra $(-m_{12},-2ξ_0)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ splits, where $m_{12}=\frac{1}{3}ξ_0^2ξ_1+ξ_0ξ_4-ξ_3^2$; we give the analogous criterion on the locus $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution and show that all other strata are fine. The proof is constructive and yields an explicit descent. We prove that the obstruction class is unramified along every divisor of the compactification, that a prime $p\ge 5$ obstructs only if the point reduces modulo $p$ into the closure of one of the two codimension-two loci $\mathcal{L}_1$, $\mathcal{L}_2$ of maps with an involution, and that $\mathcal{M}_3$ has transverse $A_1$-singularities along both, above which the class ramifies; local densities predict that $\mathcal{L}_2$ is met modulo $p$ with probability $\asymp 1/p$, so that it carries the obstruction. A census of all 214,260,288 rational points of weighted moduli height at most 7 agrees with this mechanism and supports the conjecture that the proportion of fine points tends to zero like $(\log B)^{-1/2}$.

title: Spectrality of convolution and product measures: a block decomposition approach
abstract: We study the spectrality of convolution and product measures. Let~$μ$~be a compactly supported Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$~such that ~$\mathcal{Z}(\widehatμ)\cup\{0\}=T$~is an additive subgroup, and let~$ν$~be a Borel probability measure on~$\Bbb{R}^d$. We prove that~$μ*ν$~is spectral if and only if~$T$~is a spectrum of~$μ$, ~$ν$~is spectral, and~$suppν$~is contained in a translate of the annihilator of~$T$. Moreover, every spectrum of~$μ*ν$~decomposes into full cosets of~$T$, and every choice of one point from each coset is a spectrum of~$ν$. We also obtain a convolution-factor criterion which strengthens a result of Wu. As applications, we characterize the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]}*ν$~and prove that the spectrality of~$L_{[0,1]^d}*ν$~implies that of~$ν$~without a compact support assumption. For product measures, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for an orthogonal set to be a spectrum by relating its block structure to spectra of the factors. No compact support assumptions are required.

title: A note on $σ_k$ maximal conformal volume
abstract: We establish a sharp spherical upper bound for the $σ_k$-maximal conformal volume $Λ_k$ introduced by Gursky and Viaclovsky. Let $(M^n,[g])$ be a smooth, closed, connected conformal manifold with $n\geq 3$ and $n/2<k\leq n$, and suppose that $[g]$ contains a $k$-admissible metric, we prove that $ Λ_k(M,[g]) \leq \operatorname{Vol}(\mathbb S^n,g_{\mathrm{rd}}), $ with equality if and only if $(M,[g])$ is conformally equivalent to the standard sphere. Combined with the existence and compactness theorem of Gursky and Viaclovsky below the spherical threshold, this completes their approach to the $σ_k$-Yamabe problem through maximal conformal volume in the range $k>n/2$.

title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

title: On 2-Arc-Transitive Cayley Graphs of Nonabelian Characteristically Simple Groups
abstract: The classification of symmetric Cayley graphs has attracted considerable attention. Results have been obtained for finite abelian groups and nonabelian simple groups. However, the problem remains open for finite nonabelian characteristically simple groups, although some results on normality for small valencies are known. In this paper, we determine the possible structures of automorphism groups $X$ of connected 2-arc-transitive Cayley graphs $Γ$ of $G\cong T^k$, where $T$ is a finite nonabelian simple group and $k\geqslant2$. In the quasiprimitive case, we prove that $G\unlhd X$, $Γ$ is complete, or $X$ is of product action type with restricted parameters. For the non-quasiprimitive case, we determine the possible structures of the quasiprimitive normal quotients of $Γ$.

title: Explicit weighing matrices $W(n,k)$ for all $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ with $4 \le n \le 108$, and all $1 \le k \le n$
abstract: We present an explicit weighing matrix $W(n,k)$ for every order $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ with $4\le n\le 108$ and every weight $1\le k\le n$: 1512 matrices in total, each checked in exact integer arithmetic. Of these, 961 come from classical constructions (identity, direct sums, Kronecker products, Paley matrices and skew-Hadamard doubling) and 551 are Goethals-Seidel matrices, found by exhaustive search (24 matrices, $n\le 24$) or by simulated annealing on the periodic autocorrelation cost (527 matrices, $n\ge 28$). The note is self-contained as far as the methods are concerned: it presents all the construction methods used and the algorithm that selects among them, explains the algorithm step by step, proves every identity on which the constructions rely, and illustrates each method with a matrix taken from the catalogue. It does not reproduce the 1512 matrices, which are available in the repository. It also gives a short parity obstruction to Goethals-Seidel matrices $W(4m,4m-1)$ with $m$ even, and lists the generating sequences of thirteen matrices whose parameters appear as unresolved in historical tables consulted by the author; their status in the current literature is still being checked, and no claim of priority is made.
comment: 32 pages. Code and data: https://github.com/adrianmaciasquintero/weighing-matrices (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23484194)

title: A Pythagoras Tree Grown from a Dodecahedron
abstract: The Pythagoras tree of A. E. Bosman (1942) is drawn with squares in the plane and, in the three-dimensional versions we know of, with cubes. This article documents a tree built instead from regular dodecahedra: each dodecahedron carries five smaller copies, one on each edge of a single pentagonal "crown" face, scaled by $g \approx 0.4346$ and twisted by $45^\circ$ about the edge. The construction first existed only as a pair of rendered images and two undocumented C++ programs. We recover its exact parameters from the original Blender scene, reformulate it as an iterated function system with condensation, and prove with a short computer-assisted argument that it never collides with itself: two of its dodecahedra overlap only when one is the parent of the other. A Pythagorean identity for the six face axes of the dodecahedron singles out the scale $1/\sqrt{5}$ and the twist $\arccos(1/\sqrt{5})$. With these values each child rests flat against a face of its parent, the five children together have exactly the parent's surface area, and the crown of the tree is a fractal of Hausdorff dimension exactly 2. Finally we ask whether the tree can grow on all twelve faces at once. A parity argument shows that at the artwork's proportions it cannot, but smaller scale factors admit certified clash-free all-faces trees.

title: Swirl ill-posedness for incompressible fluids in (sub)critical spaces
abstract: For the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with sufficiently smooth initial data having zero swirl $u_{0θ}\equiv 0$, Ladyzhenskaya \cite{L1968} and Ukhovskii and Yudovich \cite{UY1968} established global regularity. It has since remained open as to whether well-posedness still holds for smooth axisymmetric initial data, with the initial swirl being smaller than an \textit{absolute} constant in a critical space. In this remark, we prove \textit{norm inflation} occurs for the Navier-Stokes scalar swirl component, with initial smallness in the critical space $\dot{H}^{\frac{1}{2}}$ or even subcritical Sobolev spaces. We also obtain norm inflation for the 3D Euler swirl \textit{vector} in the Euler subcritical space $\dot{H}^3$. Our results are achieved by introducing an anisotropic scale in Luo's supercritical norm inflation construction \cite{Luo24}, as well as performing an anisotropic bootstrap argument to get a sufficiently small swirl remainder term.

title: Hodge--Deligne polynomials and $S_n$-representations on the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$
abstract: We compute the Hodge-Deligne polynomials of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus two, together with the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on their cohomology, for all $n$. Using Hassett's moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we first show that the generating function of the $S_n$-equivariant Hodge-Deligne polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ is obtained from that of the moduli spaces of minimally weighted pointed curves by plethysm with the explicit symmetric function $Z=h_1-\sum_{k\ge3}(x+x^2+\dots+x^{k-2})h_k$; numerically, this is an explicit change of variables. The latter spaces map to $\overline{\mathcal M}_g$, and over each boundary stratum they are built from punctured universal curves and Losev-Manin spaces. Combining the stratification by stable graphs with Burnside's formula and twisted characteristics, we obtain in genus two a closed formula whose only non-elementary input is the cohomology of symplectic local systems on $\mathcal M_{1,1}$ and $\mathscr A_2$, known by work of Eichler-Shimura and Petersen. This determines the $S_n$-representations on all $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for $n\le 19$ and on all even degree $H^{p,q}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for every $n$. We carry out the computation in all degrees for $n\le 18$, where it agrees with an independent computation by point counts, and in even degrees for $n\le 30$. As an application, we find that the even degree cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}$ is of Hodge-Tate type if and only if $n\le 20$: the space $H^{23,1}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is the multiplicity free $S_{21}$-representation with Frobenius characteristic $s_1\cdot h_2[e_{10}]$, of dimension $1939938$, so that $H^{24}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,21})$ is not spanned by algebraic cycle classes.

title: Explicit Coleman integration over finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
abstract: Coleman integration is an important computational ingredient of the Chabauty--Coleman method and its extensions. We extend the Balakrishnan--Tuitman algorithm to general smooth projective curves with good reduction over arbitrary finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, allowing both ramification and nontrivial residue degree. Given a suitable plane model and integral bases, we provide explicit precision bounds and an accompanying Magma implementation. As an application, a single-prime computation at $p=19$ over the unramified quadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}_{19^2}/\mathbb{Q}_{19}$ recovers all $35$ affine sporadic quadratic divisors on $X(s3,ns5)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Completeness is proved in an appendix using symmetric Chabauty and a Mordell--Weil sieve.

title: Nilpotent Lie algebras of nilpotence class at most three via graphs
abstract: In this work, we associate with each finite simple graph $G$ a nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}_G$ of class at most three, whose underlying vector space has a basis indexed by the vertices, edges, and paths of length two of $G$. Its nilpotency class is exactly three if and only if $G$ contains a path of length two. We compute the dimensions of its lower central series and describe its center. Over fields of characteristic different from two, we prove that two such Lie algebras are isomorphic if and only if their underlying graphs are isomorphic. We also give an algebraic description using quotients involving exterior and symmetric squares. Finally, we study balanced blow-ups and prove that $\mathfrak{n}_G$ is a retract of $\mathfrak{n}_{G^{(m)}}$.

title: Global $c^{1,α}$ regularity and fine behavior at critical points for quasilinear elliptic equations with Orlicz growth and unbounded drift
abstract: We investigate the global regularity up to the boundary and the fine pointwise behavior along the critical set for bounded weak solutions to general quasilinear elliptic Dirichlet problems in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. Our structural framework encompasses operators with non-standard Lieberman-type growth alongside lower-order terms featuring natural gradient growth, an unbounded source term in $L^q$, and an unbounded spatial drift weight in $L^s$. To overcome the analytical obstructions posed by the unbounded drift across the anisotropic growth gap, we first establish global Hölder continuity up to the boundary via Moser iteration. We then construct a novel smooth regularization scheme for general homogeneous constant-coefficient operators, merging the approximation frameworks of Lieberman and Cianchi-Maz'ya, to derive global $C^{1,α}$ regularity up to the boundary through a variational perturbation approach. Building upon this global theory, we employ a geometric compactness and blow-up argument to prove that at any interior or boundary critical point where the gradient vanishes, the solution achieves an improved pointwise $C^{1,α}$ regularity. Remarkably, at boundary critical points, this quantitative improvement decouples from the lower-order terms and completely bypasses both the boundary datum regularity and the domain smoothness. Finally, we discuss the sharpness of the integrability threshold required for the unbounded drift weight in the subcritical regime.

title: A Nonconvex Framework for Joint Sparse Sample Weighting and Parameter Estimation
abstract: We propose a joint sparse sample weighting and parameter estimation (SWAPE) framework that jointly optimizes model parameters and sample weights to train a model while simultaneously assigning an individual weight to each training data point. Our framework accommodates several widely used loss functions for the model parameters, including convex, weakly convex, and difference-of-convex loss, and weakly convex sparsity functions to control the complexity of the sample weights. To solve the resulting bivariate problem, we propose an alternating minimization method in which the subproblems for updating the model parameters and weights are each approximated using majorize-minimize techniques. We provide several approximation methods for the loss functions considered in this paper, and show the overall algorithm's convergence. Numerical experiments on various learning tasks and data anomaly settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in minimizing the impact of undesirable data points compared to benchmark methods.

title: Asymptotic stability of transonic steady nozzle flows
abstract: In the present article, we prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of stationary solutions to the quasi-one-dimensional barotropic Euler equations in a finite-length nozzle with variable cross-sectional area $A(x)$. We consider all stationary flow configurations arising from subsonic inflow: flows that remain subsonic throughout the nozzle, flows that pass continuously through a sonic state and remain supersonic up to the exit, and flows that subsequently return to the subsonic regime through a stationary shock. We prove that all these stationary solutions are asymptotically stable with respect to sufficiently small perturbations. No smallness restrictions are imposed on the mass flux, the magnitude of $A_x$, or the prescribed exit pressure, provided that the corresponding stationary solution exists. The only geometrical assumptions are that $A_{xx}>0$ at a smooth subsonic--supersonic transition, and $A_x>0$ at a stationary supersonic--subsonic shock. To the best of our knowledge, this gives the first nonlinear asymptotic stability result for a stationary flow passing smoothly from the subsonic to the supersonic regime in a finite-length nozzle. The principal analytical difficulty is the degeneracy of the characteristic structure at the sonic point. We overcome this difficulty by coupling energy structures adapted respectively to the subsonic and supersonic regimes. This coupling provides the dissipation needed to control the smooth sonic transition, and when combined with the dynamics of the shock, yields a unified nonlinear stability framework for smooth and discontinuous transonic nozzle flows.

title: Delta Characters and Ranks of Minimal Subisocrystals of Abelian Schemes
abstract: Using the framework of delta characters on arithmetic jet spaces, we construct a canonical sequence of filtered isocrystals associated to an abelian scheme $A$ of relative dimension $g$ over a $p$-adically complete discrete valuation ring. These isocrystals map injectively via a canonical morphism into the first (rational) crystalline cohomology group $\mathbf{H}^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A)$ of the abelian scheme $A$, directly generalizing a prior construction due to Borger and Saha. Pandit showed that the canonical morphism is a map of isocrystals. This then implies that the image of this canonical embedding coincides with the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ containing the space of invariant differential forms $H^0(A,Ω_A)$. Berthelot and Ogus showed that the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is $g$ if and only if $A$ has an endomorphism that lifts the absolute Frobenius on the special fiber of $A$. As a primary application, for a general abelian scheme $A$, we show that the minimal subisocrystal $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ can be viewed as a module obtained from primitive delta characters of $A$ via appropriate twists by the canonical Frobenius morphism $φ$ induced from the theory of arithmetic jet spaces. As a consequence, we show that the rank of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ depends on numerical invariants arising from the theory of delta characters of $A$. More precisely, the dimension of $F_{\mathrm{cris}}(Ω_A)$ is given by the sum of the exact orders of the primitive delta characters associated to the abelian scheme $A$.

title: Extrinsic Curvature Estimation by Closest Point Projection of Rays
abstract: We propose a parametrization-free framework for estimating the second fundamental form and the principal curvatures of a submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The method uses the closest point projections of a few short random rays and recovers the curvature from the curves that these projections induce on the submanifold, without coordinate charts or local fitting. We analyze the geometry of the induced curves and characterize when they are geodesics. For hypersurfaces, these results give two algorithms with error bounds: a least squares reconstruction of the second fundamental form from the curvatures of the induced curves, and a direct estimate of all principal curvatures from the eigenvalues of a $d\times d$ matrix built from $d$ rays, which needs no normal information and costs $\mathcal{O}(d^3)$ besides the projections. In higher codimension, we can also recover the second fundamental form one normal direction at a time. On point clouds, where the projection becomes a nearest neighbor query, we bound the additional error. Experiments confirm the predicted rates for hypersurfaces in up to $128$ dimensions, for surfaces of codimension up to $98$, and on point clouds, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework in practice.

title: An optimization-based property-preserving limiter for two-phase flow in porous media on non-matching meshes
abstract: Two-phase flow in porous media arises in a wide range of applications in engineering and science. A fundamental challenge in its numerical simulation is that the approximation of the saturation transport equation can violate the maximum principle, and spurious oscillations can appear even when the solution remains within physical bounds. In this work, we propose a bound-preserving anti-oscillation postprocessing limiter for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of the two-phase flow system on non-matching meshes. An optimization-based cell average limiter enforces the prescribed bounds on the cell averages while preserving global mass by minimizing the $L^2$ distance to the original cell averages. To suppress the remaining oscillations, the cell average limiter is combined with a minmod limiter, which is activated only in the cells identified by a troubled-cell detector to avoid unnecessary loss of accuracy, and a Zhang-Shu scaling limiter subsequently enforces the bounds on point values. In addition, we prove that the cell average limiter preserves the accuracy of the numerical solution at a fixed time on non-matching meshes. Numerical experiments on homogeneous, non-homogeneous, and fractured porous media demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method.

title: Berezin Transform Commutators
abstract: We study commutators of Berezin transforms $\mathcal B_α$ associated with radial weighted Fock spaces with exponential weights $e^{-α|z|^{m}}$ on the complex plane. We prove that when $m>2$, the commutator $[\mathcal B_α,\mathcal B_β]$ is compact on the space $L^{2}(\mathbb C, dA)$ whenever $α,β>0$. We further show that if $m>2$ and $α\neqβ$, then the commutator is never of finite rank.

title: EnerGNN: Learning Optimization-Compatible Energy Functions for Exact Constrained Combinatorial Inference
abstract: Learning-based approaches to combinatorial optimization often predict solutions directly or use predictions to restrict search, while expressive energy-based models typically rely on approximate inference. We introduce EnerGNN, a framework that learns energy functions over complete binary configurations and minimizes them under explicit hard constraints through mixed integer programming (MIP). EnerGNN combines a graph neural network encoder with an optimization-compatible readout and a nonlinear energy head, enabling exact constrained inference over the learned energy. An optimality-aware contrastive loss trains the energy to reflect solution quality and constraint violations. Across Quadratic Knapsack, Combinatorial Auctions, and a personalized cell therapy supply chain problem, EnerGNN achieves near-optimal solutions with 100% feasibility. On the supply chain problem, it achieves a 0.05% mean primal gap and a 17.4$\times$ speedup over the monolithic MIP. The learned energy also generalizes to larger instances and supports zero-shot constraint injection, adapting to changing constraints without retraining while preserving feasibility.

title: Gravitational Radiation Coupled to a real massive scalar Field
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of small-data global solutions to the Einstein--Klein--Gordon system with a positive-mass real scalar field in wave gauge. We show that the linearized trace component of the metric perturbation admits a $\hat t^{-1}\simeq t^{-1}$ optimal decreasing rate. Moreover, a quantitative one-point observability estimate is established: the initial Klein-Gordon energy is controlled by this leading order coefficient.

title: Optimal Experimental Design for the Polynomial Maximization Method: a Higher-Order Reserve Beyond Second-Order Design Theory
abstract: Optimal designs for regression with asymmetric errors build on the second-order least squares estimator (SLSE) of Wang and Leblanc (2008), whose gain over ordinary least squares (OLS) comes from the error skewness. With i.i.d. errors the optimally weighted SLSE solves the same estimating equation as the degree-two Polynomial Maximization Method (PMM), a family whose degree-$S$ location estimator has asymptotic variance $g_S\le1$ times that of the sample mean. We derive optimal designs for this family when the errors are independent with constant variance but have standardised cumulants of order three and higher that vary with the regressor (cumulant heteroscedasticity). For a known reduction field $g_S(x)$, the $g_S$-weighted information matrix $M_{g_S}$ obeys the Kiefer-Wolfowitz equivalence theorem. A constant field leaves the OLS-optimal design unchanged; a non-constant field can change it but need not. For symmetric errors with varying kurtosis, the PMM$_2$ and conditional-SLSE designs cannot depart from the OLS-optimal one, whereas a degree-three design can. A stratify-and-pool PMM$_S$ estimator attains $N\mathrm{Cov}(\hatθ)\toσ^2M_{g_S}^{-1}$ at every degree as all strata grow; its per-stratum reduction is below one only for symmetric errors with the symmetry imposed. For a quadratic model on $[0,1]$ with symmetric Beta errors of unit variance and dose-varying shape, the third-order design for the known field has $A$-efficiency $1.047$ relative to the OLS-optimal design, and $1.001$ under the $D$-criterion. A two-stage procedure that estimates the field from a one-third pilot builds designs of $A$-efficiency $1.014$-$1.020$ at $N=600$-$2400$; its realised mean-squared-error ratio against the OLS-optimal design ranges from $0.89$ (a loss) to $1.08$.
comment: 41 pages, 4 figures, 8 tables. Companion to arXiv:2606.11421 (second-order least squares as the degree-two polynomial maximization method). v3: adds the cost of a small asymmetry and the limit of plug-in designs; corrects the two-stage limit; code supplement v1.0.2

title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support. The existence of such a lift is a special case of Kontsevich's conjecture on holonomic $\mathcal D$-modules with prescribed arithmetic support. We prove that in this special situation such a lift is unique whenever it exists. If these lifts exists for every endomorphism with Jacobian one, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge 3$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb{A}^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. The counterexamples arise from the graph of a noninvertible symplectic endomorphism of $\mathbb A^4$ constructed by Long. We also present a different strategy for lifting $\mathcal D$-modules associated with a Jacobian-one endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ to characteristic zero via ultraproducts and show that the existence of a characteristic-zero lift in this setting is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the Berest--Wilson invariants of these $A_2$-modules, regarded as left $A_1$-modules. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

title: Improved Bounds on Proportional Choice Numbers
abstract: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $χ_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. We consider two previously posed questions regarding proportional choice numbers: (1) Is there a constant $C$ such that $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq C$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$? and (2) Is it the case that for any graph $G$, $χ_{pc}(G) \leq Δ(G)+1$ where $Δ(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$? In this paper we answer both questions: the first in the affirmative and the second in the negative. Specifically, we prove that $χ_{pc}(G) \leq 2^{χ'(G)}$ for every graph $G$ where $χ'(G)$ is the chromatic index of $G$. Consequently, $χ_{pc}(P_n) \leq 4$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$. We also prove that when $G$ is the disjoint union of $(a+b-1)$ copies of $K_{a,b}$, $χ_{pc}(G)=a+b$. In particular, for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, there is a graph $G$ with $Δ(G)=m$ and $χ_{pc}(G)=2Δ(G)$.

title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
abstract: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

title: Near-boundary asymptotics for profile score statistics
abstract: We establish asymptotic results for profile score statistics under sequences of parameters that may tend to the boundary of the parameter set. When the likelihood is profiled over a set with boundary points, the distribution of the statistic can depend, even asymptotically, on a distance to the boundary that cannot be estimated consistently. We address this in three ways. First, we give conditions under which the nuisance score has a root on an extended parameter set, and the profile score statistic formed with that root converges to a chi-squared distribution. Second, we show that the efficient score statistic converges to a chi-squared distribution under a separate condition that can hold even for estimators constrained to the original set. Both lead to confidence regions with asymptotically correct coverage probability, uniformly on sets that may contain boundary points, and the conditions allow the scores for the interest and nuisance parameters to grow at different rates or become asymptotically collinear. Third, we quantify the coverage error of applying the profile score statistic without an extended set. We approximate the distribution of the statistic and bound the error by a quantity that decays like a normal tail in the standardized distance to the boundary. The approximation also gives one-sided tests with least favorable critical values whose asymptotic size is at most the nominal level. We illustrate the results in a zero-inflated Poisson model and a one-way random effects model.

title: Dynamic Interpolation and Higher-Order Turbulence Scales in 3D Navier-Stokes Flows
abstract: We investigate the three-dimensional unforced Navier-Stokes equations through the interaction between spatial analyticity and the geometric sparseness of regions of intense fluid activity (i.e., regions where the fluid's motion varies sharply). Interpreting higher-order derivative ratios as turbulence scales, we introduce time-weighted bridge inequalities that quantify the relationship between lower- and higher-order derivative norms. The time weights give the derivative ratios greater flexibility while ensuring that the resulting lower bound on the radius of analyticity dominates the sparseness scale of the super-level sets, indicating that the flow has entered the dissipation regime. Combining this scale comparison with a harmonic-measure maximum principle on one-dimensional sparse sets yields a contraction in the relevant derivative norm, thereby excluding a class of strongly turbulent blow-up scenarios. Consequently, the strong solution extends analytically beyond the candidate blow-up time.

title: Minimum-coordinate elimination on a simplex: polynomial first-step safety and coNP-complete correctness
abstract: We study a deletion rule for strictly convex quadratic minimization on a simplex: compute the affine minimizer on the current face, permanently remove a most-negative coordinate, and repeat. Correctness is required for every linear term and every resolution of ties. We characterize first-step safety by a finite maximum principle for the constrained inverse, and correctness from every initial face by principal-inverse row inequalities. Correctness from the full simplex is a different property. The two properties coincide with at most four coordinates, but an explicit rational five-coordinate example separates them. An exact reachability condition explains the separation: boundary equalities in the constrained inverse restrict the tasks that can be entered on a facet. Away from these equalities, full-start and hereditary correctness coincide. We also determine the recognition complexity. First-step safety is decidable in polynomial bit time, by combining classical strict $n$-step-vector recognition with diagonal regularization. In contrast, full-start and hereditary correctness are coNP-complete, even on a reduction family with strict column diagonal maxima on every face. The proofs include the non-strict boundary and all affine anchors; explicit rational certificates for the finite examples are given in the text.

title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
abstract: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.

title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
abstract: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

title: A remark on the global minimality of the cracktip
abstract: We give a short proof that the planar cracktip is a global minimizer of the Mumford--Shah functional, based on interior and Dirichlet boundary regularity. We construct a Dirichlet minimizer with nonempty discontinuity set and show that this set contains no simple closed curves. The regularity results then imply the existence of an interior regular loose end, at which a blow-up yields the cracktip.

title: Persistent occupation and critical marked sums on branching random walks
abstract: We study two path functionals of a branching random walk at an exponential normalization. For centered integer displacements bounded above by one, we construct on survival one ray whose local time at every large spatial level is bounded below by a positive multiple of the square of that level. For displacements in $\{-1,0,1\}$, overlapping forward profiles give a single ray with lower coefficient $4t/(σ^2j_{1,1}^2)$, where $σ^2$ is the tilted variance and $j_{1,1}$ the first positive zero of $J_1$. The profile energy quotient is optimized exactly. For discounted marked path sums with real displacements, we prove critical-moment sufficiency without a drift assumption, and necessity under a finite ascending-ladder mean and a weighted sibling moment. At positive tilted drift, a stopping-line argument replaces the sibling condition by an $L\log L$ hypothesis. A sparse mark construction identifies an exact universality obstruction in the constant-displacement subclass. At negative tilted drift, weighted powers give explicit sufficient logarithmic-tail conditions for every exponent $t>0$ and examples excluding a universal critical-moment converse. Under our sufficient conditions, path sums converge uniformly and attain their maxima. The exact optimal persistent local-time constant and a general negative-drift converse remain open.

title: Recovery of a source of anomalous diffusion from space-time sparse data
abstract: We study an inverse source problem for a time-fractional sub- and super-diffusive anomalous diffusion equation on the unit disk with sparse boundary observations. We prove the recovery of a general class of $L^2$ sources for anomalous diffusion, with separated variables, from boundary measurements that are sparse in both space and time, using observations at two carefully chosen boundary points on a discrete set of times arbitrarily close to the final time. The analysis relies heavily on the memory effect of the model, properties of complex analysis and the representation of solutions.

title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $Ξ$ to be {\em unitary} if $Ξ^\zdagΞ=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $Ξ$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $Ξ^\zdagΞ=\mI+Γ$, where $Γ$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.

title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2πi (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
comment: 47 pages, 37 figures. This paper is the second one in a series of two. The first paper is available at arXiv:2610.28986

title: Well-posedness of the Burgers' equation on the half-line through the Cole-Hopf transformation
abstract: We rigorously establish the well-posedness of the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) for the Burgers' equation on the half-line for data in Sobolev-type spaces. The formal solution to this problem was previously derived via the Cole-Hopf transformation and the Fokas unified transform method under the assumption of smooth, Schwartz-class data. In this work, we prove the validity of this formal representation for initial data $u_0\in \tilde{H}^{s+1}_x (0,\infty)$ and boundary data $g_0 \in H_t^{{(2s+1)}/{4}}$ where $1/2<s<3/2$. Well-posedness is established under two complementary conditions: (1) sufficiently small initial and boundary data, and (2) non-positive boundary data of arbitrary size. The latter condition utilizes the strong minimum principle for the corresponding linear heat equation to ensure the global invertibility of the nonlinear Cole-Hopf map. The proofs combine linear estimates for the heat IBVP with nonlinear bounds obtained through Taylor series representations and the algebraic properties of Sobolev spaces.

title: Using artificial delays for prescribed/fixed-time static output feedback control of linear systems
abstract: In this paper, we address the prescribed/fixed-time control problem for linear time-invariant systems with relative degree $r\geq 2$ using delayed time-varying static output feedback. In addition to controllability and observability, we assume that a truncated observability matrix is nonsingular. Within the act-and-wait control framework, two types of artificial delays are introduced into the output feedback: one to realize static output feedback and the other to achieve prescribed/fixed-time control. By constructing smooth periodic delayed output feedback controllers, we achieve prescribed-time input-to-state stability (ISS) with respect to matched disturbances and measurement noise. Next, we consider systems with measurement delays. Note that existing predictor methods are not applicable to static output feedback delay compensation. We propose delayed controllers that achieve fixed-time stability in the presence of large known slowly-varying delays (with delay derivatives less than one) and even in the presence of large unknown constant delays for systems with nilpotent matrices. Moreover, we present a design for the case of discrete-time periodic measurements with a small sampling period. When the system reduces to a chain of integrators, prescribed/fixed-time convergence can be achieved with arbitrarily large artificial delays introduced by static output feedback avoiding high gain and managing with large known slowly-varying or sawtooth delays (corresponding to discrete-time measurements) or unknown constant delays. In the case of unknown constant delays, this leads to a low-gain controller that may efficiently attenuate measurement noise. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
abstract: We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $Λ^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $Λ^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations. The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra, and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions. Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.

title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$ with codimension of Jelonek set greater than one, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is neither homeomorphic to a line nor can have a single end at infinity.

title: Exploring topological features of a complex network of prime factors and composite numbers
abstract: Prime numbers are mathematical concepts of particular interest because of their relative rarity among integers, as well as the relative unpredictability of their occurrence and density along the integer sequence. They constitute the building blocks of all other composite numbers, giving rise to the interesting and important concept of prime factorization, a process guaranteed by the fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Among the several works that have been reported about prime numbers and their interrelationship with composite numbers, some have considered derived graphs and/or networks. In this paper, we derive some topological features of a bipartite complex network of prime factors and composite numbers. More specifically, we prove mathematically that the network's diameter is exactly five regardless of the number of nodes. In particular, we show that certain nontrivial sub-networks have minimal diameter equal to four, which is, again, independent of the number of nodes as long as the network is large enough. The last shows that this network is of small-world type. We also characterize exactly the number of boundary nodes in the network and present a couple of algorithms to identify the most important, relevant, influential, or central nodes of the network. Finally, we focus on the computation of the information dimensions on the basis of Shannon and Tsallis entropies of the studied complex network. The results show both decreasing as the number of nodes increases. Furthermore, both entropies indicate that box coverings at the diameters \(\varepsilon=[3,4]\), group nodes into roughly the same number of boxes, independent of the number of nodes in the network.

title: On Lewis's homotopy in distance-regular graphs
abstract: In 2000, Lewis introduced a nested sequence of normal subgroups of the fundamental group of a distance-regular graph $Γ$. While the full homotopy group itself is simply a free group, it is interesting to determine the smallest integer $k$ such that every closed walk in $Γ$ can be built, up to homotopy, from closed walks of "essential length" $k$ or less. Lewis proved that $k\le 6$ for any $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $Γ$ that is not a pseudoquotient. In this paper, we prove that $k=3$ for Johnson graphs and that $k=4$ in the case of Hamming graphs. We also compute the homotopy groups of natural cell complexes associated to the folded Johnson graphs and folded cubes. The paper finishes with some open questions and suggestions for further lines of investigation.

title: Dancing circles
abstract: Recent results on diffeomorphisms of $4$-manifolds make essential use of families of embeddings of $1$-manifolds into $4$-manifolds. We survey what is currently known about such families.
comment: 26 pages, 9 figures. To appear in the Proceedings of the 2025 Georgia International Topology Conference

title: Efficiency--Complexity Tradeoff and Constrained Percolation
abstract: We study the efficiency--complexity tradeoff for resource-limited agents through directed first-passage percolation. Nonnegative i.i.d. edge weights represent physical energy expenditure, while the logarithmic size of a constrained path family measures representational complexity. For translation-invariant families, a path-joining property yields deterministic large-distance costs in rational directions and joint convexity in constraint parameter and direction, under suitable moment and feasibility assumptions. Our main result concerns the limiting cost parameterized by path-family entropy. Using techniques from analytic combinatorics in several variables (ACSV), we establish its almost-sure existence and joint continuity in entropy and direction for nested families satisfying additional generating-function conditions, on the corresponding entropy range. Path-count asymptotics supply the change of parameter linking this cost to the constraint-parameterized cost. Two planar examples constrain the number of turns or the number of East-runs of length at least two.

title: A simple improvement on Kerman's approximation to the median of the beta distribution
abstract: Kerman's approximation to the median of the Beta$(α,β)$ distribution is the ratio $g(α)/(g(α) + g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, using the first two terms of the asymptotic expansion of the median of the standard gamma distribution. We extend this elegant ratio form to the one-parameter family with $g(x) = x - 1/3 + c_1/x$, in which $c_1 = 0$ gives Kerman's. For large shape parameters along any ray $β= rα$ with $r > 1$, the resulting approximation is eventually a lower bound on the median if $c_1 \le 8/405$ and an upper bound if $c_1 \ge 1/45$. We recommend $c_1 = 1/36$ for its simplicity: it makes $g(x) = (x - 1/6)^2/x$ a perfect square over $x$, and it is within 1% of the minimax value of $c_1$ for $α, β\ge 1$ under several error measures, while the theoretically distinguished values $8/405$ and $1/45$ are less accurate. The approximation is then $((α- 1/6)^2/α)/((α- 1/6)^2/α+ (β- 1/6)^2/β)$. Its relative error lies between -0.171% and +0.212% for all $1 \le α\le β$, compared with up to -3.8% for Kerman's. It is more accurate than Kerman's approximation wherever the latter is defined, with relative error never more than 13/32 of Kerman's, the ratio approached asymptotically. The same $g(α)$ is a useful approximation to the gamma distribution median, overestimating it by at most 0.212% for shape parameter $α\ge 1$.
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures. A Python notebook (and its source module) that reproduces the figures and numbers is in the ancillary files

title: The $\rm{v}$-number of $t$-closed neighborhood ideals
abstract: We give a combinatorial characterization of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal associated to a graph $G$, and investigate its relation with other invariants such as the $t$-domination number and the smallest size of a ball of radius $t$ in the graph $G$. We present several new cases where it is satisfied that the $\rm{v}$-number is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity. We analyze the behavior of the $\rm{v}$-number of a $t$-closed neighborhood ideal with respect to the parameter $t$. Lastly, we compute explicit formulas for the $\rm{v}$-number in the case of paths, cycles, and caterpillars, and analyze the case of Hamming graphs.

title: Omni-representations of Leibniz conformal algebras
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notion of an omni-representation of a Leibniz conformal algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ on a $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module $M$ as a Leibniz conformal algebra homomorphism from $\mathfrak{g}$ to the conformal omni-Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gc}(M)\oplus M$. We show that the right $λ$-action of a representation induces a Maurer--Cartan element. When $M$ is a free $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-module of finite rank, it also defines, via the conformal dual $M_c^*$, a $1$-cocycle with values in $M_c^*\otimes M\cong\mathfrak{gc}(M)$. Consequently, every such representation gives rise to an omni-representation on $M_c^*\otimes M$. We characterize omni-representations with values in the graph of a conformal embedding tensor. Finally, we introduce the omni-cohomology theory of Leibniz conformal algebras and establish the relation between omni-cohomology groups and the usual cohomology groups.

title: Between the Semi-Random Process and G(n,p)
abstract: We study a random graph process that connects the Erdős--Rényi random graph with the semi-random process. In each round, a uniformly random vertex is revealed together with a uniformly random candidate set of $s$ possible partners, and Builder chooses one of them. We study how this limited adaptivity $s$ changes the hitting times of monotone graph properties and how the familiar logarithmic ``coupon--collector'' delays in random graphs are reflected in this setting.

title: Solving Large SDPs from Flag Algebra Problems
abstract: The flag algebra method is a general tool in extremal combinatorics, which has been useful in tackling open problems concerning graphs, hypergraphs, permutations, point sets, and other structures. The method establishes combinatorial inequalities via sums of squares, which are usually obtained by a semidefinite relaxation of the original combinatorial problem. A typical application of the method in graph theory starts with fixing a parameter $n$ followed by constructing a semidefinite program based on the (subgraph) structure of all $n$-vertex graphs. In the standard formulation before symmetry reductions, there is a coefficient constraint for every admissible $n$-vertex graph up to isomorphism. For 3-uniform hypergraphs, there are 2,136 of them on 6 vertices and 7,013,320 on 7 vertices. While solving the resulting program for $n=6$ is an easy task on any modern computer, the programs for $n = 7$ seems out of reach, mainly because the SDP solvers need too much RAM. Yet solving such programs for as large $n$ as possible is desirable because they typically yield better bounds for the original combinatorial problems. We bypass the aforementioned memory requirements by linear programming with cutting planes. Although we do not guarantee that this cutting-plane procedure reaches an optimum in finitely many iterations, in many flag algebra instances it uses much less memory and yields improved bounds for well-known hypergraph Turán problems. We use this method to obtain numerical bounds for Turán densities and codegree squared densities of several 3-uniform hypergraphs including the tetrahedron, where we obtained the upper bound 0.55753 and tetrahedron without one edge with a new upper bound 0.2865. It also allows to tackle bounds on Turán densities of 7-vertex 3-graphs using flag algebras, which was not possible before.

title: Joint Extension Field Point Counts for Superelliptic Curves
abstract: Fix a finite field $\mathbf{F}_q$, an integer $m\ge2$ prime to $q$, and $2\leκ\le m$. For a uniformly chosen $κ$-power-free polynomial $F\in\mathbf{F}_q[x]$ of degree $D$, we determine the limiting joint distribution of the affine point counts of $y^m=F(x)$ over $\mathbf{F}_q,\ldots,\mathbf{F}_{q^n}$ as $D\to\infty$, with $q$ and $n$ fixed. The probability generating function is a finite Euler product with explicit local factors. Equivalently, the limiting vector is a sum of independent closed-point contributions, each of which may affect several extension degrees. We obtain the formula by specializing the equidistribution and motivic Euler product formalism of Bertucci-Howe. We then compute means, covariances, and moment expansions as $q$ varies in a fixed reduced residue class modulo $m$, after the degree limit has been taken. The one-field specialization recovers the power-free affine point-count distribution of Cheong-Wood-Zaman.

title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
abstract: We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

title: A Cubic Underestimator for Deterministic Global Optimization
abstract: We propose a new underestimator with pointwise and Hausdorff convergence of order three for deterministic global optimization of twice continuously differentiable functions with Lipschitz continuous Hessians. The proposed underestimator is obtained by augmenting the second-order Taylor expansion with a cubic remainder term of the objective function yielding a valid global underestimator that can be used to obtain lower bounds in a branch-and-bound method to solve nonconvex global optimization problems. The underestimator is nonconvex, and finding its global minimum could be computationally expensive. Accordingly, we derive a sufficient condition under which the proposed cubic underestimator is edge-concave, so that its minimum over a box can be found by vertex evaluation, while retaining third-order convergence. We show that the maximum separation distance between the objective function and the underestimator decreases cubically with the width of the box. This higher order convergence enables the lower bounds to converge more rapidly to the optimal value as the variable bounds are progressively tightened. The proposed underestimator is incorporated into a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm and compared with the αBB and second-order edge-concave underestimators on a collection of 130 benchmark problems. The numerical results show that the proposed underestimator outperforms the compared underestimators in terms of both the number of explored branch-and-bound nodes and total CPU time, while maintaining a competitive computational cost per node. These results demonstrate that the proposed cubic edge-concave underestimator can provide more effective lower bounds and better computational performance in deterministic global optimization.

title: On tame amenable flows and generalized Newelski's conjecture
abstract: We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit. The first main result says that, assuming tameness and hereditary amenability, this natural map is an isomorphism of topological groups. This is an abstract dynamical generalization of Newelski's conjecture, or rather a theorem of Chernikov and Simon that a natural map from the Ellis group of the flow $(S_G(M),G)$ to the definable Bohr compactification of $G$ is an isomorphism when $G$ is a definably amenable group definable in a NIP structure $M$. We give two proofs of our main result: a shorter dynamical proof and an analytic proof. In the course of the dynamical proof, we prove some results on the universal compactification flow and on the generalized Bohr compactification below a given ambit which admits a left continuous semigroup operation extending the action of $G$. The considerations around the analytic proof yield a description of the measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, which is the second main result of this paper. We also study specializations of the above abstract topological dynamics context to model theory contexts to recover some known and to obtain some new notions and results. The main new results in the model theory contexts are: (i) a description of the Bohr compactification of the group of automorphisms of a sufficiently saturated model $\mathfrak{C}$ of a first order theory $T$ below a certain fundamental ambit associated with $\mathfrak{C}$; (ii) transfer of amenability of a NIP theory $T$ to amenability of the Ellis semigroup ambit; (iii) a version of Newelski's conjecture for spaces of local types with a description of Bohr compactifications below such spaces.

title: Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
abstract: We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results. The first uses the graph transform operator to extend Elton's condition [A multiplicative ergodic theorem for Lipschitz maps. Stochastic Process. Appl. 34(1) (1990)] for the existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs. The second uses the Markov operator to generalize a displacement condition for stationary measures, introduced by Diaconis and Freedman [Iterated random functions. SIAM Rev. 41(1) (1999)] and by Kloeckner [Optimal transportation and stationary measures for iterated function systems. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 173(1) (2022)]. We present several examples illustrating the applicability of our results.

title: Optimal Control of the 2D Boussinesq Equations with Finite Codimension Constraints
abstract: We study an optimal control problem (OCP) governed by the two-dimensional (2D) Boussinesq equations, where the right-hand sides of the velocity and temperature equations are projected onto the corresponding tangent spaces of the manifolds $\mathcal{M}_1:=\{y\in\mathbb{H}:\|y\|_{\mathbb{H}}=1\}$ and $\mathcal{M}_2:=\{θ\in H:\|θ\|_H=1\}$, respectively. The resulting evolution is subject to finite-codimensional constraints, under which the state $(y,θ)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}:=\mathcal{M}_1\times\mathcal{M}_2$ throughout the time interval. A Faedo--Galerkin construction provides a unique, global, strong solution to the constrained Boussinesq system for external controls $\mathfrak{H}\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb{H})$, along with uniform energy bounds. In addition, we establish the existence of an optimal triplet $(y^*,θ^*,\mathfrak{H}^*)$ that minimizes the quadratic cost subject to the constrained Boussinesq system. Necessary conditions of the first order are obtained through a coupled state--adjoint--control system. The optimal state $(y^*,θ^*)$ remains on $\mathcal{M}$, while the optimal control lies in the tangent space: $\mathfrak{H}^*(t)\in T_{y^*(t)}\mathcal{M}_1$, for all $t\in[0,T]$. We also show that the map $\mathfrak{H}\mapsto(y_{\mathfrak{H}},θ_{\mathfrak{H}})$ in $(C([0,T];\mathbb{H})\cap L^2(0,T;\mathbb{V}))\times(C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V))$ is Fréchet differentiable. The linearized state is the unique weak solution to the constrained linearized Boussinesq system and satisfies the necessary tangency condition. Hence, the well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions are established for the Boussinesq system under nonlinear manifold constraints.

title: Critical metrics for the Dirac-Yamabe eigenvalue ratio and Einstein-Dirac equations
abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a closed spin manifold of dimension $n\geq 3$ with positive Yamabe constant. We prove that critical metrics for the mixed eigenvalue ratio $\mathcal H(g)=\frac{λ_1(D_g)^2}{λ_1(L_g)},$ where $D_g$ is the Dirac operator and $L_g$ is the conformal Laplacian are characterized by a harmonic section whose energy-momentum tensor satisfies an Einstein--Dirac equation. We discuss consequences of this result for Hijazi's inequality, and we construct an example to prove that $\mathcal H$ is unbounded above within the conformal class of the round sphere.

title: Explicit equations of three pairs of fake projective planes
abstract: We find explicit polynomial equations in their bicanonical embeddings into $\mathbb C\mathbb P^9$ for the pairs of fake projective planes labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2\},D_3), (C18,p=3,\{2\},(dD)_3)$ and $(C18,p=3,\{2\},(d^2D)_3)$ in the Cartwright-Steger classification. We do this by starting with the equations of the commensurable fake projective plane labeled by $(C18,p=3,\{2I\})$ that were found in arXiv:2512.03213.

title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
