After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

title: A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture
abstract: Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.

title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.

title: Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes
abstract: We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.

title: Cohomological change of coefficients for noncocommutative Hopf algebras
abstract: Let $A$ be a finite Hopf algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring $R$. For any map $f : R \to k$ where $k$ is a field, there is a natural map on the cohomology of $A$ under this change of coefficients $H^\ast(f): H^\ast(A, R) \otimes_R k \to H^\ast(A_k, k)$. In this paper we examine this map for $R = \mathbb Z[ζ]$ the cyclotomic integers with $ζ$ an $\ell$th root of unity. We show that under a finite generation assumption, the induced map gives a homeomorphism on the spectra of the two cohomology rings. Finally, we turn to small quantum groups defined over $\mathbb Z[ζ]$ and show that, with mild restrictions on $\ell$, every fiber map whose residue field has a good prime characteristic induces an isomorphism on cohomology.

title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
abstract: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.

title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
abstract: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

title: Classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebras on solvable Lie conformal algebras of rank two
abstract: In this paper, we give a complete classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebra structures on solvable Lie conformal algebras which are free of rank two as $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-modules up to isomorphism. We obtain ten mutually non-isomorphic normal-form types and determine the precise equivalence relations among the parameters within each family. Moreover, we also characterize the Novikov conformal algebras among the classified left-symmetric conformal algebras, thereby obtaining a complete classification of compatible Novikov conformal algebra structures in the same setting.

title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
abstract: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.

title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
comment: 81 pages, 8 figures. The main text and Appendices A and B occupy pages 1-46. Appendix C on pages 47-80 collects elementary but lengthy proofs of several claims and is intended to serve as a reference. Comments welcome!

title: Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues
abstract: For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(Ω) = \tfrac{P(Ω)^d}{|Ω|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\barλ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}λ_1(Ω)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\barμ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}μ_1(Ω)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $π$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\barλ$, and $\barμ$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.

title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space.
comment: 20 pages, 1 figure. Earlier version on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22663662

title: Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schrödinger operators
abstract: We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schrödinger operators $L_i=-Δ+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales. We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles. The proof combines one-parameter Schrödinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse Hölder potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.

title: Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
abstract: We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest for $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $α$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $β$. For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{α,β}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way. On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $Ω(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(α,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $α>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $α=1$ and $β=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded. Finally, for every fixed rationals $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,α,β)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025]. [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]

title: Energy-rate equidistribution for adaptive SSAV--BDF2 integration of gradient flows
abstract: We develop an adaptive time-stepping strategy for scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) schemes combined with variable-step BDF2 discretization for gradient flows. The strategy selects step sizes based on the instantaneous energy dissipation rate and enforces monotonicity of a computable symmetric energy through a step rejection mechanism. We show that the step-size rules used in practice correspond to equidistributing a monitor function along the energy curve, connecting energy-adaptive time stepping to the classical theory of r-adaptive mesh methods. The monitor $g = |\dot{E}|$ is asymptotically optimal as it minimises the leading-order maximum symmetric-energy discrepancy for a given number of steps. A combined monitor that switches to $g = \sqrt{|\dot{E}|}$ near equilibrium caps step growth without degrading this error bound. The arclength parameter $β$ used in prior work is shown to be the ratio of the largest permitted step to the energy-error tolerance. The controller is paired with the SSAV--BDF2 discretization. Accepted steps satisfy monotonicity of the symmetric energy, from which we deduce a bound on the physical energy that is uniform in the number of steps, $\sup_n E(u^n) \le E(u^{0}) + τ_1 + O(Δt_{\max}^2)$, and the scheme achieves second-order global accuracy under standard step-ratio restrictions. Numerical experiments on Cahn--Hilliard, Ohta--Kawasaki, Phase--Field Crystal, and functionalized Cahn--Hilliard models confirm the theory and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

title: Reflections on Trusting Lean
abstract: It is known, by works of Werner and Carneiro, that the type theory of Lean (and indeed of CIC plus a version of choice) is equiconsistent with ZFC plus "there are infinitely many strongly inaccessible cardinals". We prove a finer connection between these two formal systems; namely, given any formula in the language of second order arithmetic, that formula is provable in the aforementioned extension of ZFC if and only if the same formula, when viewed as a type in Lean, is inhabited.
comment: This work has been presented at ICMS 2026 on 23 July 2026

title: A remoteness formula for generalized Wythoff games
abstract: Smith's remoteness function records how long an impartial game lasts when the winner wins as quickly as possible and the loser delays defeat. For the generalized Wythoff game $\mathrm{WYT}(a,b)$, in which two positive integer parameters $a$ and $b$ determine which simultaneous removals from the two piles are allowed, we give a formula for the remoteness of every position, building on the known values at losing positions. The formula depends on two indices: a local index determined by the coordinates of the losing positions in a window of length $b$ ending at the smaller pile, and the integer part of the pile difference divided by $a$. When $b=1$, complementary Beatty sequences make the local index explicit, which gives an explicit formula for $\mathrm{WYT}(a,1)$, including classical Wythoff's game. We also show that if each attempted move in a finite impartial game independently fails with a fixed probability and passes the turn, the probability that the player to move wins under optimal play is an explicit exponential function of remoteness. For every success probability strictly between $0$ and $1$, the optimal attempts are exactly the moves that reduce remoteness by one.

title: Injectivity and continuity of the intersection form in infinite type
abstract: We study two fundamental properties of the intersection pairing between geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces which are classical in the finite-type closed setting: injectivity of the marked length spectrum and continuity of the intersection form. We show that geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces of the first kind are determined by their intersection numbers with closed curves, extending Otal's marked length spectrum rigidity argument from finite-type to infinite-type surfaces. In contrast, we prove that the intersection pairing is not continuous in general for the natural topologies by constructing explicit counterexamples. We then prove sufficient criteria for continuity of intersection numbers for infinite-type surfaces.

title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Liénard systems
abstract: We establish criteria for at most one or at most two limit cycles of generalized Liénard systems in a single potential well. Two independent uniqueness tests use modified quotients of the damping and restoring forces; both allow a degenerate restoring force, and one extends to continuous potential profiles with corners. Opposite convexity of the two branches of the damping quotient in the potential coordinate gives an upper bound of two. Further criteria apply to weak damping with an analytic normalized profile on a bounded potential interval under an explicit smallness condition, to small profile perturbations vanishing near the equilibrium on a bounded range of half-widths, and to parameter families satisfying curvature, monotonicity and boundary conditions. Applications give another proof of the classical quartic bound. For Selkov systems, we obtain a two-cycle bound in a specified negative-parameter region and prove existence and uniqueness in a positive-parameter region. We also prove Conjecture~2.1 in [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 2025]. Examples attain the two-cycle bound.

title: The Serrin exponent for Lane-Emden inequalities driven by sums of fractional p-Laplacians
abstract: We study positive weak super-solutions of the Lane-Emden inequality $\mathcal{L}u := \sum_{i=1}^{n}(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}u \ge u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where each $(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}$ is a fractional $p_i$-Laplacian of order $s_i\in(0,1]$ and exponent $p_i\in(1,\infty)$, and $\max_i s_ip_i<N$. Let $κ_i := (N-s_ip_i)/(p_i-1)$ be the decay exponent of the fundamental solution of the $i$-th operator, and let $\overlineκ := \max_iκ_i$. We show that the Serrin exponent of $\mathcal{L}$ is $\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}} = N/\overlineκ$. More precisely, for $0<q<\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ the only non-negative continuous weak super-solution is $u\equiv 0$, while for every $q>\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ we construct explicit positive weak super-solutions of the form $A(λ+|x|)^{-κ}$. In other words, the Serrin exponent of the sum is the smallest of the Serrin exponents $N/κ_i$ of the single operators, that is, the one of the operator whose fundamental solution decays fastest. No structural assumption relating the different operators is needed. The endpoint $q=\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is left open. The local order $s_i=1$ is treated together with the nonlocal orders, and all the arguments are carried out in the weak setting.

title: Quantitative Resolvent Calculus for Sample Covariance Matrices
abstract: In this work, we develop a quantitative resolvent calculus for sample covariance matrices tailored to applications in high-dimensional statistics. We treat single resolvents, their derivatives, and products of two resolvents with different spectral parameters in the proportional-dimensional regime. Our bounds hold uniformly over compact subsets of $\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R_{\geq0}$ with approximation errors of order $O_{\mathbb P}(\|Θ_n\|_F/\sqrt n)$ for deterministic test matrices $Θ_n$. These bounds require only uniformly bounded fourth moments and a uniformly bounded population covariance operator norm. Neither regular spectral edges nor convergence of the population spectral distribution is required. As a key technical ingredient, we develop an averaging argument for centered quadratic forms involving one or two leave-one-out resolvents. Applications of our results include precision-matrix shrinkage, prediction risk in ridge regression, and generalized cross-validation. For these problems, we obtain quantitative guarantees for estimation and data-driven parameter selection.

title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.

title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.

title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: Simple finite-dimensional binary Lie superalgebras
abstract: We prove that every complex finite-dimensional simple binary Lie superalgebra with non-zero odd part is either a simple Lie superalgebra, and hence is one of the superalgebras of Kac's list, or the two-dimensional non-Lie superalgebra $B_2$. This confirms the Grishkov--Shestakov conjecture and, together with the theorems of Grishkov and Filippov on simple binary Lie algebras, gives the answer to Shestakov's question from the Dniester Notebook (Problem 3.100(d)) over the field of complex numbers.

title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

title: Source integrability and the frontier $α=\tfrac12$ in time-fractional diffusion
abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $α\in(0,1)$, and let $\partial_{t}^α$ denote the Caputo derivative. For $\partial_{t}^αu-\nabla\cdot\bigl(A(x)\nabla u\bigr)=f$ with homogeneous Dirichlet condition and initial datum $g\in L^{2}(Ω)$, we identify which of the thresholds appearing in the energy method belong to the method and which to the equation. We compare $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ and $f\in L^{r}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ with $r>2/α$; in the subdiffusive range the second implies the first and not conversely. Existence is not at issue and we claim none of it: it is known, for both hypotheses and under weaker ones, from the work of Zacher. What we determine is the exact set of exponents each route admits and what the exponents left outside it cost. Under the weaker hypothesis the construction below reaches $α\in(\frac12,1)$, under the stronger one every $α\in(0,1)$, and in both cases the solution lies in $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$, by the mode representation and not by the energy route, which yields no such bound under the weaker hypothesis. The restriction $α>\frac12$ comes from the compactness criterion, whose admissible exponents form $[1,2α)$; the exponent $r>2/α$ is exactly what the Grönwall step consumes. A concentrating family shows that nothing weaker suffices along that route, and the mode representation lowers the requirement to $1/α$. The frontier $α=\frac12$ belongs to the equation: for every $α\in(0,\frac12]$ there is $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ whose weak solution leaves $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$. Uniqueness and Hadamard well-posedness follow.

title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-étale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.

title: Asymptotical results on the automorphism groups of canonical double cover of graphs
abstract: The canonical double cover $BX$ of a graph $X$ is the direct product $X\times K_2$. A graph $X$ is stable if every automorphism of $BX$ is induced by automorphisms of $X$ and $K_2$, and unstable otherwise. We prove several asymptotic results on stable and unstable graphs. In particular, we show that the automorphism group of the canonical double cover of almost every graph has order $2$, and consequently that almost all graphs are stable. We also prove that the dominant sources of instability are having twins and being disconnected, in that order, and that graphs arising from a known construction are the next step in this hierarchy.

title: Permutation classes need not have proper growth rates
abstract: By the Marcus-Tardos Theorem (formerly the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture), every permutation class other than the class of all permutations has a finite upper growth rate, meaning that the $n$th root of the number of permutations of length $n$ in the class has a finite limit superior. It has long been conjectured that this limit superior is in fact always a proper limit. We disprove this by constructing a permutation class whose upper and lower growth rates differ. The construction uses grid classes with cubic row-column graphs of increasing girth, obtained from Haar graphs of finite 2-groups. The corresponding hereditary property of ordered graphs also disproves an analogous 2006 conjecture of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris. Along the way, we show that every proper permutation class with a D-finite generating function has a proper growth rate. We also establish refined enumerative bounds for grid classes, which lead to a short proof of Albert and Vatter's generalization of Bevan's Theorem on the growth rates of grid classes.

title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.

title: The Porous Medium Equation and Convexity
abstract: We show that root convexity of the pressure is preserved by the porous medium equation if the initial data is root convex, positive, smooth, bounded below by a quadratic function and has bounded Laplacian. This complements a result of Daskalopoulos-Hamilton-Lee on root concavity of pressure.

title: A unified variational framework for augmented Lagrangian preconditioning of saddle point systems: applications to mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain methods
abstract: We present a general framework to derive augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising from mixed finite element discretizations. Our approach is based on augmenting the variational formulation at the continuous level prior to discretization, providing a unified strategy for designing efficient preconditioners that are robust under mesh refinement for a broad class of problems leading to symmetric saddle point systems. The robustness of the proposed preconditioners is established through a detailed spectral analysis. This framework is applied to different model problems, focusing on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain formulations involving Lagrange multipliers, with some configurations featuring large coefficient jumps. Extensive numerical experiments on different test cases and geometries are presented, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our preconditioners when used in conjunction with flexible GMRES.

title: Partial Breakdown of Integrability in Nearly Integrable Systems
abstract: We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.

title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
abstract: We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $φ$- and $ψ$-mixing sequences. Our results for $ψ$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $ψ$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations

title: A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes
abstract: In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underlineα$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underlineα$-stable Lévy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.

title: Non-Induced Representations in Characteristic Zero
abstract: This paper explores the failure of induction from all proper subgroups to generate the full representation ring, measured by a quotient group $Q_k(G)$. We extend existing results for cyclic groups to all finite abelian groups and calculate this quotient for all finite groups over fields of characteristic 0 by reducing to the abelian case. We briefly discuss extensions to positive characteristics via modular representation theory. Finally, we detail our result for certain well-known families of groups.

title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
abstract: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.

title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

title: Covering lemmas associated to maximal operators of weak type
abstract: Building on the work of A. Córdoba and R. Fefferman, we provide a necessary and sufficient covering condition on a basis $\mathcal{B}$ on a separable metric space $X$ with a Borel measure $μ$ so that the associated \mbox{geometric} maximal operator $M_\mathcal{B}$ satisfies for all $α> 0$ the weak type estimate $$μ\left(\left\{x \in X : M_\mathcal{B}f(x) > α\right\}\right) \leq \int_{X}Φ\left( γ_\mathcal{B} \left|\frac{f}α\right|\right)\,dμ\;,$$ where $Φ: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is an everywhere finite Young's function.

title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

title: A Sharp Distributional Lower Bound for Planar Discrepancy
abstract: We prove that the unnormalized discrepancy function of every $n$-point set in the unit square has absolute value at least $c\sqrt{1+\log n}$ on a set of measure at least $η$, with absolute constants $c,η>0$. Consequently, its $L_p$-quasinorm is bounded below by $c\,η^{1/p} \sqrt{1+\log n}$ for every $p>0$.

title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
abstract: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
abstract: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

title: Space curves in Hahn calculus: rotation structure, a fundamental theorem, and $q$-deformed invariants at the fixed point
abstract: We develop the differential geometry of space curves in Hahn's quantum calculus, where the derivative is the difference quotient along the contraction $σ(t)=qt+ω$ with fixed point $ω_0=ω/(1-q)$. The Hahn Frenet frame is transported along every orbit of $σ$ by rotations through turning and torsion angles, which identifies it with the discrete Frenet frame of the inscribed orbit polygon. An embedded regular Hahn curve is determined, up to linear reparametrization about $ω_0$, by its trace and the induced contraction. We prove a sharp planarity criterion and a fundamental theorem via an infinite product of rotations and the Jackson--Nörlund integral. For smooth curves, expansions uniform in $q$ show that at $ω_0$ the Hahn curvature and torsion carry the factors $[2]_q/2$ and $[3]_q/3$. These factors, a sampling effect of geometrically decaying steps, disappear under edge-length normalization, but their quotient persists in the limiting ratio of torsion and turning angles of every polygon inscribed in a smooth curve with monotonically converging vertices and edge lengths decaying with ratio~$q$. In uniformly sampled relaxation towards a stable node, the factors can become measurable biases. We characterize generalized Hahn helices by a two-step relation between turning and torsion angles; their Lancret ratio at $ω_0$ is $\pm([2]_q/2)\cot\vartheta$, where $\vartheta$ is the helix angle. Unlike the classical case, a constant ratio of torsion and curvature does not characterize helices: curves with constant curvature and torsion are never generalized Hahn helices, and, near $ω_0$, unit-speed helices with a given ratio are unique up to similarities and linear reparametrization.

title: Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs
abstract: I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.

title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
abstract: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.

title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

title: Cographs in chordal graphs
abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.

title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
abstract: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

title: Syzygy and Adjoint Matroids
abstract: We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.

title: Global well-posedness for the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equations
abstract: In this short note, we prove the global well-posedness of the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with dispersion $1<α<2$, $$\partial_t u + D^α\partial_x u + u^2\partial_x u=0,$$ over the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, for any regularity $s$ greater or equal than the sharp analytic well-posedness regularity. As a byproduct, we also derive nonlinear smoothing estimates and give a simple proof of local well-posedness.

title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
abstract: We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $λ$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.

title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.

title: Scaling H2 Factorization to Billion-Unknown Three-Dimensional Problems
abstract: Strong recursive skeletonization provides approximate direct solvers for dense matrices from integral equations and kernel methods, but distributed implementations face substantial communication costs and limited parallelism, especially in three dimensions. We present a distributed-memory $\mathcal{H}^2$ factorization solver for symmetric matrices that combines spatial box coloring, delayed Schur complement updates, streamed sketching-based interpolative decomposition, and BLAS-3 and shared-memory kernels. Spatial coloring enables every process to participate in each boundary stage, while delayed updates and streamed sketching reduce dense storage and communication. To our knowledge, this is the first distributed-memory strong recursive skeletonization factorization demonstrated for three-dimensional volume integral equations at billion-unknown scale. Experiments on up to 512 compute nodes demonstrate factorization of a three-dimensional Laplace system with 3.62 billion unknowns, alongside three-dimensional Helmholtz tests and a two-dimensional Matérn system with 268 million unknowns. Combining streamed sketching and fully delayed updates reduces factorization time by $6.9\times$ for Laplace and $8.5\times$ for Helmholtz relative to the unsketched, eager configuration, while reducing maximum per-process resident memory by 57\% and 54\%, respectively.

title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
abstract: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized Kähler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to Kähler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $ν$-soliton equation in Kähler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.

title: Temporal Exploration and Rendezvous via Weisfeiler-Leman Colorings
abstract: Temporal graphs are graphs whose edge relation changes in discrete time steps. The Temporal Exploration Problem (TEXP) asks for a temporal walk that visits all vertices. We show that every connected temporal graph with $n$ vertices can be explored in $O(qn\log^3(n))$ time steps, where $q$ is the number of vertex color classes induced by the 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman (2-WL) coloring. For small $q$, our bound substantially improves on the known worst-case bound of $Θ(n^2)$ in general connected temporal graphs. A corresponding walk can be constructed in deterministic polynomial time. The upper bound is complemented by lower bounds of $Ω(n\log(n))$ when $q$ is constant and $Ω(qn)$ when $1 \leq q \leq n$. We also apply our techniques to the Temporal Rendezvous Problem (TRP), in which two agents that do not communicate have to meet on a vertex of the temporal graph. Our exploration algorithm yields that, with only polynomial-time computational power, the agents can meet in $O(n\log^3(n))$ time steps, leaving a gap of only $\log^2(n)$ to the known lower bound. Dogeas, Erlebach, Kammer, Meintrup, and Moses Jr. [ICALP'24] have shown an $O(rn^{1+ε})$ bound for TEXP, for every fixed $ε> 0$, where $r$ is the number of orbits, and an $O(n^{1+ε})$ bound for TRP. Both results require superpolynomial computation time. Our contribution improves upon these results in several ways. First, the dependence on $n$ in the upper bounds on the number of time steps is decreased from $n^{1+ε}$ to $n\log^3(n)$ for both TEXP and TRP. Second, for TEXP, we bound the number of time steps linearly by the parameter q, which is efficiently computable and upper bounded by $r$. Third, we provide novel deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for both TEXP and TRP.
comment: Full version of a paper accepted for publication at SODA 2027. 37 pages, 3 figures

title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
abstract: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.

title: On ABP Estimates for a Class of Fully Nonlinear Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations and Applications
abstract: We establish an Alexandrov-Bakelman-Pucci type estimate for a class of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with singular or degenerate coefficients and nonlinear dependence on the gradient. The estimate bounds sub-solutions in terms of their boundary values and weighted integrals of the data. It holds for classical sub-solutions and for viscosity sub-solutions with locally Lipschitz gradients. The assumptions allow general rates of growth in the gradient, with a smallness condition on the data when the associated gradient weight has finite integral. The proof uses the classical weighted contact-set argument. As applications, we obtain sup-norm estimates for viscosity sub-solutions to a class of generalized Monge-Ampère equations, Hessian equations, Hessian quotients under an additional condition on the contact Hessian, and anisotropic mean-curvature-type equations.

title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
abstract: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.
comment: This arXiv preprint provides a detailed companion to the more concise journal-submission version of the same title. This version is not intended for separate journal publication. 415 pages

title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
abstract: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consists of sharply characterizing the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of the class of finite Gaussian mixtures. One of our key technical innovations is to sharply bound the $L^2$ bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, which may be of independent interest. As an application, we establish the regret-optimality of $g$-modeling procedures based on the NPMLE in the Gaussian Empirical Bayes problem with bounded priors.

title: A well-posedness theory for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations and a class of global-in-time solutions
abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the 2D inhomogeneous incompressible Euler equations. We show that the Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in a class of $m$-fold symmetric functions at critical regularity and allowing the velocity field to grow linearly at spatial infinity. This was a problem posed by P.L. Lions in the homogeneous, not necessarily symmetric case. A key ingredient is a variable-coefficient elliptic theory developed using quasiconformal mappings and Schauder estimates in certain scale-invariant Hölder spaces. Local well-posedness allows us to derive the one-dimensional system on $\mathbb{S}^1$ satisfied by solutions with $0$-homogeneous vorticity and density. For this system, we can obtain global well-posedness for a class of initial data away from equilibrium. We are unaware of any previous nonperturbative class of time-dependent solutions to the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Euler equations for which global well-posedness has been established. Finally, for some signed global solutions, we show a dichotomy between density homogenization and averaged relaxation in infinite time.

title: DBDSVDMR3: An MRRR-Based Bidiagonal SVD Solver Built from DSTEGR
abstract: The optimal algorithm for the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem is Multiple Relatively Robust Representations (MRRR or MR$^3$), which is capable of computing $k$ eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs in only $O(kn)$ floating-point operations. While MRRR is nearly 30 years old, it has never successfully been adapted to the bidiagonal SVD. This is not for lack of trying; two previous attempts produced implementations that were considered for LAPACK but eventually abandoned, a result of the fact that neither was reliable enough when run on test problems. The question therefore remained: is there a problem with the theory of MRRR for the bidiagonal SVD or were there simply bugs in the previous implementations that went undetected? This paper resolves this question by presenting DBDSVDMR3 -- a new implementation of the MRRR-based algorithm for the bidiagonal SVD originally proposed by Willems and Lang [ETNA 2012], which, for the first time, performs well on a variety of test problems while achieving significant speedups over both LAPACK's bisection-based solver and, in certain cases, divide-and-conquer for the bidiagonal SVD (thereby indicating that the theory is sound). DBDSVDMR3 will be available in the next release of LAPACK. In this paper, we discuss the design of our implementation, which was obtained with the help of Claude Code, and exhibit its performance on a diverse set of test problems.

title: Joint Uniform Continuity of Reduced Free Products for strong convergence
abstract: We investigate a generalization of Skoufranis' theorem on joint continuity of free products of laws in the strong topology. Namely, we show that this operation is moreover \emph{uniformly continuous}. Our methods follows those of Piser and go through the estimates of Ricard-Xu.
comment: 14 pages, no figures. No LLM's were used at any stage during this research project. Comments welcome!

title: When Standardization Spreads Factor Variation Across the Spectrum
abstract: Standardizing variables by their sample standard deviations is routine in multivariate analysis and removes marginal scale differences before dependence is assessed. The resulting correlation matrix captures both dominant common components and dependence beyond them. A central inferential difficulty arises because the same random sample variances normalize the entire spectrum. In spiked covariance models, the sampling errors of leading and residual eigenvalues can become asymptotically independent. Sample standardization fundamentally changes this behavior and can preserve their dependence, allowing strong factors to remain a major source of uncertainty even after the leading eigenvalues are excluded. To obtain valid inference for both residual and full spectrum statistics, we establish their joint sampling law for sample correlation matrices with diverging spikes. The theory reveals exact trace compensation and statistic dependent transitions between asymptotic independence and dependence as the spikes grow. It leads to tests of an identity correlation matrix under strong factors and a feasible two sample comparison of residual spectral concentration. A sex balanced HapMap analysis illustrates the substantial effect of factor variation on residual spectrum inference.

title: AnyonWiki.org
abstract: The AnyonWiki is an open-source project that provides full algebraic and numerical data of fusion and unitary modular fusion categories as a resource for the scientific community. It comes with a database, the AnyonWikiDatabase, that currently includes the classification of multiplicity-free pivotal (braided) fusion categories through rank 7 and more than 25000 fusion rings including the classification of multiplicity-free fusion rings through rank 10, with work in progress to expand. This data is available through AnyonWiki.org, a website that provides robust search and download functionality and presents each fusion ring and category via a dedicated webpage. In this short article we discuss the data available at AnyonWiki.org as well as the scientific and communal motivations for the design of its underlying AnyonWikiDatabase, which are centered around making the data accessible, independently verifiable, granularly citable, useful, and easy to work with.
comment: 10 pages, for the associated website see https://anyonwiki.org/

title: The Dynamics of RMSProp Beyond the Stability Threshold
abstract: We study what happens to RMSProp when the learning rate is too large for convergence to the minimizer. For positive-definite quadratic loss functions, we show that the minimizer is Lyapunov un- stable above an explicit critical learning rate. Nevertheless, every trajectory eventually enters a compact trapping region. We obtain explicit bounds proportional to h in the spatial variables and to h2 in the memory variables, where h is the learning rate. We also prove that nontrivial period-two orbits exist precisely above the critical learning rate, and under additional spectral assumptions, an attracting branch of these orbits emerges from the minimizer. For sufficiently large learning rates, we construct branches near admissible corners of a cube. We then explore the dynamics inside the trapping region using the parameterization method and numerical continuation, exploring invariant circles and tori, coexistence of attracting sets, circle-doubling sequences, and chaotic motions. We examine how the dynamics depend on the loss Hessian, memory decay, and dimension. Finally, we test a learning-rate reduction schedule and continue selected invariant circles into an autonomous variant of the Adam optimizer.

title: A linear, second-order, unconditionally energy-stable scalar-auxiliary-variable scheme for the CHQ viscoelastic phase-separation model
abstract: The CHQ model describes viscoelastic phase separation in a polymer--solvent mixture: a Cahn--Hilliard equation for the polymer volume fraction $φ$ is two-way coupled, through a phase-dependent cross-diffusion flux, to a damped relaxation equation for a scalar bulk elastic stress $q$. We propose a scalar-auxiliary-variable (SAV) time discretisation of this system, combining the SAV reformulation of the double-well potential with a second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2) and a second-order extrapolation of all phase-dependent mobilities: a linear, computationally cheaper complement to the reference scheme's fully nonlinear Newton solve. The resulting method is (i) linear at every time step, with a coupling structure we prove has exactly one solution at every step, for every choice of time-step size; (ii) mass conserving, exactly, as an algebraic identity of the discrete equations themselves (the only drift ever seen numerically traces to the finite tolerance of the iterative linear solver, not a failure of the conservation property); and (iii) unconditionally stable for a modified discrete energy, via an exact one-step energy--dissipation identity. We show the energy identity extends to this filtered variant as well, with two explicit extra non-negative terms. Hence, the scheme actually producing the physics results is itself provably stable for the same energy. A Fourier--Galerkin implementation verifies that the energy identity holds at every time step to within floating-point round-off. It also confirms second-order temporal accuracy, including in the steep-interface regime, and agreement with an independently implemented nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver. Compared with that independent nonlinear Newton--BDF2 solver, at equal grid resolution, the SAV method uses $2.5$--$3.0\times$ fewer linear-solver iterations and $1.7$--$2.0\times$ less wall-clock time.

title: Parallel AI Agent Collaboration as Graph-Structured Distributed Block Optimization
abstract: Parallel AI agents can produce useful local edits yet degrade a shared solution when their edits are combined. We model this coordination problem as discrete block optimization with an exactly evaluable objective and a known dependency graph. Independent sets certify compatible edits whose verified gains, measured against the same current solution, add exactly. A coordinator constructs a safe compatible candidate and can also evaluate interacting edits to capture favorable interactions. We prove that an optimal fractional coloring yields a merger that preserves a $1/χ_f(G)$ fraction of the total verified local improvement, where $χ_f(G)$ is the graph's fractional chromatic number. This guarantee is tight among mergers that select a subset of the same proposals. Under conditional local-improvement guarantees and a block error-bound condition, repeated collaboration converges geometrically in the objective gap. The rate separates task structure, agent allocation, and computation cost, yielding a linear program for agent assignment and an explicit time-cost trade-off. Code-repair experiments show that verified merging resolves conflicts between individually useful edits that cause naive merging to fail. On larger conflict-free tasks, parallel agents reduce modeled completion time at higher input-token-equivalent cost. On three public road networks, fractional integration retains 922 units of verified graph-cut improvement across 90 paired runs. For route-search agents sharing exclusive access to vehicle routes, fractional scheduling reduces measured wall time by a median of 15% across twelve paired runs, with route-cost changes varying across runs.

title: When Windowed Anderson Acceleration Converges Faster
abstract: Windowed Anderson acceleration AA($m$) combines at most $m+1$ recent iterates by least squares. For a real affine contraction $x\mapsto Wx+b$ with $q=\|W\| \in(0,1)$, we determine exactly when AA($m$) converges from every starting point with an asymptotic factor below $q$. We give a polynomial criterion for this improvement and an equivalent spectral condition: there is no probability distribution on the phases of the eigenvalues of modulus $q$ whose first $m$ cosine moments are $q,q^2,\ldots,q^m$. If such a distribution exists, we construct a starting point from which AA($m$) reproduces fixed-point iteration at every step. Otherwise, over a fixed number of consecutive steps, every run contracts the residual norm by a common factor strictly smaller than the corresponding power of $q$. The polynomial criterion also gives explicit convergence-rate bounds with constants independent of the dimension. When $q$ equals the spectral radius, this characterizes improvement over the asymptotic convergence factor of fixed-point iteration.
