For general affine contractions, the asymptotic factor never exceeds the numerical radius of $W$, and a related moment condition gives a uniform upper bound strictly below that radius.

title: Alternative moduli of twisted curves
abstract: We define new Artin stack compactifications of the moduli of smooth curves, which parameterize "relatively polarized curves" consisting of stacky semistable curves equipped with line bundles that are trivialized away from the rational bridges. Using techniques from birational geometry, we prove that stacks of relatively polarized curves admit the classical coarse space $\overline{M}_g$ of stable curves as a good moduli space. One of our main motivations is a companion paper where we construct a proper moduli space of $\mathrm{SL}_N$-bundles on relatively polarized curves. This suggests the hypothesis that relatively polarized curves are suitable sources for defining Gromov-Witten theory for Artin stack targets.

title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.

title: On the proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture
abstract: In this short note, we give an exposition of the recent proof of the Kozma-Nitzan conjecture provided by OpenAI.

title: Unitary similarity for dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices
abstract: We study unitary similarity of dual complex matrices and dual quaternion matrices. First, we characterize unitary similarity in terms of the existence of a skew-Hermitian solution to a Sylvester-type matrix equation. For $2\times2$ dual complex matrices, we obtain a complete three-trace criterion when the standard part is nonnormal and analyze the limitations of trace-word criteria when the standard part is normal. We then prove, for every $n\geq1$, that two $n\times n$ dual quaternion matrices are unitarily similar if and only if their dual complex adjoint matrices are unitarily similar, and we extend this result to finite families. As a scalar consequence, we derive a finite Trace-word criterion when the standard part is nonreal and exhibit its failure when the standard part is real.

title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
abstract: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.
comment: 36 pages, 4 tables; supplementary material (25 pages) as an ancillary file. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23440726 (https://github.com/methodtrace/2026-doubly-stochastic-xray-facets). Companion paper: arXiv:2610.24197

title: Differential powers of monomial ideals in affine semigroup rings
abstract: This article gives explicit descriptions for differential powers of monomial ideals in certain (possibly non-normal) affine semigroup rings. We use these descriptions to show that the topologies defined by the ordinary, symbolic, and differential powers of any monomial ideal are all linearly equivalent. We then prove the existence of differential signature in our settings, relating it to the volume of some convex polytope. Finally, we apply our results to pinched Veronese rings.

title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $ω_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $ω_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $ω_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $ω_\mathbb{F}$ and $ω_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.

title: On OpenAI's proof of the Nagata conjecture
abstract: These notes are an expanded account of my talk at UMass Amherst on OpenAI's remarkably simple proof of the Nagata conjecture. I hope they will be useful, especially to non-experts. The standard reduction to the normal cone and the collision of fat points into one monomial scheme reduce the problem to interpolation of monomial schemes on the normal ruled surface of a smooth plane cubic. The novelty is that the study of the asymptotics of theta functions as the cubic develops a node, together with interpolation duality, reduces the problem further to interpolation on a triangle of lattice points, which is straightforward. The same calculation determines the nef and pseudoeffective cones of a weighted blow-up of ${\Bbb P}^2$ at one point for very general local parameters when the ratio of weights is greater than nine.

title: Long-time dynamics of viscous Gröbli triangles
abstract: In 1877 Gröbli discovered that three point vortices in the plane can move self-similarly, forming a triangle that rotates while either expanding indefinitely or collapsing in finite time. We study the viscous counterpart of these configurations, namely the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes evolution starting from three point vortices arranged in a Gröbli triangle. In the expanding case, viscosity spreads the vortex cores at the same rate as the triangle grows, so the vortices remain well separated relative to their size. Building on this observation, we show that at high Reynolds number the solution stays close to three Lamb--Oseen vortices centered near the vertices of the inviscid triangle for times that grow exponentially with a power of the Reynolds number. In the collapsing case, the same description holds up to times close to the inviscid collision. As an application of the long-time result in the expanding case, we obtain a vanishing viscosity realization of the vortex burst, a nonuniqueness mechanism for point vortices in which a single vortex splits into an expanding Gröbli triangle.
comment: 68 pages, 4 figures, SageMath script in the supplementary material

title: Irregular Gabor Frames for the Poisson Kernel
abstract: Consider the semi-regular system of time-frequency shifts of the Poisson kernel $g(t) = {{1} \over {t^2+w^2}}$ $$\G(g, M \times α\Z) = \left\{ e^{2πi λt } g(t-n) \colon (λ, n) \in M \times α\Z \right\}$$ where $M \subset \R$. We obtain {\it a criterion} for $\G(g, M \times α\Z)$ to form a frame in $L^2(\R)$ for an {\it arbitrary} set $M$ of finite upper density. It turned out that the lower density alone does not determine the frame property, even when $M$ is uniformly discrete.

title: Dual Effect and Certainty Equivalence Revisited for a Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
abstract: This paper revisits the relation between dual effect and certainty equivalence (CE) through a scalar linear-Gaussian model. In dual control, the current input affects not only the immediate cost but also the information available for future decisions, and hence the future cost. Dynamic programming (DP) provides a natural framework for formulating dual control problems. At each step of the Bellman recursion, an optimal input minimizes the sum of the stage cost and the expected cost-to-go. We restrict attention to stage costs minimized by the CE input. However, CE may not minimize the Bellman objective because of the input-dependent expected cost-to-go. Classical no-dualeffect (NDE) conditions guarantee CE optimality in certain problem classes by requiring the conditional distribution of the estimation error to be independent of past controls. In the present model, we observe that CE can remain optimal at the level of a single Bellman recursion even when the classical NDE conditions fail, provided that the expected cost-to-go is independent of the current input. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a notion of NDE formulated directly at the level of the Bellman objective, which we call Bellman-side NDE. Under some mild regularity conditions, we show that Bellman-side NDE can be characterized by a heat equation. This characterization identifies the class of Bellman-side NDE functions, and further yields a decomposition of a generic cost-to-go function into a Bellman-side NDE component and a dual-effect component.

title: The recent counterexamples to the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman Ulrich problem (2003) and to Hochster's small Cohen-Macaulay conjecture (1973): a survey, with a generalization to arbitrary dimension
abstract: In September 2026 four preprints and an AI-generated manuscript moved one numerical obstruction from projective geometry to local algebra. For a smooth complex projective surface $Y$ with an ample, globally generated divisor $H$ such that $H^2<σ(Y)$, the signature, one obtains in turn: no Ulrich bundles when $H$ is very ample (Anghel, arXiv:2609.02718; extended to every dimension by Lopez, arXiv:2609.06678), answering negatively the Eisenbud-Schreyer-Weyman question of 2003 for sheaves supported on the whole variety; no arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay bundles, i.e. section rings without graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules in characteristic zero (Anghel, arXiv:2609.15589); and complete local domains without small Cohen-Macaulay modules, counterexamples to Hochster's 1973 conjecture, if $K_Y\equiv4H$ (Chen, arXiv:2609.24142, proposed) or $σ>2H^2$ (OpenAI, released 6 October). We recall the definitions and main statements, and add two things. First, through a finite projection to $\mathbb P^2$ and an identity already present in the OpenAI manuscript, the three obstructions become one variance identity; for surfaces this explains the factor $2$ between the graded bound $σ\le H^2$ and the local $σ\le2H^2$. Second, we generalize the argument of the OpenAI manuscript to every dimension $m\ge2$, with complete proofs: if $X$ is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $m$ and $H$ an ample, globally generated divisor, a small Cohen-Macaulay module over the completed section ring of $(X,H)$ forces $(K_X^2-2c_2(X))\cdot H^{m-2}\le(m+4)H^m$. Consequently the completed section rings of all Hesse pairs, including the ball quotient of the first preprint, have no small Cohen-Macaulay module, and products of Hesse surfaces with projective spaces give complete local domains with an isolated singularity, of every dimension $\ge3$, without small Cohen-Macaulay modules.
comment: 25 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Survey; Sections 9 and 10 contain new results with complete proofs

title: Zeros of $E_2$, quasi-periods, and Schwarz maps
abstract: We study the zeros of the Eisenstein series $E_2$, their distribution near rational cusps, and the values of modular functions at these zeros. Using Watson's inversion formula, we prove that the number of zeros in $0\leq\operatorname{Re}τ<1$ with imaginary part at least $Y$ satisfies \[ N(Y)=\frac{1}{2πY} +O\!\left(Y^{-1/2}\log\frac1Y\right) \qquad(Y\to0^+). \] We also determine the limiting distribution of the scaled displacements from the cusps and prove that two zeros whose difference is rational differ by an integer. At every zero $ρ$, classical transcendence theorems imply that both $j(ρ)$ and $λ(ρ)$ are transcendental. We use this fact to obtain an exact multiplicity formula for arithmetic quasimodular forms at arbitrary congruence level and to show that all ordinary derivatives of arithmetic modular functions on congruence subgroups, evaluated at $ρ$, are algebraic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}(j(ρ),j'(ρ))$. We then relate Watson's formula to the Schwarz map of a rational transform of the Legendre hypergeometric equation. Finally, we give conditional results on the transcendence of $ρ$ under modular Schanuel and period conjectures, and determine why the associated analytic subgroup fails the rank condition in Waldschmidt's theorem.

title: Tempered Langevin diffusions with polynomial-tailed targets: explosions, moment thresholds and ergodicity
abstract: For tempered Langevin diffusions (TLDs) targeting polynomially tailed measures, the convergence rate is known to change from polynomial to exponential to uniform as the temperature rises through a critical value. We explain this transition by the tails of the marginal laws of the norm of the TLD, up to a second, larger critical temperature beyond which the TLD explodes. As the temperature increases, these tails change from stretched-exponential, through super-polynomial at the first critical temperature, to polynomial, mirroring the transition in the convergence rate. Moreover, this tail analysis gives a complete quantification of the convergence rates throughout the non-explosive regime, in both $f$-variation and Wasserstein distances.
comment: 24 pages; for short YouTube presentation discussing the main results, see https://youtu.be/P0yIqm6K5r0, and proofs, see https://youtu.be/ygnPmOUINWM

title: On the gap of thresholds
abstract: We propose an algorithm to compute the gap numbers of log canonical thresholds, anticanonical thresholds, and $\mathbb{R}$-complementary thresholds for surface pairs with a given rational hyperstandard coefficient set. As an example, we compute these gap numbers for a special hyperstandard set that appears in the effective boundedness of $n$-complements for surface pairs.

title: On optimal (v,5,3,1) optical orthogonal codes
abstract: In this paper, we establish a tight upper bound for the size of a $(v,5,3,1)$ optical orthogonal code (OOC) and call such a code optimal when it achieves this upper bound. In addition, if an optimal OOC has the property that all non-identity elements of $\mathbb{Z}_v$ are covered by the list of differences of its codeword-sets then it is called perfect. In this paper, we present direct and recursive constructions for infinite classes of optimal and perfect $(v,5,3,1)$-OOCs.

title: Almost Every Pair of Interval Exchange Transformations Does Not Generate a Free Group
abstract: We show that the Lebesgue measure of the set of pairs of interval exchange transformations that generate a free group of rank $2$ is zero.

title: On the strict approximation of currents and space-time trajectories
abstract: This work establishes a wide variety of strict approximation results for space-time trajectories, a class of space-time currents that are used to model the evolution of dislocations in crystalline materials. In particular, we introduce a strict-type notion of convergence which respects quantities associated with geometric transport phenomena and prove approximation results in this topology. These results build on the classical strict approximation results for normal and integral currents developed by Federer and Fleming, which we also review and refine.

title: On $k$-connected Sets in Matroids
abstract: In 1966, Tutte defined $k$-connected matroids for each $k \ge 2$. Robertson and Seymour built on Tutte's idea to define tangles as a way to identify highly connected parts of a matroid. Motivated by tangles, a set $Z$ in a matroid $M$ has been defined to be $3$-connected if, for each $j$ in $\{1,2\}$, there is no $j$-separation $(X,Y)$ of $M$ such that each of $|Z \cap X|$ and $|Z \cap Y|$ is at least $j$. This paper solves a problem of Whittle for $k= 3$ by proving that a minor-minimal matroid having $Z$ as a $3$-connected set has at most $3|Z| - 4$ elements. We also identify the matroids for which this bound is attained.

title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.

title: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical Groups
abstract: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical GroupsLet $q$ be a power of an odd prime. For the unipotent radicals of maximal rational parabolic subgroups of the finite symplectic, orthogonal and unitary groups, we determine all complex irreducible characters, their values, and the number of characters of each degree. Each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q-1$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, in analogy with a conjecture of Isaacs for unitriangular groups. For the orthogonal radicals, the character table and the power maps do not depend on the Witt type of the residual form, whereas the isomorphism type of the radical does when the isotropic dimension is at least three and the residual dimension is positive and even. Consequently, for $3\le a\le n-1$ the radicals of the stabilizers of totally isotropic $a$-spaces in $\SO^+_{2n}(q)$ and $\SO^-_{2n}(q)$ form Brauer pairs; for $a\le n-2$ both stabilizers are maximal parabolic subgroups. Finally, we express the multiplicities through $R$-polynomials, with the unequal parameters $q^2,\dots,q^2,q$ in the unitary case.

title: Nonlinear Inviscid Damping of Couette Flow with Vorticity Perturbations Supported up to the Boundary
abstract: We establish nonlinear inviscid damping of the near-Couette flows in a finite channel, with vorticity perturbations vanishing to infinite order at the boundary. To study the boundary effect, we decompose the vorticity into dyadic layers whose supports expand toward the boundary, and use an inductive Newton scheme to track nonlinear interactions across layers. Finally, precise elliptic estimates are established to quantify the velocity generated by different layers.

title: On Divisibility Properties of Zipf Law and Relatives
abstract: We describe recursive chance mechanisms and processes involving Zipf's law and relatives, all showing up mixing properties, both geometric and Poisson. Relations to Markov processes are explored.

title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.

title: Differentiability of Shape Function for Piecewise Smooth Lagrangians in Poissonian Random Environments
abstract: We consider a family of models of directed first passage percolation type in continuous multi-dimensional Euclidean space and discrete time with admissible paths constrained to visiting a Poissonian point at each step. We show that even if the Lagrangian defining the cost or energy of a step is allowed to have gradient discontinuities, the resulting shape function, or effective Lagrangian, belongs to the class C1 and provide a formula for its gradient. We also study the limit shapes for the associated growth model. We show that the part of the boundary of the limit shape that can be called the effective front is also C1, and we describe the complementary part, the footprint. We include a study of several concrete examples and several simulations.

title: A Sharp Bound for Additive Complements
abstract: Let $A$ and $B$ be infinite sets of nonnegative integers whose sum contains all sufficiently large integers, and let $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ be their counting functions. We give a discrete proof of the sharp implication \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac32 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A(x)B(x)-x\longrightarrow+\infty. \] The constant $3/2$ is best possible. Using finite convolution sums, we show that a long gap in one set forces a gap in the other. We then compare the counting functions before and after the gap to obtain the sharp bound.

title: Rigidity of the ball for Hartree-type energies and second shape derivative via a continuity argument
abstract: We study the second shape derivative of an optimal design functional involving a nonlocal term in order to prove rigidity of the ball. Our approach relies on a continuity argument that relates the second variation to that of the corresponding local problem. The model serves as a prototype for a broader class of shape optimization problems to which the same strategy may be adapted.

title: Saturating spaces for the squared-gradient nonlinearity on compact Riemannian manifolds via Nash embeddings
abstract: We study the saturation property on smooth compact Riemannian manifolds without boundary. Starting from a finite-dimensional space of smooth functions, one considers successive iterations of the nonlinear map $f\mapsto|\nabla_g f|_g^2$ and convex combinations. We extend to the general setting of compact manifolds existing results on particular geometries, namely the torus, spheres and Lie groups. Our approach relies on the existence of an isometric embedding of the manifold into $\mathbb{R}^n$ due to Nash. As an application, we obtain global approximate controllability in arbitrarily small time for the bilinear Schrödinger equation on any connected compact Riemannian manifold, with finitely many potentials.

title: Compression Formula for Nonattacking Fillings of Non-symmetric Macdonald Polynomials
abstract: Macdonald polynomials are an important family of orthogonal polynomials that have applications to statistical physics. Corteel, Mandelshtam, and Williams proved a combinatorial model involving multiline queues for partitions; however, their work does not apply to weak compositions in general. We conjecture a first step towards this direction via a variant of the nonattacking filling model for nonsymmetric Macdonald Polynomials $E_μ$. This new model compresses the classical nonattacking filling model of Haglund, Haiman, and Loehr and mirrors the concept of trivial pairs in the multiline queue model. We prove it for a large family of weak compositions and explain the difficulty of extending this proof to the general case.

title: Existence of Minimizers for the Gaussian Mumford-Shah Model via Covariance Floors on the Value Distribution
abstract: The Gaussian Mumford-Shah model segments an image into regions by minimizing a continuous multivariate Gaussian negative log-likelihood term plus a perimeter penalty. It is used for scalar- and vector-valued images, in particular hyperspectral images, but the existence of a minimizer in general is not guaranteed. The energy is unbounded below whenever the covariance of a single region degenerates, regardless of the perimeter of the regions. A quantitative covariance floor on the covariances of all regions, or equivalently uniform Hölder continuity with exponent at most one of all one-dimensional marginals of the histogram, guarantees a lower bound on the energy and the existence of a minimizer. Our approach therefore shows that existence follows from a property of the histogram of the image, and we furthermore argue that scale-independent covariance floors cannot exist. Admitting a quantitative covariance floor is generic: it holds almost surely for all images with suitable noise. As applications of our theory, we show the convergence of regularized models used in practice and of numerical methods.

title: Twisting of affine algebraic groups, III
abstract: Let $G$ be an affine algebraic group over $\C$ and let $J$ be a Hopf $2$-cocycle for $\Os(G)$. We prove that one-sided cocycle twisting preserves Gelfand--Kirillov dimension and that $\Os(G)_J$ is simple if and only if $J$ is minimal. If $H$ is the support of $J$, we identify the primitive and maximal spectra of $\Os(G)_J$ with the closed points of $G/H$ and show that all primitive quotients are isomorphic to the minimal support algebra $\Os(H)_J$. In particular, the prime and Jacobson radicals vanish, and finite-dimensional irreducible modules exist exactly when $H$ is finite. For connected solvable $G$, we construct an iterated differential Ore presentation over an algebraic quantum torus and deduce that $\Os(G)_J$ is an affine Noetherian domain. We describe the torus-trivial Hopf $2$-cocycles on $\Os(G)$ using nilpotent solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation and identify their supports with the algebraic hulls of their carriers. We also separate the centrally supported toral sector and formulate a relative Hopf $2$-cocycle problem for the remaining classes. Finally, we compute multi-extended Jordanian examples, study a McConnell-type family of quantum differential algebras, and establish a conditional birational deletion criterion and a normal form when the unipotent radical has dimension at most one.

title: Painlevé representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
abstract: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $σ$-Painlevé III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $σ$-Painlevé V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.

title: Rudin's Problem on Uniformly Bounded Homogeneous Orthonormal Bases
abstract: Rudin's problem asks whether, in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^d$ with $d\ge2$ fixed, the Hardy space $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ admits a uniformly bounded orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous holomorphic polynomials. For $d=2$ and $d=3$ the answer is due to Bourgain, but the general-dimensional case has remained open. This paper gives an affirmative answer to Rudin's problem in every fixed dimension. More precisely, we prove that there is an orthonormal basis consisting of homogeneous polynomials $\{p_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of $H^2(\partial\mathbb B_d)$ such that $$\|p_j\|_{L^\infty(\partial\mathbb B_d)}\leq \exp\left(\frac12d\log d+O(d)\right).$$ Here the implicit constant in $O(d)$ is independent of $d$ and $j$.

title: Germwise singular Fourier--Mukai partnerships
abstract: We study how local behavior on the base controls whether integral transforms induce fully faithful functors or equivalences between singularity categories of proper flat families. By working with étale germs, we show (under mild hypotheses) that the loci where this happens are open and are compatible with étale base change. Moreover, we give examples, exhibit an autoequivalence of the singularity category which detects regularity of the base, and compute these loci for arithmetic families.

title: Small-time approximate controllability of bilinear Schrödinger equations on compact normal homogeneous spaces
abstract: We prove small-time global approximate controllability in $L^2$ for bilinear Schrödinger equations on compact connected normal homogeneous spaces. The controls act through finitely many smooth real-valued potentials. We first construct finite saturating families on compact connected Lie groups endowed with bi-invariant metrics, using Peter-Weyl theory and the Casimir operator. Their phase saturation contains the representative algebra and is therefore dense in $L^2$. We extend this construction to normal homogeneous quotients using finite generation of the algebra of highest-weight functions. Global controllability follows by combining the phase-to-gradient transport argument of [8] with the gradient generation theorem of [23] and Moser's transport of positive densities.

title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $λ$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $λ$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.

title: A PDE-theory-guided neural operator and the long-time relaxation of the two-dimensional anisotropic Boussinesq system
abstract: We design a neural operator for the two-dimensional Boussinesq system with anisotropic dissipation on the periodic box, guided by a rigorous analysis of its long-time behavior. The operator maps a small perturbation of hydrostatic equilibrium, of amplitude $\varepsilon$, to the vorticity at a late time. We prove that the flow relaxes to a stratified shear flow, with the horizontally averaged vorticity staying within $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of its initial value $\barω_0$ and the oscillation about it of order $\varepsilon$. Accordingly, the network outputs $\barω_0$ plus these two parts, each scaled to its size, which grows as $\varepsilon^2$ and $\varepsilon$, respectively. Without this guidance the training either does not converge or misses the $\varepsilon^2$ growth. With it, one network reproduces, sample by sample on $2\times10^3$ test runs over a factor of $23$ in amplitude, the quantity bounded by the theorem to a median error of $2.2$ percent. Being fast and differentiable with respect to the initial data, the network is also used to search the space of initial data, and with every candidate checked by the solver the search finds initial data for which this quantity is $4.4$ times the largest value among the test runs, raising the lower bound for the constant of the theorem by that factor.

title: Normal form approach to unconditional well-posedness of the periodic stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation with an additive noise
abstract: We develop a stochastic normal form method for stochastic dispersive equations. As a model example, we study the stochastic Korteweg-de Vries equation (SKdV) with an additive noise, posed on the circle. By replacing integration by parts (in time) in the deterministic setting with Ito's product formula in the current stochastic setting, we transform SKdV with an additive noise into a stochastic normal form equation with additive and multiplicative noises. We then use the stochastic normal form equation to prove optimal pathwise unconditional global well-posedness of SKdV in $L^2(\mathbb{T})$.

title: Preventing Model Extraction in Contextual Linear Optimization
abstract: Consider a contextual linear optimization problem, where a predict-then-optimize (PTO) system returns optimal decisions without revealing the cost vectors used in its downstream linear program. Our focus is on how to prevent attackers, who can submit context queries, from extracting the underlying prediction model. Although the cost-to-decision map is many-to-one, observations across contexts can reveal the underlying prediction model. For linear models, we provide sufficient conditions where the attacker can learn the model up to positive scaling by only observing the decision. These conditions motivate an adaptive attack that alternates inverse optimization with boundary sampling, i.e., using context queries leading to decision boundaries of the current attacker model. To prevent extraction, we propose a mechanism that perturbs decisions only when the predicted cost vector is near a decision boundary. We establish a regret bound in terms of the perturbation radius. For the attackers that fit the defended responses as optimal decisions under the evaluation distribution, we also prove a lower bound on expected extraction error. Experiments on synthetic instances and real data quantify the security-performance trade-off of the defense mechanism and illustrate that our defense can increase the extraction error.

title: Multiplicity of brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization bundles
abstract: We prove multiplicity results for geometrically distinct brake Reeb orbits on real prequantization $S^1$-bundles under geometric and dynamical assumptions. The lower bounds are expressed in terms of the sum of the mod-two Betti numbers of the real locus of the base. Our proofs combine Lagrangian Rabinowitz Floer homology with the index iteration theory for brake orbits. As an application, we obtain a sharp lower bound for the number of brake geodesics on Finsler spheres with pinched flag curvature.

title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.

title: Derived categories of threefolds near the Noether line
abstract: We show that derived categories of canonical stacks associated to general threefolds in the principal component of the moduli space of canonical threefolds on the refined Noether line are semiorthogonally indecomposable. First we generalize a criterion of Kawatani-Okawa for the indecomposability of derived categories of surfaces of general type to higher-dimensional varieties and stacks. And then we generalize a construction of Kobayashi and Hu-Zhang and a classification result of Coughlan-Pignatelli to the second and third Noether lines to show that our criterion applies to these canonical stacks.
comment: 30 pages, 1 figure. Comments are very welcome

title: Squarefree values of random polynomials are Gaussian mixtures
abstract: Fix $d\ge1$ and choose a polynomial $P$ uniformly at random from the set of integer polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients have absolute value at most $H$. We study $E_{P}$, the error in the count of squarefree values $P(n)$ for $n\leq x$. In the range $x=H^{o\left(1\right)}$, we prove that $E_{P}\left(x\right)/x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ converges to a Gaussian mixture that is not itself Gaussian, $\sqrt{C\left(G\right)}Z$, where $G$ is the weak limit, as $H\rightarrow\infty$, of the prime-indexed vector $\left(P\bmod p^{2}\right)_{p}$, $C$ is a nonnegative function and $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian. This answers a question of Sofos. Finally, in the appendix, we establish that $\log \mathbb{E}[C(G)^m]\asymp_d m^2/(\log m)^2$ as $m\to\infty$.

title: Worst-Case Finite-Horizon Analysis of Perturbed LQR via Performance Estimation Problem
abstract: We propose an exact formulation to quantify the finite-horizon robustness of a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) subject to norm-bounded Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) parametric uncertainties, using the Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) framework. Originally developed for optimization, this method allows us to reformulate the worst-case performance search as a rank-constrained Semidefinite Program (SDP). By applying operator interpolation, this formulation retains the sequence variables, allowing the worst-case to be explicitly reconstructed when a rank-one solution is found. This approach also opens new possibilities for the finite-horizon certification of broader system classes, such as data-driven models or nonlinear components. Using this framework, we observe that finite-horizon LTI perturbations do not simply follow asymptotic strategies. Instead, they align slowly decaying invariant manifolds with specific initial conditions to drive transient growth, causing a bifurcation in the worst-case behavior as the horizon length changes. Finally, we show numerically that our performance bounds sit between the upper bounds of Integral Quadratic Constraint (IQC) relaxations and a lower bound derived from a pseudospectral heuristic.

title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schrödinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Global-Local Control of Dynamic Networks with Applications to Systemic Risk
abstract: We propose a reinforcement learning framework for solving control problems on dynamic networks, where control decisions consist of a combination of graph-level (global) and node-level (local) actions. To exploit the underlying network structure in a policy-gradient algorithm, we introduce a message-passing neural network architecture with separate global and local policy heads. The architecture ensures that the resulting policies satisfy natural permutation symmetries and transparency constraints. Our main theoretical contribution is an analysis of the robustness and regularity properties of the proposed architecture. We derive explicit Lipschitz bounds with respect to both parameter and input perturbations and use these estimates to establish convergence guarantees for a projected policy-gradient algorithm. The resulting constants reveal how architectural choices and graph characteristics influence sensitivity to input perturbations and the convergence behavior of gradient-based optimization methods. As an application, we study the management of systemic risk in financial networks, where a regulator allocates capital interventions across interconnected institutions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed reinforcement learning architecture outperforms standard architectures based on feedforward neural networks while the learned policies fulfill desirable symmetry and transparency constraints. The algorithm scales to large networks and effectively combines global budget decisions with local allocation policies by exploiting the underlying graph structure.

title: Kelly's conjectures on Condorcet winner probabilities for odd electorates
abstract: Let $C(m,n)$ denote the probability that, among $n$ independent uniformly random permutations of $m$ labels, there exists a label that precedes every other label in a strict majority of the permutations. We prove that $C(m,n)>C(m,n+2)$ for $m \ge 3$ and odd $n \ge 1$, and that $C(m,n)>C(m+1,n)$ for $m \ge 2$ and odd $n \ge 3$. These results establish Kelly's two monotonicity conjectures for odd electorates. The proofs use integral representations involving probabilities associated with sums of independent Bernoulli random variables.

title: Relaxation and $Γ$-Convergence of Stretch Energy on Surface Homeomorphisms
abstract: Area-preserving parameterization of triangular meshes is an essential task in geometry processing, yet an exactly area-preserving simplicial mapping may not exist in general. In this paper, we study area preservation of simplicial mappings in the limit of mesh refinement by establishing the $Γ$-convergence of the discrete stretch energy, a functional that measures their area distortion. We first introduce its limit functional, the relaxed stretch energy on surface homeomorphisms, defined through the pushforward of the area measure, and show that it is the relaxation of the stretch energy of diffeomorphisms with respect to uniform convergence. Then, to compare simplicial mappings with homeomorphisms, we construct a geometric lift that requires no shape-regularity assumption on the image mesh. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence and show that the minimal discrete energies converge to the continuum minimum. Moreover, any homeomorphism arising as a limit of lifted discrete local minimizers in fixed-radius balls is area-preserving.

title: Observability Inequality for a Multi-Dimensional Degenerate Schrödinger Equation with an Interior Degeneracy Point
abstract: We study the observability inequality for a multi-dimensional degenerate Schrödinger equation possessing an interior degeneracy point, where the principal coefficient vanishes at the origin inside the domain and breaks ellipticity. Within a weighted Sobolev space, we establish the spectral properties, well-posedness, and regularity estimates for the degenerate operator. To tackle the failure of classical controllability tools, we develop a regularization approximation scheme. We construct a sequence of non-degenerate approximating problems. We then establish uniform a-priori estimates and solution convergence. Furthermore, we derive an observability inequality for the regularized problems and pass to the limit. This yields a non-standard observability inequality for the original degenerate equation for sufficiently large observation time, which quantifies the influence of the degeneracy strength on the observation time. Crucially, we establish the precise parameter restriction $3α+ N > 4$ to ensure that every test function in $C_0^\infty(Ω)$ belongs to $D(\mathcal A^{\frac 32})$.

title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
abstract: The random hypergraph process starts with an empty hypergraph on $n$ vertices and adds a uniformly chosen missing edge at each step. For even $n$, we prove that, with high probability, a $3$-uniform loose Hamilton cycle appears when the last isolated vertex disappears. The approach developed here adapts arguments from Kahn's work on perfect matchings. It can also be extended to obtain the corresponding hitting-time theorems for $r=2$ and every fixed $r\ge4$ satisfying $(r-1)\mid n$. Furthermore, it can be used to estimate the numbers of loose Hamilton cycles at these hitting times for every fixed $r\ge2$, up to a factor of $\exp\{o(n)\}$.

title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
abstract: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

title: On complete Ricci--flat Kähler manifolds
abstract: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat Kähler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat Kähler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no Kähler compactification.

title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].
comment: 36 pages, 4 tables. Supplementary software documentation is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190651

title: Competitive Lotka-Volterra systems with random catastrophes: invasion fitnesses and reversal of the competitive hierarchy
abstract: We study a two-type individual-based population with logistic competition subject to random catastrophes: at the epochs of a Poisson process, each individual survives independently with a random, type-dependent probability. In the large-population limit, the process converges to a competitive Lotka-Volterra system perturbed by multiplicative jumps. We show that the long-time behaviour of this system -exclusion of one type or the other, or coexistence -is governed by two averaged invasion fitnesses, obtained from the classical ones by replacing each growth rate a i with its average {ā}i = a i + rE[ln $Θ$ (i) ], where r is the catastrophe rate and $Θ$ (i) is the survival probability of an individual of type i when a catastrophe occurs. A consequence is that catastrophes can reverse the competitive hierarchy: a type doomed to exclusion in the deterministic system may persist or even exclude its competitor, when catastrophes are frequent enough, even if each catastrophe is individually more harmful to it. In the finite population setting, we also study the invasion of a mutant on the time scale ln K, where K is a scaling parameter, through a coupling with branching processes in the varying random environment generated by the resident population.

title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.

title: On the notion of reasonable functions in Cohen--Lenstra type heuristics
abstract: We elucidate the notion of "reasonable functions" in the context of Cohen--Lenstra heuristics. For a sequence $(x_i)_i$ of independent random variables valued in an infinite discrete probability space $(X,p)$, we investigate for what sets $S$ of functions on $X$ it is true that almost surely, for all $f\in S$, the average of $f$ on the sequence is equal to its expected value. We show that if $p$ decays sufficiently quickly, as e.g. the Cohen--Lenstra distribution does, then $\bigcup_{q>1}L^q(X)$ is such a set; while if $p$ decays sufficiently slowly, then not even $\bigcap_{q<\infty}L^q(X)$ has this property.

title: Roe algebras and coarse index maps for spaces with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids. II
abstract: Building on the Roe algebra framework developed in the first paper of this series, we construct equivariant coarse index maps for locally compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with proper actions of {é}tale groupoids, with coefficients in any separable groupoid C* -algebra. The construction uses the coarse structures determined by the groupoid action and requires no choice of metric. By identifying Roe algebras of canonical modules with reduced crossed products, we prove that the Baum-Connes assembly map with coefficients factors through the coarse index map.

title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
abstract: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((ρ|ρ^\vee)+\|ρ\|\,\|ρ^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.

title: Sharp Moser-Onofri inequality on the CR sphere under zero-moment constraints and its application to the stability of the CR Moser-Onofri inequality
abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. By combining a decomposition into low and high spherical harmonics with the known CR localization estimates, we first prove the existence of extremals of the subcritical Moser--Onofri inequality under zero-moment constraints. We then derive their Euler--Lagrange equation, establish their smoothness, and eliminate the moment multiplier by means of the infinitesimal CR conformal action. Using the summation identity (4.9) on the Hardy space $H^2(B^n)$, we show that the extremals of subcritical Moser-Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints are constants. By a limiting argument, we deduce the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints. As an application, we establish the stability of Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere with the best stability constant.
comment: In this paper, we establish the sharp Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere under zero-moment constraints and deduces the stability of Moser--Onofri inequality in CR sphere with the best stability constant

title: Integral trace forms of cyclic number fields without tameness
abstract: Let $K/\mathbf{Q}$ be a cyclic number field and let $T_K=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_K,(x,y)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbf{Q}}(xy)\bigr)$ be its integral trace lattice. We prove that two cyclic number fields have isometric integral trace lattices if and only if they have the same degree, signature, and signed discriminant. More generally, an isomorphism between the Dirichlet character groups of two finite abelian extensions that preserves the conductor and parity of every character yields an isometry of their integral trace lattices, equivariant for the dual identification of Galois groups. For cyclic fields, the degree, signature, and discriminant determine the character group together with these two functions. This proves Bolaños's conjecture for wildly ramified cyclic fields and gives the corresponding extension of the tame classification: in general, the signature must be retained as an additional invariant.

title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
abstract: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{à} di Bruno formula. We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

title: Recovering Plausible Transmission Outage Scenarios
abstract: Expansion planning for extreme weather needs outage scenarios that specify which transmission branches fail. However, public outage records often only report customers without power by county, making it unclear how to exploit this information to create outage scenarios. We propose a method to recover sets of outaged branches that most closely match regional load shed data. This gives us sets of plausible outages for a given hazard event. We formulate a bilevel problem with a load shedding DC optimal power flow in the lower level. We relax the binary branch states to differentiate the lower level problem, replace it with its sensitivity matrix, and use gradient descent to update the upper level. We treat the relaxed branch states as probabilities and perform randomized rounding to restore integrality. On three test systems with synthetic outages, the recovered sets reduce the load shed error to $0.02-4.5\%$. On the California Test System with storm data from December 2025, the error falls to $23\%$. These scenarios give expansion planning a reliable source of outage data tied to observed hazards.

title: Rigorous integration of semilinear parabolic PDEs: forward evolution bounds and projected boundary value problems
abstract: In this work, we present a rigorous integrator for initial and boundary value problems for semilinear parabolic PDEs. The method builds on earlier semigroup-based approaches while improving the bounds used in the fixed-point argument and extending the class of problems that can be treated. In particular, it controls the solution operator without requiring backward integration of the variational equation and allows projected boundary value problems to be studied through a simplified construction of an approximate inverse for the linearized operator. To illustrate the scope of the method, we present three applications to the two-dimensional Ohta--Kawasaki equation. For two initial value problems, we prove global existence and obtain explicit enclosures valid for all sufficiently large times around numerical approximations of stripe and spot equilibria. These results use a fixed-point formulation on an unbounded time interval, avoiding the construction of trapping regions. We also rigorously solve a projected boundary value problem with endpoint conditions chosen from linear approximations of the unstable and stable spaces of two saddle equilibria. This provides a step toward the rigorous study of heteroclinic saddle-to-saddle connections.

title: Swarmlet: a GPU-resident reformulated vortex particle method for coupled multirotor aerodynamics and flight dynamics
abstract: We present Swarmlet, a GPU solver for the unsteady aerodynamics and flight dynamics of one or many multirotor vehicles. The wake is a meshless, evolving-core vortex particle field in the reformulated (rVPM) large-eddy formulation, coupled to rotor models of three fidelities, six-degree-of-freedom vehicles and flight control. Particles carry a smooth core of compact support whose field outside four core radii is exactly the singular Biot-Savart field, so the multipole far field of the treecode carries no regularization error. The subfilter closure is a dynamic eddy viscosity on a fixed filter width, applied by core spreading with a Lagrangian exchange of its local excess under an explicit stability bound, and the strengths are relaxed by projection; global corrections make both the exchange and the relaxation conserve total vorticity and linear impulse. All rotor models shed connected bound circulation, the disks along the arcs swept in each step however long, so the wake receives the lift impulse. The solver agrees with direct summation to $5\times 10^{-7}$ and converges at third order in time. Without calibration, an actuator-line model that includes its own near sheet predicts the hover thrust of a DJI 9443 propeller within 2%. With calibrated section polars it reproduces a Crazyflie propeller's thrust and torque within 3.2% at three speeds and the near wake of a hovering quadrotor with relative $L^2$ differences of 0.08-0.21 against particle image velocimetry, while the wake keeps the delivered impulse. A closed-loop formation of 100 quadrotors, run at a coarser setting on one GPU, illustrates the coupled method at swarm scale.

title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

title: Time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for viscous-dispersive heat-conducting compressible fluids
abstract: We establish the time-asymptotic stability of generic Riemann solutions for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier-Korteweg (NSFK) system, which describes the dynamics of viscous, heat-conducting, compressible fluids with internal capillarity. We prove that, for the adiabatic exponent $γ\in(1,2]$, the solution to the NSFK system converges uniformly in space, as time tends to infinity, to a composite wave consisting of a rarefaction wave, a viscous contact wave, and a viscous-dispersive shock with a time-dependent shift, provided that the initial perturbation and the strengths of the contact wave and the shock are sufficiently small. In particular, we do not impose any smallness condition on the strength of the rarefaction wave. Because of the capillarity, the shock is viscous-dispersive and its profile equation is of third order. We treat the shock by the method of $a$-contraction with shifts introduced by Kang and Vasseur. This is the first result on the time-asymptotic stability of a viscous-dispersive shock, and of a generic Riemann solution, for the NSFK system.

title: Regularity and $v$-number of syzygies of graded maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
abstract: Let $A=Q/(\mathbf f)$, where $Q$ is a polynomial ring over an infinite field $k$ and $\mathbf f=f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a homogeneous $Q$-regular sequence. For $1\leq j\leq c$, set $w_j=\operatorname{deg}(f_j)>0.$ Let $M$ be a finitely generated graded $A$-module of infinite projective dimension. Set $M_i=\operatorname{Syz}_i^A(M)$. We prove that, for each $l\in\{0,1\}$, the sets $\operatorname{Ass}_A(M_{2i+l})$ eventually stabilize, and that $\operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$ is eventually bounded above and below by linear polynomials. If $w_j=w$ for all $1\leq j\leq c$, then the functions $i\longmapsto \operatorname{reg}(M_{2i+l})$, $i\longmapsto v(M_{2i+l}),$ and $i\longmapsto v_{\mathfrak p}(M_{2i+l}),\, \mathfrak p\in\mathcal A_l,$ are eventually linear with leading coefficient $w$, where $\mathcal A_l$ denotes the stable set of associated primes.

title: Spatial preferential attachment models: robustness revisited
abstract: We investigate robustness under percolation in the degree-driven spatial preferential attachment model. Consider a profile that is regularly varying with exponent $-δ$, where $δ>1$, and an attachment rule with asymptotic slope $γ\in(0,1)$. Jacob and Mörters (Ann. Probab. 45 (2017)) proved robustness when $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)<1. $$ We prove the converse in the strict regime: if $$ δ\left(\frac1γ-1\right)>1, $$ then sufficiently strong Bernoulli vertex thinning destroys the giant component. In particular, the strict robustness boundary coincides with that of the age-dependent random connection model.

title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ Γ=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.

title: The Kemper--Malle conjecture and isolated linear quotient singularities
abstract: We prove the Kemper--Malle conjecture, which provides a modular analogue of the Chevalley--Shephard--Todd theorem. As a consequence, the classification of isolated linear quotient singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic reduces to the classical Zassenhaus--Vincent--Wolf classification.

title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
abstract: We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.

title: Explicit finite size corrections for Toeplitz determinants and rectangular domino tilings
abstract: Finite Toeplitz truncation does not, in general, preserve multiplication. For products of $m$ $N\times N$ tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices with symbols $z+z^{-1}+a_h$, we make the two boundary corrections in Widom's product formula for finite sections explicit. The method of images gives two Hankel corrections when $m\le N+2$, a sharp uniform degree bound. For $N\ge m-1$, the ratio of the determinant of the matrix product to the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol reduces, whenever defined, to a determinant of order $2(m-1)$, which reversal symmetry splits into two determinants of order $m-1$. A rectangular Schur polynomial gives an exact formula for the Toeplitz determinant with the product symbol, including when roots coincide. For symbols nonzero on the unit circle, classical identities for rational symbols give an exact $m\times m$ determinant formula for the ratio, with an explicit confluent form for repeated roots. With $ρ_h$ the zero of $z+z^{-1}+a_h$ in $|z|<1$, the limit is $\prod_{i<j}(1-ρ_iρ_j)^2$ as $N\to\infty$ at fixed $m,a_h$. For rectangular domino tilings, these formulas compare the classical Kasteleyn--Temperley--Fisher product with the banded Toeplitz determinant formed from the product symbol. We obtain the first exponentially small correction at fixed width and relate this comparison to the Toeplitz determinant furnished by the dual Cauchy identity.

title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

title: Rayleigh's conjecture for vibrating plates: simpler planar proof and nonlinear extensions
abstract: We give a simpler proof of Nadirashvili's theorem (Rayleigh's conjecture) that among vibrating clamped plates of prescribed area in the plane, the disk has the lowest fundamental tone. The proof uses a one-shot Talenti type comparison for sign-changing solutions of the Poisson equation with mean-zero data, established in a companion paper. The comparison considers just two rearranged sources, rather than optimizing over all admissible sources as in the traditional two-ball technique. This ``paired comparison'' simplification yields immediate nonlinear extensions: the disk minimizes the clamped quotient $\|Δu\|_q/\|u\|_p$ among bounded open sets of prescribed area, for every $1\le p,q\le\infty$. Equality is characterized for $q>1$, while exceptional behavior at $q=1$ is identified. In higher dimensions, we prove ball minimality for $p=\infty$ and conjecture minimality for all $p,q$ within the compact embedding range. We also establish the corresponding interval inequality in one dimension.

title: Linear Complementary Pairs of MDS Codes from Elliptic Curves
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Linear Complementary Pairs (LCPs) of Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes that arise from elliptic curves. We establish geometric conditions for LCPs of elliptic codes and prove that they cannot consist entirely of MDS codes when evaluated over all rational points of the curve. To address this, we construct LCPs of MDS elliptic codes by restricting evaluation divisors to subgroup cosets. We apply this method to obtain explicit infinite families of LCPs of MDS codes over Mordell and supersingular elliptic curves, including large-length constructions over quadratic extensions.

title: The Diophantine Problem with constraints in some free-by-cyclic groups
abstract: In this paper we explore the Diophantine Problem, that is, the solvability of equations, in one-relator and free-by-cyclic groups, showing that this is decidable in some cases and undecidable otherwise, depending on their abelianisation and centre. In particular, we focus on a version of the Diophantine Problem which asks about the existence of solutions satisfying abelianisation constraints, and prove a number of results concerning the decidability of this problem for free-by-cyclic groups with centre, tree-GBS groups, cyclically pinched groups and the first hydra group.

title: Numerical Information of Hilbert Space Operators
abstract: For a Hilbert space operator $A\in B(H)$, the numerical range map of $A$, denoted $φ_A$ is the map sending unit vectors $x$ in $H$ to $\langle Ax,x\rangle$. From this map we define the Numerical Information of $A$, denoted $Σ_A$, which is the sigma algebra induced on the unit sphere by the numerical range map. One of the main results of the paper are that if $A,B\in B(H)$, and $φ_B=f\circ φ_A$, then $f$ is affine. Our other main result is showing that $Σ_B\subsetΣ_A$ if and only if $B=αRe(A)+βIm(A)+γI$ for some complex numbers $α,β,γ$.

title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
abstract: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(Π,τ)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(Π,τ)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.

title: A Super-Convergent Quasi-Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Advection-Diffusion Problems
abstract: The aim of the present study is to develop discontinuous Galerkin and nonconforming finite-element methods for solving the 2D advection-diffusion equation. The discrete formulations are stabilized by means of a family of numerical fluxes and the dispersion relations are constructed via a Fourier/stability analysis. The linear discontinuous P1DG and non conforming P1NC Galerkin discretizations are studied. A long time stability result is proven for the P1NC and P1DG schemes and fluxes examined here by inspecting the discrete frequencies, solutions of the dispersion relations. A super-convergent result is also demonstrated for the P1NC discrete frequency (O(h 4 ) accuracy) compared to the P1DG one (O(h 2 ) accuracy). These results are in line with those obtained in a previous paper for the shallow-water system.

title: Strong Positive Recurrence for Strongly Entropy Expanding Maps
abstract: We introduce expanding strong positive recurrence (expanding-SPR) for non-invertible systems with critical points. We then give a sufficient condition for maps to be SPR: strong entropy expansion (SEE). We prove that expanding-SPR implies good thermodynamical properties, including exponential decay of correlations of Hölder observables for the measures of maximal entropy. The class of maps that are SEE includes all C^{\infty}-interval maps with h_{top}(f )>0 and all Viana maps.

title: The three-colour bipartite Ramsey number of sufficiently long even cycles
abstract: For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{br}_3(H)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every three-colouring of $K_{N,N}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{br}_3(C_{2n})=3n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and give the lower bound for every $n\ge2$. For the upper bound, we reduce a counterexample to a finite rational weighted profile. Cycle extension and vertex-cover arguments force the critical components to have six unique minimum covers which partition the profile. The remaining component supports give a contradiction.

title: A bounded Borel set in the plane none of whose orthogonal projections is Borel
abstract: We construct a bounded Borel set in the plane whose orthogonal projection onto every line is non-Borel. This gives a negative answer to a question of Thierry De Pauw.

title: Topological degree of fewnomial maps
abstract: We study the topological degree on the positive orthant of a map $F:\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\mathcal{A}$ of $N=n+k+1$ monomials. This degree is well defined under a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope, which holds for generic exponents and coefficients.
