We give three formulas for it, all in terms of signs of maximal minors. The first one is a Viro formula: the degree is a signed count of the simplices of a regular triangulation of $\mathcal{A}$ which are positively decorated in the sense of Bihan, Santos and Spaenlehauer. The second one is a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and the third one a sum over the vertices of the polyhedron of the Gale dual system. As a consequence, the degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We also obtain a Descartes rule of signs for the degree and, in the generic case, the upper bound $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the largest number of facets of a $d$-polytope with $N$ vertices. This bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible degrees is symmetric in $n$ and $k$. Since a nonzero degree forces a positive zero, our formulas give sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity statements for their number.

title: In vitro starch digestion kinetic, formal analysis and new kinetic model
abstract: Describing mathematically the kinetics of the enzymatic hydrolysis of starch is a crucial part of nutrition and industrial applications studies. The majority of math models aim to fit the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$), so-called digestogram, whose simple shape which can be fitted equally well by various math models. A relevant model of starch digestion kinetics should be more specific of the phenomenon. This study proposes a novel analytical framework that jointly fits the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$) and the instantaneous reaction-rate coefficient ($k\_a(t)$). A large dataset comprising 672 wheat-starch time-course measurements (including normal, waxy, and high-amylose genotypes), and additional experiments on other botanical starches was analysed. Standard First-Order and Weibull models were compared with two newly derived kinetic formulations \eqref{Eq.11} and \eqref{Eq.12} based on expected starch hydrolysis' phenomenon by which $k\_a(t)$ tends with time towards an asymptotic-rate constant value, $k\_e$, following a characteristic relaxation time ($τ$). A mathematical proof of the existence of $k\_e$, specific of the type of starch, is provided, based on an analysis of the Weibull's parameters. Model ability to fit both $X\_t$ and $k\_a(t)$ was assessed by examining coefficients of determination ($R^2$) for both data types, and its adjusted version ($R^2\_{adj}$) was used to compare performances between models. All models fit very well $X\_t$ data, while $k\_a(t)$ is much more discriminant of the model formulation. Wheat starch types are well distinguished, regarding ke, by the new models, with higher susceptibility to amylase for waxy samples ($\approx 5.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$), than normal ($\approx 2.2\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) and high-amylose ($\approx 1.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) ones. The new models outperformed the other models for monotonic evolution of $k\_a(t)$, particularly digestion of high-amylose, and allow a more accurate estimation of $k\_e$. However, the analysis also highlighted limitations for modelling non-monotonic kinetics observed for waxy wheat starch digestion, suggesting a need for more sophisticated differential-equation descriptions for $k\_a(t)$. Overall, the combined fitting strategy provides a robust method for extracting physically meaningful kinetic parameters, facilitating deeper insight into the factors controlling starch digestion and supporting the development of more accurate predictive models for glycaemic response and food processing.

title: Duality in Harmonic Analysis and beyond
abstract: In this short note, we develop a duality-based, purely operator-theoretic method for proving several classical maximal inequalities on $L^p$ spaces for $p\in(1,\infty)$. The method applies to maximal ergodic operators, Hardy--Littlewood maximal functions, and maximal Radon averaging operators, and derives their boundedness directly from structural properties of the underlying operators. Further, we show that the same duality principle extends beyond maximal functions. We develop a theory of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for sequences of bounded positive monotone operators on Hilbert spaces, using soft arguments that apply to various classical operators in analysis. In particular, answering a question that had been open for some time, we give direct proofs of $r$-variational and jump inequalities for convolution operators associated with lacunary dilations of smooth bumps on $\mathbb R^d$, completely avoiding any appeal to martingale inequalities.

title: Asymmetric Likelihood-Free Hypothesis Testing
abstract: In likelihood-free hypothesis testing (LFHT), given samples from two unknown distributions $P,Q$ on $[n]$ with $\mathrm{d_{TV}}(P,Q)\geq\varepsilon$, and from a third distribution $D\in\{P,Q\}$, the goal is to identify whether $D=P$ or $D=Q$. We study asymmetric likelihood-free hypothesis testing, where the sample budgets $s_P$ and $s_Q$ for $P$ and $Q$ may differ, and characterize the feasible triples $(s_P,s_Q,s_D)$ up to logarithmic factors. We establish that unequal reference budgets can give a polynomial saving. For instance, for constant separation, $n$ samples from $P$ and $n^{3/4}$ from $Q$ allow testing with $\widetilde O(n^{1/4})$ samples from $D$, whereas both existing baselines---symmetric LFHT and unequal-sample closeness testing---require $Ω(\sqrt n)$ samples from $D$. We further apply our results to non-adaptive distribution 2-clustering, where the sample allocation among $k$ distributions must be fixed before observing any data. We obtain matching upper and lower bounds for this problem up to logarithmic factors in terms of the domain size, number of distributions, smaller cluster size, and separation, both with one cluster distribution known and with both unknown. Comparing with known bounds for adaptive sample allocation gives a worst-case adaptivity gap of $\widetildeΘ(k^{1/4})$.

title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
abstract: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2π$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

title: Stability analysis of boundary element methods for the wave equation: The weakly singular operator in $1d$
abstract: We discuss the construction of stable discrete pairs of trial and test spaces for the wave equation. Building on a general abstract operator-theoretic framework, we show how optimal pairings can be derived for a one-dimensional boundary element formulation of the wave equation with prescribed Dirichlet data, based on an indirect single layer potential ansatz. In this setting, the optimal test space can be computed analytically and has a physical interpretation, reflecting the non-local nature of the underlying operator.

title: Integer symplectic matrices in expanding boxes
abstract: We prove an essentially optimal uniform upper bound for the number of integer symplectic matrices inside a box of expanding side length and arbitrary centre.

title: Solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ in $λ$-Cantor sets
abstract: In this paper, we study the structure of the solutions of $x^α+y^α=1$ with both coordinates in a $λ$-Cantor set. We prove that, for any $α>1$, the intersection with the middle-third Cantor set has positive Hausdorff dimension, strengthening the infinitude question posed by Jiang et al. [J. London Math. Soc. 113 (2026), e70408]. To explore the structure of the solutions, for arbitrary $α$, we find that their Hausdorff dimension undergoes phase transitions as $λ$ varies: we establish the occurrence of Hausdorff phase transitions by proving the existence of zero-dimensional and positive-dimensional regions.

title: Principle of generating critical points of rational functions and Gauss-Fourier conjecture for second-kind zeros
abstract: The precise origin of critical points in rational functions remains a longstanding open problem. This paper elucidates the mechanism underlying critical point generation in rational functions. For over two centuries, a conjecture attributed to Gauss and Fourier has remained unresolved: every real zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are multiple real zeros of $p^{'}(s)$ are termed second-kind zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. By developing the root locus method, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the emergence of second-kind zeros: a second-kind zero $M$ arises if and only if at least two root loci of $2qπ$ or $2qπ+π$ degree, emitted from at least one pair of non-real conjugate zeros of $p(s)$ (in the extended complex plane, excluding the real axis), directly intersect another root locus at $M$ on the real axis. Our results resolve one conjecture of the Gauss-Fourier conjectures and reveal the fundamental mechanism by which critical points of rational functions are generated.

title: Finite zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols
abstract: We study finite products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Fock space over the complex plane. If every symbol has the form $f+\overline g$, where $f$ and $g$ are entire functions of exponential type, we prove that a finite product vanishes if and only if one symbol vanishes identically. It suffices to test the product on reproducing kernels. The proof represents the product by a two-variable entire function and transforms the equation for a left factor by $\exp(-\partial_z\partial_w)$. A Fock norm identity then permits cancellation of each nonzero factor.

title: Macroscopic Poincaré Inequalities and Weak-Type Characterizations of $p$-Energy Forms
abstract: For a class of regular strongly local $p$-energy forms on complete doubling metric measure spaces, $1<p<\infty$, we derive a macroscopic Poincaré inequality from a Poincaré inequality and a capacity upper bound at a doubling scale $Ψ$. The macroscopic inequality compares $L^p$-oscillations at any two scales and yields a uniform two-scale comparison $J_s\lesssim J_r$, $0<r<s$, for the Korevaar-Schoen functionals, strengthening their usual weak monotonicity property. Conversely, under a density assumption on compactly supported functions, the macroscopic inequality yields a regular strongly local Korevaar-Schoen $p$-energy satisfying a $Ψ$-Poincaré inequality. We also show that the macroscopic inequality forces lower $p$-scaling of $Ψ$ on scales not exceeding $\mathrm{diam} X$; together with doubling, this gives two-sided power bounds. Finally, we establish a weak-type characterization of the energy domain of Brezis-Van Schaftingen-Yung type.

title: Weighted composition operators on the Fock space
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the compactness, invertibility and isometry of the operators on the Fock space formed by multiplying a weighted composition operator with the adjoint of another weighted composition operator to form either $W_{g, ψ}W_{f, \varphi}^*$ or $W_{g, ψ}^*W_{f, \varphi}$.

title: Higher-order tangent and secant numbers, special-value integrals, and a common zero attractor
abstract: We study two families of coefficients associated with powers of the tangent function and with products of the secant and tangent functions, and develop a unified treatment of the corresponding higher-order tangent and secant numbers. The first part establishes a common identity for even derivatives of $\tanh x$ and odd derivatives of $\operatorname{sech}x$. Combined with integral formulae for these derivatives, this yields finite power-integral representations for the normalized values $ζ(2n+1)$ and $β(2n)$ and naturally introduces two polynomial families $P_n$ and $Q_n$. We determine several arithmetic and structural properties of these polynomials. In particular, we identify the exact content of $P_n$, prove that $Q_n$ is primitive, establish strict log-concavity and unimodality of their coefficient sequences, and describe their real zeros. For even indices each family has a unique negative real zero, and the two sequences of real zeros have the same limit. We also derive differential recurrences and generating functions for $P_n$ and $Q_n$. The generating functions lead to a global complex-singularity analysis. We construct a compact Jordan curve $Γ$ and prove that the complex zero sets of both $P_n$ and $Q_n$ converge to $Γ$ in Hausdorff distance. The normalized zero-counting measures converge weakly to the same equilibrium measure on $Γ$. We determine the logarithmic capacity of the enclosed compact set, give an explicit arclength density for the limiting measure, and compute its first moments. Numerical plots for $P_{20}$, $P_{50}$, $P_{100}$ and $P_{150}$ illustrate the zero-attractor theorem.

title: Elliptic rearrangement for Poisson equations with mean-zero data
abstract: The $L^p$ norm of a sign-changing Dirichlet solution of Poisson's equation is shown to be bounded by the maximum of the $L^p$ norms of the ball solutions obtained by signed rearrangement of the source and its negative, assuming the source term has mean value zero. This paired comparison on bounded open sets extends Talenti's elliptic rearrangement principle to solutions that change sign. In dimensions one and two, the paired comparison holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$, and it holds in every dimension for $p=\infty$. The inequalities are sharp and equality cases are characterized. In dimensions $n \geq 3$, paired comparison can fail for every finite $p$ although it remains valid for $p\ge(3n-1)/4$ in the special case of bang-bang sources with mean zero. The mean-zero source assumption is crucial when $p<\infty$. Without it, paired comparison can fail even for bang-bang sources. For sources of arbitrary mean in one dimension, however, the $L^\infty$ paired comparison still holds and so does a comparison for $L^p$ norms of the derivative when $1\le p\le3$.

title: Modulating flow polynomials and parity bias in homological walk counting
abstract: Long weighted walks seem to sample mod-$t$ flows uniformly, but at even moduli a persistent parity bias survives. Writing $C_G(t)$ for the flow polynomial of a connected graph $G$ of genus $g$, the proportion of nowhere-zero flows under uniform sampling is $C_G(t)/t^g$. For arbitrary positive directed weights and all moduli, we determine the exact leading corrections for both closed walks and nonbacktracking closed walks, which we call circuits. Only the circuit result requires $g\ge2$. For closed walks, the canonical character governs the leading correction through the canonical modulating flow polynomial $D_G$; for circuits, the period character, when it exists, governs the leading correction through the period modulating flow polynomial $D_{G,η}$. At even moduli these give parity-dependent corrections: the two mechanisms coincide on nonbipartite graphs and separate only in the bipartite circuit problem. More generally, each integral-homology character $ζ$ determines a balanced-dichromatic specialization $D_{G,ζ}$. These polynomials form a character-indexed family whose finite-order members give Fourier coefficients of the nowhere-zero flow set and whose retained edge sets are the central sets of a gain semimatroid. We further show that $D_G$ is a cycle-matroid invariant and a signed-Tutte specialization satisfying signed deletion-contraction. Finally, an integral nowhere-zero approximation theorem implies that asymptotically almost every weighted circuit traverses every edge.

title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric universal characterisations of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we show that passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
abstract: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $π:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.

title: Recovering the reaction coefficient in a time-fractional diffusion equation with variable coefficients in any spatial dimension
abstract: We explore the inverse problem of determining the reaction coefficient $q(x',t)$ in the time-fractional diffusion equation ${}^CD_t u-Lu+q(x',t)u=f$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,T]$, $x=(x',x_n)$, $0<α<1$, from the trace of the solution on the hyperplane $\{x_n=0\}$. Here ${}^CD_t$ is the Gerasimov--Caputo derivative and $L$ is a uniformly elliptic second-order operator with variable, $x_n$-independent coefficients and without zero-order term. For $L=Δ$ this problem was studied in dimensions $n=1,2,3$ by methods based on pointwise bounds of the kernels, which are not available for $n\ge4$. Our approach relies on the Eidelman--Kochubei fundamental solution: although its singularity on the diagonal depends on the dimension, we show that it satisfies integral bounds of the same form for all $n\ge1$. Using these bounds, we prove existence, uniqueness and stability of regular solutions of the direct problem with a Hölder continuous reaction coefficient. Without assuming additional smoothness of the solution, we show that the inverse problem is equivalent to a closed system of integral equations for $q$ and the derivatives $\partial_{x_n}u$, $\partial^2_{x_n}u$. For the inverse problem we establish a conditional Lipschitz stability estimate on the whole time interval and global uniqueness in every dimension, and prove local existence of a solution. In the case $a_{in}\equiv0$, $b_n\equiv0$ we obtain a stability estimate with explicit constants, which reduces to the known estimates for the Laplacian. An explicit two-dimensional example with a mixed coefficient and a normal drift shows that the hypotheses of the main theorems are compatible and that the corresponding terms in the trace condition cannot be omitted.

title: A branching model for selective sweeps
abstract: At every discrete time i we introduce exactly one individual whose genotype is given by a p_i sampled uniformly in (0,1). This individual will be the founder of a branching process with a geometric offspring distribution with parameter p_i. All the branching processes are independent. We show that as time goes to infinity successive selective sweeps occur. That is, ever more fit single genotypes dominate the population. Moreover, at any fixed time we prove that the dominating genotype is not the most fit genotype. Finally, we show that the rescaled point process associated to selective sweeps converges to an inhomogeneous Poisson process.

title: Choice principles in countable partition models
abstract: We study the countable partition model over a set of atoms of arbitrary uncountable cardinality $κ$. Its supports are partitions of the atoms into countably many blocks, and a permutation fixes a support when it preserves each block setwise. This model was proposed by Bruce and studied by Banerjee. We prove that dependent choice holds for every $κ$, although the filter of subgroups is not closed under countable intersections. Choice for well-orderable families holds exactly when $κ<\aleph_{ω_1}$; when $κ\ge\aleph_{ω_1}$, an $ω_1$-indexed family witnesses its failure. The Hartogs and Lindenbaum numbers of the set of atoms are both $ω_1$. The proofs use permutations matching blocks of equal cardinality and establish shift completeness of the filter. Together with Banerjee's failure of $\mathsf{DC}_{ω_1}$, these results determine which dependent choice principles hold in the model.

title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_χ)$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.

title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.

title: On Almost MDS codes holding $(n-k-1)$-designs and an open problem on Witt design
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an almost maximum distance separable (AMDS) code over the finite fields with parameters $[n,k,n-k]$ whose minimum-weight codewords support an $(n-k-1)$-$(n,n-k,λ)$ design. We first determine the parameters of the dual code $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. We also characterize the design and its complementary design supported by the minimum weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$. In particular, we present explicit formulas for the weight enumerators of all subset codes of $\mathcal{C}^{\bot}$ with length at least $k+1$. These formulas are completely determined by the cardinality of the subset, the dimension, together with the parameter $λ$, and are independent of the specific choice of subsets. As an application, we answer an open problem posed by Wang, Tang and Ding in 2023 by proving that the $3$-design supported by the minimum-weight codewords in their proposed cyclic dual code is isomorphic to the complementary design of the Witt spherical geometry design.

title: Weighted Risk Aggregation under Long-Memory Dependence: Pathwise Fluctuations of Exposure-Weighted Losses
abstract: We model insurance loss in each period as deterministic exposure multiplied by a nonnegative function of a long-memory Gaussian sequence. A weighted law of the iterated logarithm yields the exact almost-sure scale and sharp constant of centered cumulative loss. Loss per unit of cumulative exposure converges almost surely to its mean, with an exact error scale common to all admissible exposure profiles; the sharp constant depends on the exposure exponent. Lognormal and quadratic examples, of Hermite ranks one and two, and a simulation illustrate the results. A known spectral formula expresses the quadratic coefficient through a leading eigenvalue.

title: Spanning bipartite quadrangulations in even triangulations of real projective spaces
abstract: We study spanning quadrangulations of even triangulations of real projective spaces, using the higher-dimensional notion of quadrangulation introduced by Kaiser and Stehlík. We prove that every even triangulation of $\RP^d$, where $d\ge 2$, admits a spanning bipartite quadrangulation. Moreover, such a triangulation admits a spanning non-bipartite quadrangulation if and only if it is not balanced; if it is balanced, every spanning quadrangulation is bipartite. Our proofs use coloring monodromy: its orbits yield bipartite quadrangulations, while a covering-space construction gives non-bipartite ones. %In dimension three, a bipartite quadrangulation can always be chosen to induce $K_{2,2}$ on each tetrahedron. More generally, we establish a sufficient condition for the existence of spanning bipartite quadrangulations on closed manifolds in terms of the monodromy action, and derive a consequence involving the fundamental group.

title: BCC optimality for the three-dimensional Coulomb lattice energy
abstract: We prove that the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes the renormalized Coulomb energy among three-dimensional Bravais lattices of fixed covolume, up to orthogonal transformations. Using Ewald summation, we write the energy, to within an additive constant, as a sum of two positive, rapidly convergent series in real and reciprocal space. Their positivity provides finite lower bounds for all competitors. A passage to the dual lattice reduces the problem to a face-centered cubic comparison. A short basis vector estimate, a certified local Hessian, and interval bounds on a compact five-dimensional domain complete the computer-assisted proof.

title: Model Predictive Control: Systematic Design Tailored to Nonholonomic Systems
abstract: Nonholonomic systems are ubiquitous in applications such as transportation and robotics, yet their control remains challenging. In order to achieve asymptotic stability of a desired equilibrium, model predictive control (MPC) schemes without stabilizing terminal conditions have recently been proposed for nonholonomic kinematic systems. However, this approach still required lengthy system-specific calculations. This paper eliminates the need for these auxiliary calculations, as we propose a streamlined systematic design for MPC stage costs tailored to nonholonomic systems, utilizing the concepts of privileged coordinates and nonholonomic weights. Furthermore, the proposed design methodology is extended beyond purely kinematic models to a wider class of systems with non-negligible dynamics, and we highlight the geometric meaning of the resulting MPC stage costs. The systematic procedure is demonstrated using an articulated vehicle as an example.

title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems
abstract: In this paper, we develop accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave saddle point problems with bilinear coupling. Combining strongly convex Nesterov dynamics with scaled heavy-ball dynamics, we propose a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with constant damping and derive an associated algorithm by time discretization and coefficient adjustment. Under suitable conditions on the continuous scaling function $β(t)$ and the discrete scaling sequence $β_k$, we establish primal-dual gap estimates of $\mathcal O(1/β(t))$ in continuous time and $\mathcal O(1/β_k)$ in discrete time. The maximal admissible growth rates of these scales recover the exponential and linear convergence rates of strongly convex Nesterov methods in continuous and discrete time, respectively. We also prove convergence of the primal-dual trajectory and sequence, even when the dual solution is nonunique. Saddle residual estimates of $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β(t)})$ and $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β_k})$ hold under globally Lipschitz gradients in continuous time and with a possibly nonsmooth dual potential in discrete time. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed methods.

title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.

title: Will AI kill us all---or just make mathematicians obsolete?
abstract: AI's recent advances have fueled predictions of human intellectual obsolescence and fears for the future of mathematics. I argue that, impressive as these achievements are, they do not establish AI's capacity to invent new concepts and theories or sustain autonomous recursive self-improvement. Human intelligence also involves judgment, imagination, and embodied experience that standard measures fail to capture. Mathematics extends beyond proving theorems: its creative core lies in conceptual discovery and understanding. AI can strengthen this enterprise, but realizing its promise requires protecting attribution, open exchange, confidentiality, and mathematical training. I propose an academic AI consortium to provide powerful research tools with enforceable guarantees safeguarding unpublished ideas.

title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings
abstract: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.

title: Property (R) with its stability for analytic functional system and under compact perturbations
abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}_T$ be the analytic functional system generated by a linear bounded operator $T$ on an infinite dimensional complex Hilbert space. This paper characterizes the stability of property (R), a variant of Weyl's theorem, for $\mathcal{F}_T$ and under compact perturbations in terms of the spectrum on consistency in Weyl. In particular, the stability of property (R) under compact perturbations is shown to imply the (R)-stability of $\mathcal{F}_T$.

title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlevé equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlevé equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.

title: Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements
abstract: Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.

title: Optimally Emulating Smooth Functions for Bayesian Analyses
abstract: For Bayesian analyses aimed at constraining the parameter space of computationally expensive models by comparison with heterogeneous data sets, model emulators play a pivotal role. Model emulators enable searches through high-dimensional parameter spaces, searches which might otherwise require millions of full model runs. Here, an emulation strategy is presented based on the assumption that the model output can be well described by a polynomial expansion with all terms being independent of one another and with higher order terms being given decreasing weights according to a convergence parameter. It is found that if the expansion's form is constrained to being invariant to rotation and translation of the parameter space that the polynomial form becomes equivalent to that of a Gaussian process emulator using a correlation kernel with a Gaussian form. In the limit that the function is smooth, quantified by a convergence parameter, $Λ$, it is found that rather few training points are required to reproduce the full model and provide a good estimate of its uncertainty. An accuracy metric is defined based on an average of the expected uncertainty over the prior before training data are actually gathered. Analytic expressions for the expected accuracy are provided based solely on an expected value of $Λ$ and the location of the training points. This enables a tenable optimized placement of training points, which is shown to be significantly superior to random placement or that from Latin hyper-cube sampling. Examples of optimized placement are provided, and the accuracy is studied as a function of various variables, such as the number of model parameters, the number of training points, and the convergence parameter.

title: Numerical Shadow Rigidity for 3x3 Matrices
abstract: The numerical shadow of a complex matrix is the measure obtained by pushing forward that Haar measure on the unit sphere in $\mathbb{C}^n$ by the numerical range map. By the choice of measure, unitary equivalence implies same measure, but the reverse is not true for $n\geq 3$. We name a matrix $\textbf{shadow rigid}$ it its unitary equivalence class and shadow equivalence class coincide. It is known that normal matrices are rigid, but the topic has not been explored beyond this in the literature. The main result of the paper is showing that in the $n=3$ case, a matrix is rigid if and only if it is non-generic. We also show that rigidity is preserved under an affine group action and present three normal-like properties of $3\times 3$ non-generic matrices.

title: Restriction of $p'$-degree characters, fields of values, and relative normal complements
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group for a prime $p$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Centella and Navarro proved that there is a canonical bijection ${\rm Irr}_{p'}(Φ_{1_G})\to{\rm Irr}_{p'}(Φ_{1_{\textbf N_G(P)}})$ preserving fields of values, where $Φ_{1_G}$ denotes the principal projective indecomposable character of $G$. In the spirit of a result of Berkovich on the McKay bijection, we characterize when this projective correspondence can be realized by restriction, proving that it holds if and only if $\mathbf{N}_G(P)$ admits a certain relative normal complement in $G$. More generally, we establish a refined criterion incorporating fields of values, and we extend this characterization to $π$-separable groups with nilpotent Hall $π$-subgroups.

title: Parameters Robust Parallelizable Iterative Decoupled Algorithms for Thermo-Poroelasticity with Nonlinear Convective Transport
abstract: This paper presents several parallel iterative algorithms for the nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity. We introduce an auxiliary variable to transform the original model into a four-field formulation to overcome Poisson locking. The iterative idea is extended to linearize and decouple the four-field model. Different coupling strategies are employed among these three subproblems, combined with appropriately designed iteration settings, yielding distinct iterative parallel algorithms. Stabilization terms are incorporated into these algorithms to ensure parameter robustness in extreme situations. We derive error estimates and prove the convergence of these parallel iterative decoupled algorithms. Finally, numerical experiments are presented to compare the performance of the different parallel algorithms in extreme parameter settings, thereby validating their efficiency and robustness.

title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
abstract: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{ξ\in \mathbb F_q^d:ξ_1^2+\cdots+ξ_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, dσ)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $η_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $η_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.

title: On the planar Neumann--Poincaré inverse spectral problem
abstract: Does the Neumann--Poincaré spectrum determine a planar domain up to an extended Möbius transformation? We construct a pair showing that the answer is no, even for analytic, strictly convex, algebraic boundaries. Their operators are similar. We then prove a positive result for prescribed finite-dimensional families of normalised exterior conformal maps. For every $m\ge1$, the first $m$ positive eigenvalues determine $m$ real Laurent coefficients on a small truncated convex cone, provided the higher coefficients are a prescribed analytic remainder of quadratic order. Recovery is Lipschitz stable, uniformly down to the disk. The proof combines the Grunsky representation with a nondegeneracy argument for weighted Hankel matrices and differentiated perturbation estimates. Explicit two- and three-parameter examples, single-mode families with repeated leading eigenvalues, and Möbius equivalence classes illustrate the result. Direct proofs for complete polarization data show what spectral weights add to the eigenvalues.

title: Small and Large Quasi-Kernels in General Digraphs
abstract: In a digraph $D$, a set $Q$ of vertices is a quasi-kernel if $Q$ is an independent set and every vertex in $D$ can be reached from $Q$ via at most two edges. The small quasi-kernel conjecture by Erdős and Székely predicts that every source-free $n$-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - n/2$. Chvátal and Lovász' 1974 work implies a bound of $n - \sqrt{n}+1$. In 2024, Sprio shows the bound $n - \frac{1}{4} \sqrt{n \log_2 n}$. We show that there always is a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - \frac{1}{51}n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$. For the related large quasi-kernel conjecture by Spiro, we show that there always is a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]| \ge 0.2917 \cdot n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$.
comment: Preprint submitted to the Journal of Graph Theory

title: Connected Coloring Games on Corona Products of Graphs
abstract: We study the connected coloring game on corona products of graphs. For connected graphs $G$ and $H$, we prove the sharp upper bound $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)\leq\max\{Δ(G),Δ(H)+1\}+1$ and establish a further bound using the Bob-start ordinary coloring game on the second factor. We show that the difference between the Alice-start and Bob-start connected game chromatic numbers can be arbitrarily large in either direction. We further prove that a connected subgraph may have arbitrarily larger connected game chromatic number than its ambient connected graph, and that $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)$ cannot be bounded in terms of $χ_{cg}(G)$ and $χ_{cg}(H)$ alone, even when both factors have connected game chromatic number $2$. We also obtain corona products for which the difference $χ_g-χ_{cg}$ is arbitrarily large and construct infinitely many connected graphs with $χ_g<χ_{cg}$. Finally, for corona products of trees, we prove the universal upper bound $5$, characterize those attaining the value $3$, give structural sufficient conditions for the value $4$, and exhibit a broad family attaining the value $5$.

title: Triple Products of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
abstract: Stochastic Galerkin schemes (SGS) are used to approximate solutions to differential equations with stochastic parameters. In particular, they express the solution with an infinite orthogonal functional basis of the parameter space and derive a deterministic system of PDEs; the solution of this deterministic system can be used to produce a {surrogate} approximation of the original stochastic equations. When the parameters are correlated, the infinite series representation of the solution does not provably converge for all joint distributions; further, classic decorrelating transformations (e.g., Roseblatt) often introduce known numerical instabilities. Rahman (2017) established convergence in probability and distribution for correlated {Gaussian} parameters when the basis functionals are {multivariate Hermite polynomials} (MHPs), where these polynomials are only {weakly orthogonal} with respect to the underlying joint density. Due to weak orthogonality, the $N$th moments of MHPs introduced during Galerkin projection do not trivially decompose into products of one-dimensional expectations and have no closed-form expression for $N > 2$; consequently, these moments are typically estimated via brute-force sampling and quickly become prohibitively expensive to compute. In this paper, we introduce and prove several foundational results for MHPs. These results culminate in an equation that can be used to calculate the $N = 3$ moments (triple products) exactly, whose implementation dramatically reduces the computational bottleneck otherwise inherent to SGS with correlated Gaussian parameters.

title: Wave equation with unbounded terms driven by a stochastic measure
abstract: The one-dimensional wave equation with additive noise driven by a stochastic measure is considered. For the stochastic integrator, we assume only the sigma-additivity in probability and that $|y|^τ$ is integrable on $\mathbb{R}$ for some $τ>1/2$. The class of stochastic measures includes many important cases of random processes. In the equation, the stochastic measure depends only on the spatial variable. The existence, uniqueness, and Hölder regularity of the mild solution are proved. In the previous publications, similar results were obtained for the case of bounded terms of the wave equation driven by a stochastic measure. In our paper, one term may be unbounded, satisfying the linear growth condition. Nevertheless, we prove that the solution is bounded in this case.

title: On the Gauss sphere problem
abstract: In this article we improve Heath-Brown's estimate for the error term in the three-dimensional sphere problem, proving \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}=\frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{55/42+\varepsilon}). \] Incoporating the recent OpenAI quasi-GRH into our argument further improves this to \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}= \frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{\frac{2274811}{1743872}+\varepsilon}). \]

title: Perturbing the Conway sequence
abstract: We study the alternating perturbation of Conway's nested recurrence, $C(n)=C(C(n-1))+C(n-C(n-1))+(-1)^n$ for $n\geq 3$, with $C(1)=C(2)=1$. We prove that the sequence is well defined and satisfies $C(n)=ψ^{-3}n+O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, where $ψ>1$ is the real root of $ψ^3=ψ^2+1$.

title: Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincaré characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.

title: Sharp Brezis--Merle Inequalities for Polyharmonic Dirichlet Problems: Extremal Measures and Critical Asymptotics
abstract: We establish the Brezis--Merle inequality for very weak solutions of polyharmonic Dirichlet problems with integrable data on smooth bounded domains in conformal dimensions. The inequality is sharp both with respect to the admissible range of the exponent and to the quantity appearing on the right-hand side, which is characterized as the maximum of an associated one-pole Green functional. The supremum defining this quantity is not attained by any integrable datum, but remains unchanged when the admissible class is extended to Radon probability measures; in this enlarged class, the extremals are Dirac masses, and their concentration points are characterized in terms of the associated Green function. On the unit ball, we prove uniqueness of the extremal measure and obtain an explicit optimal bound extending the sharp result for the Laplacian. Finally, we determine the critical asymptotics of the sharp constant on the right-hand side and show that the possible limiting concentration points are selected by the maximum points of the polyharmonic Robin function.

title: Global existence for the semilinear regular Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation, II
abstract: In our previous work [25], we established the global existence of solutions to the semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux-Tricomi equation with power nonlinearity \(|u|^p\) in the case where the damping term dominates the mass term. In contrast, this paper studies the reverse case, namely, the existence of global solutions to the equation when the mass term dominates the damping term. We prove that small-data solutions exist globally if \[ p>\max\{p_0((m+1)n,μ), \widetilde{p}_1(n,m,μ)\} \] for \(δ\doteq(μ-1)^2-4ν^2\leq0\), where \(δ\) measures the relative dominance between the damping and mass terms, \(p_0(n,μ)\) is the \textit{Strauss-related} exponent defined by (1.12), and \(\widetilde{p}_1(n,m,μ)\) is defined by (2.5).

title: Linear Stability of Double-Double Orbits in the Equal-Mass Four-Body Problem via Index Theory
abstract: In this paper, using the Maslov-type index theory in symplectic geometry, we study the linear stability of the double-double orbits in the planar equal-mass four body problem. By analyzing its symmetry properties and variational characterization, we clarify the relationship between linear stability and its variational nature on various loop spaces and show that for any rotation angle $θ=\fracπ{n}$, the retrograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[3,30]$ and the prograde double-double orbits are linearly stable with integer $n\in[4,30]$. We also give the distributions of the eigenvalues on the unit circle of the monodromy matrices associated with the orbits. The basic idea is as follows: the variational characterization of the orbits provides information about its Morse index; based on its relation to the Maslov-type index, our stability criteria come into play.

title: Radial reduction, spherical splitting and root counts for two-sided quaternionic polynomials
abstract: We study quaternionic polynomials whose coefficients may occur on both sides of the variable, using their degree in the four real coordinates. Such polynomials can have no roots, or many more isolated roots than their degree. A simple root has an invertible real derivative, and its sign is the sign of that derivative's determinant. For a radial family, the roots over a non-real target reduce to one real equation. We obtain a sharp root bound and follow a change in the signed root count as roots escape to infinity. The main results concern spherical root sets for which the polynomial derivative is invertible in the two normal directions. Under a small polynomial perturbation, a sphere splits into simple roots corresponding to the zeros of a tangent vector field, when the derivative of that field is invertible at every zero. We obtain a sharp bound in terms of the perturbation degree and a signed count of two or of minus two. For even degrees, the construction yields polynomials with a single leading power and lower-degree terms whose simple root counts, divided by the fourth power of the degree, tend to one as the degree grows. An explicit quartic has 132 simple roots, and this count persists under small coefficient perturbations. For gradient perturbations, the roots correspond to equilibrium directions of an energy on the sphere. This correspondence gives energy thresholds for root disappearance and bounds the critical directions of polynomial orientation profiles in diffusion magnetic resonance imaging.
comment: 40 pages, 3 figures, methods and AI statement

title: Extending Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodules and noncommutative covers
abstract: Doi and Takeuchi, and independently Blattner, Cohen and Montgomery, have exhibited a correspondence between cleft extensions of an algebra $U$ by a Hopf algebra $H$ and $H$-measurings on $U$ equipped with a compatible normalized 2-cocycle. Each cleft extension is isomorphic as an algebra, a left $U$-module and a right $H$-comodule to the crossed product algebra constructed from the measuring and the cocycle. Cleft $H$-extensions are a special case of $H$-Hopf-Galois extensions, describing noncommutative principal $H$-bundles with affine total and affine base space. Corings are used to describe noncommutative space covers, allowing a description of possibly nonaffine noncommutative spaces. We propose to describe the total space of a noncommutative $H$-principal bundle by an internal $E$-coring in $H$-comodules where $E$ is an $H$-comodule algebra which is itself $H$-Hopf-Galois. This article focuses on the cleft case. As corings involve bimodules and morphisms of bimodules we extend the Doi--Takeuchi correspondence to bimodule $H$-comodules between cleft extensions on one side and bimodules of $H$-coinvariants equipped with bimodule $H$-measurings compatible with 2-cocycles on the other side. In fact, the correspondences for algebras and for bimodules are parts of a biequivalence of suitable bicategories defined in this article. As a corollary one obtains a correspondence between cleft $H$-extensions of corings and corings equipped with a nonabelian Čech 1-cocycle covalued in $H$.

title: Residue Sums Modulo Products of Two Distinct Odd Primes
abstract: Let $S_m(a)$ denote the sum of the least positive residues in one multiplicative period of $a$ modulo $m$, of length $k$. We study the equality $S_m(a)=mk/2$ for $m=pq$, where $p,q$ are distinct odd primes and $k$ is even. Complementary pairing settles subgroups containing $-1$; the remaining cases depend on their embedding in the two local unit groups. At index four, we exclude mixed cyclic subgroups with biquadratic annihilator and classify every eligible imprimitive quartic kernel using two odd integer moments at its prime conductor. For each fixed conductor, the proportion of admissible second primes giving equality is $1/4$ or $1/2$; full coset balance has proportion $1/4$. For primitive quartic characters, classical triangular character-sum identities yield explicit short-sum criteria, and the relative class-number formula gives an obstruction to a centered coset. At index six, we give structural counts and construct an infinite family modulo $19q$ in which nonzero sextic and quadratic moments cancel. These applications use a standard odd-character expansion, which also recovers the known index-two balance classification and determines the sign of its deviation. A reproducible census for $pq\le10000$ counts $75\,090$ eligible cyclic subgroups and identifies $101$ mixed index-four subgroups whose own sum is centered although some coset sums are not.

title: Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps
abstract: Stochastic flow maps promise few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) by learning to directly jump between times along the solution path, yet training these models to learn this solution map remains difficult. The primary obstacle is the Brownian path itself: it is an infinite-dimensional object which needs to be passed to the neural network and is nowhere differentiable, which makes the implementation of derivative-based losses that power the state-of-the-art deterministic flow maps just out of reach. We identify two core design principles which address these issues: a) represent the Brownian path with a basis which carries higher-order local information, and b) train with an objective that forces the network to use the full representation of the path, not just the first order. To address this, we leverage the shifted Legendre polynomial expansion with a Wong-Zakai styled objective, unlocking derivative-based losses. Finally, we propose a recipe for fine-tuning large pre-trained flow models into strong stochastic flow maps. We ablate through this design space on several toy problems and use our findings to transform a large flow model into a strong stochastic flow map on ImageNet, achieving roughly a three-fold improvement in FD-DINOv2 over SSFM at four NFE.

title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
abstract: We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g \le 2n(n-1)ω_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $ω_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le16πr, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$. Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le12π(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}μ_g\le\bigl[8π(1-v)+200π(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8π$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.

title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2π$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11π^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.

title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that R(5,10;5,8)=21 for the Generalized Threshold Ramsey Number
abstract: We prove that the generalized threshold Ramsey number R(5,10;5,8) equals 21. This number corresponds to the set Ramsey number r_5(10,8) introduced by Harborth. The proof is computer-assisted. We first enumerate all (4,6;5,8)-good and (5,10;4,4)-good graphs. Then we apply the lucky-vertex inequality derived from the McKay--Radziszowski edge identity to filter candidate pairs for a gluing search, and encode the remaining cases as SAT instances. The search yields exactly 17 non-isomorphic (5,10;5,8;20)-good graphs. Finally, we exclude all one-vertex extensions of these 17 graphs, which proves that no (5,10;5,8;21)-good graph exists.Additionally, we update the tabulation of small set Ramsey numbers r_5(m,n) for 1 <= m,n <= 10.

title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
abstract: Let $B(δ)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<δ<π/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,α}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cotδ$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.

title: A short proof of a range-relative FPTAS for polynomial integer optimization over bounded polyhedra
abstract: We give a short proof of a fully polynomial-time range-relative approximation scheme for polynomial optimization over the integer points of a bounded rational polyhedron in fixed dimension. The proof combines the reflecting-set decomposition of Cook, Hartmann, Kannan, and McDiarmid with Markov's polynomial derivative inequality and uses one integer linear feasibility query per refined cell. The running time is polynomial in the input encoding size, numerical degree, and reciprocal accuracy.

title: Inhomogeneous random graphs: how heavy tails reshape connectivity
abstract: We study inhomogeneous random graphs on $n$ vertices with independent Pareto weights of parameter $α>0$ and connection probabilities $\min(\varepsilon_n W_iW_j, 1)$. Our main focus is the infinite-mean regime $0<α<1$. Under the scaling $n\varepsilon_n^α=λ$, with $λ>0$ fixed, the global architecture of the graph is entirely governed by the Poisson point process $Π$ of rescaled extreme weights. In particular, the size of the largest component, divided by $n$, converges to a non-degenerate random variable expressed as an explicit functional of $Π$. Through the point process $Π$, we also characterize the exact limiting connectivity probability, uncovering a non-sharp connectivity threshold. The second largest component and the diameter of the largest component are bounded with high probability. The distance between two uniformly chosen vertices in the largest component is at most three with high probability. We also prove convergence of the point process of rescaled degrees and identify the limiting distribution of the maximum degree. For completeness, we obtain expected degree asymptotics, typical degree limits and connectivity regimes for all $α>0$. Due to the failure of classical branching process approximations in the infinite-mean regime, our approach relies fundamentally on analyzing the extreme weight environment $Π$.

title: The Conjugacy Problem for Recursively Presented Virtually Soluble Groups of Finite Prüfer Rank
abstract: We solve a long-standing conjugacy problem for finitely presented soluble groups of finite Prüfer rank, recorded as Problem~9.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, in the stronger setting of recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble groups. Robinson proved that, in every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble minimax group, conjugacy to any fixed element is decidable, while explicitly lefting open whether the procedure could be made uniform in the target element. We establish this uniformity. More specifically, we prove that every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble group of finite Prüfer rank has decidable Conjugacy Problem.

title: Continuity of Furstenberg entropy on Bowen Poisson bundles
abstract: We provide a sufficient criterion for continuity of the Furstenberg entropy of Bowen Poisson bundles, jointly in the random walk measure and the underlying invariant random subgroup. The criterion applies in particular for tree-like Poisson bundles of a free group and for intersectional invariant random subgroups on lamplighter groups. It also provides continuity of the boundary entropy spectrum of powers of prime measured groups.

title: Data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional traffic flow model: Dimension reduction and optimization strategies
abstract: We study the data-driven calibration of a two-dimensional first-order macroscopic traffic flow model, in which the movement along and across the road is described by a three-parameter flux model. The calibration is based on three real-world datasets, ranging from microscopic drone trajectories on German highways to aggregated urban sensor measurements. We recall the well-posedness of the underlying scalar conservation law and derive structural properties of the flux model. In particular, one parameter enters linearly and can be eliminated analytically, which reduces the non-linear least-squares problem from three to two dimensions. We solve the full and reduced calibration problem with two local optimization methods, Nelder-Mead and L-BFGS-B, and three global population-based methods Differential Evolution, Consensus-Based Optimization, and its deterministic variant Quasi-Monte Carlo consensus based optimization. In addition to accuracy and computational cost, we examine how sensitive the objective is to the parameters and how robust the algorithms are with respect to randomness and initialization. The reduced formulation is considerably cheaper and less sensitive to the choice of optimizer. The local methods are the most efficient when suitably initialized, whereas the global methods are more robust.

title: Dynamical low-rank approximations for the optimal control of matrix ODEs
abstract: We consider the open-loop optimal control of a dynamical system whose state is described by a time-dependent matrix $X(t)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$. Gradient-based optimization methods may incur substantial computational and memory costs, particularly for large-scale systems and fine temporal discretizations. To alleviate this computational burden, we develop a mathematical framework to use Dynamical Low Rank Approximations (DLRA) in optimal control problems. We study two distinct paradigms: the first one, called Optimize-then-Project (OtP), first derives the optimality system and then approximates both the state and adjoint equations using DLRA. The second one, called Project-then-Optimize (PtO), first replaces the state equation with its DLR approximation, and then derives the optimality conditions for the resulting optimization problem. The two approaches differ fundamentally concerning the role of the adjoint variable. In OtP, the adjoint variable evolves on the manifold of fixed rank matrices, whereas in PtO, the adjoint variable belongs to the tangent space to the fixed-rank manifold at the evolving state variable. This latter formulation leads to a covariant ODE describing the dynamics of the adjoint variable as the underlying tangent space evolves in time. For both approaches we establish rigorous error estimates for the approximated gradients, identifying how their accuracy depends on the low-rank approximations of initial and terminal conditions, the components of the state and adjoint vector fields normal to the relevant tangent spaces, the stability properties of the dynamics, and the manifold curvature. PtO further requires tailored time discretization strategies for the adjoint covariant ODE, which we show to be robust against small singular values of the state variable. To illustrate the framework, we apply these methods to the optimal control of a random parabolic PDE.

title: Harnack-type inequalities for nonlocal parabolic equations in the upper fast-diffusion range
abstract: We study non-negative weak solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear nonlocal parabolic equations of the form $$ (u^q)_t+\mathcal Lu=0, $$ where $\mathcal L$ is a nonlocal $p$-Laplace-type operator with a symmetric measurable kernel. We consider the fast-diffusion range $1<p<q+1$ and establish Harnack-type estimates in the upper fast-diffusion regime $\widetilde p_c<p<q+1$, where $\widetilde p_c$ is a critical exponent determined by the interplay between the temporal nonlinearity and the nonlocal diffusion. In particular, the estimates apply to the nonlocal parabolic $p$-Laplace equation and the nonlocal porous medium equation.

title: Subsequential Version of Breiman's Conjecture
abstract: We study randomly weighted sums \[ T_n=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_iY_i}{\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i}, \] where $(X_i)$ and $(Y_i)$ are independent sequences of i.i.d. random variables, with nonnegative weights $Y_i$, motivated by Breiman's conjecture. We introduce the class $ISSV$ of $I$-subsequentially slowly varying tails and establish a subsequential analogue of Darling's maximum--sum theorem. This provides a subsequential generalization of Breiman's slowly varying theorem and, as a corollary, resolves the slowly varying case of his conjecture. We also establish a subsequential analogue of Breiman's nonzero-index theorem, characterizing the existence of nondegenerate subsequential limits, distinct in distribution from $X_1,$ by the failure of slow variation of the integrated tail, for weight $Y_1$ with tail distributions outside the class $ISSV$. Finally, we formulate the subsequential separation principle, prove it under a finite-second-moment assumption, and show that its general validity would imply the nonzero-index case of Breiman's conjecture.

title: Algorithm duality from resolvent Moreau identities
abstract: Duality is classically defined as a relationship between objective functions, one that breaks down beyond convexity. We show that a more fundamental duality persists between the resolvent operators used to solve associated problems. We establish a framework from which we obtain complete characterizations of the duality-like correspondences between proximal fixed-point iterations and their alternating minimization scheme counterparts. Namely, we show the known primal-dual relationships between forward--backward splitting and Tseng's alternating minimization algorithm, and between the Douglas-Rachford method and alternating direction method of multipliers, to hold generically and irrespective of problem assumptions. The approach considered herein avoids the machinery of convex analysis entirely, providing a definitive formulation of algorithmic dualities in maximal generality while greatly simplifying their proofs. In particular, assumptions such as monotonicity, weak monotonicity, Lipschitz continuity, and injectivity of linear operators are all shown to be unnecessary. In addition, we utilize our framework to reveal and analyze a novel primal-dual relationship between backward-backward splitting and a special instance of the alternating minimization algorithm. This illustrates how our duality framework provides a principled basis for primal-dual algorithm design and analysis in nonmonotone settings. Finally, our experiments show that our backward--backward splitting--based approach reliably outperforms the FISTA and SR3 algorithms for the LASSO problem.

title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schrödinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(δ^2)$ ($δ>0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(δ^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.

title: Cartan Subalgebras of Dimension Drop Interval Algebras and Their Inductive Limits
abstract: We describe the conjugacy of non-degenerate Cartan subalgebras of the dimension drop interval algebras $M_m(\widetilde{\mathbb I}_p)$ in terms of double cosets of permutation groups, and describe their spectra by finite bi-partite multigraphs. All Cartan subalgebras are non-degenerate precisely when the two parameters are coprime. We also give splitting interval examples with prescribed finite numbers of Cartan conjugacy classes. Passing to inductive limits, we construct a unital simple AD algebra $\mathcal{A}$ of real rank zero and stable rank one, with $K_0(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z[1/3]$ and $K_1(\mathcal{A})\cong\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. It contains infinitely many mutually isomorphic but pairwise nonconjugate $\mathrm{C}^*$-diagonals. Their spectra are all homeomorphic to the dense amalgam of circles, while orbit multiplicities in the Weyl groupoids distinguish their embeddings. The same AD algebra also contains infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic Cartan subalgebras.

title: A recovery based linear finite element method for the Monge--Ampère equation
abstract: In this paper, we study finite element approximations of a fourth-order perturbed semilinear partial differential equation that arises naturally in the computation of viscosity solutions to the fully nonlinear Monge--Ampère equation. We develop a novel recovery-based $C^0$ linear finite element method for discretizing this model problem. The key analytical tool is a Miranda--Talenti-type estimate for the recovery operator, which guides the formulation of the discrete scheme and guarantees its well-posedness. We rigorously establish convergence in the $H^2$ norm by employing a fixed-point argument. Furthermore, optimal $H^1$-error estimates are derived using a duality argument. Numerical experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed method and validate the theoretical convergence results.

title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning incorporates physical knowledge into data-driven models, often through a partial differential equation (PDE) that the target is assumed to satisfy. However, how much this knowledge improves statistical performance remains unclear, especially when the physical model is imperfect. Since satisfying a PDE implies being differentiable, a natural benchmark for physics-informed regression is the best achievable performance when smoothness is the only prior information about the target function. We show that there is a characteristic threshold for the modeling error above which the physical prior cannot improve the convergence rate. The form of this threshold is common to every linear PDE and certain nonlinear PDEs. Below it, the gain depends on the equation type. For classes of elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs with constant coefficients, we establish convergence rates that improve continuously as the modeling error decreases, and prove their minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors. With exact physics, the rates correspond to learning in dimension d-1 rather than d, reflecting the freedom left by unknown boundary or initial data. We also give conditions for computing the estimator with near-linear complexity and show how to tune its hyperparameters without knowing the modeling error.

title: Geometric knowledge spaces, Attention pairing and Architectures
abstract: In this paper, we propose a geometric approach to deriving attention mechanisms and exploring potential new transformer architectures. We begin by formalizing the notions of knowledge worlds and attention pairings, then demonstrate how this framework naturally leads to the architectures of standard attention, causal attention, linear attention, tensor attention, and recurrent neural networks. Finally, we introduce several new geometric spaces that may inspire novel neural network architectures.

title: Kobayashi's problem for power semigroups of inverse semigroups
abstract: For a semigroup $S$ (written multiplicatively), let $\mathcal P(S)$ denote the semigroup of all non-empty subsets of $S$ under setwise multiplication. The finitary power semigroup $\mathcal P_\text{fin}(S)$ is the subsemigroup of $\mathcal P(S)$ consisting of all non-empty finite subsets of $S$. Kobayashi's problem asks for which classes $\mathcal O$ of semigroups every isomorphism $\mathcal P(H) \to \mathcal P(K)$ with $H, K \in \mathcal O$ maps singletons bijectively onto singletons and hence induces an isomorphism $H \to K$. We give an affirmative answer for inverse semigroups, extending previous results for groups, semilattices, and, more generally, Clifford semigroups. We also establish the corresponding rigidity theorem for finitary power semigroups. To this end, we develop a new framework that provides a common approach to both settings.

title: Cyclic group tensors and the volume ratio of projective tensor products
abstract: We revisit the problem of estimating the norm of the natural embedding from the Euclidean space $\ell_2^{n^3}$ into the projective tensor product $\ell_p^n\otimes_π\ell_q^n\otimes_π\ell_r^n$ in the range $1\le p\le q\le 2\le r\le\infty$, studied by Giladi, Prochno, Schütt, Tomczak-Jaegermann and Werner [J. Funct. Anal. 273 (2017), 471-495]. Using convolution on finite cyclic groups, we establish new lower bounds that improve their estimates and determine the exact asymptotic order of the embedding norm whenever $1/p+1/q+1/r\ge 2$. We then apply an estimate of Boedihardjo for the injective norm of random tensors to a randomly signed cyclic convolution tensor and use multilinear interpolation to determine the optimal exponent throughout the entire parameter range, up to logarithmic factors. As consequences, we obtain corresponding improvements and asymptotically sharp estimates, up to logarithmic factors, for the volume ratio of these projective tensor products.

title: Avoiding two cycles in Avoider--Enforcer games
abstract: We study the strict and monotone $(1:b)$ Avoider--Enforcer games on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$. We prove that, for integers $n\ge2$ and $b\ge6n$, Avoider can keep his graph a forest after every move, except possibly the last. Thus, his final graph contains at most one cycle. This answers Question~10 of Clemens, Ehrenmüller, Person, and Tran, which asks whether a bias linear in $n$ is sufficient.

title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
abstract: We develop the first tensor-product sparse-grid finite element discretizations of Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. We construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to full grids.

title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schrödinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
abstract: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties. Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure. With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.

title: Maximal velocity estimates for Hardy operators
