abstract: We prove maximal velocity estimates for the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator, and possibly external potentials. As an application, we give another proof of the nonexistence of the wave operator intertwining Hardy operators with and without long-range perturbations with Coulomb decay.

title: Dissipation Bounds and Hardness in Globally Asymptotically Stable Quadratic Systems
abstract: Approximating the maximum retained energy fraction in globally asymptotically stable quadratic systems of growing dimension is NP-hard at every fixed positive additive error below $1/2$, even when strict quartic Lyapunov functions and strictness proofs are constructed in polynomial time and included in the input. Polynomial-factor approximation is also NP-hard for the least dissipated fraction, energy-halving time and structured coefficient distance to loss of asymptotic stability. For a partially damped family, minimum unit-sphere coupling norm equals that distance, with two-sided inverse-square halving-time bounds at distances in $(0,1/2]$ and explicit coefficient factors. Additive hardness persists under structured coefficient perturbations and direct damping, even with global exponential stability, a strict quadratic Lyapunov function and a Hurwitz Jacobian.
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures; revised proof exposition and conclusion

title: A unified approach for estimation of unnormalized models via Stein operators
abstract: In this paper, we develop a unified framework connecting proper scoring rules and Stein's method for the estimation of unnormalized models. We construct a class of proper scoring rules that encompasses score matching, ratio matching, pseudolikelihood, and noise contrastive estimation. We show that these proper scoring rules naturally induce Stein operators. This connection yields a new construction principle for Stein operators, and enables us to study estimators based on these scoring rules through the geometry associated with the induced Stein operators. Using this geometric perspective, we provide a unified characterization of the asymptotic efficiency of the resulting estimators.

title: Finite-to-One Maps into Band-Limited Function Spaces and Cubical Shifts with a Hurewicz Bound
abstract: Let $(X,T)$ be a dynamical system with the marker property and finite mean dimension $m$. We prove that, for every integer $D>m$, there exists an equivariant continuous map $f:X\to([0,1]^D)^{\mathbb Z}$ whose fibers contain at most $\lfloor D/(D-m)\rfloor$ points; in particular, $f$ is an embedding when $D>2m$. This is the dynamical analogue of the fiber bound in Hurewicz's classical theorem (1933) for continuous maps into Euclidean cubes. For every real number $a>m$, we also construct an equivariant continuous map from $X$ into the closed unit ball of the real Bernstein space of bounded continuous functions on $\mathbb R$ whose Fourier transforms, understood in the sense of distributions, are supported in $[-a/2,a/2]$, with each fiber containing at most $\lfloor a/(a-m)\rfloor$ points. The proof adapts the signal-analysis method of Gutman--Qiao--Tsukamoto (2019) to the finite-to-one setting and simplifies its analytic and geometric ingredients for $\mathbb Z$-actions.

title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $β_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].

title: The minimal period solution of Hamiltonian systems with even potentials
abstract: We consider the autonomous system $\ddot{q}+\nabla V(q)=0$ in an arbitrary finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The potential is assumed to be even, nonnegative and of class $C^2$, to satisfy $V(x)=o(|x|^2)$ at the origin, and the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz superquadratic inequality outside a ball. We prove that, for every prescribed $T>0$, the system has a nonconstant solution with $T$ being its minimal positive period.

title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for optimal control of coupled forward-backward stochastic control systems driven by G-Brownian motion
abstract: In this paper, we study a coupled forward-backward stochastic control system driven by G-Brownian motion. Based on some detailed estimates for control system, we obtain the variational inequality for cost functional, which is a necessary condition for optimality. Furthermore, we prove that this necessary condition is also a sufficient condition under the usual convexity assumptions.

title: An Exact 93-Move Solution to a Nonlocal Crystal-Exchange Puzzle
abstract: We determine the minimum number of directional commands needed to solve alevel of Order of the Sinking Star, modeled as a crystal-exchangepuzzle on an 11*11 board. A command swapsthe player with the nearest crystal in the selected row or column, regardlessof distance; only an empty ray permits an ordinary unit walk. Two gates admitthe player to the exit exactly while all sixteen crystals occupy their targetcells. We give an explicit 93-command solution and exclude every shortersolution by an exact, cost-bounded breadth-first search. The search representsa position by its seventeen occupied cells and one active cell. Its admissibleheuristic partitions command costs between a compressed core abstraction andresidual motion, strengthened by a necessary activation detour and a cornervisit condition. The completed computation retained 605,349,215 occupied setsand 1,863,925,136 states. We prove the reductions and pruning conditions,describe the exact storage scheme, and provide source code, execution logs,and a reproduction driver. The result is a computer-assisted proof for thespecified instance, with an explicit implementation trust boundary.

title: $q$-middle Laplace transform and its applications
abstract: We introduce a $q$-analog of the one-variable middle Laplace transform defined by the first author. We establish its invertibility and preservation of irreducibility, and derive a decomposition of $q$-middle convolution in terms of this transform. As applications, we obtain integral representations of solutions to the confluent $q$-hypergeometric equation and its variant, and construct a transformation of the $2\times 2$ Lax linear equation associated with the $q$-Painlevé equation of type $A_4^{(1)}$.

title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions $2\le n\le 5$
abstract: In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $μ$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.

title: Frequency Structure of AMM Liquidity Pools: A Multiresolution Analysis of Regime Transitions
abstract: This study examines the temporal structure of liquidity pools in constant-product automated market makers. Using a sample of eighteen pools observed at a five-minute frequency over two years, it aims to identify the temporal scales at which interactions within the system occur and how these interactions reorganize in response to changes in the volatility regime. Methodologically, the study proposes a strictly causal Haar multiresolution analysis in which each variable is estimated using only the information available at the time of measurement. Within this decomposition, three dimensions are examined: the scale composition of the return-to-risk relationship, the frequency-band coupling between pool activity and price volatility, and the detection of regime transitions using a fluctuation-to-trend indicator. The results reveal a clear structural segmentation: pool variability is concentrated at fast scales, whereas the relationships among its series, signal persistence, and information on subsequent performance reside at slow scales. Aggregate measures do not distinguish this separation because they combine both components before they can be compared.

title: Local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: Trace formula approach for epsilon dichotomy
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a proof independent of the theta-lifting for the epsilon-dichotomy of the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture of real unitary groups for tempered L-parameters. The approach is based on the local trace formula and endoscopic character identities following Waldspurger and Chen-Luo.

title: Symmetry Inheritance and Exact Mirror Symmetry Reduction for Electric Field Vector Wave Problems with PEC Boundaries
abstract: A symmetry-inheritance and exact domain-reduction framework is developed for the second-order vector wave equation of the electric field in bounded domains with a perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary and general spatially varying anisotropic media. Orthogonal group actions on polar vectors, axial vectors, and second-order constitutive tensors are used to derive the transformed curl--curl equation and PEC trace directly from the original boundary-value problem. Under unique solvability, the common symmetry group of the problem data is inherited by the electric field. When the symmetry group of the electromagnetic medium admits a mirror symmetry, an arbitrary impressed current can be decomposed by the associated reflection projectors into mirror-even and mirror-odd components. The corresponding full-domain fields inherit the respective parities, and their exact restriction to one half-domain yields a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) condition for the even field and a PEC condition for the odd field. The original problem is therefore represented exactly by two independent reduced-domain problems. A symmetry-compatible first-family Nédélec discretization preserves this decomposition at the discrete level. Analytical and numerical results verify the symmetry-inheritance theory, the exact PEC/PMC reduced-domain formulations, and the discrete reconstruction for constant and spatially varying anisotropic conductive media under both symmetric and asymmetric excitations.

title: Revisiting the infinite Galois correspondence via group representations
abstract: Inspired by Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem, we interpret the Galois correspondence as a special case of a simple general principle in harmonic analysis on profinite groups. This also gives a representation-theoretic characterisation of profinite groups.
comment: 5 pages; a work came from teaching by humans

title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows
abstract: Low-NFE generative ODE sampling is constrained not only by solver order, but also by how a fixed budget of network evaluations is distributed along the flow. We develop a density-level backward-error framework that identifies the component of a solver's modified-equation defect that changes the evolving marginal, while excluding solenoidal trajectory distortion that is invisible in Wasserstein tangent geometry. The resulting residual induces a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and, through gauge freedom, an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity representatives of the same density path. This separates our approach from schedule search driven by trajectory or endpoint surrogates and from higher-order solver design. Exact Gaussian and mixture models establish the mechanism, including cases where curvature-based allocation fails and continuum-optimal transport is not discretization-optimal. On a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM probability-flow ODE, density-aware allocation consistently improves fixed-update Euler sampling in the low-NFE regime. Matched-seed convergence to a dense Euler reference confirms that the method accelerates approximation of the same high-NFE flow rather than changing the asymptotic sampler.
comment: 37 pages, including appendices. Accepted as a poster at ICOMP 2026

title: Enhanced Langlands Parameters of Regular Principal Series
abstract: We describe the enhanced Langlands parameters of the irreducible constituents of a regular principal series of a quasi-split reductive group over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Starting from the chamber parametrization by Rodier and Luo, we determine the monodromy of each constituent and show that its enhancement is trivial. In particular, we obtain the corresponding parameter of the unique irreducible subrepresentation.

title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
abstract: We prove that the set of numbers of type $n = 2m^2$ below $X$ which cannot be written as a sum of two primes has cardinality at most $X^{19/24 + o(1)}$.

title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{á}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$. In this paper, we extend their result by showing that for every positive integer $k$, the $k$-apex of any tree or any forest with average degree at least one is common. Our proof involves an application of the entropy method.

title: General function bases moment models for suspended sediment with vertical profile of concentration
abstract: We introduce a general hydrostatic shallow moment framework for suspended sediment transport with vertically varying horizontal velocity and concentration profiles. The formulation is constructed over arbitrary vertical functional bases that are numerically orthogonalised via the Gram-Schmidt algorithm. This approach allows the approximation spaces for the vertical profile to be adapted to the specific structure of each physical variable, where also the velocity and sediment concentration can be projected onto different functional spaces. To overcome the limitations due to the inherent oscillatory nature of global Legendre polynomials, we explore a specific continuous piecewise linear $\mathbb{P}_1$ finite-element basis. Furthermore, non-uniform vertical partitions are considered, enabling an enhanced representation of the vertical profiles in specific regions. Numerical experiments involving boundary layers and suspended sediment transport demonstrate that the proposed framework is accurate to reproduce the expected vertical profiles. The improvement is particularly significant for sediment concentration profiles with sharp vertical variations, where polynomial reconstructions exhibit pronounced oscillations leading to physically meaningless profiles, whereas the $\mathbb{P}_1$ bases produce a qualitatively accurate representation of the vertical profiles observed in the sedimentation processes.

title: Approximate Matrix Multiplication through Joint Leverage Score Sampling
abstract: In this paper, we investigate approximate matrix multiplication through random sampling. Specifically, we propose using a non-uniform sampling distribution constructed from the leverage scores of the two matrices, and characterize the associated approximation error in terms of the matrix spectral norm; which is well-known to better characterize the downstream error when the matrix product operator is applied to an input vector. We provide the probability error bounds for the proposed algorithm are also given, and discuss connections to data-oblivious approximate matrix multiplication, and graph sparsification algorithms.

title: Local well-posedness, blow-up phenomenon and ill-posedness for a model system of the radiating gas
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Cauchy problem for a model system of radiating gas in multi-dimensional space. Firstly, we prove that the model is locally well-posed in Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $s>1+\frac{d}{p}$ (resp., $s=1+\frac{d}{p}$, $r=1$), including the endpoint space $B^1_{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Secondly, we show that the data-to-solution map is not uniformly continuous on bounded subsets of these Besov spaces. Moreover, we construct a blow-up scenario and derive two sufficient blow-up conditions, which improve the previous blow-up condition obtained in \cite{MR3016436}. Finally, we prove that the Cauchy problem is ill-posed in the critical space $B^{1+\frac{d}{p}}_{p,r}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $r>1$ in the sense of norm inflation.

title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
abstract: Significant spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal history-dependent attenuation jointly govern wave propagation in composite materials, making full-scale direct numerical simulation (DNS) computationally prohibitive. This study proposed a high-order multi-scale (HOMS) method for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems with highly oscillatory and discontinuous material coefficients. Using a multi-scale asymptotic expansion approach, the macroscopic homogenized equation, and first- and second-order correction terms are derived to construct the high-accuracy HOMS solution. Moreover, a local pointwise error analysis identifies the leading residual eliminated by this HOMS solution and validates its local physical balance preservation. Then, a global energy-norm error estimate establishes the $O(\varepsilon)$-order convergence rate for the HOMS solution. Subsequently, an efficient spatiotemporal multi-scale algorithm integrating the finite element and finite difference methods is designed, which employs a novel fully discrete $L2\text{-}1_σ$-Newmark scheme, and corresponding unconditional shifted-energy stability and explicit convergence rates are also obtained for the macroscopic homogenized displacement and velocity, respectively. Both two- and three-dimensional examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness of the proposed HOMS method. This work provides an effective multi-scale tool for nonlocal-in-time wave simulation in engineering applications.

title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
abstract: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and étale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.

title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
abstract: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

title: A spinor-adapted geometric approach to nonlinear Dirac systems on the Schwarzschild black hole background
abstract: Building on our previous work, we extend the spinor-adapted geometric method for nonlinear Dirac systems from small perturbations of Minkowski spacetime to the Schwarzschild background. As a linear foundation, we establish integrated local energy decay estimates and an \(r^p\)-weighted energy hierarchy for spinor fields, adapting the physical-space approach of Dafermos and Rodnianski to the Dirac setting. The main focus of the paper is nonlinear. We consider a semilinear tensorial wave--Dirac model motivated by the wave-gauge reduction of the Einstein--Dirac system and prove global small-data stability. A principal difficulty is the apparent loss of derivatives arising from the coupling between the first-order Dirac equation and the second-order tensorial wave equation. We overcome this difficulty through a spinor-adapted energy hierarchy that exploits the complementary roles of the Dirac-current energy and the spinorial wave energy. In particular, the nonlinear estimates are closed without requiring the top-order Dirac-current estimate. The nonlinear analysis demonstrates that the spinorial structures remain essential on the black-hole background. The combination of Dirac-current energy, spinorial wave energy, Kosmann Lie derivatives, and the Clifford-algebraic null structure enables us to close the nonlinear estimates without imposing an independent null condition on the tensorial wave equation. Thus, the nonlinear closure relies fundamentally on structures intrinsic to the Dirac equation. A second main result is the global small-data stability of the Maxwell--Dirac system in the Lorenz gauge on the Schwarzschild background, under a vanishing-charge assumption. This extends the nonlinear stability theory to a genuine gauge-coupled Dirac system and demonstrates the applicability of the spinor-adapted physical-space approach beyond the tensorial wave--Dirac model.

title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincaré polynomial is nonzero.

title: Threshold Attainment and Sharp Asymptotics for $L^p$-Perturbed Moser--Trudinger Functionals on $\mathbb{R}^2$
abstract: In this paper, we study the critical Moser--Trudinger supremum \[ S(λ,p) = \sup_{\substack{ u\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\\ \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} (|\nabla u|^2+u^2)\,dx\le 1 }} \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \left(e^{4πu^2}-1-λ|u|^p\right)\,dx, \qquad p\ge 2. \] Building on the classification away from the thresholds by Chen, Jiang, Lu and Zhu (2026), we resolve the endpoint cases: both thresholds for $p=2$ and the finite threshold for $2<p\le4$ are attained. We also prove compactness of centred radial extremals and one-sided value expansions governed by the selected endpoint $L^p$ mass. For $p>4$, we quantify how extremals spread out as $λ\to\infty$ by establishing the two-term expansion \[ S(λ,p)=4π+\mathcal C_pλ^{-2/(p-4)} +D_pλ^{-4/(p-4)}+o\bigl(λ^{-4/(p-4)}\bigr), \] Here $\mathcal C_p$ is the maximum of a limiting variational problem at unit $L^2$ mass. An explicit correction involving the sixth moment and the full $H^1$ normalization determines $D_p$ and selects the limiting maximizers. Rescaled centred radial extremals converge strongly to these profiles in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ along subsequences. For every fixed $λ>λ_*(4)$, we further establish \[ \lim_{p\downarrow4}(p-4)\log\bigl(S(λ,p)-4π\bigr) =2\log\frac{λ_{\mathrm{loc}}}λ<0, \] where $λ_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is the local critical penalty determined by the sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg constant. The gradient energy has the same logarithmic rate, and the centred radial profiles, normalized in mass and gradient energy, converge along subsequences to sharp Gagliardo--Nirenberg optimizers. An exact transfer identity extends these endpoint and asymptotic results to every constant planar norm.

title: Continuous spectrum-shrinking maps between finite-dimensional power-associative algebras
abstract: For finite-dimensional complex power-associative algebras $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$, each equipped with its unique Hausdorff vector topology, we characterize continuous spectrum-shrinking maps $φ:\mathcal{A}\to\mathcal{B}$, i.e. maps satisfying $\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{B}}(φ(x)) \subseteq\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$. The spectrum of an element is the zero set of its minimal polynomial, computed in the unitization for nonunital algebras. No such map exists when $\mathcal{A}$ is unital and $\mathcal{B}$ is nonunital. Otherwise, we symmetrize both products by setting $x\circ y:=\tfrac{1}{2}(xy+yx)$ and factor out the nilradicals to obtain semisimple Jordan quotients. We prove that a continuous map $φ$ is spectrum-shrinking precisely when, for every $x\in\mathcal{A}$, Jacobson's generic minimal polynomials of the simple quotient coordinates of $φ(x)$ are products of fixed nonnegative integer powers of those of $x$, with an additional fixed monomial factor allowed when $\mathcal{A}$ is nonunital. Comparing degrees gives linear Diophantine equations characterizing existence, and every nonnegative integer solution is realized by a polynomial spectrum-shrinking map. Spectrum preservation, meaning equality of spectra, is equivalent to additional positivity conditions. We also determine when every continuous spectrum-shrinking map preserves spectra and show that every continuous map $f:\mathcal{A}\to\mathbb{C}$ with $f(x)\in\mathrm{sp}_{\mathcal{A}}(x)$ for all $x\in\mathcal{A}$ is $\mathbb{C}$-linear and satisfies $f(x\circ y)=f(x)f(y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal{A}$.

title: Local Lyapunov Exponent-Guided Stochastic Midcourse Correction Design of Low-Energy Earth-Moon Transfers
abstract: Midcourse correction is essential for reliable cislunar transfer missions. For low-energy Earth-Moon transfers, strongly nonuniform error growth makes conventional correction strategies less effective. This paper proposes a stochastic midcourse correction design for low-energy Earth-Moon transfers based on local Lyapunov exponent (LLE). The local error-amplification characteristics of the nominal trajectory are first analyzed using an instantaneous LLE. The analysis shows that strong sensitivity is concentrated near periapsis, and that the LLE maxima coincide with regions of strong finite-time error growth. These maxima are therefore used to segment the trajectory and define the number of corrections. Based on this segmentation, a reduced parameterization is introduced to describe the correction epochs, while second-order state transition tensors (STTs) are employed for nonlinear correction targeting. The resulting timing variables are then optimized through a sample-average approximation of the chance-constrained stochastic problem. Paired Monte Carlo simulations show that, under the same mission-accuracy requirements, the proposed strategy greatly improves the reliability and robustness of trajectory recovery while requiring less correction cost than the classical Breakwell spacing-ratio strategy.

title: Order-Specified Quaternion CP Decomposition: Models, Algorithms, and Applications
abstract: Tensor CP decomposition serves as a fundamental tool for representing multiway data. While quaternion tensors are well suited to modeling color visual data, extending CP decomposition to the quaternion domain is nontrivial due to the noncommutativity of quaternion multiplication. This paper develops an order-specified quaternion CP decomposition (OS-QCP) for third-order tensors, allowing all three factor matrices to be quaternion-valued and explicitly incorporating their multiplication order into the model. We show that different multiplication orders can yield different OS-QCP ranks for the same quaternion tensor, characterize the permutation and quaternion scaling indeterminacies, and establish a sufficient condition for essential uniqueness for any prescribed multiplication order. An explicit example further shows that OS-QCP rank can depend on the multiplication order even when the complex representation of the quaternion tensor admits an essentially unique CP decomposition. An alternating least-squares (ALS) algorithm is derived by expressing quaternion left and right multiplication as real linear operators, reducing each factor update to real least-squares problems. To accommodate order dependence in tensor completion, we further introduce an order-ensemble quaternion CP (OE-QCP) model that incorporates different multiplication orders through nonnegative weights. The model jointly estimates three quaternion factor matrices and the order weights, with each single-order OS-QCP model included as a special case. The resulting completion problem is solved by a parallel row-wise masked ALS algorithm. Experiments on color video inpainting demonstrate the effectiveness and competitive performance of the proposed method.

title: Adaptive Grid Refinement for Optimal Feedback Control
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic approach for adaptive grid refinement for solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) partial differential equation (PDE) to obtain the optimal feedback control. Traditional grid generation methods often face challenges associated with state-space dimensionality, solution regularity, and large variations in the solution. Whereas fixed grid generation methods may fail to capture the intricate details of the optimal solution, our methodology addresses this challenge by dynamically refining the grid used to solve the HJB equation, thereby optimizing computational resource usage while targeting improved solution accuracy. The reinforcement learning (RL)-based approach presented in this study seeks to reduce the node population while constructing a grid with higher node density in regions with large discretization error.
comment: Presented at the 47th Annual AAS Guidance, Navigation, and Control Conference, Breckenridge, Colorado, January 31-February 5, 2025. AAS Paper 25-056

title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.

title: Lipschitz numbers and fine differentiability on metric measure spaces
abstract: On a metric space equipped with a doubling measure supporting a Poincaré inequality, we introduce capacity-relaxed infinitesimal Lipschitz numbers and characterize Newtonian functions in $N^{1,p}$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and functions of bounded variation. If $X$ is additionally $Q$-regular, then every BV function is $1$-finely differentiable at $μ$-almost every point, and its fine differential agrees with its approximate Cheeger differential. We also extend a Sobolev regularity criterion from continuous to $p$-quasicontinuous functions.

title: An Arnold-Type Stability Analysis of Vortex Filaments
abstract: We establish nonlinear orbital stability of circular arcs with opening angle $θ\le π$ and closed circles under the Localized Induction Equation (LIE), with prescribed endpoint constraints for arcs. Our Arnold-type variational approach combines two conserved quantities, the bending energy and a component of the fluid impulse, into a functional that we prove is comparable to the squared $H^2$-distance from the corresponding orbit for all admissible curves. For circular arcs with angle $θ>π$, we prove nonlinear orbital instability using the inverse generalized Hasimoto transformation.

title: Ideal class groups of certain real quadratic number fields and factorizations of values of certain quadratic polynomials
abstract: We determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $d-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive odd integers $x\leq\sqrt{p}$. We also determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $2p-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive even integers $x\leq\sqrt{2p}$. To this end, we show that these properties of $p$ and $2p$ impose restrictions on the class numbers and fundamental units of the real quadratic fields ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{p})$ and ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{2p})$.

title: Links of minimum degree and exact covering numbers
abstract: The covering number $C(v,k,t)$ is the least number of $k$-subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset lies in one of them. We reduce the question whether a covering with $L$ blocks exists to the classification of links. If every point of such a covering lies in at least $r$ blocks and $(r+1)v>kL$, some point lies in exactly $r$ blocks, and its link, the blocks through it with the point removed, is a $(v-1,k-1,t-1)$-covering with $r$ blocks. It then suffices to list these links up to isomorphism, to prove the list complete, and to show that no link in the list extends to a covering with $L$ blocks. Completeness is certified by one unsatisfiable formula that excludes the listed classes, so the program that lists the links need not be trusted. In general the last two steps are decided by propositional satisfiability (SAT) solving, with every formula written by two separately implemented encoders and every refutation checked by a formally verified proof checker. For links with four blocks and $t=3$ we give the classification by hand, under a condition on the parameters. As an application we determine twenty-five covering numbers with $t\in\{3,4,5\}$ in which the published lower bound was one less than the size of a known covering, among them $C(39,24,3)=9$.
comment: 11 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Code, class lists, logs, DRAT proofs and a long version: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23434567

title: Commutators in selfless C$^\ast$-algebras
abstract: We show that if \((A, τ)\) is a selfless C\(^\ast\)-probability space with \(τ\) being a faithful trace, then commutators are dense in \(\ker τ\).

title: Upper and lower bounds for heat kernels with very strong degeneracy
abstract: We consider the following degenerate parabolic equation on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $0$: $\partial_t u - \nabla\cdot(\varphi(t, x) \nabla u)= 0$, where $\varphi$ is a rough weight behaving like $|x|^θ$ near $0$ for some $θ\geq 2$, and $u$ satisfies Neumann boundary condition. We prove that this equation admits a heat kernel with upper and lower Gaussian-type bounds.

title: Tamed Euler Approximation of Invariant Measures for Weakly Interacting Particle Systems and McKean--Vlasov Equations
abstract: We analyze explicit tamed Euler approximations for weakly interacting particle systems and McKean--Vlasov diffusions with additive noise and polynomially weighted locally Hölder, possibly superlinear drift.Under dissipativity at infinity and suitable stability assumptions, we establish time-uniform $W_1$ bounds by reflection coupling, separating relaxation, time-discretization, and finite-particle errors.For small step sizes, we prove existence and uniqueness of numerical invariant laws and bound their error relative to the continuous-time particle invariant law uniformly in $N$ in a normalized joint $W_1$ distance. We further bound the error of the one-particle numerical invariant marginal relative to the McKean--Vlasov invariant law by $O(θ^{\min\{α,β/2\}}+N^{-1/2})$, where $θ$ is the step size, $N$ the particle number, $α\in(0,1/2]$ the taming exponent, and $β\in(0,1]$ the Hölder exponent. Analytical examples illustrate the framework for smooth and non-Lipschitz drifts.

title: Interpretable Cutting Plane Selection for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Using Genetic Programming
abstract: Cutting planes (cuts) remove fractional solutions from mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) without excluding any feasible integer solutions, making them a key ingredient in modern MILP solvers. Current state-of-the-art solvers rely on fine-tuned handcrafted cut strategies, which, despite their effectiveness, remain inherently static and can be suboptimal. More recently, learning-based approaches have been proposed to design adaptive cut strategies; however, most of these methods are based on neural networks, offering limited interpretability and providing no guarantees of convergence. In this paper, we propose \emph{Genetic Programming and Statistics-based Cut Selection} (GPSCS), the first learning-based framework that explicitly generalizes handcrafted cut selection heuristics into a fully interpretable policy. First, a genetic programming model evolves a symbolic scoring function that ranks candidate cuts using features derived from the cuts and the solving context. Second, a lightweight statistics-based mechanism adaptively determines the number of top-ranked cuts to add at each separation round by detecting significant score dropouts. We evaluate GPSCS within the SCIP solver on seven classes of synthetic and real-world benchmark instances, with a strong emphasis on generalization: evaluation instances are on average 41 times harder than those used for training. Experimental results show that GPSCS improves average solving time by $6\%$ compared to SCIP's default cut selection strategy and achieves a two-fold speedup over both a recent neural-network-based approach and a no-cut baseline, demonstrating strong robustness and generalization across heterogeneous MILP families.

title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

title: On some problems concerning the growth of Betti numbers
abstract: We investigate several problems concerning the growth of Betti numbers over commutative noetherian rings. First, we establish uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds for the ratios of consecutive Betti numbers of finitely generated modules of infinite projective dimension over an arbitrary local ring, giving an affirmative answer to a question of Avramov. We also prove the upper semicontinuity of the curvature of residue fields of localizations over excellent rings. Next, using zeros of Hilbert series, we obtain criteria for exponential growth of Betti and Bass numbers of graded modules. As applications, we establish exponential growth of the Betti numbers of canonical modules for non-Gorenstein positively graded Cohen-Macaulay domains. Furthermore, we show that the first Betti number of the canonical module of a non-Gorenstein generically Gorenstein Cohen-Macaulay local ring is strictly larger than the zeroth. In particular, both questions of Jorgensen and Leuschke have affirmative answers for Cohen-Macaulay quotients of Gorenstein local rings by monomial ideals in regular sequences.

title: Effective stability and sharp logarithmic time scales for Hamiltonian PDEs on the circle
abstract: We prove effective stability and matching logarithmic upper bounds for small solutions of Hamiltonian PDEs on the one-dimensional torus. An analytic coefficient-majorant calculus and an explicit normal-form iteration yield stability times with logarithms of order $L^{1+1/p}/(\log L)^{1/p}$ for Gevrey weights and $L^{1+(q-1)/(pq+1)}$ for logarithmic ultra-differentiable weights, where $L=\log(1/\varepsilon)$ and $p\geq1$ measures the order dependence of the small divisors. Even frequencies are organized into the exact blocks $\{n,-n\}$; elementary frequency gaps and constant weights on these blocks close the energy estimate. We verify the hypotheses for convolution NLS, fractional NLS with every fixed noninteger exponent $η>1/2$, and a beam equation with a metric parameter and a variational gradient nonlinearity. Two fixed analytic nonlocal Hamiltonian PDEs admit finite-support solutions whose first prescribed norm amplification occurs on the same logarithmic scales along sequences $\varepsilon_n\to0$. The common lower theorem applies to every sufficiently small datum of each admissible equation. Its combination with these examples establishes sharpness of both regularity-dependent scales under the same analytic and arithmetic hypotheses.

title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.

title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.

title: Counting and constructing Latin tableaux
abstract: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams and have interesting connections to linear algebra and Rota's basis conjecture. Conjecturally, a partition admits Latin tableaux if and only if it belongs to a special class called wide partitions. We prove that various classes of wide partitions admit Latin tableaux. We extend these classes further by showing that the number of Latin tableaux is weakly increasing over certain operations on wide partitions. Additionally, we establish an explicit formula for the number of Latin tableaux using (0,1)-matrices and matrix permanents.

title: On finite-dimensional attractor to 2D incompressible fluid with stress-diffusion
abstract: We consider incompressible visco-elastic rate-type fluid flow, with the Cauchy stress defined in terms of positive-definite symmetric tensor $B$. The tensor $B$ obeys an evolution equation, combining Oldroyd-B and Giesekus model, and, crucially, a diffusion term. Restricting ourselves to the 2D periodic problem, we show existence of a finite-dimensional global attractor. We also estimate its dimension explicitely in terms of the equation parameters.

title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine their definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve the desired asymptotic time-uniform coverage for a broad class of data-generating processes, including independent and identically distributed cases. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation, particularly useful in time-series settings. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.

title: Support periods of polynomials and support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes over Galois rings
abstract: Let \(A=\GR(p^e,r)\) have residue field \(\F_q\), and let \(λ\in A^\times\). We relate coefficient compression of monic divisors of \(X^N-λ\) to support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes. At a simple-root length, the support period of every nonconstant monic divisor is preserved at each coefficient precision and equals the order of the multiplicative stabilizer of its root set. For a cyclic Frobenius-orbit polynomial, the multiple equal-difference structure determines its support period, core degree, and least relative degree of an unramified extension over which all its basic-irreducible factors are binomials. Coordinate projections give every constacyclic code over a finite commutative ring a unique maximal interleaving into copies of one support-primitive code. At simple-root lengths over \(A\), the intrinsic period of a code is the greatest common divisor of the periods of its torsion codes. The decomposition yields distance and duality formulas and the arithmetic Singleton bound for free codes. At every length, a nonzero code over \(A\) has the same minimum Hamming distance as its highest torsion code, which gives a refined bound. At repeated-root lengths, identical torsion filtrations can occur with different intrinsic periods, while a class of nonzero codes obtained by substitution from simple-root generators retains the same core and minimum distance. Trace matrices recover the coefficients of basic-irreducible cores using unit pivots, and local Hensel corrections lift compressed factors directly. For \(X^n-1\) with \(p\nmid n\), lifting and output have quasi-linear bit cost in the compressed representation when the arithmetic data and residue factorizations are given.

title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
abstract: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=ν_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.

title: Nielsen coincidence theory for $(n,m)$-valued pairs
abstract: We define a Nielsen coincidence number for pairs of maps $(f,g)$ where $f$ is $n$-valued and $g$ is $m$-valued. The classical definition of the Nielsen number does not work in this setting, but we propose a theory where coincidence classes are allowed to overlap. We invoke a notion of multiplicity of a coincidence point, which indicates to how many classes it can belong, and we show that our Nielsen number is a homotopy-invariant lower bound for the number of coincidence points with multiplicity. We show a computational result in terms of single-valued lift factors, and using this, a Wecken property for self-maps of the circle.

title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
abstract: Let $(X,ω)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. For a non-uniruled compact Kähler manifold $X$ satisfying $μ_{ω_0,\max}(T_X)=0$ for some Gauduchon metric $ω_0$, we show that the corresponding maximal destabilizing subsheaf of $T_X$ splits off holomorphically and is polystable of slope zero with respect to every Gauduchon metric. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact Kähler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $ω$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $ω$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $κ^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.

title: Scattering in spacetime cones for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$, with a class of `mixed' nonlinearities that admit soliton solutions. We are interested in the long-time behaviour of solutions with finite, but possibly large, mass and/or energy. By a spacetime cone, we mean an open set in $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}_{x,t}$ that is invariant under dilation $(x, t) \mapsto (αx, αt)$ for all $α> 0$. Our main result is as follows: let $u(x, t)$ be the solution with initial condition in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$. Let $\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}$ be the mass and energy of $u$, and let $η= η(\mathscr{M}, \mathscr{E}) > 0$ be sufficiently small. Let $C_ε$ be the complement of $N \geq 1$ of sufficiently thin spacetime cones $\{ (x, t) \mid |x-v_jt| \leq εt \}$, where $v_1, \dots, v_N$ are fixed velocities and $ε$ is sufficiently small. If the $L^\infty$ norm of $u$ in $C_ε$ is $\leq η$, we prove that $u$ scatters in $C_{2ε} \subset C_ε$.

title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_δ$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization over Decentralized Networks
abstract: We study group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) over decentralized networks, where workers collaborate to learn robust models by minimizing the maximum local risk. Existing methods optimize only dual-regularized surrogates and establish guarantees for a globally averaged model that is not available to workers. In this paper, we directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized (SemiDec) and fully decentralized (Dec) settings. A key difficulty is that applying the primal-dual decomposition from centralized GDRO yields worker-dependent losses whose evaluation requires unavailable cross-worker information. To address this challenge, we develop a novel error decomposition that recasts decentralized GDRO as (i) a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem and a prediction-with-expert-advice problem in SemiDec, and as (ii) two coupled D-OCO problems in Dec, with discrepancy terms capturing inconsistencies among local decisions. By isolating consensus errors in analysis, we develop modular frameworks that support different consensus routines. We then establish the \emph{first} per-worker convergence guarantees for optimizing the original GDRO objective over decentralized networks. Instantiations with accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip achieve an $O(\sqrt{(\log m)/T})$ convergence rate over $T$ update rounds, while experiments demonstrate improved worst-worker performance over baselines.

title: Higher-order convex orders under free multiplicative convolution
abstract: We prove that free multiplicative convolution with a probability measure on $[0,\infty)$ preserves the $k$-convex order for every integer $k\ge2$, assuming finite $(k-1)$st absolute moments for the two measures being compared and for the convolving measure. The compared measures may have arbitrary support in $\mathbb{R}$.

title: Sharp asymptotics for a free boundary touching a degenerate boundary: the perpetual Heston put
abstract: We study the exercise boundary of the perpetual American put in the Heston model near zero variance. There the pricing operator degenerates, and the exercise boundary, a free boundary in the stock--variance half-plane, touches the boundary of the half-plane. No Feller condition is imposed. The boundary is analytic at positive variance and extends as a regular $C^1$ curve tangent to the zero-variance axis. Its approach to the axis follows one of three laws, according to whether the Feller ratio $2κθ/σ^2$ is larger than, equal to, or smaller than one: a logarithmic correction to linear order, an exponential correction in the square root of the logarithm, or a fractional power. In the first two cases the leading coefficients are explicit and the tangent is not Hölder continuous at the axis. In the third case the exponent is selected by a possibly nonsymmetric stable operator on the axis, and the amplitude is finite and positive.

title: A sharp weighted commutator inequality for rank-one matrices
abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ be positive definite Hermitian, where $n\ge 2$, and define $\|X\|_A^2=\mathrm{tr}(AX^*X)$ for all $X\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$. We determine the smallest constant $C_A$ for which $$ \|XY-YX\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le C_A\|X\|_A^2\|Y\|_A^2 $$ holds for all rank-one $X,Y\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$, where $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ denotes the Frobenius norm. The constant depends only on the two smallest eigenvalues of $A$ and is determined by a strictly monotone scalar equation. This answers the sharp-constant question for rank-one matrices formulated by Fang and Cheng. We also characterize all equality pairs.

title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $π_n\starπ_m\congπ_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $π_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.

title: Strongly log-concave measures and lattices
abstract: Let $Λ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be a full rank lattice with the property that $\det Γ\ge 1$ for all sublattices $Γ\subseteq Λ^*$. We prove that there exists a symmetric random vector $X \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with a smooth, strictly positive density $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying that (1) $f$ is $α$-strongly log-concave, where $α= 2π/e$, and (2) $X + Λ$ is uniform on $\mathbb{R}^n/Λ$. Moreover, the existence of such a density characterizes this property up to a universal dilation. There are a few consequences of the above. We list some. First, for such lattices we can bound the covering radius \[ μ(Λ, K) = \max_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\min_{λ\inΛ} \left\|x-λ\right\|_K \le \sqrt{\frac{2e}π} \cdot \mathbb{E}\,\left\|G\right\|_K \] of a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ containing $0$ in its interior, where $G \sim N(0,\mathrm{Id})$. This implies an $O(n \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the flatness constant and an $O(\log^{3/2} n)$ bound for the subspace flatness constant. We also compare the entire ordered spectrum of the associated flat torus on $Λ^*$ with that of a Gaussian, yielding an alternative proof of the reverse Minkowski theorem.

title: Bistable Dynamics and Complete Classifications of A Seasonal Competition Model Between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus
abstract: The bistable dynamics and a complete classification of global dynamics are established for a competition model between Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus subject to favorable-unfavorable seasonal shifts, originally proposed by Zheng et al. (2025). More precisely, by employing Floquet theory, we prove that the unique positive periodic solution must be unstable. Consequently, bistable dynamics naturally emerge, which provides a rigorous theoretical validation of the numerical simulation results reported in the aforementioned work. Building on this, we further derive a full classification of the model's global dynamics. In addition, we carry out a comprehensive analysis of how seasonal switching mechanisms govern the competitive outcomes between these two mosquito species, thereby offering insights into their ecological coexistence and potential displacement.

title: Alexander Torsion and Floer Comparisons in the BV-BFV Formalism
abstract: We compare relative Abelian BF torsion with the Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of knot Floer homology. A meridional annulus boundary condition identifies the normalized relative torsion with the Alexander polynomial. One exact prime-cyclotomic torsion value recovers all its coefficients under a sharp genus bound, compatibly with connected-sum gluing and branched-cover formulas. We compute interface contractions and obstructions to scalar comparisons, including the pairing defect of two-sector reduction for the degree-zero torus algebra. A six-generator dg resolution yields an equivalence of perfect-module categories preserving derived pairings and admits a classical one-dimensional BV-BFV realization. In the fixed nonresonant polynomial quantum BFV sector, over characteristic zero with $\hbar$ inverted, both states and Weyl observables reduce to a vacuum field; a Hochschild invariant obstructs a Morita equivalence with the degree-zero torus algebra. These results do not establish a full geometric BV-BFV/Floer equivalence.

title: Third and Fourth Moment Phenomena for Monochromatic Edges and Applications to Graph-Based Two-Sample Tests
abstract: Given a graph sequence $\{G_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, denote by $T_n$ the number of monochromatic edges when the vertices of $G_n$ are independently colored red or blue with probabilities $p$ and $1-p$, respectively. We characterize the asymptotic normality of $T_n$, after centering and scaling to unit variance, in terms of subgraph (motif) counts and standardized moments. One of the highlights of our results is a {\it third moment phenomenon}: for every fixed $p\in(0,1)\backslash\{\frac12\}$, asymptotic normality holds if and only if the standardized third moment converges to zero. The more familiar {\it fourth moment condition}, which requires the standardized fourth moment to converge to $3$, gives an equivalent characterization except at the two exceptional probabilities $p=\frac{1\pm1/\sqrt3}{2}$. At these values, the standardized fourth moment converges to $3$ for every graph sequence with a diverging number of edges, even when Gaussian convergence fails. In contrast, in the balanced case $p=\frac12$, the fourth moment condition characterizes asymptotic normality, while the third moment condition is insufficient. These results identify three distinct regimes for moment characterizations of Gaussian convergence, determined by the coloring probability. We further show that the third moment condition remains sufficient in the sparse regime, where $p=p_n \to 0$. As an application, we derive the limiting null distribution of two-sample statistics based on undirected $K$-nearest-neighbor graphs in the Poissonized setting, identifying sharp growth conditions on $K$ for asymptotic normality.

title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
abstract: We develop an interior penalty Nitsche finite element formulation for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems, which is derived from an interior-penalty stabilized Lagrange multiplier method. A distinctive feature of the derived method is that it simultaneously combines two popular stabilization strategies: (i) a boundary penalty mechanism similar to Nitsche's methods and (ii) an interior penalty mechanism as for Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) methods. Furthermore, the normal component of the numerical flux is single-valued across the mesh skeleton and available in closed form. We establish the equivalence between the hybridized Lagrange multiplier formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche (IPN) form, and we deliver the stability and convergence analysis of the latter. For sufficiently regular solutions, we establish energy-norm error estimates for the three symmetry variants. Under a piecewise elliptic regularity assumption on the adjoint problem, the $L^2$ estimate is optimal for the symmetric variant and exhibits a half-order loss for the incomplete and nonsymmetric variants; its constant may depend on the diffusion coefficients through the adjoint regularity constant. This single-valued numerical normal flux, available in closed form, provides a starting point for locally conservative $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming flux reconstruction, left for future work. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.
comment: 23 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Reproducibility package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23524954

title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $θ(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

title: Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes
abstract: We develop a measure-theoretic framework for Temporal-Logical Stochastic Processes (TLSP), in which temporal-logic specifications induce time-indexed stochastic observables capturing the robustness of temporal satisfaction. Building upon existing probabilistic interpretations of temporal-logic robustness, we systematically investigate the stochastic-process structure of these observables. We establish their measurability, shifted-filtration adaptedness, and sample-path regularity under suitable assumptions, and characterize the action of temporal operators on stochastic processes. We derive pathwise perturbation bounds and quantify the sensitivity of temporal satisfaction probabilities through the probability mass concentrated near the logical boundary. A topology on the observable-process space and a semantic pseudometric on temporal formulas are introduced to establish convergence of temporal-logical observables under perturbations of formula parameters and temporal intervals. We further characterize conditions ensuring weak convergence of observable-process distributions and convergence of temporal satisfaction probabilities. Finally, we establish a process-level large-deviation principle for temporal-logical observables, providing a variational characterization of rare temporal events through minimum-action trajectories. The resulting framework connects temporal-logic semantics with stochastic-process topology, stability, convergence, and rare-event asymptotics, providing a mathematical foundation for the analysis of temporally constrained stochastic systems.
comment: Submitted to Stochastic Processes and their Applications journal

title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established.

title: Some Expressions involving Bernoulli, Harmonic, and Stirling Numbers
abstract: In this paper, we establish several identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers. Our approach extends the method developed by Kargin and Mutluer.

title: The Logarithmic A-Discriminant
abstract: We extend the GKZ theory of discriminants to the setting of Euler integrals where both coefficients and exponents are variables. The integrand is the likelihood function of a toric model in algebraic statistics, whose number of critical points is the volume of the Newton polytope. Our logarithmic A-discriminant vanishes when two critical points come together. This discriminant is a hypersurface, parametrized by the logarithmic Horn uniformization. Hurwitz forms of toric varieties yield a degree formula, and a description of leading coefficients. We emphasize applications and computations.

title: Small deviations for integrators in terms of Itô--Wiener expansions
abstract: In this paper, we investigate small deviations for a class of Gaussian processes, known as integrators. In general, such processes are non-Markovian and may even fail to be semimartingales. First, we investigate small deviations for the multi-dimensional Wiener process, focusing on the asymptotic behavior of the Fourier--Wiener transform of the associated hitting event. We analyze the Fourier--Wiener transform and the separate summands in its Itô--Wiener expansion. Then, we establish the asymptotic limits of the associated multiple integrals with heat kernels. Finally, we obtain the small deviation asymptotic result for the integrator $η$ associated with the continuous linear operator.

title: On the existence of independent inner functions
abstract: The existence of independent inner functions is established: there exist inner functions $\varphi$ and $ψ$, both vanishing at the origin, such that $$ \frac{1}{2π}\int_0^{2π} \varphi^m(e^{iθ}) \overline{ψ^n(e^{iθ})}\,dθ= 0, \qquad m,n \geq 1. $$ In fact, both $\varphi$ and $ψ$ can be chosen to be Blaschke products. The proof proceeds by an iterative construction, which suggests a general approach to produce inner functions with a desired joint distribution.

title: The Local Dyadic Conjecture
abstract: A rational with denominator a power of two is said to be dyadic. A long standing conjecture of Paul Seymour predicts that for an ideal clutter, the dual of the set covering problem always admits an optimal solution where all variables take dyadic values. We present a local version of this conjecture, and motivate it by proving an important special case.

title: Curvature-Scaled Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Convergence Beyond Smoothness
abstract: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) has established itself as a widely used method for training deep neural networks. Despite its popularity, existing convergence guarantees for SAM-type methods require smoothness, a restrictive assumption. Generalized smoothness conditions have recently been proposed in the analysis of gradient methods but remain underexplored for SAM. To analyze the effect of SAM's perturbation under generalized smoothness, we use relative gradient distortion to quantify how the sharpness-aware direction departs from the original gradient. Under $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness, we show that this distortion can become unbounded near stationarity for SAM and at large gradients for its unnormalized variant (USAM), with examples where SAM cycles and USAM diverges. We then establish a necessary condition for uniform distortion control among perturbations along the gradient whose nonnegative multipliers depend only on its norm. Motivated by this condition, we propose Curvature-Scaled SAM (CS-SAM), which scales both the perturbation and the descent step by suitable curvature upper bounds, and prove that it uniformly bounds the distortion. Under both $(L_0,L_1)$- and $(H_0,H_1)$-smoothness, we establish deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the best squared gradient norm on nonconvex objectives, last-iterate $\mathcal{O}(1/T)$ rates for the function gap on convex objectives with a minimizer, and linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. With zero perturbation, our guarantees recover the rates for gradient descent with $(L_0,L_1)$- or $(H_0,H_1)$-based step-sizes. Minibatch experiments on computer vision tasks demonstrate competitive performance for both variants, with the $(H_0,H_1)$ variant achieving the highest mean best-test accuracy in all four settings against tuned SAM and USAM with constant and cosine annealing schedules.

title: Partial regularity of heat flow of fractional harmonic maps to spheres
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the notation of stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps from $\R^m$ into the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{\ell-1}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{R}^\ell$, for $0<s<1$, framed through the parabolic version of Caffarelli-Silvestre's extension. We prove that any stationary heat flow of $s$-harmonic maps is smooth away from a closed set of vanishing $(m+2-2s)$-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure. This extends to the fractional settings the partial regularity theorem on the heat flow of harmonic maps into spheres by Chen-Li-Lin and Feldman.

title: A Shadow Sequence Technique for Last-Iterate Convergence Analysis of the Random Reshuffling Method: Relaxed Stepsize Conditions and Beyond
abstract: We prove two last-iterate convergence bounds of the random reshuffling (RR) method in the smooth general convex finite-sum optimization. In the proved results, the stepsize sequence $\{η_{k}\}_{k}$ of RR is an arbitrary positive non-increasing sequence with $η_{1}\lesssim 1/(\operatorname{polylog}(n)L)$, where $n$ is the number of components of the finite-sum objective and $L$ is the smoothness parameter. Specifically, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}η_{k}}+σ_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{η_{k}^{2}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}η_{l}}\right)$ of RR is proved, where $x_{*}$ is a solution of the optimization problem and $σ_{*}^{2}$ is the variance at the solution $x_{*}$. This rate is novel to the last-iterate of RR. Also, a last-iterate convergence rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\frac{\Vert x_{1}^{1}-x_{*}\Vert^2}{n\sum_{k=1}^{K}η_{k}}+nσ_{*}^{2}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\frac{η_{k}^{3}}{\sum_{l=k}^{K}η_{l}} \right)$ of RR is proved. A similar rate exists in the literature, but only under a restrictive stepsize condition $η\lesssim 1/(n L)$ and does not allow varying stepsizes. At the heart of our proof for the latter rate is an auxiliary sequence named the shadow sequence, which has the same epoch endpoints with the iterate sequence generated by RR. The shadow sequence can be regarded as an iterate sequence generated by performing an inexact RR on an auxiliary interpolated problem or performing a novel variant of random reshuffled SVRG on the original problem. The shadow sequence technique sheds light on deeper understanding of RR and may be useful in the analysis of other shuffling methods.

title: Normal approximation and self-normalized moderate deviations for the minimal random walk with random step sizes
abstract: We study the minimal random walk with independent positive random step sizes. By separating the movement count from the centered step-size noise, we obtain normal approximations and self-normalized Cramér-type moderate deviations under finite-moment assumptions. For the noise, conditioning on the movement count yields Kolmogorov, Wasserstein and Zolotarev bounds. A polynomial moderate-deviation range holds when a recalled stop can lead to movement. At the boundary where this probability is zero, we obtain a logarithmic range and construct a bounded nonsymmetric example excluding a general polynomial range. For the full position, a weighted martingale representation gives limit laws in the different regimes, nonuniform normal approximations and moment-distance bounds without logarithmic losses. Variance concentration also yields self-normalized moderate deviations in the diffusive and critical regimes.

title: A Link-Based Algorithm for Stochastic User Equilibrium with Bounded Choice and Local Detour Threshold
abstract: This study develops a novel solution method for stochastic user equilibrium (SUE) under the bounded choice model with local detour threshold (BCM-LDT SUE; Rasmussen et al., 2024), which restricts the choice set in line with observed route choice behavior. The model assigns zero probability to paths whose total cost exceeds a bound or whose local detour exceeds a threshold; thus, the path choice set varies with link costs. The proposed algorithm updates link flows while implicitly enumerating the path choice set via a depth-first search (DFS) pruned with the BCM-LDT bounds. This distinguishes it from the original algorithm, which updates path flows, and enables quasi-Newton-type acceleration. Since paths are never stored, the method can handle choice sets totaling on the order of $10^7$ paths. On a personal computer, it reached equilibrium in a few to about fifteen minutes, not only for the Anaheim network under the original settings but also for larger networks such as Winnipeg and Barcelona.
comment: 16 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Code available at https://github.com/nagae/BCMLDT

title: ORSMT: Unleashing the Potential of Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Semantic Verification and Repair in LLM-Based Optimization
abstract: Large language models increasingly automate optimization modeling from natural language problems, producing written mathematics, solver code and a returned report. Verifying one optimization problem across these artifacts requires semantic comparison: unequal models can attain the same objective, equivalent models can use different auxiliary variables, and mutually consistent artifacts can omit the same source requirement. ORSMT provides a typed semantic interface and exact SMT relation queries. It aligns observable decisions, projects auxiliary variables, proves or refutes feasible region and objective relations, localizes refutations to implicated rows or domains and links source texts when available. It then reconstructs one artifact from another, and each adopted candidate passes the required relation checks. Across 3,034 problems and six generator sizes, ORSMT improves the model-code match rate in all 72 benchmark and generator combinations before selection. Protected selection raises the aggregate rate from 43.2% to 88.2% and the share that are both correct and matched from 25.2% to 40.2%. On the 1,905 refuted outputs, certified voting under the shared fallback makes 50.9% of outputs correct and matched, compared with 44.8% for ReLoop and 49.4% for Opt-Verifier. A separate one-round source revision followed by exact reconstruction restores a model-code match for 84.4% of the refuted pairs.

title: Partially Observed McKean--Vlasov Control with Vanishing Observation Intensities
abstract: We study partially observed McKean--Vlasov jump-diffusions with controlled counting intensities that may vanish and depend on the unconditional physical state distribution. A deterministic upper bound on the likelihood supports one-sided state--likelihood variations, a smooth-test-function expansion of the physical state marginal, and a necessary maximum principle without inverse intensity or likelihood terms. We also establish a one-sided total-variation derivative of the physical probability on the fixed noise space, including a nonnegative singular component on baseline-null histories.
