Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge11$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

title: Sharp quantitative stability of the Hong--Krahn--Szegő inequality
abstract: We establish sharp quantitative stability estimates for the Hong--Krahn--Szegő inequality for arbitrary open sets of positive finite measure in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. In dimensions $d\ge3$, the optimal stability exponent is $(d+2)/2$, while in dimension two the sharp stability modulus is $t^2/\log(e/t)$. These results improve the quantitative stability estimate of Brasco and Pratelli~\cite[Theorem 3.5]{BP} and resolve Open Problem 7.56 of Brasco and De Philippis~\cite[Open Problem 7.56]{BDP}.

title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.

title: Measures of maximal entropy for meromorphic maps on compact Kähler manifolds
abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact Kähler manifold. Assume that $f$ has a strictly dominant intermediate dynamical degree $λ$ and that the number of isolated $n$-periodic points, counted with multiplicity, is at most $λ^n+o(λ^n)$. Then $f$ admits at most one adapted invariant probability measure of entropy $\logλ$. If such a measure exists, its natural extension is Bernoulli, and the isolated periodic points equidistribute towards it when counted with or without multiplicity. We apply this criterion to several classes of maps in complex dynamics, resolving longstanding open problems.

title: Low-Dimensional Reduction of Mean-Field Coupled Dynamical Systems with Units Described by Two Real Variables: Classification and Applications
abstract: Low-dimensional reduction is crucial for understanding network systems with many units. In a recent advance, Martens and Dharmavaram developed a theory of exact low-dimensional reduction for a general class of mean-field coupled dynamical systems characterized by a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure. In this paper, we classify mean-field coupled dynamical systems with a mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, where each unit is described by two real variables. Our classification is based on González-López, Kamran, and Olver's local classification of Lie systems on the plane near generic points and yields 28 types of mean-field coupled dynamical systems. For mean-field coupled systems with units described by two real variables, we first present a general theory on classification and low-dimensional reduction based on the mean-field Lie-Scheffers structure, and then discuss applications to populations of coupled oscillators. We show that low-dimensional reduction is possible for a broad class of populations of limit-cycle oscillators, extending the previously reported reducible class of populations of Stuart-Landau oscillators to include many new models.

title: Singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation II
abstract: Continuing our work in [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 1503-1518], we construct new singular solutions to the complex Monge-Ampère equation with constant right-hand side in the Bedford-Taylor sense. Let $\mathbb D$ denote the open unit disk in $\mathbb C$. For $n\geq 2$, these solutions include: (i) a bounded solution on $\mathbb D^n$ that is discontinuous almost everywhere and nowhere classically differentiable; (ii) a continuous exhaustion of $\mathbb C^n$ that does not belong to $W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb C^n)$; (iii) a continuous solution on $\overline{\mathbb D^n}$ whose Laplacian has a singular part. We construct these solutions from singular harmonic functions using partial Legendre transforms and holomorphic pullbacks.

title: Generic finiteness of solutions to parametrized systems of generalized polynomial inequalities
abstract: We study parametrized systems of $\mathit{generalized}$ polynomial inequalities, $(c \circ x^B) \in C$, for a positive variable vector $x \in \mathbb{R}^n_>$, a $\mathit{real}$ exponent matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$, a positive parameter vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^m_>$, and a positive, blunt coefficient cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^m_>$. This setting includes (i) generalized polynomial equations, $A \, (c \circ x^B) = 0$, arising e.g. from power-law dynamical systems with real exponents (and involving a real coefficient matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n' \times m}$), and (ii) generalized semi-algebraic sets. Our main result guarantees the generic finiteness of solutions modulo unavoidable exponential fibers. Building on a framework for parametrized $\mathit{polynomial}$ systems developed by Müller and Regensburger, we reformulate the problem as a system of $\mathit{binomial}$ equations on the coefficient set $P = C \cap Δ\subseteq \mathbb{R}^m_>$, where $Δ$ is a product of (standard) simplices. Solvability is governed by the monomial-dependency subspace $D$. Using elementary arguments from analysis and topology, including a logarithmic boundary analysis and Sard's theorem, we control the accumulation of solutions on the boundary and in the interior of $P$. We show that, if $\dim P \le \dim D$, then generically in both the measure-theoretic and topological sense, there are finitely many solutions on $P$ (and hence finitely many exponential fibers of solutions in $\mathbb{R}^n_>$). As an application, we prove generic finiteness of steady states (within forward-invariant sets) for parametrized power-law dynamical systems with real exponents.

title: Birthday Estimators Are Uniformly Optimal for Renyi Entropy
abstract: Collisions are a basic probe of unknown distributions, used for testing and for counting substructures in graphs, and they underlie Rényi entropy, a fundamental measure of uncertainty with applications in cryptography, machine learning, physics, and biology. Motivated by this, we study the natural birthday estimator. We prove Bernstein-type concentration for it and show that it is minimax optimal, uniformly and jointly in alphabet size, order, accuracy, and confidence, with no sample splitting, clipping, or median aggregation. This, in particular, settles the sample complexity of integer-order Rényi entropy estimation up to absolute constants in all regimes, closing the gap between the best known upper and lower bounds. Our concentration bound rests on a sensitivity analysis of collision count, and the matching lower bound on a sharp analysis of detecting a hidden spike in a plateau distribution.

title: Continuous-Time Policy Gradient from Discrete Data: Convergence Analysis and Model-Free Algorithms
abstract: Continuous-time reinforcement learning seeks an optimal policy under unknown dynamics driven by stochastic differential equations using observations collected at discrete times. We develop a policy gradient framework that combines rigorous convergence analysis with learning from discrete data. We first establish a performance difference lemma and derive policy gradient formulas for randomized and parametrized policies. We then prove exponential convergence of an entropy-regularized policy flow to the regularized optimum. For discrete parametrized updates, we derive a convergence bound that explicitly separates the contributions of critic error, policy-regression error, and the learning step size. To enable learning under unknown dynamics, we integrate this framework with PhiBE, which constructs a continuous-time surrogate generator from discrete transition data. The resulting on-policy and off-policy model-free actor-critic algorithms preserve the continuous-time structure of the control problem. Numerical experiments on an entropy-regularized linear-quadratic regulator and a nonlinear wheeled robot demonstrate the performance and stability of the proposed methods with both known and data-driven dynamics.

title: Vanishing Uniform Turán Densities: Characterization and Jumps
abstract: Uniform Turán density problems ask for the minimum density threshold that guarantees a copy of a fixed 3-uniform hypergraph $F$ in every sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraph whose edges are uniformly distributed. This line of research was initiated by Erdős and Sós in the 1980s, who introduced the notion of \emph{vertex-set Turán density} $π_{vvv}(F)$. Reiher, Rödl and Schacht later defined two related concepts, namely, the \emph{vertex-pair Turán density} $π_{ve}(F)$ and the \emph{cherry Turán density} $π_{ee}(F)$, which satisfy the chain of inequalities $π_{vvv}(F)\geπ_{ve}(F)\geπ_{ee}(F)$. In this paper, we investigate the problem for their vanishing densities. First, we characterize the 3-uniform hypergraphs $F$ for which $π_{ee}(F)=0$, thereby answering a question posed by Schacht. We show that these are precisely the so-called \emph{max-layered} 3-uniform hypergraphs recently introduced by Lamaison. Furthermore, we answer an analogous question of Lamaison for the \emph{minimum-codegree palette density} $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}$. Together, these results imply that the following are equivalent: $π_{ee}(F)=0$, $π_{ee}^{\rm pal}(F)=0$, and $F$ is a max-layered 3-uniform hypergraph. Let $\star \in \{vvv, ve, ee \}$. We say that zero is a \emph{jump} for $π_{\star}$ if there exists $c>0$ such that no $3$-uniform hypergraph $F$ satisfies $π_{\star}(F)\in(0,c)$. A famous result of Reiher, Rödl and Schacht asserts that zero is a jump for $π_{vvv}$. In contrast, we prove that zero is not a jump for either $π_{ve}$ or $π_{ee}$. This also yields a negative answer to Schacht's well-ordering question for $π_{ve}$. Together with existing results, these findings complete the picture for all three notions of uniform Turán density at zero.

title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(Δ_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.

title: The Dynamics of Collapse and Recovery in Clustered Federated Learning
abstract: Clustered federated learning (CFL) can suffer from cluster collapse. In particular, under unfavorable initialization, early client assignments concentrate heterogeneous groups on one cluster model, which is then trained toward a pooled compromise, while another model receives no updates. Since the current models determine client routing and routing determines subsequent model updates, we formulate clustered federated learning as control of an unknown dynamical system, with cluster models as the evolving state, client routing patterns as the control input, and routing interventions as state dependent controllers. In a two group linear model, we identify an initialization region in which greedy routing makes collapse self reinforcing. We then derive finite horizon error dynamics showing how routing interventions can reverse collapse by repeatedly training the starved model, primarily with updates from its compatible group. Motivated by this condition, each client uses blocked EXP3 to choose between greedy routing and interventions that redirect updates toward unused models. Experiments show that with simpler predictors and faster specialist formation, autonomous controller selection recovers usable specialists from unfavorable starts that trap standard CFL baselines. In transformed FEMNIST, the synchronized-entry configuration with persistent commitment recovers usable specialists in settings where the autonomous controller configuration often does not. Code and scripts for reproducing the experiments and figures are available at https://github.com/prsinha1/FedRecover.

title: OptScientist: Automated Discovery of Optimization Laws
abstract: Many scientific phenomena are best understood as outcomes of underlying optimization problems, yet automated scientific discovery has largely focused on recovering equations that describe observed input-output patterns. We introduce OptScientist, a novel automated framework for discovering compact symbolic optimization laws directly from data. OptScientist comprises (i) a model that infers symbolic optimization problems by first learning to represent data as an optimization problem and then extracting its symbolic form, and (ii) an LLM agentic system embedding the model in a discovery process that integrates theoretical priors from scientific literature, discovers candidate laws, abstracts their underlying mechanisms, and suggests new data to collect. We first evaluate OptScientist on OptFeynman, a novel benchmark of 99 physics-derived optimization problems, where OptScientist recovers ground-truth laws for over 80% of the problems and remains robust to noisy contextual information, while substantially outperforming machine-learning, symbolic, and LLM-based model-discovery baselines. On human risky choice and central-bank monetary policy, OptScientist discovers compact symbolic optimization laws that achieve held-out predictive performance competitive with leading baselines, while using few parameters and substantially fewer tokens than LLM baselines. Overall, OptScientist extends automated scientific discovery to uncovering optimization laws that generate observed phenomena, enabling automated theory building across the physical, biological, behavioral, and social sciences.

title: Convergence of stochastic gradient descent for learning linear neural networks
abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is the cornerstone of modern deep learning, yet its theoretical convergence properties remain poorly understood in non-convex settings. To address this gap, we study SGD dynamics in deep linear neural networks - simplified models that retain key non-convex characteristics while remaining analytically tractable. Building on recent results for gradient descent, we extend convergence guarantees to SGD under regularized squared loss. We establish almost sure boundedness of SGD iterates. Using the framework of asymptotic pseudotrajectories from stochastic approximation theory, our analysis establishes then, for both deterministic and adaptive step-size choices, convergence of SGD to the set of critical points under mild conditions (without relying on Lipschitz properties or whitened data). To our knowledge, this is the first work providing almost sure convergence guarantees for SGD in deep linear networks, bridging the gap between theoretical optimization and practical stochastic training.

title: Higher-order tangent lines to smooth hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove that for every smooth hypersurface $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d\geq n \geq 5$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the space of pointed lines $(\ell,p)$ having intersection multiplicity at least six with $X$ at $p$ has the expected dimension $2n-7$. The proof uses deformations of ruled surfaces preserving prescribed contact with $X$. As an application, we show that a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\geq 6$ in $\mathbb{P}^5$ contains at most $225d^3-1370d^2+1800d$ planes. This bound has optimal order of growth in $d$.

title: A Statistical Imaging Framework for Inverse Obstacle Scattering and Its Resolution Analysis
abstract: We develop a general statistical framework for inverse obstacle imaging and resolution analysis from far-field second moments under random illumination. The regularized $Q$-statistic is introduced and utilized to measure the minimal statistically weighted cost of synthesizing the test far field associated with a sampling point. Its reciprocal provides an imaging indicator. Under uniform full-aperture plane-wave illumination, we relate this indicator to several classical sampling indicators and derive their statistical counterparts for general random illumination. For the resolution analysis, separating the effects of radiation and noise from the statistics of induced boundary sources, we measure a correlation-free resolution limit by the one-sided half-height width of the boundary transition. In the regime of fixed wavenumber $k$ with the noise-calibrated regularization level $ρ_τ\to 0$, we establish a sharp asymptotic law for this width for simply connected domains with analytic boundaries. The width scales as \(h_Γ(x)\log\log(1/ρ_τ)/\log(1/ρ_τ)\), with $h_Γ(x)$ a geometric prefactor along the boundary determining both the boundary image contrast and the local transition width. For general boundary-source statistics, we examine how the source mean, variance, and correlation affect imaging quality. Finally, in representative scattering configurations, we provide qualitative interpretations of some typical imaging phenomena through the statistical structure of their induced boundary sources. Numerical examples illustrate these mechanisms and indicate that practical resolution is governed jointly by source statistics, radiation, the noise level, rather than by wavelength alone.

title: Strong Convergence of Fully Discrete Tamed Euler Approximations for Time-Changed Stochastic Delay Differential Equations
abstract: We establish the strong convergence of a fully discrete equidistant tamed Euler--Maruyama (ETEM) method for time-changed stochastic delay differential equations (TCSDDEs) with state-dependent $\mathrm{d}t$ drifts. A coupled one-sided condition on the subordinator-driven drift and diffusion allows superlinear coefficients with polynomial growth in both the current and delayed states. For subordinators whose Laplace exponent satisfies $ψ(λ)\geq c_1λ^α$ for all sufficiently large $λ$, with $α\in(0,1)$, we derive strong error bounds in terms of the time step $Δ$ and the subordinator sampling step $δ$, without imposing a relationship between them. Comparing the partitions generated by the exact and approximate inverse subordinators controls the sampling error without introducing a factor proportional to the number of time steps. For coefficients Lipschitz in both time arguments and Lipschitz history, the scheme achieves a strong convergence rate of order $Δ^{α/2}(1+|\logΔ|)^{(1-α)/2}+\sqrt{δ(1+|\logδ|)}$. A terminal lower bound $c(Δ^{α/2}+δ^{1/2})$ for a multiplicative-noise equation with a stable subordinator establishes the sharpness of both polynomial exponents for this Euler scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate convergence for nonautonomous and multidimensional superlinear delay equations, as well as delay equations with low-regularity time dependence.

title: Cutoff profile for the balanced generalized Bernoulli--Laplace model
abstract: We study the balanced generalized Bernoulli--Laplace model introduced by Goenka, Hermon, and Schmid (2025) and establish a Gaussian cutoff profile under spectral conditions satisfied by all reversible chains and the cyclic shift chain. Our method adapts the approach of Olesker-Taylor and Schmid (2026) for the two-urn model, combining concentration around a deterministic trajectory before the cutoff window with an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck approximation near equilibrium. We also give an instance of this model that exhibits cutoff but has no limit profile. Further, we determine the mixing time up to an additive constant for every irreducible instance of the model, identifying a $\log \log n$ correction governed by the largest Jordan block size corresponding to the slowest decaying modes.

title: Local well-posedness of wave kinetic equations associated with water waves
abstract: We prove two conceptually different local well-posedness results for wave kinetic equations associated with water-wave systems. For pure gravity waves with 2D interfaces, we establish a classical well-posedness theory in weighted Sobolev spaces: regularity is propagated, and solutions depend continuously on the initial data in the same topology. For gravity-capillary waves with one-dimensional interfaces, the situation is fundamentally different. We prove well-posedness in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces (in the sense of existence, uniqueness, and continuity in a weaker topology), but we also show that, in general, any additional regularity of the initial data is instantly lost. Moreover, continuity in time and continuous dependence on the initial data fail in the weighted $L^\infty$ norm, even for smooth compactly supported initial data. This instability is caused by degenerate three-wave resonances, which produce singular collision rates and arbitrarily short relaxation time scales. The distinction between the two theories reflects a fundamental difference in their resonant geometry.

title: Local crystallization in three-dimensional quantization
abstract: A long-standing conjecture on the quantization problem due to Gersho, which remains open in dimensions higher than two, posits that optimal quantizers crystallize into a lattice structure; in dimension three, the natural candidate is the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, known to be optimal among other lattices. In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.

title: On Nonlocal Equations under Symmetries
abstract: In this work, we establishes results of existence and regularity for solutions to nonlocal equations of the form $f(Δ)u = U(x,u(x)) ~\text{and}~f(Δ_{g})u=U(x,u(x))$ in the Euclidean context and Riemannian context respectively. We extend the results of \cite{Gorka 6} for the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ under cylindrically symmetry and compact Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ under action of a closed Lie subgroup $G \leq \text{Isom}_{g}(M)$. Our approach combines spectral theory, complex interpolation and fixed-point methods.

title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones
abstract: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.

title: Extremal secant size distributions in projective planes
abstract: Given a point set $S$ in a projective plane of order $q$, each line $\ell$ determines a secant of size $|S\cap \ell|$. We study how concentrated this secant-size distribution can be. We develop a general framework for estimating and, in several cases, determining the extremal number. We point out how the extremal constructions vary depending on the remainder of the size of the set modulo $q$, and classify several extremal families of point sets, building from concurrent lines, Baer {subplanes} and lines in general position. On the lower bound side, we rely on stability results in the Desarguesian case and applications of the standard equalities in general. Finally, we connect the problem to a novel concept, called general position on level 2 for point and line sets, which then leads to a Sidon-type problem over finite fields called projective Sidon sets, providing an additional arithmetic model for highly concentrated secant-size distributions.

title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.

title: 2-representation theory of the Taft algebra
abstract: We study the $2$-representation theory of the Taft category, the tensor category of finite-dimensional modules over the Taft algebra. This category has two left cells. We first classify suitable transitive modules over its based representation ring. For the upper cell, we recall a construction by Etingof and Ostrik giving an infinite family of pairwise nonequivalent simple $2$-representations. For the bottom cell, we pass to the semisimplification of the Taft category and identify a distinguished fusion subcategory with an adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Verlinde category. Using algebra objects associated with $\mathsf{ADET}$-diagrams and categorical Clifford theory, we classify the regular exact indecomposable module categories of this semisimplification. For these regular module categories, the split Grothendieck group is a complete invariant. Finally, we identify the two cell $2$-representations of the Taft category.

title: Towards differential expansion for generic representations
abstract: We report the first results of phenomenological analysis, based on extended set of explicitly calculated colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials in \cite{knotebook}. They concern differential expansion (DE), which separates the dependencies on the knot ${\cal K}$ and the representation $R$. %of colored HOMFLY-PT polynomials. DE is well understood for symmetric and rectangular representations, while for non-rectangular $R$ even the knot-independent basis $Z_R^X$ of DE is not known. We concentrate on two issues: the possible derivation of DE and on improved characteristic of its defect. We discuss how evolution families -- twist knots, double braids and 3-pretzels -- can be used to find DE by a peculiar triangular transformation of evolution coefficients. Once $Z^R_X$ are found for particular family, they are expected to stay basically the same for arbitrary knots -- modulo controllable reductions, characterized by the defect of DE, which puts knots into different universality classes. Contrary to original expectation, these classes appear labeled not by a single number $δ^{\cal K}$, but by a whole non-decreasing sequence $\{k_j\}$, which is squeezed between two staircases, ${ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{δ+1}\right)\leq k_j\leq{ entier}\!\left(\frac{j-1}{{\rm deg}\,Δ}\right)$, where the upper bound involves Alexander polynomial $Δ(q^2)$ and follows from the continuation of the Melvin--Morton--Rozansky-Kashaev limit to $A=q^{-m}$ with $m>0$, when the limit gives a {\it positive} power of Alexander. The old assumption $δ+1={\rm deg}\,Δ$ is oversimplified and fails for 19 non-alternating knots with 11 and 12 crossings. Last, we list the differences of non-rectangularly colored HOMFLY for various mutant pairs to demonstrate their universality (knot-independence) and nice consistency with the spirit of DE.

title: Efficient Ground-State Manifold Amplification for Rydberg Atom Arrays via Houdayer Cluster Updates
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring ground-state manifolds of maximum independent set problems, in which quantum hardware supplies the initial solutions and an entirely classical post-processing algorithm expands them, increasing the solution diversity of quantum hardware measurements by up to several orders of magnitude. Quantum optimization devices, while capable of generating high-quality solutions, can suffer from fundamental sampling limitations. This is particularly problematic for applications that strongly depend on a large variety of uncorrelated optimal solutions. We apply the Houdayer cluster update algorithm to systematically expand quantum-generated solution sets through classical post-processing. We validate our approach on a test bed of 43 problem instances from QuEra's Aquila analog annealing device, achieving diversity amplification factors, defined as the increase in the number of distinct solutions at a given set size, of up to 11923x with a median of 24.3x across different problem scales and hardness parameters. Because exact ground-state degeneracies are known for these instances, the recovered fraction of the manifold can be measured rather than bounded: post-processing recovers a median of 21% of the ground-state manifold, and provably all of it for six instances. We also demonstrate that, in some cases, the classical post-processing can discover independent sets larger than those found by the quantum hardware, thus improving on solution quality and not just diversity. While the method is non-ergodic and cannot guarantee complete manifold coverage, it consistently discovers a larger number of high-quality, and in some cases strictly better, configurations than quantum sampling alone. This work demonstrates how simple classical post-processing can enhance the utility of quantum optimization results.

title: Small and large gaps between zeros of Dirichlet $L$-functions
abstract: For every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove unconditionally that infinitely many consecutive zeros have spacing less than $1/2+\varepsilon$ times the mean. Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we also prove a positive proportion of such spacings for the Riemann zeta-function, and infinitely many spacings greater than $3.63$ times the mean for every fixed primitive Dirichlet $L$-function.

title: The $λ>0$ case for $Δu=λ-c e^u$ type equation on high dimensional spheres
abstract: Motivated by prescribed Chern scalar curvature problems in complex geometry, we study the equation $Δ_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}V+λ(e^V-1)=0$ with $λ>0$ on spheres. For $N\ge4$ and $λ>2(N-2)$ with $λ\ne2N$, we prove the existence of a nonconstant smooth solution that is axially symmetric and symmetric about the equator.

title: Variance Reduction with Delayed Feedback for Non-Convex Optimization
abstract: We study variance reduction for non-convex optimization when gradient evaluations return with a delay. The server can update the parameter while earlier evaluations remain unfinished. We first analyze an ordered recursive momentum estimator for stochastic optimization. Under average smoothness and bounded variance, its oracle complexity is $O(1+σ^2ε^{-2}+LΔ_f(1+σ/ε+τ)ε^{-2})$, where the target is an expected squared gradient norm of at most $ε^2$ and $τ$ bounds the feedback delay. We next study finite sums with $n$ components and obtain $O(n+LΔ_f(\sqrt n+\min\{τ,n-1\})ε^{-2})$ evaluations. An asynchronous snapshot variant continues updating during full-gradient computations under an explicit bound on their completion time. For the stochastic method, we further replace a maximum-delay bound by a bound on the weighted amount of missing feedback.

title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Verification code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23504589

title: Extremals for Sharp Trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev Inequalities on Convex Cones
abstract: Zugmeyer~\cite{Zug} established sharp trace Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequalities on convex cones for $a\geq n>p>1$. We classify all nonzero real-valued extremals of these inequalities. Let the cone be the epigraph of a finite convex function that is positively homogeneous of degree one, and let $H$ be any norm. We prove that equality holds precisely for functions of the form $A H(x+te+\ell)^{-(a-p)/(p-1)}$, where $A\in\mathbb{R}\backslash\{0\}$, $t>0$, $e=(0,\ldots,0,1)$, and $\ell$ belongs to the largest vector subspace contained in the cone. The result includes the critical Sobolev trace inequality at $a=n$, as well as nonsmooth norms and cones, half-spaces, and cones containing lines.

title: Quadratic hulls of osculating varieties of rational normal curves
abstract: Let $T^p c_r$ be the $p$-osculating variety of the rational normal curve $c_r\subset\mathbb{P}S^r(\mathbb{C}^2)$. We study its quadratic hull, the scheme defined by the quadratic equations vanishing on $T^p c_r$. For $r\ge2p+3$, we prove that this scheme is a complete intersection of $\binom{r-2p}{2}$ quadrics whenever \[ p\ge\binom{r-2p-1}{2}. \] When the inequality is strict, the hull is integral and strictly contains $T^p c_r$. On the boundary its support is reducible, except for $(p,r)=(1,5)$, where the hull equals the osculating variety. The proof is local at the highest weight point. Koornwinder's relation between Clebsch--Gordan coefficients and Hahn polynomials leads to a description of the tangent-cone equations in which each antidiagonal becomes an ordinary polynomial space of bounded degree. An incidence estimate then gives a normal integral tangent cone in the strict range, and the $SL_2$-action turns this local statement into global integrality.

title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.

title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations
abstract: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.

title: Discrete Exterior Calculus-based Whittle-Matérn Fields on Meshes
abstract: This work presents a sparse precision formulation for Whittle-Matérn fields based on Discrete Exterior Calculus. By treating the $k$-cochain as the latent object to be modeled, we show that a single formulation can produce Whittle-Matérn fields for all $k$ and integer $α$ values. By utilising Whitney maps we can enable a push-forward of the prior on 1-cochains, enabling inference for discrete vector fields. We demonstrate this model on interpolation of vector fields on a sphere.

title: Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term
abstract: In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.

title: A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison
abstract: In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.

title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications
abstract: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.

title: On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
abstract: Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.

title: C*-selflessness and $\mathcal{Z}$-stability for Thompson's group $F$
abstract: We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.

title: On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds
abstract: We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.

title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
abstract: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.

title: ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.

title: Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $Ψ$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
abstract: In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $μ\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $Ψ$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $Ψ$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.

title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations
abstract: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.

title: Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic
abstract: In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.
comment: Added an existence theorem for almost Ulrich bundles on threefolds

title: Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius
abstract: We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.

title: Real-analytic standard families and rotational invariant curves
abstract: In this paper we study one-parameter families of exact standard maps of the form $$\widehat{f}_{k,g}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}) =\bigl(\widehat{x}+\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x}) \bmod 1,\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x})\bigr),$$ where $k$ is a real parameter and $g:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic, 1-periodic and has zero mean. The most famous example is when $g(\widehat{x})=\frac{\sin(2π\widehat{x})}{2π}$. In this case, the closed subset $A_{\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}\subset \mathbb{R}$ of values of $k$ for which $\widehat{f}_{k,\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}$ has rotational invariant curves is conjectured to be a closed interval. Much has been done towards this conjecture, both numerically and analytically. But a complete proof has not yet been achieved. Our approach here goes in the opposite direction: we construct a function $θ:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above conditions, such that $A_θ$ is not an interval: It contains at least 2 different connected components, which are non-degenerate closed intervals.

title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management
abstract: Large retail chains must tailor assortment and pricing decisions to local customer preferences, yet even retailers with extensive sales records often have limited data for estimating demand at the store or local market level, particularly in product categories with short selling windows. Local estimation (fitting a demand model for each store on its own) can therefore be unreliable, while pooling data across stores improves estimation precision at the cost of ignoring local demand heterogeneity. We study how retailers can balance these competing effects through transfer learning under a multinomial logit (MNL) demand model. We propose a shrinkage estimator that combines store-specific demand estimates with information pooled from other stores. Unlike the linear or quadratic settings underlying much of the existing theoretical literature on information transfer in operations, the nonlinear MNL likelihood does not admit a straightforward bias-variance decomposition. By exploiting its self-concordant-like properties, we establish finite-sample performance guarantees that characterize when information transfer improves demand estimation and how the appropriate degree of shrinkage depends on local sample size, feature dimensionality, and cross-store heterogeneity. We further derive regret bounds for downstream assortment and pricing decisions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the operational benefits of shrinkage across different data environments. An empirical study using data from several hundred stores of a European apparel retailer shows that shrinkage improves out-of-sample product prioritization and revenue capture relative to both local estimation and full pooling. Our findings demonstrate how retailers can leverage information across their store networks to improve revenue management decisions while preserving local demand differences.

title: The Art of Toda Brackets-A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
abstract: This book has several fundamental aims, one of which is to serve as a reference book for computing unstable homotopy groups using methods of the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. It plays a fundamental role in dealing with composition relations of homotopy classes. This book brings together in Appendix A.3 all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained using the art of Toda brackets as the principal tool, with explicit generators. It also explains in Appendix A.2 the conventions used to name the generators. The book mainly presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n,$ as well as some $π_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n)),$ with explicit generators, while retaining two possible group structures for $π_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11)).$ In degree $29,$ the cases $7\leq n\leq14$ remain under investigation. The odd-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ in the above range can be computed with little effort; these computations essentially amount to looking up the relevant entries in existing tables.

title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.

title: Scaling limits for peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane
abstract: We construct and study peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane by successively revealing hulls of fixed radius. We prove that for any peeling process, as the radius of the hulls tends to zero, the sequence of discovered hulls converges to an explicit family of Brownian disks. We also consider the particular case of what we call nearest-neighbour peeling explorations, where the center of each new hull is chosen on the outer boundary of the previously discovered hull, naturally giving rise to an exploration curve. We provide scaling limits results for these curves, jointly with the convergence of the associated boundary-length and volume processes.
comment: This is the first part of our work, the second part will be added in a forthcoming update. Comments are welcome!

title: Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
abstract: A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.

title: Transversality at Virtual Centers
abstract: We consider the family of transcendental meromorphic functions with finitely many singular values, none of whose asymptotic values is infinity. We prove that transversality holds at any boundary point of a shell component in a dynamically natural slice of the parameter space at which an asymptotic value is a prepole.

title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for p-capacity of compact sets
abstract: We prove the capacitary Brunn-Minkowski inequality for arbitrary nonempty compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, and every $1<p<\infty$, with no assumption of convexity, connectedness, interior, or boundary regularity. For $1<p<n$ the inequality is for the variational $p$-capacity. For $p>n$ it is for the capacity determined by the constant term at infinity of the normalized $p$-harmonic Green's function with pole at infinity, and for $p=n$ for an outer regularization of this quantity, which agrees with it for $n$-regular sets and in the plane is a constant multiple of logarithmic capacity. In particular, it holds for Newtonian capacity of all compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$, and for logarithmic capacity of all planar compact sets. Previously these inequalities were known for convex sets and, for logarithmic capacity, for planar continua. When both capacities are positive, equality holds for $0<λ<1$ if and only if the filled sets, obtained by adjoining the bounded components of the complement, are convex and equal up to translation and dilation. This characterization is new for nonconvex sets, even for Newtonian and logarithmic capacity.

title: Determinant characters and multiplicative solubility of finite skew braces
abstract: Let $B$ be a finite skew brace. We prove that if the additive derived subgroup $(B,+)'$ is nilpotent, then the multiplicative group $(B,\cdot)$ is soluble. In particular, this holds for finite skew braces with supersoluble or metabelian additive group.

title: Convergence and semisimplicity of big quantum cohomology of flag varieties
abstract: We prove the folklore conjecture that the big quantum cohomology of a flag variety $G/P$ of general Lie type is convergent near the large-radius limit and is generically semisimple. The convergence relies on a slightly modified version of Iritani's reconstruction theorem, together with Cauchy's formula that avoids directly taking the non-equivariant limit at the origin. Generic semisimplicity follows from a surprising application of the big quantum $D$-module mirror symmetry for $G/P$ established by the first, third and fourth authors jointly with Hinault and Zhang. Moreover, we prove the regularity conjecture on the big quantum cohomology of $G/P$ formulated by Perrin and Smirnov, which implies generic semisimplicity.

title: Bounded Symbols and One-Component Inner Functions
abstract: Let $θ$ be a nonconstant inner function, we prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_θ=H^2\ominusθH^2$ admits a bounded symbol if and only if $θ$ is one-component, that is, if $\{z\in\mathbb D:|θ(z)|<r\}$ is nonempty and connected for some $r\in(0,1)$. This establishes the previously open necessary direction and resolves a conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi, and Timotin. For every non-one-component inner function, we construct a sequence of norm-one rank-one truncated Toeplitz operators whose infimal $L^\infty$-norms over all representing symbols tend to infinity. The quantitative lower bound is obtained by forming two inner divisors from angularly separated parts of the zero set and singular measure. The argument applies without restrictions on the Blaschke or singular parts of $θ$. The order of this lower bound is sharp, already for a family of degree-two Blaschke products. A continuation argument for local inverse branches produces the required sequence of points. Consequently, every non-one-component model space supports a trace-class truncated Toeplitz operator without a bounded symbol. Combined with known equivalences, the characterization also yields geometric criteria for weak factorization and for continuous-symbol representations of compact truncated Hankel operators.

title: A Convex Feasibility Problem for Which Douglas-Rachford Converges Only Weakly
abstract: We provide two closed, convex sets with nonempty intersection and an initial point for which the Douglas-Rachford algorithm converges weakly but not strongly. This resolves an open question as noted earlier by Aragón Artacho, Borwein and Tam (2014, Remark 2.2). Our construction is a simple lift of a recent construction by Bauschke and Tung concerning firmly nonexpansive operators.

title: Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
abstract: Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(π(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $π(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(π(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(π(P)+ε)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(π(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $π_d=π(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)λ_d\leπ_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $λ_d$ is the vertex Turán density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-π_d=\exp(-Θ(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\leπ_2\le2.15121$.

title: Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
abstract: The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. Building on \cite{Collot2023}, which constructed 2D horizontally odd solutions where the on-axis derivative $\partial_X u(t,0,Z)$ blows up at rate $(T-t)^{-1}$ with boundary concentration scale $|\ln (T-t)|^{-1}$, this paper characterizes this blow-up as forming between hyperbolic stagnation points. We derive precise asymptotic expansions for on-axis derivatives beyond leading order, identifying a horizontal concentration scale of $(T-t)^{3/2}$ characteristic of generic Burgers' singularities. Furthermore, we justify the 2D solution's expansion near the symmetry axis by proving $(T-t)^{3/2}$ is a universal lower bound on the radius of analyticity.

title: Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture
abstract: We show that the uniform random $d$-regular graph model on $n$ vertices is, in total variation distance, asymptotically close to the union of $d$ uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, provided that $n$ is even and $ω(1) = d \leq n^{1/10}$. This confirms a conjecture by Hollom, Lichev, Mond, Portier, and Wang for this range of parameters. This result has a couple of interesting consequences. First, this shows that random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exhibit sprinkling properties for some range of parameters, thereby confirming a conjecture by Isaev, McKay, Southwell and Zhukovskii in that range. Second, we give a short alternative proof of the upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture in the sparse regime.

title: On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices
abstract: A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of Östergård--Paavola and Ó Catháin--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.

title: Budgeted Admission from Timestamped Capacity Records in Shared Clusters
abstract: A cluster admission gate can receive a capacity record that no longer matches current schedulability. We study one exogenous binary schedulability unit under a bound on the joint probability of admission and unavailability. For a symmetric Markov state, we derive the stationary admission frontier for a fixed observation delay and apply finite likelihood allocation to a delay-tagged delivered record. A one-sided exact binomial endpoint calibrates each fitted policy, and exact enumeration confirms the per-policy confidence target in every tested parameter cell. A separate deterministic guard charges every unresolved admission against the realized allowance and bounds unavailable-state admissions at every prefix under truthful outcome feedback. An executable admission procedure composes the allocation and guard. The controlled system binds source sampling, NATS delivery, randomized admission, Kubernetes objects, and API-derived outcomes in one append-only record. Independent audit finds no missing event, identity mismatch, or state mismatch in the completed functional block. A separate CPU request-accounting check preserves Job and Pod identity across an unschedulable-to-complete transition.

title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.

title: A note on the cube inequality
abstract: In this note, we adapt ideas from No. 336 of OpenAI's October 6, 2026 mathematics release to prove the weighted cube inequality in all dimensions.

title: Szarek and Ball made simple
abstract: We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.

title: Near Optimal Finite Model POMDP Approximation of Controlled Diffusion with Partial Information
abstract: We study continuous-time stochastic control problems under partial information. Our main contributions are the following: (i) We show near optimality, under finite horizon as well as discounted infinite horizon cost criteria, of piece-wise constant control policies obtained via solutions to discrete-time partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) approximations, constructed via Euler-Maruyama approximations of both state and observation processes; (ii) we obtain several regularity properties of such POMDP approximate models; and (iii) using these regularity properties, we arrive at near optimal finite model approximations. (iv) These culminate into our main result which is that an optimal solution for the approximate finite POMDP model is near optimal for the original diffusion with partial information.

title: Avoiding abelian squares with three colours in the continuous setting
abstract: An $n$-colouring of the real line is a Lebesgue measurable function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to A$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ colours. An abelian square for $f$ is a finite interval $U\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ where every colour shows up in the left and in the right half of $U$ with exactly the same Lebesgue measure. It is known that every $2$-colouring contains an abelian square. On the other hand, Alon, Grytczuk, Laso{ń}, and Michałek (2009) proved that there exist $4$-colourings that avoid abelian squares, while the question for $3$-colourings remained open. We construct a $3$-colouring that avoids abelian squares, disproving a conjecture of Laso{ń} (2015). However, in contrast to the case of 4-colourings, the set of 3-colourings that avoid abelian squares is meagre. We show this using an argument based on the KKM lemma.

title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge--Ampère Equation
abstract: We establish an interior $C^2$ estimate for locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solutions of the complex Monge--Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$ under weak quadratic growth bounds on sufficiently large balls, where $f$ is positive and Dini-continuous. We assume a distributional lower bound for the Laplacian of $f^{1/n}$. The main ingredient is a pseudo-$C^2$ estimate using the Green-function averaging error, valid also when $f$ is nonnegative. As an application, we prove that every entire Bedford-Taylor solution of $\det(u_{i\bar j})=1$ with weak quadratic growth is a real quadratic polynomial, resolving a conjecture of Gábor Székelyhidi.

title: Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems
abstract: Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.

title: Thin-Layer Dichotomy in Three-Phase Mullins-Sekerka Flow: Gap Dynamics and Composite Interfaces
abstract: We study the thin-layer limit of the Mullins-Sekerka flow in concentric circular geometries at fixed wave number $k$, contrasting a two-phase annulus with a genuine three-phase layer. A dichotomy emerges: for $k\ge2$ the rates blow up like the inverse thickness when the same phase lies on both sides of the layer, whereas between two different phases the matrix governing the linearized Fourier mode extends analytically to zero thickness. Both cases share the singular Dirichlet-to-Neumann factor of the thin annulus and differ only in whether the Gibbs-Thomson law forces an order-one potential difference across it. In the three-phase case the pure thickness-modulation rate stays below the logarithmic growth rate of the mean thickness, for every $k\ge1$ and all positive tensions, and, after projection onto the mean displacement and the outer interface, the collapsed pair moves as one interface carrying the sum of the two tensions. All statements concern the instantaneous fixed-mode linearization. The singularity is a property of the phase coupling, not of the thin geometry.

title: A General Construction of Strict Models in HoTT
abstract: Homotopy type theory (HoTT) provides a natural setting for studying the metatheory of type theory, as it comes with additional extensionality principles compared to ordinary Martin-Löf type theory. In particular, it is especially suitable for developing semantics of type theory, where one distinguishes two kinds of models: strict models, which give us sound interpretations, and pseudomodels. Pseudomodels are useful as they occur prevalently and can be turned into strict models by constructions called strictifications. However, the commonly used strictifications do not translate well to HoTT, as they require assumptions that are generally not satisfied by concrete examples of models. We show how to carry out the universe model construction, due to Voevodsky, in HoTT. Under this construction, every pseudomodel together with a universe type closed under enough type formers gives rise to a strict model. We also show how to interpret type formers in the resulting model assuming that the universe is closed under them. Finally, we demonstrate that this construction generalises existing instances of strict set models in the literature, and we apply it to more examples, yielding presheaf models and assembly models of type theory in HoTT. Our results are formalised in Rocq using the UniMath library.

title: Confessions of a Masked MDP
abstract: In reinforcement learning, one presumes the action set to be known ahead of time, and, thus, one must know if any state-action pairs are not permissible ahead of computations. In some applications, determining this action mask is the main computational bottleneck. Isolating this problem to highlight its core properties, we study how to combine the search for an optimal policy with the learning of the mask itself, under a linear MDP model in which each attempted action reveals the exact value of a linear score determining its validity. In this framework, we first construct an algorithm based on deterministic optimistic optimization and show that it is minimax optimal, which we show is also computationally efficient. However, it is sub-optimal on non-degenerate instances, as we show. We propose an alternative, which is also computationally efficient, which plans its exploration strategy. This algorithm admits a formal interpretation as an analogue of information-directed-sampling for deterministic feedback, which may be of independent interest. Finally, we study an application of this framework to transfer learning, where the invalid action set changes over time.

title: Economic resources, sporting efficiency and uncertainty: a global test on the 2026 FIFA world cup
abstract: A related paper (arXiv:2610.06967) developed a stochastic optimization framework in which football performance combines GDP/population-based potential with a latent mean-reverting efficiency process. The framework was applied to a cross-section of the 24 national teams participating in AFCON 2025. This paper applies the same methodology to the full 48-team 2026 FIFA World Cup, extending the analysis beyond Africa without modifying the underlying model. Using GDP, population, FIFA ranking data, and complete tournament outcomes, it evaluates the framework against a global sample spanning all six confederations. Two findings emerge. First, GDP and population explain only 9 percent of single-tournament performance variance, compared with 33 percent for FIFA points. This gap is consistent with the model's distinction between systematic performance and match-specific idiosyncratic shocks. Second, using the less noisy FIFA-points measure, the African pattern persists globally: Morocco, Senegal, Argentina, Croatia, Portugal, and Uruguay emerge as leading GDP-relative over-performers. Conversely, several major economies, including the United States, Germany, Japan, and South Korea, underperform their GDP-implied potential. As in the related paper, we interpret the residual as a symmetric, non-structurally identified conditional performance residual, rather than an SFA-consistent efficiency estimate. We also quantify the extent to which its cross-country variance mechanically reflects the underlying performance measure. The GDP-rank/simulated-performance-rank correlation is robust to the choice of the model's unidentified dynamic parameters across a wide grid.

title: Attracting Rotations Obstruct Almost-Global Consensus on Spheres over Strongly Connected Graphs
abstract: We study discrete-time consensus on the Euclidean unit sphere, where weighted combinations of neighboring states are normalized to unit length. For symmetric weights on connected undirected graphs and ambient dimension $d\ge3$, earlier results establish instability of non-consensus fixed points under suitable weight conditions. For directed graphs on the unit circle, earlier results show that fixed points other than consensus and antipodal configurations occur only for a measure-zero set of weights. We show that these conclusions do not extend directly to general strongly connected directed graphs in higher dimensions. First, we construct full-rank non-consensus fixed points whose tangent eigenvalues all equal one, showing that strict linear instability need not hold. In a separate construction, for every $d\ge3$, we present a sparse strongly connected graph admitting full-rank fixed points on an open set of its permitted weights. Our main result establishes robust counterexamples to almost-global consensus: attracting rotating motions exist for $d=2$ with every $n\ge3$ and for $d=3$ with every $n\ge6$. These motions are locally asymptotically stable modulo common rotations and have asymptotic phase. They persist on open sets of strictly positive weight matrices. For each such matrix, an open set of initial configurations approaches neither consensus nor any fixed configuration. Thus the absence of full-rank non-consensus fixed points does not ensure almost-global convergence to consensus.

title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits for Positive Factorial Multiples
abstract: Let $τ(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values.
