title: Stochastic differential games with random coefficients and state constraints: associated stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman-Isaacs equations with Neumann boundary conditions
abstract: We study a stochastic differential game in which the state process is governed by a reflected stochastic differential equation (RSDE) and the recursive payoff is defined by a generalized backward stochastic differential equation (GBSDE). Unlike the Markovian models in \cite{Li08sicon,Fan}, all coefficients may depend directly on $ω$, so the value functions are random fields. We show that the lower and upper value functions are viscosity solutions of stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman--Isaacs (HJBI) equations with nonlinear Neumann boundary conditions, thereby extending the framework of \cite{Qiu22AAP} to reflected state constraints. Under weak boundary regularity, we derive estimates for RSDEs and GBSDEs, prove regularity of the value functions, and establish the dynamic programming principle (DPP) as well as the existence of viscosity solutions. Finally, under additional assumptions in a one-dimensional linear setting, we prove a comparison theorem and the uniqueness of bounded $(L_y,0)$-viscosity solutions, where $L_y$ is the constant coefficient of $y$ in the running generator. To prove the comparison theorem, we homogenize the boundary condition and construct smooth adapted comparison fields by solving deterministic uniformly parabolic Neumann problems in finite dimensions.

title: Nonparametric In-Context Learning and Inference via Measure-Indexed Kernel Ridge Regression
abstract: In-Context learning enables an estimator, trained across multiple tasks, to adapt to a new unseen task solely through its in-context samples, without any parameter refitting. Despite growing interest in the statistical foundations of in-context learning, two gaps still remain. First, existing convergence results do not characterize the distributional behavior of the in-context learning estimators. Second, classical nonparametric methods are not designed to handle the measure-valued inputs that in-context learning naturally produces. We address both gaps by developing a measure-indexed reproducing kernel Hilbert space framework, in which the adaptivity of the estimator is captured through the dependence of a mean functional on the empirical measure of the context. Within this framework, we propose a measure-indexed kernel ridge regression estimator computed from multiple independent tasks and establish its minimax-optimal convergence rate. We further prove that the proposed estimator is pointwise asymptotically normal, enabling the construction of confidence intervals for the mean and prediction intervals for the response on an unseen task. Notably, the estimator achieves valid uncertainty quantification without any refitting when adapting to a new task. As a special case, our framework recovers classical distributed nonparametric regression when all tasks share the same underlying function. The proposed framework is illustrated through a latent Gaussian process example.

title: Complex Projective Spaces in Rational $SO(2)$-Equivariant Stable Homotopy Theory
abstract: We show that for almost every finite dimensional complex representation $W$ of $SO(2)$ the associated complex projective space $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$ does not have the rational stable homotopy type of a specific wedge of representation spheres constructed from a chosen filtration of $\mathbb{C}P(W)_+$. This contrasts with the case for representations of finite Abelian groups where such an equivalence does hold. In the finite group case, the splitting result provides us with a classification result for projective spaces up to rational stable equivalence. In light of the non-splitting as a particular wedge of spheres in the case of projective spaces of $SO(2)$-representations, we also prove a separate classification theorem.

title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure
abstract: Improving theorems of Bourgain and Badger--Genschaw, we prove that the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure on any domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\mathbb{R}^4$, and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq3$ is at most $3-10^{-5}$, $4-10^{-7}$, and $n-(n-1)^{-(2n+6.12\sqrt{n})}$, respectively. The previous bounds in dimensions $3$ and $4$ were $3-10^{-15}$ and $4-10^{-26}$, while Bishop conjectures that the sharp bound is $n-(n-1)^{-1}$. The main difficulty in optimizing Bourgain's method is estimating non-additive $s$-dimensional Hausdorff-type contents when $s<n$ is close to $n$. Previous arguments used net contents associated to a fixed $m$-adic lattice, with $m$ large depending on $n$. We redevelop the dimension theory using pairwise disjoint cubes in general position and obtain a new estimate showing that one thin ring without large holes surrounding a cube makes it unlikely for Brownian motion to reach the cube before exiting the domain. A key feature of the construction is that the holes are round rather than rectangular. We also propose ten challenges on the dimension of harmonic measure that may provide accessible targets en route to Bishop's conjecture.

title: A Quantitative Robin Faber-Krahn Inequality in Terms of Eigenfunction Distance
abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for the first eigenvalue of the Laplacian with positive Robin boundary conditions. For every open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ of prescribed volume, we prove that \[ λ_{1,β}(Ω)-λ_{1,β}(B) \geq c\|u_Ω-u_B\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^n)}^4, \] where $B$ is a ball achieving the Fraenkel asymmetry of $Ω$, and $u_Ω$ and $u_B$ are nonnegative, $L^2$-normalized first Robin eigenfunctions, extended by zero outside their respective domains. The constant $c>0$ depends only on the dimension, the Robin parameter, and the prescribed volume. The exponent $4$ is optimal.

title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
abstract: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $ρ(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $ρ(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Blažej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $ρ(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $Θ(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.
comment: minor corrections; author metadata corrected to match the transcript

title: Intersecting families with large covering number - On a conjecture of Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige
abstract: Stability theorems on intersecting families are often formulated via the covering number of set families. Let $M(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ with covering number $t$. It is known that for any fixed $t$ and fixed $k$ sufficiently large relative to $t$, one has $M(n,k,t)=(p_{t-1}(k)+o(1))(k)\binom{n}{k}$ as $n$ tends to infinity, where $p_{t-1}(k)$ is the maximum number of covers of size $t-1$ that a $k$-uniform intersecting family can have provided its covering number is $t-1$. Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured that $p_t(k)=k^t-\binom{t}{2}k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$ for fixed $t$ as $k$ tends to infinity and they also showed that $p_t(k)=k^t-b(t)k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$, where $b(t)$ is defined as the extremum of the following minimization problem. Suppose a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F$ of covering number $t$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal F_1,\dots,\mathcal F_t$ such that for every $i$ there exists a set $X_i$ with $X_i \subseteq F_i$ for all $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$ and the $X_i$'s are pairwise disjoint and non-empty. Then $b(t)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{i=1}^t(k-|X_i|)$ over all such families, partitions and $X_i$'s. In accordance with the conjecture on $p_t(k)$, Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured $b(t)=\binom{t}{2}$ for all $t\ge 2$ and proved $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\lfloor \frac{t-1}{2}\rfloor^{3/2}\le b(t)\le \binom{t}{2}$. In this note, we present a counterexample to the conjecture showing $b(t)\le 2\sqrt2\,t^{3/2}\sqrt{\log t}$ $+O(t^{3/2})$ and improve the lower bound to $\frac{2}{3^{3/4}}t^{3/2}-O(t)\le b(t)$. The counterexample was found by ChatGPT 6.1Sol, the lower bound proof is due to the human author.

title: Harder-Narasimhan Filtrations of Hyperquiver Representations
abstract: Hyperquiver representations are generalisations of quiver representations. They are directed hypergraphs with vector spaces assigned to vertices, and for every directed hyperedge, an assignment of a linear map from the tensor product of the source vector spaces to the tensor product of the target vector spaces. We study the moduli of hyperquiver representations, where we use affine GIT to describe the (in)stability of such objects under the action of a product of general linear groups. Our main result introduces the Harder-Narasimhan filtration of a hyperquiver representation. We also derive a formula for the weights of this unique filtration, which specialise to the Harder-Narasimhan slopes of a quiver representation.

title: Inverting Dependently Random Tournaments
abstract: Let $\text{inv}(T)$ be the inversion index of the tournament $T$. Answering a question of Behague, we show that $\text{inv}(T_1\to T_2)=\text{inv}(T_1)+\text{inv}(T_2)$ does not even hold asymptotically.

title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
abstract: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.

title: Optimal aggregation in multiclass classification
abstract: This paper studies the problem of aggregation in multiclass classification, generalizing existing results for binary classification. Given a finite dictionary of score functions F={f_1,...,f_M} and a training sample, the goal is to construct a data-driven aggregate whose risk is as close as possible to that of the best aggregate (oracle) in a prescribed subset of span(F) with respect to a given loss. In particular, we investigate model selection and convex aggregation under the 0/1 and multinomial logistic losses. For the 0/1 loss, we show that the optimal aggregation rates remarkably do not depend on the number of classes K, and the corresponding empirical risk minimization (ERM) aggregates are rate-optimal for model selection and nearly-optimal for convex aggregation (up to an additional sqrt(ln(K)) factor). The situation under the multinomial logistic loss is more subtle. Although the optimal aggregation rates remain independent of K, restricting aggregation to proper aggregates in conv(F) leads to a deterioration of the achievable rates with K in certain regimes. This reveals a fundamental limitation of proper aggregation in multiclass classification. To overcome it, we propose improper probability-mixture aggregates that average the induced class probabilities rather than the original score functions and map the result back to score-function space. These aggregates achieve optimal or nearly optimal convergence rates independent of K. Finally, we introduce a different aggregation framework in which both the aggregation class and the oracle are defined directly in probability space.

title: A mean value formula for the p-Laplacian
abstract:
In this paper we introduce an asymptotic mean value formula of the form $u(x) - \B_ε^p (u) (x) =ε^2 Δ_p u(x) + o(ε^2)$ for the $p-$Laplacian, $\plap u := 
abla \cdot  ig( |
abla u |^{p-2} 
abla u  ig)$. Here $\B_ε^p (u)$ is a nonlinear expression that involve the mean value and the surmemum/infimum of $u$ in suitable balls. This asymptotic mean value formula allows us to characterize viscosity solutions to equations with different homogeneities in different sets of variables, like $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=f(x)$ (for $x=(x',x'') \in\mathbb{R}^d$, $x'=(x_1,...,x_n)$ and $x''=(x_{n+1,...,x_d})$), and the parabolic $p$-Laplace heat equation $\partial_t u (x,t)-Δ_p u(x,t)=0$. Moreover, the resulting asymptotic mean value formulas are related to two-player zero sum games whose value functions, characterized as the unique solution to the corresponding dynamic programming principle, converge as the parameter that controls the size of the steps in the game goes to zero, to the unique viscosity solution to the corresponding boundary value problem for the operator under consideration. Finally, we also include a Holder regularity result for $\plap^{x'} u(x)+\qlap^{x''}u(x)=0$ proved using the game theoretical interpretation of the problem.

title: The ABC-equation revisited: missed (quasi) integrable cases. Part II: extensions and actions
abstract: We continue here the study of the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$ and using the results obtained in the first part construct new quasi-integrable structures and compute their actions on symmetries and cosymmetries.

title: Functions determining few direction: the final missing case
abstract: By results of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme and Szőnyi, and of Ball, if a function $f: {\mathbb F}_q\to{\mathbb F}_q$ determines fewer than $(q+3)/2$ directions, then $f-f(0)$ is linear over a subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$, except possibly when $q$ is even and $f$ determines exactly $q/2+1$ directions. We settle this case: $f-f(0)$ is then additive. Hence every small minimal blocking set of Rédei type in PG(2,$q$) is linear.

title: On the average of class numbers of indefinite binary quadratic forms
abstract: We prove that the sum of class numbers of primitive indefinite binary quadratic forms with integer coefficients over positive nonsquare discriminants less than $X$ is $O(X^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log X}/(\log X)^{3/2})$. This improves the longstanding classical upper bound $O(X^{3/2}/\log X)$ and implies the same upper bound for the corresponding sum over real quadratic fields. Our main input is a uniform upper bound for the number of small fundamental solutions to Pell's equation. In particular, we prove that, for almost all nonsquare positive integers $D$, the fundamental solution $\varepsilon_D$ of $t^2-Du^2=1$ is larger than any fixed power of $D$.

title: Uncountably many settled elements are never Frobenius elements
abstract: Boston and Jones conjectured that given a number field $K$, a quadratic polynomial $f\in K[x]$, and an element $α\in K$ such that the arboreal Galois representation $ρ_{f,α}:\text{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$ attached to the pair $(f,α)$ is well defined, any element in the image of such representation that is a Frobenius for an unramified prime of $K$ is a settled element. We exhibit an explicit uncountable subset $S\subseteq \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$, consisting of pairwise non-conjugate settled elements, such that no matter how $K,f,α$ are chosen, no element of $S$ can be a Frobenius for any ramified or unramified prime of $K$.

title: Mean-field limit and Vlasov equation for a Gaussian-thermostatted Lorentz gas
abstract: We study N particles moving in a dispersing billiard under an electric field and coupled through a Gaussian thermostat. The corresponding mean-field equation is a Vlasov-type equation with specular reflection. We reformulate the equation as a fixed point problem for the time-integrated thermostat coefficient. This yields existence of weak solutions for every absolutely continuous initial datum of finite energy and, for bounded initial densities supported on velocities that are large compared with the field, uniqueness of the weak solution; under the finite horizon assumption, the upper bound on the velocities can be replaced by an exponential tail of the initial density. In these regimes, we prove convergence of the empirical measures of the particle system to the solution of the kinetic equation. In general, convergence holds along subsequences.

title: When Momentum Helps Polyak--Ruppert Averaging
abstract: Polyak--Ruppert averaging gives SGD and momentum methods the same asymptotic covariance. We characterize how fast finite runs reach it and how far they can be parallelized. For strongly convex quadratics with additive noise, we prove an online--offline bridge: the empirical risk minimizer on the samples of a tail average is one Newton step from the tail-averaged query point of any online procedure. For SGD, heavy ball, and Nesterov's method with constant momentum, this step is a boundary term at the two ends of the tail and splits the gap to the offline estimator into center, covariance, and shape errors. Necessary and sufficient conditions show that, on the least curved direction, the center error sets the pace: SGD needs $m\ggκ^2$ rounds but momentum only $m\ggκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number, so at sample size $N$ the critical batch size grows from $Θ(\sqrt{N}/κ)$ to $Θ(\sqrt{N/κ})$. The covariance error separates the momentum methods: heavy ball has relative variance excess $Θ(κ^{3/2}/m)$ along the stiffest direction, whereas Nesterov has relative error $O(\sqrtκ/m)$ in every direction. The shape error is method-independent by a Berry--Esseen bound uniform in $κ$ and batch size, so confidence intervals are valid when the other two errors vanish. We further examine how the conclusions change under heavy-tailed or state-dependent noise and clipping, and establish a first-order comparison with ERM for nonlinear Nesterov averaging under explicit conditions.

title: Elements of the Green ring related to Alperin's weight conjecture
abstract: J. L. Alperin introduced his celebrated weight conjecture, a major question in the modular representation theory of finite groups, which has now been studied for several decades. Alperin viewed this conjecture as the beginning of a ``Lie theory for the general finite group", as the title of the article indicates. This paper is intended as a tribute to Alperin's insight. In this note, we place an emphasis on projective modules and putting the numerical questions arising from the weight conjecture into a ``module form" within the appropriate Green ring of RG, when G is a finite group, and R is a suitable complete discrete valuation ring with residue field of prime characteristic p. We believe that this work moves in the direction of a structural approach to Alperin's weight conjecture.
comment: Submitted to Journal of Algebra August 30,2026

title: Radial uniqueness and nondegeneracy for the Robin Lane-Emden equation
abstract: In this paper, we study positive radial solutions of $-Δu=u^p$ in a ball $B_R\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, subject to the Robin boundary condition $\partial_νu+βu=0$, where $N\ge2$ and $β>0$. For every Sobolev subcritical exponent $p>1$, we prove the existence of a unique positive radial solution and its nondegeneracy with respect to radial perturbations. The proof relies on the strict monotonicity of the logarithmic slope of the normalized Lane-Emden profile, which follows from the radial Pohozaev identity. When $N\ge3$, the same argument also recovers the classical critical existence range $0<βR<N-2$ and proves radial nondegeneracy throughout this interval. At $βR=(N-2)/2$, we exhibit $N$ linearly independent nonradial solutions of the linearized problem.

title: Annealed correlation and quenched noise sensitivity in biased deep neural networks
abstract: In earlier work by Jonasson, Steif and Zetterqvist (2023), fully connected deep neural networks with layers of width $n$, i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian weights, sign activations and no bias terms were shown to be annealed and quenched noise sensitive with respect to any joint probability distribution $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}$ on the input $\boldsymbolω$ and its perturbation $\boldsymbolη$ satisfying a mild positive-correlation condition and $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolη \in \{\boldsymbolω,-\boldsymbolω\}) \to 0$. Here we add independent Gaussian biases of the natural order and show that quenched noise sensitivity is retained over a broad range of depths, indeed under the slightly weaker assumption that $\mathbb{Q}^{(n)}(\boldsymbolω = \boldsymbolη) \to 0$. Thus, subject to the positive-correlation condition, quenched noise sensitivity holds under the minimal requirement that the perturbed input is asymptotically unlikely to coincide with the original input. At the same time, the annealed covariance remains bounded away from zero and is entirely accounted for by fluctuations in the network-dependent output means.

title: Error-correction Decoding for 2D Convolutional Codes with a Generalized Viterbi Algorithm
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) convolutional codes are a generalization of one-dimensional (1D) convolutional codes and are naturally suitable for encoding two-dimensional data. Although their theoretical properties are well established, practical applications are limited due to the lack of error-correction decoding algorithms. While the Viterbi algorithm provides an efficient decoding method for 1D convolutional codes, no analogous approach exists for the 2D case. In this paper, we introduce a decoding algorithm for 2D convolutional codes, called the 2D Viterbi algorithm, extending the principles of the classical Viterbi algorithm to the two-dimensional setting. The presented 2D Viterbi algorithm works with linear systems representations of 2D convolutional codes and its complexity depends on the dimension of the corresponding 2D linear system. Hence, we also provide several algorithms to obtain 2D realizations of small dimension.

title: The Great Picard theorem for quasiregular values
abstract: We prove a version of Rickman's Great Picard theorem in the theory of quasiregular values. The version of the theorem that we prove is in fact stated in terms of omitted quasiregular values, unlike the previously known Little Picard theorem of the theory that is based on quasiregular values in the boundary of the image set. As a byproduct of the proof, we also prove a Riemann removability theorem in our setting, which ends up strengthening the conclusion of the previously resolved question of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin.

title: A counterexample to the fractional Michael-Simon inequality
abstract: We show that the fractional Michael-Simon inequality does not hold for general smooth hypersurfaces and for the range of 0 < s < (n-1)/n in the case p=1. We construct a family of smooth hypersurfaces, whose fractional mean curvature is nonnegative everywhere, which violates the inequality in the limit. The same construction yields a counterexample for every 1 \leq p < \infty for the range s < (n-1)/(np).

title: Remarks on space curve $L^2$ Fourier restriction
abstract: We re-examine and consider variants of the Fourier restriction theorem for space curves. In particular, we introduce a Stein--Tomas-type argument which recovers the sharp $L^2$ restriction theorem from classical oscillatory integral estimates, in the spirit of Arkhipov--Chubarikov--Karatsuba. In addition, we consider certain square function estimates which can be thought of as partial progress towards a space curve variant of the orthonormal Fourier restriction theorem of Frank--Sabin. These estimates are obtained by reducing the problem to a Kakeya-type maximal inequality, which we analyse using a formulation of the Bourgain--Guth broad/narrow method.

title: The Fourier restriction problem for biradial functions
abstract: We determine the exact strong-type Fourier restriction range for the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ on the class of $O(d-k)\times O(k)$-invariant functions, for every $d\geq4$ and $2\leq k\leq d-2$. This includes the critical estimates beyond the biradial Stein--Tomas endpoint left open by Mandel and Oliveira e Silva. The proof combines a weighted $L^2$ estimate for extension from a circular arc with the full two-dimensional restriction theorem. An appendix gives a direct proof of the classically conjectured range for axially symmetric functions on the whole sphere.

title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
abstract: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.

title: The Complexity of Minimal Positive Realization
abstract: We study the complexity of minimal positive realization for discrete-time systems. We prove that, given a strictly proper transfer matrix with rational coefficients and an order bound encoded in unary, deciding whether a positive realization exists within that bound is complete for the existential theory of the reals. We further prove hardness for stable single-input single-output transfer functions that admit positive realizations, even when the bound equals the McMillan degree.

title: Classification of SNC $(p,k)$-planes with Hodge structures of K3 type
abstract: A SNC $(p,k)$-plane is a $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$-Galois cover $π\colon X \to \mathbb P^2$ with a simple normal crossing branch locus. In this setting, there exist several intermediate quotients $Y_1, Y_2,\dots, Y_{φ_{p,k}}$ corresponding to subgroups of $(\mathbb Z/p)^k$ of index $p$. We focus on the case where each $Y_i$ is either a surface with geometric genus $0$ or $1$, with at least one with geometric genus $1$. We classify all SNC $(p,k)$-planes satisfying these conditions obtaining that an extensive list of cases are minimal regular surfaces of general type with positive geometric genus. Moreover, these assumptions allow us to have strong control over the weight-$2$ Hodge structure of the minimal model of the covering surface $X$. Therefore, we also prove that Tate and Mumford-Tate conjectures hold for such surfaces. As an independent result of our methods, we obtain a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $1$, which turn out to be precisely all K3 surfaces, and a classification of SNC $(p,1)$-planes with geometric genus $0$, which turn out to be instead rational surfaces.

title: Theta Relations
abstract: Motivated by the classical quartic and cubic theta identities, we establish a product formula for Siegel--Jacobi theta series associated with rationally isometric positive-definite quadratic spaces. Our main theorem expresses a product of theta series of arbitrary Siegel degree as a finite double character sum over quotients of commensurable lattices. For the root lattice $A_2$, it yields a finite Fourier identity for cubes of cubic theta functions, a new proof of the two-variable cubic identity, and seven independent relations in degree two. A second specialization gives a new square analogue of the two-variable cubic identity. At the origin it reduces to $a(q)a(q^2)=b(q)b(q^2)+c(q)c(q^2)$; in degree two, the same seven relation patterns recur with each cube replaced by the corresponding product at $τ$ and $2τ$. We further extend the cubic identities on $A_2$ to $\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq3$, and to $2\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq2$, in arbitrary Siegel degree. The doubled-order construction recovers Jacobi's quartic identity and gives its analogues in arbitrary Siegel degree.

title: Stability of Serrin-Type Overdetermined Problems for the $p$-Laplacian and Related Operators
abstract: We investigate a Serrin-type overdetermined problem for the $p$-Laplacian and establish a quantitative stability estimate under suitable convexity and regularity assumptions on the domain, the solution, and the operator. Our method also applies to a class of generalized divergence-form elliptic operators.

title: Kurzweil's impulsive inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian
abstract: In the present paper, we proceed with the research initiated in (S. Antontsev \emph{et al.}, Inverse Problems, 2021). We study the inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian and with a right-hand side in the integral over-determination condition, which approximates a discontinuous function at $t=0$. We rescale the problem in a neighbourhood $[0,1/n]$ and pass to the limit as $n$ approaches infinity. This leads to the inverse problem on an infinitesimal initial layer, which transforms the initial velocity into a new one.

title: Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli
abstract: We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.

title: Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable
abstract: Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.

title: Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence
abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(\varphi, ρ)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.

title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.

title: Schrödinger estimates with arbitrarily small periodic regularity on $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{T}$
abstract: Let $M=\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{T}$ carry its product metric. We prove that the Schrödinger evolution maps $L^2(\mathbb{H}^2;H^s(\mathbb{T}))$ into $L^2([0,1];L^6(M))$ for every $s>0$, without any regularity assumption in the hyperbolic variable. The proof separates hyperbolic and periodic frequencies. A localized hyperbolic kernel estimate restricts the effective interaction time at hyperbolic frequency $L$ to order $L^{-1}$. Quadratic exponential sums then give a logarithmic bound when the periodic bandwidth is comparable to $L$. A mixed-norm decoupling argument, including an $L^6$-valued extension and a periodic transference step, reduces wider periodic bands to this case. The infimum of the admissible periodic regularities is therefore zero. The estimate at zero regularity is not established here.

title: Rational analytic prismatization
abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory

title: On the Fluctuations of Associated Primes and Depths of Powers of Monomial Ideals
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the fluctuation phenomenon in the sets of associated primes and depths of powers of monomial ideals. We provide affirmative answers to two open questions posed in [8] concerning the existence of monomial ideals in K[x,y,z] whose associated primes exhibit prescribed patterns of appearance, disappearance, and reappearance of the maximal ideal across specified ranges of powers. For each construction, we also derive the corresponding fluctuation in depths. Furthermore, we construct a square-free monomial ideal that is nearly normally torsion-free but fails to satisfy the persistence property, thereby answering a question posed in [20] in the negative. This example arises as the edge ideal of the ideal minimally non-packing clutter Q_10, revealing an intriguing connection between combinatorial optimization and the algebraic properties of monomial ideals.
comment: We welcome any comments, suggestions, or constructive feedback that may help us improve the manuscript

title: U-Examples: A Unified Family of Worst-Case Instances for Optimization Algorithms
abstract: Worst-case instances show where optimization algorithms fail: the Klee-Minty cube for the simplex method, ill-conditioned and rippled bowls for gradient descent, degenerate minima for Newton's method, redundant Klee-Minty cubes for interior-point methods, unprunable trees for branch-and-bound, deceptive landscapes for metaheuristics, and degenerate cycling for active-set methods. These constructions were developed over seventy years in separate literatures, each with its own tools. This survey reviews them together. We trace the history of rule-specific worst cases across seven representative algorithm classes and organize them with one reading: in each, the optimum lies near the start, yet the algorithm's own update rule is misdirected onto a long trajectory or, at the boundary, into a non-terminating loop. We call such an instance a U-Example; the letter U stands both for the unification and for the U-shaped bowls around which descent methods are made to crawl. A common framework treats every algorithm as a rule on a state space with a progress potential, so that one definition of misdirection, and of the resulting blow-up in cost, covers pivoting, descent, interior-point, tree-search, and population methods. Each member is drawn in a common visual grammar and quantified in general dimension $n$. The blow-up is independent of the dimension for the two descent members and exponential in it for four search members, with degenerate cycling as a breakdown. We connect the constructions to neighbouring theories (oracle complexity, performance estimation, smoothed analysis, and the complexity of local search), each of which asks a different question of the same instances. We then map each worst case to the remedy that defeats it, examine how robust the instances are, and close with open challenges, in particular whether a worst case can be predicted from the update rule alone.
comment: 38 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to SIAM Review. Ancillary file: notebook reproducing Figures 3, 8, and 9

title: The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry
abstract: Amplituhedra are semi-algebraic sets of fundamental importance in particle physics. Their discovery initiated the field of Positive Geometry. We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

title: An Aldous-type tightness characterisation for the $M_1$ topology: replacing global modulus control by local control at stopping times
abstract: Aldous' criterion provides a stopping-time characterisation of tightness in Skorokhod's $J_1$ topology and is one of the standard tools for proving functional limit theorems. For the weaker $M_1$ topology, where limiting jumps can be approximated by clustered jumps or steep continuous motion, no analogous characterisation has been available and tightness classically requires controlling a global oscillation modulus over all nearby triples of times. We prove such an Aldous-type characterisation of $M_1$ tightness, replacing the global modulus condition by local estimates at stopping times ruling out rapid reversals after a large excursion. Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. They reduce the verification of $M_1$ tightness to short-time estimates for the processes restarted from its state at suitable stopping times.

title: The Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture for the Fisher-KPP equation
abstract: We resolve the Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture, which concerns the classification of all [0,1]-valued entire solutions of Fisher-KPP equations with concave C^2 reaction terms in arbitrary space dimension. We prove that every such solution is a C_{loc}^{1,2} limit of solutions generated by finitely many planar traveling fronts, possibly together with a spatially homogeneous solution. Our approach reveals an ordered linear structure underlying the nonlinear solution space, leading to a critical-subcritical spectral decomposition. The proof combines linear reconstruction of subcritical approximants with a measure representation (a kind of nonlinear Martin representation) of critical solutions, obtained through small-amplitude asymptotics and comparison with a radially symmetric entire solution.

title: Stability and instability for particle dynamics in magnetic fields
abstract: We study zero-speed equilibria of the Newton-Lorentz equation $\ddot x=\dot x\times B(x)$ in $\mathbf{R}^3$, which describes the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field $B$. We prove Lyapunov instability wherever the field $B$ does not vanish (under $C^1$ regularity), and at every isolated zero of $B$ provided it is real-analytic. These results do not assume that the field is divergence-free. In contrast, we construct a compactly supported divergence-free $C^\infty$ field that is flat at an isolated zero and makes the corresponding equilibrium Lyapunov stable.

title: Almost entropic matroids and $(k,L)$-systems
abstract: For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.

title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
abstract: Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. Numerical optimization involving stiff evolutionary and static PDEs often requires solving a large system of equations, which can be treated as a constraint. In this work, we present a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver that incorporates this constraint. We evaluate its performance across four key tasks: a) linear and nonlinear forward modeling of evolutionary and static problems, b) solving inverse problems to estimate equation coefficients, c) solving inverse problems to estimate the right-hand side, and d) learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. These capabilities make it a powerful tool for different physics and engineering applications, in particular for geophysics, where inverse problems are commonly solved in order to reduce the model uncertainty.

title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem
abstract: We study the negative Laplacian on the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$, $n \ge 3$, subject to a constant impedance (Robin) boundary condition with $α> 0$. The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+α^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. The two rates are not comparable pointwise. Each is critical for the Agmon-Hörmander space $\mathcal{B}^*$, however. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $α$, so that on the band $-α^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. The bulk block, by contrast, determines $α$.
comment: 84 pages. Part I of a two-part series

title: Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics
abstract: Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. In this work, we develop a numerical method based on the constrained gentlest ascent dynamics (CGAD) that systematically computes excited states of dipolar BECs by stably targeting constrained saddle points with any prescribed Morse index. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. This work provides a computational framework for studying excited states in dipolar quantum gases and offers insights for future theoretical and experimental investigations.

title: Classification of positive solutions to the critical Lane-Emden system
abstract: We classify all positive classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system $$ -Δu=v^p \, \, \text{in } \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, \, \, -Δv=u^q \, \, \text{in} \, \, \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $N\geq3$ and $p,q>0$ satisfy $$ \frac{1}{p+1}+\frac{1}{q+1}=\frac{N-2}{N}.$$Without assuming boundedness, decay at infinity, or finite energy, we prove that every such solution has the form $$ u(x)=λ^{\frac{N}{q+1}}U(λ(x-a)), \, \, v(x)=λ^{\frac{N}{p+1}}V(λ(x-a)), $$ for some $a\in \mathbb{R}^N$ and $λ>0$, where $(U,V)$ is the positive radial ground state centered at the origin and normalized by $U(0)=1$. Consequently, both components are radially symmetric about the same point and satisfy $$ \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}u^{q+1}\, dx = \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}v^{p+1}\,dx<\infty. $$ Our result extends the classical classification of positive solutions of the critical Sobolev equation by Caffarelli, Gidas and Spruck and Chen and Li to the critical Lane-Emden system.

title: Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints
abstract: We consider the following inverse domain uncertainty quantification problem: given a prescribed value or measurement of a hemodynamic biomarker, characterize the distribution of vascular geometries compatible with it. The problem is formulated as a Bayesian inverse problem in which a high-dimensional latent parameter encodes the cardiovascular shape and accounts for inter-patient variability. The parameter-to-observable map composes a conditional LDDMM stochastic interpolant generating the aortic surface with a high-performance numerical finite element solver for the unsteady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations, from which biomarkers of interest are evaluated. The map is nonlinear, high-dimensional and computationally expensive. To address the problem, we compare three ensemble strategies: ensemble adjusted Kalman inversion (EAKI), adaptive Bayesian updating with structural reliability (aBUS), and a Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) sequential Monte Carlo scheme. The first two approaches are derivative-free. For the third method, we introduce a novel differentiable flow-matching surrogate that reduces the cost of a single forward map evaluation at the price of a distribution shift depending on the training distribution used for the surrogate. We apply the framework to the generation of virtual patient cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops along aortic geometries affected by coarctation, and we validate and compare the three methods on synthetic data.

title: A Structure-Preserving Scheme for Computing the Gradient of the Eikonal Equation
abstract: We propose a first-order, structure-preserving method for directly computing the normalized traveltime gradient of the eikonal equation in smooth first-arrival regions. The method combines analytical derivatives of spherical linear interpolation (SLERP) in a Godunov-type upwind discretization with spherical forward Euler (SFE) pseudo-time integration. This construction gives a tangent residual and keeps every iterate on $\mathbb{S}^2$ without projection or normalization. The SLERP discretization exactly preserves a family of curved orientation equilibria. Removing the background discretization bias improves absolute orientation accuracy near these equilibria, allowing a prescribed error tolerance to be reached on a coarser grid. We prove the equilibrium-preservation property and, separately, a smaller angular error for SFE than normalized Euler in a one-cell relaxation under the stated step-size condition. Two- and three-dimensional experiments examine convergence, geometric preservation, and computational cost. Comparisons with gradient recovery from scalar traveltimes show more accurate directions on the same grid in the curved media considered. The method provides direction fields for wave propagation and geometric optics, with potential use in adjoint-based inverse problems.

title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
abstract: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.

title: Front-pinned spectral collocation for the flame problem and related ignition problems
abstract: We consider global Chebyshev collocation for the ignition problems $y'=y^q(1-y)$, $y(0)=δ$, $q\ge2$; for $q=2$ this is the flame problem, a standard stiff test equation. After rescaling to $[-1,1]$ the solution has an interior layer of width $O(μ)$, $μ=(q-1)δ^{q-1}$, at a $δ$-dependent position. Two obstacles arise: plain Chebyshev collocation needs $O(1/μ)$ nodes, and imposing the initial condition amplifies errors by a factor of order $1/μ$, which makes the collocation equations severely ill-conditioned. Our main contribution addresses the second one. Since all solutions are translates of one profile, the initial condition can be replaced by an equivalent interior condition. For an unknown $u=\varphi(y)$, imposing it where the speed $|\varphi'f_q|$ of $u$ along the orbit is maximal bounds the propagator of the linearized equation by one; for $u=\ln y$ this is $y(x^\ast)=(q-1)/q$. For the first obstacle we use the sinh map of Tee and Trefethen: the time function is explicit, the complex singularities of the profile lie exactly at $\pm(2k+1)πi$, and the map parameters follow in closed form, so that $O(\ln(1/μ))$ nodes suffice. In double precision the pinned scheme reaches the interpolation error of the exact solution in five or six Newton iterations for $μ$ down to $10^{-12}$, whereas the initial-condition form fails or converges to wrong discrete solutions, also in an integral (Birkhoff) reformulation. Computations in $256$-bit arithmetic confirm the predicted rate down to errors of $10^{-70}$, AAA approximation locates the singularities to within $2\%$, and the method carries over to an Arrhenius reaction rate, with all parameters computed numerically.
comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/boros91/flame-collocation, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23479185

title: Central Limit Theorems for Optimal Transport Functionals
abstract: We establish central limit theorems for empirical plug-in estimators of scalar functionals of quadratic optimal transport maps and potentials, including Wasserstein costs and several risk measures constructed from transport-based multivariate quantiles. We study the one-sample problem with a known reference distribution and i.i.d. observations from the target distribution. A natural approach is to combine a limit theorem for the empirical transport map with the functional delta method. We show, however, that in dimensions at least two, empirical transport-map errors admit no nonzero weak limit in $L^2$ under any normalizing scale. Instead, we linearize the functional directly in the target distribution, obtaining an influence-function expansion with a remainder controlled by the transport-map error. The influence function is characterized by a linear elliptic partial differential equation. Under regularity conditions, we use this expansion to prove central limit theorems in low dimensions and establish validity of the empirical bootstrap. We also derive semiparametric efficiency bounds and show that the plug-in estimators attain them under the same conditions.

title: Plasticity of the unit sphere of the space $c_0$
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the unit sphere of the space $c_{0}$ is plastic, i.e., every non-expansive bijection from this sphere onto itself is an isometry.

title: Free-field realizations of $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras associated with Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$
abstract: We extend the recursive construction of free-field realizations proposed by Ide, Ito, and Miyazaki to the $\mathcal{N} = 1$ supersymmetric $\mathcal{W}$-algebras $\mathcal{SW} B (n - 1 , n)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (n , n)$, associated with the Lie superalgebras $B (n - 1 , n)$ and $B (n , n)$, respectively. We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

title: The Lévy-Khinchine type representations and generalized functions on Bernstein spaces
abstract: We consider the class of all univariate probability laws whose characteristic functions do not have zeroes on the real line. This class contains the fundamental family of infinitely divisible distributions and its new extension, the set of rational-(quasi-)infinitely divisible laws. We prove that this class is dense in the family of all probability laws with respect to the total variation distance. We show that characteristic functions corresponding to this class admit Lévy-Khinchine type representations. In these formulas, the generalized spectral functions (the regularized Lévy measures) are special continuous linear functionals on the union of well known Bernstein spaces of entire functions of exponential type which are additionally bounded on the real line. We apply this spectral functions in criteria of weak convergence of distributions within the class under study. All necessary analytical constructions are proposed.

title: Finite groups with large sum of element orders compared to cyclic groups
abstract: For a finite group $G$ let $ψ(G)$ denote the sum of the orders of elements in $G$. If $G$ has order $n$ then, by a result of Amiri, Jafarian Amiri and Isaacs, $ψ(G)\leψ(C_n)$, where $C_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. We determine all finite groups such that $ψ(G)\ge\frac{1}{3}ψ(C_n)$.

title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.

title: Beta-expansions induced by general Parry polynomials and sharp iteration asymptotics of their transfer operators
abstract: This paper generalizes previous results to any Parry polynomials $p_n(z)$ \cite{Pa} of finite degree $n\geq 2$. Let $β>1$ be the unique positive root of $p_n$ and consider the transfer operator $\mathscr{P}$ induced by the map $[0,1]\ni x\mapsto βx-\lfloor βx\rfloor \in [0,1)$. Suppose all other roots of $p_n$ have magnitude less than one. Then for any smooth function $F$ on $[0,1]$ we prove two term asymptotics in $L^\infty$ of the form \begin{equation*} \big(\mathscr{P}^r(F)\big)(\cdot)= u(\cdot) \int_0^1 F(x)\: \mathrm{d} x +β^{-r}v(\cdot) \big (F(1)-F(0)\big )+o(β^{-r}),\quad r\geq 1, \end{equation*} where $u$ is piecewise constant and $\mathscr{P}u=u$, while $v$ is piecewise equal to a polynomial of degree one and $\mathscr{P}v= β^{-1}v$. When $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to functions of bounded variation $BV([0,1])$, it is known that $\vert z \vert\leq β^{-1}$ contains its essential spectrum. Thus the contribution coming from $v$ in the above estimate is not guaranteed if $F$ is not smooth enough. Furthermore, we show that when $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to $BV([0,1])$ then any $\vert z \vert<β^{-1}$ is an eigenvalue with infinite multiplicity. Moreover, we construct a meromorphic extension of $(\mathscr{P}-z)^{-1}$ to the domain $\vert z \vert>β^{-1}$, where the finite rank poles are numbers $ζ$ with $β^{-1}<\vert ζ\vert\leq 1$ such that $βζ$ is a root of $p_n(z)$. If such poles $ζ$ other than $1$ exist, then we construct eigenvectors of $\mathscr{P}^*$ in $BV^*$ obeying $\mathscr{P}^*\hat{U}=ζ\hat{U}$, where $\hat{U}(F)$ is given by series involving the values of $F$ taken in some specially chosen, finer and finer partitions of $[0,1]$. When $F$ is either a polynomial or a characteristic function like $χ_{[0,x]}$, then $\hat{U}(F)$ can be explicitly computed.

title: Payoff Polarization and Garbage Concentration in a Stochastic Garbage Disposal Game
abstract: We study a stochastic garbage disposal game on a finite graph in which agents transfer garbage through pairwise interactions governed by payoff-dependent Fermi probabilities. We investigate the long-term behavior of both payoffs and garbage distributions. We prove that payoff dispersion grows at least linearly in time almost surely, leading to payoff polarization, with the maximum and minimum payoffs diverging to positive and negative infinity, respectively. Moreover, the payoff range grows at least on the order of the square root of time. For garbage dynamics, we establish almost-sure concentration on a single agent in the two-agent case for any positive disposal efficiency. When disposal is complete and the underlying graph is connected, we further prove that all garbage becomes concentrated on a single agent after a finite random time, although the agent holding the garbage may change over time. These results characterize the emergence of payoff inequality and garbage concentration in stochastic competitive interactions on networks.

title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. However, the method usually leads to ill-conditioned linear systems with a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), limiting its application. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.
comment: Submitted to Journal of Computational Physics. 31 pages, 12 figures

title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $μ$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.

title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
abstract: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.

title: Ehrhart positivity of smooth polytopes with few facets
abstract: For each dimension $d$, we determine the minimum number of facets of a smooth $d$-dimensional lattice polytope whose Ehrhart polynomial has at least one negative coefficient. This minimum is six in dimension $d=3$, seven in dimension $d=4$, and $d+2$ in every dimension $d\ge 5$. The lower bounds follow from the classification of smooth lattice polytopes with at most $d+2$ facets, together with explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials in dimensions at most $4$. We also prove that a lattice polytope of dimension at least $3$ with a smooth vertex cannot be $2$-integral with respect to any ordered lattice basis.

title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
abstract: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

title: The Dimension Landscape of Bivariate $C^2$ Splines
abstract: Schumaker's lower bound incorporates local geometric corrections and provides insight into the dimensions of bivariate spline spaces. Building on this bound, we study bivariate $C^2$ spline dimensions from three perspectives: universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps. We prove universal attainment in degree seven for every legal realization of every triangulation. We prove generic attainment in degrees five and six for every fixed combinatorial triangulation and give explicit polynomial conditions certifying generic failure on fixed triangulations in degrees three and four. For geometric jumps with matching local direction types at corresponding interior vertices, we prove nonexistence in degree seven and construct examples in degrees three and five. In degree six, universal attainment and the existence of such geometric jumps remain open questions.

title: Non-null ruled surfaces and pseudo hyper-dual tangent sphere bundles
abstract: In this paper, the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres are defined. Then, a new family of non-null ruled surfaces associated with hyper-dual Lorentzian curves is defined via the E.Study hyper-map in Minkowski space and the definitions of the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres. Within this framework, the resulting non-null ruled surfaces are classified. Necessary and sufficient conditions for developability are obtained with their geometric interpretations in terms of hyper-dual Lorentzian curves and arc-length parameters. Moreover, explicit examples are presented to verify the theoretical results.

title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindelöf-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

title: The strong type endpoint estimate for the local spherical maximal function
abstract: Let $p_d=(d^2+1)/(d(d-1))$ and $q_d=(d^2+1)/(d-1)$. We prove that the local spherical maximal operator $\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2}|f*dσ_t|$ is bounded from $L^{p_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L^{q_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $d\geq 2$. Previously only the restricted weak type estimate was known at this endpoint. Together with known results, this completes the characterization of the strong type $L^p\to L^q$ bounds for the local spherical maximal operator. We also prove the maximal estimate \[ \Big\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|e^{it\sqrt{-Δ}}f|\Big\|_{L^{2(d+1)/(d-1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \lesssim\|f\|_{\dot H^{d/(d+1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \] for the wave equation at the critical exponent. Both results are obtained by exploiting the gain in bilinear estimates that comes from the interaction between high and low frequencies.

title: New Directions in Irrationality
abstract: Since Apéry's proof of the irrationality of $ζ(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Apéry as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $μ(ζ(2))<4.62675$ and $μ(ζ(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,ζ(3),ζ(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $μ(Aζ(3)+Bζ(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.
comment: 73 pages: 35-page main text; 17 figures. Code sources: https://github.com/RamanujanMachine/new-directions-in-irrationality

title: Absolute winning properties of exceptional sets for rational maps
abstract: We study Schmidt's game on the Julia set $J(f)$ of weak hyperbolic rational maps $f:\CC\to\CC$. For each $y\in J(f)$, let $E(f,y)$ be the set of points in $J(f)$ whose forward orbits stay a positive distance from $y$. We prove that $E(f,y)$ is absolute winning on $J(f)$ for each $y \in J(f)$. To do this, we first prove the absolute winning property for the exceptional set associated to the critical points by a potential game argument, and then use uniform expansion to obtain the result for each target point $y$.

title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
abstract: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

title: Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions
abstract: For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $ω(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leqω(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.

title: Size and spectral radius conditions for the existence of $k$-factor in graphs with given minimum degree
abstract: In recent years, characterizing the conditions for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in graphs has received significant academic attention. For integers $b\ge a\ge 1$, an $[a, b]$-factor of a graph $G$ is defined as a spanning subgraph $H$ such that $a\le d_{H}(v)\le b$ for every $v\in V(G)$. If $a=b=k$, a $[k, k]$-factor is called a $k$-factor of $G$. Let $δ(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. Hao and Li [Electron. J. Combin. (2024)] posed the problem of characterizing the size or spectral radius conditions for a graph to contain an $[a,b]$-factor with $δ(G)\ge a$. Fan, Lin and Zhu [Discrete Math. (2026)] solved the size version of this problem for the case $a < b.$ In this paper, for $a=b=k$, we characterize the size condition for a graph to have a $k$-factor with $δ(G)\ge k$. Using this result, we also characterize the spectral radius and distance spectral radius conditions for a graph to have a $k$-factor, respectively.

title: Orbital stability of standing waves for defocusing fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equations with a delta potential
abstract: In this paper, a fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a delta potential and a repulsive nonlinearity in one space dimension is considered. First, it is proved that the Cauchy problem in Sobolev spaces on the real line is globally well-posed, independently of the sign of the delta potential. Moreover, in the case of an attractive delta potential, the existence, the minimization properties and the orbital stability of standing waves under the flow of the equation are established. The stability proof is based on concentration-compactness methods for the energy/charge functional. For that purpose, no explicit calculation of the standing waves is required and the results are based on the variational properties of the solutions alone.

title: A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
abstract: We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.

title: Control variates for dry friction under colored noise: variance rates for non-smooth observables
abstract: A control variate method was introduced by Garnier and Mertz (2022) for multivalued stochastic differential equations driven by colored noise. For smooth observables, the asymptotic variance is $O(\varepsilon^{2})$, where $\varepsilon^{2}$ is the correlation time of the noise. However, for non-smooth reliability observables, such as threshold indicators and overshoot severities, rate estimates have not been established in general. In this paper, rate estimates are derived for the inertial dry-friction inclusion driven by colored noise in the three regimes whose white-noise propagators are known. The asymptotic variance of the resulting control variate estimators is $O(\varepsilon^{2α})$ for $α$-Hölder observables with $α\in(0,1]$, $O(\varepsilon)$ for observables of bounded variation satisfying a one-sided continuity condition, $O(\varepsilon^{1+α})$ for observables that are both $α$-Hölder and of bounded variation, and $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{2,1+2α\}})$ for observables with finitely many $α$-cusps, where $α\in (0, 1]$ is the cusp exponent. The last three bounds hold up to logarithmic factors. Bounds on the bias of the white-noise approximation and non-asymptotic sample-size estimates are also derived, and the comparison principle is shown to be preserved under coupled time discretization. Numerical experiments in the three regimes support the predicted rates.

title: Bulk limits of the truncated circular beta ensembles
abstract: We study the bulk limits of the rank-one truncation of the circular beta ensembles obtained by deleting the first row and column. We prove that the normalized Blaschke products of the truncated circular beta ensembles converge in law to a constant multiple (depending on $β$) of the i.i.d.~Gaussian analytic function (GAF) uniformly on compacts of the unit disk. As a consequence, we identify the bulk point process limit with the zero set of GAF, which was proved in the seminal work of Peres and Virág to form a determinantal point process with the Bergman kernel. Our method also applies to the rank-one multiplicative perturbations of the circular beta ensembles in the mesoscopic regime.

title: Spectral analysis of multi-bubble solutions to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
abstract: We investigate weighted spectral limits for separated multi-bubble configurations and refined spectral asymptotics for the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[ -Δu=u^p+\varepsilon u^q, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$ with $N\geq3$, $p=(N+2)/(N-2)$, $1\leq q<p$ and $\varepsilon$ is a positive parameter. We first determine the limits of the ordered weighted eigenvalues associated with families of positive functions admitting an $m$-bubble decomposition at distinct interior points with a remainder vanishing in $H_0^1(Ω)$. The limiting eigenvalues are those of the single-bubble problem, with all multiplicities multiplied by $m$. We then refine this analysis for positive multi-bubble solutions of this problem with comparable concentration scales, deriving precise expansions of the first $(N+2)m$ eigenvalues and characterizing their eigenfunctions when $1<q<3$ if $N=4$ or $1\leq q<p$ if $N\geq5$. The leading corrections are determined by explicit symmetric matrices involving $q$, the concentration parameters, and the Green and Robin functions. In particular, we prove that the dilation matrix is positive definite. Together, these spectral results yield Morse index bounds for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, with an exact formula when the matrix governing the translation modes is invertible.

title: Second largest eigenvalue thresholds for the vertex-connectivity of regular graphs
abstract: Let $λ_2(G)$ and $κ(G)$ denote the second largest adjacency eigenvalue and the vertex-connectivity of a graph $G$. For a non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$, Fiedler's inequality $λ_2(G)\ge r-κ(G)$ shows that $λ_2(G)<r-t$ forces $κ(G)\ge t+1$. The best such bound is known for $t=1$, by Zhang and Wang, and for $t=2$ with $r\ge4$, by Zhang. In this paper, for every $r\ge3$ and every integer $t$ with $2\le t\le r-1$, we give an upper bound on $λ_2(G)$ that forces an $r$-regular graph $G$ to satisfy $κ(G)\ge t+1$, and we determine exactly when this bound is best possible. For $\frac{r+2}{2}\le t\le r-1$, Fiedler's bound $r-t$ is already best possible. For $2\le t<\frac{r+2}{2}$, it is replaced by one of two explicit algebraic numbers, and the sign of an explicit polynomial $W(r,t)$, which never vanishes, decides which one applies. Each of the two numbers is attained exactly when $(r,t)$ satisfies an explicit arithmetic condition, and every extremal graph then consists of two cliques and an independent cut of size $t$. In this range our bound also improves a bound of Zhang that holds for every such $t$.
