Ambient variations, localized on arbitrary coincidence sets, force this measure to vanish and give strong convergence in $H^2$. We then derive the elastic equation on isolated strands and overlap bundles, describe the distribution that remains at contact, and prove balance and rigidity statements under their precise additional hypotheses. Equality in the bridge bound gives constant curvature. Combining strong compactness with quantitative competitors gives an alternative proof that elastic limits in classes with equal bridge and braid indices are covered circles. An independent recovery theorem identifies the strong $H^2$ closure with the regular $H^2$ part of the $C^1$ closure and also implies strong compactness. Finally, a whole-line contact model illustrates which estimates are needed for finer shape selection.

title: Muckenhoupt weights for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator on hyperbolic spaces
abstract: On the real hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$, the classical Muckenhoupt condition does not describe the weights $w$ for which the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$. We show that, for $1<p<\infty$, $M$ is bounded on $L^p(w)$ if and only if $w$ is a local $A_p$ weight and satisfies a two-layer condition, which compares $w$ and its dual weight on two layers of the shadow of a point. We also treat the weak type case, radial weights and the range $p\le1$, and we prove a weighted Herz principle for radial convolution operators.

title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
abstract: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. We validate our proposed offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework on an industry case study involving rideshare coupon targeting, where customer states are defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. We evaluate performance using model-based off-policy evaluation, with causal dynamics estimated from a temporal holdout. Under the observed coupon budget and RFM state representation, our optimized policy improves customer lifetime value (LTV) by 19% over the estimated behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline. Although the demonstrated action space is binary, the proposed framework is action-agnostic, yielding a general-purpose decision module for targeting systems that manage multiple interventions.
comment: Accepted for oral presentation at the ACM RecSys 2026 Workshop on Online and Adaptive Recommender System (OARS)

title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space
abstract: We determine the dimension-independent first-order query complexity of minimizing a Lipschitz geodesically convex (g-convex) function on hyperbolic space. Given a ball of radius $r$ containing a global minimizer, we prove that $Ω(ζ_r/ε^2)$ queries are necessary to attain accuracy $εMr$, where $M$ is the Lipschitz constant and $ζ_r=r/\tanh r$ captures the effect of curvature. This matches the known $O(ζ_r/ε^2)$ upper bound for the Riemannian subgradient method (Zhang and Sra, 2016). This is the first query-complexity result for g-convex optimization that is tight simultaneously in curvature and target accuracy. The standard Euclidean recipe of constructing hard instances as maxima of affine functions does not transfer to hyperbolic space, so the lower bound requires a new mechanism. Our starting point is the worst-function construction of Criscitiello and Boumal (2023, Appendix A). It gives the same lower bound for a subclass of algorithms, including the subgradient method, whose queries remain in prescribed g-convex regions. We retain this geometric setup and carefully tune and augment their hard function to accommodate every deterministic first-order algorithm. The key new mechanism is an advance-or-stall scheme: when a query lies in these regions, the oracle reveals at most one new information direction (advance); when a query leaves them, we show that the oracle can answer without revealing any new hidden direction (stall). Unlike earlier curvature-dependent lower bounds, the proof uses no ball-packing argument.

title: Data Center Oscillation Isolation and Grid Support: Fundamental Limits and Source-Selective Control
abstract: The grid integration of large data centers poses a growing power-system stability challenge. Rapidly varying computing demand can induce oscillations, while the facilities must provide a prescribed response to grid disturbances. Existing controls address load fluctuations and grid support but do not establish their jointly achievable performance. This paper derives fundamental limits and develops a source-selective controller for simultaneous oscillation isolation and grid support. A coupled closed-loop model gives a condition for distinguishing disturbance sources and reveals a direct isolation-support conflict under grid-import-power feedback alone; additional electrical measurements can remove this pointwise conflict but leave a conditional cross-frequency sensitivity limit. Guided by these limits, we design a local residual-feedback storage controller through convex frequency-domain optimization with stability, isolation, and grid-response constraints across operating points. Tests on a single-generator interconnection and a modified nine-bus network show stronger oscillation isolation than equal-order optimized comparators while meeting the prescribed grid response across operating points.

title: An Exotic Congruence for Irregular Weight Picard Modular Forms
abstract: We construct a new type of congruence from irregular weight mod $p$ Picard modular forms (for $p$ inert) to ones of regular weight, analogous to the one obtained by Kansal--Levin--Savitt in the Hilbert setting. The congruence is obtained by using a geometric Jacquet--Langlands phenomenon, as first established by Vollaard, to transfer irregular weight mod $p$ Picard modular forms from the Picard modular surface to a Shimura set. We call this an exotic congruence, since it relates mod $p$ automorphic forms associated to different groups. This congruence will be used in upcoming work of the author proving mod $p$ local-global compatibility for irregular weight Picard modular forms (in the $p$ inert case).

title: Directional Expansiveness for the chair tiling
abstract: We study directional expansiveness of the chair tiling. We show that for every direction $V$ and every $r>0$, there exist distinct chair tilings that agree on $\mathbb{Z}^2\cap V^r$. Hence the chair tiling has no expansive direction.

title: A simplified proof of the FPRAS for counting perfect matchings
abstract: We give a simplified, self-contained proof of OpenAI's FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs. As in the original proof, we use a restricted Poincaré inequality for two matchings to sample weighted perfect matchings and estimate their total weight. We simplify the proof of this inequality by isolating parts of alternating cycles directly on the original vertex set and controlling the resulting error terms. This avoids the auxiliary vertices and tree constructions used in the original proof. The argument preserves the required parameter bounds and yields the same FPRAS guarantee.

title: Uniform convergence of canonical discrete uniformization on equilateral approximations
abstract: We prove uniform convergence of the canonical discrete uniformization maps for every sequence of equilateral polygonal disks whose mesh tends to zero and whose marked Jordan boundaries converge uniformly. The limit is the normalized Riemann map, with convergence on the entire closed reference triangle. This proves Conjecture 7.3 of Luo, Sun and Wu for the original construction with Delaunay flips. The proof combines closed-domain compactness, marked lattice limits, a packing and resistance estimate for logarithmic cusp scales, and an envelope comparison principle, followed by a local affine energy argument.

title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
abstract: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.

title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for Hölder potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
abstract: The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $κ$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $κ$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives. The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures. Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.

title: Functional Model for Isometric Pairs Satisfying an Automorphic Covariance Relation - I
abstract: We derive a canonical functional model for a pair of isometric operators $(V_1, V_2)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the automorphic covariance relation $V_1 V_2 = V_2 \varphi(V_1)$, where $\varphi$ is an automorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. This extends the classical Bercovici--Douglas--Foias functional model for commuting isometric pairs to a dynamically twisted setting. When both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are pure isometries (shifts), the model simplifies to $(M_z, M_Θ W_\varphi^*)$ acting on $H^2(\mathcal{F})$, where $W_\varphi$ is a unitary weighted composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2$ and $Θ\in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}, \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}))$ is an operator-valued inner function such that $M_Θ$ is a shift. As an application, we establish a complete unitary classification theorem for automorphically covariant isometric pairs by identifying a complete set of joint unitary invariants. Notably, our results are novel even in the special case of rotation automorphisms ($V_1 V_2 = q V_2 V_1$ with $|q| = 1$).

title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
abstract: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-Østvær, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.

title: Meromorphic modular differential equations for the elliptic genus of Calabi--Yau varieties
abstract: We study differential equations -- not necessarily monic -- for Jacobi modular forms. As an application, we derive a second-order differential equation for the elliptic genus of a $K3$ surface involving the logarithmic derivative of the modular invariant $j(τ)$, and we explicitly find a third-order equation with a leading coefficient of weight 12 for the elliptic genus of any four-dimensional Calabi--Yau variety. Furthermore, we propose a simple recursive algorithm for investigating second-order differential equations with leading coefficient $E_4(τ)$ or $E_6(τ)$.

title: Socle formulas for rigid irreducible components of Lusztig's nilpotent varieties in type $A$
abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. For any irreducible component $C$ of a nilpotent variety of type $A$ let $π(C)$ be the irreducible representation of a general linear group over $F$ attached to it. We show that if the multisegment of $C$ is multiplicity free, $C$ is rigid if and only if $π(C)$ is $\square$-irreducible. In this case, \[ π(C*D)=soc\bigl(π(C)\timesπ(D)\bigr),\qquad π(D*C)=soc\bigl(π(D)\timesπ(C)\bigr) \] for every irreducible component $D$, where $*$ is the binary operation defined by Aizenbud and Lapid, in accordance with a conjecture of Lapid and Mínguez. We also give a computer-assisted example in $A_7$ of a non-simple rigid module $z\ne0$ which does not admit a proper rigid submodule $y\ne0$ such that $Ext_Π^1(z,z/y)=0$, answering negatively a question of Aizenbud and Lapid.

title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
abstract: In 1991, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked to estimate the smallest $u=u(n,d,s)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with average degree at least $d$ has a subgraph on at most $u$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$. We resolve this problem up to polylogarithmic factors for all even values of $s$. More precisely, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $d\geq s$ has a subgraph on $O_s\left(\max\left\{\frac{n}{d^{s/(s-2)}}(\log n)^{180},\log n\right\}\right)$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$, whenever $s\ge 4$ is even. This improves a result of Janzer, Sudakov and Tomon, who obtained a similar conclusion for subgraphs of average degree at least $s$. We also prove that for every positive integer $s$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite family $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs with minimum degree $s$ such that $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})=O(n^{2-2/s+\varepsilon})$. This is tight and is the first result of similar kind that applies to odd values of $s$ greater than 3.

title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
abstract: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

title: Fourth moments of prime exponential sums and exceptional sets for sums and differences of primes
abstract: We prove a square root bound for the exceptional sets in the binary Goldbach and prime difference problems under quasi Riemann Hypothesis. If every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most a fixed $1/2\leqΘ<11/12$, then $E_+(N)\ll_ΘN^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$ and $E_-(N)\ll_ΘN^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$. Here $E_+(N)$ counts the even integers greater than $2$ and at most $N$ that are not sums of two primes, and $E_-(N)$ counts the positive even integers at most $N$ that are not differences of two primes. The common analytic estimate is a fourth moment bound of the minor arcs for a smoothed prime exponential sum.

title: A McLennan formula for equiaccessible steady states
abstract: Near equilibrium, the Boltzmann distribution is corrected by the transient irreversible entropy flux, a result known as the McLennan formula. By expanding around equiaccessible steady states instead, we derive an analogue that can hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. At zeroth order, steady-state occupation is determined solely by local escape rates, yielding a strong form of the active-matter principle of "low rattling." The first-order correction measures the impact of traffic imbalances on the accessibility of each state, marking the onset of nonlocal determinants of relative occupation.

title: An Efficient Open-Source Framework for Thermohygromechanical Phase-Field Simulation of Drying Damage Refractory Castables
abstract: The water removal from refractory castables is a complex process involving heat and mass transport and thermohygromechanical stresses. In order to reduce the risk of explosive spalling by improving the heat-up curves, numerical models are critical to predict the castable behavior during drying. However, most of the existing models either neglect the thermomechanical stresses or consider them as an \textit{a posteriori} assessment of the likelihood of failure. The present work proposes an open-source thermohygromechanical phase-field model to simulate the drying of refractory castables and predict the occurrence of explosive spalling. The model is based on an adaptive two-scale time-stepping strategy that allows for a significant reduction of the computational cost associated with the simulation. The model was validated against literature results and qualitative comparisons with experimental data were carried out to assess its ability to predict the failure behavior of partially saturated porous media during heating. The numerical simulations were also applied to investigate the impact of different heating methods on the risk of failure during drying. It was found that even at the significantly lower heating rates typical of refractory castable drying - compared to the fire accidents that motivate most thermomechanical studies on concrete structures - thermomechanical stresses still play a significant role in the explosive spalling, a finding well established for concrete under fire but novel for refractory castables. As a consequence, it was also concluded that the use of heterogeneous heating methods can increase the likelihood of explosive spalling. Ultimately, feasible solutions to increase the drying efficiency and safety that are compatible with the industrial setting were proposed and a free, open-source implementation of the model is provided.

title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression
abstract: We show that gradient descent (GD) with step size $η$ can achieve $\varepsilon$ optimality gap on the multiclass logistic regression loss in a number of iterations $T$ that is independent of $\varepsilon$. To do so, the step size $η$ must be chosen large enough as a function of $\varepsilon$ (and properties of the linearly separable dataset), while $T$ is a constant that only depends on the data. The relevant properties of the data include the number of points and their margin (for $T$), and one additional quantity (for $η$) that turns out to be necessary in dimension $d \geq 3$. The proofs build on the known fact that, as $η\to \infty$, suitably rescaled GD becomes the perceptron algorithm, and the latter finds a perfect classifier in $T$ iterations. A similar claim was shown for two classes in dimension $d = 2$ using other proof techniques. This result adds to previous works that showed GD on the logistic regression loss can be accelerated by taking large step sizes. Those provoke a wild, oscillatory initial phase, followed by a stable phase. We provide results of this (qualitatively different) nature, too.

title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments
abstract: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nyström method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO$_2$ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by $198$ $p_z$-like orbitals, retaining the $2613^2$ non-negligible entries of the $198^4$-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on $1.3$ million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of $0.004\%$, at a cost of $22$ node-hours.

title: Finite convexification by Minkowski summation
abstract: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact set and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact convex set. We study the problem of when there exists $λ>0$ such that the Minkowski sum $A+λK$ is convex. First, we show that this finite convexification is equivalent to a uniform covering condition on the exposed sets of $A$ and $K$. We then show that another characterization is possible in terms of the covering radii of the iterated exposed sets after translating each exposed face of $K$ so that its relative centroid is $0$. In the case of convex polytopes, we show that it suffices to check the exposed sets in the first level of the iteration. We also study several special cases, such as strictly convex convexifiers, lower-dimensional convexifiers, strongly isomorphic polytopes, and the planar case.

title: FOMTools: Development and AI-Assisted Code Generation for First-Order Methods
abstract: We present FOMTools, an open-source Python package for developing, analyzing, and deploying first-order algorithms for parametric linear and convex quadratic optimization. The user specifies an iteration in Python, with syntax close to its mathematical description. The package represents the iteration as a computation graph of affine and piecewise affine operations. To analyze worst-case performance, FOMTools formulates a mixed-integer verification problem that maximizes a convergence residual over a specified set of problem instances and initial iterates. For probabilistic performance analysis, a batched GPU simulator collects algorithm trajectories and computes statistical bounds on the probability of exceeding a specified convergence tolerance. From the same algorithm description, FOMTools generates specialized solver code for embedded hardware, multicore CPUs, and GPUs. The package first generates the numerical data, factorizations, and matrix-vector routines without any agent. A coding agent then translates the iteration into C or CUDA code and iteratively optimizes the implementation. After each phase, the package runs the generated code on sampled inputs and compares it with a reference execution. FOMTools also serves as a CVXPYgen backend, generating and optimizing solvers for parametric CVXPY problems. We demonstrate FOMTools on sparse coding, network optimization, optimal control, and portfolio rebalancing. The verification bounds reveal worst-case behavior that sampling misses. The generated solvers run up to two orders of magnitude faster than NumPy implementations, and they outperform hand-written GPU code and the OSQP solvers generated by CVXPYgen.

title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
abstract: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.

title: A two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$
abstract: We show that a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ carries a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$; the ``if'' half is the Andô's theorem. For each of the remaining spaces we exhibit an explicit non-normal $Y \in \mathcal{M}_2$, with $(I,Y)$ an extreme point of the associated matrix ball, for which the induced linear map is contractive but not completely contractive. Since every two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has the $2$-summing property, the $2$-summing property does not imply uniqueness of the operator space structure for two dimensional complex Banach spaces.

title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
abstract: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $δ\in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-δ}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_δ((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.

title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

title: The Structure of the Ghost and Swapping Algebras
abstract: The swapping algebras and the ghost algebras were introduced in the papers of Labourie and Bridgeman--Labourie to encode the Poisson structure on spaces of length functions and generalized cross-ratio functions associated to $Θ$-Anosov representations. They used these algebras to show that correlation functions are stable under the Poisson bracket associated to Atiyah-Bott-Goldman's symplectic form and that length functions are convex along the Hamiltonian flow of other length functions. In this paper, we study the algebraic relationship between these two algebras. In particular, we show that the kernel of a natural surjection from the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra is generated by five families of relations. Consequently, we obtain an isomorphism from an explicit quotient of the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra.

title: On Diophantine tuples involving star numbers
abstract: In this paper, we discuss two related Diophantine tuple problems involving star numbers $S_n=6n(n-1)+1$. First, we investigate classical $D(k)$-tuples whose elements are star numbers. We construct infinitely many $D(k)$-pairs for several positive and negative admissible values of $k$, and we prove several nonexistence results for $D(k)$-triples and quadruples. Second, we introduce a modified notion of a star number $D(k)$-tuple, requiring $a_ia_j+k$ itself to be a star number. We construct several infinite families of $D(1)$-triples, and study their extensions to quadruples. In particular, we prove that $\{4,108,165\}$ has the unique extension $\{4,108,165,360\}$ to a star number $D(1)$-quadruple. The main tools used in this paper are generalized Pell equations, Nagell's theorem, lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms due to Matveev and Dujella-Pethő version of the Baker-Davenport reduction method in diophantine approximation.

title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet
abstract: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.

title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps
abstract: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. In contrast to direct policy optimization, which repeatedly differentiates the objective through the entire time-discretized dynamics, our method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement by explicitly incorporating state-sensitivity information from the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. For a fixed Markov control, we first compute pathwise adjoint labels by backpropagating the reward through time along simulated state trajectories, and project these labels onto the Markov state through a supervised regression step. The control is then updated by enforcing the pointwise Hamiltonian stationarity condition. We prove that the resulting projected adjoint process satisfies a discrete-time Pontryagin principle and converges, as the time step tends to zero, to the solution of the corresponding continuous-time adjoint backward stochastic differential equation. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy, stability, and scalability of the approach.

title: Symmetric Polynomials Method for the Multiple Loewner Chains
abstract: We introduce the technique of Symmetric Polynomials in the study of Loewner chains driven by a family of stochastic particle systems including but not limited to Dyson Brownian motion. As a first application of this technique we obtain the phase transitions at the critical parameter $κ=4$ in terms of the behavior of a class of symmetric polynomials evolving in time. We obtain new proofs of the phase transitions, we also obtain new closed-form expressions relevant for the models. In addition, we apply this method for some initial deterministic multiple Loewner evolutions. Finally, as this is, to our knowledge, the first paper analyzing this method in the context of multiple Loewner chains driven by root-system based multivariate processes, we also give an overview of potential future applications of this technique in the study of these models.

title: Upper tail probability estimates of suprema of Gaussian processes by matrices-A number theoretic example
abstract: We prove new lower bounds for the upper tail probabilities of suprema of Gaussian processes. We introduce a proper matrix approach. This is continuing recent works of the author on deviations of suprema and decoupling inequalities for parametrized families of Gaussian processes. An application is given to a number theoretic example related to Wintner random Möbius function.

title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
abstract: We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[ \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3α_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(α_n+β_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly. The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.

title: The Riemann zeta function at the zeros of real-rooted trigonometric polynomials
abstract: Let $P$ be a trigonometric polynomial with only real zeros. We prove that at most $\frac{2}{3}$ of its zeros coincide with the zeros of the Riemann zeta function $ζ(s)$ on the critical line. We also show that \begin{equation*} \sup_{\substack{T\leq x\leq2T\\ P(x)=0}} \log \left|ζ\left(\frac{1}{2}+ix\right)\right| \geq (1+o(1))\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{6\log\log T}}. \end{equation*} These results extend the corresponding theorems of Li and Radziwill on the zeros of $ζ(s)$ along vertical arithmetic progressions. The main novelty in our approach is the use of the work of Kurasov and Sarnak and Lee-Yang representations of Alon-Cohen-Vinzant, which show that the corresponding measure $\sum_{P(γ)=0} {\bf δ}_γ$ is crystalline.

title: Logarithmic corrections and interacting fronts in shifting environments and competition systems
abstract: We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.

title: Geodesics in the continuous Hecke monoid
abstract: A permuton is a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals, the limit shape of a sequence of permutations. The sticky product of permutons is a continuous analogue of the Demazure product in the $0$-Hecke monoid; on copulas, the distribution functions of permutons, it is given by the tropical $(\min,+)$ product $\odot$. We show that every absolutely continuous rotation-invariant probability measure $ρ$ on the plane, which we call the profile, generates a one-parameter family of copulas $C^ρ=\{C^ρ_β\}_{β\in[0,π]}$. A copula in this family is defined by a pair of projections of a $ρ$-distributed random vector onto directions at angle $π-β$. Along this family, the sticky product adds angles: $$C^ρ_{β_1}\odot C^ρ_{β_2}=C^ρ_{\min(β_1+β_2,π)}.$$ Hence every non-identity element of such a family is a sticky product of two others and has roots of every natural degree. The normalized inversion number of the copula $C^ρ_β$ equals $β/π$. For the Archimedean measure $\mathfrak{Arch}$ the family $C^{\mathfrak{Arch}}$ consists of the limit shapes of the permutations of the uniformly random sorting network, found by Angel et al. and Dauvergne. For the Gaussian measure $\mathcal{N}$ the family $C^{\mathcal{N}}$ consists of Gaussian copulas and contains $\mathit{Unif}$, the uniform measure on the square (the limit shape of the uniformly random permutation); its square root within this family is the Gaussian copula with correlation $-1/\sqrt2$. By the Herschel-Maxwell theorem the Gaussian measure is the only profile whose family contains $\mathit{Unif}$; nevertheless, $\mathit{Unif}$ has another, singular, sticky square root. A discrete analogue of the Gaussian family is the geometric sorting network generated by rotating independent Gaussian points: after rotation by $π/2$ its permutation is exactly uniform.
comment: 19 pages, 5 figures. A Russian version is available from the authors on request

title: Global Dynamics and Periodic-Annulus Bifurcations in a Reversible Quintic Liénard System
abstract: We study the global dynamics and bifurcations of the reversible quintic Liénard system $\dot{x}=y$, $\dot{y}=a_0x+a_1x^3+a_2x^5+y(b_0x+b_1x^3)$, with $a_2\ne0$. In the original five-parameter space we treat both signs of $a_2$ and determine all global phase-portrait types on the Poincaré disc with one, three, or five finite equilibria. The analysis covers generic and generalized pitchfork, saddle-node, Bogdanov--Takens, and Hopf bifurcations; nilpotent and Hamiltonian degeneracies; bifurcations at infinity; and homoclinic, heteroclinic, limit-cycle-breaking, and periodic-annulus-breaking transitions. For a parameterized class of generalized polynomial Liénard systems whose unique finite equilibrium is the nilpotent origin with exactly one elliptic and one hyperbolic sector we establish a unique critical value of the higher-order damping parameter in the intermediate-degree range, nonexistence of a large-scale periodic annulus in the critical-degree case, and its persistence when the restoring degree dominates. Here large-scale means that the annulus closure meets the boundary of the Poincaré disc. In the degree range relevant to the quintic system the critical value gives a large-scale periodic-annulus--homoclinic-orbit-family bifurcation marked by a unique separatrix connection to infinity. For the quintic system with multiple finite equilibria periodic-annulus-breaking bifurcations arise from finite separatrix connections or separatrices reaching equilibria at infinity. Using Poincaré compactification, local normal forms, rotated vector fields, and separatrix arguments we describe bifurcation sets algebraically or by uniquely characterized critical functions. We obtain complete fixed-coefficient parameter partitions outside $Ω_{14}$ and determine the admissible critical-surface configurations and their phase portraits inside it.

title: Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups and Kneser neighbours
abstract: We study Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups of even unimodular lattices of signature $(n,2)$ which arise as lifts of elliptic modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on 1-dimensional cusps. When the weight is small they have to be defined by analytic continuation. In general, they will be smooth but non-holomorphic after regularization. We show exactly in which cases we obtain holomorphic modular forms by computing the intertwining factors appearing in Langlands' constant term formula in terms of standard parameters and Rankin-Selberg $L$-values. This is related to Kneser's neighbour theory of positive-definite even lattices, which also governs the eigenvalues of these Eisenstein series. In particular, we describe the space of singular weight modular forms and construct the function $Φ_{12}$, the denominator function of the Fake Monster Algebra, as an Eisenstein series. We apply these results to show that the corresponding orthogonal modular varieties are of general type.

title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
abstract: In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms. For the Sobolev inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequality of Hang and Wang [30] (Int. Math. Res. Not., 2022) to a sharp one at $p=2$ under vanishing moment constraints of orders $m=1,2,3$. We also prove a general failure principle: if the unconstrained sharp Sobolev inequality fails, then the corresponding sharp improved inequality under moment constraints fails as well. For the Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequality, we sharpen the almost sharp inequalities of Chang and Hang [10] and Hang [29] (Comm. Pure Appl. Math., 2022) to a sharp improved inequality at the critical order $s=\frac{n}{2}$ under arbitrary finite-order moment constraints. We further investigate the best remainder constant. In contrast with the two-dimensional first-moment case of Gui and Moradifam [28] (Invent. Math., 2018), where the best remainder vanishes, we show that it is positive in several higher-dimensional regimes. We also obtain quantitative remainder estimates for general almost sharp improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities, which in turn yield sharp inequalities at different scales. We further extend recent second-moment refinements to higher dimensions and higher orders. Finally, we obtain analogous results on sharpness, non-sharpness, and quantitative remainder estimates for improved Sobolev-type inequalities under symmetry constraints on general smooth closed manifolds.
comment: This manuscript has been submitted on September 17th

title: Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
abstract: In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any $n \ge k-1\ge 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_k^n$ for some $c_k<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k \ge 3$.

title: Convergence of the critical probabilities for stopping near the top of a random walk
abstract: Let \((S_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a Bernoulli random walk with \(P(X_i=1)=p\) and \(P(X_i=-1)=q=1-p\), and let \(M_n=\max\{S_0,\ldots,S_n\}\). We consider the semi-best selection problem of maximizing \(P(M_N-S_τ\le1)\) over stopping times \(τ\le N\). Allaart showed that the optimal decision in the critical state \((n,1)\) is determined by critical probabilities \(p_n\), and conjectured that \(p_n\to1/2\). In this note, we prove this conjecture. For every fixed \(p<1/2\), the stopping value converges to \(ν=1-(p/q)^2\), while the continuation value converges to \(2pν\). Since \(2pν<ν\), stopping is optimal in state \((n,1)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Together with the known bound \(p_n<1/2\) for \(n\ge4\), this yields \(\lim_{n\to\infty}p_n=1/2\).
comment: 5 pages. Resolves a conjecture of Allaart on the critical probabilities for the semi-best selection problem

title: Critical Growth for Stochastic Adaptive Stabilization with an Unknown Input Gain
abstract: This paper studies adaptive stabilization of a class of scalar discrete-time nonlinear systems with unknown drift coefficients and an unknown nonzero input gain. Under iid Gaussian noise, we establish a necessary and sufficient polynomial criterion for global stabilizability, characterizing the admissible combinations of growth exponents. When the criterion holds, we construct a feedback combining finite calibration with adaptive control. The time average of the squared output converges almost surely to the noise variance, attaining the smallest possible value. If the criterion fails, then for every Borel causal feedback there exist fixed parameter values and an initial state for which the output magnitude diverges with positive probability.

title: Weighted potential and Green systems with Dini coefficients and primitive growth
abstract: We prove a nonexistence theorem for positive potential systems with continuous coefficients satisfying distributional Euler lower bounds and a uniform Dini modulus on normalized logarithmic dilations. The nonlinearities have positive lower logarithmic derivatives and positive primitive-to-endpoint ratios. The common radial kernel is comparable with a Riesz kernel. A localized transport identity, a primitive pressure estimate and implicit amplitude normalization give uniform local energy bounds and a dilation contradiction. And we treats the genuine Green kernel of $-Δ+V$ for nonnegative potentials under annular and Newton composition budgets and a strict gap corrected by the relative Green dilation defect. Relative endpoint differences and an exact virtual-energy cancellation retain local nonlinear energy as the only initial energy hypothesis. Independent representation arguments give these consequences, including even integer orders without initial tails. A compact family of normalized responses also yields universal interior bounds without regular variation.

title: Direct Sample-Average Learning for Queueing Control: Gradient-Free Top-$K$ Coarse-to-Fine Optimization
abstract: We study steady-state queueing control when decisions must be learned from a single persistent operating trajectory: only the implemented action produces data, and the queue is not reset when the action changes. Fixed-event-count cycles yield a direct ratio-of-totals sample-average approximation (SAA) of each action's steady-state cost rate. A Top-K coarse-to-fine search ranks these estimates, retains several promising refinement paths, and concentrates later operation on finer candidate sets, without requiring gradients, convexity, or differentiability. We decompose direct-SAA error into accumulated conditional transient bias and martingale fluctuation. For regenerative queues, a bias-function representation reduces transient effects within contiguous action blocks to boundary terms. Finite-sample stagewise bounds then link estimation accuracy to master-grid identification through guardian retention, and the required queueing and sampling conditions are verified for a persistent-workload M/M/1 implementation. At a common active set, Top-K has a weakly larger guardian margin than Top-1, and an exact-objective example shows Top-1 can discard the optimal refinement branch. Numerical experiments delineate scope rather than universal dominance: Top-K improves terminal identification in the reported LiQUAR and mixed staffing comparisons, while LiQUAR can have lower cumulative learning cost, and GOLiQ is markedly stronger on a smooth benchmark with reliable queueing sensitivities. Direct ranking is therefore best viewed as a complementary method when model-specific gradients are unavailable, inconvenient, or poorly matched to the decision space.

title: A study of the $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances with a special emphasis on $C_{ab}$ curves
abstract: In the seminal paper [13], Farrán and Munuera introduced a method to establish generic information on the $m$th Feng-Rao distance via a function on arbitrary numerical semigroups that serves as a lower bound on the generalized Hamming weights of dual one-point algebraic geometry codes whenever the semigroup is Weierstrass. In the present paper, we study what we shall call the primary and dual, respectively, $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances, which serve as lower bounds on relative generalized Hamming weights of nested primary and dual, respectively, one-point codes under similar condition. A unified method for establishing generic formulas for $m$th relative Feng-Rao distances of general numerical semigroups is developed and for a large variety of numerical semigroups generated by two elements, closed formula expressions are established complementing Delgado et al.s work [8] on the $m$th Feng-Rao distances of such semigroups. Finally, for non-singular $C_{ab}$ curves, we develop a method to estimate the $m$th relative generalized Hamming weight of dual and primary one-point codes in those regions where the generic methods may fail to provide best possible results.

title: An Extension of Galvin's Theorem Related to the Banach-Mazur Game
abstract: Let $X$ be a topological space. Galvin's theorem on the Banach-Mazur game states that if $X$ has a $π$-base $\mathcal{B}$ satisfying the following condition: \textit{For any $U \in \mathcal{B}$, there exists a disjoint family $\mathcal{A}_U$ of nonempty open subsets of $U$ such that} \[ |\mathcal{A}_U| \geq |\{ B \in \mathcal{B} : U \subseteq B \}|, \] then, in the Banach-Mazur game on $X$, the second player, denoted NONEMPTY, has a 2-tactic if NONEMPTY has a winning strategy in this game. In this paper, we extend the disjointness condition of this family by replacing it with the condition of being open finite family. With this extension of the family $\mathcal{A}_U$, we showed that, the theorem is also true.

title: Deviation probabilities for global events in two dimensions (I): independent excursions
abstract: We consider the field of local times generated by independent excursions of the two-dimensional simple random walk between the boundaries of two concentric disks, and study global events: informally, these are the events that have to occur everywhere (i.e., if such an event occurs on a set, then it also occurs on all its subsets). Examples include ``the set is completely covered'', ``the maximal local time on the set does not exceed a given level'', or ``the set does not contain a covered disk of a given radius''. For monotone global events, we show that the deviation probabilities (i.e., the probabilities that the event occurs with atypically few excursions, or does not occur with atypically many of them, or vice versa) can be obtained from the typical behaviour on different scales only, via a general decoupling argument based on soft local times.

title: Average lower bound on magnetic double-well tunneling with asymptotically large well separation
abstract: We study tunneling between two identical, smooth, compactly supported potential wells in a constant perpendicular magnetic field, with the coupling and magnetic field fixed and the well separation tending to infinity. For a sufficiently small positive magnetic field, we prove lower bounds on the hopping coefficient and on the splitting of the two lowest eigenvalues outside a set of separations of density zero. If the well centers are separated by $2d_1$ and the magnetic field strength is $bλ$, the lower bounds have the form $e^{-bλd_1^2-Cd_1^{1+δ}}$ for every fixed $δ\in(0,1)$. No radial or reflection symmetry of the single-well potential is assumed. The proof combines the explicit Landau resolvent kernel with a complex analytic estimate for logarithmic averages of the hopping coefficient.

title: Rigidity of algebraic sets with small distortion
abstract: We prove that for positive integers $k$, $n$, and $d>1$, there is a maximal $c(k,n,d)>1$ such that if $X \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a connected $k$-dimensional complex algebraic set with degree at most $d$ and $dist(X) < c(k,n,d)$, then $X$ must be a complex affine linear subspace, where $dist(X)$ denotes the distortion of $X$ and is given by the supremum of the ratios $d_{inner}(p, q)/d_{outer}(p, q)$ for all $p,q\in X$ with $p\not= q$. We also prove that $c(1,n,d)=\sqrt{2}$ for any positive integers $k$ and $n$. This result provides a sharp rigidity phenomenon for curves in the $c$-LNE category, showing that near-isometric behavior of the inner and outer metrics forces the curve to be as simple as possible.

title: On the denominators of signed harmonic sums
abstract: Let $\eps=(\eps_i)_{i\ge1}$ be a sequence with $\eps_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and let $v_n(\eps)$ be the positive denominator of $\sum_{i=1}^n\eps_i/i$ in lowest terms. We prove that $|\{1\le n\le x:v_n(\eps)\ne v_{n+1}(\eps)\}|=o(x)$ uniformly in $\eps$. In particular, the set of positive integers $n$ with $v_n(\eps)=v_{n+1}(\eps)$ has asymptotic density one for every sequence of signs. This answers a problem of Wu and Chen, \emph{J. Number Theory} \textbf{200} (2019), 397--406.

title: Approximability of Triangulated Categories under Separable Extensions
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of approximability under separable extensions of triangulated categories. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be an approximable triangulated category and let $\mathbf{T}=(T,θ,μ)$ be a smashing, stably separable exact monad on $\mathcal{B}$. Assume that the category of $\mathbf{T}$-modules $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ admits a canonical triangulated structure. We prove that if $T$ is right $t$-exact with respect to a $t$-structure in the preferred equivalence class of $\mathcal{B}$, then $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is again an approximable triangulated category. As an application, we show that, under suitable assumptions, a smashing localization functor on an approximable triangulated category induces a recollement of approximable triangulated categories, thereby yielding a converse-type result to the gluing theorem of Burke--Neeman--Pauwels. Finally, under suitable hypotheses, we prove that separable extensions restrict naturally to the intrinsic subcategories associated with approximable triangulated categories.

title: Statistical decision theory in thermodynamics
abstract: We introduce statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamic systems. Statistical decision theory integrates several statistical tasks, such as estimation, hypothesis testing, and classification. In this study, we consider statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamics, which unifies sensing, classification, and uncertainty relations. In particular, we focus on the minimax risk, the smallest achievable expected loss under the worst-case parameter choice, even with an optimal estimator. We derive lower bounds on the minimax risk using Le Cam's two-point method. The derived relationships can be used across a broader range of thermodynamic scenarios. To illustrate these relations, we study classification and distribution estimation problems in a Markov process. We demonstrate that the minimax risk provides lower bounds given by the dynamical activity in these problems. Furthermore, by examining particular dynamics, we establish that the resulting bounds simplify to uncertainty relations involving dynamical activity or entropy production.

title: Bootstrap percolation on the hypercube
abstract: In this paper we obtain the critical probability $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ for bootstrap percolation with the infection threshold $r=f(n)n^a$ on the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_{n}$, where $0<a<1$ and $f(n)=n^{o(1)}$. More precisely, we obtain the exact first-order and second-order terms of $p_c(Q_{n},r)$ by extending the main theorem of Balogh, Bollob{á}s, and Morris (2009).
comment: This paper and V5 of arXiv:2503.12607[math.CO] supersede V1-V4 of arXiv:2503.12607[math.CO] as the results have been significantly improved and a main mistake has been fixed

title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=wλ$ for real or octonion $λ$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(wλ_1)λ_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $λ_2λ_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.

title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds
abstract: Neural networks that respect the symmetries of point clouds commonly compute high-order representations of the rotation group to improve their expressivity. Such models are known to be universal, and thus able to separate any pair of point clouds, when using representations of sufficiently high order, yet no precise bound on this order, as a function of the number of points, was previously known. We establish the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations. By showing Tensor Field Networks and MACE can express all invariant polynomials of a given degree with sufficient representation order, we additionally derive the first explicit, quadratic bound on the representation order sufficient for these architectures to be complete, replacing previous existence results with concrete guarantees. We further show that, under local regularity assumptions, point cloud separation can be achieved with a message-passing-based model using invariants whose degree depends only on the size of a local neighborhood, rather than on the size of the full point cloud. Finally, we provide counterexamples showing MACE must compute high order irreducible representations to separate locally regular point clouds.

title: On a problem of Ma and Chen concerning minimal additive complements
abstract: Let $m\geq1$ be an integer and let $W=(m\mathbb N_0+X)\cup U\cup V\subseteq\mathbb Z$ be bounded below, where $X\ne\varnothing$, $[U]_m\subseteq[X]_m$, $[X]_m\cap[V]_m=\varnothing$, and $V$ contains no infinite arithmetic progression with common difference $m$. Here $[S]_m$ denotes the set of residue classes modulo $m$ represented by $S$. Suppose that $W$ satisfies the $\mathcal C$-condition modulo $m$. For $0\leq r<m$, let $V_r=V\cap(r+m\mathbb Z)$, and put $V'=\bigcup_{|V_r|=\infty}V_r$, where the union is over $0\leq r<m$. We prove that $W$ has a minimal additive complement if $V'$ satisfies the big-hole property modulo $m$. This answers a problem posed by Ma and Chen.

title: A robust finite element method for incompressible magnetohydrodynamics using Whitney forms
abstract: A stabilized semi-discrete finite element scheme for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system is presented. The scheme uses the Whitney $2$-form and $1$-form for the fluid velocity and magnetic induction, respectively. The key ingredient is a magnetic curl-jump penalty term, which allows us to prove a pre-asymptotic error estimate of order $O(h^{1/2})$ with a constant depending on solution norms but not explicitly on the fluid viscosity and magnetic diffusivity.

title: A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem
abstract: We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4π$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.

title: Pointwise Wave--Damping for Linearized Vlasov--Poisson: Compactly Supported Radial Equilibria and Relativistic Applications
abstract: We establish weighted pointwise estimates for the response Green function and the complete electric field of the linearized Vlasov--Poisson system in $\mathbb{R}_x^3\times\mathbb{R}_v^3$ around compactly supported radial equilibria. Both decompose into a dispersive wave component with $t^{-3/2}$ decay in $L_x^\infty$ and a faster-decaying Landau-damped component. The wave estimate includes the survival threshold, where the oscillatory branch meets the continuous spectrum, while the damped estimates resolve the spatial fronts associated with the velocity boundaries. The equilibrium class includes shells with independent inner and outer orders of vanishing, down to first order, and profiles positive throughout a velocity ball. The proof combines a joint treatment of pole and continuum contributions with a low-frequency normal form for the electric field. The electric-field estimates hold for real, neutral perturbations with finite weighted regularity and imply uniform scattering along free characteristics. An exact momentum--velocity correspondence for suitable filled-ball profiles yields analogous estimates and scattering for a class of nonnegative relativistic equilibria with polynomial momentum tails.

title: Rational Dyck Excursion Counts as Sums of Generalized Fuss-Catalan Products
abstract: For walks with jumps +p and -q, where p,q are coprime positive integers, we express the weak and strict rational Dyck excursion counts as finite weighted sums of generalized Fuss-Catalan products. Both sums run over the same partitions of q for every path size. Reversing the order of the steps and changing their signs transforms a returning walk with jumps +p and -q into one with jumps +q and -p, with the same heights in reverse order. This preserves both weak and strict excursions. Applying the formulas with p and q exchanged therefore gives sums over partitions of p, so we can choose the smaller of the two jump magnitudes. The indices of the Fuss-Catalan factors satisfy certain divisibility conditions that are determined by the jump magnitudes and the partition parts. The weak formula alternates in sign with the number of parts, whereas every term in the strict formula is positive. We prove both formulas by cutting unrestricted walks at their first and last visits to their lowest height. Expanding the resulting factors produces the partitions of q and the different signs. We also give equivalent binomial convolutions. Multiplying each Fuss-Catalan factor by q in the weak formula or p in the strict formula gives a positive integer. For q=1, the weak and strict counts reduce to Fuss-Catalan and shifted Raney numbers, respectively; for q=2 and q=3, the formulas yield explicit convolution identities.

title: Uniform lower bounds for the average length of finite Pierce expansions
abstract: For integers $1\leq a\leq b$, the length of the finite Pierce expansion of $a/b$ is the number of steps of the iteration $r\mapsto b\bmod r$ which starts at $a$ and ends at zero. Erdős and Shallit (1991) proved that the average of these lengths over $1\leq a\leq b$ is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log b$, and suggested that it is at least of order $\log b$. In this paper, we prove that the average length is at least $\sqrt{2\log b}-3(\log b)^{1/4}-11$ for every $b\geq2$. We also show that, for each $0<c<\sqrt2$, the proportion of numerators $a$ for which the length is less than $c\sqrt{\log b}$ tends to zero exponentially fast in $\sqrt{\log b}$, with an explicit rate. Our approach refines the interval-counting argument of Erdős and Shallit by restricting the product of the initial digits. As applications, we obtain similar bounds for reduced fractions and for numerators in a fixed congruence class.

title: Reduction of structure groups for noncommutative principal bundles
abstract: Let $G$ be a compact group and let $H \subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup. We study reduction of the structure group for noncommutative principal bundles, modelled by free C${}^*$-dynamical systems in the sense of Ellwood. We first describe how induction from $H$ to $G$ behaves on associated correspondences and their tensor structure. Using reconstruction, this leads to a Tannakian characterization of reduction of the structure group in terms of the associated tensor functor. For normal subgroups, we characterize reduction in terms of central equivariant homomorphisms and derive module- and $K$-theoretic obstructions. We conclude with a noncommutative $O(n)$-example which admits no reduction to $SO(n)$.

title: Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications
abstract: Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-Hölder bound for the map sending a Hölder potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.

title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

title: Asymptotic Enumeration of $F$-decompositions in Typical Hypergraphs and of Universal Cycles
abstract: In this paper, we determine the asymptotic number of $F$-decompositions in typical hypergraphs. More precisely, let $F$ be a non-trivial $f$-vertex $k$-graph. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $F$-divisible $(n^{-ζ},h,p)$-typical $k$-graph $G$ has $n^{\frac{f-k+o_n(1)}{|F|}|G|}$ $F$-decompositions. As an application, we asymptotically enumerate universal cycles for $k$-subsets of $[n]$, or equivalently, tight Euler tours of the complete $k$-graph $K_n^k$. For every $k\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying $k\mid {n-1 \choose k-1}$, the number of such universal cycles is $n^{(1-γ(n)){n \choose k}}$, where $0<γ(n)=o_n(1)$. More generally, for $\ell\in[k-1]$, we show that a sufficiently typical $n$-vertex $k$-graph $G$ satisfying the corresponding divisibility condition has $n^{(k-\ell-γ'(n))|G|}$ Euler $\ell$-tours, where $0<γ'(n)=o_n(1)$.

title: Surfaces Associated to Zeros of Automorphic $L$-functions
abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, Montgomery established results concerning pair correlation of zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Rudnick and Sarnak extended these results to automorphic $L$-functions and all level correlations. We discover additional geometric structures associated to the zeros of automorphic $L$-functions. In the case of pair correlation, these structures form certain surfaces which display Gaussian behavior. For triple correlation, these structures exhibit Laplace and Chi-squared distributions, revealing an unexpected phase transition.

title: General Periodic Conservation Laws Motivated by Traffic Modeling
abstract: This paper deals with the well-posedness, in the spatially periodic setting, of a mixed system of nonlocal-local conservation laws modeling traffic flow where autonomous vehicles --- informed on traffic conditions over long distances --- interact with human-driven bulk traffic. We also provide a comprehensive well-posedness theory in the periodic framework separately for general local conservation laws and for systems of nonlocal conservation laws, together with a priori total variation bounds and stability estimates.

title: Powers and Functional Calculus for $m$-Selfadjoint and Skew $m$-Selfadjoint Operators
abstract: We study powers and functional calculi of higher-order selfadjoint and skew higher-order selfadjoint operators on complex Hilbert spaces. First, we compare the behavior of their powers with the corresponding theory for $m$-isometries.
