For $μ\vdash kn$ and $ν\vdash n$, we express the coefficient of $e_ν$ in $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k(e_μ)$ as a normalized sum of positive rational weights over closed walks on a finite directed graph of $k$-restricted partitions. The proof combines the Pieri rule and a root of unity factorization for Macdonald polynomials. As a corollary, we recover the h-positivity of the symmetric functions $A_{n,k}$ of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.

title: Additive invariants of Finite-dimensional DG-algebras
abstract: Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.

title: The rank of the random $k$-XORSAT matrix beyond satisfiability
abstract: The random $k$-XORSAT matrix is an $m\times n$ random matrix $\mathbf A$ over $\mathbb F_2$ that represents a random instance of the $k$-XORSAT problem. Each row of $\mathbf A$ contains precisely $k\geq3$ non-zero entries in random positions. The rows are drawn independently. The matrix $\mathbf A$ is known to have full row rank for $m/n$ below the random $k$-XORSAT satisfiability threshold, which is known explicitly [Dubois, Mandler~2002; Pittel, Sorkin~2016]. Motivated by a problem from quantum game theory and refining a result of Cooper, Frieze and Pegden (2019), we determine the limiting distribution of the rank of $\mathbf A$ beyond the satisfiability threshold.

title: Flip classes and elementary expansions of vertical-strip LLT polynomials
abstract: After the substitution $q\mapsto q+1$, vertical-strip LLT polynomials are weighted sums of strict $P$-partition generating functions indexed by orientations of decorated unit-interval graphs, with weight $q^{\mathrm{asc}(θ)}$. A flip moves an ascending edge across a triangle while keeping its long edge. We show that the sum over every flip class is elementary-positive: it equals the sum of the elementary symmetric functions given by the highest reachable vertices of its orientations. This answers Hwang's question on the Schur positivity of LLT flip-class sums, and it holds for circular unit-interval graphs as well. Summing over classes gives a new proof of the elementary expansion of Alexandersson and Sulzgruber, and its circular analog, which was open. We also obtain a flip-class refinement of the elementary expansion of LLT cumulants.

title: Young Parabolic PDEs and the Martingale Problem for Young SDEs
abstract: Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the martingale problem associated with the hybrid Young--Lyons--Itô differential equation admits a unique solution in the natural class of solutions satisfying Krylov-type estimates, thereby establishing probabilistic weak well-posedness. Our proof relies on an analysis of the associated Kolmogorov equations, which are Young-type parabolic PDEs with irregular coefficients. The resulting theory for such Young-type parabolic PDEs is also of independent interest.

title: The Wandering Must Continue: Pure Mathematicians as Rangers of the North
abstract: Pure mathematics is an honest barometer of a civilization's scientific capacity, maintaining an unwritten culture of rigor, intellectual honesty, and precision whose primary service is not merely theorems, but human judgment. In an era of automated theorem generation and formal verification, this essay argues that establishing a result and understanding why it holds remain distinct achievements that require deliberate institutional protection.

title: Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups
abstract: We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2ν_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2ν_n(G)=0\), and \(π_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.

title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.

title: Efimov effect in an internal spectral gap of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian
abstract: We prove the existence of an Efimov sequence in an internal gap of the essential spectrum of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian. The system consists of two identical spinless fermions and one distinguishable particle on \(\Z^3\), with repulsive pair interactions. For each fixed fermion-to-third-particle mass ratio \(γ>γ_*\approx13.6069657\) and total quasi-momentum near \(π\mathbf1\), the mixed zero-range coupling is tuned to a simultaneous upper-threshold resonance. Sufficiently strong nearest-neighbour repulsion between the fermions separates the upper fermion-pair two-cluster spectrum from the free three-particle band. Infinitely many discrete eigenvalues accumulate at the lower endpoint of the resulting gap, which coincides with the free upper edge. We establish logarithmic eigenvalue-counting asymptotics with the same positive coefficient as at zero fermion--fermion coupling. This coefficient also governs accumulation above the essential spectrum throughout the closed weak-coupling interval, including its critical endpoint. We classify the channel spectrum near the free upper edge for all nonnegative fermion couplings.

title: Singular Stability Estimates for Passive Gamma Emission Tomography of Spent Nuclear Fuel
abstract: We study the joint recovery of attenuation and source coefficients from the attenuated X-ray transform, motivated by passive gamma emission tomography of spent nuclear fuel. Both coefficients are constant on known, disjoint disks of equal radius representing fuel rods. The surrounding moderator has known attenuation and zero source. We use tangential singularities of the data to give a sufficient condition on the geometry and coefficients for unique joint reconstruction from full data. For rods arranged on parallel rows separated by more than one rod diameter, with source coefficients uniformly bounded away from zero, we derive explicit reconstruction formulas and stability estimates for both coefficients. The estimates use a singular seminorm determined by two functionals per rod, computed from angular data near selected tangencies. Numerical experiments examine the approximation of these functionals from discretized data.

title: Sphere Theorems for $\frac{10}{3}$-Positive Curvature Operator of the Second Kind
abstract: In this paper, we prove that every connected closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq4$ with $\frac{10}{3}$-positive curvature operator of the second kind is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We also obtain a classification of connected closed Riemannian manifolds with $\frac{10}{3}$-nonnegative curvature operator of the second kind. The key step is to show that $\frac{10}{3}$-positivity implies the PIC1 condition. Finally, we give an example showing that $\frac{10}{3}$ is optimal for deducing PIC1 from $α$-positivity.

title: Hadamard well-posedness and nonuniform dependence for the incompressible free-boundary ideal MHD equations
abstract: We prove local Hadamard well-posedness for the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations without surface tension under the Taylor sign condition. For every $5/2<s<4$, the result holds on bounded fluid domains whose closures are diffeomorphic to the closed ball, with the velocity, magnetic field, and boundary in the standard $H^s$ spaces. No additional regularity in the magnetic direction is required. The proof rests on a fourth order geometric energy inequality whose coefficients are controlled by these $H^s$ norms, the fixed geometric bounds, and the Taylor lower bound. A harmonic extension of the boundary normal provides the coefficient control needed at this regularity. We also prove that, near every admissible initial state and at each positive time in a common local existence interval, the Eulerian solution map is not uniformly continuous on any nonempty open subset of a sufficiently small data neighborhood. The construction combines localized magnetic oscillations prescribed at the observation time with time reversal and Galilean translations.

title: Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz-based convergence analysis with approximate weakly convex subdifferentials: bundle, quadratic penalty, and moving balls approximation methods
abstract: The Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) property has been widely used for establishing global sequential convergence and analyzing local convergence rate of optimization algorithms. Most existing analysis frameworks rely on the construction of a suitable KL potential function such that along the sequence generated, it admits sufficient descents and its exact subdifferentials are suitably controlled by successive changes of the iterates. Nevertheless, a handful of important algorithms, such as bundle methods and quadratic penalty methods, are not known to have potential functions verifying the aforementioned properties, rendering their convergence analysis out of the reach of existing KL-based convergence analysis template. In this paper, we develop a new convergence analysis framework to extend the applicability of KL-based analysis. Our framework is built on a weakly convex KL potential function $ψ$. It allows approximate sufficient descents, the use of diminishing stepsizes, and controls on enlarged subdifferentials of $ψ$ known as the $\varrho$-weakly-convex-$\varepsilon$-subdifferentials. We illustrate the usefulness of our framework by establishing the global sequential convergence and analyzing the local convergence rate of some recent variants of bundle method, quadratic penalty method and moving balls approximation method. Specifically, we show that these methods fall under our framework by presenting explicit and natural choices of $ψ$, and derive suitable choices of model parameters, penalty parameters and constraint shrinkage parameters, respectively, for establishing their global sequential convergence and local convergence rate based on the KL property and exponent of $ψ$.

title: Structural aspects of $1$-limited domination in cubic graphs
abstract: A set $D\subseteq V(G)$ is a $1$-limited dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $D$ has a neighbor in $D$ and every vertex of $D$ has at most one neighbor outside $D$. The minimum cardinality among all $1$-limited dominating sets of $G$ is denoted by $γ_1^{\mathrm L}(G)$. For every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$, there exists a nonnegative integer $t$ such that $γ_1^{\mathrm L}(G)=\frac n2+t$. We establish structural properties of $1$-limited dominating sets in terms of $t$ and use them to study the induced cycles vertex number, that is, the maximum number of vertices inducing a $2$-regular subgraph. As applications, we determine the exact $1$-limited domination numbers of generalized Blanuša snarks and flower snarks.

title: Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations
abstract: We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.

title: Two pointwise estimates for singular integral operators over p-adic groups
abstract: We establish some new pointwise boundedness properties for rough singular integral operators defined over p-adic groups. The properties of these operator rely essentially on the behavior of their rough kernels and we will present two different cases that fall outside the setting of the classical Calder{ó}n-Zygmund setting.

title: Families that intersect in an arithmetic progression
abstract: For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $μ_n$ be the uniform measure on $2^{[n]}$. A family $\mathcal F \subseteq2^{[n]}$ is called $k$-AP-intersecting if $F_1\cap F_2$ contains a nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression for every $F_1, F_2\in\mathcal F$. Writing $m_k$ for the supremum of $μ_n(\mathcal F)$ over all $n$ and all such families $\mathcal F$, we prove \[ 2^{-k}\le m_k\le32\cdot 2^{-k}\qquad(k\ge3). \] This greatly improves a recent result of Gillott, who proved that $m_k \leq k^{-1/3}$ for all sufficiently large $k$, and answers his question on $m_k$'s exponential decay. We also prove a similar bound for the corresponding cross-intersection problem.

title: The resource cost of cooperative invasion
abstract: A contact network can favor cooperation by sheltering a lineage until its descendants compete with defectors as a group. We determine the contact strengths, invasion times and measurement effort needed to realize this advantage at fixed population size. Individuals reproduce according to averaged cooperation payoffs, and offspring replace neighbors through contacts of equal weight in both directions. Contact contrast is the ratio of strongest to weakest contact. Under weak selection on a six-site path, the least contrast needed to favor a single cooperator over the reverse invasion by a defector grows as $656ε^{-2}$ for uniformly placed mutants and $4050ε^{-3}$ for mutations in newborn offspring, as the benefit-cost ratio $b/c=1+ε$ approaches one. The extra power arises because rare replacement protects a site while suppressing mutation arrival there. Global bounds force two weakly coupled groups and exact mirror symmetry of the least-contrast contacts for sufficiently small $ε$. Under uniform introduction, additional contrast shortens the leading mean time to extinction or fixation in the absence of selection, from $12/ε$ toward $6/ε$ reproduction attempts, and eventually breaks the mirror symmetry of the fastest design. Estimating the uniform-introduction advantage from fixation outcomes of independent completed invasions defines a third optimum. Within the six-site family with mirror-symmetric, strongly separated contacts, we optimize contacts and selection strength with reproduction weighted linearly or exponentially by payoff. At fixed relative precision, with contrast a fixed factor above its minimum, the leading summed trial duration grows as $ε^{-3}$. Efficient measurement accepts a smaller advantage in exchange for shorter trials. The cheapest, fastest and most efficiently measured networks therefore differ.

title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
abstract: We prove the conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin: for a non-constant inner function $θ$, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_θ$ has a bounded symbol if and only if $θ$ is one-component

title: Entropy and periodic points in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes
abstract: Let $f$ be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g$ isotopic to $f$, the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ if and only if $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, $α>0$, we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the $C^0$ topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.
comment: 29 pages. Includes Appendix "Dynamics in the isotopy class of a pseudo-Anosov map" by the last three authors

title: Input-to-Output Stability and Consensus Control of Opinion Dynamics on Graph State-Space
abstract: This paper proposes a modeling of opinion dynamics in social systems with evolving structures on the Graph State-Space. It builds upon the Hegselmann-Krause (HK) model with variable influence weights, integrated into a hybrid dynamical systems framework where structural changes (agent addition/removal) are induced by inputs. We establish an Inputto-Output Stability (IOS) result under a strong connectivity assumption, using a nonsmooth Lyapunov function based on the opinion diameter; we show that the consensus expansion is then bounded by the maximal deviation of incoming agents relative to the existing convex hull. Assuming constant influence weights, we propose a consensus control result via agent injection in the social system. The results of this paper initiate, to the best of our knowledge, the analysis of resilience, stability, and control of dynamic systems on Graph State-Space.

title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.

title: Hybrid metaheuristics for architectural design optimization under small evaluation and wall-clock budgets
abstract: Architectural and structural design optimization in parametric software affords about a thousand evaluations of an expensive model for problems with tens of variables, a regime for which most metaheuristics were not designed. On the side of artificial intelligence, two hybrid metaheuristics are proposed: a covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) whose sampling is enriched with differential-evolution trial vectors, and a particle swarm with success-history parameter adaptation, differential-evolution injection and local refinement. A budget-aware delay of population-size reduction in adaptive differential evolution is also proposed. Under a hard cap of 1,200 evaluations, all counted, the CMA-ES hybrid ranks first on seven shifted and rotated functions at 10 and 30 variables and beats CMA-ES on six of seven functions at 30 variables. Ablations attribute this gain to the injection and show that a local search pays off only when its result re-enters the population. The delayed schedule improves three adaptive differential-evolution variants in 40 of 51 comparisons, with no loss. On the side of engineering application, in Grasshopper the CMA-ES hybrid and plain CMA-ES are never significantly worse than the optimizers of Galapagos, SilverEye, Opossum and Tunny on travelling-salesman instances and on a built 85-variable free-form shell, where they end 48 % below the best external tool in 15 minutes. On a 22-variable building-performance problem with binary choices, differential evolution leads instead. Shifting and rotating the functions reverses the rank of Harris hawks optimization. Solvers should therefore be selected by problem structure and stopping time, not by a single ranking.

title: Simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalences for tensor categories
abstract: In this paper, we investigate monoidal derived equivalences between tensor categories with infinitely many isomorphism classes of simple objects. We introduce the notion of a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence and prove that a simple-shifted monoidal derived equivalence gives rise to a tensor equivalence. In addition, we investigate which tensor categories have the property that every monoidal derived equivalence between them is necessarily simple-shifted, and we establish some sufficient conditions for this property. As a corollary, we prove that if a tensor category is monoidally derived equivalent to the finite-dimensional representation category of either the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, the quantized Borel subalgebra $U_q^{\geq 0}(\mathfrak{g})$, or the quantized coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}_{q}(G)$ (for a suitable $q$), it is tensor equivalent to the corresponding category.
comment: 20 pages,comments welcome. We have added a new Section 5 to the paper

title: Geographic spread of vector borne diseases in periodic heterogeneous environments
abstract: We consider a reaction-diffusion system that arises in epidemiology to describe the spatial spread of a vector borne disease. Our model is a coupled version of the classical SIR model of Kermack and McKendrick. We study the long-time behavior of the solutions, giving optimal criteria on the propagation or extinction of the disease, and compute the asymptotic speed of spread of solutions, which is given by a Freidlin-G{ä}rtner type formula. We also give some qualitative properties of the model, which yield information on the influence of the parameters on the system's long-time behavior. In particular, we identify the limit of the spreading speed when the diffusions are very large, and we show that the system behaves in this case similarly to a homogenized system.

title: Pellarin Values from Cauchy Coordinates on Arbitrary Curves
abstract: Let $A$ be the ring of functions regular outside a closed point of degree $\mathrm{N}$ on a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We express the normalized weight-one ideal Pellarin value of a rank-one Drinfeld $A$-module as an ordinary Hilbert-class trace of rational Cauchy differentials. A pairing on projective period lattices identifies the differential associated with each ideal class and computes its coefficients by finite torsion traces. For a nonfree lattice, the formula uses an isogeny with arbitrary nonzero derivative to a module with free period lattice. Each ideal-class subseries extends regularly to the characteristic point with value one, so the full series takes the value $|\operatorname{Cl}(A)|$. For every rank-one module, the quotient of the Anderson generating differential by the Drinfeld exponential is a meromorphic lattice sum whose value at zero is the Cauchy differential. Its Taylor coefficients give the higher-weight lattice differentials. For sign-normalized Hayes modules with free period lattice, an ordinary Hilbert-class trace after projection to powers divisible by $q^{\mathrm{N}}-1$ generates ideal values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q^{\mathrm{N}}-1}$. An algebraic parameter rescaling gives a trace formula for character-twisted values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q-1}$. The exact coefficient fields explain the difference between these weight ranges. For sign-normalized modules, decomposition by ideal classes also relates the element-type and ideal-type series at every positive weight. Explicit computations include the Hu--Huang--Yau module with nonprincipal period lattice and an elliptic curve with an infinite point of degree three, including the holomorphic term of its Cauchy differential. At rational infinity, the elliptic formula recovers the Green--Papanikolas identity.

title: On the hyperplane conjecture
abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

title: Sign-changing bubbling solutions on polygons for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in high dimensions
abstract: We consider the Brezis--Nirenberg problem $-Δu = |u|^{2^{*}-2}u + \varepsilon u$ in a smooth bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$, $N \geq 5$, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where $\varepsilon > 0$ is small. Two multi-peak configurations found in dimension four in \cite{PRV2} persist. In an annulus, for every even $k \geq 2$, we construct solutions blowing up at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon with alternating signs. In the ball, we construct solutions blowing up positively at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon in a coordinate plane and negatively at those of a regular $k$-gon in an orthogonal plane, for $2 \leq k \leq 5$ if $N = 5,6$ and $2 \leq k \leq 4$ if $N \geq 7$. This range is sharp: for larger $k$ no such solution exists with parameters in a compact set, while otherwise the reduced energy has a unique, non-degenerate critical point.

title: Ramsey expansions of $S$-metric spaces
abstract: Let $S\subseteq \mathbb R^+$ be a subset of positive reals. We say that a metric space is an $S$-metric space if the range of the metric is a subset of $S\cup \{0\}$. In 2007, Delhommé, Laflamme, Pouzet, and Sauer characterized those sets $S$ for which the class of all finite $S$-metric spaces has the amalgamation property. Given an amalgamation class, a natural question is what its Ramsey expansion is. Ramsey expansions are known for classes of $S$-metric spaces for which $S\cup\{0\}$ carries a natural distance monoid structure, for example for $S=\mathbb Q^+$ or when $S$ is topologically closed. In this paper, we extend this result to all amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces, thereby completing the Ramsey-theoretic classification of amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces.

title: A Matlab/Octave package for photometric stereo 3D reconstruction
abstract: The photometric stereo model allows the construction of 3D virtual replicas of real objects from images acquired under different light conditions. The assumptions of this model are strongly restrictive and are seldom fully satisfied in applications. Indeed, the surface of the observed objects may deviate from ideal conditions, and the geometry of the scene is often only an approximation of the one assumed by the model. Additionally, real-world surfaces may present reflection phenomena, which introduce distortions in reconstructions. In this paper, we present a revised version of the Matlab package \ttt{\small ps3d}~\cite{cdfrv21}, developed to implement the photometric stereo model under various conditions. The new package contains various extensions, the most notable one is the presence of an alternative model to address the presence of a reflective object surface. In addition, it implements particular metrics to analyze the compliance of a dataset to model assumptions, and it is compatible with GNU Octave. The tool allows users to test the model under different observation configurations, also in presence of reflection, using either synthetic or experimental data.

title: Critical functions and asymptotics for fractional Hartree Brezis--Nirenberg problems in low dimensions
abstract: We study the Brezis--Nirenberg problem for the fractional Laplacian with an upper critical Hartree nonlinearity on a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^N$, in the low-dimensional range $2s<N<4s$. For a continuous potential $a$, we prove that the following properties are equivalent: the Robin function of $(-Δ)^s+a$ is negative somewhere in $Ω$; the associated Hartree--Sobolev quotient ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)$ lies strictly below the best constant ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}$; and ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)$ is attained. This leads to the notion of a critical potential, for which ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)={\mathcal S_{H,s}}$ and every nontrivial decrease of $a$ lowers the infimum. For a critical potential $a$ and $V\in L^\infty(Ω)$, we determine the leading term in the asymptotics of ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a+\varepsilon V)$ as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ and describe the blow-up of almost-minimizers, including the concentration speed and the location of the concentration point. Compared with the Sobolev case, the nonlocal nonlinearity produces several new interaction terms; a key ingredient is a proof of non-attainment at the threshold based on the sharp Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality on the sphere.

title: Least singular values of Gaussian matrices with deterministic shifts
abstract: Let $A$ be a deterministic real square matrix and $G$ a standard Gaussian matrix. We determine $\E\smin(A+G)$, up to universal constants, in terms of the singular values of $A$. The expectation is comparable to the square root of the smallest zero of the expected characteristic polynomial of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$. This resolves Problem~3 in Tikhomirov's ICM 2022 survey. We also prove that the zeros of the expected characteristic polynomial are majorized by the expected ordered eigenvalues of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$.

title: A unified Carleman approach to inverse problems for coupled parabolic and hyperbolic-ODE equations
abstract: We study inverse coefficient problems for two evolution equations with relaxation: a Kelvin--Voigt viscoelastic equation and the Moore--Gibson--Thompson (MGT) equation arising in nonlinear acoustics. In both cases, we establish the Lipschitz stability for recovering a space-dependent coefficient from a single measurement. Our approach exploits an exact factorization of each operator into a classical evolution operator (the heat operator for the viscoelastic system, or the wave operator for the MGT equation) coupled with a first-order differential operator in time. This makes it possible to combine global Carleman estimates with weighted ODE inequalities. For the Kelvin--Voigt model, the data consist of an interior dynamic observation and a Cauchy snapshot at a prescribed positive time. For the MGT equation, a single boundary trace is sufficient under a standard geometric condition. The resulting argument provides a common framework for coefficient inverse problems in evolution equations with relaxation effects.

title: $L^p$-Khinchin sequences and transference principles
abstract: A sequence \((λ_n)_{n\ge1}\) of distinct positive integers is called an \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequence, where $1\le p\le\infty$, if $ n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n f(λ_k x) \longrightarrow \int_{\mathbb T}f\,d\mathfrak m $ a.e. $x\in\mathbb T$ for every \(f\in L^p(\mathbb T)\). When $1\le p<\infty$, we characterize the \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequences by a weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality for the associated averaging operators. We also establish a transference principle reducing the weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality to weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequalities for three model systems: translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the semigroup $\mathbb{N}_0$, translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the group $\mathbb{Z}$ and translation on the circle $\mathbb{T}$. As consequences, we prove that $(2^n+1)_{n\ge1}$, the Fibonacci sequence, sequences of distinct primes and their partial products are \emph{not} $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We study the special class of multiplicative sequences generated by infinite words and we show that balanced infinite words generate $L^1$-Khinchin sequences, while typical random multiplicative sequences over at least two coprime integers are almost surely not $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We also obtain a {Conze-type principle} for countably generated semigroup actions on a probability space.

title: Bayesian Geometric Inversion for Wave Equation: Well-Posedness and Multiscale Multimodal Posterior Approximation
abstract: Geometric full-waveform inversion aims to recover sharp subsurface interfaces from noisy waveform observations. We formulate this problem within a Bayesian level-set framework, where the unknown interface is represented as zero level set of a latent function endowed with a Gaussian prior. Although the level-set-to-medium-parameter map is discontinuous, we establish that the level-set-to-observation map is continuous almost surely with respect to the prior, thereby guaranteeing that the posterior measure is well-posed and locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the data in the Hellinger metric. To enable tractable posterior computation under the severe nonlinearity of the inverse problem and the resulting multimodality, we develop a multiscale multimodal Laplace approximation. A frequency-continuation strategy incorporates waveform data progressively from low to high frequencies, identifying and propagating multiple candidate modes across successive scales. At the final frequency level, local Gaussian approximations are constructed around the retained modes and combined into a Gaussian mixture, whose weights are determined by least-squares fitting to the unnormalized posterior density. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method accurately reconstructs anomalous interfaces while effectively capturing posterior multimodality and the local uncertainty associated with distinct plausible geometries.

title: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm for normal cones converges only weakly
abstract: We show that the Douglas--Rachford algorithm applied to two normal cone operators associated with closed convex sets can fail to converge strongly, even when one set is a closed vector subspace, the other is a closed convex cone, and their intersection is a singleton.

title: Prescribed Beurling densities in spectral eigen-subspaces
abstract: Let $(q,D,L)$ be a one-dimensional Hadamard triple with $2\leq m:=\#D<q$, and let $μ_{q,D}$ be the associated self-similar probability measure. Write $\mathcal T=\{t\in\mathbb Z:(q,D,tL)\text{ is a Hadamard triple}\}$. We prove that, for every $0<s<\log m/\log q$ and every $ζ\in[0,+\infty]$, there are continuum many spectra $Λ$ of $μ_{q,D}$ such that $tΛ$ is a spectrum for every $t\in\mathcal T$, $\dim_{\mathrm{Be}}Λ=s$, and $D_s^+(Λ)=ζ$. The construction combines a nested family of finite digit sets with lacunary spectral extensions. A two-sided interval-counting estimate controls the density of the prescribed subset, while the added frequencies ensure completeness for every multiplier without changing that density. Binary choices in the extension yield continuum many distinct spectra. This refines Beurling dimension interpolation in spectral eigen-subspaces by prescribing the upper density at every strictly intermediate dimension.

title: Singularities of Multidimensional Item Response Models and the Rank of the Fisher Information Matrix
abstract: Statistical models in item response theory are known to be singular. This singularity manifests itself as a loss of rank in the Fisher information matrix, and the usual theories underlying AIC and BIC, which assume regularity, cannot be applied without further justification. Chen and colleagues analyzed this degeneracy and nonregular likelihood ratio tests, but their analysis does not identify all the directions that produce degeneracy or their dimensions. In this study, we analyze the entire kernel of the Fisher information matrix as a linear space for multidimensional item response models, separating the degeneracy due to rotations from that due to an over-specified latent dimension without double counting. We determine the dimension of each component and the exact rank of the information matrix, and prove a formula for computing, from the item parameters, the dimension of the degeneracy that remains after these components are removed. These results go beyond establishing the existence of singularity to identifying its causes and extent, providing a foundation for inference and model comparison in IRT.

title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: FFT-Based Fast Algorithms and Joint Rotation--Translation Pose Denoising
abstract: Rigid-body pose signals couple rotation and translation, yet most existing denoising pipelines treat them separately and analyse them only in the Fourier domain. We show that this separation is unnecessary and often suboptimal. We fuse dual quaternions, which encode rotation and translation in a single singularity-free algebra, with linear canonical transforms, which supply flexible quadratic-phase analysis, to develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) with an explicit kernel ordering. We establish inverse and energy-preservation properties, structured spatial and frequency convolution relations, and, crucially, fast algorithms built on complex FFTs. These algorithms make the DQ-DLCT practical: a two-stage chirp-adaptive scheme then performs joint rotation--translation denoising in a single transform domain. Numerical experiments confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the fast transform and demonstrate strong denoising performance on measured pose sequences and constructed two-dimensional pose fields. The DQ-DLCT thus turns a heavy algebraic construction into a deployable tool for pose signal processing.

title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.

title: Structural conditions on trust-region radius updates. Part II: second-order convergence and asymptotic radius behaviour
abstract: Continuing Part I (arXiv:2606.30202), we ask not which structural conditions on $\{Δ_k\}$ suffice for global convergence but what the radius does; the answers separate the mechanisms by whether the radius is tied to a criticality measure. We identify three asymptotic regimes: the criticality-anchored rules give $\sum_k Δ_k^2/M_k < +\infty$, hence $\liminf_k Δ_k = 0$, and $Δ_k \to 0$ once the model Hessians are bounded; the step-driven rules inherit the summability of the step series, hence $\sum_k Δ_k < +\infty$; the fixed-factor rules keep $Δ_k$ bounded away from zero. Near a critical point with positive definite Hessian, convergence of a subsequence forces convergence of the full sequence. We then extend the framework to second-order criticality through $τ_k = \max\{\|g_k\|, -λ_k^-\}$, obtaining convergence to second-order critical points with the worst-case complexity $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-2}\varepsilon_H^{-1}, \varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$, which reduces to $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ for a common tolerance and is sharp for quadratic models. Finally we establish eventual inactivity of the constraint and superlinear convergence, isolating the two properties of the radius rule through which the mechanism enters; the rate itself is mechanism-independent. The criticality-anchored and capped gradient-scaled rules reach inactivity only under a side condition, $ζ> \overlineκ$ or $\overlineμ > \overlineκ$, with $\overlineκ$ a constant of the solution that cannot be checked in advance. These conditions are necessary, not artefacts: on $f(x) = \sin(x)/x$, $\overlineκ$ is unbounded over the minimisers, so no parameter value meets the condition at all of them. Among the rules tied to a criticality measure, only those with an unbounded multiplier escape such a constant.

title: A numerical study of radius update rules in trust-region algorithms
abstract: Part I [arXiv:2606.30202] and Part II establish which trust-region radius update mechanisms can fail and under which hypotheses they must succeed. Neither says where the thresholds sit once a rule runs with real constants, or how the rule interacts with the model Hessian and the subproblem solver. This paper turns them into nine falsifiable claims and settles what it can, on four designed problems where the theory's quantities are computable and on CUTEst, where only aggregate cost is visible. Every mechanism runs in one Julia package written for this study, so two runs differing in one component differ in nothing else. The rule is worth less than the model and more than nothing. Crossing the mechanisms with four model Hessians puts $96.5$ per cent of the variation on the model and $1.6$ on the rule, and the rules separate most under the most accurate model rather than least. Uncapped R-grad is the robust default among the criticality-anchored rules, though the retrospective rule is ahead of it on this collection. No constant escapes the side conditions. For every cap there is a minimiser at which the constraint stays active, and for every anchoring constant a flatness on which escape takes arbitrarily long. The second of these is proved here as well as measured, and the proof uses no property of the model or of the subproblem solution beyond $\|s_k\| \leq Δ_k$. The radius rule governs the length of the step, and so the cost of a run. The model decides the search direction, and with it whether the run converges at all.

title: Ampleness of non-symmetric line bundles on degenerations of abelian varieties
abstract: Answering a 1985 question of Moret-Bailly, we prove by way of counterexample that if a line bundle $\mathscr{L}$ on a degeneration of abelian varieties $G \to \mathrm{Spec}(R)$ is not symmetric, then $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on $G$ is not necessarily equivalent to $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on the generic fiber of $G$. Our technique of proof is to use the Fourier expansion principle for sections of line bundles on degenerations, due to Faltings--Chai and Lan.

title: On the Peak Estimation of Scalar Polynomial Systems via Integrability
abstract: We develop a convergent occupation measure framework for peak estimation of scalar polynomial dynamical systems with no a priori state bound. The key observation is that scalar trajectories satisfy a uniform weighted integrability bound whose exponent precisely compensates for the singularity introduced by polynomial compactification. This yields a finite measure formulation with polynomial data. We establish a superposition principle for the resulting weighted continuity equation, prove no relaxation gap and establish convergence of the associated moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy.

title: Smooth radial quantized Type II blow-up for the three-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation
abstract: We consider the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation in three dimensions. In \cite{Schmid2026CVPDE}, Schmid constructed finite-time type II blow-up solutions with a continuum of blow-up rates, while the existence of smooth finite-time type II blow-up solutions remained open. We resolve this problem by constructing, for each integer $L\ge1$, smooth radial solutions concentrating a single ground state with the blow-up rate $λ(t)=(\ell+o(1))(T-t)^{2L}$ for some $\ell>0$. Our proof follows a forward construction based on modulation analysis with the energy method. The main obstacle is the lack of a repulsive structure that can be directly exploited to control the remainder. To overcome this obstacle, we adapt Kato's smoothing theory from asymptotic stability analysis to the forward construction. This yields a global spacetime Morawetz estimate for the linearized flow, providing the spacetime control needed to bound the higher-order energy in place of the monotonicity derived from repulsive structures in previous blow-up constructions.

title: Unimodular defect and antipodal lattice points of smooth reflexive polytopes
abstract: Let $P$ be a smooth reflexive polytope and let $Q=P^{*}$ be the dual of smooth Fano polytope. Ewald's conjecture (1988) predicts that the lattice points of $P\cap (-P)$ contain a lattice basis. In general it is not even known whether $P\cap (-P)$ contains a nonzero lattice point; we call this weakest form of the conjecture the antipodal condition. We define the unimodular defect of a finite set of lattice vectors as the least number of vectors that must be removed to leave a unimodular set, and the unimodular defect of $Q$ as that of its vertex set. Defect zero gives the unimodular smooth Fano polytopes, for which Ewald's conjecture is known. Our main result is that every smooth Fano polytope of unimodular defect at most two has a \emph{flat ridge}, a ridge $W$ with $|\det(v,W)|\leq 1$ for all vertices $v$; consequently its dual satisfies the antipodal condition. We also consider removed sets of pairwise non-adjacent vertices. Using results of Nill on independent vertices, we show that every such set has at most two elements unless $Q$ is unimodular, so the antipodal condition holds whenever such a set exists.

title: The Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem for finite groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$. The Gao constant $\mathsf{E}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ contains a subsequence of length $|G|$ whose terms can be ordered to have product equal to the identity. In 1961, Erdős, Ginzburg and Ziv proved that every sequence of $2n-1$ integers has an $n$-term subsequence whose sum is divisible by $n$; equivalently, $\mathsf{E}(C_n)\leq 2n-1$, where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$. In this paper, we prove that $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p-1$ whenever $G$ contains no cyclic subgroup of index $p$. Consequently, every finite non-cyclic group satisfies $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p+p-2$, with equality if and only if $G$ contains a cyclic subgroup of index $p$. This establishes the conjectured upper bound for the Gao constant and provides a complete characterization of the equality case.

title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.

title: Study of the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method -- The Laplacian data assimilation case
abstract: We investigate the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method, in the context of the data assimilation problem for the Laplacian. We provide error estimates explicit in all the parameters appearing in the model and the method (i.e. the amplitude of noise, the size mesh, the regularization parameter and the number of iterations of the method). This allows to devise strategies to choose the aforementioned parameters, for example to guarantee convergence of the method when the level of noise goes to zero. Numerical experiments on a two-dimensional problem are provided, illustrating the relevance of the obtained estimates.

title: Dunnett's and Tukey's procedures under mixed model covariance structures: dimensional reduction of multivariate-t integrals
abstract: Dunnett's test compares several treatments with one control, and Tukey's test compares every pair for independent samples with a common variance. We investigate which designs and covariances for a linear mixed model remain on the ordinary Dunnett and Tukey integrals, and in which direction the constants move when the correlation changes. It is shown that for Dunnett's procedure AR(1), the Toeplitz band, alternating ante-dependence, and the random slope have roots below the ordinary analysis-of-variance value, while heterogeneous compound symmetry and heteroscedastic groups have roots above that value. For Tukey's procedure every computed non-spherical covariance lowers the root. The second goal is the dimensional reduction of these multivariate-t integrals: a normal probability mixed over one chi-square scale. Conditioning on the latent variables shared by the contrasts replaces that probability by a product of univariate normals, and the integral has the dimension of the conditioning vector plus one. Balanced compound symmetry leaves a double integral. The studentized range reduces to the Pearson-Hartley integral. The reduction stops for asymmetric overlap of four or more treatments, for four or more autoregressive or unstructured follow-up times, for pair-dependent variances or correlated disjoint pairs, and for a separate variance estimate in each group.

title: Absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for nonlinear Schrödinger equations
abstract: We consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ \begin{equation*} i\partial_tu+Δu+|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation*} We prove the absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for the linearized operator around the positive ground state when $d=1,2$ and $p>1$, or when $d\ge3$ and $1<p\le1+\frac4{d-2}$. Starting from the fluid variables of NLS, we derive a biharmonic wave equation for the phase gradient after linearization around the ground state. Seeking a virial identity for this equation, we identify a mechanism for establishing a repulsive structure, which guides the subsequent ODE analysis to exclude embedded eigenvalues.

title: Full-horizon magnetic control of the Vlasov--Poisson system for plasma confinement
abstract: We study the full-horizon control of a two-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system through an externally imposed magnetic field. The control is represented by time-dependent coefficients associated with smooth, spatially localized basis functions, and is designed to steer selected position and velocity moments of the distribution function while limiting particle dispersion and the control effort. Starting from the kinetic constrained optimization problem, we derive the continuous first-order optimality conditions, including a backward Vlasov equation, an elliptic adjoint equation, and the variational inequality associated with bounded controls. We then project this system onto a particle--grid representation and identify the resulting particle adjoints and control gradient. The full-horizon field is then computed on a reduced particle ensemble, initialized by an instantaneous control, and subsequently applied to a larger set of particles. Numerical experiments indicate that the instantaneous control field already provides an effective baseline, while the full-horizon correction can further reduce the relative thermal energy near the boundaries and improve confinement over the prescribed time interval.

title: An $8+9$ gluing computation for the Ramsey number $R(F_3,F_4)$
abstract: Let $F_t$ be the graph consisting of $t$ triangles with a common vertex and otherwise disjoint vertices. We prove that $R(F_3,F_4)=17$ using an $8+9$ gluing computation. Neighbourhood matching arguments give degree and clique restrictions that reduce the search on seventeen vertices to $88,294,674$ ordered seed pairs. The verified main computation excludes $88,294,634$ pairs. A cross-edge counting argument excludes thirty-four of the forty exceptional pairs, and independently checked finite-domain certificates exclude the remaining six. Together with the construction whose red graph is the complete bipartite graph $K_{8,8}$, these results establish $R(F_3,F_4)=17$.

title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $μ$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Schütt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.

title: One bubble against a ring: new sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
abstract: We consider the Brezis--Nirenberg problem $-Δu=|u|^{2^*-2}u+\varepsilon u$ in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, and we look for sign-changing solutions which, as $\varepsilon\to0^+$, blow up positively at the centre and negatively at the $k$ vertices of a regular polygon. The key observation is that, for this configuration, the gradient of the reduced energy factorises, so that the whole finite-dimensional problem is governed by the zeros of a single explicit function of the radius of the polygon. Its behaviour depends on the dimension: when $N=5$ such solutions exist for every $k\ge2$, and the ring of negative peaks approaches the boundary at distance $O(1/k)$; when $N\ge6$ there are two solutions for $2\le k\le6$, while no solution of this type exists for $k$ large. For $2\le k\le6$ the nodal set of every such solution reaches the boundary of the ball, in contrast with what happens for the almost critical problem. Nevertheless, the two solutions found for $N\ge6$ have very different nodal structures: numerically, for $3\le k\le6$ one of them has only two nodal domains, and its nodal set meets the plane of the peaks along a closed curve around the centre, while the other one can have as many as $k+1$ nodal domains. These results extend to higher dimensions a configuration previously found in dimension four.

title: Endpoint maximal estimates for the half-wave propagator
abstract: We present a proof of the strong maximal estimate for the Euclidean half-wave propagator at the critical pair $s_d=d/(d+1)$ and $q_d=2(d+1)/(d-1)$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, i.e. \begin{equation*} \biggl\|\sup_{0<t<1}|e^{it\sqrt{-Δ}}f(x)|\biggl\|_{L^{q_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)} \le C_d\|f\|_{ H^{s_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)}. \end{equation*}

title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
abstract: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

title: Counting Irreducible Components of the Semistable Global Nilpotent Cone
abstract: We discuss various methods for parametrizing and counting irreducible components of the global nilpotent cone of semistable $G$-Higgs bundles on a smooth complex curve. By restricting our study to the case of generically regular components following previous work of Faergeman and Raskin, we obtain explicit counts of semistable generically regular irreducible components for $G = \mathrm{SL}_n$, and give the first examples of such counts outside type A. These numbers are obtained by counting points in some natural polytopes associated to $G$, but our method requires a finer analysis in cases where the center of the group $G$ is disconnected.

title: Gauss-Manin connection in disguise: limiting periods and quasi-Jacobi forms
abstract: We construct a six-dimensional algebraic moduli space of elliptic curves equipped with two ordered marked points, an enhanced relative de Rham frame, and a nonzero tensor of endpoint tangents. Its normalized period map is a biholomorphism. On the classical period locus, the regular coordinates pull back under its inverse to Weierstrass, Eisenstein, and theta functions. The associated Gauss-Manin vector fields realize differential operators on quasi-Jacobi forms of integer index. To relate this elliptic space to the genus-two construction, we study a specified smoothing family over a five-dimensional space of limiting enhancements. For this family, we identify the regularized period matrix and the boundary pullback of the holomorphic part of the logarithmic connection with respect to the chosen plumbing parameter. We then compute the unit relating the algebraic smoothing parameter to the Siegel period parameter and the limits of the specified genus-two generators. Separately, we express classical Fourier-Jacobi coefficients in enhanced elliptic coordinates.

title: Solving Classes of Linear Programs with Strongly Polynomial Straight Line Complexity in Strongly Polynomial Time
abstract: Recently, Allamigeon, Dadush, Loho, Natura, and Végh (ADLNV, SICOMP 2025) introduced an interior point method for linear programs whose number of iterations is bounded by the so-called straight line complexity (SLC) of the instance. This yields a strongly polynomial bound on the number of iterations of the corresponding interior point algorithm for broad classes of linear programs. In particular, in the companion paper we give a strongly polynomial straight line complexity bound for two-variable-per-inequality linear programs. However, in order to obtain a strongly polynomial algorithm for these classes, one also needs to address two important technical issues: initialization and bit-complexity bounds. Standard IPM initialization techniques either require numerical estimates that cannot be obtained in the strongly polynomial model, or involve modifying the instance in ways that do not preserve the geometry of the original LP, potentially affecting the SLC. In this work, we present an initialization framework for interior point methods for linear programming, along with a rounding procedure that ensures the continued feasibility of the IPM. We develop a multistage scheme in which each stage can be initialized in strongly polynomial time given the output of the previous stage. Additionally, we address the challenge of controlling the bit complexity of each iterate throughout the algorithm. To this end, we show that it is possible to represent iterates as low-complexity convex combinations of vertices and extreme rays. Our combinatorial rounding step is independent of the algorithm in ADLNV 2025, and can be applied more broadly in the context of path-following methods.
comment: This paper is based on the STOC 2024 proceedings paper "A strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programs with at most two nonzero entries per row or column'' , and includes the full details of the initialization framework and the bit complexity arguments

title: Distributions of metric $n$-point invariants and applications to molecular evolution
abstract: Datasets often arise as samples from a metric measure space whose geometry reflects the data-generating process. We introduce metric $n$-point invariants, defined as functions of the pairwise distances of $n$-point configurations, to study the geometry of such spaces. This provides a unified framework for existing concepts, such as the pairwise distance itself, the Gromov product, and Vietoris-Rips persistence diagrams. The distribution of a metric $n$-point invariant $F$ over random $n$-point configurations can be used to extract geometric information from the space and is obtained as the pushforward of Gromov's $n$-th curvature measure $μ_n$ along $F$. Our main result is an explicit bound for the expected $p$-Wasserstein distance between $μ_n$ and the empirical curvature measure $\hatμ_{n}$ of finitely many sampled $n$-point configurations, and carries over to the associated distributions of Lipschitz metric $n$-point invariants. From this we derive the sample size needed to achieve a prescribed accuracy and level of confidence in the approximation of the curvature measure. As an application, we use metric $n$-point invariants to study molecular evolution. We describe how site-wise nucleotide frequencies shape the corresponding distributions in Jukes-Cantor and Halpern-Bruno substitution models, and analyse five million SARS-CoV-2 genomes, revealing increasingly common failures of the four-point condition, constrained nucleotide accessibility consistent with the biased mutation spectrum, and rare cycles in persistent homology reflecting recurrent mutations across lineages. These findings demonstrate the potential of our sampling-based approach to the geometry of data as a scalable, phylogeny-free tool for detecting and quantifying evolutionary structure in large genomic datasets.

title: On Carmichael Numbers Constructed from Consecutive Jacobsthal Numbers
abstract: We prove that no Carmichael number has the form \[ N=(2^mJ_n+1)(2^mJ_{n+1}+1)(2^mJ_{n+2}+1), \] where \[ J_n=\frac{2^n-(-1)^n}{3} \] is the Jacobsthal sequence, \(m,n\ge1\), and all three factors are prime. Assuming that such an \(N\) is Carmichael, Korselt's criterion yields divisibility conditions relating consecutive Jacobsthal numbers to powers of two. Combining these conditions with the Binet formula and a finite case analysis for \(n\le4\), we obtain a contradiction. Consequently, this family contains no Carmichael numbers.

title: Single-graph rational exponents in mixed multicolour Ramsey theory
abstract: For every rational number $γ>1$, we construct a fixed bipartite graph $H_γ$ such that $r_k(H_γ;K_N)=Θ_{γ,k}((N/\log N)^γ)$ for every fixed $k\ge 3$. Here $r_k(H;K_N)=r(H,\ldots,H,K_N)$, with $k$ copies of $H$. The lower bound uses a symmetric random algebraic graph which avoids a fixed rooted power and has sufficiently strong local density for the Alon-Rodl method. The main algebraic step establishes a nonzero obstruction within the full symmetric coefficient space; the upper bound uses the rooted graphs from the proof of the rational exponents conjecture. We also obtain induced even-cycle asymptotics in the same construction.

title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

title: On Reduced Rank Regression
abstract: We propose a decoupled solution to the Reduced Rank Regression (RRR) problem, i.e. a pair of matrices (A*, B*) whose product A*B* minimizes the least squares error under a rank constraint. Using our formalism, we rewrite two other solutions from the literature and compare them with ours. In particular, we prove that all these formulations are equivalent. We then analyze their time complexity, and compare their running time and numerical precision on synthetic data, from which we derive practical recommendations. An open-source implementation of the algorithms and experiments is available here: https://gitlab.inria.fr/trudkiew/reduced\_rank\_regression.

title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.

title: Compactness and weak compactness of linearized Holomorphic-Lipschitz maps
abstract: Any holomorphic Lipschitz map $f$, defined on the open unit ball $B_X$ of a complex Banach space $X$ and taking values in a complex Banach space $Y$, can be uniquely and canonically associated with a bounded linear operator $\widehat f : \mathcal G_0(B_X) \longrightarrow \mathcal G_0(Y)$ between the corresponding holomorphic Lipschitz-free spaces. The aim of this paper is to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the compactness and weak compactness of such operators. In particular, we obtain a general characterisation of the compactness of $\widehat f$ in terms of metric properties of its symbol $f$. We then focus on the case where the target space is a subspace of $\ell_p$, $1\leq p<\infty$. When the target space is $\ell_1$, we show that compactness and weak compactness of $\widehat f$ are both equivalent to $\widehat f$ not fixing a copy of $\ell_1$. Finally, when the target space is $\ell_p$ with $1<p<\infty$, we obtain a metric characterisation of the weak compactness of $\widehat f$. As a consequence, we show that compactness and weak compactness need not coincide, even when the target space is $\ell_p$.

title: Lagrangian invariant tori for completely resonant nonlinear Schr{ö}dinger equations
abstract: We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schr{ö}dinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.

title: Dual Reflection Groups from Solutions to the Yang--Baxter Equation
abstract: Suppose that $r: X^2 \to X^2$ is a nondegenerate, involutive solution to the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation. To this data, we can associate an Artin--Schelter regular algebra $A$ and an infinite family of groups $G_k$, where $k \geqslant 1$. For each $k$, we show that $G_k$ is a dual reflection group for $A$, in the sense the component of $A$ graded by $1_{G_k}$ is again Artin--Schelter regular. We also show that, using the additional structure afforded by the underlying solution to the Yang--Baxter equation, one can determine the centre, Koszul complex, and associated twisted superpotential for $A$.

title: Sharp thresholds and convergence for a nonlocal bistable equation
abstract: We study $u_t=J*u-u+f(u)$ on $\R^d$ with a bistable reaction and radial nonincreasing probability kernels. Under the stated hypotheses, every solution from compactly supported data between zero and one converges to zero, locally to one, or to a single nonzero decaying stationary state. At every nonzero decaying stationary state between zero and one, we assume either nondegeneracy up to translations or analyticity of the reaction near the closure of the state's range. Decaying limits are strictly radially decreasing, with centers in the initial support's closed convex hull. For $u_0=\mathbf1_{B_R}$, we give explicit threshold bounds; analyticity near $[0,1]$ yields a unique critical radius with a nonzero stationary limit.

title: Half-sized gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that the lower limit of the normalised gaps between consecutive zeros of the Riemann zeta function is at most $1/2$. Our methods utilise a more efficient method for detecting gaps with short Dirichlet polynomials. Specifically, we apply resonance to a quotient of shifted zeta functions, rather than to the number of zeros in a short interval, using a Möbius resonator adapted to the symmetry between the shifts.

title: MONODROMY AND BIG QUANTUM COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERPLANE SECTIONS OF (CO)ADJOINT VARIETIES
abstract: We study the monodromy representation of general hyperplane sections of (co)adjoint varieties. We apply this result to reduce the generic semisemplicity of the big quantum cohomology to its ambient part, and to prove that the big quantum cohomology of general hyperplane sections of IGr(2, 6) is generically semisimple and satisfies Dubrovin's conjecture.

title: A Critical Case for the Near Field Refraction Problem in Negative Refractive Index Material
abstract: This paper studies the near field refraction problem for the critical case in negative refractive index material. Snell law in vector form is first reviewed, and the physical constraint governing refraction is discussed. We then define the refractor for the critical case and analyze several of its key properties. Building on these properties, we introduce the notion of a weak solution to this problem and prove the existence of the weak solution when the target measure is either discrete or a finite Radon measure. The proof relies on the Minkowski method, an iterative approach to refraction and reflection problems in geometric optics.

title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thiéry, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thiéry, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.

title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].

title: Bernoulli property for skew products of exponentially mixing systems over Anosov bases
abstract: We study $C^{1+β}$ skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free $\mathbb{R}^k$-action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.

title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Ampère equation
abstract: For the complex Monge--Ampère equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.

title: Herzog Class of Codimension $3$ Licci Monomial Ideals
abstract: Let $S$ be the polynomial ring in three variables with homogeneous maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. Licci ideals are ideals that can be linked by a finite number of steps to a complete intersection. All licci ideals admit a rigid deformation, and two licci ideals are said to be in the same Herzog class if they have a common rigid deformation. Guerrieri-Ni-Weyman gave a parametrization for the Herzog classes of codimension $3$ licci ideals in terms of pairs of partitions associated to Schur functors. In this paper, we give an explicit formula that determines the Herzog class of a given $\mathfrak{m}$-primary licci monomial ideal.

title: A note on the solution to the standard normal Stein equation
abstract: For $z\in\mathbb{R}$ we reconsider the solution $f_z$ to the standard normal Stein equation, corresponding to the Kolmogorov distance for distributions on the real line. More precisely, we prove the Lipschitz continuity of the related function $x\mapsto ρ_z(x):=xf_z(x)$ and explain how this observation may help to remove some unnecessary technical conditions from recent Berry-Esseen bounds in the literature around the Malliavin-Stein method. We further show that the Lipschitz constants of the functions $ρ_z$ are yet not uniformly bounded in $z$ and discuss consequences of this negative result.

title: On the simultaneous zeroes of Bessel processes
abstract: Given n independent squared Bessel processes, a priori with different dimensions, we investigate the first time $ζ$ at which at least n -1 of them vanish simultaneously. We show that the tail asymptotics of $ζ$ admits a power decay, with a persistence exponent given as the first positive pole of some explicit meromorphic function. This answers a question raised by Q. Berger, L. B{é}thencourt and C. Tardif in the case n = 3. We also provide along the way a closed-form expression for the Mellin transform of the position of the remaining process at time $ζ$. The paper is concluded by a more detailed study of the case of identical dimensions.
