abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean.

title: Alpöge's counterexample to the JC, Economic Stabilization, and Zhao's Vanishing Conjecture
abstract: In this paper, we apply stabilization techniques which are economic in the number of added dimensions to a slightly tweaked version of Alpöge's counterexample to JC(3) and JC(3,7). The first idea which lead to more economic stabilization is to bypass the degree 3 reduction of Bass, Connell and Wright in the construction of a counterexample to HJC(n). We construct counterexamples to HJC(15), VC(28), and HVC(30). On the other hand, we will perform degree 3 reduction after all to obtain counterexamples of low degree. We construct counterexamples to JC(12,3), HJC(18,3), VC(34,4), and HVC(36,4). As an encore, we construct a cubic-linear counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture in dimension 90. All presented counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture (Vanishing Conjecture) are over the (Gaussian) integers.

title: Erdős-Hajnal for excluding paths
abstract: We prove the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture for excluding an arbitrary path. A major step in our proof is a novel Gyárfás path argument based on the ideas of bookkeeping blockades and splitting paths, which may be of independent interest.
comment: 39 pages including bibliography and appendices; minor updates

title: Entropy-Regularized Finite-State Mean Field Control: Regularity and Stability
abstract: We study infinite-horizon discounted mean field control of finite-state continuous-time Markov chains with unbounded transition rates and a relative-entropy rate penalty. Under mild assumptions, the value function is the unique bounded viscosity solution of the stationary Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation on the closed probability simplex. Joint convexity of a quadratically corrected flux Lagrangian and smoothness of the data yield global semiconvexity, intrinsic $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$ regularity, and optimal Gibbs feedback. For positive symmetric reference rates, an entropy-plus-value free energy gives global exponential convergence under a quantitative curvature condition. We also establish inverse-temperature limits for values and, under parameter-uniform hypotheses, for feedbacks and closed-loop trajectories. With population-independent reference rates and a potential state-cost structure, optimal planner trajectories induce discounted finite-state mean field game equilibria. As an application, size-dependent market-making quotes with exponential demand admit an exact revenue-to-entropy reformulation; a convex inventory-crowding potential connects optimal quoting to stabilization of the inventory distribution.

title: Calderón Commutators on Quantum Euclidean Spaces and Quantum Tori
abstract: In the classical setting, Calderón's first commutator theorem states that Lipschitz regularity of the symbol characterizes the $L_2$-boundedness of the first commutators. We show that the formally analogous assertion fails on every quantum Euclidean space $\R^d_θ$ with $θ\neq 0$. The same simultaneous failure occurs on $\T_θ^d$ whenever $θ$ has an irrational entry. For rational $θ$, we obtain the optimal logarithmic bound for the corresponding Calderón first commutator. We also discuss the connection between Calderón's first commutator and the $T1$ theorem, and construct an operator-valued counterexample to Calderón's first commutator theorem, which shows that there is no direct analogue of the classical $T1$ theorem in the operator-valued setting. The counterexamples and the optimality argument rely on the construction of sequences of matrices $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf A_n$ such that $\|[\mathsf D_n,\mathsf A_n]\|$ is uniformly bounded, whereas $\|[|\mathsf D_n|,\mathsf A_n]\|$ tends to infinity. This phenomenon reflects the failure of the absolute value function to be operator Lipschitz with respect to the operator norm. The logarithmic estimate, on the other hand, is obtained by combining matrix-valued $T1$ theory with a transference argument.

title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.

title: A characterization of generalized derivations and biderivations on some simple algebras
abstract: In this paper, we characterize the generalized derivations and biderivations of the simple seven-dimensional anticommutative algebra \(D\) and the seven-dimensional central simple commutative algebra \(C\). Furthermore, we prove that any local generalized derivation of these algebras is inherently a generalized derivation.

title: A Partial Duty Formulation for Crew Scheduling
abstract: We consider a crew scheduling problem with a break, working time, and duty length constraint. It is common to solve crew scheduling problems with a diving heuristic, using column generation to solve the LP relaxation of a set partitioning formulation where variables correspond with duties. We prove that computing the LP bound of this formulation is weakly NP-hard, and propose an alternative formulation based on partial duties, whose LP bound can be computed in polynomial time. We prove the same complexity results for the corresponding pricing problems. However, the partial duty formulation has a weaker LP bound. To overcome this issue, we introduce compatibility cuts which completely recover the loss in LP bound. While separation can be done efficiently, we prove that the corresponding pricing problem after separation is weakly NP-hard. Therefore, we also introduce two relaxed versions of the compatibility cuts. We demonstrate computational benefits by providing numerical experiments with a diving heuristic based on the partial duty formulation, in a case study on the metro network of the Rotterdam area, the Netherlands.

title: Random-subspace Ellipsoidal Trust-region Methods for Derivative-free Optimization
abstract: Random-subspace model-based methods offer a promising approach to solving derivative-free optimization (DFO) problems in high dimensions. However, the usual ratio of actual to predicted reduction assesses model agreement at the trial point without directly measuring subspace quality. An accurate prediction in a poorly aligned subspace may therefore trigger trust-region expansion in all directions. We introduce Random-subspace Ellipsoidal TRust-region Optimization (RETRO), a framework for unconstrained DFO using ellipsoidal trust regions. Its trust-region updates combine global size changes with additional expansion or contraction within the sampled subspace, reflecting where the trial step was computed. We define an ellipsoidal subspace alignment measure that accounts for both the subspace and trust-region shape, and analyze Haar-uniform sampling and metric-guided sampling based on the current shape matrix. We establish almost-sure first-order liminf convergence and an $\mathcal{O}(ε^{-2})$ bound on the expected number of iterations required to reach an iterate with gradient norm at most $ε$. Numerical experiments on projected low-rank problems in dimension $1000$ show that using ellipsoidal shape information in subspace selection can reduce function evaluation costs relative to ball-based QARSTA, with the most pronounced improvements occurring when the solver subspace dimension matches the projection rank.

title: On the classification of threefold flops
abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.

title: Adaptive First-Order Methods with Composite Gradient Error
abstract: We study first-order optimization with inexact gradients whose errors combine a component proportional to the true gradient norm and a uniformly bounded absolute component. We develop an adaptive gradient descent scheme that selects estimates of the smoothness constant and both error parameters through a computable backtracking condition using exact function values. Its analysis yields convergence for smooth objectives and functions satisfying Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. For strongly convex objectives, we propose a composite-error intermediate gradient method, that adapts to unknown smoothness while using known error bounds and a strong convexity parameter $μ$. With fixed smoothness $L$, acceleration is retained when $α=\mathcal{O}\left(\left(μ/ L \right)^{1/4}\right)$, larger admissible errors yield intermediate rates. Throughout the range $0 \leqslant α\leqslant 1/3$, the absolute error bound $δ$ contributes at most $\mathcal{O} \left(δ^2/μ\right)$ to the objective residual, without additional amplification by the condition number.

title: Symplectophagy
abstract: We introduce the notion of a symplectophagy, which is a symplectic isotopy satisfying conditions reminiscent of the symplectic camel. We present new symplectic rigidity results which take the form of obstructions to the existence of symplectophagies in certain situations. The main tool is the relative symplectic cohomology recently introduced by Varolgunes, as well as its extension to pairs, due to the authors and L. Polterovich, for which we establish an invariance property, which is the chief technical novelty of the present paper. An important role is also played by the recent calculations of relative symplectic cohomology in complex projective spaces due to Dickstein-Ganor.

title: Invariant and Super-median Functions for Perturbed Heat Kernels
abstract: We study super-median and invariant functions for positive and negative Schrödinger perturbations of non-negative kernels. For positive perturbations, combining Dynkin's formula for the original kernel with Duhamel's formula for the perturbation, we derive perturbed Dynkin-type identities and give integrability conditions ensuring invariance. When the perturbed kernel is given by the perturbation series, we obtain a sufficient condition for a function to be super-median without additional integrability assumptions. We also decompose every finite non-negative solution of Duhamel's equation into the perturbation series and a non-negative solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation. For negative perturbations, we obtain analogous identities under an explicit finiteness condition. We also construct functions satisfying Dynkin's formula using zero-resolvents and compensated kernels. Examples involving Gaussian, fractional, and Bessel kernels illustrate the invariance criteria and the role of non-uniqueness in Duhamel's equation.

title: Operators commuting with $L^\infty$]{Operators commuting with $L^\infty$ on Köthe--Bochner spaces
abstract: Let $E(X)$ be a Köthe--Bochner space of functions on a $σ$-finite measure space with values in a Banach space $X$. We study bounded operators on $E(X)$ that commute with the operators of multiplication by functions from $L^\infty$. If $X$ is separable, every such operator acts pointwise by an essentially bounded $L(X)$-valued function. For a nonseparable $X$, a lifting of $L^\infty$ provides a representation by $L(X,X^{\star\star})$-valued functions, and by $L(X)$-valued functions if $X$ is complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, with the sharp norm bound if $X$ is a dual space. As an application, we show that if the transformation is aperiodic, then the spectral projections of invertible weighted composition operators with operator-valued weights are operators of multiplication by $L(X)$-valued functions whenever $X$ is separable or complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, and that, if moreover the measure is ergodic and $\dim X = m < \infty$, the spectrum of such an operator has at most $m$ connected components. Finally, for $L^p(μ;X)$, $1 \leq p < \infty$, an aperiodic nonsingular transformation and a weight that is measurable in the operator norm, we prove that the spectral projections are operators of multiplication by projection-valued functions for an arbitrary Banach space $X$, for instance for $X = c_0(Γ)$ with $Γ$ uncountable. The proof uses an inverse-closedness result for the algebra generated by norm-measurable multipliers and the composition operator.

title: $\frac{1}{2}$ derivations and biderivations of 3-dimensional nilpotent Lie-Yamaguti algebras
abstract: In this paper, we investigate $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and their corresponding local and 2-local analogues on three-dimensional nilpotent Lie--Yamaguti algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic zero. Utilizing the established classification of these algebras, we explicitly determine their structures of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations. Furthermore, we characterize the matrix representations of their local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Our findings demonstrate that, for the non-abelian algebras under consideration, the space of local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations is strictly larger than that of ordinary $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. In addition, we construct examples of 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations that fail to be global $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Finally, a complete characterization of the biderivations for these algebras is provided.

title: A curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform
abstract: We prove Lebesgue space estimates for a curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform associated with the moment curve $t \mapsto (t,t^2,t^3)$. The analysis relies on smoothing inequalities for curved multilinear averages and on estimates for a three-dimensional anisotropic variant of the twisted paraproduct. The result has been formally verified in Lean 4.
comment: 27 pages; associated formalization available at https://github.com/roos-j/lean-dfr

title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open rotation interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotations in $I$ is an ellipse. A fixed $C^6$ bound may replace the Sobolev bound, with $C^1$ smallness retained. The caustic hypothesis can be restricted to a suitably chosen sequence of rational rotations in $I$ with any prescribed rational $ρ_*\in I$ as its unique accumulation point, together with finitely many supplementary rotations in $I$; this family depends only on the reference ellipse, interval, and anchor. The main linear result classifies all real $L^2$ displacements satisfying the constant rational orbit-sum equations throughout $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations, and establishes their analyticity and rational continuation in the complexified boundary parameter. The proof combines analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy with quantitative caustic estimates, finite detection, and Fourier interpolation.

title: The big cactus group, invariant tensors, and rectangular tableaux
abstract: The cactus group acts on tensor products of crystals and, through Bender--Knuth involutions, on semistandard Young tableaux. We show that the big cactus group $J'_n=π_1^{\mathfrak S_n}(\overline M_{0,n}(\mathbb R))$, $n\ge3$, is obtained from the cactus group by imposing $n-1$ Dynkin-reversal relations, which say that conjugation by the full reversal acts on the Bender--Knuth generators by the Dynkin diagram automorphism; the quotient map is induced by forgetting the distinguished marked point. We give a second presentation, in which these relations are replaced by the requirement that every reduced word for the longest element of $\mathfrak S_n$ adapted to an orientation of $A_{n-1}$ represents the full reversal. These relations also hold on rectangular tableaux, where every adapted reduced word therefore acts as evacuation, and on invariant tensors: for finite normal crystals of any complex semisimple Lie algebra, the cactus action on invariants factors through $J'_n$. We prove the latter combinatorially in type $A$ and in general via Gaudin eigenline coverings. Haiman's promotion relation follows from a single adapted-word relation, but for $n\ge4$ it is strictly weaker than the whole family.

title: Double shuffle and naive duality for multiple Dirichlet series
abstract: Multiple zeta values admit both iterated-sum and iterated-integral representations, giving rise to the stuffle, shuffle and duality relations. Although these relations are satisfied by many families of complex numbers, we show that multiple zeta values are essentially uniquely determined by the double shuffle relations within a natural class of geometric multiple Dirichlet series. We then study geometric multiple Dirichlet series satisfying the shuffle relations and a duality relation. Under suitable analytic assumptions, we show that such dualities arise from differentiable involutions. We also use this framework to derive linear functional relations among multiple polylogarithms. Finally, we consider a more naive notion of multiple Dirichlet series and discuss the restrictions imposed by the stuffle relations, together with a conjecture on the uniqueness of multiple zeta values in this setting.

title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.

title: On the long wave limit of the good Boussinesq equation
abstract: We consider the good Boussinesq equation on the line. Sufficiently regular solutions are known to converge in the long wave limit to a pair of counterpropagating solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation. We prove that this convergence holds for solutions in $H^{-\frac12}$, the largest Sobolev space in which the good Boussinesq equation is well-posed. As part of our analysis, we revisit the well-posedness theory, proving new a priori estimates and a corresponding small data global well-posedness result.

title: Kähler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
abstract: We demonstrate that Kähler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Székelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of Kähler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of Kähler-Ricci flow.

title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.

title: On the existence of a spectral gap for ergodic Markov chains
abstract: Characterizations are established regarding the existence of an $L^2$-spectral gap for ergodic (that is, irreducible, aperiodic, and positive) Markov chains on infinite state spaces. In particular, it is shown that the existence of an $L^2$-spectral gap is entirely determined by the behavior of the spectrum at 1. These results are applied in the analysis of a family of Markov chains constructed to show that the ergodic composition of two geometrically ergodic Markov kernels need not be geometrically ergodic.

title: Avoiding Distances
abstract: Given a finite planar point set $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, let $a_1<a_2< \cdots < a_s$ denote the $s \leq {n \choose 2}$ different (Euclidean) distances between points in $X$. The aim is to retain as many of the points as possible such that certain imposed inter-pair distances are avoided. For example, we show that: (A) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, an independent set of size $0.2293 n$ in the unit distance graph determined by $X$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. For any fixed $k \in \mathbf{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k>0$ such that for any set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, and set $D$ of size $k$, there exists a subset $X' \subseteq X$ of size $|X'| \geq c_k |X|$ in which no pair of points is at some distance in $D$ (we say that $X'$ avoids distances in $D$). Such a set can be found efficiently. (B) (i) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/2$ that avoids the maximum distance; this bound cannot be improved. (ii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $8n/47$ that avoids both the minimum and maximum distance; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $5n/16$ points can be retained with this property. (iii) There is a subset of $X$ of size $n/7$ whose diameter is at most half the original diameter; on the other hand, there exists $X$ such that at most $n/6$ points can be retained with this property. (C) (i) For any $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation for \textsc{MIS} in the minimum distance graph of $n$ points in the plane can be found in $2^{O(1/\varepsilon)} n^{O(1)}$ time. (ii) Given a set $X$ of $n$ points in the plane, a maximum independent set in the graph of diameters can be computed in $O(n^2)$ time. The techniques used to handle the planar case can be extended to $\mathbf{R}^d$ for any fixed dimension $d$.

title: BBP Transition for Deformed Inhomogeneous Random Matrices
abstract: We study finite-rank deformations of inhomogeneous random symmetric/Hermitian matrices $H_N=(σ_{ij}W_{ij})_{i,j=1}^N$, whose variance profile satisfies $\sum_jσ_{ij}^2=1$. Writing $σ_N^*=\max_{i,j}σ_{ij}$ for the matrix sparsity parameter, we establish the BBP transition of outlier eigenvalues at the level of the law of large numbers in two regimes of moment conditions on $\{W_{ij}\}$: (1) under a uniform sub-Weibull bound with exponent $0<α\le 2$ and the sharp assumption $σ_N^*(\log N)^{1/α}\to 0$, the convergence holds almost surely; (2) under uniformly integrable $p$-th powers for some $p\ge 4$ and the sharp assumption $N(σ_N^*)^{p-2}=O(1)$, the convergence holds in probability. Our approach combines sharp norm estimates, fixed-degree polynomial isotropic laws, and a finite-dimensional resolvent equation.
comment: 24 pages. This paper rewrites the law-of-large-numbers part of arXiv:2407.12182 for improved readability, with strengthened results

title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. With the full gradient, SGLM is the Leimkuhler-Matthews (LM) integrator, whose discretization error for the invariant distribution is of second order. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + Σ^2 h^2 + h^4)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $Σ$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $Σ^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error. Through Riesz representors, the coefficients of the numerical bias determine the coefficients of the Wasserstein-1 errors of SGLM and SGLD.

title: On dimension of posets excluding a standard example
abstract: We prove that for every integer $d \geq 3$, there exists $α<1$ such that the maximum dimension of an $n$-element poset containing no standard example of order $d$ as an induced subposet is $\mathcal{O}_d(n^α)$. For $d=3$, we obtain an upper bound $\mathcal{O}(n^{2/3}\log n)$, while we also construct a family of $S_3$-free posets with dimension $Ω(n^{1/3}/\log n)$. The proofs were found by OpenAI's ChatGPT-6 Astra.

title: A Tensor Critical Threshold in Cubic Spherical Kernel Graphs
abstract: We identify a strong-detection transition within the critical scale for testing cubic spherical kernel graphs against $G(n,1/2)$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Conditional on these points, edges are independent, with connection probability \[ \frac{1+βZ_{3,d}(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)}{2}. \] Here $Z_{3,d}$ is the normalized cubic zonal harmonic, with multiplicity $N_{3,d}\sim d^3/6$. Assume $n\to\infty$, $d=d_n\to\infty$, $β=β_n$ with $|β|\le1$, and $n\le d^A$, with $A<\infty$ fixed. Write $r_n=nβ^2/(N_{3,d}d)$. On the critical scale $r_n\to r\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the tensor variational threshold \[ r_{\mathrm{tens}} :=\min_{0<q<1}\frac{-2\{\log(1-q)+q\}}{q^6}. \] For $0<r<r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the log-likelihood ratio under the null admits an asymptotically Gaussian expansion in the signed triangle, and the total-variation distance converges to $2Φ(r^{3/2}/2)-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. For $r>r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the likelihood-ratio test is strongly consistent, although the centered signed triangle still has Gaussian fluctuations. In the strict regimes $r_n\to0$ and $r_n\to\infty$, total variation tends to zero and one, respectively, even when $β\to0$.

title: Sample complexity of weak-signal latent-variable models
abstract: We study parametric estimation in latent-variable models in the weak-signal regime, where a small signal-strength parameter $β$ controls the dependence of the observations on the unknown parameter. At $β=0$, this dependence disappears, so all parameter values induce the same observed distribution, which we call the null law. We develop a unified framework for analyzing sample complexity in the weak-signal regime by expanding the likelihood ratio around this shared null law in powers of $β$. We prove that if the unknown parameter is first globally identifiable at order $r$ in this expansion, then estimation to fixed accuracy requires at least on the order of $β^{-2r}$ samples. We further identify a likelihood-separation stability condition that is necessary for any estimator to attain this rate and, under mild regularity conditions, sufficient for both maximum likelihood and method-of-moments estimators to attain it. We also study the regime in which the target accuracy vanishes together with the signal strength, and show that global localization and local refinement may be governed by different likelihood orders, leading to distinct statistical scales. Finally, we apply our framework to broad classes of algebraically structured latent-variable models, including additive-noise channels and exponential-family models.

title: Three Machines Suffice for Local Hardening of Electromechanical Oscillations
abstract: The single-degree-of-freedom swing equation with sinusoidal coupling is locally softening: its oscillation frequency decreases with oscillation level near a stable equilibrium. Nonlinear modal interaction, however, can reverse this trend in multimachine systems. This letter gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict leading-order local hardening, measured with respect to canonical action, in two symmetric three-machine operating-point families with equal or opposite power injections at the equal-inertia machines. An exact two-coordinate reduction expresses the condition in terms of a squared modal-frequency ratio and a dimensionless nonlinear coupling measure. The proof retains the induced mean shift and second harmonic and shows that the companion modal family remains locally softening. The criterion recovers both an equal-inertia hardening example and an exact large-inertia threshold. Coherent aggregation recovers the two-machine softening law, whereas the infinite-bus limit retains two dynamic rotor angles and permits hardening. An exact coherent-group extension preserves the selected periodic family, frequency, and canonical action for every finite machine count greater than two. Thus, three finite-inertia machines are the minimum permitting local hardening in the stated undamped, lossless classical model.

title: Sharp detection and triangle likelihood limits for quadratic spherical kernel graphs
abstract: We study whether quadratic spherical geometry can be detected from a single observed graph. Latent positions are independent and uniform on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$; conditional on them, edges are independent with connection probability $K_{d,β}(t)=[1+β(dt^2-1)/(d-1)]/2$, where $0<|β|\le1$. We test this model against $G(n,1/2)$. Writing $N=(d-1)(d+2)/2$ for the degree-two harmonic multiplicity, we prove that the total variation distance tends to one when $N\ll n^{3/4}|β|^{3/2}$ and to zero when $N\gg n^{3/4}|β|^{3/2}$. At criticality, if $N\to\infty$ and $Δ_n=\sqrt{\binom n3}\,|β|^3/N^2\toΔ\in(0,\infty)$, the signed triangle captures all asymptotic testing information and the total variation distance tends to $2Φ(Δ/2)-1$, where $Φ$ is the standard normal distribution function. Polynomial finite-sample error bounds hold under polynomial signal scaling. The proof controls the likelihood of the dependent quadratic feature law through spectral recursions, covariance truncation and interpolation from a symmetric prior.

title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces
abstract: A single-track Gray code of length $n$ is a cyclic Gray code of $n$-bit words in which every column is a cyclic shift of the first. For prime $n$ the longest possible period is $2^n-2$. Whether it is attained for every prime has been open since Hiltgen, Paterson and Brandestini introduced these codes in 1996, and optimal codes were known for primes $n\le 19$. We show that a conjecture of Degni and Drisko (2007) on the reflected Gray code order of necklaces implies optimal single-track Gray codes for every prime. Their list of necklaces, conjecturally a Gray path for prime $n$, closes into a Hamilton cycle of the necklace graph after $(n-3)/2$ explicit Pósa rotations, and such a cycle lifts to an optimal code. This implication is formalized in Lean 4. Together with computation it gives optimal single-track Gray codes for every odd prime $n\le 47$: for $n\le 37$ explicit codes checked word by word by a program independent of the generator, and for $n=41$, $43$ and $47$ codes obtained from the implication after the Degni-Drisko property was verified at these lengths by two independently written programs.
comment: 7 pages, 1 table. Ancillary files: Lean 4 formalization, construction and verification programs, the codes for n <= 23, and verification logs. All codes (n <= 31): https://github.com/dzoba/single-track-gray-codes

title: Generalized Logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on Bounded Domains and exponential decay to Boltzmann states for Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes systems
abstract: We derive logarithmic Sobolev inequalities on bounded domains for nonnegative functions that are prescribed on a portion of the boundary, and for Boltzmann-weighted reference measures. We use them to address the long-time dynamics of the Nernst--Planck--Navier--Stokes system with Dirichlet, blocking and mixed boundary conditions for the ionic concentrations and a Dirichlet--Neumann boundary condition for the electric potential. We prove that solutions converge exponentially fast to the Boltzmann steady states. When at least one species of each sign of valence is in contact with a reservoir, the asymptotic rate of convergence is independent of the dielectric constant and depends only on the domain, the boundary data, the masses of the blocked species, the valences, the diffusion coefficients, and the fluid viscosity.

title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
abstract: We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$, in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$, and in the Ahlfors regular case with $p=q$ they recover Costea's logarithmic law at $sp=Q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in the space $W^s_{p,q}$. For thin annuli $(B_r,B_{r+\varepsilon r})$ under an $η$-annular decay property, we uncover a purely nonlocal phenomenon: for $sp <η$, the capacity remains bounded as $\varepsilon\to 0$, because the limiting competitor $χ_{B_r}$ already has finite energy, while if $sp\geqη$ it blows up as $ \varepsilon\to0$.

title: On reducible $\ell$-torsion representations of Picard curves
abstract: Let $C/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Picard curve and let $\ell\equiv1\pmod3$ be a prime such that the $λ$-torsion representation of the Jacobian of $C$ is reducible for a prime $λ$ of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_3)$ above $\ell$. We describe the constraints imposed by complex conjugation on the $2$-dimensional subquotient $ρ$, in particular, showing that if it is absolutely irreducible, then up to twist it descends to $\mathbb{Q}$. We then give criteria for ruling out the irreducible case, using Dickson's classification of subgroups of $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_{\ell})$, under the natural hypothesis that the characteristic polynomials of all elements in the image of $ρ$ split. We also develop algorithms to compute the set of $1$-dimensional Jordan--Hölder constitutents of the $\ell$-torsion representation over $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_3)$, and Frobenius characteristic polynomials of the $2$-dimensional subquotient $ρ$. We apply these methods to $381$ Picard curves with possibly reducible $7$-torsion representations, and to five corresponding $13$-torsion examples. Under the reducibility and splitting hypotheses, we rule out an irreducible $2$-dimensional subquotient in all of the examples considered, showing that the semisimplification of the $\ell$-torsion representation is a direct sum of $6$ characters.

title: Minimax Slope Estimation and Support Recovery under Weak Gaussian Selection
abstract: In sample selection models, identifying a regression slope does not determine how accurately it can be estimated or distinguished from zero. We establish sharp uniform limits for outcome slopes in a fixed-dimensional Gaussian/probit selection model with unknown scale and an unknown covariate density bounded above and away from zero on a cube. We prove a uniform inverse bound between slope differences and observed-law Hellinger distance, allowing every nuisance parameter to differ between the two models. A matching path lies entirely within positive-correlation nonignorable selection. On parameter classes containing a feasible weak-selection neighborhood, the minimax squared slope risk is of order $n^{-2/3}$. For each prespecified minimum-signal sequence $b_n$, uniform exact support recovery is possible if and only if $n^{1/3}b_n\to\infty$, with rules allowed to depend on that sequence. The same estimator attains uniform root-$n$ slope accuracy on $\|γ_s\|\le M n^{-1/3}$ for each fixed finite $M\ge0$, including the exact zero-selection-slope layer. A testing-based construction establishes statistical attainability without estimating the covariate density; computational efficiency is not asserted.
comment: 41 pages, 4 figures. Complete proofs in Appendices A-G; numerical experiments in Appendices H-I; code, data and detailed simulation protocols in ancillary files

title: Sharp Signed Mass and Rigidity for Critical Finsler--Liouville Equations
abstract: We study bounded-above entire solutions of critical Finsler--Liouville equations with a possibly sign-changing prescribed function and finite absolute mass. Under a lower cone-growth condition, we establish a sharp signed-mass bound without upper growth or monotonicity assumptions. With an additional growth condition, annular compactness for a sequence of dilations yields Pohozaev boundary limits and rigidity for radially nonincreasing prescribed functions. Explicit examples show that the rigidity threshold is optimal. In the Euclidean plane, the mass estimate also gives a sharp obstruction to completeness.

title: Interior gradient estimates for mean curvature equations on Riemannian manifolds
abstract:
In this paper, we study interior gradient estimates for solutions of \[ \operatorname{div}_{M}\left(  rac{
abla u}{\sqrt{1+|
abla u|_g^2}} ight) =f(x,
abla u) \] on a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. Under a Ricci curvature lower bound and a Hessian comparison for the distance function, we derive polynomial and exponential gradient bounds under structural conditions on $f$ and its horizontal and vertical derivatives. The estimates quantify the dependence on the radius, the oscillation of the solution, and the geometric and analytic parameters. In the Euclidean case, we also improve the dependence on the radius in the gradient estimate of Xu~\cite[Theorem~1.1(d)]{Xu2026}. As applications, we obtain Liouville-type results for entire solutions under suitable curvature and growth assumptions.

title: Physical measures for partially hyperbolic systems with $u$-definite subbundles
abstract: In this paper, we study \(C^{1+α}\) diffeomorphisms of a compact Riemannian manifold \(\mathbf{M}\) with an attracting set \(Λ\) admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting \[ T_Λ\mathbf{M} = E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s. \] We assume that, for every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state supported on \(Λ\), the Lyapunov exponents along each \(C_i\) are either all positive or all negative. We prove that \(Λ\) supports finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of its topological basin. Our approach relies on an empirical basin-covering theorem for attracting sets with dominated splittings. Its proof hinges on a new notion of sliding suffix times, which allows us to synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.

title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Matérn kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.

title: Universal Hölder estimates for stable solutions to semilinear equations of fractional order
abstract: We establish universal interior Hölder and fractional energy estimates for stable solutions of $(-Δ)^su=f(u)$, $0<s<1$, with $f\in C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$ nonnegative and convex. The bounds depend only on a weighted $L^1$ norm of the solution and hold under optimal conditions on the dimension and the fractional order. In particular, the half-Laplacian estimate holds through dimension eight. The estimates extend to stable finite-energy Dirichlet $L^1$-weak solutions without an a priori local boundedness assumption, and an explicit logarithmic solution proves optimality in this class. Applications include global bounds in convex domains, bounded extremal solutions, and a Liouville theorem.
comment: Generative AI was extensively used in drafting this manuscript. The author is working on a revised version to improve its readability

title: On the probability that a discrete IFR random variable exceeds its mean
abstract: Let $X$ be an integer-valued random variable with $\mathbb{E}(|X|)<\infty$ whose survival probabilities $S_j=\mathbb{P}(X\ge j), j\in\mathbb{Z}$, form a log-concave sequence. Suppose that for some integer $m$ and some $γ\in (0, 1/2]$ it holds $\mathbb{E}(X)\ge m$ and $\mathbb{P}(X=m+1)\geγ\cdot\mathbb{P}(X=m)> 0$. It is shown that \[ \mathbb{P}(X \ge m+1) \,\ge\, \fracγ{1+2γ} \, , \] with the bound being best possible. As a consequence, it is shown that if $H \sim \text{Hyp}(n, i, k)$ is a hypergeometric random variable for which both $ik/n$ and $(n-i)(n-k)/n$ are at least $\log(4/3)$, then it holds $\mathbb{P}(H >\mathbb{E}(H)) \ge 1/4$ when $\mathbb{E}(H)$ is not an integer, and $\mathbb{P}(H >\mathbb{E}(H)) \ge 1/6$ when $\mathbb{E}(H)$ is an integer, both bounds being best possible.

title: Probabilistic large deviations approach to obstacle Hamilton-Jacobi equations
abstract: In this paper, we derive a non-classical variational representation of a viscosity solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation with obstacle, in which the Hamiltonian may take infinite values. We study a nonlinear selection-mutation model with an exponential-decay mutation kernel, using a probabilistic Feynman-Kac representation of a pure jump process. To handle the singular character of this process, we rely on a non-standard tool from large deviations theory, which allows us to establish a Varadhan-type lemma. This, in turn, yields the variational representation of the viscosity solution.

title: The first Cech derived functor
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a semi-abelian category, $\mathcal{D}$ a Birkhoff subcategory of $\mathcal{C}$, and $I$ the associated reflector. For $C\in \mathcal{C}$, we establish an isomorphism between $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\check{C}(f,C))))$ (where $\mathrm{N}$ is the Moore normalization functor and $\check{C}(f,C)$ is a Cech resolution associated to $C$) and $\mathrm{H}_1(\mathrm{N}(I(\mathbb{G}(C))))$ (where $\mathbb{G}(C)$ is the canonical $\mathbb{G}$-simplicial resolution of $C$ for $\mathbb{G}$ the comonad derived from an adjunction $F\colon \mathcal{X}\to \mathcal{C}\dashv U\colon \mathcal{C}\to \mathcal{X}$ satisfying classical conditions introduced by Quillen). The former corresponds to the Hopf formula for the second homology object associated to $I$, while the latter represents the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$. Specifically, we show that both can be expressed by a single unified formula. Furthermore, we can also prove that, under certain assumptions, the first \v Cech derived functor of $I$ is naturally isomorphic to the first non-additive derived functor of $I$ (in the sense of Culot--Renaud--Van~der~Linden).

title: Cramér-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes
abstract: In this paper, we focuses on how the distribution of random step sizes affects Cramér-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes. First, with sub-exponential moment condition of random step sizes, we establish Cramér-type moderate deviation results. Consequently, moderate deviation principles are obtained. Secondly, for random step sizes with sub-exponential tails, we establish a large deviation principle on tail probabilities. Finally, for random step sizes with regularly varying tails, we obtain precise large deviations.

title: Planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
abstract: The problem posed by Hoffman, namely, to characterize graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most \(1\), was first studied by D.~M.~Cvetković in 1982 [\textit{Publ. Inst. Math. (Beograd)} \textbf{31} (1982), 15--20]. In this paper, we completely characterize all connected planar graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed $1$.

title: Numerical Analysis for a Nonlinear Coupled Thermoelastic System with Acoustic Boundary Conditions
abstract: This paper presents the first $L^2$-norm error analysis for a nonlinear thermoelastic system with acoustic boundary conditions. The model involves three coupled variables: the acoustic potential $u$, the temperature $θ$, and the normal displacement to the boundary $δ$, with nonlinearities $|u|^d u$ in the domain and $g(\cdot,u')$ on the boundary, in addition to a nonlocal term $β(\int_Ωθdx)Δθ$ in the heat equation. We establish error estimates for the fully discrete problem, using the Crank-Nicolson method for time discretization and finite element method with basis of degree $r \geqslant 1$ for space discretization. We demonstrate that the domain-boundary coupling induces a half-power loss in the spatial convergence order for the variable $u$, and this effect propagates to the remaining variables due to the thermoelastic and boundary couplings, resulting in the final error estimate $\mathcal{O}(h^{r+\frac{1}{2}} + τ^2)$. A bootstrap argument is employed to ensure the uniform boundedness of $\|U_h^n\|_{L^\infty}$, which is essential for handling the nonlinearity. Numerical results using Lagrange finite element basis of degrees $ r = 1, 2, 3 $ (linear, quadratic, and cubic) corroborate the theoretical estimates and illustrate the transition from suboptimal to optimal convergence orders when the exact solution possesses additional $L^\infty$ regularity.

title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions II
abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation on manifolds with nonflat background metrics. In the first paper, we proved that, in dimensions $3\le n\le29$, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a radial model singular solution in the flat metric on the Euclidean space with origin as its singular point---a Fowler solution. In the present paper, we show that this dimension range is sharp. More precisely, for each $n\ge30$, we construct a smooth metric on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ and a positive solution of the corresponding Yamabe equation having an isolated singularity, near which the solution blows up along a sequence at a rate much faster than that of Fowler solutions. Moreover, the singular solution defines a complete conformal metric of constant positive scalar curvature and the metric agrees with the round metric to infinite order at the singular point.

title: A least-squares lower bound for capacity
abstract: We establish a least-squares lower bound for the logarithmic capacity of an arbitrary compact plane set, extending an inequality previously known for connected sets. The bound generalizes classical inequalities involving area and moment of inertia. It is sharp for disks, and asymptotically sharp for compact sets whose capacity coincides with that of their interior. We further show that asymptotic sharpness holds for general compact sets if we replace logarithmic capacity by minimal carrier capacity.

title: Density of length ratios on Teichmüller space
abstract: We study length ratios of simple closed geodesics on finite-type hyperbolic surfaces of positive genus. We allow cusps and fix the geodesic boundary lengths. Let $d$ be the dimension of the corresponding Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. We prove that for every positive vector $(r_0,\ldots,r_d)$, the set of surfaces carrying $d+1$ distinct essential interior simple closed geodesics with lengths proportional to this vector is dense in $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{L}}(S)$. In particular, one-holed tori with three distinct simple closed geodesics of equal length are dense. The proof uses high powers of Dehn twists, asymptotics of length differentials, and the Brouwer fixed-point theorem.

title: On Non-Uniform Baranyai Factorizations
abstract: For a fixed nonempty finite set $L$ of positive integers and $k=\max L\ge2$, let $\binom{[n]}{L}=\bigcup_{\ell\in L}\binom{[n]}{\ell}$ denote the non-uniform hypergraph whose edge set consists of all $\ell$-subsets of $[n]$ for $\ell\in L$. A $1$-factor of a hypergraph $H$ is a collection of pairwise disjoint edges whose union is $V(H)$. We say $H$ is $1$-factorable if $E(H)$ can be partitioned into $1$-factors. In this paper, we study the 1-factorability of $\binom{[n]}{L}$. Earlier work of He, Huang, and Ma shows that, for all sufficiently large $n$, $1$-factorability can occur only in the residue classes $0$ and $-1$ modulo $k$: it always occurs in class $0$, whereas it occurs in class $-1$ only if $k-1\in L$. We determine exactly when $1$-factorability occurs in this exceptional class. More precisely, we define a finite gcd-peeling algorithm on $L\setminus\{k-1,k\}$ and prove that $\binom{[qk-1]}{L}$ is $1$-factorable if and only if the algorithm accepts. As a consequence, our result provides a criterion for the $1$-factorability of $\binom{[n]}{L}$ and confirms the conjecture posed by He, Huang, and Ma.

title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
abstract: We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for Hölder continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.

title: Symmetry and Monotonicity for Subcritical Fractional Hartree Equations with Singular Sets of Zero Capacity
abstract: We study positive weak singular solutions of the subcritical fractional Hartree equation \[ (-Δ)^s u = \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ} \frac{u^p(y)}{|x-y|^μ}d y \right)u^q \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminusΓ, \] where \(0<s<1\), \(N>2s\), \(0<μ<N\), and \(Γ\subset\{x_1=0\}\) is compact with zero \((s,2)\)-capacity. For solutions with a nonremovable singular point on $Γ$, we prove hyperplane symmetry and strict transverse monotonicity under global Lebesgue integrability conditions. For $N\ge2$, we also prove these conclusions under upper bounds on $p$ and $q$, using only the integrability required for weak solutions. We also establish local regularity and construct solutions with logarithmic singularities along a line segment.

title: Model Theory of Products of Chains
abstract: We show that regarding the model-theoretic properties of distributive lattices isomorphic to finite products of linear orders there is a significant symmetry: if ${\mathbb X}_i$, $i<n$ are linear orders of size $>1$, ${\mathcal T}:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits (\prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X} _i)$ and ${\mathcal T}_i:=\mathop{\rm Th}\nolimits ({\mathbb X}_i)$, for $i<n$, then ${\mathcal T}$ is finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small) iff ${\mathcal T}_i$, $i<n$, are finitely axiomatizable (resp. atomic, small); the countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) model of ${\mathcal T}$, if it exists, is the product of countable atomic (resp. countably saturated) models of ${\mathcal T}_i$; further, we describe all models of ${\mathcal T}$: ${\mathbb Y} \models {\mathcal T}$ iff ${\mathbb Y}\cong \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb Y}_i$, where ${\mathbb Y} _i \models {\mathcal T}_i$, for $i<n$, and show that ${\mathbb E} \preccurlyeq \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb X}_i$ iff ${\mathbb E} = \prod _{i<n}{\mathbb E}_i$, where ${\mathbb E}_i \preccurlyeq {\mathbb X}_i$, for $i<n$. ($I({\mathcal T},ω)\in \{ 1,{\mathfrak{c}}\}$ was proved in a previous paper.) In addition, for each $n\in {\mathbb N}$ the class ${\mathcal C}_n$ of distributive lattices isomorphic to a direct product of $n$ linear orders of size $>1$ is first order definable.

title: Poincaré-Type Hessian Quotient Equations
abstract: Inspired by the two-parameter continuity-path approach of Chen and Xu, we employ a modified continuity path to characterize the solvability of the Hessian quotient equation for Kähler metrics with Poincaré-type singularities along a divisor D, allowing simple normal crossings and self-intersections.

title: Spectra of Multivariate Vandermonde Matrices and Min-max Error Bounds for the High-dimensional Super-resolution Problem
abstract: We study multivariate rectangular Vandermonde matrices $U_N$ whose rows are indexed by the grid $G_N=\{-N,\ldots,N\}^d, $ and whose columns correspond to irregularly spaced points on the unit $d$-dimensional torus. Motivated by the problem of super-resolution (recovery of spike trains from low frequency noisy measurements), we consider configurations in which the points form several clusters, with points within each cluster separated by at most $h$ and distinct clusters are well-separated. We show that the column subspaces associated with different clusters are nearly orthogonal, i.e. for $N \rightarrow \infty, Nh \ll 1$, the minimal principal angle between any such pair is at least $ {π\over 2} - \frac{C_1}{N} - C_2Nh - \frac{C_3}{\sqrt{N}}, $ for some constants $C_1,C_2,C_3$ independent of $N$ and $h$. This near-orthogonality enables the spectral analysis of such $U_N$ to be reduced to the analysis of each individual cluster. As a consequence, we derive sharp scaling for all singular values of $U_N$, revealing how the geometry of clustered points controls the conditioning of the high-dimensional super-resolution problems. Then we establish min-max error bounds for the recovery of clustered point sources, requiring only an upper bound on the largest cluster size and no knowledge of the geometry within the clusters. These bounds coincide with the optimal rates known in the one-dimensional setting. Furthermore, when the clustered points are in generic position (i.e. do not lie on a low-dimensional algebraic variety) our results indicate that super-resolution in high dimensions is more stable than in one dimension.

title: On the Proportion of Time that a Conventional Confidence Interval Covers
abstract: The concept of confidence sequences, or `anytime confidence intervals,' has attracted significant interest in recent years. This motivates the question of how well conventional confidence intervals behave when similarly evaluated. In particular, we study the probability distribution of the proportion of time a conventional confidence interval procedure covers the population mean, when the total time $n$ spent sampling is large. We establish an invariance principle for the limiting distribution as $n$ tends to infinity and show that the limit random variable $Z(1)$ can be expressed as a functional of Brownian motion. The random variable $Z(1)$ exhibits a scale invariance property that enables the derivation of a partial differential equation (PDE) for the density of $Z(1)$ jointly with the Brownian motion at $t=1$, namely $B(1)$. We show that this density can also be computed as the stationary distribution of a two-dimensional singular diffusion, one component of which is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. We then derive an approximating Markov chain that allows us to numerically solve the PDE. This density has a number of interesting features that provide various insights into the time-averaged coverage proportion problem.

title: Inverse trigonometric and hyperbolic identities,series and products for Lucas sequences
abstract: In 1936 Lehmer observed that the inverse tangents of the reciprocals of the odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers add up exactly to a quarter of $π$. Many formulas of the same kind have been found since, each with its own proof: for the inverse tangent and for the inverse hyperbolic tangent, for sums and for differences, for the Fibonacci numbers and for the Lucas numbers. We show that these are not different results but one and the same computation, seen through three signs. A single two-term identity, valid for the generalized Fibonacci sequence and its companion Lucas sequence of any parameter, contains them all. From it follow, with short telescoping proofs, infinitely many series for $π$ whose speed of convergence can be chosen at will, series whose sums are multiples of the logarithm of the golden ratio and of its analogues, and infinite and finite products with closed values. The Fibonacci and Lucas cases are listed in full; the classical formulas of Lehmer, of Hoggatt and Ruggles, of Melham and Shannon and of Melham appear among them, and the Pell cases, among them those of Mahon and Horadam, the Jacobsthal cases, where the logarithm of the golden ratio is replaced by that of $2$, the Mersenne numbers and the Chebyshev polynomials follow by substitution.

title: Derived equivalences and isogenies of supersingular abelian varieties
abstract: We study (twisted) Fourier-Mukai partners of supersingular abelian varieties. We give a simple proof that any two supersingular abelian varieties of the same dimension at least two are derived isogenous, answering a question raised by Li, Lu, and Tang and generalizing the result of Li and Zou. Moreover, in every dimension greater than two, we construct derived-equivalent supersingular abelian varieties whose corresponding positive powers are never isomorphic. We also give conditions under which derived equivalence between two supersingular principally polarized abelian varieties implies that their underlying abelian varieties are isomorphic. In particular, this implication holds in dimensions at most three.

title: Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.

title: The Casimir on the $K$-fixed tensor square of the minimal representation of $G_{2(2)}$
abstract: We compute the quadratic Casimir on the $K$-fixed subspace of the Hilbert tensor square of the unitary minimal representation of the split real group $G_{2(2)}$. In an explicit algebraic basis of invariant tensors, the Casimir acts by a three-term recurrence. Normalizing this basis yields a symmetric Jacobi operator whose self-adjoint realization is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by $-\frac92-8x^2$ in a Wilson-polynomial model with parameters $(\frac34,\frac34,\frac7{12},\frac{11}{12})$. We give the normalized spectral density and the unitary transform. The resulting spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, equals $(-\infty,-\frac92]$, and has scalar spectral multiplicity one.

title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.

title: Void probabilities for perturbed lattices under mixing
abstract: We study void probabilities for stationary perturbed lattices with possibly dependent perturbations. Our main result gives a general upper bound in terms of two ingredients: the number of lattice sites having a uniformly positive probability of hitting the observation set, and the $α$-mixing rate of the perturbation field. For unions of lattice cubes, this yields explicit bounds without moment or regularity assumptions on the marginal distribution of the perturbations. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative estimates for growing bounded Borel sets with non-empty interior, including stretched-exponential decay under exponential mixing and polynomial decay under polynomial mixing.

title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps
abstract: Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.

title: Optimal degree bounds for sum-of-squares representations
abstract: The moment-sum-of-squares (SOS) hierarchy provides a sequence of bounds on the minimum of a polynomial over a basic closed semialgebraic set, i.e., a subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by finitely many polynomial constraints. We establish optimal bounds on the error of the SOS hierarchy in the following settings: 1. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module: the error of the Putinar-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^4/k^2)$ in the worst case. 2. If the constraints define a compact semialgebraic set: the error of the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ((\log k)^2/k^2)$ in the worst case. 3. If the constraints define an Archimedean quadratic module and satisfy linear independence constraint qualification conditions (LICQ): the error of the hierarchy at level $k$ is $Θ(1/k^{4})$ in the worst case. Here, the upper bound holds already for the Putinar-based hierarchy, while the lower bound holds even against the Schmüdgen-based hierarchy. Equivalently, these give best-possible effective versions of Putinar's and Schmüdgen's Positivstellensätze for these settings (in terms of their dependence on $k$).

title: The Yau Geometric Conjecture for Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
abstract: This paper presents a proof of the long-standing Yau Geometric Conjecture.

title: Sharp Wasserstein stability and small-delay thresholds for evolution equations with measure-valued principal-part delays
abstract: We study the dependence of solutions to coercive evolution equations on the law of a measure-valued delay acting through the principal spatial operator. For non-negative delay measures of equal mass, transport couplings and the time-translation modulus of one reference trajectory yield quantitative kernel-stability estimates. Fractional temporal regularity gives a Wasserstein rate, with explicit glueing and data criteria for its application. For moving point delays in a diffusion model, a solution-level lower bound matches both the rate and its dependence on the kernel mass. This matching estimate holds for zero prescribed history and uniformly bounded forcing in the natural dual energy space. The results also quantify concentration to positive delays and approximation by atomic quadrature. Separately, we determine a sharp class-level threshold for energy bounds uniform in the delay location. At the critical threshold, any fixed scalar mode is spectrally stable, but uniform space--time energy control fails in a small-delay, high-frequency limit. Above the threshold, the growth has an explicit asymptotic logarithmic rate.

title: Random Tournaments Are Asymptotically Almost Surely Link-irregular
abstract: Bastien and Khormali (2025) conjectured that a nontrivial link-irregular tournament with $n$ vertices exists if and only if $n \ge 6$. Their work establishes the conjecture for $n \le 100$. We present a probabilistic argument for the existence of link-irregular tournaments with $n$ vertices when $n \ge 9$ to resolve the conjecture. In fact, we show that a random tournament is asymptotically almost surely link-irregular.

title: Signed FK percolation in Ising spin glasses
abstract: We introduce signed Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) percolation for the +/-J random-interaction Ising model to characterize nonzero uniform magnetization density and two-replica overlap within the class of Gibbs distributions whose infinite-volume Edwards-Sokal (ES)/FK representation has at most one infinite FK cluster almost surely. The construction refines ordinary FK connectivity by retaining the parity of coupling products along open paths. Using the infinite-volume ES representation and its DLR equations, we study pairs of companion objects and the compatible spin assignments on them. In one replica, companions are defined by positive-parity FK connections. For extremal states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of companion densities along the chosen van Hove sequence, nonzero limiting expected magnetization density is equivalent to density distinguishability of the companions of the infinite FK cluster. For two independent replicas, companions are defined by FK connections coherent in parity. For products of extremal one-replica states satisfying the infinite-cluster assumption and almost-sure existence of the companion densities along the chosen sequence, density distinguishability of the companions is equivalent to nonzero limiting expected mutual overlap. For two independent replicas drawn from the same extremal state, this specializes to the Edwards-Anderson self-overlap.

title: Infinitesimally Euclidean metric surfaces
abstract: We prove the equivalence of several notions of infinitesimally Euclidean-like behaviour for metric surfaces appearing in the literature. We obtain in particular that metric surfaces with property (ET) are universally infinitesimally Hilbertian.

title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.

title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_σ$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $σ(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_σ$ is $σ$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_σ$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $τ(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_σ$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_σ$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.

title: Human Exposition of Claude's 2/3 Theorem on the zeros of zeta
abstract: We expose Claude's proof that $N_0(T)\ge 0.6725 N(T)$ where $N(T)$ is the number of zeros of zeta satisfying $0<\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}ρ\le T$, and $N_0(T)$ the number of those zeros that are simple and on the critical line. Unconditionally it was only known that $N_0(T)\ge 0.4166 N(T)$. This proof is simpler than the previous ones and takes a different approach.

title: Length-convexity and domination for Hitchin representations
abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. For any $n\geq 3$, let $\text{Hit}_n(S)$ be the Hitchin component and let $\text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ be the subset of representations that take values in $\mathrm{PSp}_{2m}(\mathbb{R})$ if $n=2m$ and $\mathrm{PSO}(m,m+1)$ if $n=2m+1$. In this note we prove that for any Hitchin representation $ρ\in \text{Hit}_n(S)$ there is $j \in \text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ such that $ρ$ dominates $j$ in the Hilbert length spectrum; this confirms a conjecture of Lee-Zhang and, independently, Tholozan who had proved this for $n=3$. The key step is establishing a convexity of the Hilbert length function in the Bonahon-Dreyer parametrization of $\text{Hit}_n(S)$; this uses a result from the recent work of Barman-Gupta. We also prove these convexity and domination results for translation length functions and their spectra.

title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.

title: Local quadratic convergence of iterated correlation matrices: bounds and counterexamples
abstract: Kruskal's unpublished manuscript on CONCOR gives a local argument for convergence of successive correlations to a prescribed two-class sign pattern. We identify a failure in its stated one-step estimate and establish a replacement bound for correlation matrices in arbitrary dimension. A geometric estimate for sign-aligned centered rows yields an explicit sufficient neighbourhood of convergence and a quadratic error bound. We construct invariant families of correlation matrices with an exact scalar recurrence in every dimension at least three. These families yield counterexamples to the original estimate in every dimension at least four. The failure persists on relatively open sets of positive-definite correlation matrices. In dimensions divisible by four, an explicitly solvable subfamily provides counterexamples arbitrarily close to the prescribed fixed point and attains the asymptotic coefficient in the new bound. Quadratic order is attained by the constructed families in every dimension at least three. These counterexamples concern the quantitative estimate, not the convergence conclusion: all the exhibited trajectories converge to their prescribed sign patterns.

title: The fractional Calderón problem on finite Cayley graphs
abstract: We study a Calderón-type inverse problem for the spectral fractional Laplacian on finite Cayley graphs. For a known self-adjoint operator, recovery from a single measurement reduces to two requirements: full rank of the boundary (exterior)-to-interior coupling and nonvanishing of the interior solution. We verify both requirements on Cartesian products of arbitrary finite groups with even cycles, using consecutive cyclic halves as the accessible and inaccessible sets. Fractionalization increases the coupling rank, and one fixed nonnegative nonzero input determines every nonnegative potential. Our argument relies on a discrete maximum principle and an explicit resolvent formula.

title: Complex Representatives, Similarity Invariants, and Iterates in $\bf{U(1,1;\mathbb{H})}$
abstract: We study the similarity classes of matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ and the iterates of their associated quaternionic Möbius transformations. Building on the known elliptic case, we show that every parabolic or loxodromic element of $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$ is similar, via a matrix in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$, to a complex matrix. Explicit complex representatives and matrices realizing these similarities are constructed for the different types. We then introduce the invariants $\operatorname{Tr}(T), Δ(T), η(T), κ(T)$, and prove that they form a complete system of similarity invariants for matrices in $U(1,1;\mathbb H)$. Finally, using the complex representation of quaternionic matrices and Chebyshev polynomials, we derive a fourth-order recurrence for a real sequence $(q_n)$ satisfying $Δ(T^n)=q_n^2Δ(T)$. Together with recurrence relations for the relevant matrix entries, this identity yields a complete classification of the quaternionic Möbius transformation associated with $T^n$, including the degenerate cases in which $Δ(T^n)=0$.

title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
abstract: We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory. For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$. In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

title: Short proof that Vopěnka's Principle is symmetrically stable
abstract: We show that Vopěnka's Principle is stable under symmetric extensions. Recently, de Groot and Woloszyn [1] proved this fact. We found the proof of this theorem unnecessarily complicated. In this short note we prove the same statement. We direct the reader to [3] for an exposition on symmetric extensions.
comment: 2 pages; short proof for a theorem from arXiv paper 2609.06856

title: Energy-minimized interpolatory B-spline lofting for sequences of closed contours
abstract: B-spline lofting through closed cross-sections is common in reverse engineering, but interpolating each section on its own knot vector can produce an unnecessarily large control net. We construct a common-knot method for closed section curves of odd and even degree by minimizing the strain energy of each section subject to its interpolation constraints. Feasibility for closed section data and uniqueness of the resulting saddle-point solution require full row rank of the periodic collocation matrices, a property that a previously proposed periodic Schoenberg-Whitney window condition does not always guarantee. We establish the exact parity distinction: the condition is sufficient at odd point counts but admits singular configurations at every admissible even point count. For the odd and even degrees used here, the natural and shifting anchor knots are nonsingular; at odd point counts the window condition certifies the selected candidate, whereas at even point counts a rank test with an anchor fallback is applied. The lofting method therefore retains a nonsingular square subsystem for each section and uses nestedness to transfer full row rank to the rectangular common-knot system. Across six closed-contour models the common-knot method uses 83-98% fewer control points than traditional interpolating lofting, with section energies no larger than those of a previous knot-selection method within numerical precision.

title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
