abstract: We extend the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories (Shimizu-Yadav) to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. It is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We construct examples from graded simple currents, treat the free fermion and the symplectic fermion, and compare with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

title: Rapid convergence of Langevin AIS for multimodal distributions on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: We study annealed importance sampling (AIS) driven by the overdamped Langevin diffusion, targeting a multimodal Gibbs measure $π_\varepsilon \propto e^{-U/\varepsilon}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ at low temperature $\varepsilon$. For a potential $U$ with nondegenerate critical points, finitely many wells of comparable mass, and at least quadratic growth at infinity, we show that AIS with a harmonically spaced temperature schedule produces a weighted empirical measure that approximates $π_\varepsilon$ to accuracy $δ$ at a total cost of order $\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-2}$, up to logarithmic factors, and the exponents do not depend on the dimension. This is an exponential improvement over plain Langevin Monte Carlo, whose relaxation time obeys the Arrhenius law. The assumptions cover, in particular, the potentials of Gaussian mixtures, as long as their critical points are nondegenerate and their wells carry comparable mass. The analysis extends that of arXiv:2604.17526 [math.PR] from the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$ to the noncompact state space $\mathbb{R}^d$. The two new ingredients are a weighted $L^\infty$ bound on the eigenfunctions of the Langevin generator, obtained by combining Agmon estimates at infinity with a local maximum principle near the critical points, and a Weyl-type eigenvalue count derived from the Cwikel-Lieb-Rozenblum and Lieb-Thirring inequalities. For potentials with more than two wells the eigenfunction bound requires an additional argument, which we give by constructing a perturbation of $U$ that renders every saddle an effective local maximum.

title: A direct proof of Infinity in NF-0
abstract: We give a direct proof of Infinity in the no-empty version of New Foundations, denoted NF-0, by establishing that every model of the specified theory contains an object that is not finite in a precise, internally defined sense. The version considered has extensionality, at least two distinct objects, no empty objects, and inhabited stratified comprehension: a stratified extension is supplied whenever it has a member. Finiteness combines a two-sided internally represented well-order with the exclusion of internally represented nonterminating strict transitive relations on inhabited subsets. Assuming all objects finite, partial bijections yield comparison and finite extrema of positive Frege cardinals. Positive exponentiation, singleton type-raising, and the least orbit of the genuine two-cardinal lead to the equation n = T(n) + 1. We prove separately, and in detail, that adjoining one point reverses internally defined parity: the key ingredients are a graph-rewiring proof of invariance under adjoining two points and one instance of stratified induction derived from the all-finite assumption. Since type-raising preserves parity, the cardinal equation is impossible. We identify the corresponding Lean 4 declarations and make explicit the scope of the formal verification. No model-existence or consistency theorem for ordinary NF is claimed.

title: Optimal Trading Filters and the Value of Predictive Signals
abstract: The value of a forecast depends on its accuracy, but also on its actionability. In trading, an investor must translate return forecasts into positions while accounting for trading costs and the lingering impact of earlier trades. We solve the stationary quadratic trading problem with transient price impact using tools from prediction theory: Wiener-Hopf factorization gives the optimal policy as the composition of a conditional forecast and an explicit causal linear filter. We recover the Gârleanu-Pedersen aim-portfolio under exponential resilience and derive fractional trading filters under power-law impact decay, requiring memory beyond finite-dimensional LQR control. At fixed positive risk penalty, signals of equal instantaneous predictive strength have equal frictionless Markowitz value. With trading costs, net attainable value is determined by the mean square of the friction-weighted conditional forecast. Under power-law impact with exposure bleeding, we find an intermediate optimal mean-reversion rate for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck signals.

title: Contractible Closed Reeb Orbits on Prequantization Bundles under Weak Index Conditions
abstract: In this paper we study the multiplicity of contractible closed Reeb orbits on prequantization circle bundles. Building on the existing multiplicity result Theorem 1.3 for closed Reeb orbits on prequantization $S^1$-bundles, we weaken the index assumptions by requiring only that the supporting contact form has no contractible periodic Reeb orbits with mean Conley-Zehnder index zero and no contractible good periodic Reeb orbits with Conley-Zehnder index 0, and we obtain a lower bound for the number of geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits carried by contact forms $α$ on a prequantization $S^1$-bundle under certain natural topological assumptions (Theorem 1.6). In dimension five we further relax the index assumptions and show that, under a mild index condition imposed only on simple contractible periodic orbits and the same topological assumptions on the prequantization $S^1$-bundle, every non-degenerate supporting contact form carries at least $\dim H_*(B;\mathbb{Q})$ geometrically distinct contractible closed Reeb orbits (Theorem 1.11), in agreement with the conjectural lower bound for prequantization bundles.
comment: Added a few references and made minor revisions to the text

title: Special identities of nonsymmetric bicommutative operations in associative algebra with an operator
abstract: Let $A$ be an associative non-unital algebra with a linear operator $S$ satisfying \[aS(S(b)c)=S(aS(b))c,\] and define $a\prec b=aS(b)$ and $a\succ b=S(a)b$. We determine the special identities of these two operations. If $K_n$ is the arity-$n$ kernel of the corresponding operad morphism and $D_n$ is the space of consequences of smaller-arity kernel elements, then for every $n\geq8$ the quotient $K_n/D_n$ has dimension $n-2$. A basis is given by the classes of $F_{n-2}$, $ρF_{n-2}$, $G_{n-3}$, $ρG_{n-3}$, $J_{n-4}$, $ρJ_{n-4}$ and $H_{p,n-p-1}$, $4\leq p\leq n-5$. The upper bound is proved by a direct reduction of singleton sectors, using pure normalization, rigid boundary contraction and the four-singleton corner. The lower bound is obtained from coefficient functionals and a corner projection. In particular, new independent special identities occur in every arity $n\geq8$, and the operadic kernel is not finitely generated.

title: Unique Factorization of Power Series Rings over Q-UFDs of Dimension at Most 3
abstract: Let $R$ be a Noetherian unique factorization domain containing $\mathbb Q$, with $\dim R\leq3$. We prove that $R[[t]]$ is a unique factorization domain if and only if two conditions hold: every two-generated parameter ideal $q$ in every height-two localization satisfies $\overline{q^2}\subseteq q$, and every height-three localization has depth three. No excellence or completion hypothesis is imposed. The main local result is that $A[[t]]$ is not a UFD whenever $A$ is a local $\mathbb Q$-UFD of dimension at least three and depth two. We also prove that the UFD property of $R[[t]]$ passes to every coefficient localization in dimension at most three, give an all-dimensional criterion when the completions of the maximal localizations satisfy Serre's condition $(S_2)$, and obtain an arbitrary-characteristic criterion for excellent UFDs of dimension at most three.

title: Equivariant Moment Maps and the Ricci Cocycle in Weighted Fujiki--Donaldson Theory
abstract: Let $(M,ω)$ be a closed connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$,. We discuss weighted Fujiki--Donaldson theory with respect to the measure $dν=e^hω^n/n! $ for an arbitrary smooth real-valued function $h$ on $M$. We prove that the group generated by the flows of Hamiltonians that Poisson-commute with $h$ always admits an equivariant moment map for its action on the full space of $ω$-compatible almost complex structures. The moment map takes values in the continuous dual of the Lie algebra. Its density is expressed in terms of the Hermitian scalar curvature, a local weight correction, and an $L^\infty$ function $r_h^0$ constructed from the long-time average of the polar determinant phase. The function $r_h^0$ can be regarded as a Ruelle-type asymptotic density incorporating phase comparison via a connection. The key step in the proof is to represent the Ricci cocycle as the coboundary of a continuous cochain constructed from $r_h^0$. We also consider the action of the exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on a connected component of the space of almost complex structures inducing the given orientation on a closed connected oriented manifold of real dimension $2n$. In contrast to the weighted Hamiltonian setting, we prove that, for $n>1$, this action admits an equivariant moment map if and only if the real first Chern class vanishes.

title: Comment on "The polarization hierarchy for polynomial optimization over convex bodies, with applications to nonnegative matrix rank"
abstract: We revisit the feasibility and convergence claims for the polarization hierarchy of Plávala, Ligthart and Gross [Linear Algebra Appl.\ 723 (2025) 15--32]. Counterexamples show that the stated assumption is insufficient for the feasibility characterization and for convergence of the hierarchy with the polarization constraint. We establish corrected results under a stronger algebraic condition and supply a missing compactness argument.

title: A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics
abstract: For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.

title: Accelerating Finite-Sum Bilevel Optimization with Fully First-Order Oracles
abstract: We study nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with finite-sum objectives and fully first-order oracles. We propose Sampled Implicit Corrections for Bilevel Optimization (SICBO), which combines a penalty approximation with variance-reduced corrections for the lower-level variables. Under componentwise lower strong convexity, SICBO finds a point $x$ satisfying $\mathbb{E}\|\nablaΦ(x)\|^2\le\varepsilon^2$ within $\tilde{O}(N+\sqrt{N}κ^{7/2}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient calls, where $N$ is the total number of components and $κ$ is the normalized lower-level condition number. The bound achieves square-root finite-sum dependence using only gradients and preserves the best known deterministic fully first-order condition-number exponent for smooth problems. Our improvement follows from a curvature-dependent bound for nonlinear correction errors, which permits epochs of length $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{N/κ})$ with batches of size $\tildeΘ(\sqrt{Nκ})$. A single-level reduction shows that the dependence on $N$ and $\varepsilon$ is optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed $κ$.

title: Extension of surjective isometries between unit spheres of $\ell^p$-direct sums
abstract: We study surjective isometries between the unit spheres of Banach spaces of the form $A\oplus_p B$, where $A$ is nonzero and strictly convex, $1<p<\infty$, and every unit vector of $B\neq\{0\}$ has at least two distinct unit vectors at distance $2$. For two direct sums $A_i\oplus_{p_i}B_i$, $i=1,2$, satisfying these hypotheses, we prove that every surjective isometry $$Δ:S_{A_1\oplus_{p_1}B_1}\to S_{A_2\oplus_{p_2} B_2}$$ between their unit spheres forces equality of the direct-sum exponents $p_i$ and extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry $$\widetildeΔ:A_1\oplus_p B_1\to A_2\oplus_p B_2$$ preserving the corresponding components, where $p:=p_1=p_2$. The proof identifies the component unit spheres through diametral sets and distance formulas, and then constructs isometries between the component unit balls. As a principal application, we obtain extension and representation results for absolutely continuous functions equipped with norms combining evaluation at a fixed point and the $L^1$-norm of the derivative. We also discuss Lipschitz and differentiable function spaces, distinguishing the consequences of our theorem from those already covered by existing extension results. Endpoint conclusions are derived separately, including the Mazur-Ulam property for the real absolutely continuous space with the sum norm.

title: Analysis and approximation for inverse potential problem of space-dependent variable-exponent sub-diffusion in heterogeneous medium
abstract: Anomalous transport in complex heterogeneous medium is often characterized by non-Markovian memory effects and spatially varying trapping properties. From the point of view of continuous-time random walks, such heterogeneity can be described by a position-dependent heavy-tailed waiting-time density $q(t \mid x)\sim C(x)t^{-1-α(x)}$, where $0<α(x)<1$ is the local anomalous exponent. This microscopic interpretation naturally leads to the sub-diffusion with a space-dependent variable exponent $α(x)$. Compared with constant-exponent models, the variable-exponent fractional operators generally do not commute with the spatial Laplacian, which makes both the forward and inverse analysis substantially more delicate. This paper investigates the inverse problem of recovering a spatially dependent radiative or potential coefficient in variable-exponent sub-diffusion from terminal observation data. We formulate the inverse problem as a nonlinear fixed-point equation and prove that the associated fixed-point operator is monotone such that the fixed-point iteration converges decreasingly to the unique solution. We further establish a Lipschitz-type conditional stability estimate for the terminal observation map, which also implies uniqueness of the inverse problem for sufficiently large terminal time. For numerical reconstruction, we develop a fully discrete finite element scheme and derive an error estimate for the inverse problem. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the method, even in the presence of noisy data.

title: Skew-Symmetric Formulations and Energy-Stable Schemes for Compressible Reactive Flow Equations
abstract: This paper develops skew-symmetric formulations and energy stable finite difference schemes for the reactive Euler and reactive Navier--Stokes equations. By introducing suitable transformed variables, we rewrite the governing equations into skew-symmetric forms and obtain continuous energy estimates by standard integration-by-parts arguments. The proposed formulations extend the skew-symmetric framework for compressible flow equations to reactive systems, where the chemical energy and the species equation must be incorporated into the transformed variables. Based on these formulations, we construct semi-discrete schemes with summation-by-parts (SBP) operators. The convective terms are discretized by the non-dissipative part of linear upwind SBP operators, while a nonlinear SBP--WENO operator is used only to supply artificial dissipation near discontinuities. For periodic boundary conditions, the resulting schemes satisfy semi-discrete energy estimates consistent with the continuous analysis. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions validate the designed order of accuracy and demonstrate stable performance for problems with shocks, viscous layers, detonation-type waves, and complex wave interactions.

title: Multicolor Ramsey numbers of unbalanced double stars
abstract: For integers $n\ge m\ge1$, let $S(n,m)$ be the double star obtained by joining the centers of $K_{1,n}$ and $K_{1,m}$. Ruotolo and Song proved the upper bound $r(S(n,m);k)\le kn+m+2$ under the condition $(n+1)\lceil\frac{n+1}{k-1}\rceil >m((k-1)n+m)$, as well as the matching lower bound for odd $k$. Zhao, Mao and Zhou proved the matching lower bound for even $k$ and even $n$. We establish the remaining lower bound for even $k\ge6$ and odd $n$ through a new edge-coloring construction. Combining these results, we obtain $r(S(n,m);k)=kn+m+2$ for all integers $k\ge5$ and $n\ge m\ge1$ satisfying $(n+1)\lceil\frac{n+1}{k-1}\rceil >m((k-1)n+m)$. We also determine the four-color Ramsey number for $m\ge2$ and odd $n\ge15m$, showing that $r(S(n,m);4)=4n+m+1$.

title: Local energy and vertex deletion for $A_α$-matrices
abstract: We study the change in the trace norm and the centred energy of the $A_α$-matrix of a graph under vertex deletion. A pinching argument proves that the trace norm is nondecreasing under passage from an induced subgraph to the original graph, and gives a lower bound in terms of the edges induced by the deleted vertices. Exact perturbation spectra yield sharp upper bounds for deleting a vertex or an independent set of vertices with a common neighbourhood. For $0<α<1/2$, equality in these upper bounds is characterized by star and complete bipartite components, respectively. For the centred energy, we derive explicit deletion bounds and classify all connected equality graphs for $0\leα<1$: the extremal graphs are stars and complete bipartite graphs for single-vertex and independent-twin deletion, respectively. We also characterize equality in the general-set trace-norm lower bound and prove strictness of the total centred-energy inequality for connected nonregular graphs when $0<α<1$. Examples show that centred local energy can be negative and that the degree deviation term cannot be omitted in general.

title: Curvature Effects on Boundary Accumulation of Self-Propelled Particles: A Fokker-Planck Approach
abstract: It is well known that self-propelled particles tend to accumulate near boundaries. Although the influence of boundary geometry on this accumulation has been extensively studied using individual-based models, a population-level PDE description becomes desirable when a large number of particles are involved. In this work, we investigate boundary accumulation of self-propelled particles confined in two-dimensional circular and annular domains. We develop Fokker--Planck models that qualitatively reproduce the behavior observed in individual-based simulations. The main contribution is the formulation of appropriate evolution equations for particles accumulated at the boundary, incorporating transitions between the interior free-swimming state and the boundary-contact state. Starting from a general spatial two-dimensional model, we simplify the associated boundary conditions by assuming radial symmetry and then design an exponentially weighted difference scheme that preserves the total mass of the coupled system. Because transitions between different particle states induce singular behavior near the boundary, establishing discrete mass conservation is nontrivial. In particular, the velocity space must be divided into two subdomains, with the resulting discontinuity treated explicitly. Stochastic simulations and numerical experiments are performed both to validate the proposed models and to investigate the effects of geometric and dynamical parameters on boundary accumulation.

title: The Siemons--Wagner property and Bradley's conjecture
abstract: A transitive permutation group $G\le\Sym(\Pcal)$ is said to have the Siemons--Wagner property $\star_3$ if some three-point subset has a $G$-orbit longer than the orbit of every four-point subset containing it. In this paper we develop a structural theory of three-point orbits of finite $2$-transitive groups (orbit-length hierarchies, pointwise and setwise stabilizers, and their geometric realisations, including the unital and the ovoid), and we use it to completely settle Bradley's conjecture: a finite primitive group of degree at least $8$ satisfying $\star_3$ is isomorphic to $\PSL(2,7)$ or $\PGL(2,7)$.

title: The Segal-Bargmann Transform in Neural Partial Differential Equations
abstract: We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order $ L^{-\frac{1}{2}} $, where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control $ \sup_{x}\lvert\hat{u}_{NO} - u_{truth}\rvert $ for solutions of PDEs $ \mathcal{L}u = f $ which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.
comment: 41 pages, 4 figures, all comments are welcome

title: The Neumann problem for stochastic partial differential equations
abstract: In this paper, we study the Neumann problem for second-order stochastic partial differential equations in the half space. The coefficients are random and merely measurable in time. We develop a class of weighted function spaces for this problem, and establish existence, uniqueness, and regularity results. In contrast to the Dirichlet problem, the Neumann problem admits solutions with improved boundary regularity under suitable assumptions on the coefficients and data.

title: Riemannian Submersion whose Total Manifold admits an Almost Hyperbolic Ricci Soliton
abstract: In the present paper, we investigate geometric properties of a Riemannian submersion for which the total manifold is endowed with hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. We establish conditions under which the fibers of the submersion admit hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons. Further, we derive necessary conditions for the base manifold to be an Einstein and a hyperbolic Ricci soliton. Also, we determine the scalar curvature associated with the fibers and the base manifold. Moreover, when the total space admits an almost hyperbolic Ricci soliton with a torse-forming potential vector field, we obtain conditions ensuring that the extrinsic vertical and horizontal distributions are almost generalized quasi-Einstein. We also obtain necessary conditions for the fibers and base manifold to be an Einstein and almost generalized quasi-Einstein manifold. Finally, examples are included to illustrate the existence of hyperbolic and almost hyperbolic Ricci solitons in Riemannian submersion.

title: Zero-trace index of matrices
abstract: The zero-trace index $t(A)$ of a square complex matrix $A$ is introduced. It is defined as the largest integer $k$ such that $A$ admits a $k \times k$ compression with trace zero. This concept is analogous to the zero-dilation index $d(A)$ and is closely related to the $k$-numerical range. The $k$-numerical range is characterized as an intersection of half-planes, which is used to derive a formula for $t(A)$ that reduces its computation to the Hermitian case. Conditions for $t(A) = d(A)$ are also established, and matrices satisfying $t(A) = n - 1$ are characterized. Finally, the zero-trace index is determined for several classes of matrices.

title: Erdős-Gyárfás Balanced Five-Colorings
abstract: A coloring of the edges of a complete graph with $r$ colors is balanced if the edges among any $r+1$ vertices use all $r$ colors. Erdős and Gyárfás (1999) conjectured that for all $r\ge3$ the complete graph $K_{r^2+1}$ has no balanced $r$-coloring. They proved the conjecture for $r=3$ and $r=4$. We prove the conjecture for $r=5$, the first new case settled in over two decades. There is no balanced $5$-coloring of $K_{26}$, and since $K_{25}$ has one, $K_{25}$ is the largest complete graph admitting a balanced $5$-coloring. We design a reduce--dispatch--enumerate workflow, where every machine step produces an artifact that can be independently checked. First, we use a machine-checked (Lean 4) proof to reduce the conjecture to a single extremal statement about the color class with the fewest edges: no graph on $26$ vertices has between $55$ and $65$ edges while every $6$ of its vertices span between $1$ and $11$ edges. We then search on the sparse class instead of its dense complement, which makes enumeration up to isomorphism feasible. With classical stability theorems for $K_6$-free graphs, we dispatch the five near-extremal edge counts analytically. For the exhaustive enumeration on the remaining six edge counts, we design efficient encodings with SAT modulo symmetries and parallel cube-and-conquer. We also certify all eleven edge counts: each of the $12{,}296$ subproblems carries a clausal refutation checked by the independent verifier drat-trim, and all $273{,}503{,}938$ symmetry-breaking clauses are also validated against the vertex permutations that justify them.

title: A frequency localized maximum principle and its applications to time fractional equations with rough coefficients
abstract: We establish a frequency localized maximum principle for parabolic second-order partial differential equations with the Caputo time fractional derivative $\partial_t^α$ of order $α\in(0,1)$. The leading coefficients are uniformly elliptic, measurable in time, and independent of space. We construct suitable equivalent norms on frequency localized subspaces of $L_\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$, for which a frequency localized maximum principle holds. The corresponding result may fail in the usual $L_\infty$ norm even for the classical heat equation. As an application, we prove existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates in Sobolev-Zygmund spaces with Muckenhoupt weights in time for equations with spatially variable coefficients and zero initial data. The coefficients are strongly measurable in time with values in a Hölder-Zygmund space of positive order and uniformly bounded in this space.

title: Cospan contexts and higher categories
abstract: Motivated by the desire to turn the cobordism hypothesis (a statement about the universal property of some $n$-category of bordisms) into a $1$-categorical statement, we prove that all $n$-categories can be modeled by \emph{$n$-cospan contexts}: these are $1$-categories equipped with a collection of iterated cospans that satisfy a composition property in terms of pushouts. In particular, we construct an adjunction from $\mathsf{Cat}_n$ to the category of $n$-cospan contexts which simultaneously generalizes the $n$-fold span construction of Haugseng and the twisted arrow category construction (when $n = 1$).

title: A Gauge-Invariant Finite Element Method for the Time-Dependent Ginzburg--Landau Equations
abstract: It is well known that the Ginzburg--Landau equations are gauge invariant. The most popular gauge choice in practical simulations is the temporal gauge, also known as the zero electric potential gauge. However, the commonly used Nédélec approximations may produce spurious giant vortices on domains with re-entrant corners. To address this issue while retaining the Nédélec approximation, we propose a finite element scheme that preserves the gauge invariance of the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations at the discrete level. Under the temporal gauge, the method employs lowest-order Nédélec edge elements for the magnetic potential and continuous piecewise-linear elements for the order parameter on triangular and tetrahedral meshes, and yields a linear, decoupled formulation that requires only the solution of linear systems at each time step. We prove that the scheme is gauge invariant, preserves a discrete maximum bound principle for the order parameter, $\|ψ_h^n\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\le 1$, and satisfies a discrete energy law under mild step-size and mesh conditions. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties. In particular, on domains with re-entrant corners, the scheme computes the correct physical solution, whereas conventional temporal-gauge discretizations with Nédélec elements produce an unphysical solution.

title: Vertex Removal and Vertex-Edge Domination
abstract: A vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ $ve$-dominates every edge incident with a vertex in its closed neighborhood $N_{G}[v]$. A set of vertices is a vertex-edge dominating set ($ve$-dominating set) if every edge of $G$ is $ve$-dominated by some vertex in the set. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the vertex-edge domination number $γ_{ve}(G)$, also known as the isolation number. In this paper, we study the effect of vertex removal on $γ_{ve}(G)$, establish sharp bounds on $γ_{ve}(G-v)$ and characterize the vertices whose removal decreases, preserves, or increases $γ_{ve}(G)$. Let $V^0(G)$ and $V^+(G)$ denote the sets of vertices whose removal preserves and increases $γ_{ve}(G)$, respectively, and let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ consist of the vertices in $V^0(G)$ belonging to every minimum $ve$-dominating set. We prove that \[ |V^0(G)|\geq3|V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)|+\sum_{v\in V^+(G)} \bigl(γ_{ve}(G-v)-γ_{ve}(G)+1\bigr). \] In particular, $|V^0(G)|\geq 2|V^+(G)|$. We also prove that every vertex in $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ lies on a cycle and that $V^0(T)\neq\emptyset$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three.

title: The Lattice of Coalition Logics between MCL and CL: Coatoms and Compact Meets
abstract: For a fixed finite set $N$ of at least two agents, we investigate the lattice $L_N$ of coalition logics between minimal coalition logic (MCL) and classical coalition logic (CL), with extensions required to be structural. This lattice is order-dual to an interval in the subvariety lattice of Boolean coalition algebras. The eight basic extensions obtained by imposing seriality, independence of agents, and determinism form a Boolean cube under inclusion, but not a sublattice of $L_N$. Our main results concern coatoms and compact meets. First, finite critical coalition algebras, realized as complex algebras of finite general concurrent games, yield three infinite families of pairwise distinct coatoms containing seriality, distinguished by failures of independence, determinism, or both. An explicit splitting characterizes the unique coatom omitting seriality. Second, the meet of two basic extensions is compact if and only if the extensions are comparable. For incomparable pairs, no axiomatization of the meet can use formulas of uniformly bounded modal depth, even with infinitely many axioms. Consequently, $L_N$ and three natural principal intervals are non-coherent algebraic lattices. These results reveal lattice-theoretic phenomena beyond the inclusion order of the eight basic extensions.
comment: 19 pages, one table; supplementary finite-checking Python program in ancillary files

title: Dynamic Regret and Tightened Constraint Violation for Communication-Efficient Distributed Online Bilevel Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the distributed online bilevel optimization problem with time-varying inequality constraints. In this setting, a multi-agent network is confronted with a hierarchical decision-making task characterized by coupling between the inner and outer optimization levels. We first propose a communication-efficient single-loop distributed online primal--dual algorithm based on communication compression, which tracks both the inner-level solution and the Hessian-inverse-vector product using only one update per-round. We show that this algorithm achieves a dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T+H_{1,T}+E_{1,T})$, where~$θ_1 \in (0,1)$, $P_T$ is the outer-level path variation, $H_{1,T}$ is the inner-level path variation, and $E_{1,T}$ is the gradient path variation alongside a network cumulative constraint violation bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1/2})$, which is further reduced to $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-θ_1})$ under Slater's condition. Furthermore, to eliminate the dependence of regret on the inner-level and gradient path variation, we propose a novel adaptive multi-loop distributed online algorithm to control the inner-level approximation accuracy at each round. By dynamically adjusting the number of inner-level updates based on a gradient-norm tolerance condition, this algorithm yields an improved dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{θ_1,1-θ_1\}}+T^{θ_1 } P_T)$ which depends solely on the outer-level path variation while maintaining the same network cumulative constraint violation bound. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

title: end point estimates for the bilinear circular averaging operator
abstract: We prove that the bilinear circular averaging operator is bounded from $L^1(\mathbb{R}) \times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$. The corresponding strong estimate fails, even when the inputs are nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported. We also construct nonnegative $f,g \in L^1(\mathbb{R})$ for which the average does not belong to $L^{1/2}(\mathbb{R})$. The weak estimate is proved by a dyadic decomposition of the inputs and a summation over interval pairs near each quadratic fold.

title: Smooth Quasi--Einstein Lifts of Locally Embeddable Three-Dimensional CR Manifolds
abstract: We prove a $C^\infty$ analogue of the real-analytic quasi--Einstein lifting theorem of Hill, Lewandowski and Nurowski \cite[Theorem~2.5]{HLN2008}. Every smooth, locally CR-embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex three-dimensional CR manifold admits, for each real cosmological constant, a local smooth Lorentzian quasi--Einstein lift whose null congruence is geodesic, shearfree and twisting and whose Weyl tensor has Petrov type~$\mathrm{II}$ or $\mathrm{D}$. The result extends local lifting beyond the Sasakian setting of the global constructions in \cite{GSS2020} and the local results in \cite{GGS2026}. The proof establishes smooth local solvability of the reduced semilinear contact equation by combining an $L^\infty$ contraction with subelliptic regularity.

title: A Crawling Metric on the Space of Subtrees of a Tree
abstract: We propose a crawling metric on the space of subtrees of a tree. The symmetric difference cannot tell whether two disjoint subtrees are close or far; we halve it and add the gap between them. The result is a metric, one half is the smallest factor, and the tree embeds canonically. The metric equals the least cost of crawling between subtrees by growing and shrinking without jumping. With simultaneous growth and shrinkage, subtrees of fixed length form a geodesic space.

title: A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.

title: On the $ω$-circular $*$-distribution for complex unimodular $ω$
abstract: We consider a notion of $ω$-circular $*$-distribution $μ_ω$, defined in terms of a parameter $ω\in \mathbb{C}$ with $| ω|=1$. This $*$-distribution appears as limit law in an algebraic central limit theorem (CLT) for $ω$-commuting unitaries, and interpolates between the Fermionic setting (at $ω= -1$) and the Bosonic one (at $ω= 1$). On a combinatorial level, $μ_ω$ is described in terms of pair-partitions of sets $\{1, ... ,2n\}$, where one has a total order among the $n$ pairs of the partition and where every pair is assigned a direction, to the effect that one can define the sign of a crossing between two pairs. The main goal of the paper is to study a significant subspace, with "Fock space" flavour, of the $L^2$-space associated to a natural multi-variate version of $μ_ω$. The inner product on this subspace is defined by a sesquilinear form $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ on non-commutative polynomials. We explicitly describe $\langle \cdot \, , \, \cdot \rangle_ω$ in terms of some tractable non-negative definite functions on symmetric groups, and we prove that it is non-degenerate if and only if $ω$ is not a root of unity.

title: A proof of the strong Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture
abstract: A family of nonempty sets is $r$-cover-free if no member is contained in the union of at most $r$ other members. Let $T(r)$ denote the least $n$ for which there is an $r$-cover-free family on $n$ points with more than $n$ members. In this paper, we prove that $T(r)\ge(r+1)^2$ for every integer $r\ge1$, confirming the strong form of the Erdős--Frankl--Füredi cover-free conjecture. In particular, $T(r)=(r+1)^2$ whenever $r+1$ is a prime power.

title: Transformers as Adaptive Kernel Learners across Tasks for In-Context Learning
abstract: Transformers have emerged as a dominant architecture in modern machine learning, with in-context learning (ICL) enabling models to adapt to new tasks by conditioning on prompts, without any parameter updates. To understand the attention mechanism in transformer blocks, a growing line of theoretical work interprets ICL through the lens of classical statistical estimators. Recent works have established a connection between the attention mechanism and kernel methods, while the kernel function is usually assumed to be fixed. In practice, the query and key matrices in the attention mechanism are trained, which allows the attention mechanism to serve as an adaptive kernel method. In this work, we demonstrate that transformers can act as adaptive anisotropic kernel learners. Specifically, we study ICL for low-rank linear and multi-index nonlinear regressions, and conduct numerical simulations to show that the learned attention scores closely resemble the oracle kernels for these function classes. We then develop a general framework to analyze the generalization error of ICL by connecting transformers to the oracle kernel estimator for each function class. Our theory gives an explicit and constructive implementation of the oracle kernel estimators for these function classes using a wide and shallow transformer architecture, illustrating how the prediction is carried out by the interaction between the query token and the context tokens. Our work complements existing studies by providing numerical and theoretical evidence of how the attention mechanism adapts to anisotropic kernels in both linear and nonlinear settings.

title: Dynamic Programming for Value-at-Risk Markov Decision Processes in Continuous Spaces
abstract: Value-at-Risk (VaR) is a widely adopted quantile-based risk measure in practice, yet incorporating VaR objectives into Markov decision processes (VaR MDPs) remains a longstanding challenge. Recent work has derived dynamic programming equations for VaR MDPs in finite state and action spaces but left the case of more general spaces unresolved. This paper establishes, for the first time, the validity of these equations in continuous spaces, for both finite- and infinite-horizon settings. Such cases naturally arise in many real-world dynamic decision-making problems. As an application, we study an optimal execution problem with a VaR objective and demonstrate that our framework enables the characterization of optimal dynamic strategies, resolving an open question in the field.

title: Bounded powers of edge ideals: Nearly Gorenstein polytopes
abstract: A lattice polytope $\mathcal{P} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ of dimension $n$ is called nearly Gorenstein if $\mathcal{P}$ is normal and if its Ehrhart ring is a nearly Gorenstein ring. We study nearly Gorenstein polytopes arising from discrete polymatroids of bounded powers of edge ideals. Especially, it is shown that every nearly Gorenstein polytope coming from either a complete graph or a complete bipartite graph is level.

title: Low-Bit Distributed Constrained Optimization with Application to Optimal Scheduling and Allocation
abstract: This paper proposes a distributed resource allocation algorithm in which each agent communicates only the sign of its local cost gradient, a single bit per directed link per iteration. The algorithm is based on Laplacian-gradient dynamics and preserves the equality (demand) constraint at every iterate, guaranteeing anytime feasibility irrespective of termination time. First, we provide a complete Lyapunov-based convergence analysis for the fixed-step-size regime: the iterates are shown to enter, in at most O(1/\varepsilon^2) iterations, a neighborhood of the optimizer whose radius scales as O(τ) in the decision variable and O(τ^2) in the cost residual, where $τ$ is the step-size. Crucially, the step-size bound is a time-invariant network constant (depending only on the graph Laplacian spectrum and the cost curvature bounds), so no adaptive tuning is required. Second, we characterize the invariant set under B-connected, weight-balanced digraphs, strictly weaker than the all-time connectivity and doubly-stochastic weights assumed in most prior work, and show that any odd, sign-preserving nonlinearity yields the same invariant-set and descent structure, with the single-bit protocol being the extreme communication-minimizing instance of a broader nonlinear class. Third, we address local box constraints via smooth penalty relaxation and quantify explicitly how the penalty weight interacts with the step-size bound and the optimality gap. Simulations on economic dispatch (1000 generators) and CPU scheduling (500 servers) demonstrate that the single-bit protocol achieves 5-60 times reduction in total communication cost relative to multi-bit baselines, at the price of a tunable and explicitly bounded optimality gap. A diminishing step-size schedule is shown empirically to eliminate this gap; its formal convergence analysis is identified as an open problem.

title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $β$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $β$ whose interiors are disjoint from $β$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $β$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $β$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|β| ζ(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $β$, the constants are continuous at the points where $β$ lies in a non-periodic direction.

title: Local Ore Conditions for Rainbow Pancyclicity and Vertex-Pancyclicity in Graph Systems
abstract: We investigate rainbow pancyclicity and vertex-pancyclicity of graph systems satisfying a local Ore-type degree condition. All graphs in the system share the same vertex set. We prove that if each graph is 2-connected and satisfies our local Ore condition, then the graph system is either rainbow pancyclic and vertex-pancyclic for cycles of length from 4 to n, or all graphs are identical balanced complete bipartite graphs on an even vertex set. A stronger degree threshold ensures full rainbow vertex-pancyclicity. All thresholds we obtain are tight. Our proofs rely on cycle extension techniques and neighborhood separation arguments.

title: A note on the rectangular Schoenberg-Whitney theorem for clamped B-splines
abstract: Wang et al.(Computer-Aided Design 40 (2008) 999-1008) proposed a knot-subsequence characterization of full row rank for rectangular B-spline collocation matrices. We identify an incorrect inequality in their Appendix proof, which invalidates the argument as written, and make explicit the endpoint and multiplicity conventions on which the criterion depends. The defect lies in the proof, not in the underlying result, which is valid under suitably stated hypotheses; in the lofting construction of Wang et al. these hypotheses are implicitly satisfied, so the lofted curves are unaffected. We state the corrected result and give a new proof, independent of the disputed argument, for clamped B-splines of arbitrary degree with continuous interior multiplicities. In our proof, sufficiency follows from inclusion of spline spaces and knot insertion; necessity selects independent columns and builds the reduced knot vector from them. The proof uses no recursive column-selection construction.

title: Weakly uniform computable categoricity and function composition
abstract: We introduce the definition of a weakly $X$-uniformly $Y$-computably categorical structure, relativizing a definition of Kudinov (1996), and show that this relativized notion is closely related to the 2-dimensional complexity of the pairs of partial functions $(f,g)$ with the property that the composition $g\circ f$ simulates convergent $\emptyset'$-oracle computations. We develop a general theory for computing via composition and use it to prove results about the surprisingly complex weakly uniform categoricity spectrum of the structure $(ω,S)$ where $S(n)=n+1$. Namely, that $(ω,S)$ is w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for some $X\not\geq_T\emptyset'$ and $Y<_T\emptyset'$, but $(ω,S)$ is not w.$X$.u.$Y$.c.c. for any $X<_T\emptyset'$ and $Y\not\geq_T\emptyset'$. We also construct a computably categorical structure that is not w.$\emptyset'$.u.c.c., but is w.$X$.u.c.c. for a set $X$ that is $\leq_T$-incomparable with $\emptyset'$.

title: Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization
abstract: This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.

title: Certified Fourier rounding for the real Grothendieck inequality
abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that the real Grothendieck constant is strictly smaller than $1.77987164$. The proof provides a complete interval-arithmetic realization of Ren's five-variable construction. A finite Fourier calculation encloses every scalar coefficient through degree $403$; a fourth-derivative estimate on the entire unit circle bounds the remaining coefficient sum by $10^{-4}$. Exact rational arithmetic then certifies the final inequality. We include the transfer to all finite real matrices and arbitrary vector dimensions, the analytic quadrature errors, the rational parameters, and source code for checking and regenerating the certificate.
comment: 18 pages; source code and exact certificate included as ancillary files

title: Asymptotic Normality of the Hill Estimator in Linear Preferential Attachment
abstract: We prove asymptotic normality of the Hill estimator based on the largest $k_n$ degrees in a homogeneous linear preferential attachment graph with $n$ vertices. Each new vertex sends a fixed number $m\ge1$ of edges sequentially to older vertices, with attachment weight $d+δ$ and fixed $δ>-m$. Let $α=m/(2m+δ)$. For every deterministic sequence $k_n\to\infty$ satisfying $\sqrt{k_n}(k_n/n)^α\to0$, the estimator, centered at $α$ and multiplied by $\sqrt{k_n}$, converges to a centered normal law with an explicit variance strictly smaller than $α^2$. The reduction relative to the Hill variance for independent observations separates into contributions from the different degree laws at different birth times and from competition for new edges. The contribution from competition is $1/m$ times that from different birth times. Representations using Gamma and beta functions give a consistent standard error and a studentized normal limit. The proof uses martingales indexed by edge attachments and comparisons with independent pure-birth processes, while retaining the integer degrees and their ties.

title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
abstract: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.
comment: 24 pages, correct some errors in Section 4

title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect $K^n\times K^n$ Arrays over $K$ Roots of Unity
abstract: We give a uniform, explicit and elementary recursive construction of two-dimensional arrays with perfect (ideal) periodic autocorrelation over a \emph{fixed} alphabet of $K$ roots of unity and \emph{unbounded} size: for every integer $K\ge2$ and every $n\ge1$ a perfect $K^n\times K^n$ array whose entries are $K$-th roots of unity, given by a nested sum of floor terms. The construction works with \emph{twisted} (quasi-perfect) arrays indexed by a type $v\in\Z_K^2$, of which ordinary perfect arrays are the type $v=0$ members. For $K=2$ the types are Jedwab's generalised perfect binary arrays and the recursion specialises to the doubling constructions of Jedwab--Mitchell and Wild; for prime $K$ the arrays are the relative difference sets whose existence in abelian $p$-groups was settled by Ma and Schmidt; and the bare existence of perfect $K^n\times K^n$ arrays over $K$ roots of unity follows, for every $K$, from recent constructions of group-invariant Butson Hadamard matrices. The contribution of this note is therefore not existence but the calculus: types with arbitrary entries in $\Z_K^2$; three spectral lemmas (a twisted periodic extension of a type-$v$ array has a flat spectrum supported on one coset of $K\Z^2$; interleaving arrays whose spectra are flat on disjoint cosets gives a perfect array; and a shear of the index plane with a floor-function carry permutes types through the action of $SL_2(\Z_K)$ on $\Z_K^2$, whose orbits are the classes $\gcd(v_1,v_2,K)=g$); a one-directional lift that produces every type at side $KM$ from every type at side $M$ for arbitrary $K$; and the resulting closed index function, which is the recursive form of the floor-function arrays of \cite{Blake2017}.

title: Coactions of weak multiplier Hopf algebras
abstract: In this article, we investigate the notion of a coaction for a weak multiplier Hopf algebra. We show that there is a duality for actions and coactions of weak algebraic quantum groups. Then we obtain the well known Blattner-Montgomery duality theorem for weak algebraic quantum groups in the framework of dual pairs. We form a Morita context when the weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a two-sided faithful integral and show that the coaction is Galois if and only if the map in the Morita context is surjective. As an application, we obtain the result that a grading by any groupoid $G$ can be considered as a $\mathrm{C}G$-comodule algebra. We also construct a Morita context connecting the smash product $A\# \mathrm{C}(G)$ and the coinvariant subalgebra $A^{\mathrm{C}(G)}$. Finally we construct an isomorphism between $(R\# \mathrm{C}(G))\# \mathrm{C}G$ and $R\otimes (\mathrm{C}(G)\# \mathrm{C}G)$ when $R$ is graded by $G$.

title: Stevens' Approach to Kloosterman Sums on Split Groups
abstract: We develop a uniform framework for Stevens' approach to Kloosterman sums on split groups over $p$-adic fields. The main result reduces the bounding of Kloosterman sums to that for the so-called Plücker-constrained sets, which are certain subsets of affine spaces constrained by conditions giving by the Plücker coordinates. We then give a nontrivial bound for the Kloosterman sums on the exceptional group $G_2$. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions associated with generic representations on $G_2$.

title: The Geometry of Informativeness: A Bregman-Centroid Diagnostic for Partial Pooling in Multisite Trials
abstract: Two multisite trials can have the same informativeness yet differ in how reliably individual site effects can be estimated. We show that the informativeness index averages site-specific reliabilities on the logit scale and is a Bregman centroid under Bernoulli-Kullback-Leibler divergence. This explains the geometric mean of sampling variances and yields a measure of profile dispersion. Under stated conditions, we relate profile dispersion to estimation error and show when balanced allocation maximizes informativeness at fixed total enrollment. Simulations show that estimator performance depends on the reliability profile and whether the target is individual effects, ranks, or their distribution. An online credit recovery trial illustrates the diagnostics and their conditional posterior uncertainty. We recommend reporting informativeness with arithmetic mean reliability and profile dispersion. The accompanying R package poolinfo provides tools for computing the diagnostics, posterior summaries, and design calculations.

title: On the annular overdetermined problems with linear and power nonlinearities in $\mathbb{R}^2$
abstract: In this paper, we study two classes of partially overdetermined elliptic problems on planar annular domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$, with a fixed inner circle and a free outer boundary. The Dirichlet values are prescribed to be $1$ and $0$ on the inner and outer boundaries, respectively, while the squared normal derivative is constant on the outer boundary. For the linear law $Δu=-μu$, we establish local bifurcation under a Dirichlet nonresonance condition. For the power law $Δu=u-u^p$ with $p>1$, we take the mean outer radius as the bifurcation parameter and construct large positive radial solutions on thin annuli. The limiting profile solves $-V''=V^p$ on an interval, and the principal mixed Dirichlet--Neumann eigenvalue of its linearization determines a constant $κ_p>0$. For every fixed inner radius $λ>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $K$, we obtain a critical radius $R_K=λ+λκ_p/K+o(K^{-1})$ and a smooth local curve of positive solutions with noncircular, even, $2π/K$-periodic outer boundaries. The proof combines shape derivatives, spectral estimates, and the Crandall--Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem.

title: The Four Periodic Inscription Problem
abstract: We prove that four periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribe a family of isosceles trapezoids for every angle $θ\in(0,π)$, whose similarity types are determined by the signed areas between the quotients of the curves in the infinite cylinder. In the smooth case, the problem is identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, while the continuous case follows by a convergence argument.

title: Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients
abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.

title: Spherical-Design Oracles for Zeroth-Order Optimisation: Deterministic, Variance-Free Gradient Estimation
abstract: In this work, we develop a zeroth-order (ZO) method that estimates the gradient with minimal bias and variance. Instead of the random directions often used in the ZO literature, we consider central differences with directions given by a fixed spherical $t$-design, a finite point set that integrates every polynomial of degree at most $t$ exactly. The oracle is deterministic and thus does not induce any variance.We also propose a general finite difference method in the higher-order-smoothness regime and show the bias of both finite difference methods. We then show the convergence of the proposed ZO method via the input-to-state stability concept. Numerical experiments show the superiority of our proposed method over the existing random ZO methods.

title: Pfaffian Positivity for Convex Kernels and Optimal Matching Bounds
abstract: We show that for all positive, nonincreasing, convex functions $f : (0, \infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and for any collection of $n$ points $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1 < x_2 < \ldots < x_n$ and $n$ even, the Pfaffian of the skew matrix defined by $f(x_j - x_i)$ above the diagonal is positive. More generally, we establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for Pfaffians arising from interval decompositions, which also yields quantitative lower bounds for singly and doubly bordered Pfaffians. Choosing $f(r) = r^{-2}$ proves the three nonvanishing assertions in the conjecture of Albouy and Moeckel. Further, we show that the rainbow bound (the product over the nested matching $\{1,n\}, \{2,n-1\}, \ldots \{n/2, n/2 + 1\}$) is the unique single-matching product that bounds $\mathrm{Pf}(A_f(x))$ below uniformly over $x$ and $f$ positive, nonincreasing, convex.

title: Tactix: Towards a Programmable Strategy Interface for Flexible SAT Solving
abstract: Modern SAT solvers combine a rich repertoire of proof rules with sophisticated strategies that determine when and how to apply them. Often, the internal implementations are tightly coupled to particular strategies, making it inconvenient to define new strategies without changing solver internals. We present Tactix, a proof-producing sequential CDCL solver that incorporates a wide range of techniques in state-of-the-art solvers with a clean separation of proof rules from solving strategies. This separation enables a public interface through which users can invoke particular techniques, observe their effects, and program a wide range of solving strategies. The default strategy of Tactix is programmable over this interface and outperforms state-of-the-art solvers on benchmarks from the 2024--2026 SAT Competitions. We also use the interface to develop novel strategies tailored to challenging benchmarks from two application domains, which led to performance gains over strong baselines. We intend Tactix to serve as an infrastructure for designing and evaluating novel solving strategies. Finally, we also present a self-study of the AI-assisted development process behind Tactix.

title: Tetrahedral points and classification of Almgren-minimizing sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We prove that a two-dimensional Almgren-minimizing set in three dimensions which is sufficiently close in Hausdorff distance to a tetrahedral cone contains an interior tetrahedral point. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative regularity near tetrahedral cones and we complete the classification of entire Almgren-minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

title: On the square of an isosimple module
abstract: Let $S$ be an isosimple module, that is, a nonzero module isomorphic to every nonzero submodule of itself. In this paper, we investigate if the square $S^2 := S \oplus S$ is isoantian when $S$ is an isosimple module. If the base ring is commutative, then the answer is yes. However, for noncommutative rings this is no longer true even when $\mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is a discrete valuation ring. We also give some positive results coming from quasi-projectivity and Morita equivalence. Finally, we consider when every finite powers of an isosimple module are isoantian provided it holds for the square. Our related result says that if $S^2$ is isoantian and $E = \mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is either commutative Noetherian or right semihereditary, then every finite power of $S$ is isoantian.

title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

title: Benign Overfitting Property of the Minimum $\ell_q$ -norm Interpolant Estimator in Regression Problem via Feature Space Decomposition
abstract: This paper establishes high-probability, non-asymptotic upper bounds for the population excess risk of minimum $\ell_q$-norm interpolating estimators in linear regression, valid for all $1<q<\infty$ under three scenarios: convex concentration, mild moment assumptions and log-concavity. Consequently, we derive sufficient conditions for these estimators to exhibit benign overfitting. Our analysis hinges on a Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) framework, which naturally highlights the self-regularizing properties of minimum norm interpolants as well as the role of alignment between the signal and the features for benign overfitting. From a technical perspective, our approach circumvents the traditionally used Convex Gaussian Min-max Theorem (CGMT) by instead leveraging the Dvoretzky-Milman theorem. We emphasize that the FSD method has the potential to refine standard uniform convergence approaches. Furthermore, the isomorphic Dvoretzky-Milman theorem established herein -- proven under the three scenarios mentioned above -- for the $\ell_q$-norm is of independent mathematical interest.

title: Pillai's equation between k-generalized Pell numbers and Tribonacci numbers
abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $(P_n^{(k)})_{n\ge0}$ be the $k$-generalized Pell sequence and $(T_m)_{m\ge1}$ the Tribonacci sequence. We determine, for every $k\ge2$, all integers $c$ having at least two representations $c=P_n^{(k)}-T_m$ with $m\ge2$. The starting point is an identity of Kılıç: $P_n^{(k)}=F_{2n+1}$ for $0\le n\le k$. In the range $n\le k$ the problem therefore becomes, for all $k$ at once, Pillai's equation between odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers and Tribonacci numbers, which has exactly six solutions. In the range $n>k$ we solve the problem for $k=2$ and $k=3$ using the exact heights of the Binet coefficients; for $k\ge4$ we prove a bound for $n$ polynomial in $k$. We also use the fact that $P_n^{(k)}$ is extremely close to $F_{2n+1}$ when $k$ is large to show that $k\le414$, and treat the remaining values one by one. For $k\ge4$ there are, besides the solutions common to all $k$, exactly four further solutions, for $k=4$, $5$ and $9$. The proofs combine Matveev's theorem with the reduction method of Dujella and Pethő.

title: Markoff spectra of Hecke groups
abstract: We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index $q\ge 5$. Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.

title: Minimality of $T_z^*$-Invariant Subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$
abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary conditions for the minimality of infinite-dimensional $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$. More precisely, we prove that if $M\subset H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ is an infinite-dimensional, minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspace, then, for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$, either $\overline{P_n(M)}=H^2(\mathbb D)$ or $\overline{P_n(M)}^\perp =φ_{a,θ}H^2(\mathbb D)$ where $φ_{a,θ}$ is an atomic singular inner function and $P_n$ denotes the orthogonal projection of $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$ onto $H^2(z)w^n$. As $T_z^*$ is a universal operator on $H^2(\mathbb D^2)$, this result reduces the Invariant Subspace Problem to the analysis of these two alternatives for infinite-dimensional minimal $T_z^*$-invariant subspaces.

title: The prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_{11}$- and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups
abstract: We study prime graph complements of $\mathcal{A}_n$-solvable groups, focusing on the cases $\mathcal{A}_{11}$ and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$. These provide the first classifications of $T$-solvable groups for which $|π(T)|>4$. We develop structural and representation-theoretic tools for analyzing the possible prime graph complements and use them to obtain complete characterizations for both $\mathcal{A}_{11}$-solvable and $\mathcal{A}_{13}$-solvable groups. The methods introduced also provide a framework for studying analogous classification problems for larger alternating groups.

title: Reconfiguration graphs of mutual-visibility sets
abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices in $S$ is joined by a geodesic whose internal vertices do not belong to $S$. We define a reconfiguration graph whose vertices are the mutual-visibility sets of $G$. Two configurations are adjacent if one is obtained from the other by adding or removing one vertex or by sliding one token along an edge of $G$. The subgraphs induced by configurations of a fixed cardinality are called layers. The spanning subgraph formed by token-addition and token-removal edges is a daisy cube. We study the effects of token-sliding edges on distances and connectivity to this skeleton. For a connected host of order $n\ge3$, the vertex connectivity of the reconfiguration graph lies between $3$ and $n$, and both bounds are attained. We determine several parameters of $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{M}}(K_n)$ and describe the behavior of the model for disconnected hosts and for isometric or convex subgraphs. We also give a component-based criterion for mobile mutual visibility. For complete bipartite graphs, we use a description of feasible configurations to determine connectivity and distance bounds for fixed-cardinality layers. For trees, we show that every component of a layer of cardinality at least three is isomorphic to a Cartesian product of subtrees, obtaining exact metric formulas and characterizing the connected layers. Finally, we prove that every layer of a cycle is connected.

title: Computing Multi-Slot First-Price Pacing Equilibria at Scale via Entropic Smoothing
abstract: Pacing equilibria describe how budget-constrained advertisers clear an ad market, but computing one at production scale is hard when every request fills several slots: the allocation jumps whenever two campaigns' scores cross. We consider the first-price pacing equilibrium (FPPE) of auctions with $K$ homogeneous slots and unit-demand campaigns, whose Eisenberg-Gale dual reduces, via a TopK identity, to a convex program over bids. Regularizing each request's allocation with the binary (Fermi-Dirac) entropy gives a smooth, strictly convex dual whose gradient is exactly spend minus budget and whose evaluation splits into independent one-dimensional threshold solves, one per request. The smoothed equilibrium converges to the hard one at an explicit $O(\sqrt{T})$ rate, and a duality gap certifies how far any bids are from the hard equilibrium. We implement an efficient multi-GPU solver and test it on a production ad workload. We use it to compute an equilibrium price anchor: each campaign's hindsight equilibrium cost per key result.

title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $\varphi$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.

title: The exact Euclidean window of $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{14}]$
abstract: Let $R = \mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{14}]$, let $π= 4 + \sqrt{14}$, and let $\mathfrak{p} = (2,\sqrt{14}) = πR$ be the prime ideal above $2$. Cavallar and Lemmermeyer studied the multiplicative weighted norms $φ_{t}(x) = |N(x)|(t/2)^{v_π(x)}$ and asked for which weights $t$ they are Euclidean functions on $R$. We show that the set of these weights, the Euclidean window of $\mathfrak{p}$, is $(\sqrt{5},T]$, where $T$ is the algebraic number \[ T = \sqrt{\frac{8}{104051\sqrt{2} - 55617\sqrt{7}}} = 2.2468286690\ldots = \sqrt{5} + 0.0107606915\ldots. \] Thus the window is nonempty but not open. We also obtain the integer-valued completely multiplicative Euclidean function $2^{v_π(x)}|N(x)|^{6}$ on $R$.

title: Lifting Safety Through Reduced-Order Model Architectures: An Invariant Manifold Approach
abstract: Reduced-order model architectures are often used to decompose complex safety-critical control design tasks into tractable subproblems. In this paradigm, one must ask: when does the safety of a reduced-order model lift to safety of the full system? Taking an invariant manifold perspective, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of smooth, regular lifts of compact safe sets from reduced-order models. Our characterization relies only on asymptotic stability of an embedding of a reduced-order safe set, without additional robustness or rate conditions. We apply these results to study control barrier functions in reduced-order model architectures and lifts of safe sets through cascades. Further, we use our conditions to obtain topological obstructions to the tracking of safe, kinematic reduced-order models for mechanical systems. We conclude by using these obstructions to inform safe hierarchical control design for an underactuated satellite on SE(3).
comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, Submitted to the American Control Conference (ACC) 2027

title: On the Ramanujan-Ligozat modular unit
abstract: Let $χ$ be the quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor $N$ associated with a given real quadratic field $k$ and let $X_χ(N)$ be the double covering of $X_0(N)$ associated with $χ$. In this note, we study a modular unit $f$ on the curve $X_χ(N)$. We prove that the transform of $f$ by the Fricke involution $\mathscr{w}_N$ is the level $N$ analogue of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction introduced by Lee and Park. Furthermore, if $N$ is a positive prime discriminant, then $f$ is Ligozat's modular unit, which is known from Mazur's work on the Eisenstein ideal. We extend Ligozat's construction to any positive fundamental discriminant $N$.

title: PICKLES: Covariance-Preconditioned Kinetic Langevin Ensemble Sampler
abstract: We propose a covariance-preconditioned kinetic Langevin ensemble sampler named PICKLES. This is a kinetic analogue of the affine invariant interacting Langevin dynamics (ALDI). PICKLES uses a rectangular covariance square root as a preconditioner to avoid computing matrix inverses or square roots, leading to position and momentum variables of different dimensions. Theoretically, the continuous-time dynamics are ergodic under mild regularity and growth conditions on the potential, assuming $N>d+1$ particles and a full-rank initial ensemble. We discretize PICKLES using BAOAB or OBABO splitting, with the latter convenient for Metropolization. For Gaussian targets at stationarity, we demonstrate that Metropolized PICKLES achieves an integration step size scaling of $d^{-1/4}$ to achieve fixed acceptance probabilities, as the ensemble size and dimension increase at a fixed ratio. This matches the scaling of single particle Metropolized Hamiltonian and kinetic samplers. Numerical experiments compare sampling efficiency and estimation error with non-preconditioned, overdamped, and single-chain counterparts, demonstrating improved efficiency per gradient evaluation. On a Dark Energy Survey Year 1 3x2pt cosmology benchmark, we obtain competitive effective sample size per gradient evaluation compared to a densely preconditioned No-U-Turn Sampler.

title: Constructive Universal Approximation by Infinite-Dimensional Neural Networks via Gaussian-Weighted Ridgelet Transform
abstract: Neural networks whose inputs are functions, as in operator learning, are usually shown to be universal by existence arguments, either by reduction to finite-dimensional networks or by Stone--Weierstrass-type density; these prove that approximants exist but say little about how the parameters depend on the target. We take a constructive route. We extend the ridgelet transform, an integral transform related to the Fourier, Radon, and wavelet transforms, to continuous maps on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, replacing the Lebesgue measure that is unavailable in infinite dimensions by Gaussian weights with a homogeneous mixture on the direction space. The resulting transform has a Plancherel identity and reconstruction formulas incorporating the frame operator, the correction induced by the weights, and it assigns to each target an explicit coefficient measure, one for every admissible analysis filter. From these representations we obtain uniform approximation on compact sets for all continuous non-polynomial activations of polynomial growth, including ReLU, and, by Monte Carlo sampling of the coefficient, finite-width networks with a dimension-free $O(N^{-1/2})$ error in the width $N$ for globally Lipschitz activations and coefficients with finite variation and second moments. Explicit examples include Gaussian targets and neural-operator layers. A companion Lean~4 formalization provides machine-checked proofs, with its correspondence to the manuscript documented at https://shosonoda.github.io/lean-operator-ridgelet/ .

title: The Heesch number in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is unbounded
abstract: The Heesch number of a figure is the largest number of times that the figure can be surrounded by layers of its congruent copies. Heesch's problem asks whether finite Heesch numbers are bounded. We show that in the three-dimensional Euclidean space, and thus also in higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces, they are not: for every positive integer $h$, we construct a shape whose Heesch number is finite and at least $h$. The construction is explicit, and it starts from a four-point set of integers that does not tile the line, but packs long intervals.

title: Every Extended Metric Space Is Isometrically Embeddable into the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
abstract: Let $\mathfrak{GH}$ denote the Gromov--Hausdorff class of isometry classes of nonempty metric spaces, equipped with the Gromov--Hausdorff extended pseudometric.
