In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincaré inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.

title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
abstract: We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m δ)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{ω- 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $δ$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $δ= \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $Ω(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincaré constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.

title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map
abstract: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugallé and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted étale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.

title: Robust Local Fréchet Regression: Nonasymptotic Theory and Minimax Optimality
abstract: We develop robust local Fréchet regression for heavy-tailed responses in a general metric space and propose a distance-based median-of-means estimator. We derive nonasymptotic pointwise high-probability bounds separately under local second-order smoothness and local $1$-Wasserstein Hölder continuity, and show that the corresponding optimized rates match the classical pointwise rates for nonparametric regression. We also establish matching pointwise minimax lower bounds over embedded Gaussian regression subclasses. Remarkably, our results do not require an entropy condition on the response space. Simulation studies with positive-definite matrix-valued responses, together with a real-data application involving Wasserstein-valued responses, illustrate the robustness--efficiency tradeoff and practical performance of the proposed estimator.
comment: 62 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables. Includes supplementary material

title: The maximum number of Hamiltonian cycles in tournaments
abstract: Let $C(n)$ denote the maximum number of directed Hamiltonian cycles in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $$ C(n) = \left(\frac{\cosh 1}{\cos 1}\pm o(1)\right)\frac{(n-1)!}{2^n}. $$ The bound is asymptotically attained by the regular tournament with vertices $\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z$ where $(i,j)$ is a directed edge if $j - i \pmod n< n/2$. This answers a question of Alon and proves a conjecture of Wormald. Among the other implications of these results is asymptotically determining the maximum number of Hamiltonian paths in a tournament on $n$ vertices. We provide our own exposition of these proofs, which were originally found by GPT-5.6.

title: Asymptotic stability of a Bloch skyrmion for the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
abstract: We prove the asymptotic stability of isolated skyrmions under the flow of the two-dimensional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation. We consider a micromagnetic energy functional involving the exchange energy, the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and the Zeeman interaction. We are interested in the stability of chiral Bloch skyrmions, which are local minimizers of this energy. We prove that data in H2 which are near in the skyrmion in a slighlty stronger than H1 sense, converge with exponential rate, in H2, to the skyrmion, up to a change of gauge.

title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.

title: Exact Tail Laws for Nonlinear SGD with Infinite-Variance Gradients
abstract: With infinite-variance gradient noise, SGD can have infinite expected excess objective even when most iterates are close to the optimum. We characterize its accuracy through exact first-order tail probabilities for the last iterate of nonlinear, constant-stepsize SGD. For regularly varying innovations of index $t\in(1,2)$, the leading measure transports one large gradient shock through the local Hessian flow. This is the same measure that governs the central stable Ornstein--Uhlenbeck limit; we prove its relative accuracy at shrinking tolerances above the central scale, with state-dependent noise and a growing observation horizon. The admissible window is nonempty for every available gradient moment $p>1$. The main technical step is a moment bound at the central fluctuation scale and a lower-moment control of the nonlinear error. The result yields explicit projection and excess-objective tails, extreme quantiles, and a factor $b^{1-t}$ for fixed batch size $b$. For affine population gradients, a sharper comparison gives the same law at fixed tolerances, including random sample Hessians. Coupled simulations in dimensions one to one hundred examine relative calibration, objective quantiles, batch effects, and the error due to random curvature.

title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
abstract: Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions. First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L. Price moves during the execution window are part of that P&L, so executing more slowly reduces its variance, and because impact is concave it can also lower cost per share. Urgency comes only from alpha realized while the order is being worked. The problem is governed by the signs of two quantities: (i) the duration elasticity of impact $a$, which under a structural prior equals the impact-persistence gap $β- H$ and can take either sign; and (ii) the net urgency $ν$, the rate of alpha realization net of exposure relief. When $ν$ keeps its sign over the window, an interior optimum exists, to leading order in $T/t_f$, only when both are positive; otherwise the order should be worked at the fastest or slowest admissible pace. In the interior regime the first-order condition involves no impact coefficient, order size or volume, and the objective is flat: for a large-cap example, the window within 1% of maximal Sharpe spans more than an order of magnitude. Second, given the window, we derive the schedule shape by convex programming under an envelope cost. For any increasing per-share cost of delay $w(t)$, the KKT solution is $φ\propto (λ- w(t))_+^{1/β}$. For a Hurst-scaled envelope $w \propto t^H$, the normalized schedule depends only on $(β, H)$, has a closed form via the incomplete beta function, is front-loaded, and tapers smoothly to zero, saving 10-17% of envelope cost relative to a constant-rate (TWAP) schedule of equal duration. Whether it uses the whole window depends on a single dimensionless robustness level, for which we give a calibration.
comment: 19 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables, including an appendix

title: The distribution of $αp$ modulo one in real quadratic function fields
abstract: Matomäki proved that if $α\in\R$ is irrational, then there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $|α-a/p|\le p^{-4/3+\varepsilon}$ for a suitable integer $a$. In \cite{BaMo}, Baier and the author established analogues of this result for $\F_q(T)$ and its imaginary quadratic extensions. In this paper, we extend it to all real quadratic extensions of $\F_q(T)$.

title: Logarithmic Stability for the Inverse Boundary Problem in Three-Dimensional Isotropic Elasticity
abstract: We establish logarithmic stability for the simultaneous recovery of both Lamé parameters in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. The $L^\infty(Ω)$ estimate holds uniformly on every fixed bounded $C^{22}$ class of uniformly strongly convex coefficients, without prescribed exterior coefficients, agreement of boundary values or derivatives, or smallness assumptions on material gradients. For every integer $s\ge2$, we also obtain boundary stability estimates with exponents $(s-q)/s$ for all Cartesian derivatives of orders $0\le q<s$, where the measurement error $δ$ is the operator-norm discrepancy between the Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps. These exponents are sharp on admissible classes containing a constant material satisfying the a priori inequalities strictly. On such classes, no uniform modulus of continuity exists for boundary derivatives of order $s$. The proof combines an exact four-component reduction with finite-regularity complex geometrical optics constructions, while deriving complete matrix-valued integral identities from the Betti identity for elastic displacements. An amplitude annihilated by the leading physical adjoint lift produces, at the first nonvanishing order, the third polarization in a rank-three characteristic quotient. Holomorphically weighted matrix moments, Cauchy--Plemelj factorization, and a fixed holomorphic projection then yield quantitative control of the relative transport and recovery of both coefficients. Boundary stability estimates and paired extensions transfer the analysis from an auxiliary common-exterior setting to the original measurement domain. The exact-data argument also establishes global uniqueness for $C^{22}$ Lamé parameters.
comment: A quantitative counterpart to the uniqueness theory of arXiv:2610.14741, based on the physical-solution and matrix-moment approach. Establishes logarithmic interior stability, sharp boundary derivative estimates, and global uniqueness for C^22 Lamé parameters

title: Plancherel Decompositions and Distinctions for $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n+1}$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n}$
abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We determine the Plancherel decompositions of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n+1}(F)$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(F)$, where $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})$ denotes the mirabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and study smooth distinction for both spaces. We carry out the local unfolding procedure of arXiv:1203.0039, Section 9.5, constructing unitary isomorphisms with degenerate Whittaker models by successive Fourier transforms. The isomorphism for the even model is already stated there in Example 9.5.17. The resulting Plancherel formulas are direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions from the tempered duals of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, respectively, with product Whittaker-Plancherel measures. In the odd case, the parameter map agrees with the prediction of arXiv:2409.04677. Using closed parabolic orbits and local Rankin-Selberg integrals, we prove that all representations induced from these tempered data are distinguished for the corresponding model. We also prove that essentially square-integrable representations are not distinguished for the odd model, and that supercuspidal representations are not distinguished for the even model. For the even model with $n=1,2$, we construct distinguished square-integrable representations outside the Plancherel support. Thus, the smooth tempered distinguished spectrum can be strictly larger than the corresponding $L^2$-spectrum. For $\mathrm{GL}_5(F)$, however, we prove that an irreducible tempered representation is $\mathrm{Sp}_4(F)$-distinguished if and only if it is induced from tempered representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$.

title: Order relations for the near geometric and near spectral geometric curves
Two-bridge knot epimorphisms and intersections in the character variety
abstract: We study the SL(2,C) character varieties of hyperbolic two-bridge knot groups admitting epimorphisms onto the trefoil knot group. Ohtsuki, Riley, and Sakuma give a systematic construction of an infinite family of such knots. The character varieties of these knot groups contain a component of irreducible representations arising from the epimorphism, which is distinct from the canonical component. We prove that every affine point of intersection between this component and any other component is algebraic non-integral, and therefore detects an essential surface in the knot complement. We also determine the boundary slope of each detected surface explicitly in terms of the continued fraction expansion of the two-bridge knot.

title: Confluence relations, Hoffman basis over \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}, and the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
abstract: We express every admissible word as a $\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$-linear combination of Hoffman words and explicit confluence relations. This implies that every multiple zeta value is a linear combination of elements of the Hoffman basis with coefficients having odd denominators, as conjectured by Hirose and Sato. Combined with Brown's theorem and Furusho's characterization of the Grothendieck--Teichmüller group $\mathrm{GRT}$ by confluence relations, our result identifies the de Rham motivic Galois group of mixed Tate motives over $\mathbb{Z}$ with $\mathrm{GRT}$ and gives an alternative proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture, for which a proof was previously presented in the OpenAI Math Release.

title: Dissipative solutions for fibred Wasserstein gradient flows of Cahn-Hilliard-type energies
abstract: We study fourth-order evolution equations with a fibred Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, describing spatial transport of finitely many or a continuum of types. The driving Cahn-Hilliard-like energy combines a diagonal gradient contribution with nonlinear interactions between types. We prove subsequential convergence of the fibred Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto scheme to solutions satisfying an energy-dissipation inequality. For general type distributions, the absence of compactness in the type variable is addressed through defect-based solution concepts. On $\mathbb R^d, d\le 3$, we construct dissipative solutions satisfying an additional entropy-dissipation inequality. On smooth bounded domains in any space dimension, a coercivity estimate for the metric slope allows us to construct energy-dissipating solutions without relying on flow interchange, thereby covering non-convex domains endowed with the intrinsic length distance. In both cases, a variational comparison of the piecewise constant and De Giorgi interpolants yields a common limiting energy and strong convergence of the difference to zero without requiring strong compactness. For finitely many types, the defects vanish and the construction yields weak solutions. We further establish weak-strong uniqueness of dissipative solutions in every space dimension and of energy-dissipating solutions in dimensions $d\le5$. Combined with the respective existence results, this yields strong convergence of the variational approximations whenever a sufficiently regular, strictly positive solution exists.

title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
abstract: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,σ,χ_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.

title: The Restricted Inverse Optimal Value Problem on Shortest Path under $l_\infty$ Norm on Trees
abstract: We study the restricted inverse optimal value problem on shortest paths under the weighted $l_\infty$ norm on trees (RIOVSPT$_\infty$): adjust edge weights at minimum worst-link cost so that the shortest root--leaf path is lower-bounded by a given value $D$, a restriction on a prescribed path $P_0$. Unlike the $l_1$ version minimizing total adjustment cost, the $l_\infty$ objective controls the worst link, the criterion relevant in bandwidth pricing. We characterize feasibility through the minimum cost shortest path interdiction problem (MCSPIT$_\infty$), whose optimal solution $\hat w$ splits the instance at the first edge of $P_0$ into two independent subproblems. Relative to $\hat w$, three cases arise. The first two admit closed-form optimal solutions. The third reduces to a parametric subproblem SPIT$^0_\infty(M)$: minimize the length of $P_0$ on the gate subtree under the budget $C(\hat w)+M$ with all other root--leaf paths kept at least $D$. It is solved exactly by an iterative greedy procedure. On its value function $V(M)$, the predicate $V(M)\leq D$ is equivalent to the nonnegativity of truncated-bound margins, which are monotone, continuous and piecewise affine; the smallest such $M$ gives the optimal value, located by binary search over the edge-bound breakpoints with an exact affine threshold evaluation. The same margin test on the full tree gives a uniform algorithm for all cases. Both algorithms run in $O(n\log n)$ time. Experiments on synthetic trees agree with a linear programming baseline and illustrate the two algorithms' distinct runtime profiles.

title: Universality of Annealed Complexity in the Spherical Pure $p$-Spin Model
abstract: In an influential work, Auffinger, Ben Arous, and Černý (2013) investigated the limiting annealed complexity in the spherical pure $p$-spin model associated to the Gaussian disorder. Their results, in particular, included an explicit expression for the total number of critical points of the Hamiltonian below any given energy level. In this paper, we consider the same anneal complexity associated to a disorder interpolating between an arbitrary random variable and its Gaussian counterpart. Assuming strict subgaussianity of the former, our result shows that the annealed complexity shares the same limit as in the Gaussian case.

title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
abstract: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.

title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.

title: Toward Spectral Deferred Correction Methods for Stochastic Differential Equations
abstract: The numerical solution of stochastic differential equations is computationally very demanding. Often it is of interest to evaluate certain moments, e.g., the expectation, by Monte Carlo sampling, thus requiring the computation of numerous realizations. The discretization error of the numerical scheme induces bias in the computed Monte Carlo estimator. As popular numerical schemes, like Euler-Maruyama or Milstein, are low-order, even reasonably coarse error bounds for the simulation are costly to achieve. While the evaluation of moments requires only weak convergence, in other applications like parameter estimation, strong convergence is important, but higher-order is typically harder to obtain in the strong than in the weak sense. In this paper we develop an efficient method with the potential of achieving higher strong and weak convergence order. It is based on the smooth approximation of Brownian bridges combined with spectral deferred correction methods well known for the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations. We discuss convergence, and present numerical results.

title: Cuspidal Class Number Formulae for Intermediate Modular Curves of Prime Level
abstract: Let $X$ be a modular curve lying between $X_{0}(p)$ and $X_{1}(p)$, where $p \ge 13$ is prime. The cuspidal group of $X$ is the subgroup of its Jacobian generated by the equivalence classes of differences of cusps. In this paper, we give explicit formulae for the order of the cuspidal group, and two subgroups of it defined over the rationals.

title: Local topological zeta functions of generic symmetric and catalecticant determinantal varieties
abstract: We give explicit formulas for the local topological zeta functions at the origin of generic symmetric determinantal varieties and catalecticant determinantal varieties associated with generic Hankel matrices. In the symmetric determinant hypersurface case, the formula simplifies to a closed product expression and implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture. For catalecticant determinantal varieties, we establish a simultaneous local reduction of the determinantal ideals and obtain a closed product formula for their local topological zeta functions. Together with the known Bernstein-Sato polynomial of the Hankel determinant, this also implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture in the square catalecticant determinant case. The method used in this paper also gives short proofs of Chen-Zuo/Docamposs formula in the generic determinantal case and Chen-Shi-Xu-Zuo's formula in the skew-symmetric case.

title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by Pólya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.

title: Asymptotic gradient regularity for degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equations
abstract: This is a continuation of our recent work~\cite{WZJ26} on asymptotic gradient regularity for nonlinear parabolic equations. In this paper, we consider bounded viscosity solutions of the degenerate or singular fully nonlinear parabolic equation \begin{equation*} u_t-|Du|^γF(D^2u)=f \quad \text{in } Q_1, \end{equation*} where $ γ>-1 $, $ F $ is uniformly $ (λ, Λ)$-elliptic with $0<λ\leqΛ$, $F(0)=0$, and $f\in C^0(Q_1)\cap L^\infty(Q_1)$. Given any prescribed $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that there exists $ \varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,α)>0 $ such that \[ |γ|+\left(\fracΛλ-1\right) \leq \varepsilon \quad \Longrightarrow \quad u \in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1+α,\frac{1+α}{2}}(Q_1). \] In particular, the spatial gradient Hölder exponent can be chosen arbitrarily close to $1$ as $ (γ, \fracΛλ) \to (0,1) $. This provides a fully nonlinear counterpart to the asymptotic gradient regularity result established in~\cite{WZJ26}.

title: Fourier dimension for exactly approximable matrices
abstract: We determine the Fourier dimension of exactly approximation set for all dimensions. More precisely, let $m,n\ge1$, $\boldsymbolθ\in\mathbb R^m$, and $ψ:\mathbb N\to \mathbb R^+$ be a non-increasing approximate function. Denote by $\textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)$ the set of $m\times n$ matrices which are inhomogeneously $ψ$-approximable with shift $\boldsymbolθ$, but not $cψ$-approximable for any fixed $0<c<1$. We prove that $$\dim_{\text{F}} \textrm{Exact}_{m,n}(ψ,\boldsymbolθ)=\frac{2n}{1+τ_ψ},\ \text{whenever }τ_ψ>\frac{n}{m},$$ where $τ_ψ$ is the lower order of $ψ$ at infinity.

title: Sharp $L^6$ Fourier moments and (3,$δ$)-energy estimates for fractal measures on the truncated cone in $\R^3$
abstract: For a $δ$-separated $(δ,d)$-Katz--Tao set $P$ on the truncated cone in $\R^3$, $1<d\le 2$, we prove the sharp energy bound \[ \E_{3,δ}(P)\lesssim_{\varepsilon} δ^{-\varepsilon} \max\{δ^{-(3d+2)},δ^{-(5d-1)}\}. \] The proof applies the Fu--Ren incidence theorem to triples with a fixed sum. As a corollary we also deduce a sharp $L^6$ moment estimate for the Fourier transform of Frostman measures supported on the cone.

title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
abstract: Multi-criteria models for healthcare operations need weights that express how stakeholders trade off patient waiting time, provider workload, and operating cost, but these weights are difficult to quantify. Teams of large language model (LLM) agents, each prompted to represent a stakeholder, have been used to supply them. We propose a framework for assessing the reliability of LLM-generated preferences as inputs to multi-objective optimization and quantifying how their uncertainty affects decisions. We study explicit preferences by asking agents to rate the importance of the criteria in an outpatient appointment scheduling problem, and implicit preferences by inferring trade-offs from the agents' pairwise choices between emergency department configurations. The computational experiments show that the explicit preferences respond to the clinic's operating conditions and differ across roles, but deliberation among the agents can erase these differences, whereas simple averaging preserves them. The pairwise choices used to reveal the agents' implicit preferences depend largely on which option is presented first, and we find limited evidence that a statistical model using contextual information alongside presentation order predicts the agents' choices on new comparison pairs better than a model using presentation order alone. We then formulate robust weighted-sum optimization models to account for preference uncertainty. In most cases, these models select different schedules or configurations from those obtained using average preference weights. These results indicate that LLM-generated preferences need an audit of this kind before they are used as optimization weights in healthcare decision support.

title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
abstract: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.

title: Random Sampling of Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes
abstract: We study the effect of random sampling on stochastic processes whose finite-dimensional distributions are Bohr almost periodic under time shifts. The sampling times are generated independently by a two-sided random walk with positive increments or by a two-sided subordinator. Under a non-degeneracy condition we show that the shifted finite-dimensional distributions of the sampled process converge to those of a strictly stationary process. Consequently, if the sampled process is itself almost periodic in distribution, then it must already be strictly stationary. We further prove an $L^2$-law of large numbers for sampled averages under covariance decay and a uniform second-moment bound, and identify its limit with the mean of the stationary limit process. Finally, for $m$-dependent, $L^2$-uniformly integrable almost periodic processes, we establish a central limit theorem for the centered sampled sums, whose asymptotic variance is given by the autocovariance series of the stationary limit.

title: On the asymptotic growth of the norm of the partial sum operator on $\mathscr H^1$
abstract: We show that the norm of the partial sum operator $S_N$ on the Hardy space $\mathscr H^1$ of Dirichlet series satisfies $$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\geq\frac{1-\log 2}{2π}.$$ Combined with an upper bound of Bondarenko, Brevig, Saksman and Seip, this shows that $$\lVert S_N\rVert_{\mathscr H^1\to\mathscr H^1}\asymp\frac{\log N}{\log\log N}$$ as $N\to\infty$.

title: Line spreads of W(2n-1, q), q even
abstract: Let q be an even prime power and n \ge 2. We construct line spreads of the symplectic polar space W(2n-1,q) by replacing pairwise disjoint reguli in a Desarguesian line spread. The construction is based on partitions of the points of PG(n-1,q^2) into points of a nondegenerate Hermitian variety and Baer sublines meeting that variety in exactly one point. In the plane case, the partition is invariant under a cyclic group of order q^2-q+ 1.

title: On a series related to the Möbius function
abstract: For a natural number $n>1$ let $P^-(n)$ denote its smallest prime divisor. Alladi and Johnson proved that $\sum_{P^{-}(n)\equiv l \Mod{k}} \frac{μ(n)ω(n)}{n} = 0$ for $(l,k)=1$, and Tenenbaum showed that the partial sums of this series up to $X$ are $O_\varepsilon\bigl((\log\log X)^{5/3+\varepsilon}/\log X\bigr)$. In this article, we prove that these partial sums are in fact equal to $C(k,l)/\log X + O\bigl((\log\log X)^4/(\log X)^2\bigr)$, with an explicit constant $C(k,l)$. We also investigate the behaviour of these constants. In particular, we show under GRH that the number of reduced classes $l\Mod{k}$ for which $C(k,l)<0$ is $\varphi(k)(1- o(1))$ as $k\to\infty$.

title: On conservativity of multitype continuous-state branching processes
abstract: In [4], Grey gives a condition on the branching mechanism $ψ$ of a continuous- state branching process Z ensuring that the process is conservative. This condition is obtained from the expression of the solution of the differential equation satisfied by the Laplace exponent of Z. In higher dimensions, it is generally no longer possible to make this solution explicit and very few conditions ensuring the conservativity of the process are known. In this paper, we provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for conservativity. For dimension 2, when types cannot regenerate themselves, we give a necessary and sufficient condition and we invert the Lamperti representation of the multitype branching process.

title: Three-circle inequalities for almost harmonic functions on cylinders
abstract: The three-circle method was introduced into the blow-up analysis of harmonic maps by Qing and Tian [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 1997]. We extend this method to a class of $(τ,ε)$-almost harmonic functions on long cylinders and establish three-circle inequalities for their weighted energies. These inequalities yield a dichotomy between exponential energy decay and asymptotic dominance of a critical Fourier mode, together with a characterization of the corresponding normalized limiting profiles. In the unweighted case, we prove convergence of the averaged neck curves and identify their limiting equations under additional structural assumptions. Applications include neck analysis and energy identities for harmonic maps, solutions of Rivière's equation, $α$-harmonic maps, biharmonic approximations of harmonic maps, and Willmore surfaces.

title: Maximal estimates of the Schrödinger operators with quadratic potential for orthonormal systems
abstract: We establish an equivalence principle for local mixed-norm estimates for generalized Schrödinger propagators acting on orthonormal systems. Under suitable mixed-norm conditions, estimates for generalized propagators follow from the corresponding free Schrödinger estimates for every summability exponent $1\leβ\le2$. Applications include maximal estimates for Schrödinger equations with time-dependent quadratic potentials and for the special Hermite operator, as well as almost everywhere convergence of the associated densities. For the special Hermite operator, we also obtain a single-function maximal estimate that is sharp up to the endpoint. We construct counterexamples for the Schrödinger operator, by combining single particle and many particle constructions in complementary dimensions, yielding new necessary conditions in an intermediate range of summability exponents.

title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
abstract: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.

title: On the Length of Maximum Sum-Rank Distance Codes
abstract: The classical theory of arcs in finite projective spaces provides a powerful geometric framework for studying maximum distance separable (MDS) codes and their possible lengths. In this paper, we investigate how this perspective extends to maximum sum-rank distance (MSRD) codes, whose geometric description involves systems of linear sets rather than individual projective points. Our main goal is to understand how the block structure of an MSRD code constrains its length. In dimension three, we determine the possible intersection patterns of lines with the associated linear sets and obtain explicit formulas for their characters and the weight distribution of the corresponding codes. These results lead to new length bounds and show that the block structure comes at a cost: the presence of a block of rank at least two reduces the maximum possible total length by at least $q-1$, and sufficiently long MSRD codes must be classical, that is, MDS codes over $\mathbb F_{q^m}$. We also prove that three-dimensional one-weight MSRD codes do not exist. In arbitrary dimension, we interpret shortening geometrically as projection and establish a general projection bound that extends classical counting arguments for arcs. This yields restrictions depending explicitly on the block profile and, for full-length blocks, identifies parameter ranges in which linearized Reed--Solomon codes attain the maximum possible number of blocks. Finally, we construct an exceptional three-dimensional MSRD code over $\mathbb F_9$ with three blocks of length two and propose a sum-rank analogue of the MDS conjecture.

title: Height of minimal surfaces: sharp thresholds
abstract: The confinement theorem of [CM1] gives Euclidean volume growth for a proper minimal submanifold whose height over a plane is sublinear. Such volume growth places strong restrictions on the geometry. This leaves linear height as the natural borderline and raises the question of which, if any, linearly growing cones still force Euclidean growth. Here we determine this borderline sharply for proper holomorphic curves in $C^2$. There are two sharp thresholds for the aperture depending on the Kähler angle $θ$ of the two-plane $Π$: $\tan(θ/2)$ and $\cot(θ/2)$. No proper holomorphic curve exists below the first, every such curve is algebraic below the second, and superquadratic proper holomorphic disks exist above the second. These conclusions extend to holomorphic submanifolds of arbitrary dimension and codimension. For stationary integral varifolds there are again three regimes: sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, narrow cones of aperture $\varepsilon$ force polynomial growth with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and wide cones allow arbitrarily fast growth. The order $\varepsilon^2$ is sharp: already in $R^3$, for every small $\varepsilon>0$ there are examples in a cone of aperture $\varepsilon$ whose volume grows at least like $r^{2+\frac45\varepsilon^2}$.

title: Four New Single-Error-Correcting Binary Codes
abstract: We construct a $(16, 3072, 3)$-code, a $(17,6144,3)$-code, an $(18,12288,3)$-code and a $(19,24576,3)$-code. Consequently, we get four new lower bounds: $A(16,3) \geq 3072$, $A(17,3) \geq 6144$, $A(18,3) \geq 12288$ and $A(19,3) \geq~24576$. Each of the codes consists of a union of cosets of a linear code. The constructions are the result of a computer search executing a tabu search algorithm.

title: Cavity collapse and kinetic energy concentration in three-dimensional free-boundary Euler flow
abstract: We construct smooth axisymmetric solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations in bounded domains for which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at a finite time $T$. The velocity has a single-valued potential, and the construction applies without surface tension and with any fixed positive surface tension. Both boundary components remain embedded and disjoint before collapse, while the outer boundary converges smoothly. The terminal outer meridional domain may be any smooth bounded simply connected domain whose closure is separated from the rotation axis; the interior point generating the collapse circle and the positive concentrated energy may be prescribed independently. We prove a sharp collapse law with radius asymptotic to an explicit multiple of $(T-t)^{1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{-1/4}$, determine curvature blow-up asymptotics, and show that kinetic energy concentrates uniformly on the circle. For a canonical reflection symmetric family, we identify a common cylindrical spacetime limit and sharp velocity and pressure profiles. At every fixed spatial point in the region enclosed by the limiting outer boundary and away from the collapse circle, the velocity tends to zero while the pressure tends to positive infinity. For this family, we characterize the topology of the limiting material map and prove its optimal $1/2$-Hölder regularity and sharp $W^{1,p}$ threshold $1\le p<2$, with first derivatives in weak $L^2$ but not in $L^2$. These canonical solutions admit weak continuations that preserve mass and momentum and whose total energy drops at collapse by exactly the concentrated kinetic energy.

title: Sharp maximum estimates for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients
abstract: In this paper we obtain sharp exponents in the Aleksandrov-Bakelman-Pucci maximum estimate for linear uniformly elliptic equations with measurable coefficients, originally conjectured by Pucci in 1966 \cite{Pucci}, together with corresponding sharp results under the more natural quantification of uniform ellipticity in more than two dimensions. The proofs combine a Hessian integral inequality obtained from boundary Morse inequalities with an obstacle argument. The estimates also hold on arbitrary open sets, of finite volume, without regularity assumptions on their boundaries.

title: Arithmeticity, superrigidity, and totally geodesic submanifolds of infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
abstract: Given an infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core, we show that it (infinitely) covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. This answers the general version of a question of Oh. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also give a Ratner-type classification of $\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)$-invariant Radon measures whose support intersects the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core.

title: Faber--Krahn inequality for homogeneous normalized $p$-Laplacian type operators
abstract: We establish a sharp Faber-Krahn inequality for the normalized (or game-theoretic) $p$-Laplacian, proving that, for $p\geq 2$, the ball uniquely minimizes the principal Dirichlet eigenvalue among bounded connected Lipschitz domains of prescribed volume satisfying a uniform exterior sphere condition. More generally, we prove the same inequality for the family of homogeneous operators $|Du|^γΔ_p^N u$, with $p>1$ and $-1<γ\le p-2$. Unlike the classical $p$-Laplacian, these operators lack a variational structure, preventing the use of standard symmetrization arguments. Our proof overcomes this difficulty through a level-set approach: it relies on a flux identity for the eigenvalue, for which a variational interpretation re-emerges in the special case where the domain is a ball.

title: Locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras
abstract: For an Artin algebra $Λ$, we define the class of locally Gorenstein modules, which is a generalization of semi-Gorenstein projective modules and, therefore, a generalization of projective Gorenstein modules. For a locally Gorenstein module $X\in{\rm mod}\ Λ$ we construct $\underline{χ}_X$ a subcategory of $\underline{\rm mod}$ $Λ$ and we prove that the syzygy functor is faithful and full on $\underline{χ}_X$. Using that, we prove that the Igusa-Todorov functions $φ$ and $ψ$ vanish on the family of locally Gorenstein modules. Finally, using locally Gorenstein modules, we define the locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras, and we prove that their finitistic, and the $φ$ and $ψ$ dimensions are finite.

title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
abstract: We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $μ_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^α}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $ν_t$ and its linear evolution $μ_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $ν_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant. We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $μ_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t Δ} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.

title: Reverse Urysohn inequality for functions and functional Shephard problem
abstract: The results obtained in this paper provide a generalization of some geometric inequalities to the class of log-concave functions. They describe the relationships between the Quermassintegrals of functions and bodies, giving estimates for constants involved in functional Shephard-type problems.

title: Strongly Choquet-Deny groups and invariant strictly convex renormings
abstract: We introduce and study a strengthening of the notion of Choquet-Deny groups, which we call \emph{strongly Choquet-Deny groups}. We show that a countable group $G$ is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if for every uniformly bounded representation of $G$ on any separable Banach space $X$, there exists an equivalent $G$-invariant strictly convex norm on $X$. We provide a full classification of finitely generated strongly Choquet-Deny groups and show that a finitely generated group is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if it is virtually abelian. This fully resolves a question of Mikael de la Salle for finitely generated groups. As a further application, we show that for every uniformly bounded representation of a compact extension of an abelian topological group on any separable Banach space, there exists an equivalent invariant strictly convex norm.

title: Lifting mod $p^n$ Galois representations
abstract: We generalize the results of Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis, which lift odd mod $p$ Galois representations to geometric $p$-adic representations, to geometric lifting theorems for mod $p^n$ representations whose mod $p$ reduction is odd.

title: Orthonormal maximal estimates for fractional Schrödinger operators along Hölder curves
abstract: We establish orthonormal maximal estimates for one-dimensional fractional Schrödinger operators along curves that are Hölder continuous in time and bi-Lipschitz in space. For both the convex range $m>1$ and the concave range $0<m<1$, we obtain sharp Sobolev regularity in terms of the order $m$. As an application, we obtain almost everywhere convergence of the associated densities to their initial values along the curves. The proof combines Schatten duality with kernel estimates.

title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichmüller theory"
abstract: We first correct $\boldsymbolμ_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbolμ_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbolμ_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.

title: A general recipe for data-adaptive anytime-valid envelopes for iterative algorithms
abstract: Most convergence guarantees for iterative stochastic algorithms are stated at a fixed iteration count and do not justify stopping at a data-dependent time. Recent work has constructed anytime-valid envelopes that do, but deterministic envelopes are typically too conservative for practical stopping, and existing data-adaptive ones are derived case-by-case, each coupling a specific algorithm to a specific noise model and boundary construction. This paper provides a general recipe for constructing such anytime-valid data-adaptive boundaries for a large class of iterative algorithms. Performance measures of many of these algorithms satisfy a one-step recursion that reduces the entire error analysis to a single general requirement: time-uniform concentration for predictably weighted sums of noise. We formalize this through a strongly adapted sub-$ψ$ condition, and derive off-the-shelf boundary constructions via continuous and discrete mixtures, stitching, and product betting martingales. We show how these boundaries can be directly coupled with a separate algorithmic analysis that derives the one-step recursion to provide a class of readymade anytime-valid envelopes across diverse settings including stochastic gradient descent (SGD), temporal difference learning, and Bures-Wasserstein SGD. In particular, for SGD, our framework either recovers or significantly sharpens every existing envelope we are aware of. Our constructions come with explicit implementation details and are substantiated by numerical experiments.

title: Disproof of Wright's Problems 14 and 15 on lacunary maximal functions
abstract: We disprove the proposed weak endpoint bounds in James Wright's Problems 14 and 15 from the 2017 collection of harmonic-analysis problems. For every $d\ge1$, we exhibit a fixed compactly supported singular probability measure with Fourier decay of every order $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, for which the dyadic convolution maximal operator has infinite weak $L^1$ and infinite $H^1$ to weak $L^1$ operator norms. For every finite nonempty set of dyadic scales, both optimal weak constants equal the number of scales, with the Hardy constant measured in the specified atomic norm. Increasingly separated renewal digits provide uniform real-frequency Fourier decay while allowing the disjoint output regions needed for the positive and mean-zero tests. We first establish the fixed measure, then prove the two endpoint estimates using separate normalized tests. Finally we prove the two Fourier lemmas used in the construction.

title: Visibility Sets, Empty Pentagons, and Sufficient Conditions for Hexagons
abstract: Given a set $S$ of $n$ points in general position in the plane, we define the $C$-set $C(p,q)$ of an oriented edge $(p,q)$ as the set of extreme points of the visibility set $V(p,q)$ facing $(p,q)$. Since every point of $V(p,q)$ that is not in $C(p,q)$ gives rise to an empty convex pentagon having $(p,q)$ as a boundary edge, it is natural to study the properties of $C$-sets in order to bound the number of empty convex pentagons of $S$. We prove tight bounds on the intersection size and union complexity of $C$-sets sharing an endpoint. We also consider the problem of bounding the number of empty pentagons and hexagons in terms of the number of interior and boundary points of $S$. While the hexagon bound is weak, it offers a potential step toward a superlinear lower bound. On the other hand, the two-parameter bound for pentagons, combined with the structural results on $C$-sets, yields a simple proof of an $Ω(n^{3/2})$ bound for the number of pentagons. While this is a significant improvement over previously published bounds, a recent preprint \cite{Astudillo2026} attains a better bound using completely different methods. Thus, the primary contribution of this paper lies in the structural results about $C$-sets and the two-parameter bounds for empty pentagons and hexagons.

title: Closed geodesics on compact semi-Riemannian manifolds
abstract: We study the existence of closed geodesics on compact quotients of Lie groups endowed with left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics. We construct a compact, geodesically complete pseudo-Riemannian manifold that admits no closed geodesics. We also establish the existence of closed geodesics in several settings, with particular focus on the Lorentzian case.

title: A Mixed Elliptic--Hyperbolic Monge--Ampère Problem: Modeling and a Least-Squares Solver
authors: J. H. M. ten Thije Boonkkamp
abstract: We consider a transport problem motivated by freeform optical design of a parallel-to-far-field reflector. Classical formulations rely on either elliptic or hyperbolic Monge--Ampère equations, leading to globally convex/concave or saddle-shape reflector geometries, respectively. However, the design of smooth reflector arrays may require optical surfaces combining both types of curvature. To address this, we introduce a mixed elliptic--hyperbolic Monge--Ampère system obtained by partitioning the source domain into one elliptic and one hyperbolic subregion, and we develop a least-squares method for its numerical approximation. Numerical examples demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to compute both isolated and periodic mixed-type transport solutions, yielding smooth reflector configurations.
comment: 26 pages, 10 figures, submitted to SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing

title: Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling Models: Taxonomy, Classification and Open Challenges
abstract: Over the past three decades, a large number of optimization models have been proposed for Earth observation satellite (EOS) scheduling. The main goal of this paper is to provide an overview of these models and to relate them to the characteristics of the problems they address. To do so, we first identify the main features of EOS scheduling problems and those with the most impact on the computational complexity of the model. Based on these features, we propose a new taxonomy of satellite agility and a classification of EOS scheduling problems that allows the problem under study to be clearly identified. We then propose a classification of the optimization models into five categories, based on their time and event representations, and describe representative formulations of each category in a unified notation, together with their extensions, discussing the respective advantages and limitations. The trade-offs between the alternative representations are analyzed, showing that discrete-time formulations allow time-dependent parameters, such as transition times and image quality, to be pre-computed, which preserves the linearity of the model but makes its size depend on the adopted discretization, whereas continuous-time formulations treat these parameters as functions of the start times, which introduces nonlinearities unless simplifying assumptions are adopted. Finally, we identify the main open challenges, including the exact modeling of time-dependent transition times and the integrated scheduling of active imaging satellites.

title: Primal-dual forward-reflected splitting with linesearch for distributed min-max problems under local Lipschitz smoothness
abstract: We consider a network of finitely many agents aiming to cooperatively solve a convex-concave min-max problem combining nonsmooth terms with a smooth saddle function whose partial gradients are only locally Lipschitz continuous. Without requiring prior knowledge of the local Lipschitz moduli of the partial gradients, we propose a distributed proximal-reflected-gradient algorithm which incorporates a distributed backtracking procedure to adjust the stepsizes at each iteration. The algorithm is derived by reformulating the min-max problem as a composite monotone inclusion involving the sum of a maximally monotone operator, a linearly composed maximally monotone operator, and a single-valued locally Lipschitz continuous monotone operator. To solve this inclusion, we introduce a novel primal-dual forward-reflected splitting method with linesearch and establish its convergence using a Lyapunov-based analysis. In addition, when specialised to the min-max formulation, we derive an $\mathcal{O}(1/N)$ ergodic convergence rate for a consensus-penalised gap function. Finally, applying this splitting framework with mixing matrices yields our distributed method for consensus min-max optimisation.

title: On the crystalline Artin--Mumford invariant
abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.

title: Dihedral fields with Bloch lattice index five and quadratic subfield Q(i)
abstract: We construct infinitely many Galois extensions $M/\mathbb{Q}$ with dihedral group of order ten, quadratic subfield $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and Bloch lattice index $Q_2(M)=5$. More precisely, we specify a Chebotarev set of rational primes of density $1/50$. For every prime $\ell$ in this set, at least two of four mixed cyclic quintic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ of conductor $(25\ell)$ have this index and satisfy $K_2(O_M)(5)\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/5)^2$. A two-dimensional cup-product pencil selects the extensions. Generalized Bockstein maps, integral co-descent, and a motivic genus formula then determine the tame kernel and the subfield Bloch-lattice index. The result is unconditional.
comment: 9 pages; exact-arithmetic scripts and recorded outputs included as ancillary files

title: Classification of boundary blow-ups for the Mumford-Shah functional with Dirichlet boundary conditions
abstract: We classify boundary blow-ups of minimizers of the Mumford-Shah functional on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. At every point where the discontinuity set meets the boundary of the domain, we prove that the discontinuity set of each blow-up is the tangent line to the boundary at that point. This settles the conjecture formulated by the author in 2024.

title: A Note on Carmichael Numbers of the form $ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1)$
abstract: We study integers of the form \[ N=(d+1)(3d+1)(4d+1). \] Using Korselt's criterion, we prove that, provided the three factors are prime, $N$ is a Carmichael number if and only if \[ d\equiv4\pmod{12}. \] We also show that the special case $d=2^m$ produces only $1105$ under the prime-factor hypothesis.

title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.

title: Weighted spatial averages with missing observations: Convergence and accuracy of delta-method variance approximations
abstract: Weighted spatial averages from incomplete networks are ratios whose variance is approximated by truncating a Taylor series (the delta method). Three questions remain open: whether the series converges, how large a truncation's error is, and how it behaves as the network grows. We address these for observations missing completely at random, independently with a common probability $α$. First, the truncations, which count corrections for the denominator (the total reported weight) and for its coupling with the numerator, converge for a given network only if $α>\tfrac12$ and both corrections increase together. Second, whether or not the series converges, the error of truncations correcting only for the denominator is controlled at any network size by its coefficient of variation $ρ$, with $ρ^2=\tfrac{1-α}α\sum_iβ_i^2$ for weights $β_i$, and by the probability of rare reporting patterns. Third, for uniform weights and bounded fields, these errors vanish as the network grows, at any fixed availability. If correlations also decay with distance, the first-order approximation of earlier work has error of order $ρ^4$, against $ρ^2$ for the simplest approximation. Only truncations of equal order in numerator and denominator, beginning with the first-order truncation, avoid spurious dependence on the mean level; higher ones need not be more accurate. The exact variance for uniform weights, a single sum, shows that for correlated fields the first-order approximation overstates the contribution of missing data but is conservative overall. Concentrated weights degrade it more than $ρ$ indicates. Rainfall simulations over India illustrates results, several of which extend to self-normalized estimators.

title: Weak$^*$-weak points of continuity and very smooth points in Bochner function spaces $L^{p}(μ, X)$
abstract: Suppose that $([0,1],\mathcal{A},μ)$ is the Lebesgue measure space and $1< p<\infty$ with $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. We prove that an unit vector $h\in L^{p}(μ, X)^*$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(L^{p}(μ, X)^*)$ if and only if $\frac{h(t)}{\|h(t)\|}$ is a weak$^*$-weak point of continuity of $S(X^*)$ for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $h(t)\neq 0$, where $X$ is a Banach space such that $X^*$ is separable. As an application of this result, under the same hypothesis on $X$, we prove that a point $f\in L^p(μ, X)_{1}$ is a very smooth point if and only if $\frac{f(t)}{\|f(t)\|}\in S(X)$ is a very smooth point for almost every $t\in [0, 1]$ with $f(t)\neq 0$. We give several examples to show that these results does not hold for $p=1$.

title: Reconnection in 2D Inertial Magnetohydrodynamics
abstract: We consider two-fluid equations of inertial magnetohydrodynamics in two spatial dimensions. These equations can be recast as the evolution of two active scalars, with fluid-like interaction kernels. The equations come in two flavors, left-handed and right-handed. They are conservative and have global unique solutions for both smooth initial data and for initial data in Yudovich class $L^1(\mathbb R^2)\cap L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We prove that the inviscid limit holds in Yudovich class. We prove the persistence of $C^{2,α}$ regularity of patch boundaries through merger events for the left-handed equations. We finally show numerical examples of magnetic reconnection, validating known rigorous results and uncovering new cases.

title: A Finite Element Method for the Surface Biharmonic Problem without Stabilization or Piola Transforms
abstract: For the biharmonic problem on closed smooth surfaces, we construct a nonconforming finite element method that requires neither stabilization nor the Piola transform. The reduced enriched quartic (REQ) element relies solely on vertex values and scalar edge moments. The same local construction applies to every triangle of a piecewise planar surface. The bilinear form consists of elementwise Laplacian inner products and permits standard finite element assembly. By separating the planar vertex residual from the angle defect contribution, we establish weak discrete Miranda--Talenti-type estimates on both planar meshes and closed piecewise planar surfaces. These estimates guarantee uniform stability on sufficiently refined interpolating surface meshes. We prove the well-posedness of the method, first-order convergence in the energy norm, and second-order convergence in the broken $H^1$ and $L^2$ norms. Numerical tests on three surfaces show the predicted convergence rates and examine the discrete Miranda--Talenti constants and angle defect scaling.

title: Stability of Hyperplane Projections of the Regular Simplex and $L_p$-Projection Bodies of balls in $\ell_q^n(\mathbb{R})$
abstract: We prove stability estimates for extremal hyperplane projections of the regular simplex. We further generalize the analogous stability estimates for $\ell_q$-balls by the first named author and the monotonicity theorem for normalized ratios by Barthe and Naor to the $L_p$-setting. To this end, we derive closed formulas for the support functions of their $L_p$-projection bodies, complementing those obtained by the second named author. A key ingredient in our proofs is a stability refinement of the majorization inequality for Gaussian mixtures.

title: On the skew-curvature power law relationship in a stochastic volatility model with infinite variation Lévy jumps
abstract: The short-term blow up behaviour of the ATM-IV skew is commonly modelled by either a rough volatility process with small Hurst index or an infinite variation Lévy process in the log-price dynamics. In this paper, we examine which is the effect of mixed dynamics (i.e. rough volatility and infinite variation Lévy processes) on the ATM-IV skew and curvature. The results of the paper show that the analysis of the leading terms of the short-time expansion of both ATM-IV skew and curvature allow us to determine, from a mixed dynamics model, which mechanism originates the power-law behaviour on the skew and on the curvature. Apart from showing that the mixed model also originates a power law, it has also key implications in model design and calibration. Numerical evidences for the rough Heston model with CGMY Lévy jumps are provided.

title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem
abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set from which every vertex is reachable by a directed path of length at most two. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture asserts that every source-free digraph on $n$ vertices has a quasi-kernel of size at most $n/2$, whereas the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture asks for a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood has size at least $n/2$. Spiro proved that the former implies the latter. In this paper, we establish a weighted transfer theorem: if every nonnegative integer weighting of a source-free digraph $D$ admits a quasi-kernel whose closed out-neighbourhood contains at least a $θ$-fraction of the total weight, then $D$ has a quasi-kernel of size at most $\lfloor(1-θ)α(D)+θμ\rfloor$ for $0<θ\le1/2$, where $μ$ is the maximum matching size between a maximum independent set and its complement. Using the independent blow-up construction of Spiro, we deduce that the universal small and large quasi-kernel assertions are equivalent for every such $θ$, with no loss in the parameter. In particular, the two conjectures are equivalent. As an application, we prove the half-order bound for source-free break digraphs.

title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
abstract: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. The proof is topological, using vanishing cycles and the theory of Lefschetz pencils. As an application, combined with a construction due to Miranda, we prove that for any positive rational number $δ$ there exist a blow up $Y \to X$ at finitely many points, an ample line bundle $M$ on $Y$ and a point $x \in Y$ such that $\varepsilon(Y,M,x) = δ$; Miranda proved this when $X = \mathbb{P}^2$.

title: A Structure-Preserving Semi-Lagrangian based bi-fidelity method for the Vlasov--Poisson system with uncertainties
abstract: Uncertainty quantification for the Vlasov--Poisson (VP) systems entails repeated dynamic simulations, incurring immense computational costs. We develop a structure-preserving Semi-Lagrangian (SL) b-fidelity approximation of macroscopic observables. The MUSCL is used as a low-fidelity solver for pressureless Euler--Poisson system, allowing for a more cost-effective exploration of the stochastic parameter space. A conservative SL scheme combined with high-order discontinuous Galerkin is used as a high-fidelity solver for collisionless VP system, whose mass conservation, positivity preservation, and low numerical dissipation provide a more reliable high-fidelity snapshots for bi-fidelity reconstruction. We further derive a conditional error bound that separates projection, discretization, and model errors. Numerical experiments for both deterministic and uncertain VP problems, including multispecies and higher-dimensional settings, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves accurate and robust uncertainty propagation.

title: On the relation between transformations of SDEs and of associated Kolmogorov equations
abstract: The relationship between transformations of one-dimensional stochastic differential equations and those of the associated Kolmogorov backward equations is investigated. Stochastic transformations combining deterministic time changes, space-time diffeomorphisms, and Girsanov-type changes of probability measure are shown to be in correspondence with admissible transformations of the associated linear parabolic equations, namely the transformations preserving the parabolic structure up to the possible introduction of a zero-order potential term. A distinguished subclass of transformations, characterized by the absence of any potential term in the transformed Kolmogorov equation, is shown to coincide exactly with Doob transformations of the underlying probability measure of the SDE. This characterization further establishes a correspondence between Doob symmetries of an SDE and Lie point symmetries of the associated Kolmogorov backward equation. This correspondence, in turn, yields a constructive (probabilistic) Lie symmetry classification of autonomous Kolmogorov backward equations.

title: On flat metric nilpotent Lie algebras
abstract: We study flat left-invariant pseudo-Riemannian metrics on nilpotent Lie groups. Associated with a flat metric Lie algebra $(\mathfrak{g},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ there is a canonical affine action of the corresponding group on the vector space $\mathfrak{g}$, whose linear part is the Levi-Civita representation $L$. Combining this action with Scheuneman's theorem on pure translations in nilpotent affine groups, we prove that a flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra has a nontrivial kernel of $L$, that is, $\ker L\neq 0$. As a consequence, every $n$-dimensional flat metric nonabelian nilpotent Lie algebra is a double extension of an $(n-2)$-dimensional flat metric nilpotent Lie algebra.
comment: Theorem 3.1 is incorrct and so the proof of Theorem 1.1 is wrong. Although the main result might still true

title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.

title: On decomposition thresholds for odd cycles
abstract: We determine the asymptotic minimum-degree threshold for decompositions into cycles of a fixed odd length. We prove that, for each odd integer $\ell\ge3$, every $\eps>0$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $C_\ell$-divisible graph $G$ with minimum degree $δ(G)\ge (\ell/(2\ell-2)+\eps)n$ has a $C_\ell$-decomposition, where $C_{\ell}$ denotes the cycle of length $\ell$. This settles the remaining cases $\ell=5,7,\ldots,71$ and completes the determination of the thresholds for all odd cycles. Our main ingredient is a sharp fractional decomposition theorem for weighted triangles: for every real $a\ge 1$,every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $δ(G)\ge \left(\frac12+\frac{1}{2(a+1)}\right)n$ admits a fractional decomposition into triangles with edge weights $a,1,1$.

title: More than 8/9 zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple or on the critical line
abstract: We prove unconditionally that the lower limiting proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function, which are simple or lie on the critical line, is greater than $8/9$, with zeros counted with multiplicity.

title: Are Single-Leader-Multi-Follower Problems Particular Cases of Bilevel Optimization?
abstract: For more than 20 years, single-leader multi-follower (SLMF) problems have been treated as a more difficult class of problems in comparison to bilevel optimization. In this work we challenge this common belief, studying whether SLMF problems can be reformulated as equivalent bilevel optimization problems. We consider both optimistic and pessimistic formulations. For the optimistic case the answer is positive: We derive an equivalent bilevel problem by representing the followers' equilibria as fixed points of the solution mapping of a single optimization problem. For pessimistic problems, the situation is different. We show that every optimistic trilevel problem admits an equivalent pessimistic SLMF formulation with two followers. Conversely, for every pessimistic SLMF problem verifying a mild attainability assumption we establish an equivalent optimistic trilevel reformulation. The reformulations are easy, readily tractable, and they preserve convex and linear data. Thus, unless $\text{NP}=Σ_2^p$, we deduce as byproduct that multiple followers induce an unexpected complexity gap between optimistic and pessimistic approaches, which is not the case when considering one follower alone.

title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3.
