We also prove that the action of O(2n,2n; Z) on the space of generalized complex structures leaves the category D(J) invariant. In particular, T-duality acts trivially on D(J). We construct concrete objects associated to affine Lagrangians in the derived category associated to a symplectic torus and show that their spaces of morphisms are given by Floer cohomology. We show that our construction is consistent with the homological mirror symmetry conjecture (including its non-commutative version).

title: Mod 3 Congruence Families for twisted signatures of string manifolds in dimensions up to twenty-eight
abstract: In the paper, we establish congruences for twisted Dirac indices and signatures on closed string manifolds by specializing the two-parameter modular forms of Liu and Wang to the tangent bundle. Fourier coefficient comparisons yield uniform congruences modulo $3$ in dimensions $4k$, $1\leq k\leq7$. Suitable parameter choices give explicit formulas involving only genuine twisting bundles in dimensions $8,12,16,20,24,$ and $28$, and recover the comparisons of Chen and Han in dimension $24$. The level-one Witten genus further strengthens selected Dirac congruences to moduli $729,27,27,$ and $9$ in dimensions $16,20,24,$ and $28$, respectively. The proofs use Fourier expansions in reduced $K$-theory and integer identities obtained by clearing powers of two from the denominators before reduction modulo $3$. We also construct non-string spin counterexamples in each of the six listed dimensions and identify the additional coefficient that obstructs extending the uniform argument to dimension $32$ without further information.

title: Sharp Hessian integrability for the planar Monge--Ampère equation
abstract: We determine the optimal local integrability of the Hessian for planar convex Alexandrov solutions satisfying $$ λ\,dx\leqμ_u\leqλ^{-1}\,dx, \qquad 0<λ<1. $$ The distributional Hessian satisfies the sharp endpoint estimate $$ D^2u\in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{P,\infty}, \qquad P=\frac{1+λ}{1-λ}. $$ This settles the weak estimate proposed by De Philippis and Figalli and identifies the larger optimal exponent $P$. We further construct strictly convex $C^1$ solutions for which the distribution function of the Laplacian is comparable to $T^{-P}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. Hence both the exponent and the weak Lorentz endpoint are optimal: $L^{P,\infty}$ cannot be replaced by $L^{P,b}$ for any finite $b>0$. As applications, we obtain sharp estimates in Minty coordinates and optimal quantitative bi-Lipschitz restrictions for gradient maps, including an optimal exceptional-mass bound in quadratic-cost transport.

title: Automorphisms of Free Metabelian Lie Algebras, II
abstract: We show that every automorphism of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ of rank $n\geq 4$ over an arbitrary field $K$ is almost tame; that is, it can be expressed as a product of Chein automorphisms (also called one-row transformations). Moreover, we prove that, for $n\geq 4$, the group $\mathrm{Aut}(M_n)$ of all automorphisms of the free metabelian Lie algebra $M_n$ over a field $K$ of characteristic not equal to $3$ is generated by its linear automorphisms, together with a single quadratic and a single cubic automorphism. The same result holds for fields of any characteristic if $n\geq 5$.

title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg homology groups to group cohomology groups.

title: On the Sampling of Certain Dirichlet and Prime Sums at Gram Points and their Viscosity
abstract: Consider the Dirichlet polynomial and its prime-indexed sub-sum \[ \begin{array}{ccc} E(t) := \sum_{k\le \left[ \sqrt{ \frac{t}{2π} } \right]} \frac{e^{it\log k}}{\sqrt{k}}, & ; & E_1(t) := \sum_{\substack{p\le \left[ \sqrt{\frac{t}{2π}} \right]\\ p\ {\rm prime}}} \frac{e^{it\log p}}{\sqrt p}. \end{array} \] In this work we investigate the statistical and arithmetic properties of the sets \[ \mathcal{C}_N := \left\{ E(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \qquad \mathcal{P}_N := \left\{ E_1(g_n):1\le n\le N \right\}, \] obtained by sampling these sums at the Gram points \(g_n\) of the Hardy \(Z\)-function. We refer to \(\mathcal{C}_N\) and \(\mathcal{P}_N\) as the full and prime \(N\)-th Gram clouds, respectively. The motivation is that the approximate functional equation expresses both \(Z(g_n)\) and \(Z'(g_n)\) through different projections of the same oscillatory phase configuration, suggesting that the geometry of these sampled sums may retain information about the local behavior of nearby zeros. Numerically, we find that Gram-point sampling produces highly non-generic geometric structures: good and isolated bad Gram points occupy markedly different regions of the clouds, the prime cloud of isolated bad points splits into two anisotropic lobes, and the position along the principal direction of the folded prime cloud is strongly correlated with the viscosity of the Hardy $Z$-function \( μ(g_n)=\left|\frac{Z'(g_n)}{Z(g_n)}\right|, \) with smallest-viscosity points concentrating near distinguished extremal regions of the lobes.

title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
abstract: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |Γ|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(Γ,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(Γ,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.

title: Uniformization of Julia sets of geometrically finite rational maps
abstract: A Schottky set is the complement of a collection of disjoint open disks in the Riemann sphere. We completely characterize geometrically finite rational maps whose Julia sets are quasiconformally equivalent to Schottky sets. We also prove that the closure of the basin of infinity of a geometrically finite unicritical polynomial is quasiconformally equivalent to a Schottky set if and only if either there exists an attracting cycle and all bounded Fatou components have disjoint closures or there exists a parabolic cycle of multiplicity three. An ingredient of the proof is a new dynamical characterization of pairs of arbitrary quasicircles that are quasiconformally equivalent to pairs of tangent circles.

title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $Γ$ satisfies $\exp(Γ) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.
comment: 14 pages, Theorem 3.5 was added, references were updated

title: Defense Filters for Robust Learning of Partially Observed Dynamical Systems
abstract: Robust estimation of unknown system dynamics from partial observations under attack is a core challenge in learning for control, increasingly critical in multi-agent networks subject to adversarial data poisoning. Existing methods either require highly restrictive assumptions on the adversary or yield weak error bounds. In this paper, we consider identifying partially observed linear dynamical systems subject to adversarial attacks with an attack probability $p < 0.5$ at each time. We propose a defense-filtering framework in which a system designer leverages knowledge of the observation matrix to construct a defense filter satisfying full column rank and subspace separability conditions, which enables the evaluation of a single-attack scenario against observed data. Using this framework, we analyze the constrained $\ell_2$-norm estimator and establish finite-sample error bounds for recovering the Markov parameter matrix $G^*$. This is the first approach to provide provable system identification guarantees via a defense filter for partially observed systems subject to harsh attack environments where the attack probability approaches $0.5$.

title: Gromov-Hausdorff Convergence of Constant Scalar Curvature Kähler Metrics near the Canonical Class
abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold with semi-ample canonical bundle. For any Kähler class $[ω]$, Jian--Shi--Song proved that there exists a unique cscK metric in the class $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ when $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$, using the properness criterion of Chen--Cheng. We prove that the cscK metrics in $2πc_1(K_X)+\varepsilon[ω]$ converge, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, in the Gromov--Hausdorff topology to the metric completion of the twisted Kähler-Einstein metric on the canonical model of $X$ as conjectured by Jian--Shi--Song. Based on the technique developed in this paper, we can also give a new proof the theorem of Lee--Tosatti--Zhang on the Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of the normalized Kähler--Ricci flow on $X$.

title: Explicit Ricci-flat metrics on a special Schoen threefold
abstract: We give an explicit convergent representation of the Ricci-flat Kähler metric in a one-parameter family of classes on a fixed special Schoen threefold. The threefold resolves a shifted square-torus quotient with sixteen disjoint elliptic singular curves. Radial Eguchi--Hanson product metrics and fixed flat collars define a positive background with an exact $a^4$ volume defect. Spherical harmonics, tangential Fourier modes, Frobenius recurrences, radial ordered integrals, and the flat quotient heat kernel specify the inverse of the background scalar linearized operator. A boundary transmission series has contraction factor $1/15$. Independent weighted zeroth-order and six-dimensional Schauder estimates give the inverse bound needed for the quadratic and cubic Monge--Ampère terms. The resulting source-degree recursion converges for $0<a\le2^{-2260}$, with explicit coefficient, potential-tail, and relative metric-tail bounds. The representation uses specified kernels, prescribed integrals, and convergent series; its parameter interval is a sufficient quantitative bound on this fixed model.

title: Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
abstract: We initiate a theory of ``operator spaces" (in other words subspaces of $C^*$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^*$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one. This also characterizes the $M$'s such that all completely bounded derivations into $M$ are inner. Our main tool for this is a new characterization of injective von Neumann algebras.
comment: Minor change at end of introduction

title: On the exact quantization of BCOV Theory on Calabi-Yau Manifolds
abstract: We announce the solution of constructing perturbative quantum BCOV invariants on arbitrary Calabi-Yau manifolds. In this note, we outline the construction and present an explicit solution. The quantization includes all descendant fields and all loop orders, and expresses the quantum BCOV interaction by an explicit integration over the moduli space of marked Riemann surfaces. This canonical solution provides a mathematical construction of all higher genus BCOV invariants on compact Calabi-Yau manifolds, which are conjecturally equivalent to all higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants on the mirror.

title: An introduction to algebraic groups
abstract: We review the theory of abelian varieties and, more generally, algebraic groups, with a view toward arithmetic applications. We discuss their models over the rings of integers of number fields, their reductions modulo primes, their torsion points (together with their natural Galois action), and the interplay of these notions through characteristic polynomials of Frobenius.
comment: Expository material; contributed chapter for an upcoming book. v2: fixed errors in the bibliography

title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^ν_{λ,μ}=3$, then $c^{Mν}_{Mλ,Mμ}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{λ,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $β=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $σ$, we show that if $β$ is $σ$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $σ$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $σ$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.

title: A variation on local trilinear form
abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.

title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
abstract: Many modern learning systems are used not to select a single best action, but to sample diverse high-quality outputs. Examples include entropy-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward-guided generative modeling. Motivated by these settings, we study tilted sampling: an online learning problem in which the goal is to sample from the Gibbs distribution induced by an unknown reward function. We define sampling regret as the temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence between the learner's distribution and the Gibbs target, corresponding to the suboptimality gap in entropy-regularized reward maximization. Our framework generalizes recent sampling-based and KL-regularized formulations in bandits and reinforcement learning. Our main contribution is a general regret framework that captures the different uncertainty structure of tilted sampling and classical regret minimization. While standard regret scales as $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$ due to first-order uncertainty, sampling regret is governed by squared confidence widths, yielding logarithmic-in-$T$ regret in standard settings at fixed temperature. We develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling (UCS and TS$^2$) and provide unified regret decompositions that explain and extend recent logarithmic guarantees, including the first Bayesian sampling-regret decomposition based on new bounds for posterior-random Gibbs distributions. Our results show that learning to sample from a soft-optimal distribution is statistically distinct from learning to identify a hard optimum.

title: Reconstruction of Fano manifolds from the orthogonal to an exceptional coherent sheaf
abstract: Let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth complex Fano manifolds of dimension at least three with very ample anticanonical bundles, and let $\mathcal{E}_X$ and $\mathcal{E}_Y$ be exceptional coherent sheaves on $X$ and $Y$, respectively. We prove that a Fourier--Mukai equivalence $\mathcal{E}_X^\perp\simeq \mathcal{E}_Y^\perp$ implies $X\simeq Y$.
comment: 9 pages, result is strengthened and related work updated

title: Local Convexity and Planarity Estimates for Mean Curvature Flow
abstract: We establish local convexity and cylindrical pinching estimates for hypersurface mean curvature flow under an intermediate convexity condition and integral bounds on the mean curvature. These estimates hold after a positive waiting time and do not require pointwise upper bounds for the mean curvature on the parabolic boundary. In arbitrary codimension, we also establish local planarity estimates for properly defined flows satisfying a uniform $c_n$-pinching condition, without assuming bounded curvature. As applications, the hypersurface estimates yield convexity and cylindrical pinching for complete, spacetime-proper ancient hypersurface flows with uniform Euclidean area growth, without any bounded-curvature assumption. The planarity estimates imply that every complete, connected, spacetime-proper ancient flow satisfying the uniform $c_n$-pinching condition is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-plane for all time.

title: Isaac's Condition (TU) is false
abstract: In 2006 Isaac reduced the simple normality to base $2$ of $\sqrt s$, for $s$ not a perfect square, to a property of dyadic expansions that he called Condition~(TU): the upper frequency of the digit~$1$ in $\sqrtν$, along any subsequence, depends only on the tail of the expansion of $ν$. We show that Condition~(TU) is false, already for the full sequence. We give two proofs. The first is elementary and turns Isaac's own reduction against the condition. The second uses the theorem of Kaufman and Mosquera--Shmerkin on the Fourier decay of smooth images of self-similar measures, and gives counterexamples for almost every point of a Cantor measure. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4; the second proof uses the two cited theorems as hypotheses.

title: Cutoff Phenomenon for the Glauber-Misanthrope process in a perturbative regime
abstract: We investigate the Glauber--Misanthrope process, obtained by superposing a Misanthrope dynamics with finite site capacity and a Glauber dynamics which creates or annihilates particles one at a time at each site. In a perturbative regime around the diffusively scaled partial exclusion process, we prove the cutoff phenomenon and identify the limiting mixing time. Our approach relies on the information percolation framework developed by Lubetzky and Sly and extended by Tran, which we adapt to accommodate multiple occupancy per site and account for the two distinct correlation mechanisms generated by the Misanthrope and Glauber dynamics. Our lower bound on the mixing time holds under assumptions more general than those required for the matching upper bound.

title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(Θ_{e_{a-1}}Θ_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(ω((Δ_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $Δ_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.

title: GPU Parallel Pareto Local Search for Multi-objective QUBO
abstract: We revisit Pareto Local Search (PLS) for multi-objective quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems. Multi-objective QUBO formulations have gained increasing attention as a universal modeling method and natural input for quantum optimization. While exact methods exist, their unconstrained binary structure makes them well-suited for heuristics such as PLS. At the same time, GPUs offer a powerful classical alternative to quantum-inspired optimization. We develop an efficient GPU-based parallel implementation of PLS for multi-objective QUBO problems. Our approach combines coarse-grained and fine-grained parallelization. On the coarse-grained level, an initial set of supported solutions is generated using weighted-sum optimization, from which multiple PLS processes are started in parallel. At the fine-grained level, neighborhood exploration is parallelized on the GPU by simultaneously evaluating binary-flip candidate solutions across all objectives. Non-dominated solutions are maintained using an ND-Tree data structure to support efficient Pareto updates. The implementation combines several known PLS techniques within a unified CPU/GPU hybrid architecture. We describe the algorithmic components, the GPU-specific design decisions, and report results from a computational study evaluating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Tauberian rates and the Baire property of ideals
abstract: We study Tauberian conditions on the successive differences of real sequences which ensure that: (i) ordinary convergence coincides with ideal convergence; or (ii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal cluster point; or (iii) every ordinary accumulation point is an ideal limit point. First, we prove that an ideal $\mathcal{I}$ has the Baire property if and only if there exists a positive sequence $(r_n)$ tending to zero, with $\sum_n r_n=\infty$, such that $$ |x_{n+1}-x_n|=O(r_n) $$ is a Tauberian condition for any of the three previous statements. Second, for analytic $P$-ideals, we characterize the validity of the Tauberian rate $O(1/n)$ in terms of properties of lower semicontinuous submeasures which represent it. Lastly, in the case of statistical limit points, we prove that $o(1/n)$ is a Tauberian condition for the statement (iii), whereas $O(1/n)$ need not suffice: in this sense, $o(1/n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for (iii). On the other hand, for statistical cluster points in (ii), $O(1/n)$ is an optimal one among nonincreasing rates. For every positive null sequence $(r_n)$ with divergent sum, we also construct a summable ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $o(r_n)$ is an optimal Tauberian rate for both statements (ii) and (iii).

title: Cohomogeneity one Hermann actions and backward mean curvature flows
abstract: Principal orbits of cohomogeneity one Hermann actions form a natural class of equifocal hypersurfaces in symmetric spaces of compact type. Based on Kollross's classification of cohomogeneity one actions on irreducible symmetric spaces of compact type, we obtain the time evolution of the squared norm of the shape operator and the mean curvature along the long-time solution of the backward mean curvature flows starting from their principal orbits. These results explicitly describe the authors' previous generalization of the results of Liu-Terng on backward mean curvature flows of isoparametric hypersurfaces to this class of equifocal hypersurfaces.

title: Scalar curvature, volume, and Weil-Petersson translation length
abstract: We construct metrics on pseudoAnosov mapping tori that make every fiber an intrinsically hyperbolic stable minimal surface, and which have scalar curvature identically -6. Using this, we give a new proof (with improved constant) of an inequality bounding the hyperbolic volume of a pseudoAnosov mapping torus by the Weil-Petersson translation length (and consequently, the entropy) of its monodromy.

title: Strong NP-Hardness of Rank-2 Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
abstract: Nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two nonnegative matrices with a prescribed inner dimension~$r$. The existence of an exact NMF can be decided in polynomial time for every fixed~$r$, and a best rank-$1$ NMF in the Frobenius norm can be obtained from a truncated singular value decomposition. We prove that computing a best rank-$2$ NMF in the Frobenius norm is strongly NP-hard. Our proof uses a polynomial-time reduction from \textsc{Clique} that produces symmetric positive-definite, completely positive matrices with polynomially bounded integer entries. The same reduction also establishes strong NP-hardness of rank-$2$ symmetric NMF.

title: Volterra operators on the BMOA space of Dirichlet series
abstract: In this paper, we completely characterize the boundedness and compactness of Volterra operators on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\), the BMOA space of Dirichlet series, and estimate their essential and weak essential norms. We further prove that compactness, weak compactness, and complete continuity are equivalent for these operators. In particular, every Dirichlet polynomial symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on \(BMOA_{\mathcal D}\). We also prove that every such symbol induces a compact Volterra operator on the Bergman space of Dirichlet series \(\mathcal A_μ^1\) for every admissible measure \(μ\), extending the corresponding compactness theorem, previously established for \(1<p<\infty\), to the endpoint \(p=1\).

title: On Minimum Divergence for Distribution Reconstruction
abstract: We study the possibility of generalizing maximum-entropy reconstruction, which approximately recovers a probability distribution from finitely many (generalized) moments by minimizing the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence to a reference measure. The reconstruction lies in an exponential family and is also the best KL approximation of the unknown distribution within that family: moment matching and information projection coincide. Replacing KL by a smooth f-divergence, the reconstruction still exists in an associated family, but the best approximation property does not. Specifically, a family is called entropy-adapted if the projection of any distribution matches its moments. We show that, up to equivalence, KL is the only $C^2$ f-divergence that is entropy-adapted, whatever the choice of the generalized moments. We illustrate the consequences of this failure numerically.

title: Twisted Artin-Schreier Theory I: $(C_p \rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of local function fields
abstract: Over any field $K$ of characteristic $p$, we parametrize the $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ using pairs of elements $(g,a) \in K\times K^\times$, via a "twisted" variant of Artin-Schreier theory. Focusing on the case of the local function field $K := \mathbb F_q(\!(π)\!)$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ of characteristic $p$, we use this parametrization to obtain an exact formula for the count of all $(C_p\rtimes C_{p-1})$-extensions of $K$ with a given discriminant.

title: Provably Efficient Risk-Sensitive Offline Reinforcement Learning via Optimized Certainty Equivalents
abstract: Risk-sensitive reinforcement learning (RL) addresses decision-making under uncertainty and adverse outcomes. Learning risk-sensitive policies from fixed datasets is important when additional interaction with the environment is costly. Existing work on risk-sensitive RL focuses on online settings or specific risk measures, leaving a general theoretical understanding of its offline setting underdeveloped. In this work, we investigate efficient offline risk-sensitive RL using the optimized certainty equivalent (OCE), a general class of risk measures. We consider two formulations: dynamic-OCE RL, which applies OCE recursively at each step, and static-OCE RL, which applies a single OCE to the cumulative rewards. Under the tabular setting, we develop pessimistic value-iteration algorithms for both formulations and establish tight sublinear suboptimality bounds, explicitly capturing how risk sensitivity, encoded by utility functions, affects learning difficulty. Moreover, we establish minimax suboptimality lower bounds to characterize the problem's fundamental limits. To handle large state spaces, we further develop pessimistic least-squares value-iteration algorithms that incorporate the general OCE risk criterion into linear function approximation. We establish utility-dependent sublinear guarantees with explicit dependence on the feature dimension $d$. To our knowledge, we provide the first offline algorithms along with the first upper and lower suboptimality bounds for both dynamic- and static-OCE RL.

title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $\varphi$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petruševski and Škrekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring. We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $Δ(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.

title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.

title: Localisation of the monkey walk with an "impurity" at the origin
abstract: The monkey walk is a model of reinforced random walk introduced by Boyer and Solis-Salas as a model for the exploratory behaviour of capuchin monkeys. At each step of the walk, the walker flips a biased coin to determine whether to take a simple, symmetric random walk step on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ or to "relocate", i.e. choose a time uniformly at random in its past and jump to where it was at that time. More recently, Boyer, Falcón-Cortés, Giuggioli and Majumdar looked at a modification of the model, where the probability to relocate is $ξ_0$ when the walker sits at the origin and $ξ>ξ_0$ anywhere else. We prove that, for all $ξ_0\in (0,1)$, if $ξ$ is sufficiently close to 1, then the monkey walk "localises", i.e. the position of the walker at time $n$, $W_n$, converges in distribution without any renormalisation. (We in fact prove convergence of the occupation measure of the walker.) This is in contrast with the case when $ξ= ξ_0$, for which it is known that $W_n/\sqrt{\log n}$ converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian (we say that the walk "diffuses"). Our proof relies on seeing the monkey walk as an infinitely-many colour Pólya urn (a.k.a. measure-valued Pólya process - MVPP) and then prove convergence of this urn, which is not straightforward as theorems from the literature on MVPPs do not apply directly.

title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.

title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.

title: The Calderón operator for time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in closed waveguides
abstract: We consider the time-harmonic Maxwell's equations in a closed, cylindrical waveguide with longitudinal invariant but heterogeneous permittivity and permeability. We consider minimal smoothness assumptions, i.e., the material parameters have to be in $L^\infty$ and the cross section has to be Lipschitz with a possibly non-trivial topology. First, we show that the associated Calderón operator is well-defined and bounded in the natural trace spaces $\mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{curl}_Γ;Γ) \to \mathbf{H}_0^{-1/2}(\operatorname{div}_Γ;Γ)$. Second, we consider interior Maxwell problems obtained from using the Calderón operator and analyze their well-posedness. Furthermore, we report some additional results on the location and group velocities of the waveguide wavenumbers.

title: A geometry-independent endpoint estimate for the Littlewood--Paley $g$-function generated by the Poisson semigroup
abstract: We prove a weak $(1,1)$ estimate for the full Poisson Littlewood--Paley $g$-function on every complete Riemannian manifold without boundary, with an explicit universal constant approximately equal to $3.33606$. The estimate requires no curvature restriction, volume doubling, heat kernel bound, or stochastic completeness. The proof combines a precise Poisson maximal inequality with a convex entropy identity; local elliptic regularity identifies the extension to arbitrary real $L^1$ data. As an application, we obtain weak $(1,1)$ estimates for certain spectral multipliers represented by Poisson time derivatives with coefficients in $L^2((0,\infty),dt/t)$.

title: Feeling the generalised rough SABR boundary
abstract: We provide an in-depth analysis of a generalised rough version of the SABR volatility model, widely used in the financial industry. We specifically focus on its behaviour at the origin, whether it can reach it and how fast it may do so.

title: Surjective maps preserving quasi-nilpotence of products of operators
abstract: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and let $\mathcal B(X)$ the full algebra of all bounded linear operator on $X$. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of surjective maps $φ:\mathcal B(X)\to\mathcal B(X)$ satisfying \[ r(AB)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r(φ(A)φ(B))=0 \qquad(A,B\in\mathcal B(X)). \] Without assuming additivity, injectivity, or continuity, we show that there exists a function $γ: B(X)\mapsto \C \setminus\{0\}$ such that the map $φ$ takes one of the following forms: 1. there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X\to X$ such that : \label{eq:direct} φ(A)=γ(A)SAS^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X), 2. the space $X$ is reflexive and there exists a bounded linear or conjugate-linear, invertible operator $S:X^*\to X$ such that \label{eq:dual} φ(A)=γ(A)SA^*S^{-1},\qquad \text{ for all } \quad A\in B(X).

title: The space of polarized compactifications of an affine variety
abstract: Let $X$ be a normal affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Through the lens of non-Archimedean geometry, we study the space of polarized compactifications of $X$, consisting of pairs $(\bar X, D)$ where $\bar X$ is a normal projective variety containing $X$ as a dense open subset, and $D$ is an effective ample $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor with support equal to the complement of $X$ in $\bar X$. We identify this space with a natural class of functions--the Fubini--Study functions--on the Berkovich analytification of $X$. Through a Rees correspondence, we also give a bijection with the space of homogeneous $\mathbb{Q}$-valued, finitely generated negative non-Archimedean norms (or filtrations) on the coordinate ring of $X$. Using the above identifications, we equip the space of polarized compactifications, and numerical classes thereof, with natural metrics and identify the metric completions. The latter include a space of continuous plurisubharmonic functions in the sense of Chambert-Loir and Ducros, and a space of birational curve classes as studied by Dang and Favre.

title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.

title: On the uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for the Motsch-Tadmor model
abstract: We consider the Motsch-Tadmor model, a modification of the Cucker-Smale model for flocking dynamics that incorporates asymmetric communication weights. In the case of uniformly positive interactions, we consider the validity problem for the limiting kinetic equation, proving a uniform-in-time propagation of chaos result in the moving frame given by the consensus velocities. The result is obtained by studying the reversibility of the communication weights and by implicitly characterizing the asymptotic consensus.

title: Finite Time Noncollapsing Kähler-Ricci Flow: Gaussian Type Heat Kernel, Gromov-Hausdorff Limits
abstract: In this paper, we study heat kernel estimates along the Kähler-Ricci flow with finite time noncollapsing singularities over a compact Kähler manifold. The starting point is the type-II scalar-curvature estimate, which gives the natural parabolic scale $r\lesssim T-t$ near the singular time. By combining the distance distortion and space-time cut-off estimates of Bamler--Zhang with entropy, mean-value inequality, and conjugate heat-kernel estimates, we obtain two-sided Gaussian bounds and gradient bounds that are uniform on this scale. Under the global type-I scalar-curvature estimate, the same estimates hold on every scale. We then use these estimates and the monotonicity of the $W_1$-distance between conjugate heat flows to construct a canonical singular-time pseudo-distance. The distances $d_t$ (induced by $ω(t)$) converge uniformly to this pseudo-distance. Its metric quotient is the unique Gromov--Hausdorff limit. Finally, we apply Bamler's theory and the recent work of Hallgren--Zhang to obtain the following. Every fixed-base-point type-I blow-up admits a subsequential metric-flow limit whose time slices are singular shrinking Kähler--Ricci soliton spaces with normal complex-analytic and log-terminal structure, unique tangent cones, and a polarized Fano fibration. For moving base points, the limiting metric flow, equipped with its limiting conjugate heat flow, is a metric soliton precisely under an entropy-pinching condition.

title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_δ$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_δ$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.

title: Inverse Wave Problems on Graphs
abstract: We study inverse wave problems on finite graphs from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we consider recovery of either the initial signal or the vertex wave speeds when the other is given. Initial-signal recovery is characterized by observability of the associated finite-dimensional system, while a single experiment determines the vertex wave speeds under a zero forcing condition and a natural nonharmonicity assumption. We establish stability estimates for both recovery problems, develop a nonlinear least-squares reconstruction method, and extend the results to positively weighted graphs. Numerical simulations illustrate the reconstruction and examine the effects of observation geometry, time horizon, coefficient localization, and measurement noise on its performance. Our results are motivated both by numerical approaches to continuous inverse wave problems, where spatial discretization leads naturally to graph-based systems, and by applications in which the underlying dynamics are inherently discrete and evolve on networks.

title: Lipschitz-free spaces over separable Banach spaces and their complementability in the bidual
abstract: We prove that the Lipschitz-free space over a separable Banach space is complemented in its bidual if and only if the underlying Banach space is isomorphic to a Hilbert space. This answers negatively a long-standing question of Godefroy, Lancien, and Zizler concerning the case of $\ell_1$. We also characterize the existence of a projection of norm one and extend both characterizations to nonempty open convex subsets. Our approach yields several further results which we believe may be useful for understanding the structure of Lipschitz-free spaces over Banach spaces. These include an isometric representation of such spaces as quotients of Bochner $L^1$ spaces constructed using Gaussian measures.

title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.

title: A number field extension of Ramanujan's identity and its integral representation via the generalized Riemann $Ξ$-function
abstract: On pages 219--220 of Ramanujan's Lost Notebook appears an intriguing modular transformation whose integral representation is expressed in terms of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. In this paper, we establish a number field analogue of this identity. We also obtain an integral representation for the transformation formula associated with the functional equation of the higher power of the Dedekind zeta function recently studied by the present author and Maji. Interestingly, we recover Hardy's integral representation of the well-known Jacobi theta relation involving the Riemann $Ξ$-function. We further obtain a number-field analogue of the extended Ramanujan--Koshliakov formula established by Dixit.

title: Extremals for linear functionals on $H^p$ are outer when $0<p<1$
abstract: Let $L$ be a nontrivial bounded linear functional on the Hardy space $H^p$ of the unit disc. We prove that if $0<p<1$ and if $f$ in the unit sphere of $H^p$ satisfies $L(f)=\|L\|$, then $f$ is an outer function. The proof is short and relies on a construction due to de Leeuw and Rudin. Our result complements work of Duren, Romberg, and Shields on the failure of the Hahn--Banach theorem for $H^p$. When applied to the special case $L_k(f) = f^{(k)}(0)/k!$ for $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, it resolves two conjectures of the first-named author and Saksman and one conjecture of Suffridge.

title: Hydrodynamic limits of finite range exclusion processes
abstract: We consider variants of the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) where particles are 'large'; while in the SSEP, each lattice point is either occupied or not occupied by a single particle, in our model each particle is represented by a fixed shape, and the dynamics is so that shapes cannot overlap. In one dimension, this reduces to a finite range interaction that prevents particles from coming closer to each other than a certain distance. In this case, we prove the existence of the hydrodynamic limit, and identify the relevant macroscopic PDE, which is a porous medium equation. In two dimensions, we have no rigorous results, but instead rely on numerical simulations to approximate the diffusion matrix. Under the assumption that the hydrodynamic limit exists in two dimensions, we derive properties of the diffusion matrix based on the shape of the particles.

title: Quantum-compatible Riemannian conjugate gradient for ground-state preparation
abstract: Riemannian optimization provides a natural geometric framework for designing quantum algorithms for ground-state preparation, most notably through quantum imaginary-time evolution. However, existing geometry-aware approaches primarily employ steepest-descent updates, leaving more advanced methods from classical Riemannian optimization largely unexplored. In this work, we introduce quantum conjugate gradient descent (QCGD), a quantum-compatible implementation of Riemannian conjugate gradient that combines the steepest descent direction with information retained from previous search directions. In our numerical experiments, the proposed approach achieves faster convergence per iteration than the baseline double-bracket quantum imaginary-time evolution (DB-QITE) algorithm, and we quantify the associated circuit cost with gate counts produced by Qrisp. This improvement, however, comes at the cost of increased circuit depth for each update step, revealing a trade-off between convergence rate and implementation complexity. Nevertheless, since the circuit depth for those algorithms grows exponentially with the number of iterations, the proposed method may offer practical advantages, particularly in the early fault-tolerant regime.

title: Fundamentals of Potential theory for a hypoelliptic process
abstract: This article aims at solving open questions related to the well-posedness of Potential theory objects in a hypoelliptic setting. We provide here the expression of the equilibrium measure, capacity and electrostatic energy between smooth open sets $\A$ and $\B$ for the underdamped Langevin process. Additionally, the capacity is shown to be the solution of two variational principles which extend the well-known Dirichlet and Thomson principles in the hypoelliptic setting. Due to the degeneracy of the operator at hand, the results display significant differences with the standard elliptic setting.

title: Localization induced by Sinai disorder in mass-exchange models
abstract: We introduce a conservative continuous-mass-exchange model with quenched disorder in the splitting laws on the bonds of a finite segment. Although the dynamics is generically irreversible, its stationary mean mass profile remarkably turns out to be exactly solvable through an associated birth-and-death chain and has a Gibbs representation in terms of a simple random-walk potential. If $N$ is the number of bonds and $β$ measures the strength of disorder, the parameter $β\sqrt N$ separates an asymptotically flat profile, a Brownian crossover, and a profile localized near the global minimum. We characterize the fluctuations of macroscopic masses and identify arcsine laws for the localization centre, the competition between left and right valleys, and the disorder-averaged mass measure. Furthermore, for the extremal masses, we discuss the emergent limiting random variable in terms of the literature linking finite RW paths seen from its minimum to infinite-horizon walks conditioned to stay positive. Finally, in proximity of the localization transition point $β=0$, we show that the inverse participation ratio for the extremal masses give rises to a scaling with decay of order $k^{-3/2}$ consistent with the scaling limit of the latter conditioned walk. In the same limit, the inverse participation ratio shows a scaling form.

title: Causal Sobolev spaces and gradient flows
abstract: We develop a relaxation-based approach to Sobolev functions and Cheeger energies on metric spacetimes, in analogy with the construction used in positive signature. For an exponent $p<0$, we introduce a pre-$p$-Cheeger energy built from a local steepness constant on causal functions, and define the $p$-Cheeger energy as its relaxation in $L^0$; this yields, by construction, a convex and lower semicontinuous functional together with an associated maximal relaxed subslope. We establish natural calculus rules for the resulting Sobolev class. We then define the $p$-heat flow as the gradient flow of the $p$-Cheeger energy in $L^2$ and its generator, the $p$-d'Alembertian. Combining a Kuwada-type lemma with entropy growth estimates along the flow, we show that our notion of Sobolev class and relaxed subslope coincides with the Sobolev class and weak subslope introduced by Beran et al.

title: Visible parts and projections of the affine fractal percolation
abstract: We study the visible parts and orthogonal projections of the affine fractal percolation. We show that for the affine fractal percolation $E$, conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, almost surely the dimension of the visible part is equal to $\min\{1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ from all directions except for the major contracting direction. The visible part from the major contracting direction is notably different from the other directions, and we provide a formula for its Hausdorff and box dimensions. In addition, we show that almost surely conditioned on $E \neq \varnothing$, $\dim_{\rm H} π(E) =\min\{ 1, \dim_{\rm H} E\}$ for every orthogonal projection $π$ excluding the one onto the major contracting direction, and given $\dim_{\rm H} E >1$, these projections contain intervals.

title: The linear positive torsor presentation and arithmetic purity of strong approximation
abstract: In this article, we define a notion for varieties called linear positive torsor presentation. For varieties with a linear positive torsor presentation over number fields, we establish the arithmetic purity of strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction off the empty set. As a consequence, we recover arithmetic purity for smooth toric variety with no non-constant global section. Moreover, we classify the chain connected class for rational points on such varieties over any field of characteristic zero.

title: Backward stochastic porous media equation with polynomial growth
abstract: We investigate the well-posedness of a backward stochastic porous media equation whose nonlinear term is a polynomial operator corresponding to the slow diffusion regime. The main challenge stems from the structure of this nonlinear operator, which causes the operator to lose maximal monotonicity and prevents the use of standard weak-strong convergence techniques to identify the limit. Moreover, since the Laplace operator makes it difficult to separate the operators and discuss them individually, we attempt to obtain the of limit by investigating the global properties of the operator.

title: Quotients of Calabi-Yau Generalized Fermat manifolds and Log Enriques varieties
abstract: Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties have attracted a lot of interest in the last years. In this paper we study Enriques manifolds and Log Enriques varieties that are respectively étale and quasi-étale quotients of Calabi-Yau manifolds. We produce several examples by studying quotients of generalized Fermat manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. These are complete intersections of Fermat type manifolds all of the same degree and were described recently by Hidalgo, Hughes and Leyton-Álvarez. We describe all their quotients by a fixed-point-free automorphism. Most of the quotients are Log Enriques varieties or Calabi-Yau varieties with terminal singularities. In one case we get a family of Enriques manifolds which is a subfamily of a family described previously by Boissière, Camere and the third author, which is one of the two so far known families of Enriques manifolds of Calabi-Yau type. This family is obtained as an étale quotient of order two of a Calabi-Yau manifold complete intersection of quadrics, the other family is the Hilbert scheme of $n$ points on an Enriques surface. In the last part of the paper we show that these two families are different by computing their second Betti numbers, which are equal to one and eleven respectively.

title: Pseudoconvex domains in complex Euclidean space with finite-dimensional Bergman spaces
abstract: We construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ such that the Bergman space is one-dimensional. Based on this example, for any integers $n \geq 3, d \geq 1$, we further construct a pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ such that the Bergman space is $d$-dimensional. This disproves Wiegerinck's conjecture.

title: On a critical curl-curl system of Lane-Emden type
abstract:
We study the system $
abla	imes
abla	imes u = |v|^{q-2}v$, $
abla	imes
abla	imes v = |u|^{p-2}u$ of Lane-Emden type in $\mathbb R^3$, with exponents $p,q>3$ on the critical hyperbola $1/p+1/q=1/3$. We prove the existence of a ground state solution by reducing the system to a quasilinear fourth-order curl-curl equation and minimizing the associated Sobolev-curl quotient. A concentration-compactness argument shows there are finitely many concentration points for a Palais-Smale sequence $(u_n)$. This yields a.e. convergence of $
abla	imes
abla	imes u_n$ to $
