This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain quantitative results on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of Žubrinić, which may be of independent interest.

title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
abstract: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $Γ_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ Γ_n(M)/K_n(M)\congπ_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.

title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
abstract: We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rφ)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein. As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.

title: A Scale-Critical $μ<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
abstract: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

title: A prismatic Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
abstract: We study the category of constructible $p$-Kummer-étale sheaves on the log adic generic fiber $(\mathrm{X},\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{D}})_η$ for the stratification induced by a horizontal normal crossings divisor $\mathrm{D}$, showing that it is antiequivalent to a category of finitely generated unit Laurent crystals on the log prismatic site. We give a local description of finitely generated unit crystals on a framed log affine in terms of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules, and show pushforward compatibility for strict log smooth proper morphisms.

title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
abstract: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.

title: Allen--Cahn and mean curvature flows from Clifford hypersurfaces to equators
abstract: In this short note, using OpenAI's resolution of the Solomon--Yau conjecture, we extend our joint work with Pedro Gaspar to all dimensions $n\geq2$. We construct eternal Allen--Cahn flows on $S^{n+1}$ connecting approximations of any prescribed least-area Clifford hypersurface and equatorial sphere. We also construct infinitely many eternal integral Brakke flows from least-area Clifford hypersurfaces to equatorial spheres.

title: Universal norms of partially de Rham $B$-pairs and perfectness in Lubin--Tate Iwasawa theory
abstract: We study the behaviour of partially de Rham Selmer groups of $B$-pairs along abelian $p$-adic Lie extensions. In the cyclotomic case we compare them with the universal norms studied by Berger. For analytic Lubin--Tate $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules we prove that the $Ψ=1$ eigenspace is coadmissible of the expected rank over the algebra of analytic distributions and establish a comparison result between its Lie-algebra coinvariants and the projective limit of the partially de Rham Selmer groups of the attached $B$-pair.

title: Intersecting families of loose spanning hypertrees
abstract: A loose hypertree is a hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree. Let $b\ge3$, $n\equiv1\pmod{b-1}$, and $s:=(n-1)/(b-1)$. We determine the largest $t$-intersecting families of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees on $[n]$, simultaneously for every $1\le t\le s$, provided $n$ exceeds an explicit constant depending only on $b$. The extremal families consist of all such hypertrees containing a fixed $t$-edge loose forest whose component sizes are as equal as the divisibility condition permits. In particular, when $bt\le n$, the extremal forests are matchings. We also prove a Hilton--Milner-type bound: if $n\ge C_b(t+1)$, where $C_b$ depends only on $b$, every nontrivial $t$-intersecting family has at most $(s+1)r_{t+1}(n)$ members. Here $r_j(n)$ is the maximum possible number of loose spanning $b$-uniform hypertrees containing a fixed $j$-edge loose forest. For fixed constants $b,t$, this bound is asymptotically sharp and is $O_{b,t}(n^{2-b})r_t(n)$. The proofs combine exact forest enumeration with the intersection theorems of Kupavskii for spread families.

title: K-area bounds for smooth sphere bundles
abstract: Let $E\to B$ be a smooth $S^n$ bundle with oriented Riemannian total space $(E,g)$, where $n\ge2$. We prove K-area$(E,g)\le4πn(n-1)/σ$ whenever every fibre has intrinsic scalar curvature at least $σ>0$, independently of the dimension of $B$. In particular, unit round fibres give K-area$(E,g)\le4π$. For arbitrary metrics on two-sphere fibres, K-area is bounded by the supremum of their areas. We also obtain stronger bounds from fibrewise scalar spectra.

title: Entire solutions of higher order Briot-Bouquet equations
abstract: For a meromorphic function $f$ in the complex plane, we determine when $f$ and $f^{(k)}$ are algebraically dependent. This happens precisely when $f$ belongs to the class $W$ of elliptic functions and their degenerates, or satisfies a linear differential equation $f^{(k)} + af + b = 0$ with constant coefficients. The case of functions having a pole was settled previously. We complete the proof by treating entire solutions.

title: Deformations of Holomorphic $p$-Contact Structures
abstract: We investigate the notion of holomorphic $p$-contact structure, that we introduced recently in the scalar case with H. Kasuya and L. Ugarte and in the line-bundle case with K. Broder, in the context of a holomorphic family of compact complex manifolds equipped with a holomorphic family of holomorphic line bundles. Firstly, we show that the existence of a holomorphic $p$-contact structure is {\bf deformation-open} when a non-jumping assumption is made on the $\bar\partial$-cohomology of bidegree $(p,\,0)$. This ought to become a source of further examples of holomorphic $p$-contact manifolds. Secondly, we obtain a Berndtsson-type {\bf (semi-)positivity} result for the holomorphic vector bundle over the base induced, as a direct image, by the line bundle on the total space that supports the p-contact structures. Thirdly, we introduce a moduli space of relative holomorphic p-contact structures and we show that it is {\bf Hausdorff} and {\bf open} in a certain quotient topological space.

title: The classical homotopy category is cartesian closed
abstract: The category of all topological spaces and homotopy classes of maps is cartesian closed. In fact, the $(\infty, 1)$-category of all topological spaces and continuous maps, localised at homotopy equivalences, is cartesian closed. We model the exponential object using a topological space whose points are continuous maps equipped with putative neighbourhood filters. In general, this topological space will not even be $T_1$-separated, but the evaluation map induces a natural weak homotopy equivalence witnessing the universal property.

title: On the Complexity of Linear Programs with Parametric Constraint Matrices
abstract: While sensitivity analysis for linear programs with parametric right- hand side vectors is well established, cases involving parametric constraint matrices remain less explored. To address this gap, we investigate linear programs where the constraint matrix depends linearly on a scalar parameter. Our goal is to compute the minimum and maximum optimal values of these parametric linear programs within a fixed parameter range. This corresponds to solving two bilevel programs. We show that both decision versions of these optimization problems are NP-complete by proving both NP-hardness and membership in NP. We additionally identify three sufficient conditions on the parametric matrix under which the bilevel programs are no longer NP-hard. We introduce a reformulation for both problems, together with a Farkas-based certificate for the lower-level feasibility condition, and compare the execution time for solving them on standard benchmark instances. The experiments highlight a practical dichotomy. Although both bilevel optimizations are NP-hard, computing the parameter value corresponding to the minimum of the linear program is fast, whereas computing the value corresponding to the maximum is not. We relate this asymmetry to the parametric equality constraints, whose free dual variables leave the relaxation of the maximum reformulation unbounded.

title: Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
abstract: We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=Δu+βu\,\dot W_α$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($α=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-Δ)^{-2α}$, where $0\le 2α<d_h/d_w<1+2α$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and Hölder regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(β^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2α)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.

title: Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding
abstract: We develop dual-inertial Bregman proximal methods for convex optimization and analyze their convergence through an exact signed-drift representation. For unrestarted iterations, one-sided directional curvature control yields a last-iterate $\cO((1+\log k)/k^2)$ rate, improving to $\cO(k^{-2})$ under weighted summability. A computable energy-based safeguard guarantees a global $\cO(N^{-1})$ objective-gap bound, counting all proximal oracle calls. Under a stepsize condition and local quadratic growth with suitable kernel regularity, the safeguarded methods restart finitely and eventually converge linearly. Numerical experiments illustrate the methods on entropy regression and nonnegative least squares.

title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
abstract: For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit. We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

title: The terminal leave in random greedy hypergraph matching
abstract: Let $G$ be the terminal graph of the random triangle-removal process started from $K_n$. We prove that $e(G)/n^{3/2}\to1/(2\sqrt2)$ in $L^2$. More generally, we obtain the analogous result for any fixed strictly $k$-balanced $k$-graph. Our main tool is a more general theorem on random greedy matchings in nearly regular uniform hypergraphs with few short cycles under a stability assumption on the survival equations.

title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

title: The square achievement game on $n \times n$ boards
abstract: Two players alternately claim cells of an $n \times n$ grid; the first to hold all four corners of an axis-parallel square wins, and a full board without one is a draw. The first player has a winning strategy if and only if $n \ge 5$, which answers a question of Erickson. For $n \ge 6$ one strategy serves every board: a rule with no lookup table whose moves after the second reply are all forcing, built around the plus, a stone with the four cells at a common distance from it along the axes, a shape proposed for this game by Sirgedas in 2010. The rule is checked on the boards of size $6$ to $17$, and a simulation theorem carries one checked run on the $23 \times 23$ board to every larger board. The proofs are formalized in Lean 4, and the theorem for the rule states that the tree of its own moves is winning.
comment: 16 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Lean 4 formalization and code in the ancillary files and at https://github.com/sean-reid/square-achievement, tag v1.0.0

title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by Lévy flights under stochastic resetting
abstract: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of Lévy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative Lévy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $α\in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^α$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($α=2$). For the symmetric $α$-stable case with $α\in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.

title: Two Perfect One-Factorizations of $K_{92}$
abstract: A perfect 1-factorization of the complete graph $K_{2t}$ is a partition of its edges into perfect matchings such that the union of any two of them is a Hamilton cycle. Kotzig conjectured in 1963 that $K_{2t}$ has a perfect 1-factorization for every $t \ge 2$, but apart from some infinite families and a list of sporadic orders the conjecture is open, and $92$ was one of the nine orders up to $100$ for which no perfect 1-factorization was known. In this paper we construct two non-isomorphic perfect 1-factorizations of $K_{92}$.

title: Treewidth and the Product of Tree-Independence and Tree-Chromatic Numbers
abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\mathrm{tw}(G)$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)$, and $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)$ denote its treewidth, tree-independence number, and tree-chromatic number, respectively. We prove that every nonempty graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{tw}(G)+1\leq\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)(1+\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G))\rfloor)$. This improves the quadratic bound of Koutsoutis, Krause, Liu, Redzic, and Ueckerdt. For every pair of integers $n,k\geq2$, we construct a graph $G$ with $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}α(G)=n$, $\mathrm{tree}\text{-}χ(G)=k$, and $\mathrm{tw}(G)=Ω(nk\log_2 n)$. Thus the upper bound is best possible up to a constant factor.

title: CMC foliations on Euclidean spaces are minimal foliations
abstract: In this article, we provide a complete answer to one of the most classical conjectures in differential geometry (of foliations). More precisely, we present a complete positive answer to the classical conjecture, due to Meeks III, Pérez, and Ros (2008), that states that every foliation on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ by (possibly varying) CMC hypersurfaces is a foliation by minimal hypersurfaces. Moreover, if $n\leq 6$, such a CMC foliation must consist of parallel hyperplanes.

title: On the Structure of Radical Towers and their Parametrizations
abstract: Radical parametrizations describe algebraic varieties by means of nested radicals of polynomials, and their theory relies on three varieties associated with a parametrization: the incidence, tower and radical varieties. In this paper we revisit this framework from a computational point of view and show that it is governed by the radical tower rather than by the particular parametrization. We prove that the tower variety depends only on the tower and that the incidence variety is always irreducible, so that no prime decomposition is needed. We show how to replace a tower by an isomorphic one whose tower variety is defined by the equations of the tower, so that it can be computed without elimination. We introduce universal radical parametrizations and we use them to settle, under a natural hypothesis on the coefficients, an open case in the transformation of differential equations with radical coefficients into equations with rational coefficients. We show that radical subtowers form a lattice, which yields minimal radical parametrizations, and we give algorithms to compute them. We also prove that dominance between towers induces a unique dominant rational map between their tower varieties, through which unirationality is transferred. In addition, we study towers over subfields of $\mathbb{C}$ and, in the real case, relate the real points of the tower variety to the real domains of the associated parametrizations. Finally, we present computational experiments which show that our methods succeed in many cases where the previous approach does not finish within a reasonable time.
comment: 46 pages, 3 figures. Scripts and data of the computational experiments: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23623629

title: Generalization of Strang-Fix remark for discrete maximum principles on tetrahedral meshes
abstract: Most of qualitative properties of finite element (FE) approximations for various PDE models, in particular the validity of the discrete maximum principles (DMPs), are usually guaranteed by certain geometric properties (e.g. acuteness/nonobtuseness) of FE meshes used. In this work, we revisit the linear FE discretization of the Poisson equation and discuss, in the context of DMPs, the representation of the stiffness matrix entries in terms of the edge lengths and cotangents of the dihedral angles of the tetrahedral meshes, thus avoiding the common use of face areas and element volumes. Using this type of entry representation, certain structural properties of meshes, and simple trigonometric relations, as proposed in the two-dimensional case by Strang and Fix, we show that DMPs still hold (as the stiffness matrices remain $M$-matrices) for many tetrahedral configurations with obtuse dihedral angles. Such a relaxation of the standard acuteness/nonobtuseness conditions can be vital in practical calculations, as these angle properties are difficult to preserve in global and local mesh refinements. Several representative examples are presented.

title: Potatoes and Onions
abstract: The first major step in the theory of graph minors of Robertson and Seymour was the grid theorem, a fundamental duality result describing that any graph of sufficiently high treewidth must contain a large grid as a minor. Since this pioneering work, multiple grid theorems have been established in structural graph theory, linking various width parameters of combinatorial objects with the non-existence of grid-like obstructions. In particular, Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC'15] proved a variant of the grid theorem for directed graphs that links directed treewidth with the non-existence of topological minors of large cylindrical walls. On the other hand, to study immersions of undirected graphs $-$ another containment relation that focuses on edge-disjointness, rather than vertex-disjointness $-$ Wollan [JCTB'15] introduced a parameter, tree-cutwidth, and proved that it is dual to immersions of large walls. In this work, we present a version of Wollan's parameter for directed graphs, the directed tree-cutwidth. The main result is a grid theorem for directed tree-cutwidth, establishing that it is dual to directed immersions of large cylindrical walls.
comment: This work has been accepted for presentation at SODA 2027

title: The Kaplansky-Walker Lemma for additive categories
abstract: We establish a Kaplansky-Walker type lemma for idempotent complete additive categories with direct sums. It will be used in compactly generated triangulated categories to provide a version of Kaplansky's theorem on projective modules and an isomorphism-refinement result for direct sums of countable objects.

title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $μ$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional Gaussian discrepancy, defined as $$\mathcal D(μ):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}μ}|G_R^μ(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^μ(x):=(4πR^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,dμ(z)$. Provided that $μ$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\leδ<\infty$, the so-called width of $μ$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}μ\subseteq \bar B_δ(V+x_0),\quad δ^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(μ),$$ where $\bar B_δ(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $δ$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(μ)=0$, the support of $μ$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $μ$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $μ$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.

title: GCD and ABC inequalities for abelian varieties over function fields
abstract: We prove two height inequalities for rational points on abelian varieties over function fields of characteristic 0. The first is the GCD inequality, which shows that the height with respect to a closed subscheme of an abelian variety of codimension at least 2 is much smaller than the usual height function. This can be viewed as a compact and geometric analogue of a theorem of Levin. The second is a special case of the (geometric) abc conjecture proposed by Vojta, which compares the truncated counting function and the usual counting function. This is a compact analogue of a theorem of Guo, Nguyen, Sun and Wang, and also resolves a conjecture of Buium, which was only known for traceless abelian varieties or constant abelian varieties previously. The proofs of these inequalities follow a common three-step pattern: from microscopic local estimates to local estimates, and then to global estimates. Building on the canonical Xie-Yuan heights, we control discrete counting functions by continuous integrals of Betti forms. The main new tools are uniform Nevanlinna-type estimates for families of linear entire curves on abelian varieties; combined with covering arguments based on Besicovitch theory and averaging, these handle overlaps and gaps precisely.

title: Discrete Morse Theory for Computing Filtered Cosheaf Homology
abstract: This paper addresses the computation of persistent homology for filtrations of cellular cosheaves over a fixed cell complex, where the algebraic data vary along the filtration while the underlying topological structure remains unchanged. We extend methods from discrete Morse theory to this setting, establishing conditions under which chain complexes can be reduced while preserving the associated persistence module. Building on these results, we introduce "FilteredScythe", an algorithm that identifies Morse matchings compatible with all stages of the filtration and performs reductions using Schur complements, based on the exist "Scythe" algorithm. We prove the correctness of these reductions and establish bounds on the algorithm's time and space complexity.

title: Cwikel estimates and Weyl's laws for $L\log L$ potentials on quantum tori
abstract: We prove an $L\log L$-endpoint Cwikel estimate on quantum tori $\mathbb T_θ^d$, i.e., for every $d\geq 2$ and $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_θ^d)$, \begin{equation*} \big\|(1-Δ)^{-\frac{d}{4}}λ(x)(1-Δ)^{-\frac{d}{4}}\big\|_{\mathcal{L}_{1,\infty}} \leq C_d \Norm{x}_{L\log L(\mathbb T_θ^d)}, \end{equation*} where $λ(x)$ is the left multiplication by $x$. Our argument actually gives an abstract weak Hilbert--Schmidt estimate for multiplication operators in finite von Neumann algebras whose $L_2$-spaces admit orthonormal bases of unitaries. As a consequence, it yields a critical Sobolev embedding $W_2^{d/2}\hookrightarrow\exp(L_2)$ on quantum tori. When $θ=0$, our method also gives a simpler proof of the $L\log L$ Cwikel estimate on classical tori. As an application, we use the $C^*$-algebraic principal symbol map to prove Weyl's laws for sandwich operators \[ S(1-Δ)^{-d/4}λ(x)(1-Δ)^{-d/4}T, \] where $x\in L\log L(\mathbb T_θ^d)$ and $S,T\inΠ$, the $C^*$-algebra generated by $λ(C(\mathbb T_θ^d))$ and Fourier multipliers with continuous homogeneous symbols of degree zero. We also prove a semiclassical Weyl's law for critical Schrödinger operators with $L\log L$ potentials.
comment: 27 Pages. Revised version; improved exposition and corrected minor errors

title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
abstract: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

title: A Unified Linear Programming Approach for Maximizing Vertex-Degree-Based Indices of Trees
abstract: The problem of maximizing vertex-degree-based topological indices over trees with a prescribed order and maximum degree $Δ$ has traditionally relied on ad-hoc combinatorial arguments. In this paper, we establish a unified linear programming approach that systematically resolves these extremal problems. By formulating the optimization over degree-pair multiplicities, the search for an extremal tree reduces to minimizing a discrete dual penalty. Treating vertex degrees as continuous variables yields an analytical single-variable test condition that guarantees global optimality. We apply this framework across a diverse collection of invariants. We prove that the standard basic feasible solution is optimal for the Tangent Sombor, $SO_1$, $SO_2$, Albertson, and $σ$-irregularity indices for all $Δ\ge 3$. However, the dual optimality conditions establish exact analytical thresholds at which the standard basis loses optimality, necessitating a transition to alternative basic feasible solutions. For the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) index, the standard basis is optimal strictly for $Δ\ge 9$; for smaller maximum degrees ($3 \le Δ\le 8$), optimization shifts to an alternative edge basis, allowing us to explicitly construct and characterize all extremal trees across congruence classes, including chemical trees ($Δ\in \{3, 4\}$). Conversely, for the Triangle Volume index ($SO_{11}$), the standard basis is optimal exclusively for $Δ\le 8$, while for $Δ\ge 9$ we analytically derive a novel, degree-dependent optimal basis to explicitly construct its extremal configurations.

title: On local minimality of Hausdorff dimension for round limit sets
abstract: We address a question of Canary--Taylor and Canary--Minsky--Taylor for sufficiently symmetric compact hyperbolic $3$-orbifolds with totally geodesic boundary. We give sufficient conditions on the symmetries of such an orbifold to show that, among the complete convex cocompact structures on the interior, the structure with Fuchsian ends is a critical point (respectively, a strict local minimum) for the critical exponent. We also provide an infinite family of non-rigid examples fulfilling these conditions.

title: Von Neumann Type Inequalities for NC Operator Balls
abstract: We establish finite-dimensional von Neumann type inequalities for commuting matrix tuples in noncommutative operator balls. Let $Ω=\mathbb{D}_Q$ be the NC operator ball of a linear pencil $Q$ with linearly independent coefficients. If $Ω(1)$ admits a transitive subgroup of automorphisms with NC lifts and $Ω(1)$ has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, then $\|f(T)\|\leq C_{Ω,n}\|f\|_{H^\infty(Ω(1))}$ for every commuting tuple $T\inΩ(n)$, with $C_{Ω,n}=(2ρ_ΩK_Ω)^{n-1}$; here $K_Ω$ is the Gleason constant and $ρ_Ω$ is the sum of the suprema of the coordinate functions on $Ω(1)$. The scalar coordinate bounds persist at every matrix level. The hypotheses hold for products of row and column balls, where $ρ_Ω=d$, yielding an unconditional estimate $(2dK_Ω)^{n-1}$. For a general type I Cartan domain $R_{p,q}$, we obtain only a conditional result: the same bound holds provided the scalar domain has the bounded $H^\infty$-Gleason property at the origin, which we do not establish when $\min(p,q)\geq 2$.

title: On Partial Optimality in QUBO via Quadratic Posiform Autarkies
abstract: Partially optimal assignments (also called persistencies) allow combinatorial optimization problems to be reduced by fixing a subset of variables to values consistent with at least one optimal solution. For the quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem, such assignments can be computed efficiently via autarkies of quadratic posiforms. However, the largest autarky domain and thus the number of fixed variables can depend on the specific posiform representation. We show that every quadratic posiform with the greatest possible constant term (the roof-dual bound) yields the largest autarky domain obtainable from any quadratic posiform. By computing such a roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiform and a corresponding autarky with largest domain in polynomial time, one can therefore attain the maximum partial optimality obtainable by quadratic posiform autarkies in polynomial time. This justifies the computation of roof-dual-optimal quadratic posiforms and corresponding autarkies in popular polynomial-time algorithms and establishes that finding additional partial optimality in QUBO requires going beyond autarkies of quadratic posiforms.

title: Envelope Cubic Regularized Newton Method for Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
abstract: We study nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problem $\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})$ in which the objective has $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian and condition number $κ$. We propose envelope cubic regularized Newton method (ECRN) which applies a refined inexact cubic regularized Newton method to the envelope of the primal function $Φ(\cdot) : = \max_{\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}f(\cdot,\mathbf{y})$. We show that ECRN finds approximate second-order stationary points of $Φ(\cdot)$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrtρ\,κ^{3/4}\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ second-order oracles, improving the condition number dependence $\mathcal{O}(κ^{2})$ achieved by the best known second-order methods. Our improvement comes from the key observation that the Hessian Lipschitz parameter of the envelope is $\mathcal{O}(ρκ^{3/2})$, which is sharper than the order of $\mathcal{O}(ρκ^{3})$ for the function $Φ(\cdot)$. We also conduct a lower bound on second-order methods to show that our complexity is optimal up to a logarithmic factor.

title: Weak (1,1) Shur multipliers and the Hörmander--Mikhlin--Schur theorem
abstract: Let $S_m$ be the Schur multiplier with symbol $m$. We characterize the boundedness of $S_m:\mathcal S^1\to\mathcal S^{1,\infty}$ by approximation of weighted columns in a common finite-dimensional subspace. If $W(m)$ is the weak $(1,1)$ bound and $\fD(m)$ is the column approximation constant, then $\tfrac12W(m)\le\fD(m)\le2W(m)$. These estimates hold uniformly under amplification. We also prove the Hörmander--Mikhlin--Schur weak $(1,1)$ estimate in every Euclidean dimension under the usual integer-order condition. The proof combines Cuculescu's projections, adjacent dyadic grids and tensor polynomial interpolation on a binary block decomposition.
comment: Verified HMS condition for all dimensions

title: Generation by lazy and invertible cellular automata over the Klein four-group
abstract: Let $G=C_2\times C_2$ and $A=\{0,1\}$. We characterize the submonoid of $\text{CA}(G;A)$ generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata. A cellular automaton belongs to this submonoid if and only if, whenever it maps the two free $G$-orbits onto the same free orbit, it maps both constant configurations and some two-point orbit to the same constant. The proof gives a factorization using elementary orbit collapses and three two-cell lazy maps. The criterion yields the cardinality $59\,712$ and identifies the maps missed by a weaker constant-separation invariant. Adjoining one idempotent generates the full monoid, and the generated submonoid is contained in exactly one maximal proper submonoid, of cardinality $65\,024$. The submonoid generated by lazy maps alone has $4\,007$ elements, and for both generating sets the maximum shortest-word length is six. The criterion and the cardinalities $59\,712$ and $4\,007$ are formally verified in Lean.

title: Power quotients of plactic-like monoids
abstract: In this paper we describe the quotients of several plactic-like monoids by the least congruences containing the relations $a^{σ(a)} = a$ for $σ(a) \geq 2$ for every generator $a$. The starting point of this paper is the recent paper of Reutenauer and the first author about the stylic monoid. This monoid is the quotient of the plactic monoid by the relations $a^2 = a$ for every generator $a$. The plactic-like monoids considered here are the plactic monoid itself, the Chinese monoid, the hypoplactic monoid, the sylvester monoid, the metasylvester and hyposylvester monoids. In each case we describe a set of normal forms and the idempotents. We obtain formulae for their cardinalities and we describe their isomorphism types.
comment: 55 pages, 17 Figures, 6 Tables. It is the long version of EPTCS 403.7, 2024, pp. 12-17 that is also on arXiv: 2406.16387

title: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.

title: Quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical Schrödinger map flow
abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the energy-critical Schrödinger map into the 2-sphere: \[ \partial_{t}u = u\timesΔu, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{1+2}, \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{S}^2 \] for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. Given any integer $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate \[ λ(t)\sim \frac{\left(T-t\right)^L}{\left|\log(T-t)\right|^{\frac{2L}{2L-1}}} \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow T. \] Our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by Raphaël and Schweyer [Anal. PDE 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. However, its adaptation to a Schrödinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-Virial-Morawetz Lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.

title: Quantitative lower bound for Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers
abstract: For each positive integer $N$, let $p_i$ be the $i$-th prime for $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and set $$ Φ_N=\left\{\prod_{i=1}^{N}p_i^{a_i}:a_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,N-1\}\right\}. $$ Write $f(N)$ for the largest cardinality of a subset of $Φ_N$ containing no two distinct legs of an integral right triangle. We prove $$ N^{N-1}(\log\log\log N)\ll f(N). $$

title: Equational theories of flat semirings $S(W)$
abstract: We study the finite basis problem for flat semirings of the form $S(W)$, where $W$ is a nonempty set of nonempty words, possibly infinite. We prove that $S(W)$ is finitely based if and only if the strict interior of every word in $W$ is linear; here the strict interior of a word is obtained by deleting its first and last letters. This completely resolves an open problem raised by Jackson et al.~(J. Algebra 611: 211--245, 2022).

title: The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings
abstract: For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.

title: Jump limits of continuous multiscale diffusions: Homogenization under heavy-tailed activity bursts
abstract: We show that purely continuous microscopic diffusions can homogenize to a Markov process with genuine jumps. Consider a multiscale diffusion with time-dependent generator $\mathcal{L}_{0}+r_{t}^ε\mathcal{L}_{1}$ driven by a regenerative random environment. When the integrated activity over a regeneration cycle has a regularly varying tail of index $β\in(0,1)$, the cumulative operational clock converges to a $β$-stable subordinator, compressing finite activity-driven diffusion into vanishingly short physical time intervals. To overcome the noncommutativity of $\mathcal{L}_0$ and $\mathcal{L}_1$, we develop an extended-time parametrization paired with Khasminskii-type time discretization, establishing finite-dimensional convergence and strong semigroup convergence on $C_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ toward a jump process with nonlocal generator $\overline{\mathcal{L}}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-κ(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$. Under uniform ellipticity of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$, the fractional power $(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^β$ is identified as a $2β$-stable-like nonlocal operator. We also clarify physical-time path-topology obstructions and apply the framework to Poisson resetting pulses, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, and multiscale stochastic volatility.

title: Odd mapping cone Chern character
abstract: Our previous work established the mapping cone Chern character on the even-degree side, using the powers of the mapping cone curvature associated with the given mapping cone connection. In this paper, we carry out the odd-degree version using a trivial mapping cone connection and an automorphism on a trivial complex vector bundle. This version is based on the related odd-degree transgression.

title: Planar Disk Filters and Real Chromatic Roots at Beraha Numbers
abstract: We construct simple plane triangulations whose chromatic polynomials have real roots accumulating at every noninteger Beraha number $B_\ell=4\cos^2(π/\ell)$; the integer values $0,1,2,3$ are roots of $K_4$. The construction rests on the observation that a triangulated disk with four boundary vertices acts, inside a larger triangulation, as a transfer operator lying in a commutative three-parameter algebra. Rotating such disks by a quarter turn and composing them in series moves their eigenvalue triples around this algebra in a controllable way, and for every fixed $q\in(B_{10},4)$ one can manufacture a finite disk whose two competing local eigenvalues are strictly dominated by the third -- a physical filter. Closing a grid of such disks between two poles produces a sphere triangulation, and a fused Temperley-Lieb trace identity accounts for its chromatic polynomial completely, sector by sector, with no appeal to semisimplicity at the root of unity itself -- generic semisimplicity enters only through polynomial identities continued from $δ>2$ -- and no singular higher Jones-Wenzl projectors. In the one-cap sector a Krein-type argument shows that every sweep word has exactly one expanding eigenvalue; Gram-form inertia controls every other sector uniformly in the width. At odd Beraha indices the trace coefficient of the expanding eigenvalue vanishes; at even indices two copies of that eigenvalue cancel between adjacent sectors, and a short real-variable lemma converts either situation into genuine real roots converging to the target. Indices below eleven are treated by elementary families, exact outward-rounded integer certificates, and one explicit disk at $B_{10}$ combined with Tutte's golden identity. All graphs are ordinary, simple, unweighted plane triangulations.
comment: 34 pages, 4 figures. Reproduction package (exact-certificate and audit scripts, run logs, SHA-256 manifest) included as ancillary files and archived at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23371280

title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.

title: LLCT: Learnable Linear Canonical Transform Family with Stability for Visual Feature Processing
abstract: Visual structures are often characterized by directional geometry, local oscillation, and spatial--frequency coupling. To overcome the limitations of conventional spatial convolutions mainly operating on fixed Euclidean coordinates, this article develops the learnable linear canonical transform (LLCT) framework that learns parameters within the linear canonical transform (LCT) family. The framework treats the LCT family as parameterized analytical views spanning spatial, Fourier, and intermediate linear canonical representations. The framework has the following two complementary modes. The Linear Canonical Riesz Transform (LCRT) mode combines learned linear canonical coordinates with regularized Riesz-type directional responses at sites chosen for geometric and local-structural refinement. The learnable LCT mode provides the integrated responses for latent feature sites. We establish the parameter stability of the LCT representation under admissible perturbations of the canonical matrices. Both modes use chirp multiplication and the fast Fourier transform (FFT) to preserve feature dimensions and support automatic differentiation. Experiments on crack segmentation and single-image deraining evaluate the above two modes with multiple backbones. On four segmentation backbones, the full LCRT mode gives the highest reported point estimates of F1 and IoU for the crack class among the tested variants. The learnable LCT mode gives higher values in 30 of 32 paired PSNR and SSIM measurements across four deraining backbones and four datasets. In ablation studies, the full model has the highest reported PSNR and SSIM among five tested configurations.

title: Scaled Companion Linearizations for Coefficientwise Backward Stability
abstract: A central goal in solving a polynomial eigenvalue problem is to compute eigenpairs that are exact for a nearby polynomial, with each coefficient perturbation bounded by a modest multiple of unit roundoff times that coefficient's norm. A backward stable eigensolver for a linearization does not automatically provide this coefficientwise relative guarantee. Scaling can improve accuracy, but a single scaling may not work across a widely spread spectrum. We construct a family of scaled companion linearizations that covers the nonzero complex plane. Each linearization is paired with a region and an eigenvector recovery rule for which the backward-error amplification factor is bounded at exact pencil eigenvectors, independently of coefficient norm disparities. Tropical roots guide the construction, and their multiplicities reduce the number of required solves. These results provide a basis for coefficientwise relative backward stability across the spectrum.

title: Topological degree for singular $N$-mean field equations
abstract: We determine the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Dirichlet $N$-mean field equation on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\geq2$, for every positive nonresonant parameter and singular exponents $-1<α_i\leq0$. The formula depends only on the Euler characteristic of the domain and the weights $(1+α_i)^{N-1}$. We also identify the homotopy type of every sufficiently negative variational sublevel with the corresponding weighted barycenter space. We prove quantization of interior concentration masses and exclude boundary concentration and residual diffuse mass. The degree computation uses common descent fields for nearby parameters, bounds for their trajectories, and a finite-dimensional comparison with the Euler characteristic of negative sublevels. Annular averaging and dilation provide local contractions, which are extended to establish the sublevel homotopy equivalence. The arguments apply to the nonlinear, possibly degenerate $N$-Laplacian with singular weights, without requiring a global Palais--Smale condition or isolation and nondegeneracy of solutions.

title: An upper bound for valuations of elliptic nets at primes of bad reduction
abstract: Let $E/K$ be an elliptic curve over a field defined by the short Weierstrass equation and let $\mathbf{P}=(P_1, P_2) \in E(K)^2\setminus \{(O, O), (\pm P, \pm P)\}$ be a pair of non-torsion points, where $O$ denotes the point at infinity. We give a uniform upper bound for the quantity $\min(ν(Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})), 2ν(Ψ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})))$, where $ν$ is a normalised discrete valuation associated to primes where $E$ has bad reduction and $Ψ^2_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$, $Φ_{(v_1, v_2)}(\mathbf{P})$ are rational functions for describing $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points $[v_1]P_1+[v_2]P_2$ on $E$, higher--dimensional analogues of division polynomials $ψ^2_n, φ_n$ known as net polynomials. They are also elliptic nets, which are $n$--dimensional arrays with values in $K$ satisfying the same nonlinear recurrence relation that division polynomials do as well. Hence, they are useful in studying counting problems on elliptic curves.

title: Benign Degeneracy for First-Order Methods in Exact Boolean Moment-SOS Relaxations
abstract: Pseudo-Boolean optimization -- minimizing a polynomial over $\{\pm 1\}^n$ -- includes MAX-CUT, binary quadratic optimization, and Ising models. The moment-sum-of-squares (Moment-SOS) hierarchy provides certified semidefinite relaxations that are often empirically exact at low order. We ask: once a relaxation is exact, how difficult is the resulting semidefinite program (SDP) to solve with first-order methods? Exactness does not imply regularity. At every order $d \ge 2$, a unique rank-one moment optimum is primal degenerate; moreover, if one optimal SOS certificate is strictly complementary, then the certificate set is positive-dimensional and contains singular boundary points. Thus first-order methods may converge to such singular points, around which pointwise analyses that assume regularity at the limit cannot establish a local linear convergence rate. We show that, for exact Boolean Moment-SOS relaxations in their canonical quotient form, this degeneracy is nevertheless benign. We develop an abstract mechanism, which we call residual-field rigidity, that propagates regularity from the relative interior of the optimal set to its singular boundary. It requires neither the primal nor the dual optimal solution to be unique, and it is equivalent to the first-order stall directions of the residual coinciding with the tangent directions of the optimal set. For Boolean Moment-SOS, unique rank-one exactness and the existence of one strictly complementary certificate suffice to trigger this mechanism, yielding a uniform error bound around the entire optimal set. Consequently, ADMM, sGS-ADMM, and PDHG converge eventually linearly from every initialization, even when their limiting certificate is singular. Finally, outside a lower-dimensional semialgebraic exceptional set of Boolean objectives, these hypotheses hold simultaneously at every uniquely rank-one exact order.

title: A new generalization of parking functions: $ρ$-Naples parking functions
abstract: We introduce a new model of parking functions, called $ρ$-Naples parking functions, in which each car has a certain number of spots to check preceding its preferred one before looking for available spots by moving forward. This notion, where each car has its own number of previous spots to check, generalizes that of Naples parking function, where this number is the same for all cars. We start by showing that, for a given sequence of preferences for each car, a successful parking strategy (that is, an assignment of how many backward spots each car is allowed to check) remains successful if we increase the number of backwards spots to check for some of the cars. This means that the set of successful strategies for a given parking preference is an up-set in the lattice of parking strategies, which raises the intriguing question of characterizing such up-sets. Though we are not able to completely solve this problem, we provide a characterization of those successful strategies which minimize the total number of allowed backward steps for a given parking preference, and we determine a lower bound for the number of cars which are allowed to move backwards (also showing that it can be attained). To conclude, we analyze the specific situation in which each car can take at most one backward step, and we completely characterize the set of successful parking preferences in this case.

title: Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Matérn DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Matérn kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.

title: Geometric $C^1$-stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow
abstract: We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or Hölder control of the normal is assumed. The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre. For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. This produces an instantaneously smooth evolution with the same eventual convexity and smooth exponential convergence.

title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.

title: Nonexistence of Strongly Regular Graphs via Gegenbauer Positivity and SRG Counting
abstract: This paper develops a natural extension of the multipoint spherical semidefinite method of Liao and Yu~\cite{LY}, studying the interaction between semidefinite programming and strongly regular graph counting. Starting from the positive semidefinite kernels furnished by Gegenbauer polynomials, we express weighted kernel sums and counting identities in the same labelled induced-subgraph counts. Eliminating the counting equations gives a semidefinite feasibility problem. Numerical dual solutions guide the construction of rational certificates, whose contradiction identities are verified exactly. Our aim is a systematic method that treats many parameter sets through the same construction. For least eigenvalue $-3$, it gives new counting certificates for $(351,140,73,44)$, $(550,162,75,36)$, $(703,182,81,35)$ and $(1344,221,88,26)$, previously excluded by Liao and Yu~\cite[Theorem~1]{LY}, and for six additional parameter sets: \[ \begin{array}{@{}lll@{}} (375,102,45,21), & (405,132,63,33), & (441,88,35,13),\\ (476,133,60,28), & (540,147,66,30), & (575,112,45,16). \end{array} \] Seven certificates use Gegenbauer positivity and counting information alone at the displayed orders. The cases $v=375,441,575$ additionally use proved short-vector restrictions, unique vertex extensions, and integer common-neighbour inequalities. The proofs end in displayed inequalities with incompatible signs. Their justification is given by the dual identities and the proved positivity and counting relations; accompanying code automates the longer rational arithmetic.

title: The finite basis problem and subvariety intervals for max-plus matrix semirings
abstract: Let $S=(\N,\max,+)$ be the max-plus algebra of the nonnegative integers, and let $\overline S$ be obtained from $S$ by adjoining $-\infty$ as a semiring zero. We first prove that the varieties generated by the full matrix semirings $\Mat_n(S)$ and by the upper triangular matrix semirings $\UT_n(\overline S)$ form strictly ascending chains. Every interval between distinct members of either chain has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and contains a chain and an antichain of that cardinality. The proof uses finite syntactic semirings associated with prime-cycle languages and an independent family of identities. We then construct finite commutative ai-semirings from languages of monomials closed under divisibility and prove their bounded-variable property by cancellation, explicit integer evaluations and independence in a free abelian group. A loop-block identity for upper triangular matrices and dimension-independent cubic-padding identities for full matrices show that every variety in each of the above intervals has infinite axiomatic rank. In fact, every variety between $\V(S)$ and the variety generated by all full matrix dimensions has infinite axiomatic rank. These varieties are therefore nonfinitely based, also relative to the ai-semiring axioms. Finally, for every fixed full matrix dimension, we prove equational equivalence over all six positive or nonnegative integer, rational and real coefficient domains. The original convex-ideal countermodels and their full-matrix transfer proof are recalled separately for comparison; they are not used in the algebraic proofs. Throughout, the signature consists of two binary operations and contains no constant symbols.

title: On the Hardy--Littlewood--Chowla conjecture
abstract: An old conjecture dating back at least to Hildebrand's work in 1989, asserts that the Möbius function exhibits cancellation on shifted primes; that is, $$\sum_{p\le x}μ(p+2)=o(π(x)),\quad \text{or equivalently}\quad \sum_{n\le x}Λ(n)μ(n+2)=o(x).$$ This is also a well-known model case for the parity problem in sieve theory. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. As an application, we show that each of the two sets $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=1\}$ and $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=-1\}$ has asymptotic density $1/2$ among the primes $p$ with $μ^2(p+2)=1$: \begin{equation*} \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\#\{p\le x:\ μ(p+2)=κ\}} {\#\{p\le x:\ μ^2(p+2)=1\}} =\frac12, \quad κ\in\{-1,\,1\}. \end{equation*}

title: Chow groups of symmetric products of projective spaces
abstract: Let $\operatorname{SP}^{d}(\mathbb{P}^{n})$ denote the $d$-th symmetric product of complex projective space. We prove that its integral cycle class map is split injective and has finite cokernel annihilated by $d!$. We also compute the ranks of its Chow groups. By constructing compatible integral retractions on Chow groups and singular homology, we prove that addition of a fixed point induces an isomorphism on the Chow group of $q$-dimensional cycles whenever $d\geq q$. For $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq 6$, we construct a nonalgebraic class of order two in codimension two. Its image generates a direct summand of the cycle class cokernel and remains nonalgebraic after addition of fixed points. Consequently, integral surjectivity fails both at certain finite stages with $q\leq d$ and in the infinite symmetric product. We further identify the codimension two cokernel with third unramified cohomology of the smooth configuration space. Finally, we provide an example where multiplication by an even integer annihilates a nonzero Chow class of order two.
comment: 20 pages. Content unchanged; fixed garbled text in abstract

title: The parity module of a matroid
abstract: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded Möbius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.

title: Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures
abstract: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_φ.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_φ$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$

title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or Lévy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.

title: Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields
abstract: We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.

title: Stable atomic vector bundles are 1-obstructed
abstract: We prove that every stable atomic (twisted) vector bundle on a projective hyper-Kähler manifold is 1-obstructed. In the appendix, we construct a simple atomic object that is not 1-obstructed, providing a counterexample to Beckmann's conjecture.

title: $χ$-Independence for BPS Invariants of Warped Local Curves
abstract: A well-known conjecture of Toda's asserts that the BPS invariants associated to a Calabi--Yau threefold are independent of the chosen Euler characteristic. We answer the question in the affirmative for a certain class of local surfaces, which we call warped local curves. Along the way we show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a warped local curve can be written as the global critical locus of a function. We also show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a curve fibration over $\mathbb{A}^1$ is the global critical locus of a function.

title: Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Drézet and Ballico-Ellia
abstract: We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.

title: Characterization of $C^{1,α}$-domains in terms of Carleson-type $\varepsilon$-coefficients
abstract: Let $Ω=Ω^+\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary and let $Ω^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus\overline{Ω^+}$. For $x\in\partialΩ$, $r>0$, define \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r):=\frac{1}{r^n} \inf_{H^+}\mathcal{H}^n\left(((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^+)\setminus Ω^+) \cup ((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^-)\setminus Ω^-)\right), \end{equation*} where $\mathcal{H}^n$ stands for $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and the infimum is taken over all open affine half-spaces $H^+$ such that $x\in \partial H^+$. Here $H^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus \overline{H^+}$. In this work we prove that $Ω$ is a $C^{1,α}$ open set, with $0<α<1$, if and only if there exists some constant $C>0$ such that $\varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r)\leq C\,r^α$ for all $x\in\partialΩ$ and all $0<r\leq \mathrm{diam}(\partialΩ)$.

title: Fast spectral methods for Volterra integral equations
abstract: We develop novel methods for the fast construction of spectral approximations to smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra integral operators and for the fast evaluation of smooth nonlinear Volterra integrals. The proposed methods employ the Duffy mapping, which transforms the original indefinite integral into a definite integral and maps the original causal triangular domain to a square, thereby avoiding any artificial extension of the kernel function. For smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra operators, the resulting approximations are almost-banded and lower-banded, respectively. The $N\times N$ principal finite section of these approximations can be constructed in $O(N)$ and $O(N^2)$ flops, respectively, via recurrence relations. For Volterra integrals with a smooth kernel that depends nonlinearly on a given function, recurrence relations lead to fast evaluation with a complexity of $O(N^2\log N)$ when the function is approximated by a degree-$N$ Chebyshev approximant. These spectral approximations and evaluation procedures give rise to fast and stable spectral methods for solving Volterra integral equations, as well as a broad class of problems involving Volterra integral operators. Extensive numerical experiments show that these spectral methods significantly outperform existing methods in terms of stability, speed, accuracy, and ease of implementation.

title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

title: Old structures, a vanishing formula
abstract: We identify a normalization defect in a determinantal construction of fourth-order Hahn difference equations and compare its scalar equation with Foupouagnigni's 1998 elimination and its published 2001 counterpart. On an explicit positive orthogonal family, all five prescribed coefficients vanish: the formula gives \(0=0\) and imposes no condition. Along an explicit regular perturbation, division by \(\varepsilon^2\) before specialization recovers a nonzero equation on that family, the same scalar equation as the correctly executed old shift-and-eliminate procedure. On the common nondegenerate domain specified below, both constructions give the same scalar operator up to a nonzero rational factor. The first-order degree bounds follow directly from valid identities of 1998; preserving cancellations gives a bound that can be arbitrarily sharper on explicit admissible inputs, together with exact top coefficients and cancellation criteria. Explicit coefficient formulas do not by themselves yield a new scalar equation on this domain. Our comparison does not exclude corrective or expository contributions; additional computational gain or exceptional coverage must be demonstrated.

title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
abstract: Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.

title: Macdonald dual in the semilocal case and applications to local homology and local cohomology
abstract: This paper extends Macdonald's duality theory and Cuong-Nam's local homology theory -- which is in some sense dual to the local cohomology theory of A. Grothendieck [Gro1] -- to semilocal noetherian rings equipped with the $J$-adic topology. By overcoming the key structural obstructions of the semilocal setting via Zöschinger's structure theory and semilocal Matlis duality, this work establishes topological limit duality isomorphisms and links local homology with local cohomology. Ultimately, this framework provides the foundational machinery required to extend the classical results of Macdonald [Mac] and Cuong-Nam [C-N1] to the semilocal setting.

title: New bounds for $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ shifted convolution sums
abstract: Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$.
