We also treat the corresponding sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. Here $λ_π(1,n)$ denotes the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke--Maass cusp form $π$ on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$ denotes the number of representations of a positive integer $n$ by a positive definite integral binary quadratic form $\mathcal{Q}$. The proof combines two circle methods with a different organization of the major-arc analysis. A key point is that the nonzero Poisson frequencies are kept together in a single coefficient vector, rather than estimated separately, which allows them to be controlled by a finite matrix norm. The zero Poisson frequency is treated separately: its contribution is independent of the reduced residue class, and its arithmetic mean cancels the constant term in the complementary Jutila weight before absolute values are taken. We make this cancellation explicit, including the relevant normalization and local factors. The same mechanism extends to the binary quadratic-form setting, while the remaining Jutila contribution is handled by the available correlation estimates.

title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
abstract: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ Γ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(μ)-1-m_3(μ)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ Ψ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(μ)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
abstract: A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $ε$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}ε.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $ε$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative Kähler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative Kähler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, Hörmander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.

title: Reciprocal Dynamics in Polynomial Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
abstract: Alternating reciprocal transformations of polynomial divisibility systems couple an orbit of integer points to a rational dynamical system on polynomial coefficients. For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, we prove universal four-step return to rational gauge classes. Weighted primitive representatives preserve integral continuation through nondegenerate jumps using only exact division and coefficient gcds; the stronger requirement of monic integral representatives is governed by endpoint $p$-adic valuation defects. After one integral block, constant-term valuations evolve by an explicit unimodular matrix whose trace depends only on $nm$. This gives finite-order behavior for $nm<4$, parabolic dilations for $nm=4$, and hyperbolic dynamics for $nm>4$. In the hyperbolic case, invariant thresholds, irrational eigencones, and discrete valley formulas give finite criteria for forward and bi-infinite integral coefficient orbits, although failure can be delayed arbitrarily long. Every positive-constant canonical monic coefficient chain admits an explicit positive rational four-phase gauge. At $nm=4$, geometric gauges reduce nondegenerate compatible rational point orbits to two-periodic affine recurrences, hence to sequences satisfying linear recurrences with constant coefficients. Polynomial identities of degree at most $h$ on each invariant conic admit certificates from $2h+1$ initial phase states, while integral unimodular recurrence models yield periodic modular obstructions. For $nm>4$, eventually positive normalized point orbits tending to infinity have hyperbolic logarithmic growth and cannot satisfy such linear recurrences. Finally, separated auxiliary-relation transport reduces rational rank to at most one after two alternating jumps; quadratic specialization gives exact local saturation criteria and persistence results across periodic, parabolic, and hyperbolic orbits.

title: Continuous-Time q-Learning with Nonsmooth Value Functions: a BSDE Approach
abstract: We study continuous-time q-learning for entropy-regularized diffusion control without assuming classical differentiability of the value function. Rewards and admissible policies need only be Borel measurable, which allows discontinuous rewards. The diffusion coefficient $σ$ is action independent and locally uniformly elliptic, and the drift is $b_0 + σψ$, with $b_0$ action independent and $ψ$ bounded. In this setting the q-function involves the value only through its gradient. For each admissible policy, we represent its value by a backward stochastic differential equation (BSDE) and prove that this value is continuous before the horizon, although the data are only measurable. Replacing the gradient with a measurable representation of the martingale integrand, we define the q-function up to Lebesgue-null sets and recover the classical definition when the value function is smooth. We then prove policy improvement, when the Gibbs update is admissible, and martingale characterizations of the value and the q-function from on-policy and off-policy observations. Here the candidate value need only be continuous before the horizon, and actions are sampled on a deterministic finite grid and held constant between sampling times. Under an integrability condition on the reward, we show that a second BSDE gives an upper bound for the optimal value, attained when its Gibbs policy is admissible, and we characterize its solution in the same way.

title: Quantized six-vertex realizations of frustration graphs
abstract: A recent graph-theoretic criterion for a Hamiltonian to exhibit a free-parafermion spectrum is that its frustration graph be an indifference graph. We show that an arbitrary finite indifference graph can be realized as a frustration graph of the quantized six-vertex model at odd roots of unity, by a suitable choice of the defining wiring diagram and parameters. This provides a concrete realization of the criterion through the quantum Frobenius property of the quantized six-vertex model, recently established from its three-dimensional integrable structure.

title: Integral Specializations of Polynomials: Hilbert Irreducibility, Coprimality, and Density
abstract: The Hilbert specialization property of a field, whereby irreducibility of polynomials is preserved under specialization of some of the variables, admits an integral counterpart where specialization takes place inside a ring and irreducibility is required over the ring. It is known that the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of integers of any global field $K$ satisfies this integrally Hilbertian property. Using a different approach, we reprove this result and strengthen it by showing that the corresponding integral Hilbert subsets of $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ are not only Zariski-dense, as required by integral hilbertianity, but also of positive density. A central ingredient is a generalization to the ring $\mathcal{O}_K$ of the Ekedahl--Poonen formula originally proved for $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$. This formula, of independent interest, gives the density of tuples in $\mathcal{O}_K^k$ for which coprime polynomials in $k$ variables and with coefficients in ${\mathcal O}_K$ take coprime values. Our generalization requires estimates for the number of points of bounded height in an arithmetic progression. We obtain such estimates as our third main result, thereby contributing to the theory of heights.

title: On the generalized cohomologies of almost abelian solvmanifolds
abstract: Generalized complex structures give rise to generalized Dolbeault, Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomologies. We study these cohomologies for invariant generalized complex structures on almost abelian Lie algebras $\mathfrak g_A=\mathbb R e_0\ltimes_A\mathfrak h$, where $\mathfrak h$ is an abelian ideal of codimension one, and on almost abelian solvmanifolds $Γ\backslash G_A$. We first show that the invariant generalized Dolbeault cohomology can be identified with the Chevalley--Eilenberg cohomology of the complex Lie algebra $\mathcal L$, the $+{\mathbf i}$-eigenspace of the structure, with coefficients in a character determined by the canonical line. We prove that $\mathcal L$ is itself an almost abelian Lie algebra; thus the cohomology reduces to the kernel and cokernel of an explicit derivation. Assuming that $A$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb R$, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the cohomology dimensions and compare with compact quotients. Other comparison results are discussed, noting that the cohomology of invariant forms always injects into that of $Γ\backslash G_A$.

title: Elementary Proofs of Commonality of the House Graph and $K_4$ with One Edge Subdivided
abstract: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-coloring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random coloring with an equal proportion of each color. The house graph and $K_4$ with one edge subdivided once are known to be common by the flag algebra method. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický, and Volec asked for ``human-friendly'' proofs of the commonality of these two graphs. In this short note, we give flag-algebra-free proofs that both graphs are common.

title: Gaudin from Cherednik
abstract: Let $W$ be a complex reflection group and $X$ the De Concini-Procesi wonderful model of its reflection arrangement. Inside Etingof's sheaf of Cherednik algebras on $X$ we define a subsheaf generated by the Dunkl operators that extend the standard ones on the hyperplane complement. We conjecture that at $t=0$ the image of the logarithmic vector fields in a natural module over this subsheaf is the sheaf of Gaudin algebras on $X$ defined by Aguirre, extending a construction of Bonnafé and Rouquier from the hyperplane complement to $X$. We prove the conjecture for $W=S_{3}$.
comment: 12 pages, 1 diagram, 0 figures. Minimally revised from a 2022 draft

title: Model order reduction of HDG discretizations for harmonic wave propagation
abstract: We propose and analyze a projection-based model reduction method for the rapid and reliable solution of time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation problems over a frequency band, with particular emphasis on seismic applications. The high-fidelity model is based on a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization, formulated as a generalized saddle-point system coupling the volume and trace unknowns. The basis construction combines residual-based greedy sampling of the frequency parameter, enrichment with frequency derivatives of the HDG solution, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) compression. We establish the well posedness of both the high-fidelity and reduced problems and characterize their stability with inf-sup constants. We investigate the interaction between static condensation, inherent to the HDG discretization, and projection onto the reduced spaces, characterizing its implications for the reduced formulation and approximation errors. Since these operations do not commute in general, we derive a priori error estimates for both the trace and volume variables to quantify the gap between the two operations. We further identify a lifting condition on the volume reduced space that eliminates these gaps and yields a trace error estimate independent of the volume approximation error. Numerical experiments on the two-dimensional Marmousi model and a three-dimensional heterogeneous medium, with more than $10^{7}$ unknowns, illustrate the theoretical estimates and show that the reduced model achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude compared to the high-fidelity solver.

title: The \textsc{ABC}-equation revisited: missed integrable cases. Part I: classification and (quasi) integrable structures
abstract: We consider the \textsc{ABC}-equation $Au_xu_{yt} + Bu_yu_{xt} + Cu_tu_{xy} = 0$, $A$, $B$, $C\in\mathbb{R}$, which was proved to be integrable in the case $A + B + C = 0$ (the Veronese web equation). Our study reveals ten more cases that admit integrable structures that, to the best of our knowledge, where not known before. The techniques is based essentially on the theory of the tangent and cotangent coverings.

title: An Analytic 0.48-Approximation for Non-Monotone k-Submodular Maximization under a Matroid Constraint
abstract: We give a randomized polynomial-time $0.48$-approximation for maximizing a nonnegative non-monotone $k$-submodular function under a matroid constraint, for every $k\ge2$. The algorithm combines a top-two label rule with a nested-chain potential and maximum-weight matroid bases. Its analysis reduces the approximation guarantee to a one-dimensional time allocation: a uniform local lower bound leads to a linear differential equation, concavity closes the remaining interval, and two elementary budgets complete the proof. A strict saving in the time budget absorbs sampling and discretization errors, yielding the exact $0.48$ guarantee in the value-oracle model.
comment: 22 pages, 1 figure, 1 table; author list updated to include Wenguo Yang

title: Conguences for Odd Unimodal Sequences and a Problem of Bringmann And Lovejoy
abstract: In this paper, we give a family of the arithmetic progressions in which the numbers of odd unimodal and odd strongly unimodal sequences are divisible by 2 and by 4. In particular, we answer a question of Bringmann and Lovejoy on the existence of such arithmetic progressions for odd strongly unimodal sequences modulo 4.

title: eMOOD: Entropy-Based Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection for High-Order Shock-Capturing Finite-Volume Schemes
abstract: We present eMOOD, an entropy-guided evolution of the Multidimensional Optimal Order Detection (MOOD) framework for high-order finite-volume methods on unstructured meshes. A novel troubled-cell indicator based on numerical entropy production replaces the classical relaxed discrete maximum principle. Using entropy generation as a physically motivated measure of non-smoothness, the detector targets shocks, contact discontinuities and under-resolved flow features with a compact stencil. Compared with conventional MOOD detection, eMOOD reduces flagged cells by up to 75%, improving efficiency and reducing memory-access overhead. The detector is used within both the classical MOOD cascade of progressively reduced-order schemes and a novel MOOD-CWENO hybrid, which retains inexpensive linear reconstruction in smooth regions and activates nonlinear high-order reconstruction only where needed. Implemented in the open-source parallel solver UCNS3D, the methodology is assessed on the Shu-Osher shock-entropy-wave interaction, double Mach reflection, supersonic forward-facing step, shock-helium-bubble interaction and triple material point problems. These benchmarks encompass strong shock interactions, shock-induced instabilities, multi-material interfaces and vortex-dominated flows, testing robustness, shock capturing and accuracy on unstructured meshes. Results show that eMOOD preserves the accuracy and robustness of reference CWENO and MOOD formulations while achieving speed-ups of up to 20% without loss of solution quality. Its compact detection stencil, reduced memory footprint and improved localisation offer a more scalable and efficient framework for massively parallel high-order compressible-flow simulations. title: Mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds
abstract: The goal of this work is to calculate the mapping class groups of solenoidal manifolds. We introduce the dynamical commensurator group associated to an odometer action, and develop methods to calculate the mapping class group using the dynamical commensurator. Our results generalize the previous results of Odden for the mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a Riemann surface, and of Bering and Studenmund for the pointed mapping class group of the universal solenoid over a compact aspherical manifold. We include a selection of examples.

title: Cop number of $P_k$-free graphs without a claw or a fork
abstract: In 2019, Liu proved that the cop number of any $(P_k, claw)$-free graph is at most $k-3$. In 2026, Clow and Meger improved and generalized the result of Liu by showing that every connected $(P_k, E)$-free graph has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil + 3$, where the graph $E$ is obtained by subdividing two edges of a claw. In this paper, we show that every $(P_k, claw)$-free graph $G$ has cop number at most $\lceil \frac{k-1}{2} \rceil$. This improves the result of Clow and Meger on claw-free graphs. We further show that this bound can be improved to $\lceil \frac{k}{3}\rceil$, when $G$ contains a hole of length at least $k-1$. We show that the cop number of any $(P_k, fork)$-free graph is at most $\lceil \frac{2(k-1)}{3} \rceil$. This also improves the result of Clow and Meger on fork-free graphs for some values of $k$. We further show that every $(P_7, fork)$-free graph has cop number at most $3$, and this bound is tight.

title: New Modelling and Solution Frameworks for Multiple Objectives, Decomposability and Impulsivity in Continuous-time Markov Decision Processes
abstract: Impulsive control, in the context of continuous-time Markov decision processes (CTMDPs), refers to actions that instantaneously update the state of the process, leading to theoretical complications. Previous work has overcome these complications, but at the expense of approachability and ease of implementation: those models are mathematically complex and incompatible with pre-existing solution methods. This paper presents an alternative formulation of impulsive control for CTMDPs that is easier to employ in the modelling of real-world problems and can be solved by pre-existing solution methods. This formulation is then extended to allow for multiple objectives and decomposability. A decomposition-based heuristic method is developed that leverages Dantzig-Wolfe decomposition to find approximate Pareto fronts for large multi-objective decomposable impulsive CTMDPs. The modelling framework and solution methodology are applied to a dynamic maintenance problem to demonstrate their computational efficiency, solution space coverage, and solution quality.

title: The WKB Riemann-Hilbert Problem for the Painlevé I System
abstract: In this paper, we solve the direct monodromy problem for the Borel-summed $0$-parameter solution of Painlevé~I. Using the auxiliary time equation, we first construct formal WKB wave matrices whose amplitudes are regular at the double turning point. Rigorous Borel summation then yields exact WKB matrices in each Stokes region. Uniform estimates on moving action strips provide a common exact wave matrix in a full neighbourhood of the double point, proving that all four incident jumps are identities for consistent column normalisations. We formulate the resulting normalised Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its existence and uniqueness on the Borel domains of the construction. Finally, after Painlevé scaling, the five Borel-summed solutions coincide with the five rotated tritronquée solutions of Painlevé~I.

title: A Reflection Calculus for Bar Induction and the Linearity of Consistency Strength Ordering
abstract: We introduce a novel extension of reflection calculus, $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$, to analyze a family of extensions of $\mathsf{ACA}_0$ generated by uniform $ω$-model and syntactic reflection principles, together with several other related operators. The union of these theories coincides with the theory of Bar Induction ($\mathsf{BI}$). We prove that $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$ is arithmetically sound, and that it is sound and complete with respect to a natural class of Kripke models. Leveraging these modal semantics, we demonstrate that the class of theories denoted by $\nabla$-free closed formulas is a pre-wellordering with respect to $Π^1_1$-soundness and consistency strength. This allows us to establish an ordinal analysis for $\mathsf{BI}$ and its fragments, analogous to Beklemishev's analysis of $\mathsf{PA}$. The structural properties of $\mathsf{RC_{BI}}$ naturally give rise to a novel ordinal notation system for the Bachmann-Howard ordinal which differs substantially from existing representations.

title: Identities and isomorphisms of finite graded matrix algebras
abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field and let $G$ be a group such that every finite subgroup of $G$ is cyclic. In this paper we classify the division gradings by cyclic groups on matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$. This yields the classification of the $G$-gradings on these algebras. Moreover if $G$ is abelian we prove that two matrix algebras over $\mathbb{F}$ with $G$-gradings satisfy the same graded identities if and only if they are isomorphic as graded algebras.

title: Kernel representations of fractional gradient bilinear forms. Part I. Constant coefficients
abstract: We study the representation of bilinear forms associated with Riesz fractional gradients by symmetric integral kernels. Motivated by [SS18, Open Problem 1.10], we give a complete description of the constant coefficient case. We prove that any symmetric representing kernel is uniquely determined and we derive its explicit formula in terms of the constant matrix $A$. This yields a sharp characterization of the matrices for which the kernel is either nonnegative or uniformly positive. In particular, [SS18, Open Problem 1.10] has a negative answer (even for constant matrices). We also identify a class of nonconstant antisymmetric divergence free perturbations that are invisible to the fractional bilinear form and hence leave the representing kernel unchanged. The general case of nonconstant matrices exhibits a substantially different behavior and will be the main subject of our forthcoming paper [DSV26].

title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
abstract:
We approximate the solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$ of $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$ by operator networks whose only primitives are heat-semigroup functions of a fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The main result is an emulation theorem on strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--Émery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$: an explicit scheme reaches $\dot H^1$-error $\varepsilon$ uniformly over coefficients with bounded carré du champ and bounded generator image and over $L^2$ data, with parameters depending only on the coefficient bounds, the accuracy and $K$; on the torus this gives a $C^2$-type coefficient class with constants independent of the dimension. The torus version refines this to Wiener classes of fractional regularity $A^{1+θ}$, with an explicit rate attained by the scheme's product-defect block. The scheme unrolls the Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, controls each inexact step in the operator norm of $\dot H^1$ without Galerkin truncation, and synthesises the coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$ from the product defect of one heat layer. All parameters are explicit; the results are approximation theorems for continuum operators.

title: Connectivity keeping pendant extensions of paths in $k$-connected triangle-free graphs
abstract: Motivated by Mader's conjecture on connectivity keeping trees, we study the corresponding problem in triangle-free graphs. For positive integers $k,m$, we first prove that every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with $δ(G)\geq k+\left \lceil \frac{m}{2} \right \rceil $ contains a path $P$ of order $m$ such that $G-V(P)$ remains $k$-connected. Moreover, if $κ(G)=k$, then for every end $F$ of $G$ and every vertex $v\in F$, the path $P$ can be chosen in $G[F]$ with $v$ as an endvertex. If $κ(G)\geq k+1$, then any vertex of $G$ can be chosen as an endvertex of $P$. This result confirms the conjecture of Luo, Tian and Wu on connectivity keeping trees in bipartite graphs for all paths, and it also sharpens Fujita's path theorem to the optimal minimum degree bound. For an integer $i$ with $1\leq i\leq m-1$, let $P_m^+(i)$ denote the tree obtained from a path of order $m-1$ by adding one pendant vertex adjacent to its $i$th vertex. Let $(X,Y)$ be the bipartition of $P_m^+(i)$. We further prove that every $k$-connected triangle-free graph $G$ with $δ(G)\geq k+\max\{|X|,|Y|\}$ contains a subgraph $T\cong P_m^+(i)$ such that $G-V(T)$ remains $k$-connected. The minimum degree bound is sharp, and the result confirms the bipartite conjecture for all pendant extensions of paths.

title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
abstract: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.

title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
abstract: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.

title: Ball growth at all scales in universal covers of short metric graphs
abstract: Let $Γ$ be a connected metric graph of first Betti number $b\ge 2$, and let $Γ_b$ be a trivalent graph of the same Betti number with all edges of unit length. We show that if $\text{length}(Γ) \le λ\, \text{length}(Γ_b)$, then the universal cover of $Γ$ contains a vertex around which, \emph{at every radius} $R\ge 0$, the ball is at least as long as the ball of radius $R$ in the trivalent tree whose edges all have length $3λ$. In particular, for $λ\le\frac13$, this ball is at least as long as the ball of the same radius in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, with no multiplicative loss. This improves an earlier theorem of the author, which gives the weaker lower bound $(1-3λ)$ times the ball in the universal cover of $Γ_b$, and only for $λ\le\frac16$. The proof rests on an elementary comparison principle. Among trees whose vertices have degree at least three and whose edges have length at most $c$, the trivalent tree with all edges of length $c$ has the smallest balls at every radius. As an application, we double the exponential growth rate in the author's earlier uniform lower bound for the area of balls in the universal cover of small-area surfaces of hyperbolic type, from $\ln 2$ to $2\ln 2$, beyond the hyperbolic rate. We also obtain explicit constants in the positive answer to Guth's question for surfaces. Finally, we conjecture the sharp, all-scale version of the minimal volume entropy inequality of Kapovich--Nagnibeda and Lim, and show that it would be optimal.

title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
abstract: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,δ}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $δ>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^δ$ is smooth for each $δ>0$ but degenerates as $δ\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $δ\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is Hölder continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.

title: Routes planning in a condominium company using mathematical optimization
abstract: This work focuses on planning daily routes for a group of employees of a condominium company. Given a set of employees and a set of customers with pre-scheduled visits, we want to build doubly-open routes to guarantee visits to all customers, ensuring that each customer is visited by an employee with the appropriate skills to carry out the required activity. The travel times between customers and the service time in each customer are known. The problem includes time windows for visiting customers, each employee has a maximum working time, and the daily working period is between 9 AM and 6:30 PM. The routes respect the lunch break period if they extend from morning to afternoon, which means that lunch break can be avoided if the route is fully completed in the morning or in the afternoon. The aim is to minimize the distance covered by all routes with a penalty for including lunch breaks. The distances and times between customers are collected via an API to Microsoft Azure; and the solutions are then displayed on Bing Maps. The results obtained show the operational advantages of an efficient and effective vehicle routing planning in a specific condominium management company. The model can be extended to other service provider companies.

title: On the maximum relational complexity of affine groups
abstract: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $Ω$. The relational complexity $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is the least integer $r\geq 2$ such that the $G$-orbit of every finite tuple is determined by the $G$-orbits of its $r$-subtuples; there is currently only a small collection of groups $G$ for which $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is known precisely. In this paper we study the relational complexity of finite affine groups acting naturally on a $d$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that every such group has relational complexity at most $d+2$ when $q>2$ and at most $d+1$ when $q=2$; we produce a complete classification of the primitive such groups for which these bounds are attained.

title: Finitistic dimensions of formal power series rings
abstract: We consider the big finitistic projective and flat dimensions of a commutative ring and of its formal power series ring. When the ring is Noetherian, both invariants increase by one. Coherence of the power series ring does not force either equality to hold. For every \(n\ge0\) and every \(d\) with \(n+1\le d\le\infty\), the flat pair \((n,d)\) can be realized. The finite projective pairs are realized when \(n\ge1\), and also for \((0,1)\). For every \(n\ge0\), one family realizes \((n,\infty)\) for both invariants at the same time. The seed is a zero-dimensional perfect local ring. Its power series ring has countably presented modules whose flat dimension is \(r\) and whose projective dimension lies between \(r\) and \(r+1\), for every \(r\ge1\). The remaining finite projective case is controlled by a dichotomy for perfect coefficient rings. If the Jacobson radical is nilpotent, the power series value is one; if it is not nilpotent, there is a module of projective dimension exactly three. In particular, the pair \((0,2)\) is impossible. For one fixed countable perfect ring, the power series ring has finitistic flat dimension one. Its finitistic projective dimension is \(m+2\) when \(2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_m\) with \(1\le m<\infty\), and is infinite when \(2^{\aleph_0}>\aleph_ω\).

title: Primes between 8th powers?
abstract: OpenAI (using a non-public "internal frontier model'') has recently (6 October 2026) made a number of remarkable claims, including some claims regarding the quasi-Riemann hypothesis (QRH). While there are good reasons to be cautious regarding these claims, one can nevertheless ask what (if true) their implications would be. While there is widespread agreement that any version of the QRH will provide various improved bounds on the location of the prime numbers, I feel that there is some value in making these improvements explicit. Specifically, if we assume validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH then I shall demonstrate (for all $n\in \mathbb{Z^+}$): 1) the existence of primes between eighth powers, in the interval $(n^8,(n+1)^8)$; 2) the existence of primes in the shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+8n^7)$; 3) the existence of primes in the even shorter interval $(n^8,n^8+n^7).$ Similarly for reals greater than unity $x>1$ one can demonstrate: 4) the existence of primes in the Hoheisel-style interval $(x,x+x^{7/8})$. All of this is contingent on the validity of the claimed 7/8 version of the QRH.

title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
abstract: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-Hölder continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.

title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
abstract: We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $α$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $α=α_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($α<\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $α= \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation. The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.

title: Real Tree Vineyards have Vines
abstract: We show that every vineyard can be decomposed into vines, that is, every path in the space of persistence diagrams $\mathcal{D}$ can be decomposed into a sequence of paths in $\mathbb R^2$. Moreover, we characterize which spaces $X$ have the property that every continuous map $X\to \mathcal{D}$ has such a decomposition. Our results hold not just for $\mathcal{D}$, but also for many other spaces of unordered tuples.

title: Markman--Markushevich principle and Lagrangian fibrations on O'Grady six-manifolds
abstract: To any compact holomorphically symplectic manifold and a nef BBF-isotropic class we associate a quasi-projective variety called the Markman--Markushevich space which parametrises the Lagrangian fibrations with this isotropic class modulo Tate--Shafarevich twists. We give a systematic interpretation of known results about Tate--Shafarevich twists of Lagrangian fibrations using this space, employ it to obtain a conjectural result for the last deformation type for which such a result is not yet proposed, and make some first steps towards its proof. As a byproduct, we generalise the results of Kumar on existence Shioda--Inose partners for abelian surfaces to a slightly more general class of K3 surfaces, and associate a canonical K3 surface with transcendental lattice isometric to $U^2\oplus\langle-2\rangle^2$ to a smooth cubic surface with a choice of a Schläfli double-six. Finally, we construct a noncompact six-manifold with an abelian fibration associated to a cubic surface with a Schläfli double-six, and give its interpretation in terms of the K3 surfaces we introduced.
comment: 11 pages, Section 5 replaced, Section 6 added. comments still welcome!

title: Algebraic and Symmetrized Affine star-Ricci Solitons for the Bott Connection on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
abstract: We fix a spacelike two-dimensional left-invariant distribution and its associated almost contact structure on a three-dimensional Lorentzian Lie group, and investigate the star-Ricci contraction of the curvature of the Bott connection. We compute the complete tensor for seven standard bracket families and determine all real parameter solutions of the general algebraic equation and its self-adjoint subclass. Using the symmetric part of the tensor, we also define a Bott affine star-Ricci soliton equation and classify all left-invariant vector field solutions. Every affine solution is steady, while two non-unimodular families admit branches with a nonzero symmetrized tensor. The proofs provide complete component equations, treat all degenerate parameter branches, and establish sufficiency by explicit substitution. We also distinguish almost contact structures from contact metric structures.

title: Maximal subsets of $n\times n$ board without cycles
abstract:
Define $
abla(n)$ as the least possible number of cells that must be removed from the $n	imes n$ square board in order to leave no cycles. Put $L_n=\left\lceil\left((n-1)^2+1ight)/3ightceil$. The results of Luccio, Madelaine-Stewart, and Lien-Fu-Shih imply that $
abla(n)=L_n$ in case $n\equiv 1\pmod 6$ and $n\equiv 4\pmod 6$, while for the remaining $4$ residue classes $
abla(n)=L_n$ or $

comment: 7 pages, 6 figures. The paper was originally written in 2022, and the corresponding sequence, A354673, was submitted to the OEIS. The present version incorporates previously known results from the literature to place the new contributions in context

title: On the Fomin-Kirillov algebras
abstract: The Fomin-Kirillov algebras $\mathcal{FK}_n$ are shown to be infinite-dimensional for $n\geq 6$. By computer calculations, we find an explicit nonzero primitive element of degree 14 in the identity component of $\mathcal{FK}_6$. For every $n\geq 6$, the existence of such an element implies that $\mathcal{FK}_n$ contains a polynomial subalgebra and is therefore infinite-dimensional, and that the canonical homomorphism from $\mathcal{FK}_n$ onto its associated Nichols algebra is not an isomorphism.

title: A particle swarm optimization with a reduced-subspace trust-region safeguard for contact-rich controller tuning
abstract: Contact-rich robotic insertion is challenging because uncertainty in alignment, friction, and contact conditions can lead to unsuccessful assembly, excessive contact forces, and jamming. Designing a reliable controller therefore requires balancing insertion performance, robustness, and recovery from unexpected contact. In this paper, we propose PSO+TR, a derivative-free optimization (DFO) method that combines the exploratory search of particle swarm optimization (PSO) with a trust-region (TR) procedure for local refinement to improve the search process when progress stagnates. We apply the method to derivative-free policy optimization of an interpretable robotic insertion controller, jointly tuning its motion, feedback, and recovery parameters while preserving its predefined control structure. The proposed approach is evaluated on 93 eligible benchmark problems from the bound-constrained programs (BCP) collection and a synthetic contact-rich planar insertion task under uncertain operating conditions. Three random seeds per benchmark problem yield 279 matched problem--seed instances per method. PSO+TR reaches the prescribed target on 228 of these instances (81.72\%), the highest observed target-attainment rate among the five compared methods, which also include PSO, randomized black-box optimization (VRBBO), matrix adaptation evolution strategy (MAES), and differential evolution (DE). Across eight robotic optimizer seeds, the deployed controller-selection pipeline achieves 97.78\% completion under development conditions and 58.00\% under withheld stress conditions, compared with 91.22\% and 31.12\%, respectively, for the fixed staged controller. The stress violation rate is reduced from 20.69\% to 2.19\%. These findings support combining global and local search for DFO and structured contact-rich controller tuning. The synthetic planar results require validation on physical robots.

title: Stabilities of Background Perturbations for Compressible Adiabatic Flows through Porous Media in 3-D
abstract: In this paper, we study the background stability problem for three-dimensional compressible adiabatic flows through porous media. For two given equilibrium states $(\bar{P}^k,\vec{0},\bar{S}^k)$ ($k=0,1$), under the assumption of small initial perturbations around each equilibrium state, pointwise estimates of solutions for individual perturbation problems are obtained. Based on these pointwise structures, a comparison between two individual solutions could be applied and it is proved that the difference between two solutions depends continuously on the equilibrium distance $|\bar{P}^0-\bar{P}^1|+|\bar{S}^0-\bar{S}^1|$ as well as the initial perturbation difference, with additional decay rates, thereby establishing a nonlinear comparison principle for this system. Compared with previous works on background stability problems, it is the first time to obtain stabilities in the pointwise sense. Our main tools are Green's functions, a priori energy estimates, and refined decay estimates for higher-order derivatives.

title: Sequence Factory: Families of Integer Sequences Generated by Gödel Implication
abstract: A finite Gödel chain generates not one integer sequence but a large family of them. The combinatorial mechanism is developed in a companion paper; here the sequences themselves are the primary objects. For $V_m=\{v_0<\cdots<v_{m-1}\}$, let $g_{j,n}^{(m)}$ count outputs equal to $v_j$, aggregated over all full bracketings on $n$ variables and all $m^n$ valuations. The root-pair refinement produces $N_{i,j}^{(m)}(n)=\sum_{r=1}^{n-1}g_{i,r}^{(m)}g_{j,n-r}^{(m)}$, with generating functions $N_{i,j}^{(m)}(x)=G_i^{(m)}(x)G_j^{(m)}(x)$. We prove that the initial coefficients of these products uniquely identify the unordered root-value pair. Consequently, for each fixed $m$, there are exactly $\binom{m+1}{2}$ distinct root-pair generating functions. We catalogue the factories for $m=4,5,\ldots,10$, giving the first ten terms of every base sequence and every symmetric root-pair sequence. This range contains 49 base sequences and 210 symmetric pair classes, yielding 259 indexed sequence families before additional aggregates. The catalogue provides reproducible data for integer-sequence analysis and comparison with the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS).
comment: 14 pages; 7 appendices; sequence catalogue and exact distinctness theorem

title: On the Topology of Fibers of Rational Functions
abstract: In 1988 Broughton proved that if a complex polynomial function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ is tame at infinity its fibers are homotopy equivalent to bouquets of some spheres. Since then several basic properties of polynomial functions were studied by many mathematicians in various situations. In this paper, we show some evidence for the possibility of extending Broughton's result to rational functions satisfying some tameness condition at infinity and the one at their points of indeterminacy. Specifically, assuming some conditions on a rational function on ${\mathbb C}^n$ we prove that the cohomology groups of a generic fiber of it are isomorphic to those of a bouquet of $S^1$ and some spheres. In the course of the proof, the theory of the nearby and vanishing cycle sheaves for meromorphic functions will play an essential role.

title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type
abstract: We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite. A proper wide open subgroupoid is prime if it admits no proper intermediate wide open subgroupoid. We prove a trichotomy for prime subgroupoids: they are minimal, arise from a clopen bipartition, or have a unique nonempty proper closed invariant set, which is nowhere dense. For a prime subgroupoid, the normalizer of its topological full group is maximal in the ambient topological full group precisely when it maps onto the ambient abelianization. An analogous criterion holds in every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup. For a minimal prime subgroupoid, its topological full group is maximal precisely when it equals its normalizer and the inclusion induces a surjection on first groupoid homology. We also describe all fully amplified maximal subgroups, namely those closed under local agreement. For Thompson's group $V$, the stabilizer of every simple type system is maximal, extending results of Belk, Bleak, Quick and Skipper for finite type systems and certain classes of infinite ones. Finally, every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup has continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic maximal subgroups acting minimally on the unit space.

title: Strong Negative Type of Star-shaped Manifolds
abstract: Metric spaces of negative type (NT) and strong negative type (SNT) are fundamental in wide applications across computer science and statistics. It is well-known that spheres equipped with geodesic distance are of NT, and subsets of a sphere that contain at most one pair of antipodal points (e.g. an open hemisphere) are of SNT. In this paper, we extend these results to a class of star-shaped manifolds. By constructing a metric $d$ based on layer-wise radial projections, we prove that every star-shaped manifold, equipped with $d$, is of NT. Moreover, we prove that a subset of a star-shaped manifold is of SNT under certain injectivity and directional asymmetry conditions. In particular, for a subset of a single layer, it is of SNT if it contains exactly one point from each preimage of an open hemisphere (a fully directional asymmetry); moreover, it is of SNT if and only if it contains at most one opposite-directional pair.

title: Ergodic and Metastable Behavior of Stochastic Popularity Dynamics in Social Networks
abstract: This paper studies popularity dynamics in social networks, where users' engagement with competing channels is driven by intrinsic content quality, social influence, and popularity feedback. We introduce a stochastic model in which users interact through a directed influence network and channel exposure depends jointly on these three mechanisms. We first characterize the resulting dynamics in the absence of intrinsic quality, showing that popularity concentrates asymptotically on a single channel, leading to a winner-takes-all regime. When all channels have positive intrinsic quality, we establish ergodicity of the popularity process and characterize its long-run behavior. We further show that, when intrinsic quality is small, the system exhibits metastable behavior: it can remain for long periods near configurations dominated by a single channel before transitioning to another. These results highlight how weak quality differences can coexist with strong path dependence induced by popularity feedback. We then investigate platform-level interventions and propose controls that compensate for network-induced exposure biases and mitigate excessive concentration. Analytical results are illustrated through numerical simulations and an empirical analysis of YouTube data, whose observed popularity dynamics are consistent with the proposed stochastic framework. The results provide a mathematical framework for understanding the interplay between quality, social influence, and reinforcement in online popularity dynamics.

title: MCMC Can See Can't See
abstract: It is folklore that passing "convergence" diagnostics does not guarantee that a Markov chain has converged. We prove this as an impossibility for any finite checklist of diagnostics. Running more chains, longer chains, and smarter diagnostics does not avoid this impossibility in certifying convergence. Under regularity assumptions, we determine how the worst-case undetected non-convergence decays as more diagnostics are added, and how to choose diagnostics optimally. Folklore suggests that the sampler's slowest mixing modes are the "dangerous" ones that must be monitored; we prove that the slow modes yield nearly optimal diagnostics as sampling proceeds. Given a source class, we also give an anytime-valid bound on the remaining discrepancy and show how undetected bias caps the effective sample size that a finite checklist can certify.

title: Refined blow-up behavior for semilinear heat equations with arbitrarily fast growing nonlinearities
abstract: We study radially nonincreasing, positive blow-up solutions of a class of superlinear heat equations in the non-scale-invariant setting. This class contains nonlinearities with arbitrarily fast, super-exponential growth. Under suitable structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we derive the sharp global blow-up profile in the original space-time variables. More precisely, for positive nonlinearities $f$ satisfying $$ \lim_{X\to \infty}f'(X)G(X)= q\ge1\quad \quad \hbox{ where }\quad\quad G(X)=\int_{X}^{\infty}\frac{ ds}{f(s)}<\infty\quad\forall\ X>0, $$ and assuming either the time monotonicity $u_t\ge0$ holds or $q>\frac{p_S}{p_S-1}$, we have $$ u(x,t)=(1+o(1))\,G^{-1}\bigg(T-t+\frac{|x|^2}{4q|\log |x|^2|}\bigg), \quad \hbox{as $(x,t)\to (0,T)$.} $$ This estimate in particular provides the sharp final space profile and the corresponding refined space-time profile. Moreover, our result recovers the universal structure of the global blow-up profile, given by the resolvent $G^{-1}$ of the associated ODE evaluated at a time-space building block, which only depends on the limit $q$.

title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures III: Unfoldings
abstract: We study unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We prove theorem of existence for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves for one-parameter families. We prove theorem of completeness for unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves. We also present unfoldings of foliated nonsingular varieties defined by locally free subsheaves of cotangent sheaves in the language of functors of Artin rings which is the algebraic version of unfoldings of foliated complex analytic structures. We identify first-order unfoldings and obstructions.

title: Divisibility Estimates for Gaussian Norms and Almost-Prime Orders of a CM Elliptic Curve
abstract: Let $E:y^2=x^3-x$. We prove that $\#E(\mathbf{F}_p)/8$ is squarefree and has at most two prime factors for $\gg X/(\log X)^2$ primes $p\le X$. The proof follows the Gaussian CM sieve framework of Iwaniec and Jiménez Urroz and incorporates the intersection terms identified by Xie. For a squarefree Gaussian ideal $\mathfrak{a}$, we separate its largest rational ideal factor and use the resulting divisibility of both integral coordinates to control the large-factor tail. This transfers an ideal Bombieri--Vinogradov estimate to rational norm divisibility at level $1/2$, with any fixed power of the divisor function as a weight. We prove the corresponding distribution estimate for the switched product sequence and apply the transfer to both sequences in Chen's weighted sieve. The primes counted may be restricted to $p\equiv5\pmod8$; their normalized orders are odd, squarefree, and supported on primes congruent to $1\pmod4$.

title: Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square
abstract: For all sufficiently large $n$, we prove that every Latin square of order $n$ can be made to avoid any prescribed partial Latin square of order $n$ by permuting only its rows and columns. The proof combines Hall's theorem with elementary estimates for a random permutation.

title: Minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap of continuous Markov chains, with applications to empirical concentration bounds
abstract: We study the minimax estimation of the pseudo-spectral gap $γ_{ps}$ of a Markov chain from the observation of a single trajectory. Extending earlier works on finite-state space chains by Wolfer and Kontorovich (2024), we provide an estimator in the case of a compact, continuous state-space. Our estimator appears to be minimax-optimal on the class of chains with a transition operator with Lipschitz density, up to logarithmic terms. Our estimator, combined with Paulin's version of Bernstein inequality, allows to derive empirical concentration inequalities for Markov chains. This unlocks many applications, from confidence intervals, to active learning and generalization bounds. In particular, for rested bandits with Markov rewards, we provide a version of UCB with a regret bound similar to the one in the iid case, without assuming any knowledge on the pseudo-spectral gap of the chains.

title: Sharp Sobolev inequalities under first moment constraints
abstract: Let $n\geq2$ and $1<p<n$. We study sharp Sobolev inequalities on the round sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ for functions $u\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb{S}^n)$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{S}^n}x|u|^{np/(n-p)}\,dσ=0$. We prove that \[ \|u\|_{L^{np/(n-p)}(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \leq 2^{-p/n}S_{n,p}^p\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p+B\|u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \] holds for all such functions with some $B=B(n,p)<\infty$ if and only if $1<p\leq2$ or $2<p<n<3p-2$, where $S_{n,p}$ is the optimal Euclidean Sobolev constant. This determines the exact range in which Aubin's inequality holds with the sharp gradient coefficient. For every $2\leq p<n$, we also establish the corresponding inequality with squared norms and gradient coefficient $2^{-2/n}S_{n,p}^2$. The gradient coefficient in each inequality is optimal. The proof combines stereographic averaging with quantitative stability of the Euclidean Sobolev inequality to obtain local second moment estimates that allow absorption of the localization errors.

title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
abstract: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.

title: An elementary proof of Brémont's theorem on the convergence of equilibrium measures at temperature zero
abstract: We give an elementary proof that if $f$ is a locally constant function on a topologically mixing subshift of finite type, then the equilibrium measures for $tf$ converge as $t\to\infty$, a result due to Brémont. The proof shows that the limit measure assigns an algebraic number to every cylinder.

title: New spherical codes by tuning an annealing solver
abstract: The spherical code problem asks how to place $N$ points on a unit sphere in $D$ dimensions to maximize the smallest distance between two points. It is a non-smooth and non-convex max-min problem, where few problem sizes have known optimal solutions, some have constructions, but most still only have numerically obtained solutions. We use a simple solver, with seven parameters, that anneals a LogSumExp surrogate, minimizes with L-BFGS, applies a random perturbation between anneals, and repeats with no acceptance test until a fixed limit is reached. We search the solver parameters for every instance with $N \le 1024$, $3 \le D \le 32$, and $N > 2D$, a total of 29,670 instances, using 32 parameter trials. We then run the solver for 60 seconds with the best parameters for each instance, without utilizing any symmetries or existing solutions. After enforcing monotonicity of the results and numerically polishing the solutions, we improve the best known code in 4,577 instances. When a single set of solver parameters is used for all instances, with one 60-second episode, the number of improvements is still 3,649. From our records, we find 24 codes with an exact algebraic cosine. Among our ablations, we find that 1) the repeated anneal contributes most to improvements, 2) at our $32 \times 60$-second budget only fitting one parameter per-instance is better than fitting all seven, and 3) good parameters can be predicted from the instance size. We provide the solver code, the fitted parameters, and the codes.

title: A Parametrization of Solutions to the Yamabe Equation with Isolated Singularity
abstract: Inspired by a pioneering work by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck, we study positive solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities. It is known that there is a formal one-to-one correspondence between the collection of the solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities and the collection of harmonic functions through formal infinite series determined by the harmonic functions. In this paper, we prove that these formal infinite series yield actual solutions to the Yamabe equation with a nonremovable isolated singularity. These solutions to the Yamabe equation have designated asymptotic behaviors determined by the harmonic functions. In a broader context, we provide a general method of constructing all solutions near their isolated singular points and all solutions near infinity.

title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
abstract:
We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(Ω)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, using AI, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-Δ+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.

title: Spherical Perfectly Matched Layer Method for Electromagnetic Scattering Problems with Large Wave Number
abstract: We study a spherical perfectly matched layer (PML) method for the time-harmonic Maxwell scattering problem with large wavenumber. Using vector spherical harmonics and a modal transformation for the coupled transverse magnetic components, we establish the sharp wavenumber-explicit stability estimate for the truncated PML problem and prove that its inf-sup constant is of order $O(κ^{-1})$. We then analyze the first-order Nédélec edge element method and its continuous interior penalty counterpart. Under the condition that $κ^3h^2$ is sufficiently small, the preasymptotic errors in the energy norm and the $κ$-scaled $\mathbf{L}^2$ norm are of orders $O(κh+κ^3h^2)$ and $O(κ^2h^2+κ^3h^2)$, respectively. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
abstract: Extremal constructions play a central role in the design and analysis of algorithms. Integrality-gap instances expose the limitations of relaxations, while hard configurations reveal structural sources of computational difficulty. Such constructions, however, are still typically discovered through a slow, manual process. This paper investigates how machine learning can accelerate their discovery to support algorithm design and analysis. We build on PatternBoost, a framework alternating local search with generation from a trained transformer, using its Axplorer implementation to investigate three problems: integrality gaps for maximum independent set of rectangles, integrality gaps for stabbing unit squares with axis-parallel lines, and hard instances for recursive guillotine cutting. By exploring candidate representations, local search operations, and surrogate models used to rank candidates before exact verification, we carefully adapt the framework to these combinatorial geometry problems.While naive representations and search strategies fail to find non-trivial instances, our tailored adaptation discovers numerous non-trivial constructions. For stabbing unit squares, the method reaches a gap of $20/13\approx 1.54$, improving on the literature's best known lower bound of $3/2$. Purely automated search converges rapidly and then plateaus, prompting the question of what is required to push the bound higher still. We find that initial instance diversity plays an important role: with modest expert input via a structured staircase construction, the system reaches an improved integrality gap of $14/9\approx 1.555$. These results demonstrate that machine learning and domain expertise can be combined to discover new extremal constructions that advance algorithmic lower bounds.

title: L1 Minimum Energy Estimation of Positive Systems
abstract: We present a novel class of minimum energy estimation problems for positive linear systems with linear costs subject to coupled process and measurement disturbances, where the latter is bounded by the state and the former is bounded by the noise. Through dynamic programming we show that the problem admits explicit solutions. Remarkably, the Luenberger observer structure of the optimal estimator emerges from the optimization itself, with a switching gain that inherits the sparsity of the disturbance constraints, and it is obtained from a differential equation in the finite horizon case. In the infinite horizon case, an algebraic equation characterizes the limit of the finite-horizon solution and yields a stationary estimator with a static gain. We introduce two distinct notions of detectability to characterize when the static gain stabilizes the error dynamics while preserving their positivity, and analyze under which conditions the stationary solution can be formulated as a linear program. We further establish that a disturbance perturbation of finite L1-norm yields an estimation error of finite L1-norm. The framework is illustrated on a large-scale irrigation network.

title: Trivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures for interior shells of the Grassmann scheme
abstract: Association schemes induced on the shells of the Grassmann scheme $Gr_q(N,a)$ form an important family in the study of multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. For $a<N/2$, the scheme induced on the furthest shell $X_a$ is the known bivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial scheme arising from attenuated spaces. In this paper, we prove that, for every $1\leq i\leq a-1$, the association scheme induced on the interior shell $X_i$ is both trivariate $P$-polynomial and trivariate $Q$-polynomial. The two structures share a common index set consisting of the lattice points of a bounded non-simplicial polyhedron. We establish the $P$-polynomial property through combinatorial interpretations of the intersection numbers. Using Dunkl's coordinate description of $X_i$ and the addition theorem, together with recurrence relations for the $q$-Hahn and $q$-Krawtchouk polynomials, we obtain the required vanishing and nonvanishing conditions for the Krein parameters, and hence the $Q$-polynomial structure. Motivated by this index set, we extend the notion of an $A_M$-Leonard pair from simplicial to polyhedral domains and show that every interior shell carries a polyhedral $A_3$-Leonard pair.

title: Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems of new types
abstract: For integers $r\ge1$ and $n\ge2$, let $s_r(n)$ be the least $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ vectors in $\Z^r$, each nonzero modulo $n$, contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero modulo $n$ but nonzero modulo $n^2$. Let $w_r(n)$ be the corresponding least $N$ when any nonempty subsequence is allowed. These constants were introduced as zero-sum problems of new types by Z.-W. Sun. We prove $s_r(n)\ge(2^{r+1}-2)(n-1)+1$ by constructing an explicit sequence from a lattice polytope, \emph{disproving} his conjecture $s_2(n)=4n+1$ for $n\ge4$. We obtain $w_r(2)=2r+1$ by classifying all sequences avoiding such nonempty subsequences modulo $4$. We also \emph{prove} Sun's conjecture $w_2(n)=4n-3$ for $n=2^k3^\ell p$, where $p$ is a prime and $k,\ell\ge0$ are integers, by classifying the extremal sequences of length $4p-4$ modulo $p^2$ when $n=p$. For every fixed $n\ge2$, we prove $w_r(n)/s(\Z_n^r)=O_n(r^2/2^r)\to0$ as $r\to\infty$, where $s(\Z_n^r)$ is the classical Erdős-Ginzburg-Ziv constant, with an explicit threshold on $r$ for strict inequality. Thus, for every fixed modulus $n\ge2$, Sun's proposed equality fails for sufficiently large $r$.

title: Ramanujan Conjecture and Riemann Hypothesis for the unitary groups over function fields
abstract: We establish generic local and global Langlands functoriality, namely stable base change, for the unitary groups in characteristic $p$. Main applications are the Ramanujan Conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis for extended Langlands-Shahidi $L$-functions of the unitary groups over function fields.
comment: This article is a stand-alone version of the second part of arXiv:1507.03625

title: Nonlinear fixed-distance codes via real lifts of moment configurations
abstract: Let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the largest size of a code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance $d$ over an alphabet of $q$ symbols. For fixed $q\ge2$ and $d\ge4$ we construct codes with redundancy $n-\log_q A_q(n,d)\le(d-3)\log_q n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all large $n$. No algebraic structure is imposed on the alphabet, and the codes are not linear. For $d=4$ and $d=5$ the coefficient of $\log_q n$ matches the Hamming bound, so the redundancy is determined up to lower-order terms. At distance four the codes are provably better than every linear code: by the polynomial-method bound for cap sets, $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes with $q>2$ require a strictly larger coefficient in front of $\log_q n$. The construction imposes moment checksums over an auxiliary finite field, as BCH codes do, but one fewer than the distance would normally require. The affine-line theorem from prior work describes the dependencies left by these checks. We exclude them by placing the code positions inside a specially structured subset of the field, built from Behrend's sphere construction with the help of algebraic number theory.

title: Two Companion $q$-Series Identities and Their Combinatorics
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate two companion $q$-series recently suggested for investigation by Andrews and El Bachraoui in the concluding remarks of their work. From these evaluations, we derive the corresponding partition identities and give combinatorial proofs.

title: Expansive operators on Fréchet spaces without continuous norm
abstract: We investigate the existence of (metrically) expansive operators on Fréchet spaces without continuous norm. We first solve a problem posed by Bernardes, Caraballo, Darji, Fávaro, and Peris in 2025, by showing that there is no expansive operator on the Fréchet space $ω$ of all sequences. We prove this fact by investigating the existence of orbits remaining cofinitely inside some fixed closed subspace of finite codimension. We then give examples of expansive operators on some other Fréchet spaces without continuous norm.

title: Almost-global convergence to twisted states in discrete Huygens rings
abstract: We study the discrete Huygens phase map on the ring $C_n$, the simplest oscillator network in which the coupling can be frustrated. Reciprocal coupling favours phase opposition between neighbours, while the edge phase differences must sum to zero modulo $2π$ around the cycle; for odd $n$ these two requirements are incompatible. The parity of $n$ determines the absolute minima of the potential. When $4\mid n$, the critical set also contains circles of critical points, all of which meet at two completely degenerate configurations. After quotienting by the common phase, the map is a gradient step for an intrinsic potential on an $(n-1)$-torus, and the cycle spectrum gives an explicit interval of interaction strengths on which every orbit converges to a critical point. Our main result is that, on this whole interval and for every $n\ge3$, almost every orbit converges to a uniform twisted minimum, including at interaction strengths for which the map is not invertible. When $4\mid n$, the non-minimal points of the critical circles are treated by a centre-stable manifold argument. At the two degenerate intersections, a local blow-up reduces the problem to the cubic leading term of the potential and its restriction to the unit sphere. Orbits approaching along directions where this restriction is positive form a null set, because the cubic is harmonic in the intrinsic metric. No orbit approaches along its zero level, where the critical points are non-degenerate saddles on invariant rays. Hence the degenerate equilibria also have basins of zero measure.

title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
abstract: Nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds underlies many problems in machine learning and deep learning. However, existing stochastic Riemannian retraction methods often rely on stepsizes that require prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant, a prescribed iteration horizon, or restrictive batch-size choices. We develop {\sf RGR}, a recursive gradient retraction method for stochastic nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds. Instead of recursively updating gradient estimators in changing tangent spaces, {\sf RGR} constructs them in the Euclidean space and subsequently maps them to tangent space, thereby avoiding vector transport. The method comprises three variants: {\sf RGR-SPIDER} for finite-sum optimization and {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} for online stochastic optimization. {\sf RGR-SPIDER} is Lipschitz-free and horizon-free, as its adaptive stepsize requires neither prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant nor a prescribed iteration horizon. {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} are mini-batch and horizon-free methods whose convergence guarantees do not rely on prescribed large batch sizes and whose parameters can be chosen without prior knowledge of the total iteration budget. We show that {\sf RGR-SPIDER} reaches an $\varepsilon$-critical point using $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations and $\mathcal{O}(N+\sqrt{N}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations, where $N$ denotes the number of component functions. For the online setting, {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} achieve iteration complexities of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$, respectively. Experiments on principal component analysis, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal convolutional neural networks demonstrate faster empirical convergence than methods that construct recursive gradient estimators directly in Riemannian tangent spaces.

title: A Non-Dichotomy for CSPs of Stable $ω$-Categorical Structures
abstract: We construct countable, stable, $ω$-categorical structures with at most two binary relations whose CSPs exhibit three complexity regimes: NP-complete, decidable but not in NP, and undecidable. The templates arise from a controlled Hrushovski construction of stable $ω$-categorical graphs $M_α$ for suitable irrational parameters $α>1$. Some of these graphs have NP-complete CSPs. Expanding the graphs $M_α$ by the non-edge relation turns age membership into a restriction of the CSP. For every time-constructible bound $t$, there is such an expansion whose CSP is decidable but not in DTIME$(t)$. For an explicit parameter $α$, the restriction to complete instances belongs to $\mathrm{coNP}$ and the full CSP belongs to $Σ_2^{\mathrm P}$. Separating the ages of the $M_α$ using graphs with large girth and prescribed density yields $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct CSPs of these expansions, all but countably many of which are undecidable.

title: Elementary ratio and zero limits for varying recurrences
abstract: Two theorems of Loureiro and Van Assche on ratio and zero limits provided part of the motivation for this note. Their elementary nature permits direct proofs; Appendix B gives complete proofs of both for the canonical initial conditions, using earlier continued-fraction identities. We prove ratio limits and weak limits of normalized zero measures for varying higher-order three-term recurrences with arbitrary coefficient periods and independent limiting functions for their phases. Joint local coefficient limits give ratio convergence without uniform coefficient bounds. For zero measures, convergence in measure to finite measurable profiles suffices, without boundedness or integrability; the limiting measures may have noncompact support. Coefficients may vanish, and real diagonal terms are allowed for ordinary three-term recurrences. The proofs use interlacing, partial fractions with nonnegative residues, local computations of moments, and stability of zero counts under changes of recurrence coefficients. Truncation removes the coefficient bounds from the zero theorem, whose proof is independent of ratio asymptotics. Uniform bounds give the version with compact support. Power-law limits and their explicit transform formula follow as a special case.
comment: This work generalises results previously established in arXiv:2609.02801v1

title: On the Regularization of Primal-Dual Dynamics in Time-Dependent Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: We study continuous-time primal-dual dynamics for tracking solutions of time-dependent constrained optimization problems. First, for uniformly strongly convex-strongly concave saddle functions, we establish explicit finite-time tracking and additive-disturbance bounds.
