In this paper, we compute the Waring rank of certain complete intersection forms. As an application, we compute the Waring rank of binomials whose annihilator is a complete intersection ideal. Further, we also compute the Waring rank of the product of binary forms in different sets of variables.

title: Frequency-dependent capacitance matrix formulation for Fabry--Pérot resonances. Part II: One-dimensional periodic media
abstract: We study Bloch resonances of one-dimensional periodic systems of high-contrast resonators beyond the subwavelength regime. An exact transfer-matrix formulation identifies the limiting wavenumbers with the union of the interior Neumann frequencies and the Dirichlet frequencies of the separating intervals. At each fixed reference wavenumber, we introduce a periodic frequency-dependent capacitance matrix whose positive eigenvalues determine all leading square-root splittings in the contrast parameter. A direct cyclic matching expansion proves the approximation, including multiple eigenvalues and small complex contrasts. A spectral exclusion result outside the limiting set yields a direct bandgap statement. At a common resonance of all intervals, we also derive uniform eigenmode approximations and distinguish the zero-frequency mode from nonzero double Bloch eigenvalues. For positive contrast, exact linear crossings are characterized by the monodromy matrix being proportional to the identity. A complete local classification is obtained for two resonators per cell and, through band folding, for fully symmetric arrays with any number of resonators per cell. We further formulate the weighted Zak phase for isolated bands and its quantization under reflection symmetry. Explicit two-resonator formulas and numerical illustrations complement the analysis.

title: Prescribed and simultaneous failures of log-concavity in trees with perfect matchings
abstract: We construct trees with perfect matchings and independence sequences that fail log-concavity near the independence number $α$. For every integer $k\geq1$, one family fails at $α-k$ and has a witness of order $O(k^2\log(k+2))$. For every integer $t\geq2$, a single tree has simultaneous failures at $α-1,α-3,\ldots,α-(2t-1)$, with a witness of order $O(t^3)$. All these trees satisfy $α=N/2$, where $N$ is the number of vertices, and contradict Conjecture 4.2 of Ramos and Sun. A sufficient condition uses a fixed tree and the numbers of attached leaves. For fixed $k$ or $t$, explicit bounds give geometric decay of $a_j^2/(a_{j-1}a_{j+1})$ at these indices as the trees grow; $a_j$ counts independent $j$-sets. The proofs count independent sets by empty matching pairs. The Lean proof assistant checks formal proofs of the parameterized results and their quantitative bounds; exact 90- and 180-vertex examples illustrate the constructions.
comment: 21 pages, 1 figure. Lean formalization included as ancillary files. Code available at: https://github.com/HUSTFRED/Math_open_problems

title: Multilevel Main Effects Matrix Factor Model
abstract: We propose a multilevel main effects matrix factor model (MMEFM) to extract meaningful row and column effects from groups of matrix data. As a generalization of a multilevel matrix factor model, we provide rigorous definitions of MMEFM and identifications, together with iterative algorithms for the estimators of all global and local components in the main effects and common component, including global/local main effects and core ranks, with rates of convergence spelt out. An important feature of the model is that all main effects can be nonstationary and still be consistently estimated at each time point. At the same time, our estimated global common factors are alignment independent, and hence are truly global, and can be presented and given interpretations more easily. We propose a Bootstrap procedure for detecting the existence and identifying the groups of data that are driven by the global common factors. The power of the test, together with the accuracy of various estimators, are demonstrated in extensive simulation settings. Estimation performance is also compared to other state-of-the-art methods for matrix time series by simulations and a set of U.S. equity data. All numerical works are done using the R package MMEFM, which is available at CRAN.

title: Nonuniform dichotomies via time rescaling
abstract: We establish characterizations of general nonuniform dichotomies for linear nonautonomous dynamical systems in terms of nonuniform exponential dichotomies of appropriately time-rescaled systems. In discrete time, for a class of slowly growing rates, such a characterization requires an additional condition involving a suitable notion of nonuniform ordinary dichotomy, which can be omitted for invertible systems. In continuous time, we obtain a more general characterization for a large class of growth rates, without imposing this additional condition. Our approach does not rely on adapted Lyapunov norms and applies to evolution families on arbitrary Banach spaces. As applications, we show how several results concerning general nonuniform dichotomies can be derived from their counterparts for exponential dichotomies.

title: A Practical Combinatorial Interior Point Method for Minimum-Cost Flow
abstract: In a recent breakthrough, Chen, Kyng, Liu, Peng, Probst Gutenberg, and Sachdeva (arXiv:2203.00671) designed the first almost-linear-time algorithm for minimum-cost flow. Their approach uses an Interior Point Method (IPM) to achieve complexity $m^{1+o(1)}\log U \log C$. However, the $m^{1+o(1)}$ factor hides intricate recursive data structures, large constants and multiple log factors. In this paper, we give an implementation following the core ideas of their IPM with practical data structures and empirically obtained decision rules. We compare our solver with the cost scaling and network simplex solvers of LEMON on the instance families of the DIMACS Flow Challenge 2.0 core benchmark. Our implementation scales competitively on five of twelve families and better on two. On grid_wide we observe close to linear scaling: $m^{1.04}$ against $m^{1.48}$ for LEMON. We read these results as first evidence that the almost-linear-time framework can be relevant in practice, discuss our insights gained during the implementation process, and motivate where future work should focus to bridge the theory-practice gap.
comment: Submitted to the 13th DIMACS Implementation Challenge: Network Flows 2.0

title: Attainment of the sharp stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality
abstract: The existence of minimizer for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality and the stability of Beckner conformal Log-Sobolev inequality (the endpoint case of fractional Sobolev inequality) have been established by König and Chen-Lu-Tang. The existence of minimizer for stability of the Log-Sobolev inequality is unsolved. In this paper, we solve this problem. For every $n\geq2$, we prove that the sharp $L^2$-stability constant of Beckner conformal log-Sobolev inequality on $\mathbb S^n$ is attained and is strictly less than $\frac{2\log2}{n}$. Moreover, the normalized stability constant of the fractional Sobolev inequality converges to the stability constant of the log-Sobolev inequality as $s\to0^+$. After Hersch normalization, every sequence of $L^{p_{s_k}}$-normalized minimizers for stability of the fractional Sobolev inequality, with $s_k\to0^+$, has a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2(\mathbb S^n)$ to an $L^2$-normalized minimizer of stability of the log-Sobolev inequality.

title: Lifting Prym Divisors on a Bielliptic Loop of Loops
abstract: Let $C$ be a bielliptic curve over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of odd characteristic or characteristic zero, and let $f \colon \widetilde{C} \to C$ be an étale double cover. We prove that, if $f$ specializes to a certain double cover of a loop of loops, then every Prym divisor on the loop of loops lifts to a Prym divisor of the same rank on $\widetilde{C}$. As consequences, we compute the dimension of the Prym-Brill-Noether variety $V^r (C,f)$, show that it is reduced and irreducible when the dimension is positive, and compute its cohomology class.

title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
abstract: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $σ^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $ψ(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $σ(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $σ^*(q)$.

title: Endpoint power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions
abstract: We prove sharp $L^p(|x|^α)$ estimate for spherical maximal functions. We resolve the remaining open problem for the full maximal operator for $α=1-d$ and $p<2$ and prove a more general result involving a local version of Assouad dimension of the underlying dilation set. We also make a case study with endpoint bounds for a model case involving convex sequences in $[1,2]$.

title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
abstract: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hilário, Sá, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).

title: Global well-posedness for a damped two dimensional fluid--beam system
abstract: We study the normalized surface system of an irrotational incompressible fluid of infinite depth beneath an elastic Euler--Bernoulli beam with structural damping. For every fixed damping coefficient $γ>0$, we establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial data in $H^2(\R)\times\bigl(\dot H^{1/2}(\R)\cap\dot H^1(\R)\bigr)$. The main novelty is that the admissible data include finite energy initial potentials for which neither $ψ_0$ nor $u_0=ψ_0+G(η_0)ψ_0$ has an $L^2$ representative. We also prove the exact energy dissipation identity at the regularity of the constructed solutions. The main analytical difficulties are the possible failure of $L^2$ integrability at low frequencies and the justification of energy differentiation at the solution regularity. To handle the low-frequency difficulty, we fix the low-frequency part of the initial potential and evolving an $L^2$ remainder. Homogeneous Dirichlet--Neumann estimates and a high-frequency Fourier symmetrizer yield local well-posedness with $H^{-1}$ forcing. Continuous Fréchet differentiability of the energy in these affine coordinates, together with a chain rule on $H^1\subset L^2\subset H^{-1}$, justifies the dissipation identity. The Energy identity and coercivity provide uniform bounds that yields global continuation tharough the local theory. Iterating the local uniqueness and stability estimates gives global uniqueness within the stated affine solution class and Lipschitz dependence on bounded sets over every finite time interval.

title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.

title: Weighted Norm Inequalities for Maximal Multi-sublinear Rough Singular Integrals
abstract: We continue our study of multilinear rough homogeneous singular integrals by establishing weighted estimates for their maximal truncations. Let $m\ge2$ and let $Ω\in L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})$, $1<q\le\infty$, have mean zero. For $1<p_1,\dots,p_m<\infty$ with $p_j\ge q'$ and $1/p=\sum_{j=1}^m1/p_j$, we prove $$\big\Vert \mathcal{L}_Ω^*(f_1,\dots,f_m)\big\Vert_{L^p(v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}})} \lesssim \VertΩ\Vert_{L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})} \prod_{j=1}^m\Vert f_j\Vert_{L^{p_j}(w_j)}$$ whenever $\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}=(w_1,\dots,w_m)\in A_{(p_1/q',\dots,p_m/q')}$, where $q'$ is the Hölder conjugate of $q$ and $v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}}=\prod_{j=1}^m w_j^{p/p_j}$. The estimate holds under the same multiple weight condition as the corresponding principal value estimate.

title: A topological sphere theorem for pinched Legendrian submanifolds
abstract: Let $M^n$ be a closed simply connected Legendrian submanifold of $\mathbb S^{2n+1}$, where $n\geq5$, and let $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{B}$ denote its second fundamental form and mean-curvature vector. We prove that $M$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb S^n$ if \begin{equation*} |\mathbf{B}|^2\leq \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}n+\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|^2-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|\sqrt{|\mathbf{H}|^2+4n}. \end{equation*} The equality can be attained by the Calabi products, so simple connectivity cannot be omitted. For $n\geq4$, we also prove a sphere theorem under an explicit bound and the weaker assumption $b_1(M;\mathbb R)=0$. The proof combines phase-rotated Lawson--Simons variations with a systolic inequality for finite two-complexes. We also give local constructions showing that the pinching condition allows negative isotropic curvature at a point.

title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) based on the Wasserstein distance is widely used to address this challenge. However, we find that the conventional Wasserstein ambiguity set tends to excessively amplify the probabilities of low-probability extreme events, leading to over-conservative investment decisions. To mitigate this over-conservatism, this paper proposes a novel ambiguity set that modifies the Wasserstein distance with a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization term. By leveraging the KL divergence's sensitivity to relative probability changes, the proposed set effectively curbs the unrealistic magnification of low-probability events. A two-stage distributionally robust planning model built upon this new ambiguity set is developed to optimize the installed capacity of photovoltaic, wind, and energy storage. The complex model is then reformulated as an equivalent exponential cone program with strict theoretical proofs, making it computationally tractable. Numerical results on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems reveal the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO under low-probability extreme events and validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed planning model and solution algorithm.

title: Finite-on-Top-of-Temporal CSPs in Fixed-Point Logic
abstract: We study definability in fixed-point logic with counting (FPC) for a class of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) that simultaneously generalises finite-domain CSPs and temporal CSPs. The templates for the CSPs are first-order expansions of the structure $([k] \times {\mathbb Q};<_1,\dots,<_k,\sim)$ where $<_i \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid x<x'\}$ and $\sim \, := \{((i,x),(i,x')) \mid i \in [k], x,x' \in {\mathbb Q}\}$, i.e., $k$ copies of $({\mathbb Q};<)$. Such a CSP is definable in FPC precisely when the template pp-constructs neither the ternary temporal relation $X$, which holds on three elements if the minimum is attained exactly twice, nor a nontrivial finite affine structure. Equivalently, the template has global polymorphisms that witness the tractability of the temporal CSPs on the copies, and that provide 3-4 weak near-unanimity operations on the set of copies of ${\mathbb Q}$. In this case, we prove that the CSP is even expressible in the less expressive logic FP$^*$, which is the restriction of FPC without counting terms (i.e., the extension of first-order logic by a fixed point operator and an ordered auxiliary number sort). Our algorithm samples finitely many values in each copy and then performs nested constraint-singleton consistency tests (which is a uniform polynomial-time algorithm for finite-domain CSPs). The correctness proof uses finite-domain CSP theory to combine consistency certificates by a single polymorphism term, fixing each variable to one copy without destroying the certificates needed for the temporal algorithm. We then use a known normal form for algebraic products to control the remaining interactions between different copies.

title: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Hořava-Lifshitz cosmology
abstract: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Hořava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. Moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a Cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. In particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
abstract: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.

title: Goodman-type lower bounds for odd cycles I: The dense regime
abstract: Goodman proved a lower bound on triangle counts which, in graphon language, states that every graphon of edge density $p$ has triangle density at least $2p^2-p$. Bennett, Dudek, Lidický, and Pikhurko established the corresponding bound for $C_5$, determining its minimum density at every Turán density $p=1-1/k$ with an integer $k\ge3$. We extend this bound to every odd cycle in the dense regime: for every odd integer $m\ge3$ and every graphon $W$ with edge density $p\ge2/3$, $t(C_m, W) \ge p^m-p(1-p)^{m-1}.$ For $2/3\le p<1$, equality holds precisely for balanced complete $k$-partite graphons with an integer $k\ge3$, up to graphon equivalence, and we establish qualitative stability at these densities. In the same density range, we also strengthen Kim and Lee's density-sensitive commonality inequality for odd cycles by adding the nonnegative term $t(P_{m-1},1-W)-(1-p)^{m-1}$ to the lower bound, where $P_{m-1}$ is the path with $m-1$ edges. To prove the main results, we develop a spectral excursion expansion and use Dirichlet averaging to reduce the resulting polynomial inequalities in arbitrarily many spectral variables to a one-variable problem. We prove the one-variable inequality through a uniform inequality comparing odd and even moments of shifted Gamma random variables. We also formalise the odd-cycle lower-bound theorem in Lean 4.

title: Triple Junctions in Multi-Phase Obstacle type Problems
abstract: We study the regularity of the free boundary for a multi-phase obstacle-type problem associated to quadrature domains, which arises from the minimization of the energy $$J(U,F):= \int_{B_1} (\frac 1 2 |\nabla U|^2 + F \cdot U)dx$$ among all competitors $U=(u^1,\ldots, u^N)$ with non-negative components $u^i \geq 0$ with disjoint supports, and constant forcing terms $f^i>0.$ We focus on the geometry of the free boundary at points where at least three distinct components meet (triple junctions).

title: Radon Transforms of Projection Functions and Aleksandrov-Fenchel Inequalities
abstract: The Radon transforms on Grassmannians define two families of geometric operators on convex bodies when applied to their projection functions. On the one hand, these are Minkowski's projection body maps and on the other hand these operators coincide on origin-symmetric bodies with the mean section body maps introduced by Goodey and Weil in 1992. Over the past two decades various sharp isoperimetric inequalities for projection bodies were shown to also hold for mean section bodies. However, an analogue of Lutwak's log-concavity inequalities for the intrinsic volumes of projection bodies remained open for mean section bodies. We establish new Aleksandrov--Fenchel inequalities for averages of certain mixed volumes and apply them to show that also all the intrinsic volumes of mean section bodies are indeed log-concave.

title: The operator-valued Schur-Agler class in infinitely many variables
abstract: Motivated by a recent work of G. Knese [Canad. Math. Bull., 2026], we introduce the operator-valued Schur-Agler class in infinitely many variables, consisting of functions whose restrictions to every finite-dimensional polydisk lie in the operator-valued Schur-Agler class. We first establish an operator-valued analogue of Montel's theorem and, using it as a key ingredient, establish an Agler decomposition and a realization formula for functions in this class. The series in the Agler decomposition converges in the strong operator topology, and we show that this convergence cannot, in general, be strengthened to norm convergence. The realization formula yields a holomorphic extension of every function in the operator-valued Schur-Agler class to $\mathrm{Ball}(\ell^\infty)$, the open unit ball of $\ell^\infty$. Finally, as an application, we prove an Agler-Pick interpolation theorem in infinitely many variables.

title: Improved Analysis of Adaptive Task Allocation and Non-Stationary Processing Times
abstract: We study the task allocation problem, where our goal is to develop an online algorithm that efficiently distributes tasks among workers based on their computational performance. This task is challenging since computation times are random and non-stationary in practice. Recent works have introduced different online algorithms to address this problem. One of them is Adaptive Task Allocation (ATA), a bandit-style algorithm. However, previous theoretical guarantees leave substantial room for improvement, and existing methods are designed only for stationary computation times. Using new proof techniques, our work establishes an improved analysis of ATA with better gap-dependent and gap-independent regret guarantees, improving upon all previous approaches. We also introduce a new method, Sliding Window Adaptive Task Allocation (SW-ATA), designed for more practical non-stationary environments. Finally, we prove new lower bounds in both the stationary and non-stationary settings.

title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
abstract: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators. For subcritical Schrödinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.

title: Interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations
abstract: We study interior Hessian estimates for $k$-convex solutions of Hessian quotient equations $\frac{σ_k(D^2u)}{σ_\ell(D^2u)}=1$ with $2\leq k\leq n$, $0 \leq \ell < k$, and $k-\ell \in\{1,2\}$. We first adopt the unified quantitative separation-propagation method of Li--Wu [LW26b] to derive a doubling inequality, and then use the compactness argument of Shankar--Yuan [SY25] to obtain the estimates. This approach also applies to a class of general Hessian equations.

title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.

title: One-way pressure-independent valves with hysteresis and chattering
abstract: We propose a model for the one-dimensional isothermal gas flow through a valve in a pipe. The valve aims at keeping the outgoing flow in an assigned interval; moreover, its opening and closing depend on a further parameter. The model is realized by a system of two conservation laws with suitable conditions coupling the ingoing and the outgoing flow. We study the corresponding Riemann problem, where non-classical shocks show up. Although simple, the model allows to study two key oscillatory behaviors of the flow, which are due, respectively, to the chattering of the valve, especially seen in the numerical simulations, and to the stabilizing hysteresis induced by the valve operation. We characterize the states leading to chattering and show how they depend on the parameters of the model. Through several numerical simulations, we study the interplay between the two above phenomena.

title: River ribbon tableaux and symmetric group characters
abstract: We introduce river ribbon tableaux, where a river of non-trivial ribbons is placed between two banks of single boxes. Compared to other ribbon peelings, this reduces the geometric differences across diagrams of different shapes, and the maximal number of ribbon configurations. This allows us to prove a uniform character bound for symmetric groups which, specialized to balanced diagrams, proves the conjecture of Moore and Russell. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Dousse and Féray on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

title: On Chen's conjecture for the log-concavity of the longest increasing subsequence distribution
abstract: Let $P_{n,k}$ count permutations of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. Chen conjectured that $(P_{n,k})_{k=1}^n$ is log-concave for every positive integer $n$. In this paper, we prove that Chen's conjecture is true when $n\ge 10^{10^{65}}$. The proof combines Gessel's determinantal formula with quantitative coefficient extraction, Tracy--Widom density estimates, and exact inequalities for the extreme lengths.

title: Sparse-group Convoluted Smoothed Quantile Regression in High Dimension
abstract: In many applications, covariates are naturally organized into groups, yet conventional group-selection methods often retain all variables within selected groups, failing to achieve within-group sparsity. To address this limitation, we propose an adaptive two-stage sparse-group selection procedure for high-dimensional quantile regression. The proposed method integrates convolution-smoothed quantile loss with $\ell_{2,0}$ and $\ell_0$ penalties to identify important groups and relevant variables within them, achieving sparsity at both levels. We establish theoretical guarantees for sure screening and exact support recovery at both stages, as well as consistent model-size selection using information criteria, with explicit bounds on failure probabilities. The proposed procedure is computationally efficient by restricting optimization to selected groups and active variables. Simulation studies and a breast cancer gene-expression analysis demonstrate its competitive performance in variable selection, estimation accuracy, and computational efficiency, while identifying biologically relevant genes and delivering accurate quantile predictions.

title: Composite and Stochastic Smoothed Decentralized Bregman Proximal-Gradient Methods
abstract: Smoothed decentralized Bregman proximal-gradient (SDBPG) methods combine relative-smoothness geometry with edge-dual consensus. We extend SDBPG to node-specific convex nonsmooth regularizers and unbiased stochastic local gradients while retaining its Bregman primal-dual smoothing mechanism. The analysis isolates temporal subgradient motion and aggregation mismatch as two defect sequences. For trajectories in a forward-invariant compact subset of the kernel domain and admissible parameters, finite accumulated defects yield an $O(T^{-1})$ bound on the squared best-iterate proximal residual over $T$ iterations. The stochastic bound separates accumulated oracle variance from expected defects and attains the same order when the variance bounds and expected defects are summable. Common active-structure identification, together with local subgradient conditions, gives sufficient finite-defect conditions for $\ell_1$ and group $\ell_{2,1}$ regularization. Experiments with common regularizers and heterogeneous sensing operators relate defect decay to observed support stabilization and compare reconstruction and communication with decentralized proximal and gradient-tracking methods. A separate phase-retrieval study evaluates the effect of a quartic Bregman kernel. Code and experiment scripts are available at https://github.com/shengze-xu/composite-stochastic-sdbpg .

title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
abstract: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.

title: Isometric dilations and Beurling quotient modules
abstract: In \cite{Dan-Guo}, the authors provided a characterization of all sequences of doubly commuting pure contractions that have the sequence $\textbf{M}_z,$ the sequence of the multiplication by the coordinate functions on the vector-valued Hardy space $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb {D}_2^{(\infty)})$ over the Hilbert's multidisk $\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)},$ as their minimal isometric dilation for some Hilbert space $\mathcal E$. In this article, we remove the hypothesis of doubly commutativity and characterize all sequences of commuting contractions that are unitarily equivalent to $(P_{\mathcal Q}M_{z_i}|_{\mathcal Q})_{i\geq 1}$ for some quotient module $\mathcal Q$ of $H^2_\mathcal E(\mathbb D_2^{(\infty)})$. We further characterize those sequences for which $\mathcal Q$ is a Beurling quotient module. This generalizes Theorem 3.2 from \cite{BKD} to a sequence of commuting contractions.

title: Frobenius liftability of isolated complete intersections
abstract: We classify Frobenius liftable normal isolated complete intersection singularities of dimension at least three over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. In dimension three, they are precisely the regular points and the ordinary double points; in higher dimensions, they are regular. We also characterize Frobenius liftability of the complete local hypersurfaces defined by $xy-g(z,t)$ without assuming that the singularity is isolated. Such a hypersurface is Frobenius liftable if and only if, after a formal change of coordinates, $g$ is a unit times $H^pz^at^b$ with $0\le a,b<p$.

title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $λ>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.

title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
abstract: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ Λ\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.

title: Combinatorial bounds for the v-number of binomial edge ideals
abstract: We study the local $\mathrm v$-numbers of binomial edge ideals from a combinatorial perspective. For each minimal prime $P_{\mathcal S}$ of $J_G$, indexed by a cutset $\mathcal S$ of $G$, we consider two combinatorial invariants, $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, defined in terms of transversals of suitable hypergraphs, and show that the local $\mathrm v$-number $\mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)$ satisfies $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)\leq \mathrm v_{P_{\mathcal S}}(J_G)\leq \mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$. Under a suitable hypothesis on the connected components, we provide explicit graph-theoretic descriptions of these invariants and analyze when they coincide, giving a combinatorial way to determine the local $\mathrm v$-numbers. As an application, we derive a sufficient condition for this coincidence, which applies to a broad class of graphs. Furthermore, we identify a constant that controls the gap between $\mathrm v^-_{\mathcal S}(G)$ and $\mathrm v^+_{\mathcal S}(G)$, thereby showing that the local $\mathrm{v}$-number lies within a bounded interval. Applications to cycles and trees illustrate both the equality criterion and the resulting bounds.

title: Hyperelastic Modeling of Cardiac Tissue Deformation for Data Registration
abstract: This work proposes a biomechanical registration framework designed to combine functional optical-mapping data with structural high-resolution MRI of cardiac tissue. The two acquisitions are performed in different mechanical configurations: optical mapping is obtained after stretching the sample, whereas MRI is acquired in a fixed resting state. To estimate the deformation between these configurations, the tissue is modeled as a nearly incompressible transversely isotropic hyperelastic material, and the traction amplitude is identified from optical-map marker positions through an inverse problem. Two-and threedimensional simulations show physically admissible deformations and provide a first proof of concept for the proposed strategy.
journal_ref: CinC 2026 - 53rd Computing in Cardiology conference, Sep 2026, Madrid, Spain

title: Interpolation and coherence in multiple testing
abstract: In the literature on multiple testing methods that control the familywise error rate, a fundamental concept is "coherence". A procedure is coherent if it is "logically consistent" (Hochberg and Tamhane, 1987) in the sense that if a hypothesis is rejected, then all hypotheses that imply it are also rejected. If a method is not coherent, then it can be made coherent without increasing the familywise error rate. Recently, the concept of coherence was generalized to a much broader class of multiple testing procedures, namely all methods that provide simultaneous confidence bounds for false discovery proportions. Such procedures were defined to be coherent if they cannot be further improved through a process called "interpolation". However, we show that such a coherent procedure can sometimes be further improved by exploiting remaining logical inconsistencies. This leads to what we call a "perfectly coherent" method. Thus, interpolation does not necessarily lead to perfect coherence. However, we provide conditions under which it does. Fortunately, many methods based on interpolation turn out to be perfectly coherent.

title: A counting proof for the smallest critical set in a Latin square
abstract: A critical set in a Latin square is a set of entries that determines the square uniquely and is minimal with this property. We prove that every partial Latin square of order $n$ with fewer than $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ filled cells has an even number of completions. Consequently every critical set in every Latin square of order $n$ has at least $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$ entries. Since the cyclic Latin square has a critical set of exactly this size, the minimum size of a critical set over all Latin squares of order $n$ is $\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor$. This confirms a conjecture attributed to Nelder (1979) and made independently by Mahmoodian and by Bate and van Rees. Hatami and Qian had shown that this minimum is at least $n^2/10^4$ for large $n$. The proof is a counting argument modulo two that uses only expansion of products, cancellation in pairs and the pigeonhole principle, and it is illustrated with partial Latin squares of orders three to seven. An appendix discloses the substantial use of AI in developing the proof and writing the exposition.

title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature
abstract: We prove that every tangent flow at the first singular time of a smooth, closed, embedded mean curvature flow has smooth support, provided that the total curvature satisfies $\sup_{t\in[0,T)}\int_{M_t}|A|^n\,dμ_t<\infty$. This extends Ilmanen's smoothness result for tangent flows to higher dimensions.

title: Finite groups with conjugacy classes of size $2p^n$
abstract: We extend Burnside's $p^a$-Theorem on conjugacy classes of prime-power size by proving that no non-abelian finite simple group possesses a conjugacy class of size $2p^n$ for any prime $p$ and $n\geq 0$. Based on this, we partially extend a well-known result of L. Kazarin by showing that, given a finite group $G$, the subgroup generated by a conjugacy class $x^G$ of size $2p^n$ where $x$ has odd order, is a solvable normal subgroup of $G$. If instead the subgroup $\langle x^G \rangle$ generated by such a class $x^G$ is non-solvable (which forces $x$ to have even order), then $p= 5$ and $\langle x^G \rangle/S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ is isomorphic to the symmetric group $S_5$, where $S(\langle x^G \rangle)$ denotes the solvable radical of $\langle x^G \rangle$.

title: Large deviations, gradient flows and fluctuating hydrodynamics for fractional diffusion
abstract: This work is a step towards a general understanding of fluctuations for systems of particles described at large scale by fractional diffusion. First, we derive formally a Large Deviation Principle for the empirical measure of mean-field interacting particles with a L{é}vy-type noise. In the case of independent particles, this unveils a generalized gradient flow structure at large scales. Second, we derive and solve numerically a stochastic Partial Differential Equation describing the fluctuating hydrodynamics of this system. The results compare well with direct numerical integration of the particles' dynamics.

title: Backward and reflected backward stochastic differential equations under initial enlargement of Brownian filtrations
abstract: We investigate the effect of initially enlarging a Brownian filtration by its terminal value on backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs (RBSDEs). We establish the Brownian innovation representation and the predictable representation property in the enlarged filtration, highlighting the singular information drift arising from the semimartingale decomposition of the original Brownian motion. We derive transfer identities under suitable integrability conditions and provide explicit counterexamples showing that the resulting singular equations may fail to admit unique square-integrable solutions, including in the reflected case. We further develop a conditional parametrization of regular BSDEs and establish a conditional comparison principle for Snell envelopes, illustrating both the strict value of additional information and the failure of general pathwise domination. An exact projection identity is also obtained for zero-driver terminal payoffs. Finally, we discuss possible extensions to irregular obstacles and more general information structures.

title: Uniqueness of solutions to the 2D compressible Navier-Stokes equations for bounded densities
abstract: We prove the uniqueness of global solutions to the two dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations within the regularity class introduced by Danchin and Mucha [14], for general $C^1$ pressure laws. A crucial assumption is that both solutions have bounded divergence, locally integrable in time, which ensures that their densities remain bounded without excluding vacuum or requiring spatial regularity of the density.

title: Multi-dimensional centered rarefaction waves of gas dynamics with vacuum states
abstract: We establish the local-in-time structural stability of two centered rarefaction waves bounding a vacuum region for the two-dimensional isentropic Euler equations with $p(ρ)=kρ^γ$, for $γ\in(1,1.3]\cup\{\frac75,\frac53\}$. For general sufficiently small perturbations of the planar Riemann data, allowing nonzero vorticity, we construct an entropy solution that is continuous for positive time and whose five regions are separated by four characteristic surfaces. The conservative solution has uniform spatial $W^{2,\infty}$ bounds on each time slice of the central region in coordinates $(x_1/t,x_2)$; for $γ=7/5,5/3$, we also obtain spacetime $W^{2,\infty}$ regularity in $(t,x_1/t,x_2)$. The proof develops characteristic geometry directly for the symmetric first-order Euler system and uses two overlapping characteristic charts to separate matching with the exterior flow from estimates uniform up to vacuum. Fixed commutators without sound-speed weights exhibit a first-order null structure, while subtraction of explicit approximate solutions produces damping that cancels the leading antidamping bulk terms in the energy identity. An explicit analysis of the initial-slice ODEs identifies fractional powers and logarithmic terms at zero sound speed. The logarithmic coefficients couple vorticity to tangential variation of the initial data, revealing an obstruction to higher spatial regularity even when the powers of the sound speed have integer exponents. This analysis determines the finite approximation order used to close the energy and geometric estimates in the stated range. These ingredients provide the geometric and energy framework for the forthcoming second paper of this series, which will use finite evolving profiles to treat the full range $γ\in(1,\frac53]$.
comment: corrected typos, improved presentation, unified conventions

title: Numerical simulation of biological capsules based on interface-fitted polygonal meshes
abstract: In this work we introduce a numerical framework for the simulation of biological capsules based on meshes that adapt iteration-wise to the shape of the membrane. The discretization leverages a Hybrid High Order method (HHO) to solve a Stokes problem with a source term distributed on the interface between the internal and the external phases. The HHO discretization supports meshes composed of general polygons, permitting to use fitted meshes that can be easily generated by cutting the elements intersected by the interface. Moreover, polygonal meshes allow arbitrarily accurate interface discretizations without introducing bulk degrees of freedom. The presentation of the simulation algorithm is completed with a proof-of-concept numerical test on a well-established benchmark: the deformation of an elastic capsule immersed in a shear flow.

title: Automorphisms of medium algebras and quasi-anisotropic real affine Grassmannians
abstract: We study automorphisms of Hausel's medium algebras by identifying them with equivariant cohomology algebras of affine Schubert varieties of a complex reductive group $G$. The automorphisms in question are then given by the action of either complex automorphisms or real structures of $G$ on affine Schubert varieties. We focus on describing the fixed points of those automorphisms on the spectra of medium algebras, and prove that the torsion-free quotients of the corresponding coinvariant algebras are isomorphic to equivariant cohomology rings of fixed loci in affine Schubert varieties. In the case of real structures, this naturally leads to and involves the study of affine Grassmannians for quasi-anisotropic (also called quasi-compact) real reductive groups, closely related to recent work of O'Brien. We also discuss relations to automorphisms of Higgs bundle moduli and to symmetric pair variants of medium algebras.

title: UQ-ACE: Stability-Aware Counterfactual Controller Tuning via Bayesian SINDy
abstract: Retuning feedback controllers in critical processes is challenging when experiments are costly, open-loop excitation is infeasible, and candidate controllers must be screened before deployment. The existing Adaptive Sampling for Counterfactual Explanations (ACE) method provides a sample-efficient approach for finding minimal controller-parameter changes that recover prescribed closed-loop performance, but it does not explicitly account for stability of candidate controllers proposed during the search, which may be destabilizing under plant uncertainty. This paper introduces UQ-ACE, a stability-aware retuning method based on Bayesian SINDy. In UQ-ACE, closed-loop trajectories are used to infer a posterior distribution over local dynamical models, from which candidate controllers are screened for stability before implementation. Extensive simulations show that UQ-ACE achieves valid retunings with few closed-loop experiments while preventing deployment of unstable candidates.

title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension
abstract: We study learning an unknown element $g$ of a group acting with finite orbits on a countable set, from examples $(x,gx)$. After a sample on $A$, the consistent hypotheses are the restrictions of a coset of the pointwise stabilizer of $A$, and the sample forces exactly the labels of points this stabilizer fixes; for a Galois group, they form the field generated by the data. Through this correspondence, multiclass dimensions become group invariants: the DS and graph dimensions equal the height, the Littlestone dimension the longest irredundant sequence length, and the teaching dimension the minimal base size. Among deterministic learners, symmetry makes empirical risk minimization optimal: on nondegenerate classes every consistent learner, whatever its tie-breaking, attains the optimal realizable sample complexity up to constant factors, and every consistent online learner the optimal mistake bound. Agnostically, every ERM's sample complexity exceeds the known lower bound by at most the DS-to-Natarajan ratio, up to constants. For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.
comment: 55 pages, 5 figures. The abstract has been shortened to meet arXiv's submission requirements

title: From a Student's Question to the Half-Derivative: A Constructivist Teaching Model - Part I
abstract: This paper presents a conceptual, cognitive-constructivist model for teaching the half-derivative. The model starts from a student's question and frames it as the problem of generalizing the familiar operation of differentiation. On a suitably chosen space of monomials, under the assumptions of linearity and of lowering the exponent by one half, the requirement that the operator applied twice give the ordinary derivative produces a recurrence for the coefficients. The freedom of normalization becomes visible, and an additional convention yields a formula compatible with the monomial rule of the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative. The domain of the operator and its relation to the Riemann-Liouville and Caputo operators are treated separately. The mathematical results rest on the author's earlier preprints; the contribution of this paper is their transformation into an instructional pathway organized in phases, with diagnostic questions, an analysis of typical errors, and comparative problems. The model is a design proposal: its effectiveness has not yet been established by systematic empirical research. The interactive Socratic implementation and the detailed diagnostics are the subject of Part II.

title: Alternating Hamilton Paths and Cycles in Poset Products
abstract: We study alternating Hamilton paths and cycles in the comparability graphs of finite posets. We prove that if a finite poset $P$ with at least two elements admits an alternating Hamilton path, then $P\times B_r$ admits an alternating Hamilton cycle for every $r\ge2$, where $B_r$ is the Boolean lattice. As a corollary, we settle a conjecture of Katona [Discrete Appl. Math., 2013]. Furthermore, we characterize the divisor lattices admitting alternating Hamilton paths and cycles.

title: Reverse Translation and Convolution Estimates in the Framework of the Mehler-Fock Transform
abstract: In this paper, reverse translation and convolution estimates in the frame of $μ^{th}$ order Mehler-Fock transform are obtained. Continuity properties of these operators on the test function space $\mathfrak{H}_{l,r,n}$ have been discussed. Moreover, Sobolev space $S_{r,p}^{N,α}$ has been introduced and again continuity properties of these operators in this Sobolev space have been discussed.

title: Standard identities for polynomial vector fields
abstract: Let $W_n$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields in $n$ variables over a field of characteristic zero, and let $s_k$ denote the alternating sum of compositions of $k$ vector fields. The identity $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ has been asserted for arbitrary $n$. We give an explicit counterexample in dimension five, verified by an exact integer computation of a $34$-commutator. Together with the known vanishing of $s_{35}$, this shows that $35$ is the least degree of a standard identity on $W_5$. We then prove that $s_{n^2+2n-1}=0$ for every even $n\geq2$. The proof uses Lie algebra homology with coefficients in the polynomial algebra modulo constants and a lemma on invariant tensors. We describe the computation and provide the source code and verification results.
comment: 8 pages, no figures; verification code and results available at https://github.com/nurtasshyntas/n-commutator-verifier

title: Topological entropy of saturated sets for Lorenz attractors
abstract: We study the topological entropy of saturated sets for continuous flows, with emphasis on singular hyperbolic dynamics. For a $C^r$-generic ($r \geq 2$) vector field $X$ carrying a geometric Lorenz attractor $Λ$, we prove that for every nonempty compact connected set $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(Φ,Λ)$ and every open set $U \subseteq M$ with $U \cap Λ\neq \emptyset$, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(Φ,G_{\mathcal{K}}(Φ) \cap \operatorname{Trans}(Φ,Λ) \cap U)=\inf_{μ\in \mathcal{K}} h_μ(φ_1)$, where $Φ=(φ_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is the flow induced by $X$ and $\operatorname{Trans}(Φ,Λ)$ denotes the set of points whose positive orbits are dense in $Λ$. The same formula holds $C^1$-generically for singular hyperbolic attractors. In contrast with the uniformly hyperbolic case, we also prove that, for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^r(M^3)$, geometric Lorenz attractors admit a positive-entropy invariant measure with no generic points. An analogous conclusion holds for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^1(M)$ whose non-trivial singular hyperbolic attractors contain singularities and satisfy $\dim E^{cu}=2$. These examples show that the discrete-time saturated entropy theory does not extend directly to singular flows.

title: Excess inertia of finite metric spaces
abstract: This paper classifies the possible inertias that are realized by an excess matrix of a finite metric space with at most nine points. For the classification, we make use of relationships between finite metric spaces and non-obtuse and acute sets in classical geometry. As an application, we prove that the small-scale limit of the magnitude function of any six-point metric space is at least one whenever this limit exists.

title: Extensions of Operator Systems, Hyperrigidity and Quantum Double Suspension
abstract: We introduce a class of extensions of unital operator systems satisfying a certain Toeplitz type property and show that these extensions induce corresponding extensions of the $C^*$-algebras they generate. We prove that an extension in this class is hyperrigid in the $C^*$-algebra it generates if and only if both operator systems from which it is constructed are hyperrigid in the $C^*$-algebras they generate. We then introduce the quantum double suspension of operator systems as a special case of this construction and show that its iterates yield the Hong-Szymański quantum double suspensions at the $C^*$-algebra level, including the Vaksman-Soibelman quantum spheres. In particular, we construct hyperrigid operator systems that generate the $C^*$-algebras of these quantum spheres. As a further application, we show that every counterexample to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture gives rise to a sequence of counterexamples. We identify the Šilov ideal and the $C^*$-envelope of these extensions and derive a $K$-theoretic condition under which each such sequence contains infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic counterexamples. In particular, Scherer's counterexample gives rise to infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic counterexamples. Finally, we compute the propagation number, an invariant of operator systems introduced by Connes and van Suijlekom, for this class of extensions.
comment: Minor modification due to the very recent commutative counterexample that appeared in arXiv:2610.26556. A few typos corrected, references added

title: Density of polynomials whose Aron--Berner extensions attain their norms
abstract: We establish a polynomial analogue of Lindenstrauss' theorem in full generality. More precisely, we prove that, for every real or complex Banach space X and every positive integer n, the n-homogeneous scalar-valued polynomials whose Aron-Berner extensions to the bidual X** attain their norms form a dense subset of the space of continuous n-homogeneous polynomials on X. This resolves a problem posed by Aron, Garcia and Maestre in 2003, extending their result for quadratic polynomials to arbitrary degrees without imposing any structural assumptions on the underlying Banach space. We further establish the corresponding theorem for vector-valued polynomials with arbitrary Banach space codomains. Our approach relies on a new perturbation scheme based on averaged linear contractions, which provides simultaneous control of the multilinear variables and yields norm attainment through iterated limits in the bidual.

title: The one percent property for free groups
abstract: We prove that for every $\varepsilon >0$, there is $δ>0$ such that for every probability measure $μ$ on a free group $\mathbb{F}$, if the operator norm of the action of $μ$ on $L^2\mathbb{F}$ by convolution exceeds $\varepsilon$, then there is a coset of an abelian subgroup of $\mathbb{F}$ with $μ$-mass at least $δ$.

title: Stability Analysis of Bounded Solutions to 2-D Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in L^2_uloc Spaces
abstract: This paper examines the stability analysis of two-dimensional incompressible fluids in $L^2_{uloc}$ spaces. Extending the classical stability framework for Euler equations in Yudovich-type settings, we establish the convergence of Navier-Stokes solutions toward Euler solutions as viscosity $ν\to 0$, under the weakened assumptions $u^ν_0 \in L^\infty$ and $ω^ν_0 \in L^\infty$ without imposing decay conditions at infinity. We first derive a priori estimates for the Navier-Stokes equations in $L^\infty$ spaces. Then, using harmonic analysis tools including Littlewood-Paley decomposition and Bony's paraproduct calculus, we prove the $L^\infty$-convergence of the velocity field and $L^2_{uloc}$-convergence of the vorticity as $ν\to 0$.

title: Actions of central Morita monoidal groupoids, and seven term exact sequences of all types
abstract: We introduce a strict monoidal groupoid associated with a given commutative ring $K$. It acts on the Clifford extension systems of $K$-central algebras which are graded by a group $G$, as well as on the generalized collective characters, both of type $φ\in$ Hom$(G,$ Aut$(K))$. These actions partition the two sets above with respect to graded Morita equivalence. By that we establish a seven term exact sequence of type $φ$, which boils down to the celebrated Chase-Harrison-Rosenberg sequence when $φ$ is Galois.

title: On the Convexity of the Upper Bild
abstract: We give a proof of the convexity of the upper bild of a quaternionic matrix, a theorem of So and Thompson. After reduction to $2\times2$ matrices, we introduce real coordinates on a sphere and obtain two representations of the upper bild over the closed unit ball, involving a convex function and a concave function. Minimizing the first and maximizing the second over parameters with a fixed real part yield a convex lower boundary function and a concave upper boundary function, from which convexity follows.

title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact Kähler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,ω}(f^n)=C_{f,ω,i}\,λ_i(f)^n+O(η^n), \] for every $\sqrt{λ_{i-1}(f)λ_{i+1}(f)}<η<λ_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.

title: Computational framework NetBiF predicts and classifies steady-state bifurcations in biochemical systems via reaction network structure
abstract: Dynamics of biochemical systems are dictated by the stoichiometry and kinetics of reaction networks. These systems may admit positive steady states that could undergo qualitative change in response to varying rate parameters. These changes are called steady-state bifurcations, and they correspond to biologically meaningful processes. Classical bifurcation analysis relies on exact kinetics and rate parameters, which are often unknown or difficult to measure for complex systems. To address this, structural bifurcation analysis (SBA) was introduced to predict bifurcations using only the system's associated reaction network. In this work, the computational package NetBiF (Network Bifurcation Finder) is introduced to implement SBA. NetBiF is applied across diverse biochemical systems, including fundamental metabolic pathways, signaling and gene regulatory networks, and a large-scale carbon cycle model, to predict steady-state bifurcations. Crucially, for biochemical systems governed by power law kinetics, the implementation of NetBiF also classifies the steady-state bifurcations as saddle-node, transcritical, or pitchfork via a structural analog of Sotomayor's theorem. To this end, explicit formulations for the bifurcation criteria were derived for these biochemical systems. Determining and classifying bifurcation behaviors provide insight into biochemical systems' abilities to adapt to changing and fluctuating conditions. Collectively, the study presents NetBiF as a scalable, structure-based, and consistent computational tool to implement SBA. Our findings enable researchers to systematically study dynamical behaviors of biochemical systems through their reaction network structures without requiring explicit kinetic information.

title: Tournaments, flags, and spinors
abstract: It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schrödinger Operator on a Compact Graph
abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schrödinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative

title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $γ: \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $Ω$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(γ(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ of $T_γM$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $Ω$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabré et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^Ω\subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^Ω:= \mathscr{W}^Ω\cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^Ω$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^Ω$ via a foliation in the case $Ω$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.

title: Groups with the fixed-point property
abstract: We propose the study of the class of groups that fix a point for every continuous action on any convex compact space. Oliver completed the corresponding program of classifying the finite groups that have this fixed-point property in finite dimensions. Turning to infinite groups, the Schauder--Tychonoff theorem establishes that the integers have the fixed-point property, but this has not been shown for any other infinite, finitely generated group. We establish a local transfer principle and use it to show, as a proof of concept, that $\mathbf{Z} \times (\mathbf{Z}/p\mathbf{Z})$ belongs to this class of groups.

title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
abstract: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;χ,ψ)$ and $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $χ_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;χ_{163},χ_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;χ,χ)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.

title: Non-additive symmetric rank-metric codes
abstract: We study non-additive rank-metric codes contained in the space of symmetric matrices over a finite field. Our main focus is on symmetric $2$-codes. For odd $q$, we introduce a quotient construction for $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ in which rank-one differences are described by isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form on $\mathbb F_q^4$. This leads to a correspondence with partial ovoids of the elliptic quadric $Q^-(5,q)$. Using a construction of Cossidente and Pavese, we obtain a non-additive symmetric $2$-code in $\mathrm{Sym}_3(q)$ of cardinality $q^4+2q^3$, improving the previously known general lower bound. We also give an explicit matrix description of this family. Lastly, we present a block-based construction for symmetric $2$-codes that extends the three-dimensional improvement to all odd dimensions. In particular, for every odd $n\geq3$ and every prime power $q>2$, we obtain \begin{equation*} A_q^{\rm sym}(n,2) \ge q^{(n^2-1)/2}+q^{(n^2-3)/2}+q^{(n^2-9)/2}, \end{equation*} which is strictly larger than the maximum cardinality of an additive symmetric $2$-code with the same parameters. This yields the first infinite family (as the matrix dimension $n$ varies) of non-additive symmetric $2$-codes whose size is larger than the largest achievable size of an additive code with the same parameters; before this, such a gap had only been established for $n=3$.

title: A new approach for estimating the number of spikes in high-dimensional Gaussian models
abstract: In this paper, we study the estimation of the signal subspace dimension $k$ in a $p$-variate signal-plus-noise complex Gaussian model, when the noise covariance matrix is assumed to be diagonal or Toeplitz. We consider the high-dimensional asymptotic regime in which both the data dimension $p$ and the available sample size $n$ diverge to infinity at the same rate, while we also allow $k$ to diverge at a slower speed. In this context, the classical estimates of the literature, consistent in the high-dimensional regime, often rely on the a priori knowledge of an upper bound $k_*$ of $k$, which can be misspecified in practice. Our proposed approach relies on building estimates of the tracial moments of the noise covariance matrix using the $p-k_*$ smallest eigenvalues of the sample covariance matrix (SCM), which are in turn used to build a threshold above which the $k$ largest eigenvalues are isolated. The resulting estimate of $k$ is proved to be consistent in the high-dimensional regime, even for the misspecified situations where $k_* < k$. Numerical experiments in different challenging scenarios illustrate the improvement of the proposed approach over the aforementioned methods.

title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,θ}μ$, $θ\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $μ$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}μ$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $μ$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and Hölder images. First, $\dim_{qH}μ$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^sμ=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}μ$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_Hμ$, $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}μ$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,θ}μ$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $θ$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_Hμ<\dim_Pμ<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}μ)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_Pμ_V=\min\{\dim_Pμ,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $α$-Hölder maps $f_ω:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $μ$, $\dim_Pμ_{f_ω}=m$ almost surely if and only if $αm\leq\dim_{qH}μ$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}μ=\dim_Pμ$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.
comment: This manuscript supersedes and substantially extends the results presented in arXiv:2604.18222 and arXiv:2609.11301. It incorporates all the main results of both preprints into a unified and more comprehensive treatment, providing further developments and a deeper analysis

title: A Smoothed Augmented Lagrangian Method for Mathematical Programs with Vertical Complementarity Constraints
abstract: We propose a smoothed augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) for solving mathematical programs with vertical complementarity constraints (VCCs). The augmented Lagrangian function involving the VCCs is smoothed by the Lasry--Lions double envelope, which is an extension of the Moreau envelope that enjoys enhanced smoothness properties.
