As applications, we obtain deviation bounds for a median-of-means Nadaraya--Watson regression estimator, for the MoM kernel density estimator, and for empirical and Bahadur-type estimators of Value-at-Risk and Conditional Value-at-Risk. Finally, we show that the sampling of bulk materials, where the measurements form a spatially dependent random field, reduces to the one-dimensional setting if the samples are taken in well-separated groups.

title: The $λ$-chain condition for unit interval determinantal fiber rings
abstract: It is shown that certain finite partially ordered sets arising from unit interval determinantal facet ideals satisfy the $λ$-chain condition. In addition, their applications to commutative algebra are briefly discussed.

title: A Khintchine type inequality for non-independent random variables
abstract: In this short note we give a Khintchine-type inequality involving non-independentrandom variables. The basic setting is inspired by Breuer-Major theorem and the proof is based on a hypercontractivity argument.

title: Small area learning
abstract: Small area estimation (SAE) traditionally borrows strength across domains through a prespecified working model. We introduce small area learning (SAL), a learner-agnostic framework that formulates SAE as a multi-target semi-supervised learning problem and treats outcome prediction as a nuisance task. Areas may differ through unrestricted covariate shift and structured conditional shift, with information shared through common and area-specific components. We develop standard and cross-fitted estimators for low-complexity and flexible learners, unifying synthetic, model-based, and fully residual-corrected estimation. For area means, we establish consistency and asymptotic normality and provide variance estimators and confidence intervals. We extend the theory to settings with only aggregated population covariates and characterize the resulting aggregation bias. SAL reveals a bias--variance trade-off: partial residual correction can reduce mean squared error, whereas full correction yields estimators robust to working-model misspecification, potentially at higher variance. Simulations yield RMSE reductions of 34\%--49\% relative to direct estimation, with the best configuration varying across settings. An empirical application favours a cross-fitted estimator using a flexible learner under the chosen validation criterion. The numerical studies also illustrate how shrinkage can produce overly optimistic confidence intervals at the expense of strong modeling assumptions.

title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.

title: Uniform-in-Time and Uniform-in-Temperature Particle Approximations of Coulomb MMD Flows
abstract: We study particle approximations of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) flows with the Coulomb kernel on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d\ge2$, driven by thermal noise of strength $τ\ge0$. For smooth, strictly positive initial and target densities and i.i.d. initial positions, we prove that the expected Wasserstein-1 distance between the empirical measure and the mean-field solution is at most of order $N^{-1/d}$ for $d\ge3$ and $\sqrt{(\log N)/N}$ for $d=2$, uniformly in time and in the temperature $τ\ge0$, including the deterministic case $τ=0$. At each fixed $τ>0$, we also prove propagation of chaos in total variation for any $k$-fold marginal distributions of particles, uniformly in time, with a bound of order $\sqrt{k/τ}$ times the empirical convergence rate. Our proof uses the modulated free-energy method of Bresch, Jabin, and Wang to reduce the particle convergence estimate to a relaxation estimate that controls the time integral of the mean-field velocity gradient uniformly in $τ\ge0$. Near zero temperature, where the smoothing effect of the noise degenerates, we obtain this estimate by recentering the dynamics at thermal equilibrium and using the damping generated by the Coulomb interaction.

title: Nonlinear Feedback Control in High Dimensions using the Polynomial-Polynomial Regulator
abstract: We consider the problem of computing Taylor approximations to the optimal feedback law and value function for infinite-horizon finite-dimensional nonlinear optimal control problem---also known as Al'brekht's method. The scalability of existing Al'brekht-based approaches to computing approximate solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation associated with the optimal control problem has been severely limited by computational resources. The computational time issue has been partially mitigated by recent works leveraging tensor-structure to develop efficient numerical methods. However, RAM requirements still have remained a major hindrance to scaling beyond state dimensions of a few hundred or low thousands. We propose an acceleration to compute the expensive higher-order terms in a reduced space, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. A fast and scalable \textsc{Matlab} implementation is provided open-source for general purpose use, with the ability to accommodate arbitrary polynomial nonlinearities in the control-affine state equation, as well as polynomial state-dependence in the cost function, and the ability to handle systems in generalized form with a non-identity mass matrix, such as finite element models. Combined with the exploitation of sparsity and modern low-rank Riccati solvers, this permits computing approximations to polynomial feedback laws based on Al'brekht's method in hundreds of thousands of states.

title: A clarification of Fermi's formula for the maximum of partial sums
abstract: In Fermi's 1926 note, the expression assigned to the probability that all partial sums remain below a threshold is the complementary crossing probability. We obtain the correct probability from the same diffusion equation and locate the inconsistency in the final integration. We then state the limit for independent increments under the Lindeberg condition. A counterexample with smooth densities shows that small individual variances do not suffice to justify this limit. The probabilistic results are classical; the purpose of this note is to reconcile the stated event with the printed calculation and to make the sufficient hypotheses for the discrete limit explicit.
comment: 5 pages; historical clarification with a precise diffusion-limit statement

title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
abstract: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.

title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $Φ$. A subset $S\subseteqΦ$ is \emph{closed} if $α,β\in S$ and $α+β\inΦ$ imply $α+β\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings and simultaneous separation of positive imaginary roots, together with an addition lemma for fundamental imaginary roots. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.

title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincaré-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(λ\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.

title: An Efficient, Lean 4 Verified Necessary and Sufficient Condition for Membership in Pedigree Polytopes
abstract: The set \(P_{n}\) consists of the characteristic vectors of pedigrees, which are combinatorial encodings in one-to-one correspondence with Hamiltonian cycles. For \(n \geq 4\) and \(τ_{n} = \binom{n}{3}-1\), the Membership Problem for the Pedigree Polytope (M3P) asks whether a given vector \(X \in \mathbb{Q}^{τ_{n}}\) belongs to \(\mathrm{conv}(P_n)\). This paper gives a complete account, with the full proof statements and machine-verified Lean~4 certificates, of the necessary and sufficient (\NS) condition established in Chapter~5 of \emph{Pedigree Polytopes: New Insights on Computational Complexity of Combinatorial Optimisation Problems} (Arthanari, 2023): membership of $X$ in $\mathrm{conv}(P_n)$ is characterised by the feasibility, at every stage $k=4,\dots,n-1$, of a recursively constructed layered network, together with, when needed, a multicommodity flow problem $\mathrm{MCF}(k-1)$ achieving its maximum possible flow $z_{\max}$. We present the construction, the \NS{} condition itself, and the proofs of this characterisation, together with the resulting polynomial-time algorithm for M3P. Both directions of the \NS{} condition --- sufficiency and necessity (the multicommodity-flow feasibility argument of the book's Chapter~5) --- are machine-verified in Lean~4/Mathlib4 with zero unresolved \texttt{sorry}s in either dependency chain. The \NS{} characterisation therefore follows directly from the two machine-checked implications. The complete Lean~4 project is publicly available. A companion introductory article (arXiv:2507.09069) presents the same material for a broader readership, without the Lean~4 verification; the present paper adds full statements, proof sketches, and the complete machine-checked certificates.
comment: 23 pages, 1 Table giving Lean~4 files and their corresponding results in $\emph{Pedigree Polytopes} \cite{arthanari2023book}$

title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
abstract: The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity. First, we resolve the core open problem on the topic by showing the virtual extension complexity can be exponentially smaller than extension complexity. Second, we show there are matroid base polytopes with exponential virtual extension complexity by adapting a semi-algebraic counting argument by Hrubeš that extends the counting arguments of Rothvoss. Finally, we show that the maximum virtual extension complexity of a polygon with $n$ vertices is $Θ(\sqrt{n})$. This resolves an analogue of a question on extension complexity of Fiorini, Rothvoss, and Tiwary in 2011 in the case of virtual extension complexity.

title: Ordinary and measurable colorings of Euclidean three-space
abstract: A proper coloring of Euclidean space is a coloring that assigns different colors to points at distance one. Using the planar character-law rigidity theorem of OpenAI, we prove that every finite proper coloring of $\R^3$ can be replaced by a proper Lebesgue-measurable coloring with the same number of colors. As a corollary we obtain that the ordinary and measurable chromatic numbers of $\R^3$ are equal, and both lie between $7$ and $15$.

title: Lack of exponential stability for thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions
abstract: In this paper we prove that the classical thermoelastic Timoshenko and Bresse systems with thermal coupling acting only on the bending moment are not exponentially stable under full homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions if the equal wave speed condition is not satisfied. Combined with their well-known converses, our results provide complete characterizations of exponential stability in terms of the coefficients of each system. To the best of our knowledge, these characterizations were previously known only under mixed boundary conditions. The proof is based on the introduction of a boundary correction term in the standard trigonometric ansatz so that the full homogeneous Dirichlet conditions are satisfied.

title: The $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance via $3\times3$ block matrices (with application to $p$-Bures-Wasserstein barycenters)
abstract: We study the $p$-Bures-Wasserstein distance $D_p(A,B)=(\mathrm{tr}\,A^p+\mathrm{tr}\,B^p-2\|A^{1/2}B^{1/2}\|_p^p)^{1/2}$ on positive semidefinite matrices; it equals the Bures-Wasserstein distance for $p=1$, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distance for $p=2$. We prove that $D_p$ is a metric for every $1\le p\le2$, by proving a stronger 2014 conjecture of Lin and van den Driessche on $3\times3$ block matrices. Our main tool is a partition inequality for Schatten norms, proved by complex interpolation. We also characterize Fréchet means for $D_p$ by a fixed-point equation and prove geometric convergence of the associated iteration.
comment: 20 pages; 4 appendices; one synthetic experiment included

title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
abstract: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.
comment: 29 pages, 4 figures, 6 tables. Data, certificates and code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23303466. Submitted to PRX Quantum

title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellensätze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

title: Low-rank perturbation of symplectic matrices
abstract: In this paper the generic behavior of the Jordan structure of symplectic matrices under low-rank structure-preserving transformations is considered. So far, only the case of rank-one perturbations was covered in the literature, and this result is now extended to the case of arbitrary rank $k$. As a key step toward the main result, it is shown that all symplectic matrices that differ from the identity by rank $k$ can be represented as a product of $k$ symplectic reflectors unless they are similar to a diagonalizable matrix having only the eigenvalues $\pm 1$.

title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and the failure of Fourier-Schur transference
abstract: Given $1 < p < \infty$ and a function $m \colon \mathbf{N}_0 \to \mathbf{C}$, we provide a characterization of radial Schur multipliers $M(x,y) = m(d(x,y))$ on the Schatten $p$-class of a tree $(X,d)$ equipped with its graph metric. That is, the operator norm of the radial Schur multiplier $S_M$ is controlled by the norm of the Fourier multiplier $T_m$ on the torus: \[ \big\| S_M \colon S_p(X) \to S_p(X) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}} \lesssim \frac{p^4}{(p-1)^2} \, \big\| T_m \colon L_p(\mathbf{T}) \to L_p(\mathbf{T}) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}}, \] with both quantities being comparable when the tree $X$ has infinite diameter. This is a rather unexpected inequality, which necessarily fails at the endpoints $p=1,\infty$ due to the work of Haagerup, Steenstrup and Szwarc. As an application, we construct the first examples of completely $S_p$-bounded Herz-Schur multipliers in the free group that are unbounded as Fourier multipliers. This result disproves Fourier-Schur transference---a longstanding open problem since the work of Neuwirth and Ricard in 2011. In line with this, our main result also implies the surprising fact that free balls Schur multipliers are uniformly $S_p$-bounded, in sharp contrast to their Fourier behavior. In addition, we disprove Fourier-Schur transference over the algebraic groups $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbf{Q}_q)$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$ with $\mathrm{K}$-biinvariant counterexamples, the latter involving additional geometric and probabilistic techniques.

title: Entropy-Regularized Mean-Field Games with Average-Reward Criterion: Span-Seminorm Contractions and Model-Free Learning
abstract: We study stationary discrete-time mean-field games with finite state and action spaces under the average-reward criterion, with an entropy-regularized objective and population-dependent dynamics and rewards. Under a minorization condition, the soft Q-operator is a span-seminorm contraction for the full transition kernel, so relative value iteration does not require the minorizing measure. When the Lipschitz constant of the kernel is below the minorization mass and the temperature exceeds an explicit threshold, the equilibrium fixed-point operator is a contraction: an equilibrium exists, its population distribution is unique, and a fixed-point iteration converges to it geometrically. We then learn the equilibrium model-free from a simulator, combining soft Q-learning at a fixed population distribution with an empirical transition kernel. We prove a finite-sample bound for soft Q-learning in the span seminorm, with temperature-independent constants, and derive convergence rates for the learned population distribution and policy. A congestion-aware routing game illustrates the results.

title: Semiprime and real submodules of arbitrary modules are intersections of prime and real prime submodules
abstract: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A submodule $N$ of an $R$-module $M$ is semiprime if $m\in(N:m)M$ implies $m\in N$. It is known that every semiprime submodule of $R^n$ is an intersection of prime submodules, and Aryapoor extended this to finitely generated modules. We show that no finiteness assumption is needed: every semiprime submodule of an \emph{arbitrary} $R$-module is the intersection of the prime submodules containing it. The proof is short and uses neither coordinates nor presentations; its key step is that a nonzero element $q$ of a semiprime module $Q$ satisfies $sq\notin\p Q$ for all $s\notin\p$, where $\p$ is any minimal prime over the annihilator of $q$. We define an $R$-module $M$ to be real if $\sum_i m_i\otimes m_i=0$ in $M\otimes_RM$ implies $m_i=0$ for all $i$, and a submodule $N\subseteq M$ real if the module $M/N$ is real. We prove the corresponding result for real submodules: every real submodule of an arbitrary module is the intersection of the real prime submodules containing it. On $R^n$ our notion of realness coincides with the coordinate definition used in earlier work on real Nullstellensätze for free modules.

title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.

title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of Kähler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform à priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.

title: A note on the Slater$\unicode{x2013}$Vélez permutation
abstract: We study the greedy sequence of positive integers introduced by Slater and Vélez. They proved that it is a permutation of the positive integers but left open whether its sequence of consecutive absolute differences is also a permutation. We prove that it is.

title: The operad of anti-pre-Lie algebras and its Lie elements
abstract: We initiate a systematic operadic approach to anti-pre-Lie algebras. We study the operad controlling anti-pre-Lie algebras, its relationship to the operad of Novikov algebras and its cyclic structure. We establish that the Lie bracket of an anti-pre-Lie algebra satisfies the standard identity of degree five. We also establish a quadratic maximality property of the anti-pre-Lie operad with respect to this identity. We then show that the anti-pre-Lie operad and its Koszul dual are not Koszul and give a full description of the latter. Finally, we identify the Lie elements in the Koszul dual operad with the operad of metabelian Lie algebras.

title: Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for singular $L^k$ interaction kernels with rates
abstract: Based on a semigroup approach, we prove quantitative uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for two systems of interacting particles with singular interaction kernels $K$ of type $L^k$, $k>d$, and a contractive Lipschitz confinement force field. First, we consider a system with moderate interaction, which means that the particles interact through the mollified kernel $K\ast V^N$, for some approximation of identity $V^N = N^{dα} V(N^α\cdot),\, α>0$. Assuming that $\|K\|_{L^k}$ is sufficiently small, we obtain that for any $\varepsilon>0$ the uniform-in-time rate is of order $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. Second, for the classical, non-mollified particle system we establish uniform-in-time propagation of chaos with rate $N^{-\min\left(α,\frac12-\frac{dα}{2}-\varepsilon\right)} + \|K-K\ast V^N\|_{L^{k}}$, plus an exponentially small in time contribution of the initial condition. The method relies on the regularity properties of the solution of the associated nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation combined with estimates of the Duhamel formulation of the mollified empirical measure, together with partial Girsanov transforms for the non-mollified system of particles.

title: Unrectifiable surfaces with intrinsic regularity in Carnot groups
abstract: In any noncommutative Carnot group, for every $0\le α<1$, we show the existence of a $C^{1,α}_\mathrm H$ surface that is unrectifiable with respect to the Euclidean distance. Precisely, the surface has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension higher than its topological dimension. We show that in step-2 Carnot groups the construction gives hypersurfaces of maximal Euclidean Hausdorff dimension, equal to $q-\frac{1+α}{2}$, where $q$ is the topological dimension of the group. Here the range of unrectifiability is sharp, since for $α=1$ the surface is rectifiable in the classical sense. In step-2 Carnot groups, it is also possible to prove that the $(q-\frac12)$-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure of every $C^1_\mathrm H$ hypersurface is zero. These results extend the seminal work by Kirchheim and Serra Cassano in the first Heisenberg group.

title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.
comment: 30 pages. Supplementary catalogue of 101 OEIS sequences and check programs in ancillary files. Lean 4 formalization at https://github.com/ahaankallat/congruence-phenomena-lean and https://github.com/ahaankallat/congruence-phenomena-higher-order-lean

title: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules
abstract: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, Γ)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.

title: Regularity for Minimizers of Mixed-Smoothness Variational Integrals
abstract: We establish the first partial regularity results for minimizers of a class of suitably quasiconvex variational integrals defined on anisotropic Sobolev spaces. These variational integrals are related to higher gradient continuum models for pantographic metamaterials.
comment: 22 pages. Accepted for publication in Nonlinear Analysis

title: Finite Length of Locally Analytic Vectors for $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $D_F^\times$
abstract: Let $F/\mathbf Q_p$ and $E/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite extensions, and let $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ or $D_F^\times$, where $D_F$ is the quaternion division algebra over $F$. Let $Π$ be an admissible Banach $E$-representation of $G$ whose locally $\mathbf Q_p$-analytic vectors $Π^{\mathrm{an}}$ have an infinitesimal character. If $p>2$ or $F=\mathbf Q_p$, we prove that $Π^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $Π$ have finite length in their respective admissible categories.

title: Open substacks preserving moduli spaces: classification and bounds
abstract: For a smooth locally reductive stack admitting an adequate moduli space, we show that there are finitely many open substacks preserving the adequate moduli space, and give a complete classification of such opens. For $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions, this becomes an explicit description in terms of the codimension-one Bialynicki-Birula strata. Moreover, for a stable adequate moduli space, we show that the number of preserving opens are bounded by 3 raised to the relative Picard rank. As an application, the number of fixed components for $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions is at least the relative Picard rank.

title: The theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations of groups
abstract: Motivated by recent work on $λ$-fold near-factorizations by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations as combinatorial structures with prescribed representation multiplicities. Such a factorization consists of two subsets of a finite group whose products represent each nonidentity element exactly $λ$ times and the identity exactly $μ$ times. These structures generalize $λ$-fold near-factorizations and provide a common framework for several families arising in combinatorial design theory, including strong external difference families with two equal-sized subsets, as well as binary sequence pairs with two-level correlation. Their associated $\{0,1\}$-matrices satisfy the Bridges-Ryser equation $XY=λ(J-I)+μI$, linking the factorization problem to a classical matrix framework for combinatorial designs. We establish the foundational theory of $(λ,μ)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
comment: Updated abstract, minor revisions, and several additional references

title: Separating Statistical Inference from Experimental Runtime: An Architecture for Sequential Scientific Analysis
abstract: Sequential statistical procedures are increasingly embedded in scientific systems in which observations arrive incrementally from heterogeneous sources. In such systems the statistical update is only one part of the computation: observations must also be acquired, aligned across inputs, ordered, delivered, persisted, and replayed, and results must be passed to systems that display them or act on them. Sequential methods are nevertheless missing from the general software toolkit. They run inside proprietary experimentation platforms and commercial statistical packages, or exist as offline functions over complete data, and the batch fit interface that dominates machine-learning libraries has no place for a procedure that listens, keeps state, and decides when to stop. We propose an architecture that separates statistical inference from data topology, execution runtime, run lifecycle, persistence, and external action. Its central abstraction is the Sequential Procedure: a state-transition function that maps an inferential state, a valid statistical input, and a statistical random state to a new state and a scientific output. The procedure does not define how observations are acquired, paired, scheduled, stored, or acted upon. We specify the architecture semantically rather than through an object model, derive seven conformance invariants that any implementation can be tested against (among them synchronous/asynchronous, checkpoint, replay, and batch equivalence), and describe a dependency-free reference implementation in which all seven hold bitwise. Lorden's 2-SPRT for the Kiefer-Weiss problem serves as the reference procedure; the same contract accommodates sequential estimators, Bayesian filters, change-point detectors, and stateful predictive models.

title: Equivariant formality for rational $\C_{p^k}$-spaces
abstract: In this paper, we discuss equivariant formality for spaces equipped with a primary cyclic group action. We study the behavior of equivariant formality with some topological constructions. The algebraic complexity needs to deal with injectivity. In the end, we discuss equivariant intrinsic formality.

title: Weak type (1,1) bound criterion for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough kernels
abstract: This paper proves the weak type (1,1) boundedness for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough non-convolution kernels of the form $Ω(x-y) K(x,y)$, where $Ω$ is homogeneous of degree zero with $Ω\in L\log L(\sS^{d-1})$ and $K$ is a standard Calderón-Zygmund kernel. This extends the recent resolution of the classical convolution case by Lai \cite{Lai2025weak} to a wider class of operators.

title: Koszul Duality in an Equivariant Context
abstract: This article takes steps to show that an equivariant version of the well known phenomena of Koszul Duality can be formulated in a manner not considered prior: via dg (co)algebra valued functors on the orbit category. As such techniques used in this article mix traditional and modern categorical methods in homotopy theory.

title: The Diagonal of a Regular Pentagon
abstract: We demonstrate the well-known fact that the diagonal of a unit regular pentagon has length the golden ratio. While similar to other proofs, we provide a novel figure that we believe is particularly well-suited to achieve full understanding at a glance.

title: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
abstract: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.

title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular flat boundaries
abstract: We develop an $N$-adic modification of the construction of David-Jeznach-Julia for compact subsets of the real line $\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ for which harmonic measure for the complementary domains has no dimension drop. In particular, we show that for every $s\in(0,1/2)$, there exists an $s$-Ahlfors regular compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}\subset\mathbb{C}$ such that $\mathrm{dim}ω^\infty=s$, where $ω^\infty$ denotes harmonic measure for $\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ with pole at infinity. Combined with a result of the third author, this shows that the threshold $1/2$ is sharp.

title: A Sharp Bound for the Second Betti Number of Hyperkähler Sixfolds
abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth compact irreducible hyperkähler manifold of dimension six. We prove that the second Betti number satisfies $b_2(X) \le 23$. Furthermore, we show that the third cohomology vanishes whenever $b_2(X) \ge 19$, and that all odd cohomology vanishes when $b_2(X) = 23$. If the second Chern class lies in the subalgebra generated by $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})$, then $b_2(X) \in \{5,8,23\}$. The proof uses the Looijenga--Lunts--Verbitsky decomposition, curvature inequalities for Segre classes, and the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the projective cotangent bundle.

title: Sub-Gaussian Confidence Intervals for Heavy-Tailed Data: Characterizing the Limits of Inference
abstract: We investigate the problem of uncertainty quantification in the mean estimation framework. Given an i.i.d. sample from a distribution with unknown mean $μ$ and variance $σ^2$, we want to construct an estimator $\whμ_n$ and provide a computable and size-optimal upper bound for the error $|\wh μ_n - μ|$. While estimators possessing strong deviation guarantees are well known, no data-dependent non-asymptotic upper bounds for their performance exist in general. We show that this gap can be bridged by introducing a parameter that characterizes the ``effective sample size'' available for uncertainty quantification. This parameter captures the difficulty of the problem, interpolating between ``easy'' cases where sub-Gaussian confidence intervals exist and ``hard" cases where their construction is impossible. Using this characterization, we design confidence intervals of optimal length that are fully adaptive to the unknown variance. Numerical experiments confirm that our approach maintains nominal coverage even in asymmetric and heavy-tailed regimes where other existing methods fail.

title: A Multiplicative Horn Obstruction to the Unitary Categorification of a Rank-Twelve Modular Datum
abstract: We study the rank-twelve potential modular datum denoted $12^{39,406}_{4,1276.}$ in the low-rank classification tables. Its global dimension is $(1287+351\sqrt{13})/2$, and its fusion ring agrees with that of the known rank-twelve Haagerup modular category. The datum satisfies the modular relations, has nonnegative integral Verlinde coefficients, and passes several familiar genus-one necessary tests. We prove, nevertheless, that it cannot be realized by a unitary modular tensor category. The obstruction already occurs in the representation of the three-strand braid group on $\operatorname{Hom}(C_{[10]},B^{\otimes3})$. Generalized Frobenius--Schur indicators determine the eigenvalues of the two-strand generator on this twelve-dimensional space. The central relation in $B_3$ then reduces the problem to a product of three prescribed unitary conjugacy classes. A sixfold symmetry reduces the $1302$ determinant-compatible cases to $217$ representatives. Rank-one inequalities leave only $17$ of these, and ten explicitly displayed degree-zero rank-two Schubert inequalities exclude the remaining cases. A violated inequality with gap $2/117$ is worked out explicitly. All calculations used in the obstruction are exact. The argument uses unitarity essentially and leaves non-unitary categorification open.

title: Quantum ordinal optimization under a fixed comparison budget
abstract: Ordinal optimization selects designs that are good enough rather than optimal when evaluation is expensive and the budget is small. The alignment probability measures the chance that the selected set contains at least a prescribed number of truly good designs. We formulate quantum ordinal optimization as a class of problems that maximize this probability under a fixed oracle budget. We study exact, coherent pairwise comparisons with one selected design as a first instance, with the budget counted in comparison queries. For every classical comparison budget smaller than the number of designs, we prove that a knockout among uniformly sampled designs attains the optimum. The sample is drawn without replacement and contains one more design than the number of comparisons. For a uniformly random order, the selected design's rank has a polynomial probability law. At the same comparison budget, the maximum quantum degree is at most twice the classical maximum, a factor attained whenever there are more than twice as many designs as comparisons, so a quantum algorithm can realize rank laws that no classical algorithm with the same budget can. We determine the quantum optimum with one comparison for every number of designs and every good-enough set. For selecting the best of n designs, the optimal success probability with one quantum comparison is approximately 3.30/n for large n, compared with 2/n for one classical comparison. When the best design is sought, one quantum comparison gives a higher alignment probability than two classical comparisons whenever there are more than nine designs.
comment: 22 pages, 4 tables. Adds a fixed-fraction limit and updates the discussion of two-comparison results

title: Inference on the Value of Policy Improvement in Adaptive Experiments
abstract: In this paper, we develop an asymptotically normal estimator for the value of policy improvement (VPI) under adaptively collected data. This value, which is defined as the gap between the value of the best treatment policy in a class and that of a baseline policy, gauges whether or not it is worth deploying a personalized treatment policy. Building an estimator for the VPI is naturally more difficult than estimating the value of a fixed policy. This is because, in addition to contending with the correlated data and decaying propensities associated with adaptive experiments, any estimator must also handle the non-regularity, or lack of pathwise differentiability, of the underlying estimand when the optimal policy is non-unique. Our proposed estimator works by sequentially fitting a weighted empirical welfare maximizing policy on historical data and then evaluating it using inverse propensity weighting on future samples. We neither assume that the optimal policy is unique nor make a margin assumption on the underlying heterogeneous treatment effects. A key difficulty in analyzing our estimator is showing that the regret incurred through policy learning is asymptotically smaller than the standard error of the estimator. We accomplish this by showing faster regret rates for policy learning under decaying propensities, which may be of independent interest. We not only evaluate the coverage of our estimator on a mix of synthetic and semi-synthetic data, but also employ it to estimate the VPI in an adaptive experiment evaluating the efficacy of job assistance programs in Jordan due to Caria et al. Although our estimates are generally more conservative than their hierarchical Bayesian analysis, which assumes that the optimal policy is unique, we still corroborate the benefits of personalization amongst Syrian refugees.

title: Explicit counterexamples to Frank-Loss optimizer conjectures for critical Dirac and vector Sobolev inequalities
abstract: Frank and Loss proposed critical Sobolev inequalities for the Dirac operator and for vector fields. They conjectured optimality of their spinorial family and wrote that it is conceivable that the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau potential is an optimizer. Wang and Zhang recently disproved both optimizer claims using direct comparison and instability arguments. We compute closed-form quotients for two elementary families of explicit competitors with strictly smaller quotients. For every $d\geq2$, the spinorial competitor is a constant spinor multiplied by a scalar Aubin-Talenti optimizer. For every $d\geq3$, the vector competitor is the planar azimuthal field \[ A_d(x)=\frac{d}{(1+\lvert x\rvert^2)^2} (-x_2,x_1,0,\ldots,0). \] It lies in the nonlinear gauge and its quotient is computed in closed form. For every odd $d\geq3$, it gives an explicit proof of nonoptimality of the higher-dimensional Loss-Yau-Dunne-Min potential. In dimension three, this field is a specific member of the competitor family of Wang and Zhang: it is a linear combination of the Loss-Yau potential and its reflected twin. Its axisymmetry gives a negative answer to their question about minimization within the $\mathrm{SO}(2)\times 1$-invariant class.

title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $Ω\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $Ω$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.

title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
abstract: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.

title: Minimal Product Sets in Finite Metacyclic Groups
abstract: Minimum product-set problems ask how small a product of two subsets of prescribed cardinalities can be in a finite group. Although the problem is completely understood for finite abelian groups, exact results in the nonabelian setting are available only for particular classes. We determine the minimum product-set function $μ_G$ for every finite metacyclic group, without assuming that the relevant cyclic extension splits. Our proof converts the extremal problem into a finite recursive arithmetic description of the feasible cardinality vectors of subset trios. The recursion combines the subgroup structure of finite metacyclic groups with the structural classification of maximal critical subset trios. The resulting characterization recovers the previously known formulas for abelian and nilpotent groups, dihedral groups, and nonabelian groups of order $pq$. It also yields metacyclic examples in which the minimum product-set size lies strictly between the classical lower and upper arithmetic bounds for finite solvable groups. For faithful split metacyclic groups, we further show that requiring one factor to be symmetric, contain the identity, and generate the whole group can force a strictly larger product set than the unrestricted minimum. The latter constraint admits a vertex-isoperimetric interpretation on connected Cayley graphs.

title: GPU-Accelerated Nested Schur-Complement Solvers for Atmospheric Flow Simulations Using Horizontally-Explicit, Vertically-Implicit Schemes and Discontinuous Galerkin Methods
abstract: Horizontally explicit, vertically implicit (HEVI) time integration removes the acoustic time-step restriction imposed by fine vertical grids in nonhydrostatic atmospheric models, but requires fast solvers for the resulting vertical linear systems, especially on GPUs. We present GPU-accelerated nested Schur-complement solvers for these systems for a split-form discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method on Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes applied to the compressible Euler equations with gravity. In time, we use a Rosenbrock-W method, a linearly implicit Runge-Kutta scheme that retains its order and stability with approximate Jacobians. This allows a sparse vertical Jacobian that captures vertical acoustic waves and gravity on curvilinear meshes with orography and decouples into independent column systems. The solvers are nested: a global Schur complement (static condensation) exploits the LGL sparsity to condense each column onto a few element-edge unknowns, and a local Schur complement eliminates all variables but the vertical momentum within each element, exploiting that the pressure depends only on the potential-temperature density. We propose and analyze two condensation strategies, which lead to banded and block-tridiagonal reduced systems. The resulting HEVI schemes conserve total mass and potential-temperature density to round-off. The solvers are implemented for CPUs and GPUs in TrixiAtmo.jl, the atmospheric extension of Trixi.jl. We verify high-order convergence with linear inertia-gravity waves in a 2D channel and demonstrate robustness on the sphere with the baroclinic instability, a mountain-induced baroclinic instability, and the DCMIP-2025 gap-flow and vortex-shedding cases. For the baroclinic instability without orography, the scheme achieves 18.8 and 2.9 simulated years per day at 100 and 50 km resolution on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU in double precision.

title: An optimization problem for $δ'$ leaky stars
abstract: We consider singular Schrödinger operators with an attractive $δ'$ interaction of strength $β$ supported by a star graph and prove that the ground-state eigenvalue is uniquely maximized by stars of the maximum symmetry. Two different proofs are presented, one for an even number of edges using a comparison to the $δ$ interaction star, the other general based on Birman-Schwinger technique.

title: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
abstract: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.

title: Parabolically induced representations of $GL_n(O_l)$
abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the ring of integers of a non-Archimedean local field with uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $\mathcal O_\ell=\mathcal O/\varpi^\ell\mathcal O$ for $\ell\geq1$. In this article, we study representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$ parabolically induced from characters of the Borel subgroup $\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell)$. For $n=3$, we establish a criterion for the irreducibility of these induced representations in terms of the relative conductors of the inducing characters. Motivated by this result, we formulate a conjecture characterizing the irreducibility of such representations for arbitrary $n$. We further show that when all inducing characters are equal, the resulting induced representation is not multiplicity-free, implying that the corresponding triple $(\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),\mathrm{B}_n(\mathcal O_\ell),χ)$ is not a Gelfand pair. Finally, we study the irreducible decomposition of these representations for $\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathcal O_\ell)$ when two relative conductors attain their maximal values. Using the decomposition theory for $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathcal O_\ell)$, we describe the irreducible constituents and determine their dimensions.

title: Failure of dimension drop for harmonic measure on Ahlfors regular boundaries of dimension close to $1$
abstract: For every $0<s<1$ we construct a compact $s$-Ahlfors regular set $K\subset\mathbb C$ for which harmonic measure of $\mathbb C\setminus K$ with pole at infinity is comparable to $\mathcal H^s|_K$. In particular, there is no dimension drop for any dimension $s<1$. The construction is $N$-adic and based on configurations close to the $N$-th roots of unity. We adjust the positions of the children by small polynomial deformations so that the logarithmic potential of the natural Bernoulli measure becomes constant in the limit. A first-mode correction gives the range $s<2/3$, while corrections of arbitrary finite order yield the full range $0<s<1$.

title: On the inverse Goldbach problem
abstract: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.

title: Small-speed solitary-wave stability and global well-posedness for a Bessel-regularized Airy equation
abstract: We prove orbital stability of minimizing solitary waves at sufficiently small positive speeds for an Airy equation with a quadratic interaction filtered by a Bessel potential of order one. The stability hypotheses are verified: constrained minimization gives one negative direction, the small-speed KdV limit and operator-norm perturbation of the profile resolvent give a one-dimensional translation kernel, and a differentiable rescaled branch with uniformly bounded derivative gives a positive slope of the quadratic invariant. A conserved Lyapunov functional then proves orbital stability in the three-halves-derivative energy space and the perturbation also gives uniqueness of centered minimizers at small speed. The dynamical framework is supplied by a direct Bourgain-space bilinear estimate, local well-posedness in the square-integrable class, unconditional uniqueness from one-quarter derivative onward, and global well-posedness in the half-derivative energy space. For every prescribed positive speed, constrained minimization constructs smooth positive profiles that are symmetric, strictly monotone away from their center, and exponentially localized. At general positive speeds the stability criterion remains conditional on nondegeneracy and the slope condition.

title: Fractional symplectic Fourier transforms and their actions on function and distribution spaces
abstract: We consider symplectic analogues of the fractional Fourier transforms and obtain convenient representations in terms of Bargmann transforms and Wigner distributions. We show that they act as homeomorphisms on Schwartz spaces, the space of square integrable functions, the space of tempered distributions, and on Fourier-invariant Gelfand-Shilov spaces and their corresponding distribution spaces. More generally, we establish their homeomorphism properties on a broad class of spaces defined through (Wigner-)Hermite expansions. In addition, we prove that these transforms preserve norms on Schatten-von Neumann symbol classes associated with the Weyl calculus.
comment: 43 pages. This is the first version. A thorough update is expected for the second one

title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.

title: Lie Algebras of Locally Finite Derivations over Fields of Positive Characteristic
abstract: Let $F$ be a field of positive characteristic, and let $A$ be a finitely generated commutative associative $F$-algebra. We study Lie subalgebras of $Der \, A$ generated by locally finite derivations. We prove that if all commutators of the generators satisfy a natural local finiteness condition, then the associative subalgebra of $End_{F}\, A$ generated by these derivations is finite-dimensional.

title: Adaptive Robust Confidence Sets in High Dimensions
abstract: We study adaptive confidence sets for mean vectors of multivariate Gaussians with identity covariance under Huber contamination when the contamination proportion is unknown. We show that an information-theoretically optimal adaptive confidence set can be constructed by simultaneously quantifying uncertainty across all one-dimensional projections. The resulting confidence set achieves the optimal diameter and reveals a substantial adaptation cost compared with the minimax estimation error. Although statistically optimal, this construction is computationally infeasible. We establish a Statistical Query (SQ) lower bound showing that achieving diameter $O(m^{-1/2})$ requires either exponentially many queries or query tolerance $d^{-Ω(m)}$. Thus, in contrast to robust mean estimation, adaptation to the unknown contamination proportion incurs both a statistical cost and a computational barrier within the SQ framework. Finally, we give a low-degree moment-matching algorithm that constructs an adaptive confidence set using $d^{O(m)}$ samples and time. Its diameter bound contains an additional $O(m^{-1/2})$ term beyond the information-theoretic rate, matching the dependence on $m$ in the SQ lower bound. Together, these results characterize the statistical limits of adaptive robust confidence sets under Huber contamination and quantify a computational barrier within the SQ framework.

title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
abstract: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.

title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
abstract: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$. The resulting vector field has exactly sixteen hyperbolic equilibria. We also prove a general transfer theorem that preserves exponential mixing under certain singular changes of coordinates.

title: Sharp Rogers--Shephard Inequalities for Rényi Entropy
abstract: We establish sharp weighted Rogers--Shephard inequalities for Rényi differential entropy. For independent copies $X,X'$ of a log-concave random vector in $\R^n$, we prove $h_p(aX-bX')\le h_p(X)+n\log(a+b)$ for all $a,b>0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, where orders $1$ and $\infty$ correspond to Shannon entropy and min-entropy, respectively. The Shannon case settles the entropic Rogers--Shephard conjecture of Madiman and Kontoyiannis and its higher-dimensional formulation. For $1\le p<\infty$, equality holds precisely for invertible affine images of random vectors with independent exponential coordinates. At $p=\infty$, the larger equality class is characterized by possibly extended-valued convex potentials that are positively homogeneous of degree one. For every $0<p<1$, uniform laws on sufficiently high-dimensional simplices violate the unweighted bound. Thus $p=1$ is the critical order for this bound to hold in every dimension. The proof combines weighted convex intersections with an exponential lift to a log-affine probability density. At the Shannon endpoint, this lift yields an exact deficit decomposition with a conditional mutual information term for an additive channel with asymmetric Laplace noise.

title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
abstract: We count the integral solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ weighted by $Φ(x_3/M)$, for $M$ smaller than $\sqrt D$. Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant $D$, of a function of their distance to the point $i$. We evaluate it by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. Throughout, $θ=7/64$. For square $D=n^2$ the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to the single geodesic from $0$ to $\infty$. For every $n$ and both parities of $x_3$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with error $O(n^{1+θ+\varepsilon}M^{-1/2})$, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec (and the theta group for the parity of $x_3$). It is non-trivial for $M\ge n^{71/96+\varepsilon}$. This improves the range $n^{5/6+\varepsilon}$ of the elementary method, and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square $D=f^2D_0$ the geodesics are closed. A Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant $D_0$. We obtain an error $O(D^{\varepsilon}f^{1+θ}D_0^{2/3}M^{-1/2})$, using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with the cubic moment bound of Young and of Andersen-Wu. For $D\equiv 5 \bmod 8$ this counts all solutions, and the range $M\ge D^{1/2-1/1332}$ of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to $M\ge D^{4/9+\varepsilon}$. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
comment: v2: Theorem 3 now holds for all non-square D (the restriction to odd D_0 is removed, using the cubic moment of Andersen-Wu and the Weyl bound of Petrow-Young); relation to Humphries-Radziwill clarified; acknowledgement added. 27 pages, 2 tables. Written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic; see Subsection 1.6. Numerical checks as ancillary files

title: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
abstract: Let \(α, β\in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((ξ_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(α\) and \(β\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = ξ_1 + \cdots + ξ_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((α, β)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.

title: Symplectic four-manifolds and hyperbolic $π$-orbifolds
abstract: We construct closed symplectic 4-manifolds admitting the structure of hyperbolic $π$-orbifold, addressing LeBrun's conjecture. Our simplest example has Euler characteristic $304$, is tessellated by $64$ copies of the right-angled hyperbolic $120$-cell and admits a four-fold branched covering over a product of two surfaces of genus $4$.

title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part II. $k$-Hessian case
abstract: We study admissible entire subsolutions and radial boundary blow-up solutions of $S_k^{\frac1k}[ΔuI-D^2u]=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ for $1\leq k<n$, continuing our study of the determinant case $k=n$ in Part I. Under structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2$. Our results cover the non-Lipschitz case $0<q<1$ with a possibly vanishing zero-order term, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and sign-changing gradient coefficients. We also characterize finite-radius blow-up of radial solutions and derive two-sided estimates for the blow-up radius, as well as pointwise upper bounds for their profiles in terms of inverse Keller--Osserman functions.
comment: 48 pages, 0 figures; companion paper to Part I

title: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
abstract: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.

title: Sharp conditions for fully nonlinear equations with $(n-1)$-Hessian matrix: Part I. Monge--Ampère case
abstract: We study positive $(n-1)$-convex entire subsolutions of the normalized real $(n-1)$ Monge--Ampère equation $\operatorname{det}^{\frac1n}\bigl(ΔuI-D^2u\bigr)=f(u)+g(u)|Du|^q$ in $\mathbb R^n$. Under two sets of structural assumptions on the continuous, non-decreasing coefficients $f$ and $g$, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of entire subsolutions when $q<2-\frac1n$. Our results cover the pure-gradient degenerate case $f\equiv0$ with $0<q<1$, the gradient-singular case $q<0$, and the case where $g$ changes sign. For $q=2-\frac1n$, we recover the Keller--Osserman condition for the gradient-independent equation, prove nonexistence when $g$ is eventually positive, and obtain an exponentially weighted condition when $g$ has a nonpositive limit at infinity. This is the first of two companion papers and treats the determinant case.
comment: 44 pages, 0 figures; companion paper to Part II

title: Notes on Uniform Policy Score Bounds and Lipschitz Continuity for Truncated Gaussian, Product Cauchy, Boltzmann, and Softmax Policies
abstract: We establish uniform score bounds and Lipschitz continuity for truncated Gaussian, Cauchy, Boltzmann, and softmax policies under explicitly stated parameterizations.

title: When do explicit penalties improve flow matching?
abstract: Flow matching can learn structure directly from data, raising the question of when additional constraints improve generation. We study penalties that encode such constraints, with physics-informed flow matching as a motivating example. Satisfying a constraint more closely need not make the generated distribution more accurate. We therefore compare penalised and unpenalised generative modelling through their expected squared $2$-Wasserstein error. Our analysis covers both vector-valued and functional data in a Hilbert-space setting. We first derive geometric criteria that account for constraint violations and the distribution of samples after projection onto the constraint set. We then solve the statistical comparison explicitly for specific velocity-field classes and constraints via flow matching. In this model, penalisation improves accuracy exactly when the reduction in estimation variance outweighs the increase in squared bias. The resulting formula shows how this trade-off depends on sample size, the model class, the noise schedule, and the penalty weight.

title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.
comment: 42 pages, comments are welcomed. Will soon be separated into part I and II

title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
abstract: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states. Equal periods are not essential: locking persists under small nonzero mismatches, with persistence and loss governed by a shifted phase balance. The analysis covers the full state-dependent impulsive dynamics, including transverse stability. Nearly simultaneous emissions may make the return discontinuous; under an explicit regularity condition the global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse--Smale dynamics.

title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.

title: Bipartite edge frustration of nut graphs: proofs and constructions
abstract: The bipartite edge frustration of a graph $G$, $\varphi(G)$, is the minimum number of edges that must be removed from $G$ to obtain a graph that is bipartite. Core graphs are singular graphs on $2$ or more vertices, for which the kernel of the adjacency matrix contains a full eigenvector. A nut graph is a core graph of nullity one. Nut graphs $G$ are non-bipartite. It is proved here that $\varphi(G) \geq 2$ if $G$ is a nut graph, i.e. every nut graph requires deletion of at least two edges to produce a bipartite graph. In addition, we give a constructive proof that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many chemical nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Furthermore, for $3 \leq d \leq 8$, the values $k$, for which a $d$-regular nut graph $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$ exists, are characterised. It is shown here that for every integer $k \geq 2$ there exist infinitely many cubic polyhedral nut graphs $G$ with $\varphi(G) = k$. Two ways of producing larger nut graphs from smaller are described: the cut and frustration constructions. One straightforward consequence is that total double subdivision of a nut graph (i.e. simultaneous insertion of two degree-$2$ vertices into every edge) yields a nut graph.

title: Explicit matrix hitting points for noncommutative algebraic branching programs
abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-resource black-box identity test for noncommutative algebraic branching programs (ABPs), using ordinary matrix evaluations of the output polynomial. Given an alphabet of size $m\ge1$ and an ABP vertex bound $S\ge1$, we construct one fixed tuple of integer matrices of order $R=(m+2)d(d+1)/2$, where $d=(m+2)S$, with entry bit length $O(d\log(d+1))$. Every nonzero polynomial computed by an ABP with at most $S$ vertices has a nonzero evaluation at this tuple. The construction accesses neither the hidden ABP nor its intermediate gates. A rectangular variant improves the order to $O(m^{3/2}S^2)$. Matrix order, description length, and all returned entries are counted; the total resources are polynomial. The result holds in characteristic zero and in characteristic $p>\binom d2$. The main ingredient is a fixed polynomial frame spanning the joint cyclic module of every matrix tuple from every prescribed vector. A compensating block makes a tagged encoding nilpotent of index at most three, while preserving the original cyclic module. A differential exterior-vector argument then gives a single triangular recurrence with polynomially many outputs. Its shared left-linear circuit is converted into actual integer query matrices by coefficient duality. Two-sided pairing further gives deterministic nonadaptive reconstruction of an equivalent ABP from polynomially many output-only matrix queries. The same frame gives polynomial-cardinality explicit trace separators for simultaneous-conjugation orbit closures, and a fixed nilpotent substitution for bounded-dimensional recognizable series. The latter also tests rational formulas whose given syntax is defined at the scalar origin. We provide complete proofs, construction costs, and exact implementation checks.
comment: 24 pages. There's statement about reproducibility and Lean verification in section 5

title: A greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method for nonlinear equations
abstract: In this paper, we develop a greedy double-block nonlinear Bregman-Kaczmarz method to efficiently find sparse solutions of nonlinear equations. The theoretical convergence rate of the proposed method is established under certain assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the competitive performance and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
abstract: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $σ(a)=σ(b)$. Erdős Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $δ>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^δ$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.
comment: 4 pages. Lean 4 formalization of the conditional lower bound available at https://github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824

title: Blow-down and immediate onset of positivity in the Neumann problem for (super-)fast diffusion equations
abstract: For the degenerate parabolic equation $u_t=\nabla\cdot (u^{m-1}\nabla u)$, the homogeneous Neumann problem in smoothly bounded domains $Ω\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ is considered in the (super-fast) diffusion range when $m\in (-\infty,1)$. Upper and lower estimates for solutions are inferred by means of two Moser-type iterations, and optimality properties of these bounds are derived using comparison arguments. On the basis of the accordingly obtained information on regularization into spaces of bounded and uniformly positive functions, a result on global solvability in an associated initial-boundary value problem is achieved for all nonnegative and nontrivial initial data belonging to $L^1(Ω) \cap \bigcup_{s>n(1-m)/2} L^s(Ω)$.

title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
abstract: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between spectrally equivalent modes.

title: Geodesic Models for Loop Spaces on Riemannian Manifolds
