abstract: A topological group, defined in terms of ``composable minimal geodesics'' is constructed and shown to be homotopy equivalent to the pointed loop space of a path-connected, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of positive convexity radius. This construction is analogous to John Milnor's free group model for the pointed loop space of a connected simplicial complex. Related models built from composable minimal geodesics are also obtained for the free loop space of $M$ and for the space of maps from any finite two-dimensional CW-complex into $M$.
comment: 27 pages, to appear in Fields Institute Communications

title: Uniform adjacency-degree probes from differential rigidity
abstract: We construct a fixed triangular family of noncommutative polynomials that spans the joint cyclic module of a real symmetric pair from any prescribed vector. In dimension at most $N$, when the second matrix has spectral diameter at most $N-1$, the family has $N(N+1)/2$ members, degree at most $N-1$, and a shared arithmetic circuit of size $O(N^2)$. No rank-dependent choice of coefficients is made. The proof uses a rational differential connection with a small self-adjoint residue: a primitive polynomial exterior vector for an invariant subspace must have an integer degree smaller than one. For connected trees, the probes and the pointed adjacency--degree reconstruction theorem give one explicit self-adjoint polynomial $p_N\in\mathbb{Z}\langle a,d\rangle$ whose trace separates all trees of order at most $N$. Its circuit has $O(N^2)$ gates, formal degree at most $3N-2$, and polynomial bit complexity. Only the original adjacency and degree matrices, the identity, and ordinary matrix arithmetic are used. A separate integer sum-of-squares construction gives a fixed positive semidefinite representative on which the all-one vector is cyclic; its degree is $O(N^2)$. A linear trace-degree lower bound shows that the first construction has the correct asymptotic degree scale.
comment: There's statement about reproducibility and scope of computation in Appendix B

title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

title: Equidistribution of mesh patterns of length 2 on involutions
abstract: We classify all 1024 length-two mesh patterns on involutions into exactly 287 equidis- tribution classes, consisting of 262 trivial classes and 25 nontrivial classes. Since many bi- jections on arbitrary permutations do not preserve the involution condition, our proofs use several involution-preserving bijections, including conjugation and local adjacent-transposition operations, transposition of the RSK recording tableau, prefix-rank swap bijections and marked-occurrence bijections. In particular, we establish the equidistribution of INV-099, a nontrivial class closely related to the unrestricted Class 69, by adapting the marked- occurrence bijection of Zhang and Zhao through a symmetric closure of the marked set. We also obtain explicit distribution formulas and recurrences for several classes, including continued fractions obtained by specializing known labeled Motzkin-path formulas and rational expressions derived from paired skew decompositions of involutions.

title: Transport Polynomial Exactness for Direct ALE-DG Methods with Nonsmooth mesh motion: A Conservative Coefficient-Evolution Framework
abstract: High-order direct arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian discontinuous Galerkin (ALE-DG) methods can suffer severe order reduction under nonsmooth mesh motion despite satisfying the geometric conservation law (GCL). To address this limitation, we propose a new ALE-DG framework applicable to moving triangular and quadrilateral meshes. This framework successfully overcomes the uniform Lipschitz constraint inherent in existing direct ALE-DG methods, retaining high-order accuracy even when the mesh-velocity gradients are unbounded. This capability is driven by transport polynomial exactness (TPE($k$)), which is a structural property stronger than the GCL. TPE($k$) ensures the exact transport of polynomials of degree at most $k$ under arbitrary mesh motion. To incorporate TPE($k$) into a direct ALE-DG method, we introduce a coefficient-evolution (CE) formulation. Reconciling strict local conservation, an indispensable requirement for accurate shock capturing, with the preservation of the TPE(\(k\)) property constitutes the principal technical challenge. We resolve this by evolving the coefficients using the third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta method, paired with a conservative correction executed via Simpson's rule integration. Crucially, this correction strictly vanishes for exactly transported quadratic polynomials, thereby ensuring that our third-order scheme rigorously satisfies the TPE($2$) property. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed scheme retains third-order accuracy when the discrete mesh-velocity Lipschitz estimate grows as $\mathcal O(h^{-1})$, whereas a representative existing direct ALE-DG scheme exhibits order reduction under the same mesh motion. Tests with discontinuous solutions further demonstrate robust and high-resolution performance under random and Lagrangian mesh motions.

title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).

title: Weighted Frames and the Douglas-Foias problem
abstract: Let $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ be a commuting tuple of bounded linear operators on a separable Hilbert space $\mathcal{K}$, and let $\{a_α\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ be strictly positive weights. Under mild assumptions on the weights, we characterize the weighted frame vectors and weighted Parseval frame vectors, that is, those vectors $ξ$ for which $\{a_α\mathbf{T}^αξ\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}_+^n}$ is a frame or a Parseval frame. We reduce the problem to characterizing surjective module maps from the reproducing analytic Hilbert module associated with the weights onto the module $\mathcal{K}$, equipped with the module structure defined by $\mathbf{T}$. It is shown that weighted Parseval frame vectors differ by a unimodular scalar whenever they exist. If the kernel defined by the weights has the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property, then any two associated weighted frame vectors are similar whenever they exist. We also focus on the case of the Hardy kernel on the polydisc, that is, the case $a_α=1$ for all $α\in\mathbb{Z}^n_+$. This is related to the famous Douglas--Foias problem: whether two similar quotient modules of the Hardy spaces $H^2(\mathbb{D}^n)~(n>1)$ are equal. Our result shows that the answer is negative. This leads to the conclusion that frame vectors for representations of $\mathbb{Z}_+^n$ $(n>1)$ may fail to be similar. It means that, for the case $a_α=1$, there exists a tuple $\mathbf{T}=(T_1,\dots,T_n)$ with $n>1$ on $\mathcal{K}$ and two distinct frame vectors for $\mathbf{T}$ which are not similar.

title: A trace lower bound for totally positive units in $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)^+$ and its application to fusion category
abstract: Let $p = 4q + 1$ be a prime integer, where $q$ is an odd prime. Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)^+$ denote the maximal totally real subfield of the $p$-th cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$. In this paper, we prove that if $U_L^+=U_L^2$ (i.e., every totally positive unit is a square in $L$), then for any non-trivial subfield $K \subseteq L$ and any non-trivial totally positive unit $\varepsilon \in U_K^+$, the absolute trace satisfies the sharp lower bound $\Tr_{K/\mathbb{Q}}(\varepsilon) \ge p - 4$. As an application, we show that a spherical fusion category $\C$ with global dimension $\dim(\mathcal{C})=p=4q+1$ is pointed, where $2$ is a primitive root modulo $q$, or $p=4q+1<2^{22}$ and $p\neq 29$.

title: On Mok's uniqueness problem of holomorphic isometries from complex unit balls of maximal dimension into classical domains
abstract: We prove that every holomorphic isometric embedding, with respect to the Bergman metrics, from a complex unit ball of maximal dimension into irreducible classical bounded symmetric domain of rank at least two that is not biholomorphic to a Type IV domain is equivalent to Mok's embedding. This completely resolves a problem of Mok.

title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
abstract: Let $C_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the cycle $C_n$. The equivalence covering number $\operatorname{eq}(G)$, studied by Alon, is the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover all edges of $G$. King conjectured that $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=Ω(k)$ for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $k$. We study $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)$ and prove that, for every $n \geq 2k + 2$, we have $1 + \lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil \leq \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k) \leq 1 + 2\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$. We further show that, whenever $n\ge(k+1)\max\{41,5\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\}$, \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)\in\left\{1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil,\,2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil\right\}. \end{equation*} Moreover, for every integer $n\ge \max\{2k+2,k^2(k+2)\}$, the following exact values hold in the indicated cases: \begin{equation*} \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=\begin{cases} 1+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1\neq2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ or }(k+1)\mid n,\\[3pt] 2+\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil, & k+1=2^{\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil} \text{ and }2\nmid n. \end{cases} \end{equation*}

title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative rough singular integrals
abstract: We establish the weak type \((1,1)\) endpoint estimate for operator-valued rough singular integrals with kernels satisfying the classical \(L\log L\) integrability and cancellation conditions. This extends Seeger's endpoint theorem [{J. Amer. Math. Soc.} \textbf{9} (1996)] to the noncommutative setting. A key ingredient is an off-diagonal analysis that controls interactions between different kernel scales and avoids an additional logarithmic loss.

title: Maximum degree for random geometric graphs in the connectivity regime and beyond
abstract: A random geometric graph is a random graph model whose vertex set is a binomial point process, where two vertices are connected by an edge if each lies within the ball of radius $r$ centered at the other. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic fluctuations of the threshold radius required for the maximum degree of the graph to reach a target value. Assuming this target value grows with the number of vertices $n$ at an order of at least $\log n$ but strictly less than $(\log n)^d$, we show that these fluctuations follow a Gumbel distribution. We also investigate the spatial configurations of vertices with extremely large degrees, and show that the point process marked by their degrees converges in distribution to a Poisson point process.

title: Diagonal recovery from noisy Fourier--Hermite coefficients: exact orders of the error
abstract: We consider the recovery of functions of the weighted Wiener classes $W_s^μ$ from perturbed Fourier--Hermite coefficients in the metric of $L_\infty(\mathbb R)$. For the summation methods of the class $\mathcal S^θ$ we find error estimates on $W_s^μ$. The estimates take into account the behaviour of the Hermite functions both in the oscillatory region and near the turning point: the maxima of functions with different indices are attained at different points, and the supremum of a sum over a block of indices is substantially smaller than the sum of the suprema. Owing to this, in particular, we establish a common lower bound for all finite diagonal methods; for $s\ne4/3$ and $p\ne4/3$ it matches the upper bound and gives the exact order of the error in this class, while at the critical points the gap between the bounds does not exceed $(\log(e/δ))^{1/4}$ up to a constant. If, in addition, $s>4/3$ or $p<4/3$, then this order is also optimal among all recovery operators that use the whole sequence of data.

title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
abstract: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction. Exact triangular and trapezoidal families are complemented by positive-genus investigations exhibiting bounded amoeba-complement components. These results show that a perfectly exposed amoeba contour does not determine the real structure, logarithmic sheet number, or Harnack type of the underlying curve.
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, all comments are welcome

title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
abstract: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior. These constructions show that smoothness of the complete contour does not force contour--boundary equality and that internal critical-value branches persist under monomial transformations, controlled perturbations, and finite monomial coverings.21 pages, 14 figures
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures, all comments are welcome

title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part II: Existence and Topological Degree
abstract: This paper is a continuation of Part~I \cite{QTWPartI}, where blow-up analysis and compactness results for the CR Nirenberg problem were established. We prove some existence and degree results for the CR Nirenberg problem on the standard sphere. More precisely, we first prove existence results under antipodal and, more generally, finite-group symmetries. Without symmetry, we derive a Leray--Schauder degree formula under natural flatness conditions, yielding existence results for positive prescribed curvatures with certain homogeneous expansions at critical points. We also obtain Aubin-type inequalities under a vanishing first-moment condition, uniformly near the critical exponent.

title: Negative Sobolev regularity and optimal decay for the fractional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system
abstract: We establish global well-posedness and sharp higher-order decay estimates for the fractional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system in $\R^{3}$ with fractional Lamé--Navier dissipation $\Lame^αu$ with $α\in[1/2,1]$, and Riesz coupling $Λ^{2β}φ=ρ-\barρ$ with $β\in[0,1]$, where $Λ:=(-Δ)^{1/2}$ and $\barρ>0$ denotes the constant background density. For small perturbations of a constant equilibrium in $H^{Nα}$ with $N\geq3$ and $Nα>5/2$, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions. Furthermore, we propagate the negative Sobolev norms with uniform-in-time bounds and derive the higher-order decay estimates, provided that the initial perturbation additionally belongs to $\dot{H}^{-\vartheta}$ for some $\vartheta\in[0,3/2)$. Moreover, we establish the optimality of these decay rates within the prescribed initial data class for the velocity and the Riesz potential in their natural energy norms. The density decay exponents are also optimal whenever the available regularity permits the full Riesz-induced gain. The analysis relies on a nonlinear energy structure adapted to both fractional dissipation and Riesz interaction, together with Sobolev interpolation. The optimality of the decay is proved by constructing smooth initial data localized at low frequencies and proving matching upper and lower decay bounds for the resulting solutions. These solutions show that the low-frequency linear dynamics including the Riesz-induced density gain, persists under nonlinear evolution.

title: Topological extensions of elementary measurable spaces
abstract: An elementary space is a pair $(X, \mathcal A)$, where $\mathcal A$ is an algebra of subsets of $X$. Every elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$ is naturally a topological space when equipped with the topology $τ_{\mathcal A}$ generated by $\mathcal A$. Elementary mappings on elementary spaces are defined in a manner analogous to measurable mappings on measurable spaces. In addition, the notion of an {\it extension} of an elementary space is introduced. Let $M(X, \mathcal A)$, denote the ring of all real-valued elementary functions on $(X, \mathcal A)$. In this article, we study the ring $M(X, \mathcal A)$ and extensions of an elementary space. We show that, for any elementary space $(X, \mathcal A)$, there exists a unique compact elementary extension $(β_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A})$ of $X$, analogous to the Stone-$\check C$ech compactification, which contains every other extension of $X$. This extension has the property that every elementary map from $X$ into any compact topological space extends continuously to $β_{\mathcal A}X$. Next, we show that $β_{\mathcal A}X$ contains a realcompact extension $(\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X, \bar{\mathcal A}_R)$ of $X$, such that every elementary map from $X$ into any realcompact topological space extends continuously to $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Moreover, $\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$ is the smallest realcompact extension of $X$ and $(X, \mathcal A)$ is realcompact if and only if $X=\upsilon_{\mathcal A}X$. Also, we see that, every metric space equipped with the $σ$-algebra of all Borel sets is realcompact. Finally, we observe that the maximal ring of quotients of $M(X, \mathcal A)$ is the direct limit of locally constant (continuous) functions on dense open subsets of $(X, τ_{\mathcal A})$. Some questions raised in the literature are also answered.

title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.
comment: (v2) The proof is simplified and shortened further relative to the previous version. A discussion about the Lie brackets and the generators is added (v3) A proof of the closure of grt(F_2) under the Ihara bracket is added. (v4) Added Section 4.4 on the OpenAI injectivity argument

title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations in the half-space and exterior domains
abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

title: Adjoint Transfer and Order-Lifting Dichotomies for 2 x 2 Matrices over Prime-Power Rings
abstract: For an odd prime p, we study the change in matrix order under lifting from Z/p^k Z to Z/p^(k+1) Z. The first variation of the order defect is an affine translate of a cyclic adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p). We classify the full-order transfer for every q in GL_2(F_p): its rank is 3 for scalar elements, 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p = 3, and 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p > 3. For a Jordan element q = lambda(I + U), U^2 = 0 and U != 0, the vanishing first-order transfer for p > 3 admits an exact higher-order refinement. Writing d = (p - 1)/2, the full-order perturbation has depth d when tr(UX) != 0, depth p - 1 when tr(UX) = 0 and X is not in the span of U, and vanishes identically for X in the span of U. For p = 3, among the 27 lifts of a nonscalar order-preserving parent with determinant fixed to +1 or -1, exactly 9 preserve its order and 18 triple it; after the first increase, every further lift triples the order. We also give a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among unrestricted Jordan lifts.

title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(τ)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.

title: Homogenization of an optimal control problem for a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a 3D perforated domain
abstract: We study the homogenization of an optimal control problem governed by a Navier-Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system in a periodically perforated three-dimensional domain. The obstacles are Lipschitz sets of size $\varepsilon^α$, $α>3$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period. The fluid satisfies the no-slip condition on the outer boundary and the free-slip condition on the obstacles, the phase-field equation contains a source term, and the convective term carries a pore-scale Reynolds number that tends to zero as $\varepsilon\to0$. The control is a distributed body force, and the cost functional tracks the velocity in $L^2$ and the order parameter in $H^1$. Since uniqueness of weak solutions of the state system is not known for fixed $\varepsilon$, the control-to-state relation is multivalued, and we pose the microscopic problems over control-state pairs. We prove the existence of microscopic optimal pairs and the sequential $Γ$-convergence of the cost functionals to the cost functional of a control problem governed by the unsteady Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard system on the full domain. As a consequence, the optimal values converge, every cluster point of microscopic optimal pairs is optimal for the homogenized problem, and the optimal controls converge strongly along the corresponding subsequences. The $\liminf$ inequality follows from the homogenization of the state system, including the strong convergence of the gradients of the order parameter. Only the recovery sequence requires uniqueness of weak solutions of the homogenized system, which we prove when the outer boundary is of class $C^{2,1}$.
comment: 33 pages, 1 figure. We welcome comments and suggestions

title: Explicit Bounds for Restricted Invertibility with Prescribed Group Cardinalities
abstract: We prove an explicit lower spectral bound for independent random vectors with prescribed group multiplicities. Let $v_{ij}\in\mathbb C^d$, $1\le i\le l$, $1\le j\le k_i$, be independent random vectors with finite support and $\mathbb E v_{ij}v_{ij}^*=A_i$, where $\sum_{i=1}^l A_i=I_d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(A_i)\geε$. Set $k=\max_i k_i$, $n=\max_i\operatorname{rank}(A_i)$, and $K=\sum_{i=1}^l k_i$. If $n>(6+4\sqrt2)k$ and $2\sqrt{nk}-k<ε\le n/2$, then, with positive probability, \[ λ_K\left(\sum_{i=1}^l\sum_{j=1}^{k_i}v_{ij}v_{ij}^*\right) \ge n-(\sqrt{k}+\sqrt{n-ε})^2. \] As a consequence, we obtain a restricted invertibility result selecting exactly $k_i$ vectors from the $i$th group of a Parseval frame. The proof combines interlacing families, a reciprocal transformation of mixed characteristic polynomials, and a multivariate barrier estimate that accommodates repeated differentiation in the same variable.

title: Synergistic Learning in Domain Adaptation with a Known Link: A Minimax Understanding
abstract: When can combining source and target data yield much better performance than using either alone? From a minimax viewpoint, writing $R(n,n_T)$ for the minimax risk from $n$ source and $n_T$ target observations, we ask when $R(n,n_T)$ decays strictly faster than both $R(n,0)$ and $R(0,n_T)$. We call this the Synergistic Learning Phenomenon (SLP) and quantify it by the Synergistic Advantage Ratio $\mathrm{SAR}=\min(R(n,0),R(0,n_T))/R(n,n_T)$. We study domain adaptation with a known link: source regression $f$, target regression $g=\mathcal{A}f$ for a known operator $\mathcal{A}$, and possibly different designs. Three links---identity, integration, and differentiation---and the density ratio $ρ=h_T/h_S$ determine whether synergy is possible, at what rate, and in which sample-size window. For the identity link (covariate shift) with a Beta$(a,1)$ source and uniform target, a known necessary condition for SLP is $a\geq2+1/(2β)$, where $β$ is the smoothness of $f$ (Result I). An integral link $g(x)=\int_0^xf(t)\,dt$ can yield the joint rate $(nn_T)^{-1/2}$ even for a bounded ratio (Result II), and under a Beta$(a,1)$ source has a phase diagram with cuts at $a=2$ and $a=3$: integral SLP for $1<a<2$, an extra level-split rate $n_T^{-1}$ for $2<a<3$, and covariate-shift-type spatial SLP for $a>3$ (Result III). A derivative link $g=\dot f$ synergizes only under a stronger singularity (Result IV), giving a sharp integration--differentiation asymmetry under a bounded ratio. Across all three links, synergy arises from role separation: each dataset resolves a distinct bottleneck associated with the link and designs. We characterize the sample-size windows for synergy and how SAR varies with $n$ and $n_T$. Simulations support the predicted phase structure, and a mirrored integration--differentiation analysis of real vehicle and smartphone signals illustrates the asymmetry.

title: Walk-on-Ambient-Patch: Solver-Adapted Isometric Embeddings for Projected Walk on Spheres
abstract: Projected Walk on Spheres (PWoS) solves surface PDEs through ambient sampling and closest-point projection, but tightly folded embeddings can force short steps or ambiguous projections despite simple intrinsic geometry. We introduce Walk-on-Ambient-Patch (WoAP), which treats the embedding as a solver variable. Edge-isometry constraints and tangent-point repulsion separate intrinsically distant regions, optionally in higher codimension; patch states track residual projection branches without introducing PDE boundaries. We analyze the resulting geometry--sampling tradeoff: additional dimensions provide separation freedom but reduce uniform tangent progress, while strong tangent-biased proposals incur large importance-weight moments. Folded-surface experiments demonstrate reduced projection conflicts, a separate hard-constraint pilot verifies metric preservation, and an internal fixed-RMSE comparison favors higher dimensions at stricter accuracy targets. Together, these results motivate choosing the embedding and projection state jointly with the stochastic solver.

title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
abstract: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwiłł to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>θ_0\), with \(θ_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(θ\), where \(1/2\leqθ\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{θ,\varepsilon}X^{g(θ)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(θ)=\frac{θ(5-4θ)}{2(2-θ)}. \] Thus every fixed \(θ<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.

title: Rank-based Model Average Estimator for Average Treatment Effects
abstract: Model averaging emerges as an attractive ensemble technique that strategically synthesizes all available information from potential candidate models to enhance estimation accuracy. Despite of having been widely practiced in various areas in biostatistics and economics, its application to causal inference is rather limited. We propose to estimate the average treatment effect (ATE) by forming the weighted combination of the robust rank-based estimators obtained from a series of candidate models, where the model weights, selected via the growing window cross-validation, dynamically adjust the importance of candidate models. The proposed robust rank-based model averaging ({\sf RRMA}) is not only robust to handle potential outliers and heavy-tailed error distributions but also capable to reduce the risk of model mis-specification and enhance the flexibility and the accuracy of estimation. Theoretically, we establish the desirable asymptotic properties of {\sf RRMA}, including the asymptotic optimality, consistency and asymptotic distribution. Moreover, motivated by the asymptotic distribution of {\sf RRMA}, an easy-to-implement confidence interval is also developed for the ATE. Simulation experiments and an empirical application demonstrate the superiority of {\sf RRMA} over existing competitors in estimation accuracy, coverage probabilities and widths of confidence intervals.

title: K_1 of matroids
abstract: Using the geometric realization spectral sequence and the Serre spectral sequence, we compute $K_1(\operatorname{Mat}_*)$, the first K-theory group of the proto-exact category of pointed matroids, answering a question of Jun, Sistko and Wright.

title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.

title: Two characterizations of chain partitioned probe graphs
abstract: Chain graphs are exactly bipartite graphs without induced $2K_2$ (a graph with four vertices and two disjoint edges). A graph $G=(V,E)$ with a given independent set $S\subseteq V$ (a set of pairwise non-adjacent vertices) is said to be a chain partitioned probe graph if $G$ can be extended to a chain graph by adding edges between certain vertices in $S$. %there exists a set $E'\subseteq\binom{S}{2}$ such that the graph $G'=(V,E\cup E')$ is a chain graph. In this note we give two characterizations for chain partitioned probe graphs. The first one describes chain partitioned probe graphs by six forbidden subgraphs. The second one characterizes these graphs via a certain ``enhanced graph'': $G$ is a chain partitioned probe graph if and only if the enhanced graph $G^*$ is a chain graph. This is analogous to a result on interval (respectively, chordal, threshold, trivially perfect) partitioned probe graphs, and gives an $O(m^2)$-time recognition algorithm for chain partitioned probe graphs.
journal_ref: Annals of Operations Research 188 (2011) 279-283

title: KKT Residual Sliding Manifolds: A Projection-Free Structured Finite-Time Solver for Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation
abstract: Nonlinear Constrained Optimisation (NCO) requires simultaneous satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. Existing methods enforce these conditions through projections, penalties, barriers, or sequential approximations, potentially introducing computational complexity and convergence difficulties. For nonconvex problems, a KKT point need not be a local optimum. This paper reformulates NCO as stabilisation of a unified KKT sliding residual manifold and develops SM-KKT, a projection-free solver. Stationarity, equality feasibility, and regularised Fischer-Burmeister complementarity are integrated into a unified residual system, with complementarity encoding inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementary slackness. The manifold's zero set is shown to be equivalent to the KKT conditions. The required Jacobian saddle-point inertia is characterised and shown, under stated assumptions, to be equivalent to the simultaneous satisfaction of the Linear Independence Constraint Qualification (LICQ) and Second-Order Sufficient Condition (SOSC). This characterisation establishes local stability of the structured correction algorithm under these conditions and distinguishes nondegenerate locally optimal KKT solutions from points failing second-order optimality. SM-KKT computes structured primal--dual corrections and applies a discrete sliding reaching law to drive the KKT residual into a prescribed boundary layer in finite time. Four nonlinear benchmarks show recovery of reference constrained optima with KKT residuals below $10^{-6}$, earlier boundary-layer reaching, and favourable KKT accuracy compared with projected primal-dual, augmented-Lagrangian, quadratic-penalty, and log-barrier baselines.

title: Beyond Aggregate Drift: Optimal Client-Specific Windows in Federated Learning
abstract: We study federated learning from continuously arriving data: each client samples from its own distribution, these distributions drift over time, and the server must track the minimizer of the clients' weighted average loss. Clients are not alike as they collect data at different rates, with different noise, and change at different speeds. The main question is how much history should each one keep? A single shared window must serve every client at once, and so makes a fast-changing client carry the sampling noise of a slow, nearly stationary one. We give each client a memory of its own, sized to that client's noise, arrival rate, and drift, and refresh it by restarted accelerated method that starts from a common point. The tracking error is then bounded by \[ R\left(\sum_m w_m^{3/2}\,σ_m\sqrt{γ_m/λ_m}\right)^{2/3}, \] for clients with weight $w_m$, noise $σ_m$, arrival rate $λ_m$, and drift rate $γ_m$ on a domain of diameter $R$. This is never worse than what any common window can achieve, and strictly better whenever noise and drift are spread unevenly across clients. A lower bound that puts different groups of clients on different drift clocks shows this quantity is the right one. The two bounds agree up to a constant whenever the clients occupy boundedly many refresh scales, and in general differ only by the sixth root of the number of scales. Experiments show the gain comes from the memory rather than from the solver: it persists across accelerated, stochastic-gradient, and one-step methods, and against a separately tuned common-memory baseline.

title: On Baireness of the Wijsman Topology
abstract: We give negative answers to Questions 4.4 and 4.5 in Cao's survey on the Wijsman topology. We construct a metrizable space $Y$ and a compatible metric $d$ such that every finite power $Y^n$ is Baire, while $(\mathrm{CL}(Y),τ_W(d))$ is not Baire. The construction realizes the Vietoris hyperspace of a suitable metric space as an open subspace of a ball hyperspace. We also study the set $S_d$ of points having an open $σ$-$d$-totally bounded neighborhood. We prove that Baireness of $(\mathrm{CL}(X),τ_W(d))$ implies Baireness of $S_d$, and that, whenever $S_d$ is dense in $X$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $(\mathrm{CL}(X),τ_W(d))$ is Baire, $X$ is Baire, and $S_d$ is Baire. As consequences, we obtain complete characterizations for locally $σ$-$d$-totally bounded metric spaces, countable metric spaces, and $σ$-compact metrizable spaces. In our counterexample, $S_e$ coincides with a non-dense discrete component for every compatible metric $e$, showing that the density assumption is essential.

title: Tuza's Conjecture under an Edge-Count Condition
abstract: For a graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ denote the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles and let $τ(G)$ denote the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. Tuza's conjecture asserts that $τ(G)\le 2ν(G)$ for every graph $G$. We first note that Tuza's conjecture is equivalent to the following statement: for every fixed $c\ge 0$, if $G$ is a sufficiently large $n$-vertex graph with $e(G)\ge n^2/4-cn$, then $τ(G)\le 2ν(G)$. In this paper, we prove this statement for every $c<2$.

title: Hull Variation in Symplectic Linear Codes
abstract: We study the variation of hull dimensions of symplectic linear codes under equivalence transformations preserving the symplectic distance. For a symplectic linear code $C$, we introduce an even-valued invariant $Δ(C)$, which depends only on the equivalence class of $C$. This invariant can be expressed as the generic rank of an associated space of alternating matrices and, equivalently, as twice a corresponding matroid matching number. If $C$ has dimension $k$, we prove that the minimum symplectic hull dimension among all codes equivalent to $C$ is $k-Δ(C)$. Consequently, $C$ is equivalent to a symplectic LCD code if and only if $Δ(C)=k$. We further show that every symplectic MDS code of even dimension is monomially equivalent to a symplectic LCD code. For a symplectic self-orthogonal code $C$, we determine all attainable hull dimensions: for every integer $r$ with $0\le r\le Δ(C)/2$, there exists a monomially equivalent code whose symplectic hull has dimension $k-2r$. We also refine a standard form for the generator matrix of a symplectic self-orthogonal code and derive the corresponding parity-check matrix and the Gram matrix of the dual code. In the self-dual case, we characterize $Δ(C)$ through minors of an associated symmetric matrix. Furthermore, we relate hull variation to graph matchings, establish a bound for $Δ(C)$, and give graph constructions producing symplectic self-dual MDS, optimal, and best-known codes.

title: A chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks
abstract: A connected graph $G$ is matching covered if it contains at least one edge and every edge belongs to some perfect matching of $G$. A matching covered graph is a brick if it is 3-connected and after removing any two vertices, the resulting graph has a perfect matching. Bricks are the building blocks of matching covered graphs. A brick $G$ is extremal if the incidence vectors of all perfect matchings are linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. Zhou et al. [On planar extremal nonsolid bricks, J. Graph Theory, 2026] proved that for every planar extremal brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar extremal bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ has a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$, where $G_i/T_i$ means contracting the triangle $T_i$ into a single vertex. In this paper, the result of Zhou et al. is generalized to planar PM-compact bricks, a larger class of bricks including extremal bricks. We present a chain theorem for planar PM-compact bricks: for every planar PM-compact brick $G$, there exists a sequence of planar PM-compact bricks $G_0,G_1,\dots,G_n$ such that the underlying graph of $G_n$ is an odd wheel, $G_0=G$, and each $G_i$ $(0\leq i < n)$ contains a triangle $T_i$ such that $G_i/T_i = G_{i+1}$.

title: A Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlinear Damping and Supercritical Variable-Exponent Logarithmic Sources
abstract: We investigate a viscoelastic wave equation with nonlinear variable-exponent damping and a variable-exponent logarithmic source, allowing supercritical growth. The main difficulties arise from the failure of the source to map the energy space into $L^2(Ω)$, the sign-changing logarithmic potential, and the lack of Sobolev control of the displacement for supercritical damping. Under an exponent condition linking the source and damping exponents, we prove local existence, an energy identity, and a continuation criterion. We prove finite-time blow-up for nontrivial solutions with nonpositive shifted initial energy. We also establish a blow-up criterion based on a sufficiently large initial displacement--velocity pairing, with a threshold depending on the positive part of the shifted initial energy, and derive an explicit upper bound for the lifespan. This criterion allows us to construct blow-up data at every prescribed level of the original energy. For initial data in a suitable stable region, solutions exist globally. For damping within the Sobolev range, a general relaxation condition yields energy decay estimates that include exponential and polynomial rates. Beyond this range, a time-weighted displacement estimate and a splitting of the memory integral give logarithmic decay.

title: A Counterexample to Three Conjectures of Luo
abstract: We give a single counterexample to Conjectures 1--3 as stated in Luo's paper: a minimal two-tetrahedron triangulation of the lens space L(3,1) with a null-homotopic loop edge. The proof uses quadrilateral matching equations, an explicit calculation of shape parameters, and known results on volume maximization.

title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Padé approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $ζ_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Padé approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.

title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonné theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the étale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.
comment: 25 pages. Course notes for the workshop 'A Sprint on Local Systems', Wuppertal, 2026. To appear in the workshop proceedings

title: On a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type
abstract: We consider a family $(Λ_λ)_{λ\in \Bbbk^\times}$ of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type over an algebraically closed field $\Bbbk$, where $\Bbbk^\times:= \Bbbk\setminus \{0\}$, and for each $λ\in \Bbbk^\times$, $Λ_λ$ is socle equivalent to $Λ_1$, which is the trivial extension of a hereditary algebra of type $\tilde{A}$. We compute their Hochschild cohomologies, which shows that $Λ_λ$ is not derived equivalent to $Λ_1$ if $λ\neq 1$. This means that a derived equivalence classification of weakly symmetric algebras of Euclidean type given by Bocian--Holm--Skowro{\' n}ski is not complete.

title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$ψ$ Ablation study
abstract: We investigate how geometric priors shape neural approximations of the complex Monge--Amp`ere equation on the quintic Calabi--Yau threefold. This fixed-$ψ$ diagnostic compares four single-patch ans"atze: a coordinate SIREN potential model, a direct-metric Cholesky baseline, an algebraic section ansatz, and a section-plus-neural hybrid. In a 96-run learning-rate and frequency archive, section-based models reach validation $σ=4.14$--$4.16%$, whereas SIREN and Cholesky remain at $41.29%$ and $44.27%$. Multi-seed controls use a shared affine-$η$ evaluator and five fresh validation clouds. Stable section settings give $3.84$--$4.77%$, compared with $28.46$--$30.59%$ for Cholesky and $34.73$--$38.13%$ for SIREN. Hybrid projective features do not improve best-case accuracy, but they stabilise the stressed regime. They limit $σ$ to $4.26$--$4.41%$, versus $4.45$--$205.45%$ for raw coordinates. Within this protocol, section-based geometric structure is the main driver of accuracy; coordinate-only models plateau at substantially higher error, and raw hybrid flexibility can amplify instability. We provide a projective-scaling derivation, document protocol asymmetries, and identify projectively consistent hybrid corrections as the next step.
journal_ref: 2026 Mach. Learn.: Sci. Technol. 7 035049

title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.

title: From Product Evidence to Access Rights: Auditing and Routing Non-Firm Grid Connections
abstract: Non-firm connection products can accelerate grid access while reinforcements are delayed, but their planning value depends on evidence supporting the contractual promise. We develop a one-way evidence-to-access framework for calendarized products. Stage A constructs and fixes directional restriction calendars from public residual-load and day-ahead price-timing signals. Stage B audits the submitted calendar and one bounded common repair, tests joint threshold attainability under the shared annual budget, and applies an aggregation-aware Power Transfer Distribution Factor (PTDF) certificate. Stage C treats the resulting ledger as fixed in queue-aware allocation and intervention planning. In the primary policy-package evaluation, the evidence-supported menu returns the same $2.119$~GW allocation as firm-only access, whereas authorizing the uniformly derated fallback raises awards to $6.442$~GW and reduces backlog from $136.076$ to $113.601$~GW-years; all $4.489$~GW of non-firm awards use the fallback. In a target-free matched control, evidence-routed and state-blind fallback menus attain primary objectives equivalent within EUR~1 and return the same accepted applicants, award years, routes, and intervention portfolio. Thus, in the reported testbed, fallback authorization rather than calendar-specific evidence support drives the access-volume effect.

title: Orbital stability of solitary wave solutions of the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the endpoint case
abstract: In this paper, we consider the orbital stability of solitary waves for the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation $$iq_t+q_{xx}+i\partial_x\bigl(|q|^2q\bigr)=0, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}.$$ For the endpoint solitary waves satisfying $c>0$ and $c^2=4ω$, we prove the orbital stability in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ without any additional assumptions. The proof uses conservation of mass and the second Hamiltonian $\mathcal{H}_2$ to keep the Bäcklund-transformed solution small in $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ uniformly in time. We establish an inverse Bäcklund compactness result to reconstruct the algebraic solitary wave as the spectral zero approaches the negative real axis.

title: Symmetric Bases and $\ell^p$ Embeddings in Musielak--Orlicz Sequence Spaces under $δ_2$
abstract: We study isomorphic embeddings into Musielak-Orlicz sequence spaces \(\ell_Φ\), where the normalized generating sequence \(Φ=\{φ_n\}\) satisfies the \(δ_2\) condition. Using admissible normalized blocks, we construct an associated limiting family \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) of Orlicz functions. If a Banach space \(X\) with a symmetric basis embeds into \(\ell_Φ\), then there is a function \(ψ\in\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\) such that the basis of \(X\) is equivalent to the canonical basis of \(\ell_ψ\). An Orlicz sequence space \(\ell_ψ\) embeds if and only if \(ψ\) is equivalent near zero to a member of \(\mathcal C_{Φ,τ}\); in particular, \(\ell^p\) embeds exactly when such a member is equivalent to \(t^p\). Assuming differentiability of the generators on a common interval near zero, we also derive the necessary bound \(p\leq b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\), where the upper growth index incorporates the summable errors in the \(δ_2\) condition. The same index yields cotype \(q\) for every \(q\geq2\) with \(q>b_{Φ,(c_n),δ}\). Examples with nonuniform growth and lacunary weights illustrate this bound. For alternating Nakano exponents, the explicit limiting family gives a sharper restriction than the index alone. For general Nakano exponents, we recover the known exact cotype criterion, including attainment of the optimal exponent. For weighted Orlicz spaces, we express the cotype criterion through summable scalar errors and recover the formula using the global upper growth index when \(w\in\mathcal A\).

title: Toeplitz determinants for starlike mappings of order α in several complex variables
abstract: Let $F(z)=zf(z)$, where $f$ is a normalized scalar holomorphic function on the unit ball $\mathbb B$ of a complex Banach space $X$ or on the unit polydisk $\mathbb U^n$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$. We establish sharp bounds for two Toeplitz determinants involving the second, third and fourth Fréchet derivatives of $F$ when $F$ is starlike of order $α$, $0\leqα<1$. The first bound is sharp for the full range $0\leqα<1$, while the second is sharp for $0\leqα\leq 2/3$. The extremal mappings are explicitly identified, confirming the sharpness of the estimates.

title: Hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of a product of two space forms
abstract: We complete the classification of hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of dimension greater than or equal to three in the product of two space forms.

title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
abstract: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points. When X is a homogeneous variety over the field of complex numbers, this is a well-known theorem of Kim-Pandharipande.

title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $Λ$, and let $μ$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}Λ$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*μ=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}μ\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $δ_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q\geδ_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $δ_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-β)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $χ$. A real zero close to one forces $χ(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.

title: Whitney--Lagrange Decomposition for the First Family of Finite Element Differential Forms
abstract: We derive polynomial bubble duality in barycentric coordinates and construct explicit nodal bases for the first family of finite element differential forms. Logarithmic coordinates give an elementary proof of the Whitney--bubble decomposition. The Hessian of negative entropy defines a metric whose normalized Hodge star maps bubble generators to complementary-degree polynomial forms. This gives a direct geometric description of the known dualities and proves nondegeneracy of their integral pairings. Combining Whitney forms with shifted Lagrange polynomials then gives bases dual to tangential point evaluations in every dimension and order. The construction extends to scalar nodes that are unisolvent on every face. The interpolant is independent of the roots and commutes with face restriction.

title: A noetherian Hopf algebra has bijective antipode
abstract: We prove that a Hopf algebra over an arbitrary field has a bijective antipode if either its left or right regular module has finite uniform dimension. In particular, this solves Skryabin's conjecture, posed in 2006, that every noetherian Hopf algebra has a bijective antipode. Starting from Skryabin's injectivity theorem for weakly finite Hopf algebras, we associate to each finite-dimensional subcoalgebra an essential left ideal of common denominators that is also a right coideal in the antipode image. An annihilator identity makes this image essential in the original algebra as a left module over the image, yielding finite left uniform dimension from finite right uniform dimension. A second denominator construction inside the antipode image, together with a restricted inverse-antipode identity, proves surjectivity.

title: Schatten class membership of products of composition operators and their adjoints
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the Schatten class membership of the product of a composition operator and the adjoint of another composition operator on the Hardy and Bergman spaces. We provide several sufficient conditions and necessary conditions for these operators to belong to the Schatten classes. Moreover, for some specific symbols including linear fractional maps, finite Blaschke products, and inner functions, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions.

title: Bimodule duality and Artin's problem for skew field extensions
abstract: Emil Artin asked whether the left and right dimensions of an extension of skew fields must agree. Cohn and Schofield gave counterexamples through elaborate constructions. It has been a long-standing open question whether there is any division ring, infinite-dimensional over its center, for which the left and right indices agree whenever at least one is finite. We give the first such examples. Call a division ring index-symmetric if every division subring with at least one finite index has equal finite indices. Using a duality formula for bimodules over division algebras, we prove that every twisted Calabi--Yau division algebra is index-symmetric. The examples include the Weyl skew fields and, more generally, the quotient division rings of rings of differential operators on smooth affine varieties in characteristic zero. Further examples are the quotient division rings of enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras, Ore extensions of twisted Calabi--Yau noetherian domains, quantum affine spaces, and group algebras of torsion-free polycyclic-by-finite groups.

title: FirstFit coloring process of random bipartite graphs and an online coloring lower bound in the random order model
abstract: FirstFit colors each arriving vertex with the smallest positive integer absent from its previously colored neighborhood. We prove that this rule can require $n^{Ω(1)}$ many colors on certain bipartite graph of $n$ vertices even when the vertices arrive in a uniformly random order. This refutes the conjecture of Bosek, Gutowski, Lasoń, and Przybyło [BGLP24] that FirstFit uses a polylogarithmic expected number of colors on every bipartite graph in the random order model. We obtain the lower bound by analyzing the FirstFit coloring process on random bipartite graphs, where vertices arrive to either side with equal probability, and with an independent edge density $n^{-x}$ for some $0 < x < 1$. Our result can also be viewed as a qualitative strengthening of Kučera [Kuč91], who showed that, for every $ε> 0$, there are graphs with chromatic number at most $n^ε$ on which FirstFit uses $Ω(n/\log n)$ colors in expectation under a uniformly random order. Our result shows that such poor behavior of FirstFit already occurs for $χ(G) = 2$.

title: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
abstract: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(μ_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {é}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.

title: Temporal invariance of evolutionary entropy and comparative demographic analysis
abstract: Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time. When within-class timing is unknown, a uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. For constant post-maturity hazard and fertility, continuous exponential and discrete geometric descriptions correspond exactly at every time scale. Thus, for a fixed reference duration, evolutionary entropy is a property of the reproductive process, not of its temporal partition. These results provide a mathematical basis for comparing demographic models across different temporal scales by identifying the information required to separate differences in reproductive organisation from effects of the chosen age-class representation.

title: Boundary Vanishing Orders and Asymptotic Expansions for Planar Harmonic Functions with a Sublinear Robin Condition
abstract: We study boundary vanishing orders and asymptotic expansions of planar harmonic functions satisfying the sublinear Robin condition $\partial_νu=λu-|u|^{p-1}u,$ with $λ\geq0$ and $0<p<1$. For nontrivial global solutions on bounded connected Lipschitz domains, we bound the number of nodal domains by the number of Steklov eigenvalues strictly below $λ$ and establish finite vanishing order at every boundary point. The boundary scaling gives the critical exponent $\frac{1}{1-p}$. On $C^1$ boundaries, every positive subcritical vanishing order is an integer, and the leading term is a unique homogeneous Neumann profile in conformal coordinates. At a noninteger critical order, the rescaled solution converges in normalized graph coordinates to an explicit homogeneous profile determined by $p$ up to sign. Every supercritical bulk vanishing order $m$ is an integer, with a unique homogeneous Dirichlet profile in conformal coordinates. The boundary trace has vanishing order $\frac{m-1}{p}>m$. Integer critical vanishing orders are excluded if the boundary is $C^1$ with Dini mean oscillation.

title: Classification of minimal-mass blowup solutions to the mass-critical Hartree equation at the $L^2$-critical level
abstract: In this paper, we study the focusing mass-critical Hartree equation \[ iu_t+Δu=-\bigl(|x|^{-2}*|u|^2\bigr)u \] at the ground-state mass $M(Q)$. We prove that, up to the symmetries of the equation, every global minimal-mass non-scattering solution is a solitary wave, while every finite-time minimal-mass blowup solution is a pseudo-conformal image of a solitary wave. This extends the results of \cite{LZ28,Miao-Xu-Zhao3,Wang-Gao} to the scaling-critical space $L^2$ and removes the radial assumption in the global case.

title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
abstract: We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the Monge-Ampère equation and the constant quadratic Hessian equation, based on the two-point maximum principle. The arguments require only one differentiation of the equation. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the inhomogeneous term is assumed to be positive and continuously differentiable. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$.

title: An overring characterization of Gorenstein Prüfer domains
abstract: We prove that a commutative integral domain is Gorenstein Prüfer if and only if every overring is Gorenstein flat over the original domain. It is enough to test overrings that are finitely generated as algebras. The proof combines finite duality with a conductor-quotient argument. Under the overring hypothesis, the conductor quotient of a proper overring generated by two elements as a module is an IF-ring, and degree-one duality lifts first syzygies of finitely presented quotient modules to totally reflexive modules. This gives a bound of one for the Gorenstein flat dimension of every module annihilated elementwise by conductor powers. Quadratic integral elements provide such conductors at nonnormal localizations, while normal localizations give principal-ideal neighborhoods. Constructible compactness yields a finite cover, and a bounded complex of localizations combines these bounds over the original domain. Consequently every finitely generated ideal is Gorenstein flat and the domain is coherent. Examples distinguish finite-type from module-finite tests and Gorenstein flatness from ordinary flatness.

title: The First Modular Zhu Algebra of $L(\frac12,0)_F$ in Characteristic Seven
abstract: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $7$, and let $V=L(\frac12,0)_F$. For the degree-four singular vector $q=(L(-2)^2-2L(-4))\mathbf1$ in the universal vacuum vertex operator algebra $\bar V$, set $V_q=\bar V/I(q)$. We prove that the natural quotient map induces an isomorphism $A_1(V_q)\cong A_1(V)\cong F[T]/(T(T-4)(T-5))\cong F^3$. Explicit $O_1(V_q)$-relations and four families of triangular PBW straightening relations give the upper bound, while three one-dimensional homogeneous subspaces give the matching lower bound.

title: Turán Numbers of Linear Stars and Expanded Trees
abstract: For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$, let $\ex_r(n,\mathcal H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of $\mathcal H$. The $r$-uniform expansion $T^{(r)}$ of a tree $T$ is obtained by adding $r-2$ new vertices to each edge, with the added sets pairwise disjoint and disjoint from $V(T)$. In particular, the expansion of $K_{1,k}$ is the linear star $\mathcal L_k^r$, whose $k$ edges intersect pairwise in a single common vertex. Chung and Frankl (1987) determined $\ex_3(n,\mathcal L_k^3)$ and all extremal hypergraphs for every $k\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$. We extend the odd-$k$ part of their result to every $r\ge5$, determining the exact Turán number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism for sufficiently large $n$. More generally, we extend this result to expansions of trees for which the minimum degree among the vertices in the smaller color class is odd and at least three. For every $r\ge5$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish lower and upper bounds on their Turán numbers. When no two vertices attaining this minimum degree in that color class have a common neighbor, we determine the exact Turán number and the unique extremal hypergraph up to isomorphism. The proofs combine the delta-system method with stability arguments and a detailed analysis of extremal constructions.

title: Gorenstein Prüfer domains with non-Prüfer integral closure
abstract: There exists a one-dimensional local Gorenstein Prüfer domain whose integral closure is not Prüfer. We prove that the recently constructed coherent counterexample to the normalization problem has this stronger Gorenstein property. The argument establishes permanence of divisoriality of finitely generated ideals under ultraproducts and quotients by divided primes. It also supplies uniform matrix factorizations: in an ultraproduct of plane-curve domains, every nonzero ideal generated by $r$ elements is a cycle of a two-periodic totally acyclic complex with free terms of rank $r$. The divided prime defining the one-dimensional example is flat, so these complexes descend through the quotient and localization. A specified two-generated ideal remains noninvertible in every integral overring. Over the normalization, its associated Laurent overring has nonzero first Tor with every injective cogenerator, although both rings are Gorenstein flat over the original domain. Examples distinguish this failure from a nonnormal Gorenstein curve with Prüfer normalization and show that the periodicity conclusion is stronger than the Gorenstein Prüfer property alone.

title: On modular vector invariant fields
abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of any characteristic and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ the general linear group over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Suppose $W$ denotes the standard representation of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$ acts diagonally on the direct sum of $W$ and its dual space $W^*$. Let $G$ be any subgroup of $\rm GL(n,\mathbb{F}_q)$. Suppose the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W)^G=\mathbb{F}_q(f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k)$, where $f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k\in\mathbb{F}_q[W]^G$ are homogeneous invariant polynomials. We prove that there exist homogeneous polynomials $\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}$ in the invariant ring $\mathbb{F}_q[W\oplus W^*]^{G}$ such that the invariant field $\mathbb{F}_q(W\oplus W^*)^{G}$ is generated by $\{f_1,f_2,\dots,f_k,\ell_1,\ell_2,\dots,\ell_{n}\}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
journal_ref: Algebra Colloquium 27:4 (2020) 749--752

title: Spectral Gårding Elliptic Equations
abstract: We study spectral Gårding elliptic equations on compact Kähler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal Gårding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Székelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact Kähler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal Gårding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

title: Oka complements in algebraic tori and their logarithmic covers
abstract: Suppose $n\ge2$ and $K\subset\C^n$ is compact and polynomially convex. Write $q(z)=(e^{-iz_1},\ldots,e^{-iz_n})$, $X_K=(\C^*)^n\setminus(K\cap(\C^*)^n)$, and $Y_K=\C^n\setminus q^{-1}(K)$. We prove that $X_K$ and its logarithmic covering $Y_K$ are Oka. More strongly, $Y_K$ admits normalized holomorphic families of entire embeddings through prescribed holomorphic sections. The proof combines polynomial pair Hamiltonian transport in multiplicative coordinates, compatible with the coordinate hyperplanes, with a fixed Fatou--Bieberbach model. Applications include Oka slab crosses over arbitrary nonempty connected planar domains, complements of periodic equal-radius Euclidean balls centered at products of planar lattices, and complements of sufficiently small closed metric balls in products of elliptic curves.

title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$π\mapsto I_π(f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $π$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.

title: Every n points in the plane contain (m1 + o(1)) n points with no unit distance
abstract: Let $f(n)$ be the largest integer such that every set of $n$ points in the plane contains $f(n)$ points no two at distance $1$, and let $m_1$ be the supremum of the upper densities of Lebesgue measurable planar sets with no two points at distance $1$. Larman and Rogers observed that $f(n) \ge m_1 n$. We prove that $f(n)/n \to m_1$; that is, $f(n) = (m_1 + o(1))n$. This is the first half of a conjecture of Dúcz and Varga, and with the bound $m_1 \le 0.247$ of Ambrus, Csiszárik, Matolcsi, Varga and Zsámboki it gives $f(n) \le (0.247 + o(1))n$. The proof builds a random independent subset of the algebraic plane, invariant under algebraic translations and rotations, whose probability of containing the origin is at least the worst finite independence ratio, and turns it into a measurable planar set of at least that upper density. Its only non-classical input is the Haar rigidity theorem for wild character laws from the OpenAI preprint The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable, which has a machine-checked Lean proof. The whole argument has been formalized in Lean 4 on top of it.

title: General Constructions of Permutation-Fair Dice
abstract: Suppose that each of $n$ players rolls a different die and the players are ordered by their rolls. Can the dice use disjoint labels such that ties are impossible, while all $n!$ orders remain equally likely? We give two general constructions of such dice and solve some related problems.

title: A Berry--Esseen Bound of Order $(1+\log n)/\sqrt n$ for Peng's Central Limit Theorem
abstract: We derive a quantitative central limit theorem under sublinear expectations from a spatial endpoint regularity estimate for the one-dimensional \(G\)-heat equation. For bounded Lipschitz initial data, the second spatial derivative and the time derivative of its solution are Lipschitz in space and \(1/2\)-Hölder in time away from the initial time. In particular, \([u_{xx}(t,\cdot)]_{\mathrm{Lip}}\le C_G\Lip(φ)/t\). Combining this estimate with the nonlinear Stein identity introduced in Song \cite{Song2020} and a replacement argument yields a bound of order \((1+\log n)/\sqrt n\) for bounded Lipschitz tests when the third absolute moment is finite and the lower variance is positive. The final replacement step is estimated directly, avoiding the nonintegrable singularity at time zero.

title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.

title: Discrete intermediate dimensions: endpoints, spectra and quasi-isometric invariance
abstract: We introduce upper and lower discrete intermediate dimensions for unbounded subsets of Euclidean space and extend them to metric spaces. The definitions restrict the covering radii within a scale-dependent range of dyadic shells and take a supremum over an auxiliary parameter. The resulting dimensions are monotone in the parameter and recover the Barlow--Taylor discrete Hausdorff dimension at zero. We prove continuity at every positive parameter, with a sharp quantitative bound, and give an example with a jump at zero. At the upper endpoint, the upper dimension equals upper mass dimension for uniformly discrete Euclidean sets; the analogous lower mass identity fails. We establish a mass distribution principle and prove quasi-isometric invariance under a uniform coarse packing condition. For spaces with uniform polynomial volume growth, we construct clustered subsets attaining the continuity bound. Independent thinning truncates these spectra at the resulting mass dimension, almost surely for all parameters simultaneously. Applications include the discrete Heisenberg group with its word metric and the ranges of simple symmetric random walks.

title: One boundary, infinitely geometries
abstract: Let $N$ be a 3-dimensional integral homology sphere. We prove the existence of a sequence of 4-dimensional topologically negatively curved manifolds $M_k$, $k=1,2,\dots$, satisfying the following: (1) all aspherical manifolds $M_k$ have the same universal cover $U_N$ depending only on $N$; (2) all fundamental groups $π_1(M_k)$ are hyperbolic and share the same Gromov boundary $X_N$ depending only on $N$; (3) the groups $π_1(M_k)$ represent infinitely many distinct quasi-isometry classes. The last conclusion, which represents the new feature, shows that negatively curved geometries in dimension 4 exhibit substantially richer structure than those in dimension 3.

title: Uniqueness of prescribed-node radial bound states for a zero-mass double-power equation
abstract: We study radial bound states of \[ Δu-\abs{u}^{q-1}u+\abs{u}^{p-1}u=0 \quad\text{in }\R^n, \qquad n\ge3,\qquad 1<q<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}. \] For every integer $k\ge1$, we prove that there is exactly one radial bound state with $k$ simple zeros and $u(0)>0$. Its absolute maximum is attained at the origin. This confirms the zero-mass, Sobolev-subcritical case of Tang's double-power uniqueness conjecture. The proof adapts Tang's phase-transition analysis and combines it with a finite-level separation argument inspired by Cortázar--García-Huidobro--Yarur. Three main difficulties arise in the zero-mass double-power setting: the sign changes of key comparison quantities in the low-amplitude region, the possible failure of pointwise positivity of an auxiliary quantity when $n=3$ and $p+q<3$, and the absence of exponential decay at infinity. We overcome these difficulties by introducing bridge functionals to propagate the required sign information through low amplitudes, establishing a weighted integral positivity estimate in the exceptional three-dimensional range, and combining a radial-flux tail estimate with finite-level inverse-branch comparison. We also establish the strict ordering of the bound-state shooting heights and show that the shooting variation along the \(k\)-node state has exactly \(k+1\) simple zeros.

title: On the convergence of doubly stochastic block gradient descent method for linear inverse problems
abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and randomized block coordinate descent (RBCD) belong to two fundamentally different classes of stochastic iterative regularization methods, and are promising and popular for solving large-scale inverse problems, due to their excellent scalability with respect to data size and signal size, respectively. In this work, we propose a doubly stochastic block gradient descent (DSBGD) method with early stopping, by integrating the updating strategies of both SGD and RBCD, for solving linear inverse problems in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
