For the EFIE, the single layer representation and the surface Piola transformation give the result in Maxwell trace spaces, whereas the result for open surfaces or screens is obtained by introducing suitable restriction and extension by zero operators. As opposed to existing results, we do not rely on an affine-parametric representation of the boundary deformations, thus allowing for more general parametric shape variations. Finally, we establish shape holomorphy of the shape-to-solution map for the EFIE, subject to interior electric Maxwell nonresonance on closed surfaces but with no such condition on screens. Under suitable summability and stability assumptions, these shape holomorphy results provide an analytic basis for the dimension-robust convergence of interpolation and quadrature methods used in computational uncertainty quantification (UQ) of scattering problems with high-dimensional, shape-parametric uncertain geometry.

title: A Domain-specific adaptation network for elliptic interface problems
abstract: Deep learning provides a flexible mesh-free framework for solving elliptic interface problems. However, domain-specific neural approaches often rely on separate networks for individual subdomains, causing the model complexity to grow rapidly as the number of subdomains increases. To address this limitation, we propose a Domain-Specific Adaptation Network (DSAN), which combines a shared backbone with lightweight subdomain-specific adapters to provide local represen- representation flexibility without replicating a complete network for each subdomain. We further establish a stability and error analysis showing that the continuous physics-informed residual controls the solution error, and decompose the resulting error into approximation, optimization, and sampling components. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional problems with multiple regular and irregular interfaces demonstrate that DSAN achieves accuracy comparable to or better than fully decomposed multi-network methods while requiring substantially fewer trainable parameters. More- over, the parameter savings become increasingly pronounced as the number of subdomains grows, demonstrating the scalability of the proposed domain-specific adaptation framework.

title: Are implicit schemes needed in adaptive time stepping for PDEs?
abstract: Implicit time integration is the standard way to overcome the tight CFL time step restriction when solving nonstationary PDEs numerically. However, within an adaptive time accurate integration, the time step size selection is governed not only by stability but also by accuracy requirements. Therefore, an eligible question to ask is: is (unconditionally) stable implicit time stepping really needed if the time step is restricted by accuracy considerations anyway? And how much do we then lose (in terms of the time step size) when switching from the expensive implicit time stepping to stabilized explicit schemes? An answer to this question is also important because such a switch is often done when solving large scale nonstationary PDEs on massively parallel computers. This paper attempts to answer these questions by numerical tests for two particular adaptive time accurate settings: (i)~nonstationary convection-diffusion equations and (ii)~nonlinear heat equations.

title: From Cauchy to Gaussian: Sharp Lower Deviations and Ehrhard-Type Inequality
abstract: We establish dimension-free, pointwise optimal lower-deviation bounds for convex functions under spherically symmetric Cauchy-type measures. These bounds use either mean-variance normalization or moments about the median, the latter covering the Cauchy case where the mean and variance are unavailable. By approximation with a parametrized family the Cauchy-type measures, our results recover the Gaussian setting of Paouris and Valettas \cite{PaourisValettas18} and strengthen their variance-sensitive estimate to a sharp bound, with a complete equality characterization. This goes beyond the partial improvements obtained in subsequent work. We also prove an Ehrhard-type inequality for arbitrary convex sets under these Cauchy-type measures in every dimension and characterize all equality cases. This resolves a conjecture posed by Byczkowski, Małecki and Żak \cite{ByczkowskiMaleckiZak22}. The proof follows from a variational argument combined with the joint concavity of fiber rearrangement. The geometric inequality reduces distributions of convex observables to one-dimensional convex transforms, yielding the sharp lower-deviation bounds.

title: Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
abstract: Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class. These computations enlarge the class of Filippov invariant sets for which the Conley index is known and extend previous results on low-codimension singularities to periodic dynamics.

title: A smooth non-compactly generated category
abstract: Let $A=\mathbb{Q}[t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0]$ and consider $A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, a skew Laurent polynomial ring, where $σ(t^q)=t^{2q}$. We study the kernel of derived extension of scalars along $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\longrightarrow\mathbb{Q}[u,u^{-1}], $ the quotient by $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$, with $\mathfrak{m}=(t^{\frac{1}{2^n}}:n\geq 0)$. A finite free resolution of $\mathfrak{m}A[u,u^{-1};σ]$ over $ A[u,u^{-1};σ]\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \bigl(A[u,u^{-1};σ]\bigr)^{\mathrm{op}} $ proves smoothness. A specialization inequality for matrix ranks supplies a nonzero exact colimit-preserving functor that vanishes on every compact object, proving failure of compact generation.

title: Differential operator approach to the $\imath$Howe duality
abstract: The iHowe duality for iquantum groups of type AIII/IV was established in \cite{LX22} via two approaches, based on partial flag varieties and quantum coordinate coalgebras respectively. In this paper, we provide a new construction of this iHowe duality via quantum differential operators. Moreover, by deriving explicit action formulas, we prove that our construction coincides with the two constructions given in \cite{LX22}.

title: Global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Kähler manifolds
abstract: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Ampère equation with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side on a compact Kähler manifold.

title: An unbounded convex set with the fixed point property for nonexpansive mappings
abstract: We construct an equivalent norm on $\mathbb{R}\oplus\ell_2$ and a nonempty closed convex unbounded subset having the fixed point property for nonexpansive self-mappings. The ambient renormed space has the fixed point property on bounded closed convex subsets. The main point is a geometric localization estimate at a distinguished point of the unbounded set; the fixed point conclusion then follows from the Kirk--Ray localization theorem.

title: Stability and Error Estimates with Optimal $\varepsilon$-Dependence for Strang Splitting of the Allen--Cahn Equation
abstract: In this work, long-time Sobolev stability and error estimates with optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence are established for the Strang splitting method applied to the Allen--Cahn equation with periodic boundary conditions. By combining the modified energy dissipation law, and Hölder-Gagliardo-Nirenberg product estimates, the numerical solution is proven to admit uniform-in-time $H^r$-seminorm bounds $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-r}+1)$, consistent with the corresponding Sobolev bounds of the exact solution. A second-order error estimate $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^2τ^2)$ is further established on any prescribed finite time interval, exhibiting quadratic dependence on $\varepsilon$. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the optimal $\varepsilon$-dependence of both the stability and error estimates.

title: A Countable Three-Generated Orthomodular Lattice with No $σ$-Complete Embedding
abstract: We give an explicit countably infinite orthomodular lattice generated by three specified elements and a direct argument that it admits no injective homomorphism into any $σ$-complete orthomodular lattice. In particular, it does not embed into any set-sized complete orthomodular lattice. The source is a generated subalgebra of a cofinite reduced product of finite-dimensional real subspace lattices. A nonzero finite term $a$ is orthogonal to the orbit of a terminal line under every finite word in three Sasaki projections, while another finite term $X$ satisfies $π_aπ_X(t)=a$. If the image of this countable orbit has a supremum in a target orthomodular lattice, Sasaki adjunction forces that supremum to commute with the generator images. This forces the image of $a$ to vanish. The proof imposes no atomicity, modularity, Hilbert representation, cardinality bound on the target, or preservation of source infinitary operations. All target lemmas are derived from the orthomodular axioms.
comment: 8 pages, no figures; AI-use disclosure updated, verification scope retained; mathematical statements and proofs unchanged

title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
abstract: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

title: There are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in $L^p$ spaces, $p \ne 2$
abstract: We proved recently that there are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in the space $L^p(Ω)$, $1 \le p < 2$, for any set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite measure. For $p > 2$, we proved that the same holds provided that $Ω$ has nonempty interior, but the general case remained open. In this note we close this gap, i.e., we establish that exponentials cannot form an unconditional Schauder frame in $L^p(Ω)$, $p \ne 2$, without any additional assumptions on the set $Ω$ of finite measure other than measurability.

title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.

title: Parameter-Free Adaptive Extragradient Methods for Generalized-Smooth Variational Inequalities
abstract: Variational inequalities (VIs) provide a unified framework for optimization, saddle-point, equilibrium, and learning problems, where operators need not be globally Lipschitz. The $α$-symmetric generalized-smoothness condition allows local operator variation to grow with the operator norm, but existing extragradient methods often require unknown problem-specific constants. To address this issue, we propose PF-AEG, an explicit, line-search-free extragradient method whose stepsizes use quantities generated during the iterations, without prior knowledge of these constants. Under $p$-quasi-sharpness, we prove full-sequence convergence and last-iterate squared-distance rates: linear convergence for $0<p\le2$ and $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2/(p-2)})$ for $p>2$. The latter matches existing parameter-dependent rates under comparable assumptions, while the linear guarantee extends the previous $p=2$ result to $0<p\le2$. Building on the idea of PF-AEG, we develop AEG-VR, a variance-reduced adaptive extragradient method for finite-sum VIs. We prove almost-sure convergence and, under mild conditions, obtain analogous expected last-iterate rates, while retaining independence from the unknown problem-specific constants in stepsize selection. Experiments on synthetic generalized-smooth VIs and several learning problems show that the proposed methods are competitive with, and in several tested regimes outperform, existing baselines.

title: Rota-Baxter operators and factorization of Lie affgebras
abstract: We introduce Rota-Baxter operators on Lie affgebras by an identity independent of the choice of origin and prove that they induce descendant Lie affgebra structures. We establish a bijection between ordered affine Lie factorizations and idempotent operators split at a chosen idempotent fixed point. A cokernel obstruction determines the existence of this point, while invariance under the structural endomorphisms characterizes splitting. We also determine when weighted descendants satisfy the affine Jacobi identity and when operators of nonzero weight give affine doubles. For canonical Lie affgebras, we describe all affine Rota-Baxter operators by Lie subalgebra decompositions and translation vectors, and classify them up to automorphism in dimensions at most two.

title: Averaged derivatives and reverse inequalities in quasiregular Bergman spaces
abstract: We study weighted Bergman spaces of quasiregular mappings on the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with weight $(1-|x|)^α$, $α>-1$. For every fixed distortion bound $K\ge1$ and every $p>0$, we characterize Bergman integrability by averaged derivatives. We also give geometric conditions under which integration over a subset, or against another measure, controls the full Bergman integral. When $K$ is sufficiently large, the dominating sets are precisely the relatively dense sets. For comparison, we determine the dominating sets for the Möbius class $K=1$ in dimensions $n\ge3$. At the critical exponent $p=n+α$, its domination criterion differs from that for every fixed $K>1$. Our results extend aspects of the Bergman theory developed by Nolder~\cite{Nolder90} and by Oleinik and Vuorinen~\cite{OV}, and complement the recent work of Adamowicz and González~\cite{AG21,AG25} and Adamowicz and Caamaño~\cite{AC} on quasiregular Hardy spaces.
comment: 30 pages; submitted to a journal on September 21

title: Multi-type $Λ$-Wright--Fisher processes with polynomial drift: Bernstein duality, long-term behaviour, and simulation of moments
abstract: The $(d+1)$-type $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process with polynomial drift is a Lévy-type process on the $d$-dimensional unit simplex whose generator entails a particular jump and diffusive component, as well as a polynomial drift component. In this work, the process is connected to a (Bernstein) dual process, which admits an interpretation as an urn model with coloured balls. Exploiting this duality, we identify various parameter regimes: one in which the $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process is absorbed almost surely at a vertex of the simplex, and others in which it admits a unique nontrivial ergodic probability measure. The results include verifiable criteria for absorption versus persistence, as well as representations of absorption and stationary measures. Moreover, the duality relation is exploited to devise and implement a simulation-based approach for estimating moments of the $Λ$-Wright--Fisher process.

title: New bounds for off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
abstract: We study a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, which characterizes the $3$-graphs $H$ for which the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,n)$ is polynomial. We prove the conjecture for $3$-graphs with at most five tight components. Additionally, we show that the full conjecture is equivalent to its specialization to linear $3$-graphs. We prove quasipolynomial upper bounds for a class of `forward-doubleable' $3$-graphs, which includes the Fano plane. Finally, we give an exponential lower bound for `non-forward-laminar' $3$-graphs and use this to completely classify the Ramsey growth of a natural family of 3-graphs called chains.

title: Ex Ante and Scenario-Conditional Value of Information in Dynamic Portfolio Choice
abstract: Portfolio decisions are often made under uncertainty about expected returns, and investors revise their beliefs as new information arrives. Although richer information generally cannot reduce optimized value ex ante, the trading strategy it induces need not improve on the strategy induced by a less informative information structure in every fixed-drift scenario. We introduce scenario-conditional expected utility and value of information to evaluate strategies selected under the investor's current belief. In a finite-horizon Gaussian portfolio choice model, we compare a fixed-belief investor, a price observer, and an attentive investor who also processes an auxiliary signal under an attention capacity constraint. Ex ante, price learning and auxiliary attention are valuable, and the total value of attention increases with capacity. Scenario-conditionally, learning creates a correction benefit by reducing the initial trading-position gap relative to the full-information strategy, but also a fluctuation cost through belief revisions, so the ex ante ranking can reverse. We derive the current-belief distribution of scenario-conditional value and the associated underperformance probability, defined as the probability of negative scenario-conditional value relative to fixed-belief choice. Over sufficiently short horizons, the scenario-conditional value of learning is negative when belief error is small relative to posterior uncertainty. For a given horizon, sufficiently high attention capacity yields a higher scenario-conditional value than any fixed finite-capacity benchmark across all drift scenarios. We also derive sharp convergence rates to full-information performance under Shannon and Tsallis technologies.

title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{λ,μ}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities ($λ\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $μ\in\mathbb{R}$).

title: On the nonnegative integer solutions to the equation $F_n^2+F_m=2^{a}$
abstract: The Diophantine equation $F_n^x+F_m^y=2^a,$ where $F_k$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $n,m,a\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$, has attracted attention in recent years. The cases $(x,y)=(1,1)$ and $(x,y)=(2,2)$ were completely resolved by Bravo and Luca, and by Jeong and Park, respectively. In this note, we investigate the mixed exponent case $(x,y)=(2,1)$ and we completely determine all nonnegative integer solutions.

title: A Counterexample To The TF-cone Conjecture
abstract: The TF-cone conjecture of Asai and Iyama predicts that the TF equivalence class of an integral $g$-vector is the open cone generated by the canonical summands of all its positive multiples. We give a counterexample to this conjecture. For the tensor product of the three-arrow Kronecker algebra with the path algebra of $s\to t$, a vector $w$ has a two-dimensional TF equivalence class, whereas every positive integral multiple $mw$ is generically indecomposable. The cone generated by these canonical summands is therefore a single ray. The same example disproves the relative-interior version proposed by Haerizadeh and Yassemi.

title: On best approximation and estimates of Bohr--Favard type on the sphere for functions with bounded Laplacian
abstract: We determine the best constants in estimates of the $L^\infty$ norm of functions on the sphere with bounded Laplacian whose first spherical harmonic components vanish. In every dimension $d\geq2$, these constants are expressed through weighted $L^1$ extremal polynomials. On $S^2$ the constant is an explicit positive series, and the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is $7ζ(3)/4$. On $S^3$ the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is a positive integral involving the Hörmander--Bernhardsson extremal function. In higher dimensions the rescaled extremal polynomials converge to weighted entire extremals, which give asymptotic formulas for the Bohr constants on $S^4$ and $S^6$. The most unexpected and, in our view, interesting observation is that, for every fixed $n\geq2$ on $S^2$ and $S^3$, the constants in best approximation estimates are \emph{strictly smaller} than the corresponding Bohr--Favard constants.

title: Combinatorics of degeneracy in vertical systems
abstract: We characterize the generic consistency of vertical systems in terms of the iterated circuits of the column matroid of the coefficient matrix. More precisely, we prove that such a system is generically consistent if and only if there exists an iterated circuit such that the dimension of the Minkowski sum of the associated Newton polytopes is equal to the rank of the coefficient matrix. We also give an equivalent characterization in terms of $G$-spanning flags of the dual matroid. With this, we derive a combinatorial formula for the codimension of the locus of parameter values for which the system has a solution, extending known results on dual defects of toric varieties. When this locus has codimension one, its defining equation yields a generalization of the sparse resultant to vertical systems, which applies also to $\mathcal{A}$-discriminants. Finally, we characterize when the solution set is contained, for generic parameter values, in a finite union of hyperplanes parallel to a coordinate hyperplane.

title: The CR Nirenberg Problem, Part I: Blow-up Analysis and Compactness
abstract: We establish a priori estimates and compactness results for positive solutions of the CR Nirenberg problem under natural weighted flatness conditions. The proofs combine refined blow-up analysis, Pohozaev identities, and the complete classification of positive entire solutions to the critical CR Yamabe equation recently obtained by Li--Liu--Ma \cite{LLM2026} and Li \cite{L2026}. Existence and degree results are established in our subsequent paper \cite{QTWPartII}.

title: On the Julia sets of the non-autonomous iteration of exponential maps
abstract: This paper studies non-autonomous iterations of $λe^z$, where at each step the parameter $λ$ is chosen from a bounded interval. Urbański and Zdunik introduced and developed a thermodynamic formalism for random dynamics of exponential maps, extending the autonomous result established independently by Rees and Lyubich to typical parameter sequences in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $1/e<A<B<\infty$. In this paper, we show that the same conclusion indeed holds for all parameters in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$, Our proof is based on carefully crafted uniform versions of pullback arguments, inspired by the original methods of Rees and Lyubich. In a related direction, Urbański and Zdunik established a non-autonomous analogue of Misiurewicz's theorem for the exponential map, later refined by Lech. We further extend their work by providing a refined condition for the Julia set to be the entire complex plane.

title: Global Well-Posedness and Uniform Long-Time Control for a Class of Periodic NLS-Dysthe Equations
abstract:
We study a class of periodic NLS-Dysthe (NLS-Dy) equations, also referred to as higher-order nonlinear Schrödinger equations (HNLS), of the form $i\partial_t u+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $ x\in\mathbb T$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb R$, $abc
eq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. For $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive PDEs, including the Klein-Gordon equation and the Serre-Green-Naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves. We prove local well-posedness in $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $H^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. In the parameter regime $e
eq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $H^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. This result does not require the non-resonance condition appearing in Takaoka's periodic theory, while the condition $e
eq0$ naturally arises in the modulation setting considered here. Finally, motivated by the long-time regime relevant for modulation, we establish uniform long-time control without imposing a smallness assumption on the initial datum. Using the conservation laws of cubic NLS and their invariance under the commuting complex mKdV flow, we obtain uniform $H^s$ bounds on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for integer $s\ge2$. For non-integer real $s\ge2$, the maximal $H^s$ solution exists on the same time scale, while uniform control is obtained at a lower regularity, with a loss of less than one derivative.

title: Graphs on Topological Spaces
abstract: Graphs defined on groups, such as power graphs, enhanced power graphs and commuting graphs, form a hierarchy under inclusion of edge sets. We develop an analogous theory for topological spaces. To a space X we attach five graphs on the vertex set X, all invariant under homeomorphisms: the specialization, inseparability, closure-meeting, Urysohn and functional graphs. They form a diamond-shaped hierarchy whose members are null exactly when X is T_1, Hausdorff, Urysohn or functionally Hausdorff. The Urysohn graph always contains the square of the inseparability graph, with equality for Alexandrov spaces, and the hierarchy is compatible with products via the strong product of graphs. Every countable graph, together with isolated vertices, is the inseparability graph of a second countable T_1 space. For finite spaces we characterize the graphs that occur as inseparability graphs (every edge lies in the closed neighbourhood of a simplicial vertex), determine all coincidences between members of the hierarchy, and show that the specialization graph determines the weak homotopy type but not the space itself. Using Dowker duality we prove that the complexes of inseparable and of closure-meeting families are always homotopy equivalent and, under an acyclicity hypothesis, recover the weak homotopy type. We show that if the closure-meeting graph is a cograph then it is chordal, an analogue of a recent result for enhanced power graphs; the same holds for the inseparability graph of an Alexandrov space but not in general. Finally, following Cameron's work on topologies preserved by permutation groups, we show that for a topology invariant under a primitive group each graph is null or connected, and that the neighbourhood filters of the five graphs reverse the hierarchy, giving spaces whose specialization graph contains the Rado graph as a spanning subgraph.

title: Decomposition of functions of bounded variation in Ahlfors-regular PI spaces
abstract: We prove that, on a non-compact Ahlfors-regular PI space, every function of bounded variation $f$ can be decomposed as a countable sum $\sum_{n=1}^\infty f_n$ of monotone functions of bounded variation $f_n$, in such a way that the total variation of $f$ is the sum of the total variations of the functions $f_n$. Our result extends a Euclidean result of Bianchini and Tonon to the metric setting.

title: A Unified Framework for Randomized Row-Action Methods for Structured Data Fitting and Constraint Geometry
abstract: We study randomized row-action methods for problems with linear observations, convex constraints, and non-Euclidean geometry. Our starting point is a unified formulation in which the data-fitting term acts in observation space, while the feasible set and the regularizer encode structure in variable space. It covers constrained least squares, nonnegative and simplex-constrained models, regularized data fitting, and equality-constrained Bregman selection problems. The structure of these problems leads naturally to two algorithmic branches. The first uses primal Bregman-proximal row steps for soft data-fitting problems. The second uses dual Bregman--Kaczmarz steps for problems with hard equality constraints. We first derive a common one-step inequality. We then give deterministic and stochastic convergence results for the soft branch under relative smoothness. For constrained least squares, the normalized row oracle has exact first- and second-moment identities. They yield an expected ergodic bound in the inconsistent case, an $O(1/K)$ bound in the interpolating case, and linear convergence of the actual iterates under a residual error bound. For equality-constrained selectors, we prove linear convergence in expected Bregman distance under a residual-to-Bregman error bound. We recall global sufficient conditions for this bound and derive local constants for the nonnegative quadratic geometry and the entropy geometry on the simplex. Numerical experiments illustrate the noisy stepsize trade-off and the local entropy selector theory, and show that entropic row-action updates can recover interpretable factors in a simplex-structured nonnegative matrix factorization problem.

title: A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices
abstract: In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(λ_1,λ_2,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and $λ_2$ real, then $(λ_1+t,λ_2\pm t,λ_3,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with eigenvalues $λ_1\ge\dots\geλ_n$ and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $λ_1+d_1,\dots,λ_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list Guo-extreme if none of Guo's moves can be reversed within the set of symmetrically realizable lists. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modelled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if $A$ is irreducible and every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and vanishes wherever $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every trace-preserving direction (in every direction, if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry) and remain symmetrically realizable; in particular it is not Guo-extreme.

title: Clifford Invariants and Three-Copy Quantum Tests
abstract: We give an explicit treatment of the third tensor power of the Clifford representation on $n$ qutrits, for $n\geq2$. This representation has five pairwise inequivalent irreducible constituents, with multiplicities $1,1,1,1,2$. The decomposition reduces the Clifford twirl of a tensor cube to four real parameters. Two of them are spectral moments of the input. The other two are cubic invariants expressed as sums of cubes of the Weyl characteristic function and the discrete Wigner function. On trace-one Hermitian matrices, the invariant polynomials of degree at most three are spanned by the constant function and four algebraically independent functions. These functions do not separate Clifford orbits. For pure inputs a single parameter suffices. We recover its range and the characterization of its maximum by stabilizer states. We bound the stabilizer fidelity, determine full separability across the three copies in the symmetric family, and recover the criterion for a complex projective $3$-design. We classify the jointly invariant quantum Boolean functions. For stabilizer testing and for testing unknown observables we give explicit bounds on copies and queries. We also give character formulas for the finite projective Clifford groups and record the complete character table for two qutrits.
comment: GAP code is available in the GitHub repository: https://github.com/luanyongzhi/qutrit-character-table

title: Generic nondegeneracy of constant mean curvature radial graphs
abstract: Given a smooth domain $D\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$, $N\geq 3$, and a positive constant $H$, we study radial graphs over $D$ with constant mean curvature $H$ which meet orthogonally the boundary of the cone spanned by $D$. The corresponding problem is given by a quasilinear elliptic equation on $D$ with homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. We investigate the structure of the solution set under smooth perturbations of the domain which are parametrized by an open set of $C^{3,α}$-diffeomorphisms of the sphere. After pulling the equation back to a fixed reference domain, we apply a classical transversality theorem and prove that, in the class of domains for which $N-1$ does not belong to the Neumann spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, there is a residual set for which every solution is nondegenerate. A consequence of our result is that, for every such domain and every $R>0$, the set of solutions whose $C^{2,α}$-norm is bounded by $R$ is finite.

title: Bounds for (k,c) model functions over p-adic fields
abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $ρ$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $ρ$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $ρ$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.

title: Nontrivial domains for the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem with small constant vorticity
abstract: In this paper, we first apply the implicit function theorem to find nontrivial solutions to the following Bernoulli's overdetermined problem \begin{equation} -Δu=γ\,\, \text{in}\,\,Ω\setminus\overline{D}, \,\, u=1,\,\,\partial_\mathbf{n} u=Q\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partial D, \,\,u=0\,\,\text{on}\,\,\partialΩ\nonumber \end{equation} for a fixed boundary $\partialΩ$ and a free boundary $\partial D$ in $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ with $N\geq2$, where $γ$ is a sufficiently small constant, the Bernoulli value $Q$ is determined by the construction, and $Ω\setminus\overline{D}$ is a bounded ring-shaped domain. In dimension $N=n+1$ with $n\geq2$, we further study the existence of a nontrivial unbounded domain $Ω\setminus\overline{D}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$ such that the Bernoulli's overdetermined problem admits a solution. This unbounded domain we construct is periodic in one variable and radial in the other variables by bifurcation analysis.

title: Unique Determination of the Lamé Parameters in Three Dimensions
abstract: We prove that the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for static isotropic elasticity uniquely determines both smooth Lamé parameters in a bounded smooth domain of \(\mathbb R^3\) under strong convexity. The proof uses an exact four-component Laplace-type reduction, but its decisive identities are obtained from physical elastic solutions. The characteristic quotient of the reduced system has rank three, whereas the leading physical adjoint lift supplies only two directions. We construct the missing polarization from the first nonvanishing correction of a reduced amplitude in the kernel of that lift. Paired with fixed primal and adjoint quotient frames, the resulting complex geometrical optics solutions yield a complete family of holomorphically weighted \(3\times3\) matrix moments through the physical Betti identity. Cauchy--Plemelj factorization converts these moments into an invertible relative transport normalized in the common exterior. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction and transport rigidity then determine a material ratio and the shear modulus, hence both Lamé parameters. No smallness, symmetry, separability, or analyticity hypothesis is imposed.

title: Sharing a unit, measuring a length: a didactic analysis of a teaching progression for fractions from Grade 1 to Grade 8
abstract: Fractions require learners to revise properties associated with whole numbers. This paper presents a design rationale and a critical analysis of an eight-level source progression for fractions (Grades 1-8, nominal ages 6-14), from which the French-curriculum and International Baccalaureate chapters published at https://commeunjeu.org are assembled. Its central hypothesis is a bridge from sharing to numerical measure: a share of one unit is represented by a bar, read as a length relative to a specified unit, and located on the number line. The reference unit is kept stable in the initial tasks to focus attention on fraction magnitude, equivalence and operations; changing the unit is deliberately postponed, without treating this as a mathematical requirement or an established reduction in cognitive load. Three principles organise the meanings: sharing one unit, coordinating bars and number lines, and establishing fractions as numbers before explicitly treating them as scalar operators. Two supporting principles concern valid local justifications before formal generalisation and chains of equalities, introduced in Grades 2-3, with written reasons in lessons from Grade 4. The analysis relates these choices to the research literature and selected curricula, examines task strategies and feedback, and distinguishes realised features from discrepancies and proposed revisions. The source documents and their curriculum projections do not establish the order actually experienced by pupils. No empirical evaluation is reported. Primary hypotheses address transfer between representations, coordination of units and the numerical status of fractions before operators; the audit also identifies limits to the reproducibility of its findings.

title: Poisson occupancy of paths on permuted regular graphs
abstract: In the classical occupancy problem, $B$ balls are placed independently and uniformly into $d$ boxes. We study a graph analogue of this model. Let $G$ be a directed $r$-regular graph on $d$ vertices and fix a vertex $i$. Consider all paths of length $L$ starting from $i$, and let $N_L(i,j)$ denote the number of such paths ending at a vertex $j$. Thus the vertices play the role of boxes and the $r^L$ paths play the role of balls. In general, these occupancies depend strongly on the geometry of $G$. We show that inserting independent uniform permutations between successive layers restores the classical Poisson behavior at the empirical level. Although the path endpoints remain strongly dependent, their empirical occupancy distribution has the same limiting Poisson law as independent balls thrown into boxes. More precisely, at the critical scale $r^L/d\toλ\in(0,\infty)$, provided $rL/d \to 0$, the empirical path multiplicity distribution converges in Wasserstein distance to $\operatorname{Pois}(λ)$, independently of the geometry of the underlying graphs. We also prove a local Poisson limit theorem and a Berry-Esseen bound for the empirical distribution functions. These estimates determine the full total-variation transition of the normalized path multiplicities toward uniformity. For arbitrary doubly stochastic kernels, we further establish exact covariance and Frobenius norm identities, together with an exact contraction formula for the chi-square divergence. As applications, we study synchronous opinion averaging, obtaining an explicit cutoff profile for equal-size groups and quantitative convergence to consensus for heterogeneous group sizes.

title: Stochastic Geometrically Exact Beams: Continuous-Time Geometric Principles and Variational Discretizations
abstract: Geometrically exact beams naturally arise in physical phenomena and engineering practice for modeling flexible structures, such as soft robotic manipulators and DNA structures. To the best of our knowledge, there appear to be no geometric integrators for stochastic geometrically exact beams in a variational formulation. In this paper, we introduce variational principles for the dynamics of stochastic geometrically exact beams, in both continuous- and discrete-time settings. By introducing perturbations via stochastic potentials and stochastic kinematics, we derive the equations of motion from a variational viewpoint. The resulting stochastic geometric integrators simultaneously discretize time and space in a parallel manner, which provides a distributed computational framework for solving the stochastic dynamics of complex beam systems. In particular, the proposed integrators are shown to be a stochastic extension of the well-known deterministic staggered leapfrog scheme for the wave equation, and also a stochastic extension of Yee's scheme for spatially one-dimensional computational electromagnetism. Numerical results are shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

title: Induced-Count Discrepancy in Uniform Hypergraphs
abstract: Let $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ be the maximum, over all $k$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs $F$, of the absolute difference between the number of induced copies of $F$ in $H$ and its expectation in the binomial random $r$-graph with the same number of vertices as $H$ and edge probability $p$. Let $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ be the minimum of $u_k^{(r)}(H,p)$ over all $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraphs, and let $D_r(n,p)$ be the distance from $p\binom nr$ to the nearest integer. For fixed $r\ge3$, $k\ge2r$ and $\varepsilon>0$, the quantity $u_k^{(r)}(n,p)$ has order $\max\!\left\{D_r(n,p),p(1-p)\right\}n^{k-r}$ whenever $p(1-p)n^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor/(\binom{2r-2}{r}-1)}\ge\varepsilon$. Using local moment estimates and switchings in a sparse reservoir, we construct one hypergraph with the nearest-integer edge count that controls all induced orders simultaneously.

title: C*-algebras of Essentially Tracially Rank One
abstract: We introduce the notion of essential tracial rank at most one for simple $C^*$-algebras. We show that separable simple $C^*$-algebras with essential tracial rank at most one have several regularity properties, including stable rank one, strict comparison, and tracial approximate divisibility. A finite amenable simple $C^*$-algebras with this property is $\mathcal Z$-stable. We also prove the converse. Thus this property gives a new characterization of separable simple finite amenable $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras and shows that these algebras admit a one-dimensional tracial approximation. In the unital real-rank-zero case, this approximation can be strengthened to show that the algebra has tracial rank zero. This completes a long-standing project. As a byproduct, we prove that every tracial state on a unital separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra is quasidiagonal and that the algebra itself is quasidiagonal. Consequently, every separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra of finite nuclear dimension has finite decomposition rank. None of these results requires the UCT.

title: The price of a weak shadow variable: inference under nonignorable missingness as relevance vanishes
abstract: When an outcome is missing not at random, identification is commonly restored by a shadow variable: a covariate that predicts the outcome but is excluded from the response mechanism. The literature treats the first requirement, relevance, as a yes-or-no condition. We make it continuous, parametrizing it by a scalar that scales the shadow variable's entire contribution to the moment conditions, and ask what inference costs as that scalar vanishes. One functional of the inverse weight governs the answer. We characterize it exactly, show that it fixes the effective sample size, and use it to sharpen the rates of the estimator that avoids the weight. The characterization is concrete. Whether the functional saturates or diverges turns not on boundedness of the outcome but on whether the tilting variable has an atom at its essential supremum: a binary outcome saturates, a uniform one does not. It also bounds how far a scanned set reaches, and that reach grows only as the square root of the logarithm of the sample size, so a thousandfold increase buys one unit of tilt while the set to be scanned widens. A reanalyzed credit-scoring study shows the cost: a characteristic an optimizing selector uses cannot satisfy exclusion.
comment: 45 pages, 2 figures. Replication package: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23262505. v2 consolidates the work into a single document at the moderators' request. v1 was the theoretical part only; v2 adds the diagnostics, an application to a published credit-scoring study, and an impossibility result for selective labeling. Parts are under review separately as two papers

title: Diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices and $φ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices
abstract: In this article, we present the diagonalization of skew-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary equivalence. For a unit quaternion $φ$, we also obtain the diagonalization result of $φ$-Hermitian dual quaternion matrices in the sense of unitary $φ$-congruence, which generalizes the Autonne--Takagi factorization of symmetric complex matrices and $φ$-Hermitian quaternion matrices.

title: Sylow $2$-Subgroups of Finite Groups with a Single Conjugacy Class of Involutions
abstract: We solve Brauer's Problem 33 by determining the finite $2$-groups that occur as Sylow $2$-subgroups of finite groups with a single conjugacy class of involutions. Besides the Sylow $2$-subgroups arising from the relevant non-abelian simple groups in Table 1, these are precisely the homocyclic, generalized quaternion, and Suzuki $2$-groups. The classification of finite simple groups is used in this paper.

title: Pairwise Compatibility Graphs of Unweighted Caterpillars
abstract: In this paper we study pairwise compatibility graphs whose witness tree is required to be an unweighted caterpillar. This is a natural restriction of PCGs, in the same line of research as the study of star witnesses, which led to the class of double-threshold graphs. In the caterpillar case, we show that this restriction is equivalent to a one-dimensional difference-labelling problem: a graph admits such a representation if and only if its vertices can be assigned integer labels so that adjacency is determined exactly by whether the absolute difference of two labels belongs to a given interval. Using this characterization, we derive structural properties of the class, including bounded twin-width, and study its relation with familiar graph families. We show that the class contains cycles and two-dimensional grids, while it excludes natural obstructions such as the subdivided star $S_{2,2,2,2,2}$, the cube graph $Q_3$, the wheel $W_6$, and the complement of the $3$-sunlet. We also consider restricted representations, including centipede witnesses and representations with a given interval and we give a polynomial-time recognition algorithm when the interval is fixed.

title: Upper tail large deviation for the first passage time in the frog model on $Z^d$ with $d\geq 2$
abstract: We study upper tail large deviations for the first passage time in the frog model on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge 2$. Let $\mathrm{T}(0,x)$ denote the first time at which the infection, started from the origin, reaches $x$, and let $μ$ be the associated time constant. We prove that, for any Euclidean unit vector $v\in\mathbb R^d$ and $ξ>0$, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} -\frac{1}{\mathfrak{s}_d(n)} \log \mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathrm{T}(0,\lfloor nv\rfloor) \ge (μ(v)+ξ)n\bigr) =\mathfrak{r}_dξ, \] where $\mathfrak s_2(n)=n/\log n$ and $\mathfrak r_2=π$ for $d=2$; $\mathfrak s_d(n)=n$ and $\mathfrak r_d$ is the escape probability of simple random walk for $d\ge3$. Moreover, on the upper tail large deviation event, we show that a certain slowdown mechanism occurs near the endpoint. To rule out other mechanisms, we analyze the growth of the infection near the starting point using a modified exploration process, and investigate its propagation through the intermediate region using the renormalization and covering arguments.
comment: 66 pages, 1 figure. The main results of this paper were announced in 2023

title: Development and operational deployment of a staff rostering system using mathematical optimisation in a municipal water utility
abstract: We developed a staff rostering system for complex employment and staffing requirements at a municipal water utility and deployed it in routine operations at the Water Purification Office of Suita City Waterworks Bureau, Japan, in May 2026. We estimated that preparing a monthly roster took approximately 2-3 h after deployment, compared with 12-18 h previously. The system represents roster states, effective staffing and office assignments using binary and auxiliary integer variables and optimises the entire planning horizon. When the normal model yields no feasible solution, a second stage attempts to generate a reference roster by penalising weekly day-off shortages while retaining the other hard constraints. Outputs identify shortages and meeting-date changes applied before solving. Computational experiments used operational inputs for 14 staff over 245 days. The baseline was solved to optimality in approximately 177 s; a modified meeting-day scenario produced a reference roster with five staff-days of shortage. Independent monthly solving without history produced 16 staff-week cases of excess days off across two month-boundary weeks. This case demonstrates the practical value of optimisation-based decision support for staff rostering in municipal water utilities by showing how mathematical optimisation can be integrated into roster preparation and checking workflows with reduced preparation time.

title: Stable and effective restarting of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing partial eigenpairs of Hermitian matrices
abstract: We consider stable and effective restarts of the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for computing the eigenpairs of a large Hermitian matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with the $n_{ev}$ eigenvalues in a given interval. Taking the CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR methods for instance, we prove that the commonly used restart scheme and its orthonormalized variant, named the natural restart schemes, are not numerically stable, thereby lowering attainable accuracy of approximate eigenpairs and missing some of the $n_{ev}$ desired eigenpairs. To cure these deficiencies, we propose a new restart scheme, called the combination restart, that takes the $n\times \ell$ starting matrix to be the product of the matrix, which consists of the selected $n_{ev}$ approximate eigenvectors, and an $n_{ev}\times \ell$ Gaussian random matrix. We prove the remarkable mathematical and numerical superiority of the combination restart over the natural restarts, then present a hybrid restart scheme that fully exploits the advantages of the natural restart and combination restart, and finally develop CJ--SS--RR and CJ--SS--RRR algorithms with the hybrid restart. Numerical experiments confirm that the new algorithms are numerically backward stable to the working precision and more efficient than the CJ--SS--RRR algorithm with the natural restart. The combination restart and hybrid restart schemes can be straightforwardly extended to the SS--RR and SS--RRR methods for general standard and generalized eigenvalue problems.

title: Sharp decay estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear equations in thin domains
abstract: We reduce the problem of establishing pointwise upper decay estimates in thin domains for viscosity subsolutions of fully nonlinear partial differential equations to solving a one-dimensional differential inequality. The resulting estimates make explicit the interaction between the transverse geometry of the domain and the ellipticity of the equation, and are shown to be sharp. Our framework allows the ellipticity to degenerate at infinity and accommodates nonhomogeneous equations with lower-order terms. As an application, we obtain decay estimates for $p$-subharmonic functions when $1<p\leq 2$

title: Learning Optimal Robust-Pathwise Control of Elliptic Equations with Random Coefficients
abstract: Conventional control approaches to optimization problems under uncertainty entail a practical compromise: deterministic controls offer robustness at the expense of pathwise accuracy while stochastic controls can adapt to individual realizations but suffer from the curse of dimensionality. To achieve both robustness and adaptivity, a neural operator-based approach is proposed in this paper for distributed elliptic optimal control problems with high-dimensional random inputs. A data-driven training algorithm is first established to learn the mapping from coefficient realizations directly to their optimal pathwise controls. To bypass the burden of generating training data pairs, a physics-informed training algorithm is then proposed and recast as weakly supervised learning using pseudo label targets produced by standard adjoint-based control updates. Numerical experiments with rough coefficients are conducted to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our robust-pathwise controls, which outperforms the benchmark robust deterministic control on unseen coefficient realizations owing to the generalization capability and fast inference of trained models.

title: Euler Cutting Planes for Fractional CVaR Programming
abstract: We maximise expected reward per unit of marginal tail risk, a reward-to-CVaR ratio against a baseline. The standard Dinkelbach route re-solves a Rockafellar--Uryasev LP or QP with one auxiliary variable per tail scenario at each multiplier update. Our method eliminates the multiplier iteration and keeps scenario auxiliaries out of the master, while still evaluating tail risk to generate cuts. A Charnes--Cooper/Schaible homogenisation removes the reward/risk multiplier, and the remaining convex constraint is separated on demand: each cut coefficient is an Euler allocation vector, read off a ranking and an average. The result is a single convex program, finitely terminating at the global optimum, with size independent of S --- an LP in $M{+}1$ variables, or a second-order cone program in $M{+}2$ for a concave quadratic numerator. The method runs 20--100 times faster than the exact Dinkelbach formulation and only needs single-digit cut counts.

title: Liouville theorems for stable solutions to the mean curvature equation
abstract: We study stable solutions of the mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-1}u $$ in domains of $\mathbb R^n$. We establish Liouville-type results in three settings. First, for globally stable solutions in $\mathbb R^n$, we prove that $u\equiv0$ if $1<p<p_{JL}$, where $p_{JL}$ is the Joseph--Lundgren exponent. Second, for solutions in $\mathbb R^n$ that are stable outside a compact set, we show that if $n>2$ and $p=p_S$, where $p_S$ is the Sobolev critical exponent, then $u\equiv0$. Third, for solutions of the Dirichlet problem on connected unbounded domains with smooth boundary satisfying an epigraph-type geometric condition, we prove that if $n>2$, $1<p\le p_S$, and the solution is stable outside a compact set, then $u\equiv0$. The proofs are based on a gradient estimate for stable solutions, an integrability result, conservation laws and Pohozaev-type identities, and a unique continuation argument. These results extend Liouville-type theorems for stable solutions from the semilinear Lane--Emden equation to the mean curvature equation.

title: Occupation Times at a Moving Interface and Sharp Yosida Rates for MacKean-Vlasov BSDE with Jumps and Fuzzy Selections
abstract: We study a forward-backward McKean-Vlasov system with jumps whose backward equation contains a source obtained by evaluating the minimal-norm selection of a maximal monotone operator along the forward state. This selection changes branch across an interface that moves with the state law, the control, and an imprecisely known parameter described by fuzzy cuts. Assuming normal non-degeneracy and finite-statistics dependence of the interface on the law, we prove that the first and second moments of the time spent within a given distance of the interface are bounded, respectively, by a constant times that distance and by a constant times its square. The second-moment estimate makes it possible to integrate the source error before squaring it, which yields a Yosida error of first order in the regularization parameter in the natural solution norm; a first-moment argument gives only order one half. An explicit example shows that the first-order rate is sharp. For compact classes of admissible selections, the corresponding solutions form the cuts of a fuzzy solution set. These cuts are compact, stable with respect to the fuzzy level and the data, and approximated at the same first-order rate in Hausdorff distance. All estimates are uniform over a non-dominated family of probability measures representing volatility uncertainty. The quantitative results are obtained for separable quadratic potentials with finitely many affine branches.

title: The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite Artin algebras
abstract: We prove that every representation-finite Artin algebra of finite global dimension has integral Cartan determinant one.
comment: 8 pages. The main result is extended to representation-finite Artin algebras

title: Generalized reflection complexity
abstract: The reflection complexity of a sequence, introduced recently by Allouche, Campbell, Li, Shallit, and Stipulanti, counts the factors of a given length up to reversal. We generalize this notion considering a group $G$ generated by antimorphisms over a given alphabet $\mathcal A$. The $G$-complexity of a sequence over $\mathcal A$ counts the factors of a given length up to the action of $G$. For $G$ generated by the reflection alone, the $G$-complexity coincides with the reflection complexity. We characterize eventual periodicity in terms of the $G$-complexity. Then we focus on the binary alphabet and the group $H$ generated by reflection and the antimorphism exchanging letters. We provide a simple formula for the $H$-complexity in the case of $H$-rich sequences and determine the precise values for complementary symmetric Rote sequences and generalized binary Thue-Morse sequences. Finally, we describe the aperiodic recurrent sequences having the minimum $H$-complexity -- they are exactly the complementary symmetric Rote sequences, while the binary sequences with the minimum reflection complexity correspond to the Sturmian sequences.

title: Examples of Bessel Functions of Order Zero Related to the Functional Equation of the Riemann Zeta Function
abstract: In 2010, M. A. Chaudhry et al. introduced a class of functions Sigma satisfying an L^1-condition. They proved that every function phi in Sigma gives rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. They also provided an example of a function outside Sigma for which the functional equation still holds. In this paper, we present several examples of Bessel functions of order zero that do not belong to Sigma but nevertheless give rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, we show that J_0(a sqrt(x)), J_0(ax), and Y_0(x) exhibit this phenomenon.

title: Dimension-independent eigenvalue approximation for sparse matrices
abstract: Many applications in science and engineering require solving sparse Hermitian eigenvalue problems that are so large that even algorithms whose runtime scales linearly with the matrix dimension are unacceptably slow. Responding to this challenge, there is a growing body of work on sparsified iterative methods and submatrix selection methods that often perform well in practice. However, theoretical understanding of these methods is limited. In this paper, we take a step toward better understanding sublinear-time eigenvalue computation by analyzing the sparsified power method. We prove that the method approximates a leading eigenpair to a prescribed accuracy in a number of iterations comparable to the standard power method. The required number of retained nonzeros depends explicitly on the target accuracy, the initial overlap with the leading eigenvector, the compressibility of the leading eigenvector, and the relative spectral gap. When these quantities and the column sparsity are independent of dimension, the runtime is independent of dimension. In contrast, we show that a comparable worst-case guarantee cannot hold for a prototypical sparsified submatrix selection method. Submatrix selection is the approach of choice in many quantum chemistry applications. However, we show that, even with substantial initial eigenvector overlap, a single iteration of the method can produce a vector that is orthogonal to the leading eigenvector, after which the method cannot recover. Nevertheless, experiments on matrices from the SuiteSparse matrix collection and quantum chemistry problems illustrate the practical effectiveness of submatrix selection methods in a variety of domains despite these worst-case limitations.

title: Poisson contingency tables, Gibbs permutations, and entropic optimal transport
abstract: We study random contingency tables obtained by conditioning a matrix of independent Poisson entries on its row and column sums. We identify such a table with the block counts of a random permutation drawn from a Gibbs measure of Mallows type, an exact coupling whose normalizing constants recover Barvinok's permanent identity. We use this correspondence to study the table at three scales. For finite dimensions, a transference principle compares the table with a matrix of independent Poisson entries whose means form the static Schrödinger bridge, the solution of a discrete entropic optimal transport problem. As the dimensions grow and the margins and prior means converge, the normalized histogram of the table converges to a limiting Schrödinger bridge at a quantitative rate. The fluctuations of the table around the bridge are characterized in two complementary ways. Linear statistics satisfy a central limit theorem for bounded test functions, with limiting variance equal to the squared $L^2$-distance, under the bridge, of the test function to the subspace of additively separable functions; as a process they converge to white noise with intensity given by the bridge, conditioned to have vanishing marginals. Spectrally, the limiting spectral distribution of the centered table is governed by a Dyson equation whose variance profile is the density of the bridge. The key ingredient is an asymptotic formula for the partition function of the Gibbs measure in terms of a Fredholm determinant given by the canonical correlations of the bridge. For Mallows-type random permutations, our results prove Pal's conjecture on the limiting partition function and Mukherjee's conjecture on the central limit theorem for linear statistics, both in greater generality.

title: The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with scattering damping
abstract: The focus of this article is to establish the existence portion of the Strauss conjecture for wave equations with spatially dependent scattering damping. In the current setting, the damping is not sufficiently strong to alter the critical Strauss exponent. In a subsequent study, the authors will consider the case of damping coefficients with critical decay where a shift of the Strauss exponent is expected. While several recent studies of the Strauss conjecture have relied upon weighted Strichartz estimates, here, instead, an approach that is based only on integrated local energy estimates, in particular those with both $r^p$ and ghost weights, is developed. This technique also applies to the problem for the free equation. Space-time Klainerman-Sobolev estimates provide the necessary decay to close the argument.

title: On trace-zero norm forms of orders of rational quaternion algebras with applications
abstract: In this paper, by normalizing the trace-zero norm forms according to the parity of orders of definite rational quaternion algebras, we give an explicit formulation to the even Clifford correspondence followed by the reciprocity of ternary forms. We obtain an exact identity between ternary representation numbers and the number of elements of an order with prescribed reduced norm and trace, which applies to all orders without squarefreeness constraint on the reduced discriminant. Applications include a criterion for realizing ternary forms as trace-zero norm forms, a formula for traces of Brandt matrices in terms of representation numbers, and explicit theta series relations associated with local reciprocity. We also describe reciprocal orders and order chains, and interpret the ternary forms occurring in the congruent number problem through their associated quaternion orders.

title: The Strauss conjecture for the wave equation with critical damping
abstract: The Strauss conjecture concerns wave equations with power-type nonlinearities and seeks the optimal range of powers that admit global solutions for all sufficiently nice and sufficiently small initial data. In three spatial dimensions, it is well known that small data global existence is available provided that the power $p>p_c(3)=1+\sqrt{2}$, where $p_c(n)$ denotes the critical power in $n$-spatial dimensions. In the current article, the analogous problem is considered for damped wave equations where the damping coefficient is at the critical scaling. When $a$ denotes the constant multiple applied to the damping term, it is shown that the corresponding critical power is $p_c(3+a)$ provided that $a$ is sufficiently small.

title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
abstract: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.

title: A new convergence proof for an iterative scheme for elliptic Cauchy problems based on alternating orthogonal projections
abstract: We consider an elliptic Cauchy problem for the Poisson equation in which both Dirichlet and Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on a portion of the boundary, while no boundary conditions are available on the remaining part of the boundary. Such problems are severely ill-posed. In this work, we study the convergence of an iterative method based on the alternating imposition of Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We formulate the scheme within a Hilbert space framework, where a yet another alternation becomes apparent: each iteration can now be interpreted as an orthogonal projection onto an appropriate closed subspace. This perspective provides a transparent geometric interpretation of the algorithm and yields a concise convergence proof based on von Neumann's classical result on alternating (orthogonal) projections. In addition to elucidating the convergence of the method, this alternating projections perspective also offers a general rate of convergence in terms of the Friedrichs angle (between two closed subspaces). We point out by means of an example that such convergence rate estimate degenerates for the elliptic Cauchy problem under consideration.

title: Products of Berezin Transforms on Generalized Fock Spaces
abstract: We study products $B_{α,m}^{(d)}B_{β,m}^{(d)}$ of Berezin transforms on generalized Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^d$. We establish a result for $m\neq2$: if $B_{α,m}^{(d)}B_{β,m}^{(d)}$ coincides with another such product, then the weight parameters of the second product must be $(α,β)$. As consequences, we characterize when two Berezin transforms commute and when the product of two Berezin transforms is again a Berezin transform.

title: Spectral-Edge Continuation, Dimensional Crossover, and Endpoint Stability for Partially Confined Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations
abstract: We study the global geometry and endpoint dynamics of positive solutions of $-Δu+|y|^2u+λu=g(u)$, $(y,z)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, $m=N-d$. Despite the loss of coercivity at $λ=-d$, we construct a connected component of centered positive solutions with frequency projection $(-d,\infty)$, assuming subcritical asymptotics of $g$ at zero and infinity, a zero-mass Liouville condition, and a strict Hamiltonian sign condition. At the lower edge, $λ+d\rightarrow 0^+$, anisotropic rescaling selects the lowest confined harmonic mode coupled to an $m$-dimensional scalar ground state. As $λ\rightarrow\infty$, isotropic blow-up yields the $N$-dimensional scalar ground state, revealing a dimensional crossover. The endpoint profiles and mass laws hold for every sequence of centered positive solutions, not merely along this component. The proof combines Gaussian--exponential localization on compact frequency strips, Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, compact spectral perturbation, and Leray--Schauder continuation. At both ends, we establish uniqueness and differentiability of the centered branch, identify the Morse indices and symmetry kernels of the real and imaginary linearizations in the full energy space, and derive sharp mass-slope asymptotics. Under standard Hamiltonian-flow hypotheses, the resulting slope criterion classifies orbital stability and instability away from the mass-critical powers. The mass map on this component, combined with endpoint control on the full centered solution set, yields existence, nonexistence, and multiplicity for normalized standing waves, revealing the roles of both critical exponents $2+4/m$ and $2+4/N$.

title: Orbit stratifications and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds with rank-one nonabelian symmetry
abstract: We study closed simply connected six-manifolds with positive sectional curvature and an effective isometric action of $SO(3)$ or $SU(2)$. Starting from Liu's corrected orbit-space analysis, we refine the stratification and recover smooth topology in several previously unresolved cases. For a boundaryless $SO(3)$ quotient, singular isotropy is connected, the weighted nonprincipal graph belongs to nine necessary families, and every action with only cyclic exceptional isotropy is classified equivariantly. The remaining branching families admit explicit rational intersection and Pontryagin formulas. For a three-ball $SO(3)$ quotient, the uniform-boundary configurations give sphere bundles over $S^4$ and a completely distinguished odd-integer family of non-spin six-manifolds. A doubled-quotient argument excludes the configuration with two boundary fixed points and an interior singular orbit, while the configuration with one fixed point and an exceptional interval has underlying manifold $\mathbb{CP}^3$. For a boundaryless $SU(2)$ quotient, an adjoint-weight matching argument reduces the exceptional three-orbit case to a unique action on the Eschenburg flag and identifies every two-orbit candidate with a weighted action on $S^2\times S^4$. These classifications imply rational ellipticity throughout the stated symmetry class. We also establish restricted curvature obstructions for the two diagonal product actions, without asserting nonexistence for arbitrary invariant metrics. Abstract graph restrictions, smooth realizability, and positive-curvature realizability are kept distinct. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.
comment: 33 pages, 1 figure. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors. Comments are welcome

title: Entanglement-Capability-Aware Finite-Bond Circuit Cutting for Distributed Quantum Computing
abstract: Distributed quantum computing distributes workloads that exceed a single processor's capacity across resource-constrained components. Circuit cutting enables this decomposition, but its effectiveness depends on partition choice. We present SACE, a Simulation-Aware Circuit Partitioning framework with Entanglement-Capability-Aware Screening. EP-Cost screens partitions using a parameter-dependent entanglement-capability proxy and native implementation cost. Under reconstruction constraints, finite-bond refinement selects the candidate that minimizes the worst-subcircuit discrepancy between normalized MPS simulations at bond dimensions $χ$ and $2χ$. Across 14 exhaustively enumerated small-scale candidate spaces, EP-Cost-guided genetic algorithm selections attain co-optimal native quasiprobability decomposition (QPD) overhead, with a median within-circuit Spearman correlation of 0.9965 between EP-Cost and QPD overhead. At matched cut counts, EP-Cost reduces QPD overhead by $25.20\times$ and $16.89\times$ for 8- and 9-qubit QFT circuits, respectively, and improves sampled reconstruction. On 12-qubit approximate QFT, deterministic reconstruction reduces Pauli-observable mean absolute error in all six low-bond conditions and total-variation distance in five. With five cuts and 7,776 QPD terms, SACE is best on all four reconstruction metrics in four of six conditions. At 24 qubits, SACE improves exact-local QFT accuracy in all 30 instance-bond-dimension conditions against each EP-Cost-only, Kernighan-Lin, and spectral baseline. The 50-qubit QFT comparisons remain favorable as reference convergence improves. Weighted QAOA circuits provide complementary, more bond-sensitive evidence. Refinement benefits persist across three search methods; larger candidate panels improve the optimized proxy without guaranteeing lower exact-local error.

title: Shake concordance in the topological concordance class of the Hopf link
abstract: Within the topological concordance class of the Hopf link, we construct infinitely many classes under the equivalence relation generated by smooth $0$-shake concordance. Each contains infinitely many smooth concordance classes represented by links that are pairwise strongly $0$-shake concordant and whose second components have unbounded smooth slice genus.

title: Sharp projection inequalities for antichains in cone orders
abstract: We establish sharp projection inequalities for $k$-antichains under orders defined by open convex cones. For integers $n\geq2$ and $k\ge 1$, let $C\subsetneq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open convex cone. A set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is a $k$-antichain with respect to the order $x\prec_C y\iff y-x\in C$ if it contains no chain $x^1\prec_C\cdots\prec_C x^{k+1}$. For every such set $A$ and every $v\in C$, we prove \[ \mathcal H^{n-1}(A) \leq k\frac{\|v\|}{α_C(v)} \mathcal H^{n-1}(P_v(A)), \] where $P_v$ is the orthogonal projection onto $v^\perp$, $\mathcal H^{n-1}$ denotes normalized Hausdorff outer measure, and $α_C(v)$ is the minimum of $\langleξ,v\rangle$ over unit vectors in the dual cone $C^*$. In particular, every weak antichain $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq\mathcal H^{n-1}(Δ_i(A))$ for each $i$, where $Δ_i(x)=(x_j-x_i)_{j\ne i}$. This proves the skewed projection conjecture of Engel, Mitsis, Pelekis and Reiher. As an application, we recover the bound $\mathcal H^{n-1}(A)\leq kn$ for $k$-antichains in the unit cube under the coordinatewise order.

title: Quantitative Stability and Sample Complexity for Regularized Gromov-Wasserstein Distance
abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance provides a principled framework for comparing two probability distributions supported on different metric spaces by matching their individual intrinsic geometric structures. In practice, the GW distance is estimated from finite samples and often incorporates regularization for statistical and computational tractability. This motivates a quantitative understanding of the stability and estimation error of regularized GW distances. In this work, we study a general family of divergence regularized GW distances, including entropy and Tsallis regularizations over the full range of powers, from a nonasymptotic perspective. Specifically, we establish Lipschitz continuity of the value of regularized GW and H{ö}lder continuity of its optimal coupling under Wasserstein perturbations of the input probability measures. Moreover, we derive the parametric rate of convergence for the empirical regularized (2,2)-GW distance on compactly supported Euclidean spaces.

title: A Safeguarded Accelerated Proximal ADMM Algorithm for Solving Structured Cardinality Penalized Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper considers a class of structured cardinality penalized optimization problems with nonsmooth convex loss functions, for which the proximal mapping associated with the structured $\ell_0$ penalty is generally unavailable. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a chain of exact reformulations based on variable splitting, exact penalization, and continuous relaxation, and establish rigorous equivalence relationships among these resulting models. In particular, we define a class of strong local minimizers for the original problem and show that these minimizers are equivalent to weak $d$-stationary points of the relaxation problem. Further, we propose a safeguarded accelerated proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (SAP-ADMM). We prove that the sequence generated by SAP-ADMM converges to a weak $d$-stationary point of the relaxation problem. Depending on the parameter settings and algorithmic regime, we establish $O(1/k)$ or $o(1/k)$ convergence rates for both the objective function value gap and the KKT residual. Numerical experiments on signal and image denoising demonstrate the effectiveness of both the proposed models and SAP-ADMM in terms of reconstruction quality and computational efficiency.

title: Global Well-Posedness and Persistence of H2 Regularity for the Three-Dimensional Primitive Equations with Horizontal and Topography-Adapted Thermal Diffusion
