For a given sequence of smooth, strongly convex objectives, we use convergence bounds and distances between minimizers to construct a model of the total iteration cost. We derive closed-form two-level budgets for Nesterov's accelerated gradient method and a convex reformulation for multiple levels. We also develop an online switching rule that updates the cost comparison using the gradient at the current point. We test the techniques on a logistic-regression problem using HIGGS data. The online rule reduces weighted iteration cost in all 27 tested configurations, with a median cost of 52.8% of direct optimization. The results illustrate why updating the switching decision can be more effective than fixing the budget from an initial convergence bound.
comment: 30 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to Journal of Global Optimization

title: The Exact Degree Threshold for Complement Connectivity
abstract: For a graph $G$, we investigate sufficient degree conditions under which either $G$ or its complement $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Motivated by a theorem of Hellwig and Volkmann, we introduce the notion of complement connectivity admissible pairs and define the parameter $\mathcal{C}(k)$ as the minimum degree threshold guaranteeing that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected whenever $δ(G)\ge\mathcal{C}(k)$ and $Δ(G)\le |V(G)|-1-\mathcal{C}(k)$. We prove that $\mathcal{C}(k)=2k-2$ for every $k\ge2$, thereby determining the exact degree threshold. As an application, we derive a Nordhaus--Gaddum type product condition, showing that for $n\ge4k-5$, the condition $δ(G)δ(\overline{G}) \ge (2k-3)(n-2k+2)$ guarantees that either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ is $k$-connected. Finally, we show that no analogous product condition depending only on $k$ can exist.

title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $°p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=α\,q(βz+h)+k$ or $p(z)=α\,\bar q(βz+h)+k$ for some $α,β,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|α|=|β|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.

title: Harmonic numbers and Lerch functions behind falling factorial generating functions
abstract: We study a family of special numbers and polynomials introduced by Simsek whose exponential generating function has as denominator a falling factorial in the exponential variable. Using the partial fraction decomposition of this denominator, each member of the family is expressed by a single finite sum involving Bernoulli polynomials, Apostol Bernoulli polynomials and two variable Fubini polynomials evaluated at reciprocals of integers. A second expansion, around the point where the denominator vanishes, expresses the same numbers through Stirling numbers of the second kind and generalized harmonic numbers, and yields closed formulas for the first few members. We construct a function, built from the Hurwitz zeta function and Lerch s transcendent, which interpolates the polynomials at the negative integers and gives a closed form of a multiple series recently introduced by Pokaz, Ribicic Penava and Simsek, we give an Euler type integral representation for it, and show that the numbers are signed combinations of moments of geometric random variables. Recurrence relations, asymptotics and an extension to arbitrary distinct nodes are also given.

title: Parametric Families of Minimal Positive Cubature Formulas of Degrees 4 and 6 on the 2-Sphere
abstract: We study minimal positive cubature formulas on the two-dimensional sphere of degrees four and six, with ten and eighteen nodes, respectively. We prove the regularity of Popov's symmetric formulas and establish that their local families of deformations are two-dimensional, up to rotations. We obtain algebraic relations between the weights and pairwise inner products of the nodes. For degree four, we construct a one-parameter family with half-turn symmetry connecting the formulas of Popov and Heo--Xu. We also give a self-contained proof that eighteen nodes are minimal for degree six.

title: Zero-Crossing Time Lower Bounds for the Homogeneous Super-Twisting Algorithm
abstract: High-frequency switching and chattering are well-known problems in sliding-mode control. Although the super-twisting algorithm produces a continuous control input, the sliding variable may still cross zero repeatedly near the sliding manifold. This paper studies how fast these crossings can occur and whether they can accumulate in finite time for the scalar homogeneous super-twisting algorithm. Two lower bounds on the time required to return to zero are derived, together with a bound on the time needed to complete a full excursion. These results give minimum separation times and upper bounds on the number of crossings associated with excursions above a prescribed amplitude. Although zero crossings may accumulate in finite time, the amplitudes of the complete excursions considered here must vanish and satisfy a summability condition. Thus, crossings associated with excursions above any prescribed nonzero amplitude cannot accumulate in finite time. When the perturbation-rate bound is zero, the estimates recover the scaling imposed by homogeneity. For the classical super-twisting algorithm, the square-root scaling also holds for nonzero perturbation-rate bounds. Numerical simulations illustrate the results.

title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.

title: Representation homology of involutive algebras and hyperoctaherdral homology
abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the (involutive) representation homology of involutive algebras, following the development of representation homology of associative algebra in our earlier papers. Our main motivation is to understand the hyperoctahedral homology of involutive algebras. We show that over a field of characteristic $0$, the hyperoctahedral homology of an involutive algebra is isomorphic (as a graded commutative algebra) to its one dimensional involutive representation homology. This result enables the explicit computation of the hyperoctahedral homology of the universal enveloping algebras of involutive (DG) Lie algebras. For group algebras $k[Γ]$ equipped with the involution $g \mapsto g^{-1}$, we relate the involutive representation homology of $k[Γ]$ to the representation homology of the group $Γ$ with coefficients in $μ_2$, and we show that the latter is the homology of the loop space of the mod $2$ Dold-Thom space of $BΓ$; more generally, we compute the representation homology of $Γ$ with coefficients in an arbitrary diagonalizable group scheme. As a consequence, the hyperoctahedral homology of $k[Γ]$ is concentrated in degree $0$ in characteristic $0$, for every $Γ$.

title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
abstract: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank. We also show that if $E$ has rank $\le 3$ we can replace stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ by stability of $E$ but we cannot do so if $E$ has rank $4$. We also generalize these results to reflexive sheaves on some mildly singular normal complex projective varieties.

title: Polytopal invariance for Lusztig's $q$-weight multiplicities
abstract: Let $Φ$ be an irreducible root system normalized so that long roots have length $\sqrt{2}$, and let $μ\leqλ$ be dominant weights. We associate to $(Φ,μ,λ)$ the convex polytope $$P^Φ_{μ,λ} = (μ+C)\cap(λ-C)\cap(\overline{D}-ρ),$$ where $C=\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}Φ^+$ and $\overline{D}$ is the closed dominant Weyl chamber. We prove that if $P^Φ_{μ,λ}$ and $P^{Φ'}_{μ',λ'}$ are isometric, then $$K^Φ_{λμ}(q)=K^{Φ'}_{λ'μ'}(q),$$ where $K^Φ_{λμ}(q)$ is Lusztig's $q$-analogue of the $μ$-weight multiplicity in the irreducible highest-weight representation $V(λ)$, often called the generalized Kostka-Foulkes polynomial. Moreover, we construct the polynomial directly from the metric shape of the polytope, and we classify when two such polytopes are isometric. Such coincidences are abundant and can occur in different Dynkin types, and in different Dynkin families. By the Lusztig-Kato theorem, the main theorem gives a metric analogue, in the spherical setting, of the combinatorial invariance conjecture for Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials.

title: Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_{2}$ and Gelfand-Tsetlin basis for $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$
abstract: We construct an explicit realization of finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_λ$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$ using the representation theory of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$. We consider $V_λ$ as the evaluation representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})$ and restrict it to the subalgebras $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. Then $V_λ$ is completely reducible as a representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. It allows us to use the explicit formulas for irreducible representations of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$.

title: Solution of a system of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on a network
abstract: We extend the study of Hamilton-Jacobi equations on networks from a single equation to a weakly coupled system of two equations on a star graph, and we develop a numerical scheme for it. Instead of prescribing the boundary values and imposing a junction condition, we compute the solution on each branch from its outer vertex toward the junction and determine the boundary values for which these branchwise solutions agree at the junction. On each branch, we replace the right-hand sides by their cell averages and solve the resulting problems exactly on every cell. This gives an iteration whose limits we compute in closed form. From these limits, the values of the discrete solution at the junction are affine functions of the boundary values on the branch, with a $2 \times 2$ matrix whose rows sum to one and whose determinant factors into explicit contributions of the cells. We use these formulas to characterize the boundary values that give solutions continuous at the junction and monotone on every branch: when the matrices are nonsingular, the admissible boundary values of one branch form a convex polygon, bounded by conditions on the difference of the two components and by positivity conditions, and the boundary values on the other branches follow from them. We also treat the singular case, and we illustrate the results with numerical experiments.

title: Characterizations for quasiconformal weighted Bergman spaces
abstract: We establish characterizations of planar quasiconformal mappings in weighted Bergman spaces $A_α^p(\mathbb D)$. For $p>0$ and $α>-1$, our characterization involves the convergence of certain integrals involving superlevel set areas, the Hausdorff measure of boundary superlevel sets, and the averaged derivative. These include quasiconformal analogues of characterizations established by Karafyllia and Karamanlis for conformal mappings. Moreover, for $-1<α\leq 0$, we obtain an additional equivalent characterization in terms of the Hausdorff measure of level sets. The power $α$ is sharp: for every $α>0$, we construct a bounded $K_α$-quasiconformal mapping for which the weighted level-set length integral with exponent $α+2$ diverges.

title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $τ\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_τg(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty τ_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^τ$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $τ\mapsto T_τ$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_τ$ to the inverse of $τ$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $τ$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^τ$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $τ$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.

title: Bipartite Carrier Compression and Machine-Certified Bounds in Schönhage Trilinear Multiplication Tensors
abstract: Under the conditional framework breaking the longstanding O(n log n) integer multiplication barrier (originating from OpenAI Preprint #109), the asymptotic time complexity exponent T(n) = O(n (log n)^{1-κ}) is governed by bounding the second moment E[X^2] < 1 of recursive branching processes over trilinear tensor carrier graphs. In this work, we present a constructive combinatorial optimization over the alternating carrier bipartite matching graphs of the Schönhage trilinear tensor decomposition at dimensions h=23 and h=25. Through an alternating augmenting path search, we uncover a non-trivial cluster-unlocking cascade that eliminates 185 carrier roles (95 roles in h=23 and 90 roles in h=25), reducing the global physical wire width by 377,890 wires from the reviewed baseline W = 177,284,805 down to W = 176,906,915. Evaluated over the exact 10^{-14} rational grid, this wire reduction certifies an improved second-moment coefficient AB = 5,164,059 / 125,000,000,000 and establishes the sharpened conditional exponent κ= 826,215,307 / 20,000,000,000,000 \approx 4.131076535 \times 10^{-5}, strictly surpassing the preceding record on this architecture (κ\approx 4.123864 \times 10^{-5}). All 47 polynomial constraints and 7 rational security margins are audited in exact Q-arithmetic with zero floating-point error, and the fundamental wire reduction identity is formally verified in the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover without unproven axioms.
comment: 5 pages, self-contained. Lean 4 formal proofs, standalone certificate verifier, and full experimental artifacts openly available at Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23268580

title: Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications
abstract: Let $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $κ_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.

title: Explicit Solutions in a Probabilistic Cellular Automaton Model for Self-Assembled Monolayer Degradation
abstract: Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), formed by the adsorption of a monomolecular layer of adsorbate onto a surface, have emerged as leading candidates for plat- forms for electrochemical biosensors. In order to characterize the working age of a SAM-based biosensor, it is necessary to understand the long-term degradation of the monolayer, with particular emphasis on the intermolecular forces present in the self-assembly process. In this work, discrete- and continuous-time proba- bilistic cellular automaton (PCA) models for the degradation of SAMs involving adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are proposed in which adsorbate molecules desorb at a rate dependent only on the number of adsorbed neighbors. Impor- tantly, we make no assumptions on the relationship between degradation rate and adsorbed neighbors. Using techniques from generating function theory and complex analysis, the expected degradation curve is solved for explicitly in one dimension and shown to be a sigmoid curve related to the Gompertz function.

title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by Gł{\k a}b and Prus-Wiśniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.

title: On the calculation of an integral introduced by Hubert Delange
abstract: In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irréductibles de dénominateur $n$ ou de dénominateur au plus égal à $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{φ(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $φ$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. He was able to evaluate the integral for $q=1$ but stated that ''Malheureusement, nous n'avons pas su jusqu'à présent faire cette évaluation pour $q>1$''. In addition to its intrinsic interest, this calculation would help understand the asymptotic distribution of the $φ(n)$ totatives of $n$ relative to $φ(n)$ equidistributed numbers in $[0,n]$. In this paper, we first provide some general properties of the integral for any $q>1$ and reduce the problem to its calculation for odd square-free integers with at least two distinct prime factors. We then analyse into more detail the case $q=2$ for which we provide a formula that reduces the problem to the evaluation of the fourfold Möbius sum, of integer valued modular sums related to generalized Dedekind sums.

title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperkähler manifolds
abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperkähler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

title: Restricting Odd Antiholes in Critical Graphs via List Coloring
abstract: By the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem, every graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique number contains an odd hole or an odd antihole. We investigate the structure of odd antiholes in critical graphs with fixed maximum degree. We prove that if $G$ is a $k$-critical graph with maximum degree $Δ$ then every odd antihole in $G$ has length at most $2(Δ-k)+7$, and conjecture that, in the odd-hole-free setting, equality forces the graph itself to be the corresponding odd antihole. We verify this extremal characterization when $Δ\geq 2k-5$, extending recent results for $Δ=k$, and construct $k$-critical odd-hole-free graphs showing that the next possible odd antihole length $2(Δ-k)+5$ below the extremal bound can occur. Our proofs use a list-coloring theorem for graphs on $2\ell-1$ vertices whose complements are hypomatchable. This motivates the conjecture that every odd antihole $\overline{C_{2\ell-1}}$ is strongly $\ell$-chromatic-choosable; we show that this conjecture would imply the full extremal characterization. We also obtain degree and attachment restrictions for odd antiholes in critical graphs.

title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
abstract: A classical uniformization theorem of Ahlfors from 1963 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipschitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a large class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
abstract: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone. For every rotational cone of positive slope we construct a smooth embedded rotational end and prove that its profile is the only positive solution of the profile equation with the prescribed slope at infinity. Its angular defect $xu'-u$ is strictly negative, which yields $r$-admissibility, and the profile has a complete asymptotic expansion for $u(x)/x$ in powers of $x^{-(r+1)}$, valid after arbitrary differentiation. The profiles depend real analytically on the slope and, on sufficiently distant exterior regions, foliate the image of the corresponding family. Our main result removes the symmetry assumption: two ends that converge smoothly, with multiplicity one, to the same circular cone coincide outside a compact set. The proof transforms the equation for their difference into an almost-eigenfunction inequality for a drift Laplacian on an auxiliary conical metric and applies Bernstein's asymptotic analysis on weakly conical ends. The argument extends to strictly $r$-admissible cones whose links have constant principal curvatures.

title: An Abresch-Rosenberg type tensor and a gap theorem for CMC hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$
abstract: We construct a symmetric trace-free tensor for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ that extends the Abresch-Rosenberg tensor. Within its natural class, it is characterized by the linearity of its Codazzi defect, and its complete connected zero set consists exactly of the rotational CMC spheres. An exact integrated Simons identity yields explicit gap theorems, valid for every $h>1$ in $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and every $h>(n\int_0^{π/2}\sin^{n-1}r\,dr)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$. We compare the pinching thresholds with the pointwise algebraic level that implies convexity. In $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the explicit pinching conditions imply strict convexity, so there the method gives an independent proof with explicit constants. In $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the pinching region exceeds the convexity level for $n\in\{3,4\}$ and every admissible $h$, and for $n\geq5$ whenever $h^2\geq n/(6(n+2))$; there the gap theorem does not require convexity to be known in advance. We also determine second-order large-$h$ asymptotics of the thresholds.

title: Tight surgeries on torus knots
abstract: We give a complete classification of tight contact structures on manifolds obtained from any surgery along any torus knot, which provides the first such classification on an infinite family of knots. The main tools are the classification of non-loose torus knots, bordered contact invariants via their immersed curve interpretations, and non-thickenable tori in knot complements. As a byproduct of this classification, we also give the first classification of contact structures on some surface bundles over the circle with fibers of genus larger than $1$. The symplectic fillability of these contact structures is also studied and leads to, among other things, the disproof of a conjecture of Ghiggini and Van Horn-Morris on Stein fillability of some contact structures on a Brieskorn sphere.

title: The Path Partition Conjecture and 3-(quasi-)Transitive Digraphs
abstract: A digraph $D = (V,E)$ is 3-transitive (respectively, 3-quasi-transitive) if whenever $(u,v,w,z)$ is a directed path of length 3, $(u,z) \in E$ (respectively, $(u,z) \in E$ or $(z,u) \in E$). These digraphs extend the concepts of transitive and quasi-transitive digraphs, respectively. For 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs, only the strong case has been characterized. In this paper, we introduce the notion of semi-acyclic digraphs and use it to describe completely the structure of 3-transitive and 3-quasi-transitive digraphs. As an application of this type of structure description, we prove that the path partition conjecture holds for the class of extended semi-acyclic digraphs, which generalizes two previously known results on the conjecture.

title: Non-adjacent triples of cells in a triangular grid: proofs of three conjectured generating functions
abstract: Let $\Tn$ be the triangular grid of side $n$, with its $n^2$ unit cells, and let two cells be side-adjacent if they share an edge and point-adjacent if they share a vertex. We count the orbits of $3$-element sets of pairwise non-adjacent cells under the rotation group $C_3$ and under the full symmetry group $D_3$ of $\Tn$. Three of the four resulting sequences are OEIS A397730, A397731 and A397732, for each of which the only formula on record is a generating function conjectured by Sean A.\ Irvine on 14 July 2026. We prove all three conjectures. The route is Burnside's lemma, together with exact lattice counts for each fixed-point term. The side-adjacency graph turns out to be bipartite, so its triangle count vanishes, and the triangles of the point-adjacency graph have a clean structural description, which gives that count too. Along the way we obtain the first explicit closed forms for the three sequences, each a quasi-polynomial of degree $6$ and period $3$, $6$, $3$ respectively. The same machinery settles the fourth member of the family, whose closed form has been recorded at A289230 without proof since 2017, and the labeled count A289224 that feeds it.

title: The $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups
abstract: We say that a group $G$ has the $R_{\infty}$ property if the number $R(\varphi)$ of twisted conjugacy classes is infinite for any automorphism $\varphi$ of $G$. The $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree is the least integer $c$ such that $G/γ_{c+1}(G)$ has property $R_{\infty}$; in case this integer does not exist, we say that $G$ has infinite $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree. In this paper, we determine the $R_{\infty}$-nilpotency degree of some lollipop GBS groups by using different approaches, such as Sylow subgroups, normal forms and presentation of nilpotent quotients, and diagrams of exact sequences. We also compute the $R_\infty$-nilpotency degree of all 2-generated lollipop GBS groups and of all GBS groups whose associated graph is a tree.

title: Strong-type endpoint obstructions for bilinear spherical maximal operators
abstract: For the bilinear spherical averages in dimension $d\geq2$, we show that the lacunary maximal operator is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ whenever $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1/r=1+1/q$. The obstruction is realized by fixed nonnegative inputs; a second construction proves quantitative failure on smooth compactly supported functions and finitely many dyadic scales. The same conclusions hold for the full maximal operator. We give a sharp Lorentz-index criterion in the range $q>d/(d-1)$ and extend the negative result to all multilinear spherical maximal operators with an $L^1$ input. We indicate the precise strong-type boundary statements to which these conclusions apply, without drawing conclusions about separate weak-type or interior estimates.

title: A Functorial Classification of Toric Stacks
abstract: Toric stacks enrich the study of toric varieties by accounting for quotients of actions of diagonalizable groups. In practice, toric stacks are constructed and understood via "stacky fans" generalizing the fans appearing in toric geometry. Previous attempts to make this construction into an equivalence of categories have either run into crucial errors or have been restricted to special cases (e.g. only considering separated Deligne-Mumford stacks). In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a new 2-category $\mathsf{StkFan}$ of stacky fans and constructing an equivalence of 2-categories between $\mathsf{StkFan}$ and a 2-category $\mathsf{TStk}$ of toric stacks. Along the way, we develop a theory of "toric categories" which categorifies the classical theory of toric monoids. We also explain how working with toric categories provides a simple axiomatic framework for Gale duality.

title: Global Convergence and Reliable Stopping in a Safeguarded Modified Anderson--Björck Method
abstract: The modified Anderson-Bjorck (modAB) method was first proposed in 2023 by Ganchovski and Traykov for solving nonlinear equations in structural mechanics. It was improved further in 2026 by introducing better switching criteria with account to function symmetry, and bisection fallback based on measuring the bracket reduction rate. Although the algorithm demonstrated superior performance across a great variety of functions, it lacked formal mathematical analysis and proof of convergence. In addition, some discrepancies were noted by L. Tomov in the latest version that need to be addressed: premature application of the Anderson-Bjorck (AB) correction on the first AB step, caused by retaining the endpoint-update record from the preceding bisection step, and using the corrected endpoint ordinates in symmetry factor calculation instead of the true residuals. The purpose of the present paper is to provide rigorous mathematical proof of global convergence in exact arithmetic, remove the above discrepancies, and provide floating-point safeguards for interpolation, switching and stopping, with explicit treatment of infinite and NaN values, underflow, overflow and round-off errors. These safeguards do not certify the accuracy of the supplied function values. Additional performance improvement was introduced by allowing for early bisection fallback when AB fails to make progress on reducing either the bracket width or the residual, while retaining a finite bound on consecutive exceptions to the prescribed width condition.

title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
abstract: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

title: Categorifying Quantum Spin Systems
abstract: We develop a homotopical framework for understanding the space of quantum spin systems based on topological $n$-nets, which assign associative unital algebras to local regions in an $n$-dimensional space in a manner that captures the locality structure of the underlying lattice theories. The net-theoretic perspective admits a natural categorification, in which the category of topological $n$-nets carries the structure of a higher Morita category. Moreover, the nets of greatest physical interest form a Karoubi-complete subcategory that shares many of the characteristic structural features of the category of finite TQFTs. Our main result identifies the group of locality-preserving symmetries of (3+1)-dimensional quantum spin systems (i.e. quantum cellular automata modulo stabilization, finite-depth quantum circuits, and translations) with the full Witt group of nondegenerate braided fusion categories, thereby answering a question posed by Haah.

title: Intrinsic Contraction Theory and Stabilization of Probability Measures on the Wasserstein Space
abstract: Deterministic flows can contract Wasserstein distances between probability laws without being contractive in point-state space. We develop a differential contraction theory for pushforward flows on forward-invariant subsets of the 2-Wasserstein space that quotients out the gauge freedom of the continuity equation. Weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition and the Wasserstein contingent cone define the weighted horizontal tangent cone (whtc). Requiring the contraction quadratic form to be nonpositive only on the whtc yields the Intrinsic Wasserstein Contraction Condition (IWCC), which generalizes the classical contraction LMI and recovers it on Dirac measures. An almost-everywhere Euler approximation based on the superposition principle and Banach-valued Lebesgue differentiation theorem proves that IWCC is sufficient for intrinsic Wasserstein contraction. Law contraction without point-state contraction is illustrated by a rotationally symmetric shear example. Finally, a new comparison lemma yields an incremental Wasserstein ISS theorem; for Brockett's integrator, we prove exponential stabilization of a class of axisymmetric laws to the uniform law on a circle via a smooth feedback.
comment: 17 pages. Submitted to the IEEE in August 2026 for possible publication

title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
abstract: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and Járai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. Járai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$, using the transience of random walk. We prove, using a different method, that avalanches are also finite for $d=2$.

title: The Tate Conjecture for Ordinary Calabi-Yau Threefolds
abstract: We use the theory of canonical lifts to prove the integral geometric Tate conjecture for ordinary Calabi-Yau threefolds over finite fields, and also for divisor classes on certain ordinary Calabi-Yau varieties.

title: A Riesz-Map Preconditioned Extragradient Method for Price Formation in Mean Field Games
abstract: We develop and analyze a projected extragradient method, preconditioned by a Riesz map, for a first-order price-formation mean field game in one space dimension. The model couples Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and transport equations through a global market-clearing constraint. Finite propagation justifies truncating the first-order transport equation to a bounded interval. A monotone weak formulation incorporates the mixed initial--terminal data. Its Riesz map uses $L^2$ norms for density and price directions and a space-time $H^1$ norm for value-function directions, preconditioning the residual without adding higher-order regularization terms to the MFG equations. A density-only argument rules out cocoercivity on the localized admissible set in every equivalent Hilbert metric, motivating extragradient updates. For $H(x,p)=p^2/2$, we use a monotone upwind discretization with adjoint-consistent transport and a state-constraint boundary closure. We establish a mesh-independent Lipschitz bound on bounded convex admissible sets with uniform density, slope, and price bounds. With exact metric projection onto these sets, the iteration converges to a solution of the discrete variational inequality on each fixed grid, with an admissible step-size threshold independent of both mesh sizes. Convergence under mesh refinement is not proved. On a quadratic benchmark, all reported runs reach the stopping tolerance with one fixed step size across a factor-of-16 reduction in both mesh sizes. Price errors and value-function errors measured away from low-density regions decay approximately at first order under refinement, while density errors decrease more slowly.

title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
abstract: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight strong-generation induction and $C_2$-cofiniteness, semisimple descent for a full corner of Zhu's algebra, modular Galois symmetry, and holomorphic $E_8$ extensions.
comment: Initial announcement. A full manuscript with complete details is forthcoming and will replace this announcement. The working manuscript and certificates are available at https://github.com/Doctorfm98/Haagerup_VOA . AI was used extensively in the discovery, and the author welcomes community feedback on the presentation and appropriate attribution

title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
abstract: The expressivity of a neural network $Φ$ describes the class of functions that a network can express. The term topological expressivity refers to a family of measures particularly suited to understand binary classification and is often formulated in terms of the Betti numbers of a decision boundary $β(Φ^{-1}(0))$. Despite its popularity, this measure is not as useful for regression and other problems that do not involve a decision boundary. Instead, we propose to study topological expressivity in terms of the Betti numbers of the output of a neural network $β(Φ(X))$. We formally prove that a ReLU network with architecture $(d,\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d } β_k(3k+2),\sum\limits_{k=1}^{d}β_k(k+1))$ can express spaces homotopy equivalent to wedge sums of spheres with arbitrary Betti numbers. This gives upper bounds for any arbitrary connected ($β_0=1$) sequence of Betti numbers, but by constructing spaces homotopy equivalent to products of $N$ spheres of dimension $d_1,...,d_N$ we achieve much better bounds $(\sum\limits_{n=1} d_n, 3\sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + 2N, \sum\limits_{n=1}\limits^N d_n + N) $ for Betti numbers given by $\prod_n (1+x^{d_n})$. Finally we conjecture a much stronger tight bound which gives the architectural bound $(d,d+1,d+1)$ for a space homeomorphic to the sphere.

title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
abstract: The main result is an obstruction to the presence of contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension. As a first application, we prove a 5-dimensional analogue (under stronger assumptions) of a Reeb stability theorem for confoliations in dimension 3 due to Eliashberg and Thurston. Refining work of the first author with Cardona, we further give two new notions of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension generalizing the 3-dimensional notion of Eliashberg-Thurston. As a second application of our main theorem, we then give an example, in any ambient odd dimension, of a c-symplectic (and in fact strong symplectic) foliation that cannot be contact approximated, in either of these two senses. This relies on the property, of independent interest, that contact structures approximating (in these senses) a weakly c-symplectic confoliation are also weakly fillable. The proofs of all these statements rely on pseudo-holomorphic curve theory. Lastly, we describe several natural classes of examples of these types of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations.

title: An Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients
abstract: We give an exposition of a proof, discovered by Astra, of an Aleksandrov estimate for kinetic equations with rough coefficients. We explain this method in the simpler elliptic and parabolic settings as well.
comment: This work is part of the "We need ABP'' project; see https://weneedabp.github.io/

title: An Infinite Family of Apéry-like Recurrences for Euler's Constant
abstract: Euler's constant $γ$, also known as the Euler-Mascheroni constant, remains one of the most elusive constants in mathematics. Despite extensive study, its irrationality is still unproven, and Apéry-like approximations of it are remarkably scarce. We present a novel identity that expresses $γ$ in terms of a Meijer G-function and its first few derivatives. This identity is then generalized and used to systematically generate infinitely many Apéry-like approximations of $γ$ using a Conservative Matrix Field construction based on the Meijer G-function.

title: Markov Chain Convergence in Kernel-Induced Geometry
abstract: We study the convergence of Markov chains in the geometry induced by Hilbertian embeddings associated with positive definite kernels, also called Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). Under a contraction assumption in the kernel-induced geometry, and a standard spectral gap assumption, we establish non-asymptotic, high-probability bounds for the convergence of the empirical occupation measure to the invariant measure. The obtained bounds separate the roles of the two conditions: the spectral gap determines the effective sample size in the leading term, while the kernel contraction enters only through a linear correction. As an application, we study one-step prediction of dynamical systems from a single trajectory, deriving fast learning rates for a nonlinear least-squares estimator. The rates highlight the interplay between mixing properties in the kernel-induced geometry and the classical source and capacity conditions used in the analysis of least-squares.

title: The Bernstein problem in higher dimensional Heisenberg groups
abstract: In every sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group $\mathbb H^n$, with $n\geq 2$, we prove the existence of a global perimeter minimizer whose boundary is a smooth, non-characteristic, entire intrinsic graph but it is not a vertical hyperplane.

title: Fundamental Limits of Covert queueing under Busy-Period Observations
abstract: Consider a queueing system operated by Bob, which is intended to serve only jobs generated by a legitimate user, Willie. Willie's jobs arrive according to a Poisson process, and the service times are exponentially distributed. Bob seeks to covertly serve additional jobs arriving according to an independent Poisson process, without Willie detecting their presence. As the legitimate user, Willie is provided with certain statistics of each busy period by Bob. In particular, we consider two statistics: (i) the number of jobs served during each busy period and (ii) the duration of each busy period. We establish that, under either statistic, the maximum expected number of additional jobs that Bob can covertly serve obeys a square-root law. Specifically, over n busy periods, Bob can covertly serve additional jobs in the order of square root of n, whereas any scaling which is above square root of n enables Willie to asymptotically detect the presence of these additional jobs with vanishing error probability. Furthermore, we characterize the scaling constant associated with the square-root law, which we refer to as the covert queueing constant, for each of the two statistics. We compare the scaling constants corresponding to the two statistics and argue that the scaling constant under statistic (i) is no greater than that under statistic (ii).

title: Counting with Hiccup Sequences
abstract: The $(0,x,1,2)$-hiccup sequence starts at $x$ and increases by 1 when the current index has already appeared as a value, and by 2 otherwise. We prove directly that for $x\geq3$ the gaps between its missing values are $1,2,3,\ldots$, each repeated $x-2$ times, and we derive closed formulas, an explicit error bound, and a generating function in terms of Ramanujan's theta functions. The counting functions of the complements satisfy nested recurrences. The sequences of missing values are the partial complements of polygonal numbers. In particular, the $(x-2)$-fold composition of the enumeration of the positive integers that are not $x$-gonal is the hiccup sequence minus 1. We extend the nested recurrence and a tree interpretation to every miss increment $z\geq2$ and every initial value $x\geq2$. Further interpretations involve polyomino vertices, monochromatic pairs, and, by a theorem of Bickle, Ramsey core numbers.

title: Fast and Stable Arbitrary Precision Approximate Matrix Multiplication
abstract: We present several new and surprising results on the theory and practice of Arbitrary Precision Approximate (APA) matrix multiplication, which refers to algorithms that output merely approximations to matrix multiplication even in exact arithmetic. While APA algorithms have been around for nearly half a century, and despite the fact that they have potentially lower (asymptotic) cost than many fast exact matrix multiplication schemes, they have not been studied as closely, to the extent that relatively little is known about their numerical properties. In this paper, we shine a spotlight on these algorithms by presenting three important results. First, we provide a new search algorithm for APA routines that is easy to use, automatically generates encoding matrices with functional entries, and can match or beat the best known APA algorithms for several sizes. In particular, we improve the upper bound on the border rank of $\langle 2,4,5 \rangle$ matrix multiplication. Second, we combine this insight with alternative bases to minimize the number of additions in an APA algorithm, thereby improving its leading coefficient. Finally, we prove the same kind of stability that characterizes fast exact matrix multiplication for an algorithm of Bini [Calcolo 1980] that computes an exact product of two matrices using a modified APA scheme (with or without alternative bases).

title: Property $R_\infty$ for Artin and Coxeter groups whose outer automorphisms are length-preserving
abstract: We prove that every length-preserving automorphism of a nonspherical Artin or Coxeter group has infinite Reidemeister number. As a consequence, we establish property $R_\infty$ for large-type free-of-infinity Artin groups, infinite strongly rigid Coxeter groups, and infinite virtually abelian Coxeter groups, including all affine Coxeter groups. We also prove that the automorphism group of every infinite irreducible non-affine strongly rigid Coxeter group is acylindrically hyperbolic.

title: The Inviscid Limit in Uniformly Local Yudovich Spaces
abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes and Euler equations with the velocity in $L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and the vorticity in the uniformly local Yudovich space $Y^θ_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $θ$ grows sufficiently slowly, then for every $T>0$, solutions of the Navier-Stokes equation converge to solutions of the Euler equation in $L^{\infty}([0,T];L^2_{ul}(\mathbb{R}^2))$ as $ν\to 0^+$, provided they are generated from the same initial data.

title: A Lean Formalization of the Hamilton--Perelman Proof of Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
abstract: We formalize the Hamilton--Perelman Ricci-flow proof of Thurston's geometrization conjecture. The public Lean declaration is reproduced in this paper. Its geometric interpretation follows, and verification is recorded in 4.

title: Counterexamples to Minkowski-type inequalities and the Rees converse for modules via mixed Buchsbaum-Rim Multiplicities
abstract: In this paper, we explore mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities of finite-colength submodules of free modules over Noetherian local rings. We extend the Hilbert-polynomial construction to submodules in arbitrary homogeneous degrees and prove a product formula for the resulting coefficients. We then examine module analogues of Teissier's coefficient inequalities and the Minkowski inequality. Explicit examples show that the coefficientwise power inequalities, log-convexity, and the product-root inequality can all fail; several failures occur over regular local rings. We also prove that equality of integral closures forces equality of all mixed Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicities, while a one-dimensional example shows that the converse fails for arbitrary modules. A converse is recovered when the module closures are the integral closures of modules of the form $IF$ for $\mathfrak m$-primary ideals $I$. The general converse problem in dimension at least two is stated at the end.

title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.

title: Ground states and sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for logarithmic Schrödinger equations with partial confinement
abstract: We study the logarithmic Schrödinger equation with an arbitrary positive semidefinite quadratic potential and a periodic potential in the unconfined directions. The main variational difficulty is to turn a constrained minimizer into a critical point when the energy is extended-valued and not of class $C^1$ on the natural Hilbert space. We establish an abstract principle for convex lower semicontinuous energies with a smooth perturbation, allowing a scaling law for the full energy without requiring homogeneity of its convex part. Combined with a profile decomposition under integer translations, this principle yields a positive ground state for every rank of the quadratic form. When the periodic potential vanishes, we prove a sharp anisotropic logarithmic Sobolev inequality, determine its optimal constant and all equality cases, and classify positive ground states as explicit anisotropic Gaussons, unique up to translations along the kernel of the quadratic form. When the periodic component is constant, we also establish existence and classify all normalized ground states at every prescribed positive mass, with explicit formulas for the minimum energy and the associated Lagrange multiplier.

title: Unranking $S$-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets
abstract: Given a finite family of combinatorial objects with a total order, ranking asks for the position of a given object, and unranking asks for the object occupying a given position. Both provide algorithmic access to families too large to enumerate. Kagey gave a polynomial-time algorithm for several position-restricted families and left open the case of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations. We show that when $|S| = 2$, the graph of forbidden squares is $2$-regular, a disjoint union of cycles, and that fixing a prefix leaves only paths and untouched cycles. This yields polynomial-time prefix counting, ranking and unranking for every two-element set of offsets, covering $\{-1,1\}$. The same structure gives a short proof that the number of $\{-1,1\}$-avoiding permutations equals the $n$-th ménage number for odd $n$ and exceeds it by $2$ for even $n$, proving a conjecture recorded in the OEIS entry A354152.

title: Necessary conditions for benchmarking next-generation AI in materials discovery
abstract: Current AI predicts materials by speeding up energy minimisation and training on large databases. However, scaling data generation prevents manual analysis by domain experts. If novelty is evaluated by chemical compositions or traditional representations in Crystallographic Information Files, or standard structure matchers based on manually chosen thresholds, one can easily generate millions of ``new'' compositions or files without discovering truly novel materials. This paper uses a hierarchy of crystal invariants to continuously trace and quantify structural novelty based on the new mathematical definition of a crystal structure and asymptotic guarantees for invariant descriptors. The invariant-based analysis through cascade computations on a modest computer exposes the unexpected scale of duplication in the world's largest materials databases, shown here in the high-profile case of GNoME datasets. To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.

title: Interacting Stochastic Systems with Agent-Based Sampling and Connection-Based Reinforcement
abstract: We introduce a general class of interacting reinforced stochastic systems evolving on a network. The dynamics are governed by two distinct interaction structures: a sampling network, which determines how information is acquired, and a reinforcement network, which determines how the sampled information influences future evolution. Processes generate Bernoulli observations through preferential, de-preferential, or mixed sampling, while observations are transmitted through an edge-dependent affine reinforcement mechanism. We formulate the dynamics as a stochastic approximation scheme and study their asymptotic behaviour. We establish sufficient conditions for almost sure convergence to a deterministic limit and, when the sampling and reinforcement graphs coincide, derive graph-theoretic criteria involving odd cycles, mixed-sampling vertices, and subcritical reinforcement. Under additional structural assumptions, we establish almost sure convergence and partial synchronization in a random-limit regime. In the deterministic regime, we also prove a law of the iterated logarithm and a central limit theorem under suitable spectral and regularity conditions. Finally, we show how the framework encompasses interacting urn models with edge-dependent reinforcement, urns with memory, and random walks with memory.

title: Existence and large-field asymptotics of Hopfions in a continuum model of frustrated magnets
abstract: We study a continuum model of frustrated magnetism that supports particle-like field configurations with nontrivial Hopf index. The energy functional combines competing second and first order exchange interactions with a stabilizing external magnetic field and gives rise to a variational problem for maps from three-dimensional space into the two-sphere. We prove the existence of energy minimizers in infinitely many nontrivial homotopy classes. We further establish the existence of a unit-charge Hopfion in the regime of strong external fields. Finally, we analyze the corresponding large-field limit, identify the natural concentration scale, and prove strong convergence of suitably rescaled minimizers to a minimizer of a limiting variational problem.

title: Best proximity point results of operator type condensing mappings via measure of noncompactness and application to an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$
abstract: We propose a new class of cyclic (noncyclic) operator type condensing mappings and establish conditions that guarantee the existence of best proximity points (pairs) using measure of noncompactness. The results obtained are further applied to investigate the optimum solution of an infinite system of differential equations in $c_0$ and $\ell_1$.

title: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
abstract: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.

title: Sharp Robertson-type coefficient estimates for radial starlike and quasi-convex of type B mappings of order α in complex Banach spaces
abstract: In this paper, we study biholomorphic mappings $F: \mathbb{B} \to X$ of the form $F(z) = f(z)z$ for $z \in \mathbb{B}$, where $f: \mathbb{B} \to \mathbb{C}$ is a holomorphic function satisfying $f(0) = 1$. Our main contributions are as follows: We establish sharp estimates for the coefficients of starlike functions of order $α$ as well as quasi-convex functions of type $B$ and order $α$ by employing the notion of majorization. The results established here directly extend the results due to Robertson \cite{Robertson-1936} to the broader setting of complex Banach spaces.

title: Characterizing higher-dimensional Hölder domains via spherical geometric functions
abstract: In this paper we characterize the regularity of a domain in terms of the behavior of a certain spherical function. More precisely, given two domains we show that a certain spherical spectral function (first defined in \cite{FTV23}, see also \cite{AKN21}) has Hölder decay if and only if the domains are complementary and separated by a $C^{1,β}$-manifold. This extends the analysis in \cite{Ca24} to dimensions $\geq 3$ and in \cite{FTV23, CTV25} to regularity above the continuous threshold. Along the way, we introduce a spherical analogue of the Jones $β$-numbers and show that the decay of these numbers implies geometric regularity of the domain on which they are defined. We believe this result is of independent interest and partially addresses a question of Fleschler-Tolsa-Villa \cite[Question 1]{FTV23}.
comment: 32 pages, 9 figures; no use of AI (except to make pictures)

title: On Divisor Function Polynomials and Dirichlet Series
abstract: We find the Dirichlet series and convergence bounds for the counting function of sum systems (collections of sets of non-negative integers whose Minkowski sum is an arithmetic progression). This motivates the definition and study of divisor function polynomials, which are generating functions for the non-trivial divisor function and for the balanced divisor function that counts, up to a sign, non-trivial ordered factorisations into squarefree factors. These divisor function polynomials turn out to be intimately connected between each other and with Bernoulli numbers and ordered Bell polynomials.

title: Degree similar and net-degree similar signed graphs
abstract: Two graphs are degree similar if their adjacency matrices and their degree matrices are simultaneously similar, a notion recently introduced by Godsil and Sun. We extend it to signed graphs in two ways, degree similarity and net-degree similarity, according to whether the degree or the net-degree matrix is used. We prove that signed trees are determined by their degree similarity class, but not by their net-degree similarity class. We then develop constructions of (net-)degree similar signed graphs, based on a signed version of Godsil--McKay switching, on partial transposition and on block extensions. As a byproduct, we obtain infinite families both of pairs of net-degree similar unicyclic signed graphs with non-isomorphic underlying graphs, and of unicyclic signed graphs, not necessarily regular, which are not determined by their degree similarity class. This settles the net-degree version of a problem of Godsil and Sun on unicyclic graphs.

title: Clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers: spectral bounds and anticodes
abstract: Using spectral and polynomial methods, we show several sharp spectral bounds for the clique and chromatic numbers of graph powers that only use spectral information from the original graph. In particular, we strengthen earlier spectral-radius estimates to obtain an asymptotically sharp colouring bound for general graph powers, and prove a sharp bound for powers of line graphs with a complete characterisation of equality. We also develop polynomial methods yielding upper and lower bounds for clique numbers of graph powers. Regarding the connection between the clique and coloring parameters of graph powers, we propose a spectral analogue of Wegner's conjecture, determine the extremal values for graph squares, and establish the conjecture for all powers when the spectral-radius bound is sufficiently small. Finally, we connect our spectral polynomial method with coding theory: we prove that for distance-regular graphs, optimisation over the adjacency algebra recovers Delsarte's linear programming bound for anticodes.

title: Weighted, GIT and Néron--Tate heights on genus-two moduli and Jacobians
abstract: We compare three heights attached to a curve of genus two: the weighted height of its Igusa--Clebsch invariants, the GIT height of a binary sextic defining it, and the Néron--Tate height on its Jacobian. For a morphism from an abelian variety to a weighted projective space we define a weighted Néron--Tate height and show that the weighted height differs from it by a linear form and a bounded function; the linear form vanishes when inversion is induced by an automorphism of the weighted projective space. For binary sextics we prove the explicit inequality $h_{\inv}\le h_{\text{GIT}} + \frac{1}{2} \log 302$, with nonnegative local differences at the finite places that vanish at places of good reduction. We then construct a family of semistable binary sextics over $E\times E$, where $E:y^2=x^3-2$, whose relative Jacobian carries a section of infinite order, and we show that the Jacobian over the base point is absolutely simple. Along every curve in the parameter space through the base point, the Néron--Tate height of the section is a positive multiple of the weighted moduli height up to an error of square-root size, and up to a bounded error when the curve is rational. As applications, we obtain explicit families of genus-two Jacobians of positive rank over $\mathbf{Q}$, an infinite congruence lattice of fibres of positive height, and canonical-limit formulas along elliptic curves in $E\times E$.

title: A counterexample to Nirenberg's conjecture on closed asymptotic curves
abstract: We construct a smooth embedded annulus in Euclidean 3-space with negative Gauss curvature in its interior whose boundary consists of strictly convex curves in planes tangent to the annulus, and which contains closed asymptotic curves. This gives a counterexample to a 1962 conjecture of Nirenberg. The construction is based on Lelieuvre's formula, which yields a closed curve that is then realized as an asymptotic curve on a ruled annulus. The second asymptotic curve is obtained from a periodic solution of a Riccati equation.
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures. Minor changes to improve the exposition and graphics

title: A Network Simplex Framework For Discrete Unbalanced Optimal Transport
abstract: The network simplex method is a classical algorithm for minimum cost flow problems formulated as linear programs, that has attracted recent interest from the optimal transport community. Indeed, discrete optimal transport is a subclass of minimum cost flow for which network simplex techniques compute exact solutions while leveraging the inherent problem sparsity. However, extending these approaches to other, nonlinear optimal transport formulations has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this paper, we adapt the network simplex algorithm to unbalanced optimal transport. Our proposed framework is applicable to various unbalanced formulations, and can be implemented explicitly in the most common cases, including semi-unbalanced optimal transport. The resulting algorithms are memory-efficient, and perform competitively with existing approaches, as shown by our experiments on a range of transport and barycenter calculations.

title: On diagonal sections of Markov products of copulas
abstract: Given a bivariate copula $C$, the bivariate copula $Ψ(C)$ is defined as the Markov product of $C^T$ and $C$. In this paper we consider the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$ under the additional assumption that its value at a single point is known. We determine the exact upper and lower bounds for the diagonal section of $Ψ(C)$, given that $Ψ(C)(a,a)=d \in [a^2,a]$, where $a \in [0,1]$ is a fixed point. Furthermore, we describe some additional properties of the transformation $Ψ$, such as its behavior under ordinal sums and the survival operation. We also study checkerboard copulas in the range of $Ψ$ and matrices associated to them.

title: Dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for $\mathbb R^2$-valued polynomials
abstract: We prove a dimension-free Markov--Bernstein-type inequality for polynomial mappings $(f_1,f_2)\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^2$ of degree at most $d$. For product probability measures whose one-dimensional marginals have densities bounded by $1$, we obtain a lower bound for the integral of the Gram determinant of $\nabla f_1$ and $\nabla f_2$ in terms of the Gram determinant of the $d$-th derivative tensors $D^df_1$ and $D^df_2$, with a constant depending only on $d$. For pairs in a fixed Wiener chaos, the resulting Gaussian inequality answers a question of Nourdin, Nualart, and Poly concerning a lower bound for the expectation of the Malliavin determinant in terms of the determinant of the covariance matrix.

title: Geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble
abstract: We study the geometry of semi-infinite geodesics in the Airy line ensemble. We establish sharp estimates for disjointness probabilities involving geodesics with nearby directions and endpoints in the top line of the Airy line ensemble. Moreover, we obtain a power law upper bound on the coalescence depth of two semi-infinite geodesics with same asymptotic direction and establish exponential concentration estimates for geodesic jump times more generally. We also establish pathwise Hölder $1/2^-$-continuity of Busemann profiles associated to semi-infinite geodesics with common asymptotic directions (in terms of the asymptotic direction). We characterize exceptional behaviour of semi-infinite geodesics through their Busemann profiles and establish geometric properties of the associated sets of non-coalescence and non-uniqueness. Finally, we determine the Hausdorff dimensions of collections of semi-infinite geodesics: collections with a fixed top-line endpoint and arbitrary positive asymptotic direction almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $1$, while collections with a fixed positive direction and arbitrary endpoint almost surely have Hausdorff dimension $3/2$.

title: Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces in rearrangement-invariant and Hardy spaces
abstract: In 1981, Bourgain, Rosenthal, and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1 < p < \infty$, $p \neq 2$. We extend their construction to rearrangement-invariant spaces and Hardy spaces. For any separable rearrangement-invariant space $X$ with non-trivial Boyd indices, we show that these subspaces are complemented, previously obtained by Ghawadrah via a different argument, and establish the following dichotomy: Either one can extract an uncountable family of pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces, or they are all isomorphic to $X$. To this end, we introduce an ordinal index that detects whether $X$ embeds complementably into an arbitrary separable Banach space. On the other hand, we give sufficient conditions which imply that in certain spaces close to $L_1$ and $H^1$, these subspaces fail to be complemented.

title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.

title: Monodromy of Tate-Linear varieties
abstract: We answer a question of Chai about the rigidity of Tate-linear subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$: we show that that a smooth subvariety of a central leaf of $\mathcal{A}_g$ which is Tate-linear at one point is Tate-linear at every point. This is achieved by a careful analysis of the $p$-adic monodromy groups of Tate-linear varieties, building on recent work of D'Addezio and van Hoften.

title: Counting cographs in locally dense graphs
abstract: An $n$-vertex graph $G$ is $(ρ, d)$-dense if for all $U \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $ρn$, the induced subgraph $G[U]$ contains at least $\frac{d}{2}|U|^2$ edges. In 2010, partly motivated by the theory of quasirandomness, Kohayakawa, Nagle, Rödl, and Schacht conjectured that, for any fixed graph $F$, the number of homomorphic copies of $F$ in a given $n$-vertex $(o(1),d)$-dense graph is at least $(1-o(1))d^{e(F)}n^{v(F)}$. Despite considerable effort, only a few graphs are known to satisfy the conjecture. We find a new broad class of graphs that satisfy the conjecture, including cographs.

title: Two-orbit right-angled Polytopes and Hypertopes
abstract: Abstract polytopes and hypertopes are thin and residually-connected incidence geometries or, equivalently, chamber systems. Their degree of regularity is understood by looking at the action of their automorphism group on the set of their chambers. When this action has only one orbit, they are called regular. In this article, we are interested in polytopes and hypertopes with exactly two orbits on their chambers. Let $I = \{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. For any $J\subsetneq I$ with $|I| \geq 3$, we show that there exists a class $2_J$ two-orbit hypertope whose diagram is any graph on $|I|$ vertices, with edges all labeled by $\infty$. In order to do so, we first establish a general framework for constructing hypertopes as quotient of chamber systems, and then exploit the machinery of acylindrically hyperbolic groups for showing that this framework can be used to create two-orbit polytopes and hypertopes of class $2_J$. Note that all polytopes and hypertopes constructed in this paper are infinite.

title: Existence and uniqueness of bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
abstract: Standing waves $e^{iωt}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves a nonlinear elliptic ODE of the form $Δu+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation, on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and nonlinearities $f$. Under mild assumptions, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

title: Warm-IP: A Path-Following ADMM Warm Start for Interior-Point Quadratic Programming
abstract: Interior-point (IP) methods are powerful second-order optimization algorithms but can make slow progress during early iterations. We propose Warm-IP, a hybrid framework that combines a path-following variant of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with a primal--dual IP method. The ADMM phase generates a warm start that remains close to the central path, enabling the subsequent IP phase to rapidly refine the solution to high accuracy. We evaluate Warm-IP on a diverse collection of real-world and synthetic quadratic programming (QP) instances and compare it with leading commercial solvers (MOSEK and Gurobi) and open-source solvers (Clarabel, PIQP, and OSQP). We also curate and release a new benchmark of large-scale QPs from cancer radiotherapy treatment planning, built from real patient data and provided in canonical QP form, with instances containing hundreds of thousands of constraints. Warm-IP substantially outperforms existing solvers on large-scale problems. On the large-scale radiotherapy benchmark comprising 60 lung cancer cases, for example, Warm-IP solves an instance in 47 seconds on average with no failures, while the strongest competitors, MOSEK and Gurobi, average 55 seconds with failures on 23\% of the cases and roughly 240 seconds with no failures, respectively. To support reproducibility and future benchmarking, we publicly release the implementation and benchmark data through a \href{https://github.com/Radiotherapy-Optimization/Warm-IP}{GitHub repository}. These results demonstrate that appropriately warm-started IP methods can combine the rapid initial progress of first-order methods with the high-accuracy convergence of second-order methods.

title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
abstract: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.
comment: 9 figures, 3 tables. Code available at https://github.com/bydeng01/linpde-gp

title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic à la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic à la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic à la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

title: Linearity of Graph Manifold Groups
