The proof combines a global elliptic estimate obtained by Sobolev truncation with strict perturbations of one-dimensional comparison profiles.

title: Global Well-Posedness and Energy Decay for an Abstract Viscoelastic Wave Equation with Nonlocal or Friction Damping
abstract: This paper investigates an abstract viscoelastic wave equation in a separable Hilbert space, in which the damping term depends on a power of the velocity norm. Depending on whether the power exponent is zero or nonzero, this damping corresponds to friction damping or nonlocal damping, respectively; the equation also contains a viscoelastic damping represented by an integral term with a relaxation function. We establish global well-posedness for initial data in \(\mathcal{H}_1\) by combining monotone operator theory with the Faedo--Galerkin method, and prove uniqueness for all exponents greater than \(-1\), with the singular range between \(-1\) and \(0\) handled through the monotonicity rather than the Lipschitz continuity of the nonlocal damping operator. We then study the long-time behavior of the energy via integral inequalities, multiplier techniques, and Nakao's method, and obtain explicit decay estimates showing that the energy decays exponentially in the friction case and polynomially in the nonlocal case. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to consider the combined effects of viscoelastic damping and nonlocal damping in such an abstract framework, and it is also the first to analyze nonlocal damping with negative exponents.

title: Derived plethystic algebra
abstract: We prove comparison results about $\infty$-categories of derived commutative rings with extra algebraic structure. For example, we show that several notions of derived $δ$-rings agree and obtain similar results for derived $λ$-rings, derived binomial rings, and derived Boolean rings. Our comparison results apply more generally to modules over a specific kind of monad on derived rings that we call derived plethory.

title: Precise propagation rates of the fractional Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries
abstract: In this paper, we determine the propagation rates of the Fisher-KPP equation with free boundaries and fractional diffusion $(-Δ)^s$ $(0<s<1)$, which was considered in \cite{CDN26} as a model for species spreading, where the density function $u(t,x)$ satisfies the fractional Fisher-KPP equation $u_t+(-Δ)^su=f(u)$ over a one-dimensional spatial domain $(g(t), h(t))$, representing the expanding population range, with $x=g(t)$ and $x=h(t)$ the free boundaries. It was shown in \cite{CDN26} that the model is well-posed, and its long-time dynamics exhibits a spreading-vanishing dichotomy. We show in this paper that, when spreading occurs, \[ \begin{cases} \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t^{1/(2s)}} =\left(\frac{2^{1-2s}μ}{1-2s}\right)^{1/(2s)} & \mbox{ if $s\in(0,1/2)$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t\ln t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t\ln t} =μ& \mbox{ if $s=1/2$,}\\[2mm] \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{h(t)}{t} =\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{-g(t)}{t} =c_0(s) & \mbox{ if $s\in(1/2,1)$}, \end{cases} \] where $c_0(s)\in (0,\infty)$ is uniquely determined by the associated semi-wave problem. The level sets of $u(t,x)$ propagate with the same rates as the free boundaries. The proof uses delicate upper and lower solutions constructed from a smooth profile function in the case $s\in (0, 1/2]$, and from the semi-wave profile when $s\in (1/2, 1)$.

title: Connectivity, toughness, and hamiltonicity of simplicial polytopes
abstract: For every $d\ge4$, every prescribed connectivity $r\ge d$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a simplicial $d$-polytope whose graph has connectivity exactly $r$, is nontraceable, and has toughness less than $\varepsilon$. Thus the classical theorems of Whitney (1931) and Tutte (1956), which guarantee hamiltonicity under sufficiently high connectivity in dimension three, have no higher-dimensional counterpart. This answers a question posed by Bojan Mohar in 2001 on whether sufficiently high connectivity guarantees hamiltonicity of $4$-polytopal graphs and the connectivity questions raised by Ikegami, Maezawa, and Zamfirescu in 2021. For fixed $d\ge4$, $r\ge d$, and integer $k\ge2$, the examples can be chosen to have no closed spanning walk with at most $k$ visits per vertex, no spanning tree with degrees at most $k$, and nontraceable prisms. For fixed $d$ and $r$, we obtain graphs on $n$ vertices whose longest paths and cycles contain $O(\sqrt n)$ vertices. Consequently, the family of simplicial $d$-polytopes with connectivity exactly $r$ has Grünbaum--Walther shortness coefficient zero and shortness exponent at most $1/2$.

title: Riemannian Hessian analysis of Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem
abstract: Sobolev gradient flows for the Gross--Pitaevskii ground state problem are Riemannian gradient descent methods on the sphere under a metric induced by a discrete elliptic operator. We analyze their convergence through the condition number of the Riemannian Hessian at the ground state. Bounds of the Rayleigh quotient of the Riemannian Hessian give a uniform analysis of these methods for different metrics. The uniform analysis applies to the classical metrics, such as the shifted Laplacian and the energy-adaptive metrics. Inspired by this analysis, we also consider three new metrics. One of them is a Thomas--Fermi metric, whose condition number is bounded uniformly in the interaction strength for the one-dimensional harmonic trap and whose iteration count does not grow in the Thomas--Fermi regime in the numerical tests. The performance suggested by our analysis is consistent with three-dimensional numerical tests with up to one billion unknowns, for both Riemannian gradient descent and Riemannian conjugate gradient methods, whose practical performance is also related to the Hessian condition number. The Thomas--Fermi flow needs the fewest iterations, while the metrics inverted exactly by tensor-product solvers are the fastest in computational time on one GPU card.

title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
abstract: Given an integer $k \geq 2$ and a prime $p$ large enough depending on $k$, we show that, if $A \subseteq \mathbb F^n_p$ does not contain a restricted polynomial progression of the form \begin{align*} x, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1 \\ y_2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n \end{pmatrix}, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^2 \\ y_2^2 \\ \vdots \\ y_n^2 \end{pmatrix}, \ldots, x+\begin{pmatrix} y_1^{k-1} \\ y_2^{k-1} \\ \vdots \\ y_n^{k-1} \end{pmatrix}, \end{align*} where $x \in \mathbb F^n_p$ and $y \in \{0,2, 3, \ldots, M_k\}^n \backslash \{\vec{0} \}$, for some fixed $M_k$, then $A$ must have density bounded above by $\frac{C}{(\log^{(k^{O(k)})} n)^c}$, where $C, c>0$ only depend on $k$ and $p$. For $k\geq 4$, the best previously known bound came from the density Hales--Jewett theorem and was of inverse Ackermann type. The proof uses a recent inverse theorem for noise stability of Bhangale, Khot, Liu and Minzer, which arose in the study of constraint satisfaction problems. The main new ingredient is a proof that the underlying distribution counting restricted polynomial progressions does not admit a nontrivial abelian embedding.
comment: 26 pages. The paper is formalized, up to a single admit for the inverse Theorem 1.4, at this URL https://github.com/lacey-gatech/restricted-polynomials-lean

title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

title: Brane space localization and genus-0 T-duality with $H$-flux
abstract: We construct a geometric theory on the brane space $S^2M=C^\infty(S^2,M)$ associated to a gerbe with connection on $M$. Normalized logarithmic holonomy around the latitude circles defines an average holonomy line bundle on the brane space, whose connection and averaged flux give an equivariantly flat superconnection. We prove that the completed periodic exotic twisted cohomology defined by this superconnection localizes to the twisted cohomology of $M$. This {\bf brane space localization} happens in two stages: circle localization lands on the free path space of $M$, and contracting the paths, after a correction of the twisting form, brings us back to $M$. Parallel transport along the meridians lets us average gerbe module connections, after which the circular iterated-integral construction applies. The resulting {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern forms} restrict to the twisted Chern forms on $M$; their variation is described by {\bf twisted brane Bismut-Chern-Simons forms.} For a T-dual pair, transporting the classical Hori morphisms through localization yields {\bf graded genus-0 T-duality} on brane cohomology. The composite of each morphism with its dual is minus the Euler operator in the level variable, so these morphisms are isomorphisms at every nonzero level. At level one these morphisms are compatible with the brane character and twisted $K$-theory T-duality.

title: A kernel-independent precorrected-FFT method
abstract: The precorrected-FFT has been used to rapidly evaluate $N$-body sums arising in electromagnetics and acoustics settings. It has, however, been historically limited to kernels that satisfy a Green's identity. In this work, we demonstrate that, using an improved version of the method of proxy points, the precorrected-FFT can be used to efficiently compute $N$-body sums with a wide variety of kernels. This algorithm requires no analytic information beyond pointwise access to the kernel. Our examples include kernels from non-local PDEs, Matern kernels, anisotropic kernels, and the Green's functions of high order PDEs. We also provide a detailed algorithm for choosing the proxy points and spreading grid, as implemented in the new pcfft package. We show these algorithmic choices result in favorable scaling when compared to other kernel-independent fast summation methods. Finally, we use the algorithm to accelerate a wide variety of integral equations solvers involving non-standard kernels, with applications in surface scattering, geophysics, and microbial community formation.

title: A Simple Explicit Construction of Smaller Strong Blocking Sets
abstract: Alon, Bishnoi, Das and Neri constructed sequences of strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space $P({\bf F}_q, k-1)$ with sizes at most $Cqk$, where $k$ goes to the infinity and $C$ is a fixed positive constant not depending on $q$, in their paper published in Transactions AMS, vol. 277, pp. 5389-5410, 2024. This is equivalent to a sequence of minimal $[n_i,k_i]_q$ codes with positive rate $\frac{k_i}{n_i} \geq c$, where $k_i$ goes to the infinity and $c$ is a fixed positive constant only depending on $q$. They solved one of the main open problems on minimal codes. The Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri construction was based on asymptotically good sequences of algebraic geometric codes and expander graphs. However, the constant $C$ is large for small prime power $q$. In this paper, based on a simple approach using $(q-1)$-power intersecting algebraic geometric codes via concatenation to construct minimal codes, we construct explicit strong blocking sets in $(k-1)$-dimension projective space with sizes around $2(q^2-1)k$, equivalently, explicit minimal $[n,k]_q$ codes with length around $2(q^2-1)k$. This is an essential improvement on the previous result of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri, when $q \leq 11$. For large $q$, strong blocking sets and minimal codes in our construction are worse than the previous construction of Alon-Bishnoi-Das-Neri. However, our approach is much simpler and does not depend on expander graphs.

title: Compact Mean Curvature Flows from Non-Compact Initial Data
abstract: We construct compact, embedded solutions to the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ that arise from various non-compact initial data and exist for a finite time.

title: Reciprocal LCM powers and Robin's criterion
abstract: For $κ> 1$, we study the reciprocal LCM-power function \[ σ^{[κ]}_{-1}(n) := \sum_{d \mid n}μ(d)\,σ_{-1}(n / d)^κ. \] We determine its average and extremal orders. A natural Robin-scale normalization is strictly increasing in $κ$ and tends to $σ_{-1}$, yielding an RH-equivalent criterion. Unconditionally, the corresponding Robin inequality holds eventually on every bounded parameter interval. Directed interval arithmetic proves the inequality for each $n > 5040$ and $1 < κ\le 100{,}000$.

title: Large deviations for additive functionals of one-dimensional zero-range processes
abstract: We prove a large deviation principle for additive functionals of local Lipschitz functions of a one-dimensional symmetric zero-range process on the diffusive scale. The rate function is obtained from the dynamical large deviation principle for the empirical density and is characterized by a variational constraint involving the density at a fixed spatial point. On the microscopic side, a super-exponential replacement is needed to replace the local observable with a function of the empirical density. On the macroscopic side, the spatial regularity enjoyed by finite-rate trajectories is needed to pass from spatial averages to point evaluation.

title: Stability threshold of the Couette flow in 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations on $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$
abstract: In this paper, we study the transition threshold problem for the 2D Navier-Stokes Boussinesq equations around the Couette flow with a constant background temperature in two domains: $\mathbb{T} \times [-1, 1]$ and $\mathbb{R} \times [-1, 1]$. It was proved that if the sizes of initial perturbations of the vorticity and the temperature in Sobolev spaces are $ν^{\fr13}$ and $ν^{\fr56}$, respectively, then this system admits a globally stable solution. Besides, we derive the enhanced dissipation estimate for the vorticity and temperature, as well as the inviscid damping estimate for the velocity. The coupling in the equations poses some difficulties to the analysis. We overcome these challenges and establish the results via the quasi-linear method and energy estimates.

title: Quasipositive Braids, Presentations, and Garside Structures
abstract: We provide a presentation of the braid group in which the generating set is the set of all positive half-twists, the relations are balanced positive relations, and every relation is conjugate to one in a finite list. We then prove that for any such presentation, its positive monoid is not isomorphic to the quasipositive braid monoid. Finally, we show that the quasipositive braid monoid has no proper Garside family. These results settle a problem of Calegari from the K3 problems list.

title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
abstract: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.

title: A conditional bound $Λ\le0.13963$ for the de Bruijn--Newman constant
abstract: Assuming that $ζ(s)$ has no nontrivial zero with $\mathrm{Re}\, s > 7/8$, as asserted in a recent unrefereed preprint of OpenAI, we obtain $Λ\le 13963/100000 = 0.13963$ for the de Bruijn-Newman constant. A published Polymath boundary computation supplies a finite-region strip of half-width $1/5$. We derive an approximation on $3 \le \mathrm{Im}\, z \le 6$ from its general Riemann-Siegel coefficient bounds. At height $61/20$, a fixed cutoff permits two differentiations, and comparison with $ζ$ bounds both the zero-density kernel and its vertical derivative. A new conjugate-pair inequality and a twenty-four-step strip comparison give the stated bound. The finite scalar and polynomial certificates are included in the paper; earlier comparisons giving $0.17973$, $0.17172$, and $0.16408$ are retained to show the source of the gain. The argument uses neither Gordon's analytic inputs nor Gomila's new computations. The seven-eighths hypothesis remains an assumption, and the published numerical boundary input is retained.

title: Polyconvex neural-network surrogates with learned paired directional features for anisotropic hyperelastic homogenization
abstract: Approximating the effective anisotropic hyperelastic response of a representative volume element (RVE) requires constitutive expressiveness, mechanical consistency, and computational efficiency. This work develops a polyconvex physics-augmented neural network (PANN) construction based on paired directional features whose orientations, stretch powers, and determinant exponents adapt to the RVE response. The features are composed with convex, componentwise nondecreasing cores, realized as an input-convex neural network (ICNN) or an input-convex Kolmogorov-Arnold network (ICKAN). The complete energies satisfy objectivity, an exactly stress-free reference, two-dimensional polyconvexity, and prescribed growth conditions by construction, and nonnegative energy is certified separately for the selected models. On a multicavity and a single-cavity periodic cell, these energies are compared with an Unconstrained energy, trained identically without the curvature and growth constraints, and with three hyperreduced projection-based reduced-order models (HPROMs), which serve as physics-based references. On the first cell, learning the features lowers the stress error sevenfold, and six features suffice on both. The constrained energies remain below one percent in stress error and in the displacement error of a tensile-coupon FE$^2$ application with a full-order reference, whereas the Unconstrained energy and the HPROMs are more accurate inside the data. Beyond the data, however, the Unconstrained energy loses rank-one convexity, and under confined compression it stops below half of the 500 MPa that the constrained energies reach. These results quantify what the guarantees cost in accuracy and what they secure beyond the data.

title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carathéodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $σ$-complete, lattice-$σ$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

title: Reflexivity of Grothendieck Spaces and Strongly Normal Sequences
abstract: A normalized sequence $(y_n)$ in the dual $E^{*}$ of a Banach space $E$ is called normal if it is weak-star null, and strongly normal if [ G(y_n)=\left{x\in E:\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n(x)|<\infty\right} ] is dense in $E$. We prove that, within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, reflexivity is characterized by the subsequence behavior of normal sequences: a Grothendieck space $E$ is reflexive if and only if every normal sequence in $E^{*}$ contains a strongly normal subsequence. If $E$ is nonreflexive and Grothendieck, then $E^{*}$ contains a normalized weakly null sequence none of whose subsequences is strongly normal; more strongly, it contains a closed hereditarily $\ell_{1}$ subspace $Y$ with a normalized weakly null Schauder basis such that no sequence in $S(Y)$ is strongly normal. We also obtain an exact quotient criterion valid for arbitrary Banach spaces: a normal sequence has a strongly normal subsequence precisely when, for some subsequence $z=(z_n)$, the quotient $E/\bigcap_n\ker z_n$ is separable. The proofs combine a weak-star basic-sequence argument with results of Haydon, Johnson--Maurey--Schechtman and Popov. Concrete realizations are given in $(L_{\infty}(μ))^{*}$ for nonatomic probability spaces (and, more generally, for $σ$-finite spaces with a nonatomic part) and in $\ell_{\infty}^{*}$.
comment: 23 pages. Main results include a characterization of reflexivity within the class of Grothendieck Banach spaces, an exact separable-quotient criterion for strongly normal subsequences, and hereditary $\ell_1$ obstructions

title: Chern classes of Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds
abstract: We construct closed Levi non-degenerate CR manifolds with non-vanishing Chern monomials. For every $n \geq 2$ and $\lceil n / 4 \rceil \leq m \leq \lfloor n / 2 \rfloor$, there exists a $(2 n + 1)$-dimensional example of signature $(\lfloor n / 2 \rfloor, \lceil n / 2 \rceil)$ on which all Chern monomials with positive indices at most $m$ and total weight at most $n - m$ are non-zero in cohomology with real coefficients. Taking $m = \lceil n / 4 \rceil$ gives examples with $c_{1}^{\lfloor 3 n / 4 \rfloor} \neq 0$. For $n = 4$ or $n \geq 6$, the latter examples show that the Chern-class vanishing theorem for strictly pseudoconvex CR manifolds does not extend to the Levi non-degenerate case. In these dimensions, their underlying manifolds admit no strictly pseudoconvex CR structures. The construction uses circle bundles over products of integral pseudo-Kähler manifolds.

title: On the Isotropy Groups of Locally Finite Derivations of Laurent Polynomial Algebras
abstract: Let $A_n=\mathbb{k}[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_n^{\pm1}]$ be a Laurent polynomial algebra over a field $\mathbb{k}$ of characteristic zero. We determine explicitly the automorphisms commuting with each locally finite derivation \[ D_μ=\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i x_i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}, \qquad μ=(μ_1,\ldots,μ_n)^T\in\Bbbk^n. \] These are precisely the automorphisms $ρ(x_i)=λ_i x^{m_i}$, where $λ_i\in\mathbb{k}^\ast$, the exponent vectors $m_i$ are the columns of a matrix $M_ρ\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)$, and $μ^TM_ρ=μ^T$. We also give an explicit parametrization in dimension two and relate these automorphisms to symmetries of diagonal flows on algebraic tori.

title: Coordinate-Free Automatic Differentiation
abstract: Automatic differentiation (AD) is a cornerstone of modern machine learning. Since all AD frameworks implicitly fix a basis of Euclidean space to define gradients and Jacobians, they natively process mathematical objects that are arrays of a fixed set of coordinates. This makes it awkward to express objects such as rotations, volume forms, and curvatures that arise, for example, in applications of AI to science. Bespoke workarounds lack reusability. We show that (i) a single, basis-independent derivative operator can represent many geometric differential operations, and (ii) this operator can be expressed entirely in terms of existing AD primitives. This reusable transformation can be composed with JAX batching, compilation, and hardware acceleration. Geometry enters as algebraic data. We experimentally demonstrate its reuse across different manifold operators, its composition through a spacetime inverse-problem pipeline, and its use in optimization over different rotor subgroups.

title: Distributionally Robust Adaptive Iterative Covariance Steering for Small-Body Proximity Operations
abstract: Autonomous small-body proximity operations require continuous-thrust guidance under uncertain gravity, solar-radiation pressure (SRP), and stochastic disturbances. We combine iterative covariance steering (iCS) with $L_1$ distributionally robust adaptive control ($L_1$-DRAC) to provide risk-aware collision avoidance despite mismatch between the nominal planning model and the true dynamics. Iterative covariance steering plans a nominal feedback policy satisfying distributionally robust conditional value-at-risk keep-out constraints, while $L_1$-DRAC compensates for dynamics uncertainty and bounds the residual distributional mismatch through a Wasserstein radius used by the planner. In $\mathbf{1000}$ paired Monte Carlo trials with gravity, SRP, and diffusion mismatch, $L_1$-DRAC adaptive control reduces the keep-out violation rate from $\mathbf{32.7\%}$ to $\mathbf{0.2\%}$ and the physical collision rate from $\mathbf{16.4\%}$ to zero, without actuator saturation.
journal_ref: https://space-robots.org/events/iros2026; https://openreview.net/group?id=IEEE.org/IROS/2026/Workshop/SRW

title: Wiener's lemma for quasicrystals: hull-uniform decay of covariant kernels on Delone sets
abstract: This paper studies continuous covariant kernel families over hulls of Delone sets of finite local complexity using graded Wiener-algebra methods. The norm given by the least common weighted summable off-diagonal profile is identified isometrically with a graded $\ell^1$-norm. The resulting Banach $*$-algebras are symmetric, spectrally invariant in the reduced groupoid C*-algebra, and stable under holomorphic functional calculus. Exact physical weights give preservation of polynomial and stretched-exponential classes, including a fixed stretched-exponential rate. A configuration with dense orbit has a faithful regular representation. Invertibility on that configuration therefore gives an inverse family with one profile valid throughout the hull; for repetitive sets every configuration has this property. For polynomial weights of order $s>0$, return-vector counting yields a differential estimate with parameter $κ/(κ+s)$, where $κ$ is a growth exponent of the return vectors and may be taken equal to $d$ for Meyer sets. Combined with established norm-controlled inversion criteria, this gives explicit bounds in the common-profile norm. Explicit bounds are also obtained for stretched-exponential physical weights and for gapped Fermi projections.

title: Efficient lifts into odd dimensions of Spherical $5$- and $7$-designs with Balanced Halves
abstract: We propose constructions of spherical $5$- and $7$-designs in odd dimensions by lifting balanced halves of even-dimensional designs to several layers of suitable latitudes. For every odd dimension, we obtain an explicit spherical $5$-design with at most $60(d^2-1)$ points, attaining the optimal quadratic order in the dimension. Assuming Zauner's conjecture, this bound improves to $7.5(d-1)^2$. For every odd $d \geq 9$, we also construct a spherical $7$-design with $110M$ points from a complex projective $3$-design with $M$ points in $\mathbb{CP}^{(d-3)/2}$.

title: Detecting Random Geometric Graphs with General Kernel
abstract: We study testing a random geometric graph with a fixed kernel against an Erdős-Rényi graph with the same edge density. Under the null hypothesis, the graph has $n$ vertices and independent edges with probability $p$. Under the alternative hypothesis, latent points $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent and uniform on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and edges are conditionally independent with probabilities $K(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)$, where $p=\mathbb{E}[K(\langle X_1,X_2\rangle)]$. The goal is to determine a critical dimension $d_\star = d_\star(n,K)$: the total variation distance between the two graph laws tends to one for $d\ll d_\star$ and to zero for $d\gg d_\star$. For dense graphs, [BDER16] established $d_\star\asymp n^3$ for hard threshold kernels, whereas [MWX26] proved $d_\star\asymp n^{3/4}$ for smooth kernels with $K'(0)\ne0$. We connect these results by characterizing the detection thresholds for kernels that need not be differentiable at zero. We also determine the thresholds for smooth kernels whose first nonzero derivative at zero has finite order greater than one. Throughout these classes, signed triangle or quadrilateral counts attain the optimal detection threshold. For certain nondifferentiable kernels, quadrilateral counts are optimal while triangle counts are suboptimal.

title: Generic mean curvature flow has finitely many singularities
abstract: We show that for a generic compact initial surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and any generic compact initial mean convex hypersurface in higher dimensions, the mean curvature flow encounters only finitely many singularities. This resolves the full generic Morse regularity conjectures of Ilmanen and Colding-Minicozzi-Pedersen in the above two cases. More generally, we show that if a mean curvature flow of a compact hypersurface has only multiplicity one spherical and cylindrical singularities, then after a small perturbation of the initial condition only non-degenerate cylindrical and spherical singularities appear.

title: A Rigid Analytic Curve Can Have a Dense $p$-adic Orbit
abstract: Let $\mathcal D$ be a product of Drinfeld upper half spaces and let $J$ be the corresponding product of projective linear groups acting on $\mathcal D$. We prove that if $Y$ is a reduced, quasi-compact separated strict $\mathbb C_p$-analytic space and $f: Y\to\mathcal D$ is analytic with $\dim Y<\dim\mathcal D$, then $J f(Y(\mathbb C_p))$ is closed and nowhere dense in $\mathcal D(\mathbb C_p)$. The quasi-compactness assumption is necessary even when the source is a strict rigid analytic curve, while a quasi-compact perfectoid source can still have an orbit closure with nonempty interior. For every finite extension $F/\mathbb Q_p$ and $d\geq3$, we construct a closed smooth irreducible non-quasi-compact curve in $Ω_F^{d-1}$ with dense orbit under a fixed diagonal one-parameter subgroup. We also construct a $\mathbb Q_p$-defined analytic map from the open unit disc to $\mathbf P^2$ with dense $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit, and an analytic map from a one-dimensional affinoid perfectoid torus to $\mathbf P^2$ whose $\operatorname{PGL}_3(\mathbb Q_p)$-orbit closure has nonempty interior.

title: High-Index Asymptotics of Mathieu Spectral Gaps and Splittings
abstract: Consider the Mathieu operator $L=-d^2/dx^2+2a\cos(2x)$ for fixed $a\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$. For large enough $n$, the periodic ($n$ even) or anti-periodic ($n$ odd) problem on $[0,π]$ has exactly two algebraically simple eigenvalues $λ_n^-,λ_n^+$ in the disc $|λ-n^2|<1$. We prove that, as $n\to\infty$, $λ_n^+-λ_n^-=\pm\frac{8(a/4)^n}{[(n-1)!]^2}\exp\left[-\frac{a^2(n+2)}{4(n^2-1)^2}-\frac{15a^4}{128n^7}+O(n^{-8})\right]$, where the sign depends on the labelling. For real $a$ with $λ_n^-<λ_n^+$, this difference is the length of the $n$th spectral gap. Expanding the exponential determines the relative corrections of orders $n^{-4}$ to $n^{-7}$, beyond the correction $-a^2/(4n^3)$ obtained by Anahtarci and Djakov (2012) with a relative $O(n^{-4})$ remainder. By isospectrality, the same formula holds for the potential $ce^{-2ix}+de^{2ix}$ with $a^2=cd\ne0$.

title: Algebraic Vector Bundles on Cluster Varieties
abstract: We study algebraic vector bundles on cluster varieties. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, every algebraic vector bundle is trivial on a cluster variety with principal coefficients at an acyclic seed of irreducible finite Dynkin type. The proof is based on integral contractions of cellular $\mathbb A^1$-chain complexes and successive freezing. We also construct smooth cluster varieties admitting indecomposable rank-two vector bundles, whose nontriviality is detected by quadratic Euler classes. The cellular calculation also gives a criterion for stable freeness and computes integral real cohomology and the images of cycle class maps.

title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
abstract: We develop a neural transport framework for nonlinear, nonlocal aggregationdiffusion equations arising in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and related applications. Based on the Onsager variational principle, we reformulate the governing equation as a constrained optimal control problem, taking the velocity field as the control and evolving the density via the associated continuity equation. The velocity field is parameterized by a neural network trained on the variational objective evaluated along particle trajectories. By coupling the density and generalized score equations into a single system solved via the Euler method, the score function propagates efficiently for loss evaluation. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous error analysis that decomposes the total error into approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization components, and prove corresponding error bounds. Numerical experiments across several representative models demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: Minimax Rates for Estimating Powered Sliced Wasserstein Functionals
abstract: We study the two-sample estimation of the powered Sliced Wasserstein functional under projected $r$-th moment assumptions. Let $N=n\wedge m$, where $n$ and $m$ are two sample sizes. We establish the minimax rates in the noncritical regimes. When $p<r<2p$, the minimax risk is of order $N^{-(r-p)/r}$, while for $r>2p$ it is of order $N^{-1/2}$. In both cases, the natural plug-in estimator is minimax rate-optimal. At the endpoint $r=p$, the minimax risk is bounded away from zero, so uniformly consistent estimation is impossible. At the critical order $r=2p$, we obtain the exact worst-case rate of the plug-in estimator and a lower bound for the minimax risk, leaving a logarithmic gap between the lower and upper bounds. The exact minimax rate in this critical case remains open.

title: $G$-Equivariant Hilbert Schemes and Quadratic Forms
abstract: For a finite abelian group $G$ acting linearly on the plane let $\mathcal{X}$ be the associated quotient stack. We analyze a fine moduli space which parameterizes zero dimensional substacks of $\mathcal{X}$ whose corresponding subschemes of the plane have a given representation type, denoted by $\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]}$. By means of a Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch theorem of Toën we give explicit representation theoretic formulas of $\dim(\mathcal{X}^{[ρ]})$ for all $ρ\in \operatorname{Rep}(G)$ which are similar to the McKay correspondence. We also give a classification of all such quotient stacks according to an associated quadratic form called the Euler form. For $[\mathbb{A}^2/μ_n]$ given by the cyclic action $ζ\cdot (x,y) = (ζx, ζ^{-1} y)$, we give an interpretation of the corresponding Euler form in terms of border strips which may be removed by a diagram, an equational characterization of $n$-core partitions, and the number of significant arrows of a monomial ideal as defined in "Smooth and Irreducible Multigraded Hilbert Schemes" by D. Maclagan and G. Smith.

title: Childcare Waitlists
abstract: Parents seeking childcare often face long waitlists. At the same time, vacancies at childcare centers can remain unfilled for extended periods. We trace this paradox to two persistent features of childcare services. First, families consider multiple child care options due to enrollment uncertainties, resulting in phantom listings that remain on waitlists even after families have found care elsewhere or no longer need a slot. Second, filling a slot is time-consuming: centers learn whether a family is actively seeking enrollment only after making an offer and waiting for a response. As families pursue alternatives while they wait and their children age, these delays and feedback effects amplify the mismatch between demand and available capacity. We study two operational remedies. First, we examine regular verification that removes phantom listings before offers are made, improving the efficiency of enrollment and reducing vacancies. Second, we study mixed-age classrooms, in which some slots designated for older children can be flexibly used by younger children. This flexibility increases utilization, shortens waits, and reduces wasted offers. Its benefits extend beyond conventional pooling: as children move between age groups, classrooms can be filled through internal flows rather than costly external search, further reducing enrollment delays. Together, verification and mixed use offer a way to expand effective capacity in early childhood classrooms, where regulatory and operational constraints make adding physical capacity particularly costly.

title: Equivariant Steklov homogenisation and stability of spectral representations
abstract: We prove that isolated spectral clusters preserve their finite-group representation under equivariant spectral convergence. In particular, an irreducible limiting eigenspace cannot split into several nearby eigenvalues, while an isotypic limiting eigenspace imposes corresponding divisibility constraints on the multiplicities in the approximating cluster. We then construct a one-parameter equivariant Steklov homogenisation on closed orientable surfaces, allowing Laplace spectral representations to be transferred to Steklov spectral clusters. Applied to the hyperbolic surfaces of Fortier Bourque, Gruda-Mediavilla, Petri, and Pineault, this yields first Steklov multiplicities 16 and 21 in genera 10 and 17, and at least 24 in genus 37. These examples give counterexamples to Jammes's conjecture on first Steklov multiplicity.

title: Effective-dimension bounds in the central limit theorem for centered Euclidean balls
abstract: We establish a nonasymptotic Gaussian approximation bound over centered Euclidean balls for sums of independent, not necessarily identically distributed, random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\). Let \(S_n\) denote the sum, let \(Σ=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\), and let \(G\sim N(0,Σ)\). Define the effective rank and the normalized squared spectral mass by \[ r(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}Σ}{\|Σ\|}, \qquad v(Σ)=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(Σ^2)}{\|Σ\|^2}. \] Under a uniform directional fourth-moment condition, covariance-balance assumptions, and the spectral conditions \(r(Σ)\le C_Σv(Σ)\) and \(v(Σ)\ge6\), we prove \[ \sup_{z\ge0} \left| \mathbb P\{\|S_n\|^2\le z\} - \mathbb P\{\|G\|^2\le z\} \right| \le C\,\frac{r(Σ)^{3/2}}{n}. \] The constant depends only on the fixed parameters in the assumptions and is independent of the ambient dimension and individual small eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. The bound is uniform at the endpoint \(v(Σ)=6\), without a logarithmic loss. Its main feature is the combination of the \(n^{-1}\) rate with dependence on effective rank, including this endpoint. Consequently, the bound can vanish when \(r(Σ)=o(n^{2/3})\), even when \(p\) is much larger than \(n\). The same estimate extends to random elements of a separable Hilbert space with trace class covariance. The proof builds on the Fourier and symmetrization methods of \citet{GoetzeZaitsev2014}, combined with moment matching, truncation, and comparison estimates that retain the covariance structure.

title: The Stable Marriage Polytope is Box-Totally Dual Integral
abstract: A stable matching in a bipartite preference system is a matching that has no unmatched pair whose endpoints both prefer each other to their current assignments. Rothblum gave a linear description of the stable marriage polytope, the convex hull of the incidence vectors of stable matchings. We prove that this polytope is box-totally dual integral. The proof uses the affine representation of the stable marriage polytope as an order polytope together with the matricial characterization of box-TDI polyhedra. Since Kiraly and Pap proved that Rothblum's description is totally dual integral, our result further implies that Rothblum's system is box-totally dual integral.

title: Tandem Queues with Hybrid Abandonment in Heavy Traffic
abstract: Hybrid-abandonment systems, where jobs abandon from certain stages of service but not others, occur frequently in medical, service, and computing systems. Abandonment affects the heavy-traffic behavior of both the stages with and without abandonment. In contrast to existing heavy-traffic works that focus on cases where there is abandonment at either all stages or no stages, we focus on the heavy-traffic behavior for these hybrid-abandonment systems. We provide the first heavy-traffic characterization of the second queue length in a two-stage tandem queue with abandonment only in the first stage. We characterize the scaled mean of the second stage queue length and prove that the scaled second queue length is asymptotically exponentially distributed and asymptotically independent of the first stage queue length. We derive our results by analyzing Markovian arrival process queues with countably infinite phases. We do this by extending techniques used to analyze queues with Markov-modulated arrivals to the broader class of infinite Markovian arrival process queues. We prove asymptotic results for a more general infinite phase process condition, an infinite birth-death phase process, and the hybrid-abandonment tandem case. We also empirically demonstrate that our heavy-traffic approximations are good approximations across various system settings.

title: SDDP has polynomial iteration complexity in the horizon
abstract: Stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) and its variants are run in practice with forward passes that sample the noise at random. Recent iteration-complexity results favour another choice: when the trial points are selected deterministically, for instance along the scenario with the largest gap, the number of iterations is polynomial in the horizon $T$, whereas every bound we know of for randomly sampled forward passes is exponential in $T$. We show that this is not intrinsic to random sampling, for a broad class of trajectory-following dynamic programming algorithms, which includes SDDP, stochastic dual dynamic integer programming and stochastic Lipschitz dynamic programming. With random sampling, and with Lipschitz constants, diameters and per-stage loss ranges bounded independently of the stage and of the horizon, the expected number of iterations whose policy is not $T\varepsilon$-optimal is $O(T\varepsilon^{-(d+1)})$, where $d$ is the state dimension: linear in $T$, as for deterministic selection rules. The proof needs no particular scenario to be sampled: the gap between the expected cost of the current policy and the current lower bound equals the expected sum of one-step Bellman residuals along the sampled path, and Lipschitz cuts that are tight at the visited states turn the positive residuals into permanent increases of a bounded potential. The results extend to noise without finite support, to backward passes on a sample average approximation, and to stationary and periodic infinite-horizon SDDP with geometric pass lengths.

title: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
abstract: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.

title: Pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise Hölder continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise Hölder continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.

title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.

title: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
abstract: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.

title: Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three
abstract: We prove that every finite ordered set of width at most three and cardinality at least four is reconstructible from its deck. This settles the width-three part of an open problem posed by Schröder in Ordered Sets; the separate question concerning ordered sets of height one is not addressed here. The new ingredient is a criterion for recovering the marked maximal deck of an ordered set with exactly three maximal elements from its unmarked maximal deck and the isomorphism type of the suborder obtained by deleting all maximal elements. We express the criterion as an orbital balance condition on the attachment ideals in this common base. Necessity follows by double counting; sufficiency uses the structure of automorphism actions in width at most three. The full-deck theorem then follows from reconstruction results of Schröder concerning maximal cards and marked maximal cards. A local reattachment argument correcting one intermediate step in the two-maximal-element case is included in an appendix.

title: An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
abstract: We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.

title: Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wiśniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.

title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question remains open. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

title: A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations
abstract: The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.

title: The square function estimate for the cone in four dimensions
abstract: We obtain the $L^3$ reverse square function estimate for the light cone in four dimensions from the critical local-smoothing and round-cone propagation statements in the September 2026 OpenAI manuscript. We state these inputs, together with the plate maximal theorem of Di Plinio and Parissis, in a preliminaries section. The proof passes from geometric concentration of packet coefficients to regularity of the analyzed wave, and then from free waves to arbitrary functions supported near the cone. As a consequence, we obtain the corresponding $L^3$ estimate for the sphere and elliptic paraboloids in three dimensions.

title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
abstract: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.

title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Grünbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Grünbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gröbner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincaré series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gröbner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.

title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.

title: Stochastic Modelling of Telomere Length Dynamics During Hematopoiesis
abstract: We introduce a new stochastic model of telomere length dynamics during hematopoiesis. The numerous cell divisions occurring in this setting makes telomere length dynamics, and in particular their attrition, a crucial aspect of hematopoiesis. After recalling the main aspect of the biological setting, we describe an individual based model of hematopoietic population cells. We then study its behaviour in the large population limit, as well as its fluctuations.

title: Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
abstract: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.

title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a one-time symbolic phase, the runtime bus-type projection overhead is entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The framework is realized in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 24.4-30.1x faster than the MATPOWER- style baseline and 6.0-7.8x faster than the Schafer-Braun optimized assembly. End-to-end, the grid-level solve time is 11.7x-154.3x faster than pandapower 3.5.4 with Numba, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. Compared with the native C++ LightSim2Grid 1.0.0, grid-level performance is comparable on IEEE 39 and 1.3x-1.8x faster on IEEE 118 and the PEGASE systems. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

title: Median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo for nested integration
abstract: Nested integrals $\int f\left(\int g(\boldsymbol{y},\boldsymbol{x})\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{x}\right)\mathrm{d}{}\boldsymbol{y}$ where $\boldsymbol{y}\in[0,1]^{d_1}$ and $\boldsymbol{x}\in[0,1]^{d_2}$ frequently arise in Bayesian experimental design, medical decision making, and computational finance. Statistical estimators for nested integrals are more computationally demanding than for standard integrals. Recent studies demonstrate that the median randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (mRQMC) method achieves super-polynomial convergence rates for analytic integrands. We extend mRQMC methods to nested integrations and propose a novel double-loop mRQMC estimator with super-polynomial convergence rate if both the inner and outer integrands are analytic. Established estimators for nested integrals, such as double-loop or multilevel Monte Carlo, are by contrast limited to algebraic convergence rates. However, expected information gain (EIG) applications from experimental design typically do not fulfill this condition due to a lack of regularity in the outer integrand. We address this through a theoretically-grounded importance sampling regularization scheme. Although super-polynomial convergence rates remain achievable for the inner integral, only the algebraic rate $α+3/2-ε$ for any $ε>0$ can be theoretically guaranteed for the outer integral in the EIG, where $α\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$ denotes the order of the mixed derivatives of the regularized outer integrand. Our approach shows substantial improvements over double-loop randomized quasi-Monte Carlo methods based on the sample mean in moderately high-dimensional settings for a simple polynomial example. Moreover, we demonstrate improved convergence behavior of the median-based estimator for the more challenging setting of EIG estimation.

title: Optimal Rates for Federated Variational Inequalities under different relaxations of bounded variance assumption
abstract: We study how interpolation affects local steps and parallel sampling in monotone variational inequalities (VIs), with $m$ workers, $K$ oracle calls per worker per round, and $N$ rounds. Under the strong growth condition (SGC), we determine the minimax rate for affine VIs, attained by local extragradient with worker averaging. For nonlinear monotone VIs and convex-concave saddle problems with Lipschitz operators satisfying SGC, we improve the stochastic terms of bounded-variance expected-gap guarantees from $(KN)^{-1/2}$ to $(KN)^{-1}$ with local steps and from $(mKN)^{-1/2}$ to $(mKN)^{-1}$ with minibatches. Under strong monotonicity, we improve the noise-dependent condition-number scaling of existing extragradient bounds from quadratic to linear. The resulting monotone-gap and strongly monotone accuracy bounds match lower bounds up to logarithmic factors in $m$. Under generalized smoothness and SGC, adaptive steps give polynomial dependence on the initial radius. For affine VIs with globally bounded oracle variance, we also attain the minimax rate: the deterministic rate over $KN$ sequential calls plus the statistical rate over all $mKN$ samples. For composite VIs with smooth convex sample interpolation and an exactly evaluated monotone Lipschitz component, accelerated mirror-prox sliding achieves an $N^{-2}$ gradient term, a $(KN)^{-1}$ monotone term, and a $(mKN)^{-1}$ sampling term, without assuming SGC.

title: Frugal coloring in planar graphs with maximum degree 4 and 5
abstract: A proper coloring of vertices of a graph $G$ is called $t$-frugal if no color appears more than $t$ times in the neighborhood of any vertex of $G$. While $1$-frugal coloring coincides with $2$-distance coloring, we study $2$-frugal colorings of planar graphs with maximum degree $4$ and $5$, respectively. We prove that every planar graph with maximum degree $4$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $7$ colors, while a planar graph with maximum degree $5$ admits a $2$-frugal coloring with $10$ colors. The results present variations of parts of the famous Wegner's conjecture, which for planar graphs with maximum degree $Δ\in\{4,\ldots,7\}$ states that their $2$-distance chromatic number is at most $Δ+5$.

title: The first homology of square-section braid groups
abstract: We compute the first homology of the unordered configuration space of $n$ open unit-squares in the $w$ by $h$ rectangle for all positive integers $n$, $w$, and $h$. Letting $w$ and $h$ vary, these square configuration spaces form a bi-filtration of the unordered configuration space of $n$ points in the plane, so their fundamental groups approximate the $n$-strand braid group. Using a pair of spectral sequences, we prove that these square and point configuration spaces have naturally isomorphic first homology groups if $w,h\ge 3$ and $n\le wh-3$. In the $h=2$ case, we show that the first homology groups of these square configuration spaces are free of rank $n-1$ for $n\le 2w-2$, whereas they are free of rank $w-1$ for $n=2w-1$.

title: Equality Cases in the Tu-Deng Conjecture Bound
abstract: The Tu-Deng Conjecture, made in 2011, asserts that for $k\geq2$ and $1\leq t<2^k-1$, the set \[ S_{t,k}=\left\{(a,b)\in\{0,1,\ldots,2^k-2\}^2: a+b\equiv t\pmod{2^k-1},\quad \wt(a)+\wt(b)<k\right\} \] satisfies \[ |S_{t,k}|\leq 2^{k-1}. \] Proofs of the conjecture were given independently by the author and by Liu, Luo and Xie in arXiv in 2026. Let $r=\wt(t)$, and let $z=k-r$ be the number of zeros in the $k$-bit expansion of $t$. We prove that equality holds in the Tu-Deng Conjecture if and only if every cyclic distance between consecutive zeros is at least $z$. We give several other simple necessary and sufficient conditions, including a forbidden-pattern condition, a packing condition for the zero positions, a composition condition for the gaps, and equivalent conditions involving the coefficients of the polynomial $H_W(u,v)$ in the proof of the Tu-Deng conjecture. We also count the equality words having a prescribed number of zeros.

title: Pointed Gromov-Hausdorff Distance between $l^p$-Wedge Sums and Isometric Embeddings of $l^\infty$
abstract: The paper studies $l^p$-wedge sums of metric spaces and provides a two-sided estimate for the pointed Gromov-Hausdorff distance between them. Using an upper bound for the Gromov-Hausdorff distance, the existence of an isometric embedding of $l^\infty$ into the Gromov-Hausdorff space of all non-empty metric spaces is proved.

title: Removing Boundary Smoothness from the Hot-Spots Conclusion in the Simple-Eigenvalue Case
abstract: We give a reduction from a smooth-domain theorem excluding interior critical points of first positive Neumann eigenfunctions to a non-strict hot-spots conclusion on arbitrary bounded simply connected planar domains with compact Neumann resolvent and simple first positive eigenvalue. The main analytic step is spectral convergence under exhaustion by conformal images of concentric disks. A reflection extension, conformal invariance of Dirichlet energy, and compactness of the Sobolev embedding give a direct proof. A truncation argument justifies square integrability of the transferred extensions without any boundary regularity. The smooth-domain theorem proved by OpenAI is an external input; the approximation argument is proved here in full. The paper was generated by ChatGPT with prompts from the listed author.

title: A cyclotomic gluing construction for lattice sphere packings
abstract: For a positive integer $d$, let $Δ_d^L$ denote the supremum of the densities of lattice sphere packings in $\mathbb R^d$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large $d$, $Δ_d^L \gg d^2\log\log d\,2^{-d}$. Abuya-Gargava-Zhao obtained the same bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions by combining Venkatesh's cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag's stochastic ellipsoid method. We introduce a multi-cyclotomic gluing construction that allows this argument to work in every sufficiently large dimension.

title: Mesh-Native Tokenisation: Retrofitting Foundation Models to Unstructured Data
abstract: Physics foundation models are an increasingly popular approach for building versatile emulators for spatiotemporal systems. They require tokenisation layers that lift physical field data into a latent representation suitable for dynamic processing. A typical choice for this layer is a convolutional encoder, which lifts field information in a locality-aware way and can be trained very efficiently. However, this choice cannot be applied to a large class of scientific computing problems where data are represented on unstructured meshes, for example simulations on domains with curved boundaries. Such data typically require graph neural network architectures, which are more expensive to train and, in the form currently used, encode information differently from their CNN counterparts, thus limiting the portability of physics emulators between these data regimes. In this work we introduce Mesh-Native Convolution (MNC), a locality-aware tokenisation layer that encodes unstructured mesh-based data in a way that is analogous to CNNs. This approach leads to models that can be trained once on mesh data and then deployed to arbitrary unstructured meshes, even if these are irregular, with minimal retraining. We show that this tokenisation approach can be used to retrofit grid-pretrained foundation models efficiently on unstructured meshes and provide theoretical results to confirm the consistency of this approach with classical CNN encoders. We demonstrate the favourable performance of this retrofitting approach, which in many cases reaches acceptable accuracy even in zero-shot deployment, and outperforms existing baselines after only a few epochs of fine-tuning, thus providing an efficient bridge between the two data regimes.

title: Maximal Linear Arrangement is NP complete on Bipartite Graphs
abstract: The linear arrangement of a simple graph $G = (V,E)$ is a bijective labeling $π$ of the vertices of $G$ to the set $\{1, \ldots, n\}$. The maximum linear arrangement ($\texttt{maxLA}$) problem is to determine whether $G$ has a labeling such that the sum of labels across $G$'s edges, $\sum_{uv \in E} |π(u) - π(v)|$, is at least a given value $k$. Minimum linear arrangement ($\texttt{minLA}$) is defined analogously. Both $\texttt{maxLA}$ and $\texttt{minLA}$ are known to be NP complete for general graphs. $\texttt{minLA}$ has shown to be NP complete for bipartite graphs by Evans and Shiloah in 1975. It has been an open problem whether the same holds for $\texttt{maxLA}$. In this paper we prove that $\texttt{maxLA}$ is NP complete for bipartite graphs.

title: Ultrafilter characters and local $π$-bases
abstract: We completely resolve Question~5.3 of Kania's paper \cite{Kania} and establish a more general realization theorem. We show that for infinite cardinals $μ\leqslantν<κ<λ$, a space with \[ \pc(X)=μ,\qquad\pcl(X)=ν,\qquad \pcc(X)=κ,\qquad\pcd(X)=λ\] exists if and only if $κ\leqslant2^μ$. The witnesses may be zero-dimensional and Tychonoff spaces, of the least possible cardinality $λ$. They may have the least possible number of non-isolated points, or alternatively be crowded. The main ingredient is an exact computation of the centered local $π$-character of star filter spaces in terms of ultrafilter character, obtained from a finite selection lemma for filter pushforwards. We also construct a single space with countable $r$-linked local $π$-bases for every finite $r$, centered value $ω_1$, and any prescribed decreasing value greater than $ω_1$.

title: Fourier Transform-Based Computation of Two-Electron Four-Center Coulomb Repulsion Integrals
abstract: We present a Fourier-based method for evaluating two-electron four-center Coulomb repulsion integrals over Slater-type orbitals. Spherical Fourier-Bessel coefficients of the convolution factors are precomputed and reused. Since the spherical part of the integral can be evaluated directly, there remains only a one-dimensional quadrature problem in the radial direction. For the ten reference integrals reported here, the largest absolute discrepancy is $1.7\times10^{-9}$. A preliminary resident-cache benchmark computes approximately $4.2\times10^5$ unique integrals per second on an NVIDIA V100 at the contraction stage.

title: Properness of the Cuspidal Hilbert Eigenvariety
abstract: We prove that for any prime $p$ and tame level $N$, the weight map from the cuspidal Hilbert eigenvariety constructed by Andreatta-Iovita-Pilloni for a totally real field $F$ to the weight space is proper in the sense of Buzzard-Calegari, under a non-vanishing hypothesis on certain Sen polynomials of Galois representations at the primes above $p$. In particular, this yields the properness of the eigenvariety away from non-positive integral Sen weights. Our approach extends the $p$-adic Hodge-theoretic argument of Diao-Liu.

title: LInearity of Tubular Groups
abstract: We prove that a tubular group is linear if and only if it is residually finite, equivalently virtually primitive. Every such group embeds in $\SL_n(\Z[u])$. For a primitive tubular decomposition with at most $m$ edge slopes at each vertex, our representation has dimension $2\max\{2,m\}$. In particular, Gersten's group embeds in $\SL_6(\Z[u])$, and this dimension is minimal.

title: Ancestral circulation beyond two Fleming-Viot particles
abstract: Reversible motion can produce a directed circulation of surviving ancestry in a \FV\ particle system. We prove that two particles are the exact threshold for universal ancestral balance in finite systems with uniform copying. For two particles, the stationary current of surviving labels vanishes for every finite irreducible reversible Markov chain and every positive killing vector. On a fixed complete three-state graph, nonzero circulation occurs for each population size at least three on an open dense set of killing vectors of full Lebesgue measure. A single killing vector produces circulation simultaneously for every population size at least three, and such vectors form a dense $G_δ$ set of full measure. The current is divergence free and vanishes on bridges, so three sites and three particles are the smallest possible setting for circulation. We also identify the probabilistic effect of this circulation: for sufficiently rare transplants, migration followed by fixation is more likely in one direction than in the reverse direction.

title: Global obstruction property and its applications
abstract: We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite.
